*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 5-1. - Legal status.
   (a)   Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall control the classification
of all buildings as to use group and type of construction and the definition of
all terms relating thereto in the city.
   (b)   Saving clause. Nothing in this chapter or in the building code hereby
adopted shall be construed to affect any suit or proceeding impending in any
court, any rights acquitted, liability incurred, or any cause or causes of
action acquired or existing, under any act or ordinance hereby repealed, nor
shall any just or legal right or remedy of any character be lost, impaired or
affected by this chapter.
(Ord. No. 86-369, §§ 200.1, 200.2, 10-7-86)
Secs. 5-2—5-25. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - BUILDING CODE ***
Sec. 5-26. - Adoption.
   Certain documents, copies of which are on file in the office of the city
clerk, being marked and designated as the Michigan Building Code 2000 edition
along with Appendixes G and H, Michigan Residential Code 2000 edition along
with Appendixes A, B, C, D, E, F, F, G, J and K, 2003 Michigan Rehabilitation
Code for Existing Buildings as amended, 2000 Michigan Plumbing Code, 2000
Michigan Mechanical Code are hereby adopted in their entirety along with any
subsequent amendments as the building code of the city for the control of
buildings and structures; and each and all of the regulations, provisions,
penalties, conditions and terms of the above are hereby referred to, adopted,
and make a part hereof, as if fully set out in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 86-369, § 1, 10-7-86; Ord. No. 94-618, 1-3-95; Ord. No. 97-702, 5-20-
97; Ord. No. 03-927, 4-1-03)
State Law reference— Authority to adopt technical codes by reference, MCL 117.3
(k).
Sec. 5-27. - Additions, insertions and changes.
   The following sections of the Michigan Building Code, 2000 Edition, adopted
in this article are hereby added or revised as follows:
    (1)   Section 107.1. Permits required. Permits shall be obtained before
starting work in the city, and such permits must be displayed in the front
window or other prominent place on the job site, clearly visible from the
street. Failure to obtain a proper permit before commencing work or failure to
properly display a permit on the job site will be deemed a violation of this
code. In such cases a "Stop Work" sign will immediately be posted, and no
further work will be permitted until such time as proper permits are obtained
and/or displayed and all required fees paid. Refer to Section 1.05 of the 2000
Michigan Building Code for Permits required.
      a.   Changing the established grade level of any lot or part of any lot.
Whenever, in the opinion of the building official or the city engineer, such
proposed changing of the grade level will tend to create a nuisance or hazard
to the adjoining property or to the public health, welfare and safety, no
permit shall be issued.
      b.   The temporary obstruction of any street or sidewalk required by any
building operation. Notice of all such permits shall be transmitted to the
police and fire departments.
      c.   The construction or installation of all above or below ground
storage tanks, vaults, or containers.
      In computing the time limit listed in this section, the contractor shall
not have charged against him any delays caused by good faith labor disputes,
strikes, or acts of God.
   (2)   Section 108.8. Display of permit. With each and every permit issued
for building or other structures, the department shall issue to the owner or
their agent a weatherproof card properly filled out, and it shall be their duty
to place such card in a conspicuous place on the premises before the
construction work is started and maintain it while the building operation is in
progress, the card to be unobstructed from the public view and to be accessible
to the inspector.
   (3)   Section 111.5. Building grade requirements. Subsequent to the issuance
of a building permit and prior to the commencement of construction, the permit
holder, or their authorized agent, shall set survey stakes on the property
which shall delineate the building grade in conformance with the approved plot
plan.
   (4)   Section 111.6. Grading requirements. No holder of any permit shall
receive a final inspection or final certificate of occupancy until the property
upon which the building or structure is located has been graded in strict
compliance with the approved individual plot plan and the requirements of this
code.
   (5)   Section 112.3.1. Fees. All fees for permits, licenses and inspections
are contained in chapter 9 of this Code.
   (6)   Section 113.2. Required inspections. It shall be the duty of the
holder of every permit for a building or other structure or installation to
notify the building and safety department, 24 hours prior to the time for which
an appointment for inspection is being made, by giving the street address,
permit number, and type of inspection requested.
   (7)   Section 116.4. Violation penalties. Any person who shall violate a
provision of this code or shall fail to comply with any of the requirements
thereof or who shall erect, construct, alter or repair a building or structure
in violation of an approved plan or directive of the building official, or of a
permit or certificate issued under the provisions of this code, shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor punishable by fine of not more than $500.00, plus costs, or by
imprisonment not exceeding 90 days, or both such fine and imprisonment. Each
day that a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.
   (8)   Section 117.2. Unlawful continuance. Any person who shall continue any
work in or about the structure after having been served with a stop-work order,
except such work as he is directed to perform to remove a violation or unsafe
conditions, shall be liable to a fine of not less than $100.00 or more than
$500.00 or by imprisonment not to exceed 90 days or both, plus costs.
   (9)   Section 121.2. Membership of the board. The membership of the building
board of appeals shall consist of five members and two alternates appointed by
the mayor in accordance with the city charter and confirmed by the city
council. One member shall be a licensed contractor, one a professional
architect and one a professional engineer.
   (10)   Section 121.2.3. Chairman of board. The board shall select one of its
members to serve as chairman for a period of one year or until their successor
has been selected, and the building official shall designate a clerk from the
department to serve as secretary to the board, who shall keep a detailed record
of all proceedings.
   (11)   Section 121.4.1. Powers and duties of the board. The building board
of appeals shall hear, review, decide and determine the following matters from
building, mechanical, refrigeration, electrical, plumbing, fire, boiler and
property maintenance codes:
      a.   Appeals from a decision of the building official refusing to grant a
modification to the provisions of this code covering the matter of construction
materials to be used in the erection, alteration or repair of a building or
structure.
      b.   All other matters which the board is required to review or act upon
under this code or any other ordinance of the city.
   (12)   Section 121.4.2. Application for appeal. The owner of a building or
structure or any other person may appeal from a decision of the building
official refusing to grant a modification to the provisions of this code
covering the manner of construction or materials to be used in the erection,
alteration or repair of a building or structure to the building board of
appeals. Application for appeal may be made when it is claimed that: the true
intent of this code or the rules legally adopted pursuant to this code have
been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of this code does not fully apply,
or an equally good or better form of construction can be used. An appeal must
be filed within 30 days from the date of the decision appealed from, by filing
with the building official and the board a notice of appeal specifying the
ground thereof, and paying a filing fee.
   (13)   Section 121.6. Decision of board. Three members of the board shall
constitute a quorum, and the board shall affirm, modify or reverse the decision
of the building official by a concurring vote of three members.
   (14)   Section 121.6.1. Resolution of board. Every action of the board shall
be by resolution, and copies shall be furnished to the appellant.
   (15)   Section 121.7. Court review. Any person aggrieved by a decision of
the board may apply to the appropriate court for a review of such decision.
Application for review shall be made to the appropriate court within 20 days
after the filing of the board's decision in the office of the building
official.
   (16)   Section 916.1. Fire hydrants. Change six inches to eight inches.
   (17)   Section 3407.2. Unlawful to move building without permit. It shall be
unlawful to move a building in the city form its foundation to some other
location either within or outside the city, unless from the building official;
provided however, that in case of used houses or structures which were
constructed outside the city, such houses or structures shall not be moved into
the city within the intention of being temporarily or permanently located
therein unless and until a permit to do so is first obtained from the council
of the city.
   (18)   Section 3407.3. Permits to move buildings. Except as otherwise
provided in this code, any building in a good physical condition may be moved
from one location to another after a permit has been obtained from the building
official and after the payment of the prescribed fee therefore had been made.
Such building may be moved upon the public streets when a permit has been
obtained from the building official approving moving such building through any
such public streets, alleys or other public property.
   (19)   Section 3407.4. Approval of application. Before a permit shall be
issued by the department of building and safety for the moving of any building
or structure through or upon any public street, alley or other public property
in the city, the application therefore must be approved by the chief of the
fire department, the chief of the police department, the health officer of the
city and the director of building and safety.
   (20)   Dangerous building prohibited. It is unlawful for any owner or agent
thereof to keep or maintain any dwelling or part thereof that is a dangerous
building as defined in subsection (21).
   (21)   Dangerous buildings defined. As used in subsections (20) to (24),
"dangerous building" means a building or structure that has one or more of the
following defects or is in one or more of the following conditions:
      a.   A door, aisle, passageway, stairway, or other means of exit does not
conform to the approved fire code of the city.
      b.   A portion of the building or structure is damaged by fire, wind,
flood, deterioration, neglect, abandonment, vandalism, or other cause so that
the structural strength or stability of the building or structure is
appreciably less than it was before the damage and does not meet the minimum
requirements of this act or a building code of the city for a new building or
structure, purpose, or location.
      c.   A part of the building or structure is likely to fall, become
detached or dislodged, or collapse and injure persons or damage property.
      d.   A portion of the building or structure has settled to an extent that
walls or other structural portions of the building or structure have materially
less resistance to wind than is required in the case of new construction by
this act or a building code of the city.
      e.   The building or structure, or a part of the building or structure,
because of dilapidation, deterioration, decay, faulty construction, the removal
or movement of some portion of the ground necessary for the support, or for
other reason, is likely to partially or completely collapse, or some portion of
the foundation or underpinning of the building or structure is likely to fall
or give way.
      f.   The building, structure, or a part of the building or structure is
manifestly unsafe for the purpose for which it is used.
      g.   The building or structure is damaged by fire, wind, or flood, is
dilapidated or deteriorated and becomes an attractive nuisance to children who
might play in the building or structure to their danger, or becomes a harbor
for vagrants, criminals, or immoral persons, or enables persons to resort to
the building or structure for committing a nuisance or an unlawful or immoral
act.
      h.   A building or structure used or intended to be used for dwelling
purposes, including the adjoining grounds, because of dilapidation, decay,
damage, faulty construction or arrangement, or for other reason, is unsanitary
or unfit for human habitation, is in a condition that the Building and Safety
Department or health officer determines is likely to cause sickness or disease,
or is likely to injure the health, safety, or general welfare of people living
in the dwelling.
      i.   A building or structure is vacant, dilapidated, and open at door or
window, leaving the interior of the building exposed to the elements or
accessible to entrance by trespassers.
      j.   A building or structure remains unoccupied for a period of 180
consecutive days or longer, and is not listed as being available for sale,
lease, or rent with a real estate broker licensed under article 25 of the
occupational code, 1980 PA 299, MCL 339.2401 to 339.2518. For purposes of this
subdivision, "building or structure" includes, but is not limited to, a
residential, commercial, or industrial buildings or structures. This
subdivision does not apply to either of the following:
         (i)   A building or structure if the owner or agent does both of the
following:
            (A)   Notifies a local law enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction
the building or structure is located that the building or structure will remain
unoccupied for a period of 180 consecutive days. The notice shall be given to
the local law enforcement agency by the owner or agent not more that 30 days
after the building or structure becomes unoccupied.
            (B)   Maintains the exterior of the building or structure and
adjoining grounds in accordance with this act or a building code of the city.
         (ii)   A secondary dwelling of the owner that is regularly unoccupied
for a period of 180 days or longer each year, if the owner notifies a local law
enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the dwelling is located that the
dwelling will remain unoccupied for a period of 180 consecutive days or more
each year. An owner who has given the notice prescribed by this subparagraph
shall notify the law enforcement agency not more that 30 days after the
dwelling no longer qualifies for this exception. As used in this subparagraph,
"secondary dwelling" means a dwelling, including, but not limited to, a
vacation home, hunting cabin, or summer home, that is occupied by the owner or
a member of the owner's family during part of a year.
   (22)   Notice.
      a.   Notwithstanding any other provision of this article, if a building
or structure is found to be a dangerous building, the enforcing agency shall
issue a notice that the building or structure is a dangerous building.
      b.   The notice shall be served on the owner, agent, or lessee that is
registered with the city. If an owner, agent, or lessee is not registered, the
notice shall be serviced on each owner of or party in interest in the building
or structure in whose name the property appears on the last local tax
assessment records and all parties in interest on a title commitment.
      c.   The notice shall specify the time and place of a hearing on whether
the building or structure is a dangerous building. The person to whom the
notice is directed shall have the opportunity to show cause at the hearing why
the hearing officer should not order the building or structure to be
demolished, otherwise made safe, or properly maintained.
      d.   Hearing officer; filing of notice with officer. The hearing officer
shall be appointed by the mayor to serve at their pleasure. The hearing officer
shall be a person who has expertise in housing matters including, but not
limited to, an engineer, architect, building contractor, building inspector, or
member of a community housing organization. An employee of the enforcing agency
shall not be appointed as hearing officer. The enforcing agency shall file a
copy of the notice that the building or structure is a dangerous building with
the hearing officer.
      e.   The notice shall be in writing and shall be served upon the person
to whom the notice is directed either personally or by certified mail, return
receipt requested, addressed to the owner or party in interest at the address
shown on the tax records. If a notice is served on a person by certified mail,
a copy of the notice shall also be posted upon a conspicuous part of the
building or structure. The notice shall be served upon the owner or party in
interest at least 10 days before the date of the hearing included in the
notice.
   (23)   Hearing; testimony; decision.
      a.   At a hearing prescribed by subsection (22), the hearing officer
shall take testimony of the enforcing agency, the owner of the property and any
interested party. Not more than five days after completion of the hearing, the
hearing officer shall render a decision either closing the proceedings or
ordering the building or structure demolished, otherwise made safe, or properly
maintained.
      b.   If the hearing officer determines that the building or structure
should be demolished, otherwise made safe, or properly maintained, the hearing
officer shall enter an order that specifies what action the owner, agent, or
lessee shall take and sets a date by which the owner, agent, or lessee shall
comply with the order. If the building is a dangerous building under subsection
(22), the order may require the owner or agent to maintain the exterior of the
building and adjoining grounds owned by the owner of the building including,
but not limited to, the maintenance of lawns, trees, and shrubs.
      c.   If the owner, agent, or lessee fails to appear or neglects or
refuses to comply with the order issued under subsection b. herein, the hearing
officer shall file a report of the findings and a copy of the order with the
city council not more than five days after the date for compliance set in the
order and request that necessary action be taken to enforce the order. If the
city council has established a demolition board of appeals under subsection
(26), the hearing officer shall file the report of the findings and a copy of
the order with the board of appeals and request that necessary action be taken
to enforce the order. A copy of the findings and order of the hearing officer
shall be served on the owner, agent, or lessee in the manner prescribed in
subsection (22).
      d.   The city council or the demolition board of appeals of the city, as
applicable, shall set a date not less than 30 days after the hearing prescribed
in subsection (21) for a hearing on the findings and order of the hearing
officer. The city council or the board of appeals shall give notice to the
owner, agent, or lessee in the manner prescribed in subsection (22) of the time
and place of the hearing. At the hearing, the owner, agent, or lessee shall be
given the opportunity to show cause why the order should not be enforced. The
city council or the demolition board of appeals of the city shall either
approve, disapprove, or modify the order. If the city council or the demolition
board of appeals approves or modifies the order, the city shall take all
necessary action to enforce the order. If the order is approved or modified,
the owner, agent, or lessee shall comply with the order within 60 days after
the date of the hearing under this subsection. For an order of demolition, if
the city council or the demolition board of appeals of the city determines that
the building or structure has been substantially destroyed by fire, wind,
flood, deterioration, neglect, abandonment, vandalism, or other cause, and the
cost of repair of the building or structure will be greater than the state
equalized value of the building or structure, the owner, agent, or lessee shall
comply with the order of demolition within 21 days after the date of the
hearing under this subsection. If the estimated cost of repair exceeds the
state equalized value of the building or structure to be repaired, a rebuttable
presumption that the building or structure requires immediate demolition
exists.
      e.   The cost of demolition includes, but is not limited to, fees paid to
hearing officers, costs of title searches or commitments used to determine the
parties in interest, recording fees for notices and liens filed with the county
register of deeds, demolition and dumping charges, court reporter attendance
fees, and costs of the collection of the charges authorized under this act. The
cost of demolition, of making the building safe, or of maintaining the exterior
of the building or structure or grounds adjoining the building or structure
incurred by the city to bring the property into conformance with this act shall
be reimbursed to the city by the owner or party in interest in whose name the
property appears.
      f.   The owner or party in interest in whose name the property appears
upon the last local tax assessment records shall be notified by the assessor of
the amount of the cost of the demolition, of making the building safe, or of
maintaining the exterior of the building or structure or grounds adjoining the
building or structure by first class mail at the address shown on the records.
If the owner or party in interest fails to pay the cost within 30 days after
mailing by the assessor of the notice of the amount of the cost, the city shall
have a lien for the cost incurred by the city to bring the property into
conformance with this act. The lien shall not take effect until notice of the
lien has been filed or recorded as provided by law. A lien provided for in this
subsection does not have priority over previously filed or recorded liens and
encumbrances. The lien for the cost shall be collected and treated in the same
manner as provided for property tax liens under the general property tax act,
1893 PA 206, MCL 211.1 to 211.157.
      g.   In addition to other remedies under this act, the city may bring an
action against the owner of the building or structure for the full cost of the
demolition, of making the building safe, or of maintaining the exterior of the
building or structure or grounds adjoining the building or structure. The city
shall have a lien on the property for the amount of the judgment obtained under
this subsection. The lien provided for in this subsection shall not take effect
until notice of the lien is filed or recorded as provided by law. The lien does
not have priority over prior filed or recorded liens and encumbrances.
   (24)   Enforcement of judgment against other assets; lien; effectiveness;
priority.
      a.   A judgment in an action brought pursuant to subsection (23)g. may be
enforced against assets of the owner other than the building or structure.
      b.   The city shall have a lien for the amount of a judgment obtained
pursuant to subsection (23)g. against the owner's interest in all real property
located in this state that is owned in whole or in part by the owner of the
building or structure against whom the judgment is obtained. A lien provided
for in this section does not take effect until notice of the lien is filed or
recorded as provided by law, and the lien does not have priority over prior
filed or recorded liens and encumbrances.
   (25)   Noncompliance with order as misdemeanor; penalties. A person who
fails or refuses to comply with an order approved or modified by the city
council or demolition board of appeals under subsection (23) within the time
prescribed by that section is guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by
imprisonment for not more than 120 days, or a fine of not more than $1,000.00,
or both.
   (26)   Board of apeals.
      a.   The city council hereby establishes and creates a demolition board
of appeals to hear all the cases and carry out all of the duties of the city
council described in subsection (23).
      b.   The board of appeals shall be appointed by the mayor and approved by
the city council and shall consist of the following members:
         (i)   A building contractor.
         (ii)   A registered architect or engineer.
         (iii)   A member of the general public.
         (iv)   A member of the City Council or its designee.
         (v)   An individual registered as a building official, plan reviewer,
or inspector under the building officials and inspectors registration act, Act
No. 54 of the Public Acts of 1986, being sections 338.2301 to 338.2313 of the
Michigan Compiled Laws. The individual may be an employee of the enforcing
agency.
      c.   Board of appeals members shall be appointed for three years, except
that of the members first appointed, two members shall serve for one year, two
members shall serve for two years, and one member shall serve for three years.
A vacancy created other than by expiration of a term shall be filled for the
balance of the unexpired term in the same manner as the original appointment. A
member may be reappointed for additional terms.
      d.   The board of appeals annually shall elect a chairperson, vice-
chairperson, and other officers that the board considers necessary.
      e.   A majority of the board of appeals members appointed and serving
constitutes a quorum. Final action of the board of appeals shall be only by
affirmative vote of a majority of the board members appointed and serving.
      f.   The city council shall fix the amount of any per diem compensation
provided to the members of the board of appeals.
   (27)   Appeals. An owner aggrieved by a final decision or order of the city
council or the demolition board of appeals under subsection (23) may appeal the
decision or order to the circuit court by filing a petition for an order of
superintending control within 20 days from the date of the decision.
(Ord. No. 86-369, § 3, 10-7-86; Ord. No. 94-619, 1-3-95; Ord. No. 98-740, 10-6-
98; Ord. No. 02-878, 2-5-02; Ord. No. 03-928, 4-1-03; Ord. No. 04-999, 3-16-04;
Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-28. - Posted property; unlawful to remove posting.
   It shall be unlawful to remove, alter, deface and/or destroy any notice
posted on property under authority of the City Code of Ordinances, including
but not limited to "Unlawful to Occupy," "Illegal Occupancy," "Unfit for Human
Habitation," "Dangerous and Unsafe" and "Stop Work," unless directed by the
director of the department of building and safety or their designee.
A violation of this section shall be misdemeanor offense.
(Ord. No. 06-1071, 5-15-06; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-29. - Nonresidential building inspection and occupancy requirements.
   (a)   Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following definitions
shall apply:
      (1)   "Building with independent units" shall mean a building with one or
more spaces occupied or designed to be occupied independently of the other
units, and which are independently serviced by utilities, regardless of whether
each unit is identified by a separate street address or by a suite number.
      (2)   "Multipurpose common building" shall mean a building with a common
address and suites that are serviced by common utilities.
   (b)   Certificate of occupancy required. It shall be unlawful for any
person, firm or corporation to occupy or reoccupy, or for any owner or agent
thereof, to permit the occupation or reoccupation of any building or part
thereof, for any nonresidential purpose until a certificate of occupancy has
been issued by the economic and community development department.
   (c)   Certificate of occupancy required for sale or transfer. It shall be
unlawful for anyone, including, but not limited to, the owner, attorney,
representative lending institution, title company, real estate firm, broker, or
salesman to assist in consummating a sale, transfer, lease, or other
transaction involving nonresidential real property in the city regardless of
where the closing of the sale or lease occurs, without first presenting the
purchaser or tenant with a copy of the inspection report or certificate of
occupancy issued by the economic and community development department within
six months prior to the date of such sale, lease, or transfer.
      (1)   Ownership change: application for name change in lieu of inspection
when no change in use or tenant. When the ownership information contained on a
nonresidential certificate of occupancy changes as a result of the sale of a
building, transfer between corporate entities, or any other event, and the
ownership change does not result in a change in the occupancy, use, or tenancy
of the building, the requirement of an inspection for sale may be waived
provided that the new owner files an application with the economic and
community development department for an owner name change, and submits the fee
for a name change according to the schedule provided in chapter 9 of this Code.
The owner of a building with independent units shall apply for a name change
for the certificates of occupancy of each unit within the building. The owner
of a multipurpose common building shall obtain a name change on the certificate
of occupancy for the building as a whole. A certificate of occupancy name
change will not alter the schedule for interval inspections provided for in
this Code.
         a.   Any building for which outstanding code violations exist, and/or
which do not have a final certificate of occupancy for the building or any part
thereof, and/or which have only a temporary certificate of occupancy for any
building or part thereof shall not be eligible for a name change in lieu of
inspection until all outstanding violations are corrected. If outstanding
violations remain upon the closing of the sale, transfer, or lease of the
building, the new owner or lessee shall correct those violations before a
certificate of occupancy is issued, and a full certificate of occupancy
inspection will also be required.
         b.   An owner who fails to apply for a name change and submit the
required fee, or who voluntarily requests a certificate of occupancy inspection
for sale shall be deemed to have waived the option to submit an application for
name change in lieu of inspection, and shall be required to correct all
violations identified in the inspection report as a condition of obtaining a
final certificate of occupancy for the building and its units.
      (2)   Period of validity. A final nonresidential certificate of occupancy
shall remain in effect for the life of the building or structure, or part
thereof, as long as the specific operation conducted within the building or
structure or use of the land continues, except that the certificate of
occupancy of a building or structure, or part thereof, that is found to have
code violations during an interval inspection shall be deemed a temporary
certificate of occupancy that shall expire 90 days after the date of the
inspection report unless the building official determines that all violations
identified on the inspection report have been corrected, or an extension of
time for compliance with the inspection report has been granted by the building
official.
   (d)   Interval inspections. The building official shall cause to be
inspected from time to time, and as nearly as possible once a year, as
determined by a schedule established by the economic and community development
director or his or her designee, all nonresidential buildings and facilities in
the city to ensure that they are being maintained to comply with minimum
health, safety, and public welfare requirements. Fees for interval inspections
shall be assessed as provided in chapter 9 of this Code. When an interval
inspection results in a finding that code violations exist, the building
official shall cause an inspection report to be issued that identifies each
violation, and the owner shall ensure that all violations are corrected within
90 days of the date of the inspection report.
   (e)   Construction. The provisions of this section shall be construed, if
possible, in such manner as to make such provisions consistent with all other
ordinances of the city, including all future ordinances of the city, and all
amendments thereto; provided, however, that where any inconsistency or conflict
cannot be avoided, then the most restrictive of such inconsistent or
conflicting provision shall control and prevail.
(Ord. No. 11-1340, 12-12-11)
Sec. 5-30. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 15-1454, adopted January 27, 2015, repealed §
5-30, which pertained to building permits; expiration; extension and derived
from Ord. No. 14-1434, adopted September 9, 2014.
Secs. 5-31—5-70. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - STREET ADDRESS NUMBERS ***
Sec. 5-71. - Required.
   It shall be unlawful for any owner, or agent in charge of premises, not to
post or not to have posted in a conspicuous place on the front of any principal
building located on or along any street in the city, or to fail, neglect or
refuse to repair or to replace the number of the street address assigned
thereto by the city engineer. This article is needed in the interest of public
safety for the quick identification of any premises by the police and/or fire
departments, as well by other departments in the city and in serving the public
convenience.
(Ord. No. 81-90, §§ 1, 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-72. - Specifications.
   (a)   The size of numbers on residential buildings shall be at least three
inches in height and shall be posted on, at or near the front door, readily
visible to passersby.
   (b)   The size of numbers on commercial buildings shall be at least four
inches in height, shall be posted on, at, or near the front door, and shall be
displayed in such a manner as to be readily visible to occupants of vehicles
immediately in front of such buildings during all hours of normal daylight.
   (c)   The color of the numbers shall be in contrast with the immediate
background on which they are mounted.
   (d)   This section shall be so construed to mean that if the numbers are
hidden by an awning or other appurtenance, the owner of such building, or agent
in charge thereof, shall provide supplementary numbers in such a manner as to
comply with this article.
(Ord. No. 81-90, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-73. - Enforcement.
   The director of building and safety, the fire chief and the police chief are
hereby charged with the responsibility of enforcing the provisions of this
article, and if any such principal building along any street does not have a
street address number posted thereon in accordance with the requirements of
this article, the director of building and safety is hereby authorized and
directed to notify in writing by registered mail the owner of such premises, as
indicated by the current records in the city assessor's office, which notice
will give such owner ten days within which to post and install a suitable
number indicating the street address of the premises in question. On the
failure of such owner to comply with such notice within the time specified, the
director of building and safety is hereby authorized to obtain and procure a
number representing such street address made of suitable material and post such
number on the exterior of the premises near the front door thereof in a
conspicuous place, and any and all expense incurred by the city, including
labor and materials, in posting such number shall be charged to the owner of
the premises, and if not paid at the end of the calendar year after an invoice
therefor has been sent, the amount of such expense shall be added to the
consolidated miscellaneous assessment roll for that year and shall remain a
lien against such premises until full payment therefor has been made; provided,
however, that the minimum charge for obtaining and posting such number shall
not be less than $5.00 for each street address number posted.
(Ord. No. 81-90, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Secs. 5-74—5-90. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III.5. - STORAGE, USE, MANUFACTURE, SALE, HANDLING AND
TRANSPORTATION OF EXPLOSIVES ***
Sec. 5-91. - Definitions.
   The terms:
   Blaster shall mean any person who has been duly licensed by the department
of building and safety to use, handle or transport explosives in the city.
   Explosives or detonators wherever used in this article shall mean and
include any chemical compound or mechanical mixture that contains any oxidizing
and combustible units, or other ingredients in such proportions, quantities or
packing that may be ignited by fire, friction, concussion, percussion or
detonation of any part of the compound or mixture which may cause an explosion
of such violence as is capable of producing harmful effects to life or
property.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-92. - Permit required.
   No person, firm or corporation shall bring within the limits of the city or
have in their possession any explosives, caps or other detonators (except in
the form of the official United States Pharmacopeia solution), until a permit
has been secured from the department of building and safety.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-93. - Exceptions.
   Nothing in this article shall be held to mean and include any small arms,
ammunition or device or compositions used to obtain visible or audible
pyrotechnic effects which are covered by special ordinance, nor shall this
article be applicable to persons, firms or corporations governed and regulated
by council resolutions passed pursuant to section 12 of Ordinance No. 32 or
section 1.8 of Ordinance No. 60-1354.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-94. - Transportation restrictions.
   No person shall carry or transport any explosives within the corporate
limits of the city upon his person or in or upon any conveyance which is
carrying passengers, except co-employees, without a permit as provided herein.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-95. - Fees for permits; exception.
   No person, firm or corporation shall handle, use, store, transport or sell
any explosives within the corporate limits of the city, except as provided in
section
5-105, until a permit has been obtained for such using, handling,
transportation or selling.
   Fees for the issuance of permits, evaluation of applicants for permits and
for inspections required under the provisions of this article shall be
collected by the building and safety department are established as follows:
   Explosives permit ..... $60.00
   Plan review fee for explosives permit ..... 60.00
   Provided, however, that where such explosives are to be used by any person,
firm or corporation under contract with the City of Dearborn, the City of
Detroit, the Board of Wayne County Road Commissioners or the Michigan State
Highway Commissioner, then such person, firm or corporation shall be exempt
from the payment of fees for permits required for specific blasting operations
for use of explosives, but shall be required to obtain such permits.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 5, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06)
Sec. 5-96. - Application for permits.
   Permits for the use, storage, transportation or sale of explosives shall be
obtained from the department of building and safety. Before such permit shall
be issued, an application shall be made in writing, giving the name and address
of the applicant, the location where explosives are to be used, the kind of
explosive to be handled, the time required to complete the blasting and the
name of person or persons licensed to handle high explosives. Upon the receipt
of such application, the fire department shall investigate the conditions as
set forth in this article and if found satisfactory, shall issue an approval,
upon receipt of which the building and safety department shall issue a permit
as petitioned for in the application. Permits shall not be issued for the use,
storage, handling, transportation or sale of explosives to any person in time
of riot without the approval of the director of the department of building and
safety, the fire chief and/or the police chief. Permits shall not be issued for
the use, storage, handling, transportation or sale of explosives in time of war
until the applicant has complied with all federal and local requirements.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 6, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-
25-22)
Sec. 5-97. - Storage.
   (a)   No permanent storage of explosives shall be allowed within the
corporate limits of the city. For temporary storage of explosives, a magazine
shall be provided in accordance with the current fire code. On the outside of
each magazine, there shall at all times be kept conspicuously posted a red sign
or signs with the words "Magazine-Explosives" legibly printed thereon in
letters not less than four inches high.
   (b)   Magazines shall be located at the maximum distance from inhabited or
occupied buildings, public highways and passenger-carrying railways on the
property where they are placed.
   (c)   Detonators, blasting caps, electric or otherwise, shall not be stored
in nor in dangerous proximity to a magazine with other explosives. They shall
be kept in closed containers and shall not be transported in the same vehicle
with other explosives.
   (d)   Ample covers such as mats, pads or equivalent protection shall be used
in blasting operations where persons or property may be endangered.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 7, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06)
Sec. 5-98. - Miscellaneous.
   (a)   A special permit may be granted by the building and safety department,
if approved by the fire department, where it is necessary to carry on a
particular blasting operation, but such permit shall not be granted for a
longer period than 30 days without renewal.
   (b)   Amounts stored in magazines shall be limited to one day's supply and
shall in no case exceed 150 pounds in each magazine.
   (c)   Mining or quarrying companies carrying on continuous blasting
operations underground may carry longer quantities when stored in a manner
satisfactory to the fire department.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-99. - Strict compliance.
   All explosives within the limits of the city shall be stored, used, handled
and transported in strict compliance with the requirements of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-100. - Vehicle regulations.
   (a)   Every vehicle, while carrying explosives, shall have on the rear in
easily legible letters, at least six inches high, "EXPLOSIVES - DANGEROUS,"
printed or painted in white on a red background.
   (b)   It is prohibited for any person in charge of a vehicle containing such
explosives to smoke in or upon such vehicle, drive the vehicle while
intoxicated, to conduct himself in a careless or reckless manner, or to load or
unload such vehicle in a careless manner or while smoking.
   (c)   It is prohibited for any person to place or carry in the bed or body
or cause same to be placed in the bed or body of any vehicle containing
explosives, any metal tool or pieces of metal.
   (d)   It is prohibited for any person to place or carry or cause to be
placed or carried in the bed or body of any vehicle containing explosives, any
exploders, detonators, blasting caps or other similar explosive material or to
carry in or upon any such vehicle any matches.
   (e)   The vehicle transporting explosives shall traverse such streets as are
subject to traffic regulations and which are commonly termed "through" or
"stop" streets, whenever possible, and shall use the least traveled streets of
this type consistent with the expeditious movement of the explosives to
destination. All vehicles carrying explosives shall be provided with an
approved fire extinguisher.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-101. - Magazines.
   (a)   No artificial light shall be used in magazine except portable electric
safety battery lamps.
   (b)   All magazines must be kept locked except when being inspected or when
explosives are being placed therein or being removed therefrom.
   (c)   No matches or fire shall at any time be permitted near a magazine.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-102. - Blaster.
   All applicants for a blaster's permit to use, handle or transport explosives
in the city shall first comply with the following requirements:
      (1)   Shall be at least 21 years of age and a citizen of the United
States.
      (2)   Shall have a reasonable understanding of the English language and
be able to answer satisfactorily such questions as may be asked him upon his
evaluation.
      (3)   Produce such evidence of his character, habits and past employment
as may be satisfactory to the fire department, for which purpose the fire
department may require him to appear for examination before the proper
officials of the police department.
      (4)   In addition to the foregoing requirements, an applicant, must
present satisfactory evidence of experience in handling high explosives, either
as a blaster or blaster's helper, for a period of not less than two years, and
that he is properly qualified to perform the duties as a blaster. A blaster
shall confine his activities to those designated on his permit.
      (5)   Each application for such permit shall be accompanied by three
unmounted photographs of the applicant, one and one-half inches by one and one-
half inches, taken in ordinary working clothes, one of which shall be attached
to the application and the other to the permit when issued. The permit shall be
carried by the blaster at all times during blasting operations.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 12, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06)
Sec. 5-103. - Contractor.
   Before an explosive permit may be issued, the applicant must first register
with the office of the city clerk. The contractor’s registration fee, listed in
Chapter 12, Section 6, must be paid prior to the issuance of a permit.
Contractors are required to meet insurance and other requirements, as noted on
the contractor registration application form.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 13, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06; Ord. No. 22-1724,
2-8-22)
Sec. 5-104. - Revoking of permits.
   The building and safety department, the fire department and/or the police
department shall have the authority and it shall be their duty to revoke any
permit to store, use, handle or transport explosives when they shall ascertain
by reasonable proofs that the holder of such permit has been careless or
negligent or incompetent in the use, storage, handling or transportation of
explosives, that he has been smoking or has been intoxicated while working with
or using explosives, that he willfully or through negligence permitted or
allowed explosives to be used or taken away by unauthorized persons, or that he
has used or permitted others to use, any of the explosives in their care for
improper or criminal purposes.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 14, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1112, 12-18-06; Ord. No. 22-1733,
1-25-22)
Sec. 5-105. - Interstate commerce regulations.
   Nothing in this article shall be deemed to conflict with the interstate
commerce regulations for the transportation of explosives or detonators in or
through the city.
(Ord. No. 81-97, § 15, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-106—5-120. - Reserved.
