Sec. 5-121. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Board-on-board fence shall mean any fence with alternating vertical boards
over horizontal structures that give the fence a finished look on both sides.
   Chain-link or cyclone fence shall mean any fence that is constructed of some
type of woven wire fence, with a minimum 11½ gauge in residential districts, a
minimum of 9 gauge in commercial districts, and a minimum 6 gauge in industrial
districts.
   Compliance certificate shall mean an approval issued by the City of Dearborn
pursuant to the provisions of this article.
   Decorative fence shall mean any fence no more than 30 inches high not
intended for the purpose of preventing persons and/or domestic animals, from
crawling or passing through the fence, except at established gateways. A
decorative or ornamental fence shall not include a fence constructed of chain
link material or any other type of woven wire fence.
   Decorative top shall mean an open framework made of strips of material
matching the fence placed in a decorative pattern. Decorative tops may not
exceed one foot in height, must have a solid top rail, and shall not exceed 50
percent coverage of open viewing.
   Delinquent owner shall mean any party who owns a lot or parcel of land,
either as deed holder or contract purchaser, and who refuses or neglects to
build or assist in building or repairing a partition fence or to contribute his
portion of the expense for the building or repairing of a partition fence, in
accordance with the provisions of this article.
   Department shall mean the department or division within the City of Dearborn
where the Building Official is assigned.
   Fence shall mean a structure serving as an enclosure, barrier or boundary
including but not limited to posts, boards, wire, concrete or gates.
   Line fence shall mean any fence erected on the boundary line of any lot or
parcel of land.
   Ornamental fence. See Decorative fence.
   Picket fence shall mean any fence with in-line boards no larger than one
inch × three inches with gaps equal to the width of the boards.
   Privacy fence shall mean a sight-obscuring fence used to block the area
enclosed by the fence from view from neighboring properties or public rights-
of-way.
   Privacy screen shall mean a sight-obscuring fence, erected adjacent to or
around a selected use or area (such as a patio, deck, courtyard or swimming
pool), designed to screen the area behind it from observation by persons
outside its perimeter. Privacy screens shall be of reasonable length as
determined by the building official or his/her designee and not the entire
property line. Privacy screens shall comply with the regulations specified in
section
5-128.
   Semi-privacy fence shall mean a fence designed and intended to be sight-
obscuring, such as a board-on-board fence, or a vinyl fence with vertical slats
with gaps between the slats.
   Shadow-box fence. See Board-on-board fence.
   Solid fence. Any fence which presents a solid surface without any gaps in
materials, such as a stockade fence.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 16-1533, 4-12-16; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-
22)
Sec. 5-122. - Right to build fence at owner's expense.
   (a)   Anything in this article to the contrary notwithstanding, the owner of
any land in the city is hereby authorized and empowered to build and maintain a
line fence at his or her sole expense, if the location of such proposed fence
is established and a compliance certificate therefor is obtained in accordance
with the provisions of this article.
   (b)   The respective owners of lots adjacent to each other in the city may
construct and maintain fences between such adjacent lots at an equal expense
and cost to each owner, subject to the provisions of this article; provided,
however, by mutual consent of adjacent owners such fence may be omitted in
whole or in part. All owners of lots shall be responsible for the building,
repairing, care and upkeep of all fences contiguous to or bordering upon
alleys, all partition lines and property boundaries as herein specified.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-22)
Sec. 5-123. - Compliance certificate required; exceptions.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to build, replace, remove, repair or
relocate a line fence in the city without first having secured a compliance
certificate therefor from the department.
Exceptions:
    (a)   A compliance certificate is not required for minor repairs that do
not exceed ten percent of the length of the fence along any one property line
within any 12-month period, provided that the fence is permitted style and is
being repaired with like material.
   (b)   A compliance certificate is not required for a decorative fence, but
shall comply with the general requirements in section
5-127.
   (c)   A separate compliance certificate is not required if the proposed work
on an approved compliance certificate includes relocating the gate and/or
portion of a fence on the adjoining property.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 16-1533, 4-12-16; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-
22; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-22)
Sec. 5-124. - Application for compliance certificate.
   (a)   An application for a compliance certificate shall be filed with the
building official made on a form prescribed by the department, along with other
documentation as specified on the application form. If a fence is proposed in
conjunction with a development that requires site plan review then the fence
shall be shown on the site plan, which shall be reviewed in accordance with
normal site plan review procedures.
   (b)   Such application shall indicate that it is being made with the joint
approval and consent of the adjacent owners, and it shall be signed by such
owners or their authorized representatives. The application shall further
indicate the names of the respective owners of the adjacent lots or properties
separated by such line fence.
   (c)   In connection with such application and before it is approved, there
shall be submitted for approval an accurate land survey or a site plan,
locating such fence line, as herein referred to, or an agreement in writing,
signed by the adjacent owners, stating that they have mutually agreed upon the
line and that appropriate stakes have been placed establishing such line, as
required by this article.
   (d)   It shall be the duty of the department to issue a compliance
certificate upon the filing of such application properly filled out and the
approval thereof by the director or their designee, and after a compliance
certificate fee has been paid. Compliance certificate fees and other related
fees shall be in accordance with
chapter 9.
   (e)   Every fence compliance certificate issued shall expire 180 days after
date of issuance. Extensions may be granted by applying to the department and
after applicable fees are paid in accordance with Section
9-10.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-
22)
Sec. 5-125. - Application for compliance certificate—When adjacent property
owners do not agree.
   (a)   If the owners of the adjacent properties do not consent to the details
of the construction, replacement, removal, repairs or relocation of a line
fence, in addition to the requirements set forth in section
5-124, the applicant shall show proof that an attempt was made to obtain the
adjacent owner's consent by certified mail with return receipt requested of the
applicant's desire to have such line fence built, replaced, removed, repaired
or relocated in accordance with the provisions of this article. Notice shall be
mailed by the department to adjacent property owners by certified mail and
first-class mail advising them of the request for a compliance certificate and
that same will be issued within 15 days unless adjacent owners can show a valid
reason for withholding the compliance certificate.
   The conditions of an existing fence, the consistency of the fence styles in
a neighborhood and the timeframe in which a building board of appeals decision
was made on an existing fence will be reviewed. If a resolution cannot be
agreed upon, an applicant may apply to the building board of appeals. The
building board of appeals will also take the above factors into consideration
when making their decision.
   (b)   If there is a legitimate dispute between such adjacent owners
regarding the location of a fence, the owner who desires to have the fence
built shall obtain the services of a registered surveyor who shall make a
survey of the partition line in question and shall install such suitable
markers establishing the partition line. If the adjacent owners agree on the
location of the line fence, a registered survey shall not be required.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-
22)
Sec. 5-126. - Right of reimbursement for condemned fence.
   If the director of the department or their designee orders any owner to
build, replace, remove, repair or relocate the whole or any part of a line
fence, it is the responsibility of all property owners adjacent to the fence to
pay for all expenses incurred to comply with the order.
   If necessary, the director of the department or their designee shall
determine the reasonable cost of building, replacing or repairing such fence,
along with the cost of survey, application and permit fee. A prorated amount
shall be charged to the responsible property owners.
   If a property owner is delinquent in paying their share of expenses incurred
to the appropriate party(ies), then the city may pay the responsible party(ies)
for expenses incurred and charge appropriately for reimbursement.
   If the costs and charges due the city are not collected on or before
December 31 of the year in which the expenses were incurred by the city, the
same shall be reported by the finance director to the city council to be
collected by a special assessment, in accordance with the provisions of
chapter 15 of the Charter of the city.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-
22)
Sec. 5-127. - General requirements.
   (1)   Permitted fence styles. Permitted fence styles include, but are not
limited to, board-on-board, shadow-box, privacy, semi-privacy, solid fences,
chain link, cyclone, picket, and wrought iron, provided that all other
requirements of this article are met. Board-on-board, shadow-box, privacy
screens, privacy, and semi-privacy fence styles may include a one-foot-high
decorative top.
   (2)   Prohibited fencing.
      (a)   Prohibited fence styles include, but are not limited to, masonry
fences and vinyl slats inserted in chain-link or cyclone fences.
      (b)   Animal enclosures such as dog runs, kennels or pens are prohibited.
      (c)   Decorative fences are prohibited on side and rear property lines.
   (3)   Materials.
      (a)   All fences built or repaired shall have posts made of either iron
pipe one and five-eighths inches outside diameter, wood posts four inches in
diameter, reinforced concrete posts four inches across, or any other material
of equal stability sunk in the soil at least three feet encased in concrete. On
the posts shall be properly fastened materials commonly used in conventional
fence construction, such as wood, metal, vinyl or vinyl clad wood.
      (b)   Fences which carry electric current, razor wire are prohibited.
      (c)   Barbed wire may be used at the top of fences for security purposes
around storage areas located in the Industrial B (Medium Industrial District),
Industrial C (Intensive Industrial District), and Industrial D (General
Industrial District) zoning districts.
         1.   Barbed wire is prohibited in the Industrial A (Light Industrial
District).
         2.   Location requirements. Barbed wire shall not be permitted on
fences in the front yard or along frontages on streets defined as arterial or
collector roads.
         3.   Design regulations.
            a.   No strand of barbed wire shall be permitted less than eight
feet above ground.
            b.   The barbed wire strands shall be installed on supports that
slant inward toward the interior of the site.
      (d)   No owner or lessee, or their respective agents, of any building in
the city shall erect or cause to be erected or maintained on or about the
stairway to the entrance of such building, or on or about its exterior building
line, or upon fences or upon any portion of the sidewalk adjacent to such
building, any railing, fence guard or other projection on which there shall be
affixed or placed, in any manner attached, any spike, nail or other sharp
pointed instrument of any kind or description. No wire or other fence materials
shall be affixed to the fence with the top edge having any sharp or pointed
projections of any kind; provided, however, if such fence is constructed of
pickets, such pickets shall have an angle at the top of not less than 90
degrees.
   (4)   Finished appearance.
      (a)   The finished appearance of a fence shall face the exterior of the
lot. If, because of the design or construction, one side of the fence has a
more finished appearance than the other, the side of the fence with the more
finished appearance shall face the exterior of the lot.
      (b)   All finished styles shall be approved by the building official or
his/her designee.
   (5)   Location of posts.
      (a)   Line fences shall be constructed on common property lines.
      (b)   On all streets running generally east and west, the posts shall be
placed contiguous to and on the westerly side of the dividing line, and the
boards, woven wire or other material on the easterly side of the posts; and on
all street running generally north and south, the posts shall be placed on the
northerly side of the dividing line and the boards, woven wire, or other
material on the southerly side of the posts; provided, however, if the owners
of adjacent lots mutually agree in writing, the posts can be placed on either
side of the partition line. The lot owner upon whose property the posts are
located shall be responsible for building, relocating, replacing, removing or
repairing the front half of the fence and the rear half of the opposite fence.
The junction of the posts and boards, or the posts and wire fence or other
materials, shall always be considered the lot line.
      (c)   In the case of line fences along the rear lot lines, the owner on
whose property the posts are located shall be responsible for building,
relocating, replacing, removing or repairing that half of the fence leading to
the higher house numbers, while the adjacent owner shall be responsible for
building, relocating, replacing, removing or repairing the other half of such
partition fence.
   (6)   Location of fences.
      (a)   Fences shall provide for unobstructed sight area standards which
include:
         1.   Not obstructing the area formed at the corner intersection of two
(2) public right-of-way lines, the two (2) sides of the triangular area being
twenty-five (25) feet in length measured along abutting public rights-of-way
lines, and third side being a line connecting these two (2) sides.
         2.   Not obstructing the area formed at the corner intersection of a
public right-of-way and a driveway, the two (2) sides of the triangular area
being ten (10) feet in length measured along the right-of-way line and edge of
the driveway, and the third side being a line connecting these two (2) sides.
         3.   Not obstructing cross-visibility between a height of thirty (30)
inches and six (6) feet above the lowest point of the intersecting road(s).
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-7003.png]
 
      (b)   Unless otherwise determined unavoidable by the building official,
no fence shall be erected where it would prevent or unreasonably obstruct the
use of the applicant's property or adjacent property, nor shall a fence be
erected where it would obstruct or prevent the continued safe use of an
existing driveway or other means of access to the applicant's property or
adjacent property. In enforcing this provision, the building official may
require a fence to be set back in a minimum distance from a driveway or
property line.
      (c)   Fences that are a part of an approved site plan by the Planning
Commission may deviate from the location standards in this ordinance as long as
they meet unobstructed sight area standards and do not generate public safety
concerns.
   (7)   Fence maintenance.
      (a)   Fences shall be maintained in good condition. Rotten or broken
components shall be replaced, repaired, or removed. As required, surfaces shall
be painted, stained, or similarly treated. If a fence is found to be in need of
repair by the building official or his/her designee, he or she may issue orders
to complete such repairs. Failure to comply with a written notice from the
building official or his/her designee shall be deemed a violation of this
ordinance. All owners of lots upon which a fence is erected shall hereafter be
responsible for the care and maintenance of the fence.
      (b)   Any person building, repairing, replacing or completing any fence
or a part of a fence for a delinquent owner may enter upon the premises of such
delinquent owner to the extent reasonably necessary to build, repair, replace
or complete such fence.
      (8)   This section shall not apply to property owned by the city.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 16-1533, 4-12-16; Ord. No. 16-1558, - -
16; Ord. No. 1752, 6-15-22)
Sec. 5-128. - Fence regulations in residential districts.
   (1)   Location and height.
      (a)   Line fences in residential districts shall not exceed six feet in
height.
      (b)   Permitted one-foot-high decorative tops on new fences are allowed
provided that the height of the fence does not exceed six feet.
      (c)   No fence shall be permitted to extend into one's own front yard. No
fence shall be located beyond the rear yard or project into the side yard
farther than three feet from the side grade door opening to enclose the door in
a side yard.
      Exemptions:
         1.   Decorative fences;
         2.   Houses located on corner lots may extend to the established front
building line provided that the adjacent yard is not a front yard.
      (d)   Fences shall be permitted on the side street lot line on corner
lots between the established building line and the front lot line. Such fences
shall taper from four feet in height at the building line to two feet at the
front lot line or such fences may have a uniform height of two feet.
      (e)   Fences located on a corner lot with no residential housing on the
relevant side street may be located on the property line or no closer than one
foot to the edge of the sidewalk.
      (f)   Only one fence may be constructed on any common or adjoining
property line.
      (g)   Where no house is built on a residence-zoned lot, a line fence or a
fence across the lot shall not be built closer to the street than the
established front building line along such street.
      (h)   Where a house has a side yard that is at least 16 ft. in width, but
does not have a side door opening, a line fence or a fence across the lot shall
not be built closer to the street than 10 ft. behind the building line along
such street in order to enclose the side yard.
   (2)   Privacy screens. Privacy screens may be placed on the interior of the
lot in the rear yard, subject to the following:
      (a)   A minimum clearance of six feet shall be provided between the
proposed privacy screen and along any other fence, structure, or property line.
      (b)   Privacy screens shall not exceed six feet in height.
      (c)   Privacy screens shall be constructed of the materials cited
previously in this article, subject to review and approval by the building
official.
      (d)   Privacy screens shall be freestanding and self-supporting.
      (e)   Only one privacy screen may be constructed along any common or
adjoining property line.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 16-1533, 4-12-16; Ord. No. 20-1693, 12-8-
20; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-22)
Sec. 5-129. - Fence regulations in nonresidential districts.
   (1)   Process. All nonresidential fences are subject to administrative site
plan review in accordance with the standards for site plan approval outlined in
Section
32.02 E of the City's Zoning Ordinance.
   (2)   Location.
      (a)   Fences shall be permitted in the rear or side yards of
nonresidential districts and may only extend up to the front building line.
      (b)   Fences located on a corner lot may be located on the property line
no closer than one (1) foot to the edge of the sidewalk.
   (3)   Height. Fences in commercial districts shall not exceed six feet in
height. Fences in industrial districts shall not exceed eight feet in height.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-22)
Sec. 5-130. - Referral to building board of appeals.
   When special conditions exist, the director may refer such conditions to the
building board of appeals, or the parties themselves may appeal to the building
board of appeals to determine what is fair and reasonable and to adjust any and
all differences and disputes which may exist between the department and the
parties involved, or between adjacent owners, in order that justice may be done
and an equitable solution of the problem achieved.
(Ord. No. 08-1192, 12-15-08; Ord. No. 22-1752, 6-15-22)
Secs. 5-131—5-160. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE V. - EARTH CHANGING ACTIVITIES ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Secs. 5-161—5-185. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - SOIL EROSION CONTROL **
Sec. 5-186. - Enabling authority; designation of a municipal enforcing agency
and official; and adoption of statute and rules by reference.
   (a)   This division is adopted under the authority of part 91, SESC, of the
Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, 1994 PA 451, as amended
(hereinafter "part 91").
   (b)   The department of economic and community development is the municipal
enforcing agency responsible for administering and enforcing this division and
part 91 within the municipal limits of the city.
   (c)   The city building official or his duly authorized representative shall
be the municipal enforcing official responsible for administering and enforcing
this Division and Part 91 within the municipal limits of the city.
   (d)   Part 91 and the rules promulgated under part 91 ("rules") are
incorporated by reference into this division.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-187. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Accelerated soil erosion shall mean the increased loss of the land surface
that occurs as a result of man's activities.
   Building official means the director of the department of economic and
community development or his duly authorized representative who has
successfully completed the training requirements for administering part 91.
   Earth change shall mean a manmade change in the natural cover or topography
of land, including cut and fill activities which may result in or contribute to
soil erosion or sedimentation of the waters of the state.
   Erosion shall mean the process by which the ground surface is worn away by
action of wind, water, gravity or a combination thereof.
   Excavation or cut shall mean any act by which soil or rock is cut into, dug,
quarried, uncovered, removed, displaced or relocated and shall include the
conditions resulting therefrom.
   Floodplain shall mean that area which would be inundated by storm runoff or
flood water equivalent or that which would occur with a rainfall or flood for
an intermediate regional flood.
   Grading shall mean any stripping, excavating, filling, stockpiling or any
combination thereof, and shall include the land in its excavated or filled
condition.
   Permanent soil erosion and sedimentation control measure shall mean those
control measures which are installed or constructed to control soil erosion and
sedimentation and which are maintained after project completion.
   SESC permit shall mean a permit issued to authorize work to be performed
under this division.
   Stripping shall mean any activity which removes or significantly disturbs
the vegetative surface cover, including clearing and grubbing operations.
   Temporary soil erosion and sedimentation control measures shall mean interim
and control measures which are installed or constructed for the control of soil
erosion and sedimentation until permanent soil control is effected.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-188. - Permits required; submission of plans.
   Prior to undertaking an earth change in the city involving one or more acres
of land, or within 500 feet of the water's edge of a lake or stream, an erosion
and sedimentation control permit shall be obtained from the building official.
Request for a permit shall be initiated by submitting an application and SESC
plan in accordance with rule 1703 promulgated under part 91.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-189. - Top soil removal.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, whether, owner, lessee, licensee or
trespasser, to scrape off, dig out or remove the top soil from any land, lot or
plot of ground in the city for the purpose of selling or appropriating to his
own purpose such top soil; provided, however, that any builder or contractor,
in connection with any building or construction work, may remove and scrape
back the top soil for the purpose of excavating in the place where the top soil
was formerly located, and if such top soil cannot be used in connection with
landscaping the grounds after such construction work is completed, such top
soil may be disposed of in an approved manner, in accordance with regulations
established by the building official.
(Ord. No. 81-88, § 1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-190. - Compliance required for occupancy.
   No certificate of occupancy for any building will be issued unless the
applicant for such certificate shall have obtained approval from the building
official indicating compliance with all grading plans and specifications and
completion of all permanent soil erosion control measures.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-191. - Permits and fees.
   Upon payment of the necessary fees to the city treasurer, the submitted
plans shall be reviewed and approved and a permit shall be issued, provided the
plans meet the standards and specifications of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 6, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-192. - Bond requirement.
   (a)   An SESC permit shall not be issued unless the permittee shall first
post with the city clerk a bond executed by the owner and a corporate surety
with authority to do business in this state as a surety.
   (b)   The bond shall be in a form approved by the city attorney, payable to
the city, and in the amount of the estimated total cost of all temporary or
permanent soil erosion control measures. The total cost shall be estimated by
the building official. The bond shall include penalty provisions for failure to
complete the work on schedule as specified on the grading permit. In lieu of a
surety bond, the applicant may file with the city a cash bond or an instrument
of credit approved by the city attorney in an amount equal to that which would
be required for the surety bond.
   (c)   Every bond and instrument of credit shall include and every cash
deposit shall be made on the conditions that the permittee shall comply with
all of the provisions of this division and all of the terms and conditions of
the SESC permit, and shall complete all of the work contemplated under the SESC
permit within the time limit specified in the SESC permit, or if no time limit
is specified, within 180 days after the date of the issuance of the SESC
permit.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 7, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-193. - Extension of time.
   If a permitee is unable to complete the work within the specified time, he
may, at least ten days prior to the expiration of the permit, present in
writing to the building official a request for an extension of time, setting
forth the reasons for the requested extension. If such an extension is
warranted, the building official may grant additional time for the completion
of the work, but no such extension shall release the owner, the surety on the
bond or the person furnishing the instrument of credit or cash bond.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 8, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-194. - Failure to complete work.
   In the event of a failure to complete the work or failure to comply with all
the requirements, conditions and terms of the permit, the building official may
order such work as is necessary to eliminate any danger to persons or property
and to leave the site in a safe condition, and he may authorize completion of
all necessary temporary or permanent soil erosion control measures. The
permitee and the surety executing the bond or person issuing the instrument of
credit or making the cash deposit shall continue to be firmly bound under a
continuing obligation for the payment of all necessary costs and expenses that
may be insured or expended by the city in causing any and all such work to be
done. In the case of a cash deposit, any unused portion thereof shall be
refunded to the permitee.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 9, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-195. - Denial of permit.
   SESC permits shall not be issued where:
      (1)   The proposed work would cause hazards to the public safety and
welfare;
      (2)   The work as proposed by the applicant will damage any public or
private property, interfere with any existing drainage course in such a manner
as to cause damage to any adjacent property, result in the deposit of debris or
sediment on any public way or into any waterway, or create an unreasonable
hazard to persons or property;
      (3)   The land area for which grading is proposed is subject to
geological hazard to the extent that no reasonable amount of corrective work
can eliminate or sufficiently reduce settlement, slope instability or any other
such hazard to persons or property; or
      (4)   The land area for which the grading is proposed may lie within the
floodplain of any stream or watercourse, not specifically designated and
delineated by the city as an area subject to flood hazard, unless a hydrologic
report, prepared by a professional engineer, is submitted to certify that the
proposed grading will have, in his opinion, no detrimental influence on the
public welfare or upon the total development of the watershed.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 10, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-196. - Modifications of approved plans.
   All modifications of the approved grading plans must be submitted and
approved by the building official. All necessary reports shall be submitted
with any proposal to modify the approved grading plan. No grading work in
connection with any proposed modification shall be permitted without the
approval of the building official.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 11, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-197. - Responsibility of permittee.
   During grading operations the permittee shall be responsible for:
      (1)   The prevention of damage to any public utilities or services within
the limits of grading and along any routes of travel of the equipment.
      (2)   The prevention of damage to adjacent property. No person shall
grade on land so close to the property line as to endanger any adjoining public
street, sidewalk, alley or any public or private property without supporting
and protecting such property from settling, cracking or other damage which
might result.
      (3)   Carrying out the proposed work in accordance with the approved
plans and in compliance with all the requirements of the permit and this
division.
      (4)   The prompt removal of all soil, miscellaneous debris or other
materials applied, dumped or otherwise deposited on public streets, highways,
sidewalks or other public thoroughfares during transit to and from the
construction, where such spillage constitutes a public nuisance or hazard.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 12, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-198. - General requirements.
   (a)   Any earth changes shall be conducted in such a manner which will
effectively reduce accelerated soil erosion and resulting sedimentation.
   (b)   Any persons engaged in earth changes shall design, implement and
maintain acceptable soil erosion and sedimentation and control measures, in
conformance with this division.
   (c)   All earth changes shall be designed, constructed and completed in such
a manner which shall limit the exposed area of any disturbed land for the
shortest possible period of time.
   (d)   Sediment caused by accelerated soil erosion shall be removed from
runoff water before it leaves the site of the earth change.
   (e)   Any temporary or permanent facility designed and constructed for the
conveyance of water around, through or from the earth change area shall be
designed to limit the water flow to a nonerosive velocity.
   (f)   A person shall install temporary soil erosion and sedimentation
control measures before or upon commencement of the earth change activity and
shall maintain the measures on a daily basis. A person shall remove temporary
soil erosion and sedimentation control measures after permanent soil erosion
measures are in place and the area is stabilized. A person shall stabilize the
area with permanent soil erosion control measures under approved standards and
specifications as prescribed by rule 1710.
   (g)   Permanent soil erosion control measures for all slopes, channels,
ditches or any disturbed land area shall be completed with five calendar days
after final grading or the final earth change has been completed. When it is
not possible to permanently stabilize a disturbed area after an earth change
has been completed or where significant earth change activity ceases, temporary
soil erosion and sedimentation control measures shall be implemented
immediately. All temporary soil erosion control measures shall be maintained
until permanent soil erosion control measures are in place and the area
stabilized (rule 1709(5)).
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 13, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-199. - Maintenance requirements.
   Persons carrying out soil erosion and sediment control measures under this
division, and all subsequent owners of property concerning which such measures
have been taken, shall maintain all permanent antierosion devices, retaining
walls, structures, plantings and other protective devices.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-200. - Minimum design standards for erosion and sediment control.
   All SESC plans and specifications including extensions of previously
approved plans which include provisions for erosion and sediment control in
accordance with, but not limited to, the standards contained in this division.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 15, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-201. - Variances and exceptions.
   No earth-changing activity (SESC) permits shall be required for the
following:
      (1)   Grading or an excavation below finished grade for basements,
footings, retaining walls, or other structures on plots of less than one acre
and more than 500 feet from any lake, stream or drainage course.
      (2)   Although no permits are required under subsection (1), the
operations and constructions exempted from obtaining permits must comply with
the rules and regulations concerning grading and erosion specified in this
division.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 16, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-202. - Inspection.
   (a)   The requirements of this division shall be enforced by the building
official. The building official shall inspect the work and may require adequate
inspection of compaction by a soil engineer or by a soil testing agency,
approved by the building official.
   (b)   If the building official finds any existing conditions not as stated
in any application, SESC permit or approved plan, he may refuse to approve
further work until approval of a revised SESC plan which will conform to the
existing conditions.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 17, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-203. - Enforcement.
   (a)   Notwithstanding the existence or pursuit or any other remedy, the city
may maintain an action in its own name in any court of competent jurisdiction
for an injunction or other process against any person to restrain or prevent
violations of this division.
   (b)   The building official may enter at all reasonable times in or upon any
private or public property for the purpose of inspection and investigating
conditions and practices which may be a violation of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-111, § 18, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Sec. 5-204. - Violations.
   (a)   Performance. It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to perform
any act required by this division or to perform any act prohibited by this
division.
   (b)   Knowledge. It shall be unlawful for any person having a possessory
interest in any land to knowingly permit, acquiesce, assist, aid or encourage
any other person to violate the provisions of this division.
   (c)   Continuance of work. It shall be unlawful for any person to continue
any earth change activity after having been served with a stop-work order until
such order has been rescinded.
(Ord. No. 09-1233, 8-17-09)
Secs. 5-205—5-220. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - DUMPING **
Sec. 5-221. - Business license required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, whether as owner or lessee, to engage
in the business of providing a place or places in the city for hire in which
rubbish, junk, organic material, parts or trimmings of trees, shrubs, bushes,
wire, glass, paper, old iron, metal cans or containers, wood or pieces of
concrete or similar waste material can be dumped or filled in without first
obtaining a license for each location in the city where such activity will be
carried on.
(Ord. No. 81-132, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-222. - Application for license.
   Any person desiring to engage in the business of providing a place for the
dumping of materials for hire, as described in section
5-221, shall apply to the city clerk for a license to carry on such business.
The application shall state the name of the applicant, their residence and
business address, the location where such dumping operations shall be carried
on, the approximate size and cubical capacity of the area to be filled in by
such dumping operations, the legal owner of the land on which the dumping will
take place and the type of materials acceptable for the dumping operation.
After such application is filed and the fee therefor paid to the city
treasurer, the application shall be referred to the building and safety
department, the department of health, the fire department and the police
department for investigation. If the dumping will not violate any of the
ordinances of the city, including the zoning ordinance, and the rules and
regulations promulgated by any city departments, the application will be
approved and, upon the receipt of such approval from the several departments of
the city, the clerk will issue the license in question.
(Ord. No. 81-132, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-223. - Nuisance prohibited.
   In connection with dumping under this division, the applicant shall promise
and agree in the application to fill in the land to such elevation that will
allow at least 36 inches of good soil to be covered thereon, which good soil in
turn will be rough graded to the established elevation. The applicant must
further promise and agree not to fill in or dump any garbage or animal matter
that will tend to create an unfavorable health condition, create a stench,
attract rats or other rodents and to carry on the program so that the whole
dumping operation will not become a nuisance in the city.
(Ord. No. 81-132, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-224. - Bond requirement.
   (a)   A dumping permit shall not be issued unless the permittee shall first
post with the city clerk a bond executed by the owner and a corporate surety
with authority to do business in this state as a surety.
   (b)   The bond shall be in a form approved by the city attorney, payable to
the city, and in the amount of the estimated total cost of all temporary or
permanent soil erosion control measures. The total cost shall be estimated by
the city engineer or building inspector. The bond shall include penalty
provisions for failure to complete the work on schedule as specified on the
dumping permit. In lieu of a surety bond, the applicant may file with the city
a cash bond or an instrument of credit approved by the city attorney in an
amount equal to that which would be required for the surety bond.
   (c)   Every bond and instrument of credit shall include and every cash
deposit shall be made on the conditions that the permittee shall comply with
all of the provisions of this division and all of the terms and conditions of
the dumping permit, and shall complete all of the work contemplated under the
dumping permit within the time limit specified in the dumping permit, or if no
time limit is specified, within 180 days after the date of the issuance of the
dumping permit.
Sec. 5-225. - License fee.
   In connection with every application for license to dump materials as
provided in this division, the applicant shall pay to the city treasurer an
annual license fee of $300.00 for each location. Each annual license shall
expire at 12:00 midnight following December 31 of each year after such license
becomes effective, and may be renewed on similar terms.
(Ord. No. 81-132, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-226. - Suspension and revocation of license.
   (a)   Any license issued under the provisions of this division will be
subject to suspension and revocation for cause upon proof of charges filed with
the city council by the director of building and safety or any authorized
inspectors in the city, specifying with reasonable detail the facts on which
the suspension is based. Among the grounds for suspending or revoking any
license issued under this division are falsification of any material fact in
the application for a license, carelessness or negligence in the performance of
the licensee's duties in connection with their work, or showing that such
licensee has violated or permitted a violation of this division, or that this
division or any other ordinance or statute has been violated in connection with
work for which the licensee was responsible or of which the licensee was aware
or in the exercise of reasonable diligence, should have been aware that such
violation occurred.
   (b)   Upon the filing of such charges, the director of building and safety
department shall forthwith suspend the license involved and shall give to such
licensee notice of a hearing upon such charges, which hearing shall be held by
the city council not less than two weeks after the date of such notice unless
an earlier date is agreed upon in writing by the licensee affected. Such notice
shall be by personal service or certified mail and shall state the time and
place of such hearing and shall contain a copy of the charges. If such charges
are sustained by the city council, the director shall immediately revoke the
license involved or the council may modify or alter the suspension of the
license or reinstate it and shall notify the licensee in writing of such
finding.
(Ord. No. 81-132, § 5, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Secs. 5-227—5-240. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VI. - BUILDING CONTRACTORS AND SUBCONTRACTORS ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-241. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Registered design professional shall mean any registered design professional
licensed under article 20, 1980 PA 299, MCL 339.2001 et seq., R 408.30513.
   Residential, commercial and industrial building contractor shall mean any
person engaged in the construction, alteration or demolition of residential,
commercial or industrial structures, or a combination of residential,
commercial and industrial structures, who for a fixed sum, price, fee,
percentage, valuable consideration or compensation, other than wages,
undertakes or offers to undertake with another for the erection, construction,
replacement, repair, alteration or any addition to, subtracting from,
improvement, movement of, wrecking of or demolition of, a residential,
commercial or industrial structure or combination of residential, commercial
and industrial structure, and who is skilled in the planning and superintending
of residential, commercial and industrial construction or a combination of
residential, commercial and industrial construction, and has a practical
knowledge of the same, and who is familiar with the laws of the state and the
ordinances of the city governing residential, commercial and industrial
construction.
   Subcontractor shall mean any tradesman who takes a contract from a general
contractor or another subcontractor including, but not limited to, the
following trades: Masonry, carpentry, lathing, plastering, cement work, tile
work, roofing materials, painting and waterproofing, except that mechanics
hired by a licensed general contractor on an hourly basis will be exempt from
this provision of securing a license; provided further, that any subcontractor
already licensed under another city licensing ordinance or by a community with
which this city reciprocates shall be exempt from the requirement of securing a
license under this article.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 1.3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 02-877, 2-5-02)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Secs. 5-242—5-260. - Reserved.

and classification of the licensee shall be kept as a public record in the
office of the city clerk, and shall be available for public inspection.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 1.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-271. - Term of license.
   All licenses issued under this division shall expire on December 31.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 1.14, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1038, 6-6-05)
Sec. 5-272. - Suspension or revocation of license.
   The suspension and revocation of licenses issued under the provisions of
this division shall follow the procedures outlined in chapter 12 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 1.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-273. - License fees.
   Every applicant for a license or license renewal of any classification
referred to in this section shall at the time of applying for such license pay
the annual fee specified in
Chapter 12, Section 6 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 2.3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1038, 6-6-05; Ord. No. 22-1724,
2-8-22)
Sec. 5-274. - Unlawful employment.
   It shall be unlawful for any contractor to violate any of the provisions of
this chapter, for any person to aid or abet any contractor in violation of the
provisions of this chapter or to conspire at its violation, or to employ an
unlicensed person or mechanic or to permit such employment for the purpose of
doing or performing any of the acts required under the terms of this chapter to
be done or performed by a licensee under this division.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 2.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-275. - Unlawful use of licenses.
   No person having procured a building contractor's license or a
subcontractor's license shall permit or allow the use of his name by any other
person, directly or indirectly, for the purpose of obtaining a permit to do any
construction, installation, alteration or repairs to any building or structure
within the city.
(Ord. No. 81-135, § 2.2, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-276—5-290. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - FIRE REPAIR CONTRACTORS **

Chapter 12, Section 6 of this Code.
   (b)   The fees charged under this division shall be in lieu of all other
permit and inspection fees in connection with:
      (1)   Temporary repairs after a fire, such as protecting the building
from the elements with a temporary cover.
      (2)   Making provisions for ceiling, door and window openings.
      (3)   Installing temporary heating, plumbing, lighting or other
utilities.
      (4)   Installing temporary street barriers where needed.
      (5)   Removing debris from premises.

   Permits must be taken out on all repair work contemplated after a fire. The
method of construction must be shown on a plan submitted to and approved by the
department of building and safety prior to the issuance of a permit.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 2.2, 11-4-81)

*** ARTICLE VII. - HIGH PRESSURE BOILER CODE ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-311. - Scope.
   This article, except those items specified in section
5-312, shall apply to and govern:
      (1)   All steam boilers.
      (2)   All hot water boilers.
      (3)   All steam or fuel actuated prime movers (engines and turbines).
      (4)   All ammonia refrigeration systems used in commercial or industrial
buildings or facilities, or in multiple dwellings containing six housing units
or more. (Refrigeration systems for buildings of six housing units or less
shall be governed by the city mechanical code.)
      (5)   All refrigeration systems having a unit capacity of over 50 tons.
All refrigeration systems using all new classifications, or their equivalent
refrigerants as defined by the American Standards Association for Mechanical
Refrigeration Code, or ANSI/ASHRAE, to include all amendments and revisions
thereto.
      (6)   All refrigeration systems with a capacity over 50 tons when used in
buildings or facilities of public assembly such as: educational, fraternal,
governmental, religious, sports, amusements, hospital, penal or institutional
level.
      (7)   The regulation and licensing of all stationary engineers, boiler
operators, refrigeration operators and turbine and reciprocating engine
operators.
      (8)   The regulation, licensing, and operating procedures of power plants
over 15 megawatts (MW), and high pressure heating plants over 50,000 pounds/
hour.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 1.2, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-
20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-312. - Exclusions.
   This article shall not apply to the following:
   Absorption refrigeration systems that are installed in accordance with the
American Standard Code for mechanical refrigeration, as published by the
American Society of Refrigeration Engineers. However, absorption systems that
are mechanically driven, solid fuel-fired, or nuclear powered must have a
licensed steam operator on duty.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 1.3, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-313. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning.
   Aggregate shall mean the total of the horsepower/tonnage or heating surface
in a group of equipment.
   Alteration shall mean a change in the piping structure or construction of
boilers, fired pressure vessels, unfired pressure vessels or any equipment
coming within the scope of this article.
   Annual operating permit shall mean the written permission granted by the
building and safety department to an owner to operate a power plant for a
specified period.
   Appurtenance shall mean an adjunct or accessory required in connection with
boilers, fired pressure vessels, unfired pressure vessels, prime movers or
their auxiliaries. For example, the water column, blow-off valves and steam
pressure gauge are appurtenances of a boiler.
   Attending licensed operator shall mean the licensed operator who is
designated by the person having control or management of the property, or other
person, to operate the equipment.
   Automatic monitoring shall mean any Underwriters Laboratory approved energy
system which operates a mechanical and/or electronic device or system.
   Auxiliary shall mean any of the various pieces of equipment such as but not
limited to: fans, stokers and pumps required in the operation of a boiler,
fired pressure vessel or prime mover.
   Auxiliary room shall mean space enclosed or set apart, in which the
auxiliaries incident to a boiler or fire pressure vessel are housed.
   Banked operation , the banked operation of a boiler or fired pressure vessel
shall mean that the fuel supply has been positively cut off so that no fuel
shall be introduced into the firing chamber, either automatically or manually;
that air supplied in the firing chamber shall be below that used under normal
operating conditions and blocked securely so that it cannot be increased toward
the normal operating level; that the pressure in the vessel is below the
authorized maximum at the time the fired pressure vessel is banked; and that
the pressure in the vessel will continue to recede from the authorized
pressure.
   Board shall mean the Board of Safety Engineers in the city as established by
this article.
   Boiler shall mean a pressure vessel containing a liquid and in which vapor
is generated or pressure is developed by the application of heat resulting from
the conversion of any form of energy. For the purpose of this article, the
above shall be the definition of a boiler together with the following:
Superheaters, whether integral or separately fired, economizers, all boiler
appurtenances, all steam or vapor piping and fittings connecting the boiler
drum to superheaters, all piping from the boiler inlet and outlet connections
up to and including the stop valve or valves required by the A.S.M.E. Boiler
Code, all feed piping and fittings starting with the inlet valve to the
economizer or to the boiler drum and all boiler blow-off piping and fittings
from the boiler proper, water walls, or economizers, to and including the valve
or valves as required by the A.S.M.E. Boiler Code.
   Boiler classification shall mean boilers classified as follows:
      (1)   High pressure boiler shall mean a fired pressure vessel carrying
over 15 psig or, where vapor is not generated, a boiler in which the liquid
temperature exceeds 250 degrees Fahrenheit and the liquid pressure exceeds 160
psig.
      (2)   Low pressure boiler shall mean any fired pressure vessel in which
the maximum allowable working pressure for steam or other vapor is limited to
15 psig or, where vapor is not generated, a boiler in which the liquid
temperature does not exceed 250 degrees Fahrenheit and the liquid pressure does
not exceed 160 psig.
   Boiler horsepower shall mean ten square feet of boiler or fired pressure
vessel heating surface. The horsepower of vapor generating pressure vessels of
a type not having heating surface exposed to products of combustion may be
based on accepted energy units, conversion factors and conduction formulae.
   Boiler room shall mean a space enclosed or set apart, in which one or more
boilers or fired pressure vessels are installed.
   City shall mean City of Dearborn.
   Compliance officer shall mean the city employee designated by the director
of the building and safety department to enforce this division.
   Department shall mean the Building and Safety Department.
   Director shall mean the Director of the Building and Safety Department in
the City of Dearborn.
   Examiner shall mean the examiner of the Building and Safety Department in
the City of Dearborn.
   Engine horsepower shall mean 33,000 foot pounds per minute or the expanding
of 42.42 BTUs per minute.
   He shall be used as a nonsexist term referring to men and women alike.
   Heating surface shall mean any part of a boiler or fired pressure vessel
having liquid or vapor on one side and heat resulting from combustion on the
other side which can be determined by the state boiler board of boiler rules
and the A.S.M.E. Code.
   License shall mean a formal permission granted by the department of building
and safety permitting an individual person to operate for a specified period
specific classes of boilers and other equipment coming within the scope of this
article.
   Licensed operator or engineer shall mean a person holding any one of the
licenses issued in accordance with the provisions of this article, authorizing
him to operate, or supervise the operation of, specified classes of boilers,
and other equipment coming within the scope of this article.
   Low load shall mean a reduced capacity or idle/banked rated capacity with no
more than 50 percent utilization of the maximum rated capacity of either
heating or cooling systems.
   Occupied shall mean periods of time the building is open for business or
operational activities.
   Operation outside of normal business hours shall mean the presence of a
licensed operator shall not be required when the premises served by steam
boilers or hot water boilers (as for example, nights, weekends and holidays)
are closed to normal operations or public usage, provided all of the following
requirements are met:
      (1)   The aggregate heating surface of the boiler system does not exceed
1,500 square feet.
      (2)   Steam boilers are equipped with approved safety relief valves set
and stamped to relieve at not more than 15 psig, and hot water boilers are
equipped with approved safety relief valves set and stamped to relieve at not
more than 160 psig.
      (3)   An approved automatic means of feeding water into the boilers is
provided.
      (4)   Boilers are equipped with an approved pressure control with a
maximum setting not to exceed 90 percent of the setting of the safety relief
valves or safety valves, and, in addition, hot water boilers are equipped with
an approved temperature control with a maximum setting of 250 degrees
Fahrenheit.
      (5)   An approved control requiring manual resetting is installed which
will shut off the fuel and air supply in the event of low water.
      (6)   During this period the boiler shall be used only for space heating,
indirect hot water supply heating, or the maintaining of temperatures of idle
processes.
      (7)   Such methods of operation shall not be put into effect until
written permission has been granted by the department.
      (8)   The equipment must have two approved low water cutoffs as required
by the city boiler code.
   Operate shall mean to have control and responsibility for the safe operation
of heating and/or cooling systems or equipment.
   Permit shall mean written permission granted by the department of building
and safety a person to install, replace, alter or construct a specified piece
of equipment at a specific location.
   Portable boiler operating permit shall mean a permit to operate boiler used
for temporary heating, to process steam, or for heating water for industry-type
operations. A portable boiler operating permit may be issued with the approval
of the building and safety department for a maximum of six months.
   Post of duty shall mean the station place or position to be occupied by a
person licensed under this article while carrying out his assigned tasks and
responsibilities.
   Power plant shall mean a building or factory including all of the equipment
for generating power or for purposes of a heating boiler plant.
   Premises shall mean a lot, plot or parcel of land, including any structure
thereon.
   Pressure shall mean pounds per square inch (psig).
   Prime mover shall mean an initial source of motive power, such as an engine
or turbine, which receives heat or energy in some other natural form and
converts it into mechanical power which is then applied to drive other
machinery.
   Weld shall mean to unite metallic parts by heating, to a plastic or fluid
state, and then allowing the metal to flow together with or without the
addition of other molten metal.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 1.4, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-
20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.

** DIVISION 2. - BOARD OF SAFETY ENGINEERS **
Sec. 5-331. - Created; membership.
   (a)   There is hereby created a board of safety engineers.
   (b)   The board of safety engineers shall consist of five members appointed
by the mayor and who shall serve at the discretion of the mayor in accordance
with the city charter. The director of building and safety, or his designee,
and the compliance officer, shall be ex-officio members of the board and shall
be permitted to vote on matters coming before the board. The mayor shall
further appoint one qualified alternate for a term of three years. The
alternate shall be subject to call.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.1, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-332. - Qualifications of members.
   (a)   All members of the board of safety engineers shall be residents of the
city and first class stationary engineers in the city. All members of the board
shall have a minimum of ten years experience as a stationary engineer. One
member of the board shall be either a professional or chief engineer, licensed
mechanical engineer, or a city and state licensed boiler installer. One member
of the board shall be a registered energy manager, a certified plan engineer,
or a licensed mechanical operator.
   (b)   A chairman and vice-chairman shall be elected by the members and shall
have the right to vote. The chairman may act as chief examiner of applicants
for licenses under this article or appoint an examiner with the approval of the
director of the building and safety department.
   (c)   The residency requirement may be waived as to two members of the board
in the sole direction of the director.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.1.1, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742,
10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-333. - Rules, regulations and procedures.
   The board of safety engineers shall prescribe its own rules and regulations
for carrying out its functions and duties as prescribed in this division. The
director shall appoint a secretary to the board who shall be a qualified
employee from the building and safety department who shall have the following
duties:
      (1)   To keep all records and minutes and proceedings of the board and to
assist the compliance officer in making and keeping such records as required of
him by the provision hereof.
      (2)   To be in attendance at all open meetings of the board insofar as it
is possible.
      (3)   To send out any and all necessary notices authorized by the board,
director, or compliance officer this Code.
      (4)   To perform such other duties as the board, director, or compliance
officer may delegate to him.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.1.2, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-334. - Powers and duties.
   The board of safety engineers is hereby authorized and empowered:
      (1)   To hear and conduct appeals from rulings or decisions of the
director or compliance officer as to the requirements of this article, when it
is impossible for a building contractor or an owner to obtain the materials
specified for use in this article; or when it is undesirable to use the
materials specified because of improvements or new discoveries made, or when it
is impractical or undesirable to follow the method or procedure prescribed by
this article. The board, in its discretion, may approve any material proposed
as a substitute for those specified in this article, or may in its discretion
approve any method or procedure as a substitute for that herein prescribed. In
interpreting this article, the board shall give due consideration to the
practical difficulties in carrying out the strict letter of the article, but
shall in all cases so interpret this article as to observe the spirit thereof,
secure the public safety and do substantial justice.
      (2)   To conduct hearings on the suspension or revocation of all
licenses, as provided in this article, and to make recommendations to the
department.
      (3)   To conduct investigations and make recommendations pertaining to
the effective operation and application of this article to the department.
      (4)   To review examinations of applicants for licenses issued under this
article.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.2, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-335. - Quorum.
   Three members of the board of safety engineers shall constitute a quorum,
and the concurring vote of at least three members shall be necessary to take
action by the board.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.3, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-336. - Inspector—Appointment.
   The compliance officer shall be appointed by the director of building and
safety by and in accordance with the civil service provisions of the City
Charter. The compliance officer shall hold any licenses or certifications that
may be deemed necessary to perform his duties.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.4, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-337. - Same—Duties.
   The compliance officer shall have the following duties:
      (1)   He shall carry out and enforce the terms and provisions of this
article and any and all rules and regulations adopted pursuant hereto.
      (2)   He shall prepare, subject to the approval of the board and the
joint commission of reciprocating municipalities, the examination questions of
applicants for licenses under this article, and shall hear and conduct all such
examinations, which examinations shall consist or oral and written questions
and practical demonstrations which shall be sufficient to prove the competency
of the applicant for the license applied for. All such examination questions
and the answers thereto shall be kept in the possession of the department and
shall be kept under lock and key at all times; provided, however, that all such
answers to the examinations shall be regarded as confidential and shall be open
to inspection only by members of the board, its secretary, or by the applicant
himself, for a period of not more than 60 days after the examination has been
taken by the applicant. The compliance officer shall be chief examiner of
examinations and may appoint an examiner with the approval of the director of
the building and safety department with concurrence of the board of safety
engineers.
      (3)   He shall be authorized to suspend the license of any person holding
such license under this article for any of the following reasons:
         a.   Intoxication while on duty.
         b.   Incompetency.
         c.   Neglect of duty.
         d.   Failure to keep apparatus under his charge in good operating
condition and order.
         e.   Leaving the apparatus under his custody without a competent
substitute thereof.
         f.   For any reason, even though not listed above, which in the
judgment of the compliance officer, shows conduct on the part of the licensee
that would endanger the safety of persons or property.
   Immediately upon such suspension, the department shall notify the owner of
the apparatus or equipment which the licensee was operating, or his agent, of
such suspension with a written statement of the reasons thereof, and shall file
a copy of such notice and reasons with the secretary of the board who shall
thereupon forthwith notify such licensee to show cause within ten days from the
date of such suspension why his license should not be revoked, and such show
cause shall be served upon the inspector or director and forwarded to the
department as soon as possible. At the time of giving such licensee notice to
show cause, he shall be served with a copy of the reasons for his suspension.
It shall be unlawful for any person whose license is suspended to operate any
boiler or pressure vessel or equipment covered by this article, and the
inspector is hereby authorized to take into his possession the license of any
and all certificates issued to the licensee by the city and hold them until a
hearing on the suspension has been held and a determination made by the board
as to whether the license will be revoked. The board of safety engineers shall
conduct a hearing within a reasonable time after such show cause is delivered
to the division or department so as to afford substantial justice.
      (4)   The compliance officer may approve additional operating capacity of
up to 20 percent of the existing aggregate total if warranted by special
conditions and with the approval of the board and the building and safety
department. Operations of this type shall obtain a new annual operating permit.
Required applications and approval must be granted by the board and the
director of the building and safety department, and all required fees paid.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.5, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-338. - Procedure on appeal.
   If any person desires to appeal to the board of safety engineers any
decision or ruling of the inspector or director of building and safety or
examiner on any matter or variance under this article, such appeal shall be
made in writing and filed with the secretary of the board 28 days before the
board meeting, and, at the same time, such person shall pay to the finance
department any and all required fees. These fees shall not be refundable. If
giving notice of hearing before the board is not otherwise provided for herein,
the secretary of the board shall give such notice to all the known interested
parties who are not members of the board at least 28 days before the date of
such hearing either by personal service or certified mail, and the hearing
shall be held at such time and place in the city as shall be therein stated.
Proof of service or giving of such notice shall be made and filed with the
board prior to the hearing.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.7, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-339. - Compensation.
   Members of the board of safety engineers, excepting officers and employees
of the city, shall be paid such compensation as the city council shall
determine.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 2.6, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Secs. 5-340—5-355. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - INSTALLATION **
Sec. 5-356. - Standards.
   (a)   The rules for construction of power and low pressure heating boilers,
as formulated by the boiler code committee and published by the A.S.M.E.
(American Society of Mechanical Engineers), 1984 edition, and the rules and
construction of unfired pressure vessels, 1981 edition, being a report of the
subcommittee of boiler code committee of unfired pressure vessels and published
by the A.S.M.E. and the American Standards Association ANSI/ASHRAE 15-78 (B9.1)
Code for Mechanical Refrigeration set forth the standards for and shall govern
boiler, pressure vessels and refrigeration construction installation,
inspection, operation, and safety for all apparatus and equipment covered by
this article in the city, together with all amendments thereto and shall be
regarded as good practice in such work the requirements of the State of
Michigan Board of Boiler Rules (Michigan State Boiler Act of 1965, as amended)
and the National Board Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code.
   (b)   The compliance officer or director shall have the authority to issue
notices of violation or appearance tickets that may be necessary to enforce
this code of ordinances or protect the health and safety of the community and
building occupants.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.1, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-356A. - Authority.
   (a)   [Operating rules.] All power plants shall meet the following
guidelines in reference to operating rules. All new power plants must submit
drawings and plans to the board of safety engineers and an outline of their
mode of operation. The compliance officer shall review all license requirements
and make recommendations to the board chairman and department of economic and
community development for the minimum number of engineers needed on duty and
the grade of license required.
   (b)   [Approval authority.] The board of safety engineers or director shall
have the authority to approve drawings, plans, specifications and approve the
minimum number of licensed engineers per power plant.
   (c)   Board authority .
      (1)   The board of director shall have the authority to order the
compliance officer to investigate a violation regarding the safe operation of a
power plant or facility. The board shall make recommendations and develop
guidelines based on the following national standards:
         a.   ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code.
         b.   Hartford Steam Boilers standards and lots.
         c.   State Mechanical Code or BOCA National Mechanical Code of 1999
and amendments.
   (d)   [Annual permit required.] The operators of power plants and heating/
cooling systems must obtain an annual operating permit to be issued by the
department of economic and community development subject to compliance with
this article.
(Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99; Ord. No. 09-1262, 12-14-09)
Sec. 5-357. - Unlawful construction or installation.
   It shall be unlawful to construct or install in the city an apparatus or
equipment covered by the provisions of this article which does not conform to
this article governing new installations; provided, however, that all boilers
or unfired pressure vessels installed and ready for use or in use at the time
this article takes effect shall be made to conform as nearly as possible to
this article as to such existing installations, and the procedure prescribed in
this article shall be used in determining the maximum allowable working
pressure for such apparatus or equipment; provided, however, that boilers,
pressure vessels and refrigerating systems constructed or installed in
compliance with the standards in effect at the time of such construction or
installation shall be required to conform to standards subsequently adopted
only to the extent that the department shall deem necessary for the safety of
persons and property.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.2, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-358. - Insurance company inspector reports.
   The department may accept a copy of the state certificate internal
inspection report in lieu of city internal inspection if the inspector has a
national board license and the insurance company writes boiler and machinery
insurance in the state, and if the owner makes a written request for such
acceptance to the department of building and safety. All insurance inspectors
must report violations governed by this article to the department within 72
hours and comply with all rules and regulations of the city boiler code and
safety code. A permit shall be required.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.3, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-359. - Suspension.
   The director or compliance officer may at any time suspend a license or
permit when in his opinion the apparatus, equipment, or system is a safety
hazard or does not conform to this article.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.4, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-360. - Permit and license fees.
   The fees for annual inspections are listed in chapter 9 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.5, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-361. - Records.
   The inspector is hereby directed, empowered and charged with the duty of
making and filing with the department a complete record of the type or kind,
serial number, name of manufacturer, size, age, condition, allowable pressure,
location and date of last inspection, and date of issuance of inspection
certificates covering all apparatuses or equipment governed by this article and
of all insurance company inspection reports and applications for permits
approved by him as required in this article. All inaccurate or missing records
shall be corrected within 18 months from the adoption of this article.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 3.6, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-362. - Automatic and/or monitoring devices; operation during low load
conditions.
   If a high or low pressure boiler system or refrigeration system is equipped
with an automatic and/or monitoring device or system, the presence of a
licensed boiler operator shall not be required during low load conditions such
as holidays, weekends, and other low load times, provided all of the following
requirements have been met:
      (1)   The owner or operator of the building where such device or system
is located must have an annual operating permit for the automatic monitoring
device. Such permit shall be approved by the director of economic and community
development or his designee. The fee for permit shall be as set forth in
section
9-68 of this Code.
      (2)   The aggregate heating surface of the boiler system does not exceed
1,000 square feet.
      (3)   All steam boilers and refrigeration systems equipped with such
devices or systems must be equipped with approved energy management systems.
      (4)   All steam boilers equipped with such devices or systems must be
equipped with approved safety relief valves set and stamped to relieve pressure
at not more than 15 psig. All hot water boilers equipped with such devices or
systems must be equipped with approved safety relief valves set and stamped to
relieve at not more than 160 psig.
      (5)   An approved automatic means of feeding water into the boiler must
be provided.
      (6)   Boilers are equipped with a master control which includes an
approved pressure control device with a maximum setting not to exceed 85
percent of the setting of the safety relief valves or safety valves. Hot water
boilers must be equipped with an approved temperature control device which
includes a maximum setting of 240 degrees Fahrenheit.
      (7)   An approved control device or system must be installed which
requires manual resetting and will shut-off fuel and air supplies in the event
of a low water situation.
      (8)   The boiler room must have two means of ingress and egress and
comply with all applicable provisions of the building code.
      (9)   All boiler and chiller systems must have required safety controls.
Boilers must have two approved low water cut-off devices of systems with manual
reset. Chillers must be equipped with manual rest.
      (10)   All refrigeration systems must have required safety controls
approved by the current ASHRAE Mechanical Refrigeration Code or Underwriters
Laboratory energy management systems.
      (11)   Such methods of operation shall require the approval of the board
and the director of the economic and community development department. The
board may grant temporary approval if conditions necessitate approval for one
season.
      (12)   The compliance officer or the director may revoke approval if any
condition of approval has not been met upon providing written notice to the
property owner. Such approval may be revoked if the required renewal fees are
not paid or property owner is in violation of any applicable codes or
ordinances to the equipment.
   Furthermore, the compliance officer may enter the premises at any time
during normal business hours for the purpose of testing any monitoring or
automatic control device in order to ensure code compliance and to ensure the
public health, safety, and welfare.
(Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99;
