Ord. No. 09-1262, 12-14-09)
Secs. 5-363—5-380. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 4. - LICENSES **
Sec. 5-381. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Attending licensed operator shall mean the licensed operator who is
designated by the person having control or management of the property, or other
person, to operate the equipment.
   Licensed operator in responsible charge shall mean a person holding any one
of the licenses issued in accordance with the provisions of this article
authorizing him to operate or supervise the operation of specified classes of
boilers, fired pressure vessels, prime movers, refrigeration and equipment.
   Person to be in charge of shall mean the immediate licensed supervisor of an
employee at the time of the operation of the apparatus or equipment governed by
this article when relating to such person being in charge of or having
supervision over persons in this section.
(Ord. No. 85-323, §§ 4.1, 4.1a, 4.1b, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord.
No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-382. - Required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to be in charge of or to operate,
supervise or to be in charge of persons operating any apparatus or equipment
governed by this article in the city without a license to do so; provided,
however, that no license shall be issued to any person who has not attained the
age of 18 years.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.1, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-383. - Classification of licenses—Established.
   There shall be issued in the city the following classifications of licenses
involving apparatus and equipment.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-384. - Same—Low pressure boiler operator.
   There shall be a classification of license known as low pressure boiler
operator which shall be issued to persons properly qualified for the operation
of boilers where steam pressure does not exceed 15 pounds per square inch, the
liquid pressure does not exceed 160 psig or the liquid temperature does not
exceed 250 degrees Fahrenheit. Such licenses shall be limited to operation of
equipment having an aggregate of 5,000 square feet of heating surface and shall
be issued to any person who has had a minimum of one year's experience in the
operation of maintenance of low and high pressure boilers, prime movers or
their auxiliaries and has passed a satisfactory examination. The time spent as
a boiler trainee, or general helper, will be credited toward actual experience
for qualification prerequisites.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(a), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-385. - Same—High pressure boiler operator.
   There shall be a classification of license known as high pressure boiler
operator which shall be issued to persons properly qualified for the operation
of boilers in which the steam pressure exceeds 15 pounds per square inch, the
water pressure exceeds 160 psig, or where the liquid temperature exceeds 250
degrees Fahrenheit. Such license shall be limited to the operation of equipment
having an aggregate 5,000 square feet of heating surface and shall be issued to
any person who has had two years' experience in the operation or maintenance of
high pressure boilers, prime movers, or other auxiliaries, and has passed a
satisfactory examination showing that he is familiar with and can operate such
boilers with safety to life and property. The applicant shall possess a low
pressure boiler operator's license and have been actively employed as such an
operator for a minimum of one year or shall have spent two years as a boiler
trainee, boiler room fireman or apprentice.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(b), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-386. - Same—Fourth class stationary engineer.
   There shall be a classification of license known as fourth class stationary
engineer which shall be issued only to persons who operate hoisting portable
boilers and privately owned track locomotive equipment, excluding locomotive
boilers used on railroad trunk lines. Each person to whom this classification
of license is issued must have at least two years' experience in the operation
of such mechanical equipment, working under the direction of a licensed
engineer and must pass a satisfactory examination that he has reasonable skill
and familiarity in the operation of such an apparatus. The license issued for
this classification shall be in a card form and must be carried on the person
of the operator when engaged in the operation of such hoisting or portable
apparatus. It shall be unlawful for any person to operate hoisting or portable
apparatus without such a license, except that a person who holds a first class
stationary engineer's license may operate this equipment.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(c), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-387. - Same—Third class stationary engineer.
   There shall be a classification of license known as third class stationary
engineer which shall be issued to personnel who have had three years experience
in the operation of power boilers in a high pressure boiler plant, plus
sufficient experience in the actual operation of steam prime movers. The
applicant shall be given credit for boiler maintenance experience or as an
apprentice in an approved training program. Such person shall pass a
satisfactory examination showing he is competent and understands the operation
of high pressure boilers and prime movers. The department, with the concurrence
of the board of safety engineers, may waive the length of experience for this
classification if the applicant submits documentary evidence of equivalent
education. Such licenses shall be limited to the operation of equipment having
an aggregate heating surface of 10,000 square feet, or less, or steam prime
movers not exceeding 150 horsepower.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(d), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-388. - Same—Second class stationary engineer.
   (a)   An applicant for a second class stationary engineer shall meet one of
the following experience requirements:
      (1)   He shall possess a third class stationary engineer license and
shall have had at least one year of experience as a third-class stationary
engineer.
      (2)   He shall be an engineering graduate of an engineering college of
recognized standing and have been actually employed in the engineering or
research division of a steam-electric power generating unit for at least one
year.
      (3)   He shall have at least four years of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 10,000 square feet, the foregoing experience to be
established by documented evidence from present and previous employers.
      (4)   He shall have at least one year of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 10,000 square feet, plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of steam prime movers in excess of 100 horsepower to make
a total of at least four years, the foregoing experience to be established by
documented evidence from present and previous employers.
      (5)   He shall have at least one year of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 10,000 square feet, plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler plant having an
aggregate heating surface of more than 5,000 square feet to make a total of at
least four years, the foregoing experience to be established by documented
evidence from present and previous employers.
   (b)   He shall pass a satisfactory examination showing he is competent to
operate and understands the operation of a high pressure boiler and prime
mover. The department, with the concurrence of the board of safety engineers,
may waive the experience requirement for this classification if the applicant
submits documentary evidence of equivalent education. Such a license shall be
limited to the operation of equipment having an aggregate heating surface of
25,000 square feet or to prime movers of 250 horsepower.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(e), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-389. - Same—First class stationary engineer.
   (a)   There shall be a classification of license known as first class
stationary engineer which shall be unlimited as to horsepower of boilers,
engines and refrigeration. Such license shall be granted to any person who
passes satisfactory examinations showing he is competent and understands the
operation of any and all boiler, engine, and refrigeration equipment covered by
this article and meets one of the following experience requirements:
      (1)   He shall have a second class stationary engineer's license and
shall have had at least two years of experience under such license.
      (2)   He shall have at least six years of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 20,000 square feet, which experience is
established by documented evidence from present or previous employers.
      (3)   He shall have at least two years of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 20,000 square feet, plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of steam prime movers in excess of 250 horsepower to make
a total of at least six years, which experience is established by documented
evidence from present and previous employers.
      (4)   He shall have at least two years of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 20,000 square feet, plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an
aggregate heating surface of more than 10,000 square feet to make a total of at
least five years, which experience is established by documented evidence from
present and previous employers.
      (5)   He shall be a graduate mechanical engineer from a recognized
college or university, shall have had two years' experience in any steam plant,
and shall have had a second class stationary engineer's license for at least
one year, with the further provision that one year of the steam plant
experience may be waived by the board if the applicant has been employed in the
engineering or research divisions of a steam-electric power generating plant to
make a total of at least six years experience, which experience is established
by documented evidence from present or previous employers.
   (b)   The department, with concurrence of the board of safety engineers, may
waive the experience requirement for this classification if the applicant
submits documentary evidence of equivalent education.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(f), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-389A. - Facility engineer.
   There shall be a classification of license known as facility engineer, which
shall be unlimited as to horsepower of boiler and refrigeration systems. Such
license shall be granted to any person who passes an examination showing he is
competent and understands the operations of any and all equipment in buildings
with over 350,000 square feet of building space. These facilities shall have a
licensed facility engineer on site. In addition to the above, all applicants
shall have at least six years of experience in boilers and refrigeration
equipment, three years experience as a supervisor, and have knowledge of
building, and energy safety codes. In lieu of the above, and with the approval
of the board, an individual may:
      (1)   Possess a first class stationary engineer license for two years;
      (2)   Be a graduate mechanical engineer or have a degree in facilities
from a recognized college or university, with two years experience in
powerhouse boilers and refrigeration systems; or
      (3)   The board will waive the experience requirement with the
recommendation of the code compliance officer if all other requirements are met
and written evidence of such is presented to the board and the department of
building and safety.
(Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-389B. - Chief powerhouse stationary engineer.
   There shall be a classification of license known as chief powerhouse
stationary engineer which shall be unlimited as to horsepower of boilers,
engines, turbines, and refrigeration systems. Such license shall be granted to
any person who passes a satisfactory examination showing he or she is
competent, who meets all the requirements and understands the operation of any
and all equipment, and who has the supervisory experience necessary to assume
responsible charge of various engineering duties covered by the code. In
addition, the applicant shall meet one of the following experience and
educational requirements for all facilities over 500,000 square feet, said
facilities being required to have a licensed chief powerhouse engineer on site:
      (1)   The individual shall have a first class stationary engineer's
license with at least two years of experience under such license; or
      (2)   The individual shall have at least eight years of experience in the
actual operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 25,000 square feet plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of prime movers in excess of 500 horsepower; or
      (3)   The individual shall have had at least eight years of experience in
the actual operation of a power-house in a high pressure plant having an
aggregate heating surface of more than 25,000 square feet which experience is
established by documented evidence from present or previous employers; or
      (4)   The individual shall have been a licensed supervisor in the field
of a large powerhouse high pressure boiler and prime movers with sufficient
experience in the operation and maintenance of equipment in a steam-electric
power generating plant for at least eight years; or
      (5)   The individual shall be a graduate mechanical engineer from a
recognized university or college; shall have had four years experience in any
steam plant and shall have had a first class stationary engineer license, or
equal grade of professional license if the board approves the application.
(Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-390. - Same—Refrigeration operators.
   (a)   First class refrigeration operator. Refrigeration systems of unlimited
tonnage using any kind of refrigerant may and shall be under the supervision of
a licensed operator in responsible charge possessing at least a first class
refrigeration operator's license. An applicant for a first class refrigeration
operator's license shall have had at least two years experience in the
operation of nondomestic refrigeration systems, or, he shall be an engineering
graduate of a college of recognized standing, or, shall have satisfactorily
completed an acceptable course in refrigeration engineering, as established by
completion letters or certificates indicating in detail his schedule of time
and studies, and shall have at least one year of experience in the operation of
construction of nondomestic refrigeration systems. In addition to the above,
all applicants for first class refrigeration operators license shall take an
appropriate examination.
   (b)   Second class refrigerator operator. Refrigeration systems, the largest
of which contains not more than 1,000 pounds of refrigerant or is driven by
motors not in excess of 300 tons, shall be under the supervision of a licensed
operator in responsible charge possessing at least a second class refrigeration
operator's license. An applicant for second class refrigeration operator's
license shall have had at least one year of experience in the operation of
nondomestic refrigeration systems; or he shall be an engineering graduate of a
college of recognized standing or shall have satisfactorily completed a written
examination or acceptable course in refrigeration engineering, as established
by completion letters or certificates indicating in detail his schedule of time
and studies, and shall have at least six months experience in the operation or
construction of nondomestic refrigeration systems.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(g), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-391. - Same—Turbine and reciprocating engine operator.
   There shall be a classification of license known as turbine and
reciprocating engine operator. Each person to whom this classification of
license is issued shall have at least four years of experience in the operation
of such equipment and must pass a satisfactory examination showing that he
understands the operation of such apparatus.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(h), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-391A. - Trainee operators.
   There shall be a classification of license known as trainee who shall work
under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer. This individual:
      (1)   Shall have at least six months of experience or equal hours of
formal education approved by the board or the compliance officer;
      (2)   Shall have at least eight credit hours of schooling or college
courses in boilers and refrigeration and three months of work experience; or
      (3)   The board may waive the experience requirement upon recommendation
of the code compliance officer.
(Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-391B. - Limited license.
   A license may be issued by the director upon approval of the board of safety
engineers for one approved building only. This license is applicable only to
buildings with 3,000 square feet low pressure boilers and/or 400 ton
refrigeration systems. Applicants must have one year of documented experience,
and are subject to approval of the board of safety engineers. This license must
be upgraded after two years to an appropriate license in this article.
(Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-392. - Post of duty—Low pressure boiler operators and engineers.
   In low pressure boiler plants, the post of duty of the licensed operator in
responsible charge shall be in the boiler rooms which contain the auxiliaries
pertinent to the operation of such boiler or boilers, providing such rooms are
accessible for passage, visibility or audibility. "Post of duty" need not apply
when banked operations are met.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(i), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-393. - Same—High pressure boilers operators and engineers.
   In high pressure boiler plants or stationary prime mover plants where
licensed personnel are required by this article to be in attendance, the post
of duty of such operator or engineer shall be in the room where such boilers,
engines, turbines, or auxiliaries are located pertinent to the plant operation,
if such rooms are readily accessible for passage, visibility or audibility.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(j), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787,
8-3-99)
Sec. 5-394. - Same—Refrigeration operators.
   In all facilities that have refrigeration systems that function primarily as
support for actual testing and production and not for human comfort cooling,
the post of duty of the licensed refrigeration operator at all times when the
systems are in operation shall be on the premises within easy reach and hearing
distance of where the equipment which he is licensed to operate is located,
provided that the operator may be absent for a period of not more that 60
consecutive minutes during any two hours for the purpose of inspecting or
adjusting parts, auxiliaries or appurtenances of the system which he is
licensed to operate; provided further that the compliance officer or director
of the economic and community development department shall be permitted to
modify, by written notice to the owner, any of the above limitations where
special conditions warrant such action, and on systems where in the opinion of
the department, the refrigeration plant design is such that the operation does
not endanger the life or health of individuals. The post of duty of the
operator when the systems are in operation shall be on the premises in which
the refrigeration systems are located.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(k), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742,
10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99; Ord. No. 09-1262, 12-14-09)
Sec. 5-395. - Same—Exceptions.
   Fulltime licensed personnel in attendance will not be required for the
following equipment:
      (1)   Boilers or pressure vessels operating under banked operation or
under the requirements of section
5-313.
      (2)   Low pressure steam boilers with 1,000 square feet aggregate or less
of heating surface.
      (3)   Low pressure hot water heating and hot water supply boilers having
1,000 square feet aggregate or less of heating surface.
      (4)   Direct low fired pressure hot water heaters used for purposes other
than space heating whose self-contained capacity does not exceed 120 gallons;
whose heating surface does not exceed an aggregate total of 750 square feet
regardless of pressure or temperature conditions. Such apparatuses shall,
however, be designed and constructed for the pressure carried, shall be
equipped with A.S.M.E. approved safety valve and appliances, and must comply
with all requirements of the state board of boiler rules and the city boiler
code.
      (5)   All rooftop refrigeration systems under 150 tons aggregate provided
they are properly monitored and maintained by an approved ASHRAE and Mechanical
Refrigeration Code or Underwriters Laboratory energy management system. The
compliance officer and the director of the economic and community development
department may modify these limitations, if the plant designs are such that the
operation does not endanger the life, safety or health of individuals.
Operators of refrigeration systems under these exceptions shall be required to
file an annual reliability report to the board of safety engineers.
      (6)   All refrigeration systems classified as a low probability system as
described in the 2006 Michigan Mechanical Code during established non-core
business hours and/or operations, provided the system is equipped with a
central control board as defined in subsections 5-396(b) through (j).
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.2(l), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-742,
10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99; Ord. No. 09-1262, 12-14-09)
Sec. 5-396. - Same—Centralized control.
   (a)   Post of duty requirements for all refrigeration systems and plants
with low pressure boilers with an aggregate of not more than 5,000 square feet
of heating surface are as follows: the attending licensed operator may be
absent from the area monitored by a central control station in which the
equipment is located for not more than four hours, provided that the safety of
the plant is not jeopardized by his absence.
   (b)   A central control board must monitor all levels of operation of
equipment being controlled, including all safety alarms, valve states,
temperatures and pressures as necessary to ensure complete safe operation. All
equipment shall have manual reset controls on equipment with alarms.
   (c)   A central control station must be continuously manned by personnel
licensed to operate all classes of equipment under centralized control.
Personnel may be absent for up to ten minutes provided that an alert pager
system is in use and approved by the department of economic and community
development.
   (d)   A central control board failure or "no signal" condition shall cause
immediate shutdown of the equipment involved. All such equipment, when shut
down, shall require manual restart at the equipment location. All shut down
alarms causing damage to equipment shall be reported to the department in
writing within 72 hours of detailing the type of alarm and damage caused.
   (e)   The central control station operator shall maintain one year a
continuous separate readout of all system messages. In addition, a working log
may be kept. The operator must obtain a system readout of all equipment at
least twice per shift.
   (f)   The central control system, together with all operator requirements,
and any significant changes that alter the intent of any previously granted
appeal, shall be approved by formal appeal to the board of safety engineers or
the department for the interim period. The written approval shall remain in
force only so long as the system is maintained and operated in a manner such as
to eliminate any undue safety hazard to life, limb, or property.
   (g)   The central control system must have the approval of Underwriters'
Laboratories or other nationally approved independent testing laboratories,
national fire codes, National Electric Code, 1990 BOCA Mechanical Code, and all
amendments thereto.
   (h)   The fee for a special permit required to be issued annually is to be
based on the size of the equipment and chapter 9 of this Code.
   (i)   Licensed personnel may continue to operate equipment under their
control as of June 4, 1985, if approved by the department. Any new employee
must obtain the proper license for the equipment to be operated as required by
this article. The department may require a higher grade license if unusual or
hazardous conditions warrant same. The license requirements shall be subject to
review if there is any change or alteration in equipment at an existing
location.
   (j)   Any holder of a first class engineer license issued under the
requirements of Ordinance No. 81-66, as amended, which license was in good
standing on June 4, 1985, shall, upon payment of fees therefore, be entitled to
a first class stationary engineer license and a first class refrigeration
operator license without further requirements.
(Ord. No. 85-323, §§ 4.2(m)—(o), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95; Ord. No. 98-
742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99; Ord. No. 09-1262, 12-14-09)
Sec. 5-396A. - Licensed engineer required.
   Each power plant facility owner must employ a licensed stationary engineer
as described below, who shall be in responsible charge of the power plant
facilities and be registered with the building and safety department.
   (a)   A chief engineer is required for all facilities over 500,000 square
feet, or over 450-megawatt capacity, or 450,000 pound/hour boiler capacity.
   (b)   A facility engineer is required for all facilities over 350,000 square
feet, or over 200-megawatt capacity, or 300,000 pounds/hour boiler capacity.
   (c)   The board of safety engineers may waive the above requirements upon a
showing by the facility owner of sufficient and adequate safeguards and
automatic monitoring systems.
(Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Sec. 5-397. - Application and examination.
   Applicant forms, approved by the board, shall be supplied to any applicant
by the department for all classifications of licenses provided for in this
division. All information and data pertaining to the applicant set forth on
such application form must be answered in full, sworn to before a notary public
and, upon payment of the filing fee, filed with the secretary of the board.
Falsification of any material fact upon the application shall be grounds for
revocation of any license granted. Regular examinations as prescribed by the
board shall be held at a time and place specified by the board in its rules and
regulations. Applicants will be notified of the time and place where such
examinations will be held. Special examinations may be held at the discretion
of the department and at such time and place as designated by the board. When
any applicant for a given classification has passed the required examination
prescribed by the board, the department shall certify such fact to the city
clerk and, upon the payment of the registration fee listed in
Chapter 12, Section 6, the city clerk shall issue the particular license
specified by the department to which such applicant is entitled.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.4, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 5-398. - Posting license.
   Every license granted or issued to any person under this division shall be
hung under glass in the boiler or engine room where such person operates the
mechanical apparatus, except that of fourth class stationary engineer.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.5, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-399. - Issuance of lower classification of license; reexamination.
   Any person applying for a particular classification of a license and failing
to pass the examination required for that classification may, in the discretion
of the department or board, be issued a license of lower classification than
that applied for to which his qualification and his examination may entitle
him, but such person shall not make a reapplication for the license, the
examination for which he failed to pass, or for a higher classification until
after a period of at least 90 days has expired.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.6, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-400. - Expiration and renewal.
   Engineers, and operators, licenses issued under this article shall expire at
12:00 midnight one year from the date of original issuance or one year from the
last expiration date, and shall be renewable at the office of the city clerk
upon approval by the department and upon payment of the fee set forth in
Chapter 12, Section 6. If any licensee fails to apply for a renewal of his
license within 60 days after the expiration thereof, such license will be
deemed to have lapsed. Any person allowing his license to lapse will be subject
to reexamination before obtaining a renewal thereof.
   Before any license shall be issued after an examination or reexamination of
the licensee, as provided in this section, such licensee shall pay the fee as
prescribed in
Chapter 12, Section 6 for the original issuance of the license.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.7, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 5-401. - Periodic refresher training required.
   All engineers licensed in the city must provide proof of satisfactory
completion of a state-approved refresher course in the field of stationary
engineering, every five years commencing January 1, 2001.
   All chief powerhouse engineers and refrigeration engineers must provide
proof of satisfactory completion of a state-approved refresher course in the
field of stationary engineering every five years commencing January 1, 2002.
(Ord. No. 99-787, 8-3-99)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 99-787, adopted Aug. 3, 1999, replaced §
5-401, which formerly pertained to the exception of miniature boilers and
unfired pressure vessels, and derived from Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.8, adopted June
4, 1985, with a new §
5-401 to read as herein set out.
Sec. 5-402. - Reciprocal clause.
   (a)   The city may participate with other municipalities or states in a
reciprocal program for the licensing of stationary engineers, boiler operators
and refrigeration operators.
   (b)   A person desiring to be licensed as a stationary engineer, boiler
operator or refrigeration operator shall obtain such license in the
reciprocating municipality or state where he is, or will be, employed to
operate boiler plants, steam prime movers or refrigeration systems. Prior to
being issued a license, such person shall submit to the reciprocating
municipality or state a formal notarized document setting forth his
qualifications for same.
   (c)   Municipalities or states desiring to participate with the city in a
reciprocal program for licensing shall have had approved, by an affirmative
action of their legislative bodies, licensing provisions meeting the
requirements set forth in this article. In addition, any state or municipality
which has a department with authority to issue stationary engineers licenses
and examinations equal to that of the city, and which has comparable types of
grades of licenses and requirements, will be acceptable. City reciprocal
licenses may be registered with all communities that are in good standing and
members of the reciprocal committee after payment of a registration fee. The
reciprocal licenses shall be obtained in the municipality wherein the applicant
maintains his principal place of employment.
   (d)   The right of any municipality or state to participate in the
reciprocating provisions of this division shall be determined by the department
and the board of safety engineers. A joint committee of an equal number of
members of the reciprocal agreement may be established to recommend fees and
changes to portions of this article.
   (e)   The fee for the reciprocal registration of any and all of the license
classifications described in section
5-396, which have been issued by a reciprocating municipality and are in good
standing with that body, shall be according to chapter 9 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 4.9, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-403. - Chief powerhouse stationary engineer.
   There shall be a classification of license known as chief powerhouse
stationary engineer which shall be unlimited as to horsepower of boilers,
engines, turbines, and refrigeration steam generations. Such license shall be
granted to any person who passes a satisfactory examination showing he is
competent and meets all the requirements and understands the operation of any
and all equipment and has supervisor experience as is necessary to assume
responsible charge of various engineering duties covered by the within code and
meets one of the following experience and educational requirements:
      (1)   He shall have a first class stationary engineer's license and shall
have had at least two years of experience under such license; or
      (2)   He shall have had at least eight hears of experience in the actual
operation of boilers in a high pressure boiler plant having an aggregate
heating surface of more than 25,000 square feet plus sufficient experience in
the actual operation of prime movers in excess of 500 horsepower; or
      (3)   He shall have had at least eight years of experience in the actual
operation of a powerhouse in a high pressure plant having an aggregate heating
surface of more than 25,000 square feet which experience is established by
documented evidence from present or previous employers; or
      (4)   He shall have been a licensed supervisor in the field of a large
powerhouse high pressure boiler and prime movers with sufficient experience in
the operation and maintenance of equipment in a steam-electric power generating
plant for at least eight years; or
      (5)   He shall be a graduate mechanical engineer from a recognized
university or college, shall have had four years experience in any steam plant
and shall have had a first class stationary engineer license, or equal grade of
professional licenses if the board approves his application.
(Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95)
Secs. 5-404—5-420. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - PERMITS **
Sec. 5-421. - Required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to construct,
install, alter, replace or repair any apparatus or equipment governed by the
provisions of this article, or to begin such work in or for any building or
structure in the city without first having a permit issued therefor. An
application for a permit must be made in writing and permit issued pursuant
thereto by the department prior to beginning any work governed by the
provisions of this article. It shall be unlawful to fail or neglect to comply
with the conditions of the permit issued, as hereby required. Any person when
applying for any such permit shall furnish the department with all necessary
plans and/or specifications for such proposed construction, installation,
alteration, replacement or repair and with all proper and sufficient
information relating thereto, and the approval in writing of the department
regarding such plans and/or specifications shall be first obtained before such
permit shall be issued; provided, however, that the department may waive the
above requirement of a permit in the case of alterations, replacements or
repairs, anything herein to the contrary notwithstanding, to any existing
apparatus or equipment governed by this article where the estimated cost of
such alteration, replacement or repair, both as to labor and materials, will
not exceed $100.00, if such alteration, replacement or repairs will not add to
the capacity of such apparatus or equipment and will not, in the opinion of the
department, be of such a nature as to render an inspection of same necessary.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.1, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-422. - Test data, measurements, ratings, capacity.
   Before a permit shall be issued by the department for the installation,
alteration, replacement or repair of any apparatus or equipment covered by this
article, the person seeking such permit shall furnish the department with such
test data, measurements, ratings, capacities or other information as may be
required for the purpose of establishing ratings or capacities of such
apparatus or equipment in accordance with the engineering provisions of this
article.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.2, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-423. - Certificate required.
   All test data, measurements, ratings or capacities submitted to the
department, as required in this article, shall be accomplished by an engineer's
certificate certifying to the correctness of such information; such certificate
shall be made by an engineer employed by the manufacturer of the apparatus or
equipment for which the test data, measurements, ratings or capacities is
submitted.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.3, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-424. - Secondhand apparatus or equipment.
   The department may require such data, certification, or testing as may be
deemed necessary to determine the rating or capacity of any secondhand
apparatus or equipment governed by the provisions of this article which is no
longer manufactured, or for which the manufacturer's test data, measurements,
ratings or capacity, as required by this article, are not available.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.4, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-425. - Repairs ordered; condemnations.
   Whenever the department shall order in writing repairs to be made to any
apparatus or equipment covered by this article, such repairs shall be made
within two weeks from the date of such order if practical; provided, however,
in cases where life or property would be endangered by the use of such
apparatus or equipment without such repairs, the department may in its
discretion shut down such apparatus or equipment forthwith to prevent its
continued use, and may suspend the inspection certificate until the necessary
repairs are made.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.5, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-426. - Fees.
   Permit fees for all work governed by this article shall be as specified in
chapter 9 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 5.6, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-427. - Unlawful acts.
   In addition to the unlawful acts heretofore designated as violations of this
article, it shall be unlawful for the owner, operator or any person using any
apparatus or equipment governed by the provisions of this article to:
      (1)   After the limits, adjustment, or connection of any safety device in
a maneuver that would change its operation or create a hazard.
      (2)   Alter the adjustment of the safety valve to increase the pressure
in a boiler.
      (3)   Allow hazardous accumulation of scale in the water column pipes to
the boiler.
      (4)   Use apparatus or equipment after suspension of the license of the
operator or the inspection certificate.
      (5)   Operate any apparatus or equipment without a valid and subsisting
license to do so.
      (6)   Willfully neglect to abuse any apparatus or equipment.
      (7)   Operate or cause to be operated any apparatus or equipment in the
city without having complied with the provisions of this article or allowing
any licensee under this article to absent himself from his post of duty without
a licensed person to take his place.
      (8)   Prevent or attempt to prevent any licensee under this article from
performing any act required to be performed by this Code or require or attempt
to prevent a licensee from restoring boiler control devices or the automatic
monitoring of the boiler to proper operating conditions.
      (9)   To operate or to start boiler control devices or automatic
monitoring boilers from a remote location without written permission from the
compliance officer and the department of building and safety.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 6.1, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Sec. 5-428. - Portable boilers.
   Every owner or user of portable or semiportable boilers in the city, on or
before March 1 of each year, shall furnish to the department a written list
setting forth the number of such boilers used, the description of each boiler
and the location thereof in order that an inspection thereof may be made. It
shall be unlawful for any person to use in the city any such boiler until it
has been inspected and an inspection certificate has been given in accordance
with this article.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 6.2, 6-4-85)
Sec. 5-429. - Safety alarms and cut-off controls.
   Each and every boiler governed by this article shall have two low water
safety alarms and cut-off controls of a type easily tested by the compliance
officer without interfering with the operation of the boiler. The alarms shall
be connected with the boiler so that the low water alarm will be sounded when
there is less than two inches of water over the highest point of tubes or crown
sheets and with manual reset controls.
(Ord. No. 85-323, § 6.3, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 98-742, 10-20-98; Ord. No. 99-787, 8-
3-99)
Secs. 5-430—5-445. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VII.5. - REFRIGERATION CODE ***
Sec. 5-446. - Scope.
   The provisions of this article shall apply to all new and used refrigerating
systems hereafter installed, to all existing refrigerating systems and to all
repairing, servicing, alterations or additions to new and existing
refrigeration systems; provided, that this article shall not apply to
refrigerating systems in private passenger motor vehicles using refrigerants
designated as Group 1 Refrigerants in the American Standards Association Safety
Code for Mechanical Refrigeration, A.S.A. B9.1-1958, or the latest revision
thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 1.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 95-631, 4-18-95)
Sec. 5-447. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this article is to provide reasonable regulations and
safeguards for persons and property and to correct certain practices which are
inconsistent with public safety.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 1.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-448. - A.S.A. standard.
   All refrigerating systems shall be constructed, installed and maintained in
accordance with the provisions of the American Standards Association Safety
Code for Mechanical Refrigeration, A.S.A. B9.1-1958, or the latest revision
thereof, together with the rules adopted thereunder.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 1.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-449. - Regulations of other agencies not affected.
   Nothing herein contained shall be deemed to nullify or affect the federal or
state statutes or rules and regulations governing the storage and use of
flammable and explosive gases and chemicals, or the requirements of the
Interstate Commerce Commission or other statutes governing the transportation
and use of hazardous gases, explosive and other flammable substances.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 1.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-450. - Definitions.
   For the purposes of this article the following definitions shall apply:
   Additional definitions means the definitions as set forth in section 2 of
the American Standards Association Safety Code for Mechanical Refrigeration,
A.S.A. B9.1-1958, or the latest revision thereof, shall be applicable to and
made a part of this article by reference.
   Alter means the addition to or removal of any equipment or refrigerant in a
refrigerating system by which the refrigerant, refrigerant capacity,
refrigerating capacity, pressure allowed or location of any part of the system
is changed.
   Board means the mechanical refrigeration board created and established by
this article.
   City means the City of Dearborn, Wayne County, Michigan.
   Council means the City Council of the City of Dearborn.
   Department means the Department of Public Works and Facilities in the City
of Dearborn.
   Division means the Division of Building and Safety in the Department of
Public Works and Facilities in the City of Dearborn.
   Existing installation means and refers to a refrigerating system or a part
of a refrigerating system installed prior to the effective date of this
article.
   Major replacement means the replacement of a compressor, receiver,
condenser, heat exchanger, evaporation condenser and cooling tower which are
part of a refrigerating system or any such items, and any change of refrigerant
piping from original specification or installation in excess of one and one-
half inch nominal diameter and piping up to and including one and one-half inch
nominal diameter when more than a 20-foot run of such piping is replaced.
   Refrigerant is a substance used to produce refrigeration by its expansion or
vaporization.
   Refrigeration contractor means any person, firm, co-partnership, association
or corporation duly licensed by the city under the provisions of this article
to install, alter or service, or to contract to install, alter or service
refrigerating systems in the city.
   Refrigeration maintenance means and includes alteration, repair or
replacement of piping and fittings, compressors, condensers, evaporators,
receivers, generators, absorbers and controls of refrigerating systems.
   Refrigerating system means a combination of interconnected refrigerant-
containing parts constituting one closed refrigerant circuit in which a
refrigerant is circulated for the purpose of extracting heat.
   Superintendent means the Superintendent of the Division of Building and
Safety in the Department of Public Works and Facilities in the City of
Dearborn.
   Supervising employee means such person as is qualified by written and oral
examinations to act as an employee responsible for and in charge of all
installations, alterations, repairing or servicing of refrigerating systems in
the city by a firm, co-partnership, association or corporation licensed as a
refrigeration contractor by the city.
(Ord. No. 81-91, §§ 2.1-2.16, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
*** ARTICLE VIII. - MECHANICAL CODE ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-451. - Adopting code by reference.
   Inasmuch as MCL 117.3, MSA 5.2073(k) provides that each city shall have
power, whether so provided in its charter or not, to adopt by reference an
ordinance or any refrigeration code which has been promulgated by an
organization or association which is organized and conducted for the purpose of
developing such code; if such code is clearly identified in the adopting
ordinance and its purpose published with such ordinance; if printed copies
thereof are kept in the office of the city clerk available for inspection by
and distribution to the public at all times; if a complete copy of such code is
available for public use and inspection at the office of the city clerk; and if
the publication shall also contain a notice to that effect; therefore, notice
is hereby given that a complete copy of the 1996 International Mechanical Code
and 1997 Supplement thereto, is hereby adopted by reference in this article for
the purpose of furnishing material standards for construction, installation,
inspection and operation of refrigerating systems and equipment, and other
mechanical systems, and that such ordinance is available for public use and
inspection at the office of the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 11.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 97-703, 5-20-97)
Secs. 5-452—5-470. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - LICENSES **
Sec. 5-471. - Required.
   No person acting in the capacity of a refrigeration contractor, as governed
by the provisions of this article, shall install, construct, alter or service,
or contract to install, construct, alter or service any refrigerating system in
the city without first securing a refrigeration contractor's license therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-472. - Issuance.
   All licenses shall be issued by the city clerk to every applicant qualified
as authorized in this article, and upon the payment of the registration fee
listed in
Chapter 12, Section 6. A refrigeration contractor's license shall be issued
upon the approval of the board of safety engineers.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 5-473. - Examination papers to be filed.
   All written examination papers when submitted to the board shall become the
property of the city, and shall be kept on file in the department for a period
of not less than 60 days after the examination has been taken by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-474. - Time for holding examination.
   Examinations for a license under this article shall be held each month on
such day prescribed by the rules and regulations of the board, except when such
day is a holiday, in which case it shall be held on the following day on which
the city hall is open. Special sessions of the board may be called by the
director for the purpose of holding examinations when, in his discretion,
necessity may require it.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-475. - Application forms.
   Applications for a refrigeration contractor's license shall be made on blank
forms furnished for such purpose by the department. The application, which
shall be sworn to, shall, as a minimum, provide the following information:
      (1)   Name, age and residence address of applicant.
      (2)   If application is that of supervising employee, show name and
address of employer.
      (3)   Refrigeration experience of applicant; describe in detail.
      (4)   If applicant is a corporation:
         a.   Full and accurate corporation name.
         b.   When and where incorporated.
         c.   Full names and addresses of officers of corporation.
         d.   Name and refrigeration experience of officer or supervising
employee designated to take the examination for the corporation; describe
experience in detail.
      (5)   If applicant is a partnership:
         a.   Names and addresses of copartners and the name and refrigeration
experience of the partner or supervising employee designated to take the
examination for the partnership; describe such experience in detail.
      (6)   If the applicant conducts business under a trade or assumed name,
the following additional information shall be given:
         a.   Full trade name.
         b.   Name together with residence address of the person or persons
doing business under such trade or assumed name.
      (7)   Two references from former employers or persons having knowledge of
refrigerating experience.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-476. - Conduct of examination.
   The board shall determine, by written and oral examination and/or practical
demonstrations, the qualifications of an applicant. There shall be at least
three members of the board present at any examination of any applicant unless
otherwise changed by the board.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-477. - Examination required.
   No license shall be issued to an applicant until he has shown to the board
that he has been actively engaged in the installation or servicing, or both, of
refrigerating systems for a period of at least three years for Class A
applicants, four years for Class B applicants and five years for Class C
applicants; or has had in his regular employ and actively in charge a
supervising employee who has been previously engaged in the installation or
servicing of refrigerating systems for a period of at least three years for
Class A applicants, four years for Class B applicants and five years for Class
C applicants; provided that credit varying up to a maximum of three years of
such actual experience in the installation or servicing of refrigerating
systems shall be extended to any applicant who is a registered professional
engineer or who possesses at least a bachelor of science degree in mechanical
or chemical engineering, or who is a graduate of a refrigeration trade school.
In any event a minimum of two years of practical experience on actual
installations shall be required for all applicants. Also, the applicant shall
show the refrigerants and sizes of refrigerating systems with which he has
familiarized himself during his experience and education in the installation or
servicing, or both, of refrigerating systems. An applicant holding a master
warm air heating and air conditioning contractor's license, or a heating
engineer's license with the city or holding a Class "A" or "B" gas and/or oil
burner contractor's license of reciprocating municipalities, that are
recognized by the reciprocal heating council of this area, shall be examined by
the board for a Class "B" refrigeration license, or for a restricted
refrigeration contractor's license, the choice of examination and license to
rest with the applicant.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-478. - Age.
   All applicants for license shall have attained a minimum of 21 years of age.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-479. - Classification and limitation.
   (a)   A refrigeration contractor's license shall be classified and limited
as to definite refrigerants and size of refrigerating systems with which the
applicant is familiar in installing or servicing, and the applicant shall be
licensed for that particular refrigerant or refrigerants and size of systems;
provided, however, that any person if properly qualified, may make application
for and receive a license to engage in the installation and servicing of all
sizes of refrigerating systems involving any, or all, approved refrigerants.
   (b)   A contractor's license shall be classified as follows:
      (1)   Class "A" license shall be limited to the installation and
servicing of completely self-contained refrigerating units in domestic boxes
for private use in residential occupancies.
      (2)   Restricted license shall be limited to the installation of self-
contained refrigerating systems used for air conditioning for human comfort and
employing group one refrigerants, installed only in residential, commercial, or
industrial type occupancies, when actuated by motors or engines of not in
excess of 7½ horsepower. The holder of this class license may not service any
of the refrigerant-containing parts of the system.
      (3)   Class "B" license shall be limited to the installation and
servicing of refrigerating systems actuated by motors or engines of not in
excess of 7½ horsepower.
      (4)   Class "C" license shall govern the installation and servicing of
refrigerating systems unlimited as to horsepower and servicing.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-480. - List of contractors and supervising employees.
   A register or list of licensed refrigeration contractors and supervising
employees shall be maintained by the department, showing their respective names
and addresses, dates licenses issued, classification of licenses, and in case
of supervising employee, the name of employer and employment starting and
terminating dates of the supervising employee shall be shown.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-481. - Termination of services.
   Should the supervising employee's services terminate, the installation and
service operations of the employer shall cease within ten days after such
termination. It shall be unlawful for any person or employer to continue such
operations after the expiration of such ten-day period unless and until another
supervising employee has been registered on the list of supervising employees
in the office of the department. When the services of a supervising employee
have been terminated by an employer, the department shall be notified in
writing by both the employee and by the employer when such change takes place,
and the new supervising employee's name shall be forwarded by the employer and
entered on the register of supervising employees maintained by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-482. - Expiration and renewal.
   All refrigeration contractors' licenses shall expire at 12:00 midnight
following August 31 of the same year that the contractor's state license
expires, and shall be renewable within 60 days thereafter, or if renewed after
such date, an examination as to fitness may be required by the board in its
discretion.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.12, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 99-802, 12-21-99)
Sec. 5-483. - Revocation and suspension.
   (a)   No license shall be suspended or revoked except for cause upon proof
of charges filed with the department by the director or authorized inspector,
specifying with reasonable detail the facts on which such suspension is based.
Among the grounds for suspending or revoking any license issued under this
article are falsification of any material fact in the application for a
license, carelessness or negligence in the performance of the licensee's duties
in connection with his work, showing that such licensee has violated or
permitted a violation of this article, or that this article or any other
ordinance has been violated in connection with work for which the licensee was
responsible, or of which the licensee was aware, or in the exercise of
reasonable diligence, should have been aware that such violation occurred.
   (b)   Upon the filing of such charges, the director shall suspend the
license of the person involved, and shall give to such licensee notice of a
hearing upon such charges, which hearing shall be held by the board of
examiners not less than ten days after the date of such notice unless an
earlier date is agreed upon in writing by the licensee affected. Such notice
shall be by personal service, or certified mail, and shall state the time and
place of such hearing and shall contain a copy of the charges. If such charges
are sustained by the board, the director shall immediately revoke the license
involved, or the board may modify or alter the suspension of the license or
reinstate it and shall notify the licensee in writing of such finding.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-484. - Reciprocal clause.
   The city shall permit refrigeration contractors legally licensed by other
municipalities of the state to engage in the business of installing,
constructing, altering, repairing or servicing or contracting to install,
construct, alter, repair or service refrigerating equipment covered by this
article, parts or accessories thereof, or appurtenances thereto, within the
corporate limits of the city upon registering with the department, and the
payment of a prescribed registration fee; provided that such municipalities
reciprocate in recognizing refrigeration contractors and supervising employees
duly licensed under the provisions of this article by granting them the same
privileges and charging substantially the same license and registration fees.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-485. - Conditions of participation in reciprocal licenses.
   The licensing ordinance, examinations, and examination procedures of such
municipalities having a desire to participate in reciprocal licensing shall be
substantially similar to the requirements set forth in this article, and their
regulations governing the installation and maintenance of refrigerating systems
shall meet recognized standards acceptable to the board. No refrigeration
contractor's license shall be recognized for the purpose of registration by the
city which has been issued by a municipality which has failed to approve by
affirmative action of its legislative body, the reciprocal licensing provisions
similar to those contained in this article.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-486. - Right to participate in reciprocal licensing.
   The right of any licensee to have the benefit of the reciprocating
provisions of this division shall be determined by the board based upon the
qualifications outlined in this article.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-487. - Payment of personal property taxes.
   No license or renewal thereof shall be issued to any person under this
article, unless and until a certificate has been obtained from the city
treasurer to the effect that all personal property taxes levied and assessed
against such applicant for license have been paid in full.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 3.17, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-488—5-505. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - APPEALS **
Sec. 5-506. - Mechanical refrigeration board.
   A mechanical refrigeration board is hereby created and established
consisting of five members as follows:
   The director of the department of public works, the superintendent or an
inspector from the department designated by him, and three members appointed by
the mayor in accordance with the provisions of section 8.8 of the Charter, one
of whom shall hold a refrigeration contractor's license, one a first class
stationary engineer's license, and one a mechanical engineer's license, all of
whom shall be residents of the city.
   The chairman of the board shall be elected by the members and shall have the
right to vote. In his absence, the vice-chairman, who also shall be elected by
the board, shall act as chairman. Three members of the board shall constitute a
quorum and the concurring vote of at least three members shall be necessary to
take action by the board. The board shall prescribe its own rules and
regulations for carrying out its functions and duties as herein prescribed.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 4.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-507. - Compensation.
   Each member of the mechanical refrigeration board who is not working on a
full time salary with the city shall be paid such sum as the council of the
city may from time to time determine for each examination or board of appeals
session attended by such member; provided, however, that the member shall not
be paid for attending more than 12 meetings in any one calendar year.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 4.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-508. - Powers and duties of the board.
   The powers and duties of the board shall be:
      (1)   Determine by examination as herein prescribed the qualifications
and ability of an applicant for a license. Such examination shall consist of
oral, written and practical tests and shall cover the theory and practice of
cooling, refrigeration, engineering and the interpretation of charts,
blueprints and plans for installations, repairing or alterations. The board
shall file with the department a written report of its findings and
recommendations in each case.
      (2)   Where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the
provisions of this article will result in unnecessary hardship or involve
practical difficulties, the board shall have power upon appeal in specific
cases to authorize such variation or deviation from the terms of this article
as will not be contrary to the public interest, in order that the spirit of
this article shall be observed, public safety secured and substantial justice
done.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 4.3(a, b), 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-509. - Right of appeal.
   (a)   Any person aggrieved by any decision, ruling or order of the director
may take an appeal to the building board of appeals, which board is hereby
empowered and authorized to hear and consider such appeal. Such appeal shall be
taken within ten days after the decision, ruling or order complained of by
filing with the director a notice of appeal directed to the board, specifying
the grounds thereof and the relief prayed for. The director shall forthwith
transmit to the board all papers constituting the record upon which the
decision, ruling or order appealed from has been taken.
   (b)   The board shall adopt appropriate rules giving a reasonable time for
hearing of the appeal which shall provide for giving due notice thereof by
ordinary mail to the parties in interest at their last known addresses. The
board shall decide the appealed question within a reasonable time. Except in
cases of emergency, such appeal shall act as a stay of any construction,
installation, alteration, repairing, ruling or order until either approved,
modified, or set aside by the board.
   (c)   A fee, as specified in section
5-534, shall be paid to the city treasurer at the time the appeal is filed, and
if paid by check or money order, it shall be made payable to the city
treasurer. The board, upon hearing such appeal, shall either affirm, modify or
set aside any such decision, ruling or order.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 4.3(c, d), 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-510—5-525. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 4. - PERMITS AND FEES **
Sec. 5-526. - Required.
   No person shall install, construct, alter or make replacements of receivers,
condensers, evaporator condensers, cooling towers, compressors, piping, or any
change in piping from the original specifications or existing installation in
any part of a refrigerating system except as herein provided until such person
has filed an application with the department and received a permit for the work
specifically intended on each individual system, except as exempted from this
requirement in sectiion 5-527; provided that in cases of emergency the permit
shall be obtained within 72 hours from the time that the installation,
alteration or major replacement was started.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-527. - Exceptions.
   Permits will not be required for the installation, alteration or major
replacement of completely self-contained refrigerating units containing ten
pounds or less of refrigerant in domestic boxes used for the purpose of
preserving food, groceries and/or beverages in residential occupancies, nor for
the installation of units on commercial and privately owned vehicles used on
public thoroughfares for the purpose of producing refrigeration for trucks,
trailers, buses and similar conveyances, provided that such unit systems and/or
units and systems comply with all other requirements of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-528. - Applications for permit.
   Permit applications shall be made on forms provided by the department and
shall contain information deemed pertinent by the department for the proper
description and completion of the work intended except as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-529. - Ventilating or air circulating systems.
   Ventilating or air circulating systems to be used in conjunction with
refrigerating systems shall not be installed, or any alteration made, governed
by the installation provisions of this article relating to the safety of the
refrigeration system, without a permit issued by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-530. - Blueprints required.
   Blueprints or suitable sketches shall be submitted for all refrigerating
systems installed, except unit or other systems for which pertinent ordinance
requirements can be shown on the application for permits.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-531. - Details on blueprints.
   Blueprints shall be made in duplicate, shall be drawn to a workable scale
and shall show all pertinent data relating to the installation, such as
construction and location of machinery room and method of its ventilation; size
and location of piping, valves, fittings and safety devices; volume of rooms
where applicable to this article; location of ducts and plenum chambers and
protective devices appertaining thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-532. - Failure to obtain permit.
   All refrigerating systems installed, constructed or altered, or on which a
major replacement was made within the city without a permit having first been
obtained, as required in this division, shall constitute a violation of this
article. A written notice shall be given to the contractor and owner of the
refrigerating system of such condition, and, upon posting on the premises of a
stop work order, such refrigerating system, or part thereof, shall not
thereafter be operated until a permit is issued, an inspection made and
approval is granted by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-533. - Sale and purchase of refrigerants.
   The sale or purchase of gasses or liquids which are intended for use as
refrigerants, governed by this article in the city, shall not be made other
than from distributors, jobbers or manufacturers and by licensed refrigeration
contractors or persons having a permit from the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-534. - Fees for permits, licenses.
   The fees for permits and licenses under this article shall be as follows:
      (1)   Permit fee for the installation or alteration of each refrigerating
system or compressor unit.
         a.   Five horsepower or less, inclusive ..... $ 5.00
         b.   Six horsepower to 50 horsepower, inclusive ..... 10.00
         c.   Horsepower over 50 ..... 20.00
      (2)   Annual inspection fee, each refrigerating system or compressor
unit, except where annual maintenance permit is issued under the provisions of
the building code ..... 5.00
      (3)   Special inspection fee, each unit or system in the field ..... 5.00
      (4)   Original refrigeration contractor's license ..... 25.00
      (5)   Renewal contractor's license ..... 25.00
      (6)   Each registration under reciprocal provisions ..... 10.00
      (7)   Written examinations ..... 5.00
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-535. - Fees not to be refunded.
   Any and all monies paid as fees for permit or licenses issued under this
article shall be retained by the city treasurer, and no refund shall be made if
such permit or license has been granted and is later revoked, or is denied
unless there has been an error made by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-536. - Inspection license required.
   No person shall use or cause to be used any refrigerating system or
compressor unit which is subject to annual inspection under the provisions of
this article without first securing a license for such use from the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-537. - Annual inspection license.
   An inspection license shall be renewed annually for each refrigeration
system or compressor unit subject to annual inspections under the provisions of
this article.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 5.12, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-538—5-555. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - SYSTEM CLASSIFICATION **
Sec. 5-556. - Classes enumerated.
   (a)   Refrigerating systems or compressor units, other than multiple
domestic systems, shall be classified as follows, depending on the horsepower:
      (1)   Class A—Five horsepower or less, inclusive.
      (2)   Class B—Six to 50 horsepower, inclusive.
      (3)   Class C—Over 50 horsepower, inclusive.
   (b)   Buildings equipped with multiple domestic systems shall be classified
as follows, depending on the number of apartments:
      (1)   Class D—Systems serving ten apartments or less, inclusive.
      (2)   Class E—Systems serving 11 to 20 apartments, inclusive.
      (3)   Class F—Systems serving 21 to 30 apartments, inclusive.
      (4)   Class G—Systems serving 31 or more apartments.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 6.1, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-557—5-575. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 6. - ACCIDENTS **
Sec. 5-576. - Notification of accident by licensee.
   The holder of any license under this article knowing of an accident in which
there was personal injury or property damage shall immediately notify the
department of every such accident.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 7.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-577. - Unlawful to use system following accident.
   Where an accident involves damage to any part of a refrigeration system, or
in which there was a personal injury or property damage, it shall be unlawful
to use such refrigerating system until after an investigation is made and
approval for continued use is granted by a representative of the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 7.2, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-578—5-595. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 7. - INSPECTION AND ENFORCEMENT **
Sec. 5-596. - Right of entry.
   The director and his authorized agents shall have the authority during
reasonable hours to enter any building, structure or premises within the city
without hindrance for the purpose of examining equipment licensed under this
article and enforcing the provisions covered thereby.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-597. - Inspections required.
   It shall be the duty of the director and his authorized agents to inspect
all refrigerating systems within the city, except as hereinafter otherwise
provided.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-598. - Qualifications for refrigeration inspector.
   In addition to passing a civil service examination, the applicant for a
position as an inspector must have a heating, air conditioning and
refrigeration license with the city and have at least five years' experience
with refrigeration and air conditioning installations.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-599. - Inspection of equipment.
   (a)   The director or his authorized agents shall make an inspection of all
refrigerating systems or repairs or alterations thereto at the time of
installation where such installation, repair or alteration requires a permit
under this article.
   (b)   All refrigerating equipment and refrigerating systems installed must
comply with the manufacturer's instructions and be in accordance with this
article to the approval of the inspector. The director or inspector may
require:
      (1)   Additional precautionary measures where necessary to prolong the
life endurance of the equipment.
      (2)   The installation of a drier (in the liquid line) or a drier
replaced that has been exposed to air or moisture.
      (3)   A system vacuumed after pressure test and before charging.
      (4)   Vibration eliminators installed in the suction line or hot gas
line.
      (5)   Any other requirement that may be considered necessary during the
installation of refrigerating equipment or within a reasonable length of time
thereafter to safeguard the public.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-600. - Power to test and inspect.
   The director or his authorized agents are hereby empowered to make or cause
to be made such tests and inspections as are deemed necessary for the purpose
of the enforcement of this article with reference to the public health and
safety to ascertain the condition of the piping, tubing, fittings, apparatus
and machinery used in any refrigerating system.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-601. - Reports of inspectors.
   The inspectors of the department shall make a written report of each
inspection made under this article and file same in the records of the
department. When requested, a copy of such report shall be mailed to the owner
or holder of the licensed equipment.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-602. - Equipment found unsafe.
   If, upon annual or special inspection of equipment covered by this article,
such equipment should be found in an unsafe condition, the department shall
thereupon serve a written notice of the findings upon the owner or person in
charge of such equipment, stating a time when recommended repairs must be
completed, except that where the work or repairs required is in the nature of
an emergency, the neglect of which would endanger human life or the public
safety, such work or repairs may be ordered to be done forthwith, and the
equipment shall be sealed out of service until such work or repairs are
completed. After the service of such notice, it shall be the duty of the person
receiving such notice to proceed within the time allowed to make such repairs
or changes as are necessary to place such equipment in a safe condition. It
shall be unlawful to operate such equipment after the date stated in such
notice, unless an extension of time, in writing, has been obtained from the
department until such repairs or changes have been made and the equipment
accepted by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-603. - Power to put equipment out of service.
   The director shall have the power to close down and seal out of service any
refrigerating equipment for the following reasons:
      (1)   For failure to secure a license or to renew such license, after the
lapse of a 72-hour warning period.
      (2)   When in case of emergency, in the opinion of the director or his
authorized agent, any equipment governed by this article is in such condition
as to render it unsafe for operation.
      (3)   For willful failure to comply with orders issued by the department
for the correction of violations.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-604. - Notice of sealing out of service.
   Before sealing any refrigeration equipment out of service, the department
shall serve written notice upon the owner or person in charge of such
equipment, stating its intention to seal the equipment out of service and the
reasons therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-605. - Unlawful to remove seal.
   Any refrigeration equipment sealed out of service by the department shall be
plainly marked with a sign or tag indicating such fact and setting forth the
reason for such sealing, and any defacing or removal of such sign or tag, or
any tampering with or removal of such seal without the approval of the
department shall constitute a violation of this article, and any person found
guilty of such violation shall be subject to penalties.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 8.9, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-606—5-620. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 8. - INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS **
Sec. 5-621. - Application of division.
   In addition to the requirements, as provided in the American Standards
Association Safety Code for Mechanical Refrigeration A.S.A. B9.1-1958 adopted
by and incorporated into this article, the requirements as provided in the
following sections of this division shall also apply.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-622. - Soldered joints on copper tubing.
   All joints soldered (brazed in accordance with A.S.A. B-9 Code) on copper
tubing in the field or on the job on remote and other refrigerating systems
shall be fabricated with alloys having melting points of not less than 1,000
degrees Fahrenheit, except for servicing of approved self-contained units
containing six pounds or less of group one refrigerants and when approved by
the inspector or board.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-623. - Check valves.
   A discharge check valve shall be provided in the discharge line from each
compressor used on a refrigerating system containing more than 40 pounds of a
Group 2 or Group 3 refrigerant.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-624. - Equipment not covered by code.
   Upon recommendation by the department inspector and approved by the board,
the director may approve the use of any approved equipment design, material,
construction or device not specifically covered by this article but consistent
therewith.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-625. - Concealed equipment.
