   Soft annealed copper tubing which is concealed shall be encased in rigid
conduit, except that such tubing completely buried in concrete may be encased
in flexible conduit. Hard copper tubing which is buried underground or under
the lowest floor of a building shall be encased in rigid conduit. Hard copper
tubing which is completely buried in concrete shall be encased in either rigid
or flexible conduit. Permanent inspection openings shall be provided in the
covering of concealed tubing joints. It shall be unlawful for owners,
contractors or workmen to lath over or in any way conceal any piping, outlet
boxes or other part of a refrigerating system until an inspection has been made
thereof and due notice given that the work has been passed upon by the
department. In case any obstruction has been placed so as to conceal any piping
or part of the installation before the department has made an inspection
thereof, the department may remove or cause to be removed any such lath or
obstruction, which may conceal the work so that proper inspection may be made.
Under urgent conditions, upon proper notification, it shall be the duty of the
department to make a proper inspection within 72 hours from the time it is
notified.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-626. - Certificate of approval.
   When any work, whether construction, installation, alteration or major
replacement, for which a permit is required under the provisions of this
article, has been completed to the satisfaction of the department, there shall
be issued a certificate of approval certifying that the installation is in
accordance with the provisions of this article and that the refrigerating
system may be operated. Such certificate shall be posted in a conspicuous place
in the proximity of the compressor.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-627. - Other refrigerant.
   No refrigerating system shall be maintained or operated employing a
refrigerant other than what is specified in this article without a permit
issued by the department, upon such conditions consistent with the provisions
of this article as are deemed necessary in the interest of public safety by the
director.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-628. - Charging or removing refrigerants.
   Charging a system with a refrigerant or removing same therefrom shall be
done by a licensed refrigeration contractor or a supervising employee or other
authorized employee, provided that in case of fire or emergency, the system may
be discharged by the fire department.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-629. - Existing installations.
   If in good repair, existing installations may be continued in their present
form, provided that such installations conform basically to approved standards
and present no apparent hazards through methods of installation or operation.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-630. - Installation in residential zones.
   Refrigerating systems, or window or wall type refrigerating air
conditioners, installed in residential zones shall not protrude the exterior of
a building when such building is located less than ten feet from the lot line
and/or less than 20 feet from the nearest adjoining building, unless permission
is granted by the board.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 9.10, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-631—5-645. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 9. - WATER SAVING EQUIPMENT **
Sec. 5-646. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Primary water shall mean city water supplied by the makeup line to the
makeup float of a cooling tower or evaporative condenser.
   Secondary water shall mean water recirculated from the tower to the air
conditioner and back to the tower.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 10.2, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-647. - Subject to city provisions.
   (a)   All water saving equipment, including cooling towers, evaporative
condensers and air-cooled condensers, erected in the city shall be installed in
accordance with all applicable city ordinances and codes, including the
building, plumbing and electrical codes and the zoning ordinance.
   (b)   All water piping and drainage shall be installed in accordance with
the provisions of the plumbing code of the city.
   (c)   All electrical wiring and equipment shall be installed in accordance
with the provisions of the electrical code of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-91, §§ 10.1, 10.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-648. - Refrigeration contractor's permit.
   The refrigeration contractor may install all refrigeration equipment
including secondary water piping as a part of his original permit.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 10.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-649. - Color coding.
   All primary and secondary water piping shall be identified by color coding;
provided, however, that at least one foot of every 30 feet in each room of
primary water piping shall be painted blue, and at least one foot in every 30
feet in each room of secondary water piping shall be painted brown; provided,
further, that if the city inspector believes that more of any such piping
should be painted, he is hereby authorized to require such additional coloring
to be installed in any such case.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 10.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-650. - Permit.
   A licensed refrigeration contractor shall obtain a permit in accordance with
the provisions of this article and all other applicable ordinances and codes of
the city whenever any structure as a part of a refrigeration system including
air conditioning equipment is being installed.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 10.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-651. - Plans and specifications.
   (a)   A mechanical pencil or line sketch shall be furnished for all
refrigeration systems up to and including 40 tons capacity. Such sketch shall
show among other things the kinds of piping and the location of the cooling
tower.
   (b)   Detailed structural and mechanical plans and specifications shall be
furnished for all refrigeration systems in excess of 40 tons capacity, which
plans and specifications shall be signed and sealed either by an architect
registered under the laws of the state, or by a civil or structural engineer so
registered.
   (c)   Such detailed plans and specifications shall show:
      (1)   Details of water saving equipment and how it should be erected and
supported.
      (2)   Location on the roof, or elsewhere if it is to be installed on or
above the ground level.
      (3)   The location and size of all primary and secondary piping.
      (4)   The electrical wiring in detail to the tower fan and pump.
      (5)   A sworn statement that they were prepared by or under the personal
supervision of such architect or engineer.
   (d)   All such sketches, plans and specifications shall be approved by the
department of building and safety before any permit therefor shall be issued.
(Ord. No. 81-91, § 10.5, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-652—5-669. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE IX. - HEATING CODE ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-670. - Code adopted.
   There is hereby adopted by reference the BOCA National Heating Code, Seventh
Edition, 1990. A copy of which shall be available in the office of the city
clerk.
Sec. 5-671. - Scope.
   This article shall establish minimum standards for, relate to and regulate
the construction, installation, replacement, repair or alteration in any and
all buildings or structures within the city of any piping, apparatus,
equipment, appliances, devices or accessories for steam, vapor, hot water, warm
air or any other type of heating systems, air conditioning plants, ventilation
systems, boilers, steam pressure vessels and boiler burner units, including
apparatus, equipment and piping for the generation and conveyance of steam for
any purpose up to 15 pounds per square inch pressure, the purpose and intent of
this article being to protect life and property from fire, to safeguard against
possible asphyxiation of persons and to protect them from injury by explosions
from either gas, steam or excessive water pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 1.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-672. - Unfired pressure vessels excepted.
   Unfired pressure vessels, such as those containing compressed air or
refrigerants used in commercial refrigerating systems or similar vessels, are
not included within the terms and meaning of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 1.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-673. - Definition.
   For the purposes of this article, the word "contractor," either unlimited or
limited, shall mean any person maintaining a business establishment and holding
himself out to the public as engaged in, having direct charge of and skilled in
the planning, laying out and superintending the installation, alteration,
replacement or repair of any heating, steamfitting, warm air furnace, air
conditioning, oil burner, gas burner or stoker system requiring a permit under
this article from the department in the city, and is familiar with the laws,
rules and regulations governing the same.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 1.10, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-674—5-690. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - LICENSES **
Sec. 5-691. - Required; examination, reexamination.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in or work at the business or
trade of installing, replacing, altering or repairing any heating, ventilating
or air conditioning equipment or system in the city until he has first been
licensed to carry on such work, as provided for in this article. Every
applicant for a license shall have attained a minimum of 21 years of age and
shall, before such license is issued, pay the required examination fee to the
city treasurer and pass an examination given by the board of examiners as
provided in this article showing his ability and qualifications. Anyone failing
to pass such examination may apply again after a period of 30 days has elapsed
by paying the required fee to the city treasurer and taking the examination
above referred to, which procedure may be repeated by such person as many times
as he desires. When an applicant for a given classification has passed the
required examination prescribed by the board, the department shall certify such
fact to the city clerk and, upn the payment of the registration fee listed in
Chapter 12, Section 6, the city clerk shall issue the particular license
specified by the department to which such applicant is entitled.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 5-692. - Application.
   Every person desiring to be licensed under any of the classifications of
this division shall file with the secretary of the board of safety engineers an
application on forms to be furnished for such purpose by the department. The
application in affidavit form shall contain, in addition to other requirements,
the following:
      (1)   Name, age, business and home address of applicant.
      (2)   Qualifications of applicant.
      (3)   If applicant is a corporation:
         a.   Full and accurate corporation name.
         b.   When and where incorporated.
         c.   Full names and business and home addresses of officers of
corporation.
         d.   Name and qualifications of officer or supervisory employee
designated to take the examination for the corporation.
      (4)   If applicant is a partnership, the names and addresses of members
thereof and the name and qualifications of the partner or supervisory employee
designated to take the examination for the partnership.
      (5)   If applicant conducts business under a trade or assumed name:
         a.   Complete and full name and date of registration with county
clerk.
         b.   The name of person or persons doing business under such trade or
assumed name.
         c.   The name and qualifications of the individual or supervisory
employee who is to take the examination.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-693. - Performance of work restricted.
   No person shall install, alter, replace or repair heating, air conditioning,
oil burner, gas burner or stoker equipment, as required by this article, unless
he is licensed to do so under this division or unless a licensed heating
contractor is in charge.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-694. - Classification, limitation.
   Licenses required by this article shall be classified as follows and subject
to the limitations set forth:
      (1)   Class A gas. Listed gas designed sectional boilers having inputs of
not more than 1,000,000 B.T.U. per hour, utilizing a thermocoupletype safeguard
designed to shut off the main gas supply at not more than 75 seconds after
pilot flame failure, and all other gas fired equipment and appurtenances
limited to input ratings of less than 400,000 B.T.U. per unit.
      (2)   Class B gas. Gas fired equipment and appurtenances with all input
ratings (unlimited).
      (3)   Class A oil. Oil fired equipment and appurtenances designed for the
use of No. 1 or No. 2 fuel oils, as defined in U.S. Department of Commerce,
Commercial Standard CS 12-48, or latest revision thereof, having a maximum
firing rate of less than five gallons per hour.
      (4)   Class B oil. Oil fired equipment and appurtenances unlimited as to
size or capacity and designed for any grade of fuel oil.
      (5)   Fuel oil storage tanks only, but not including burner or burners.
      (6)   Space heating: 
         a.   Warm air. The installation and/or alteration of warm air
distribution systems.
         b.   Steam and hot water. The installation and/or alteration of steam
and hot water distribution systems.
         c.   Electrical heating. The design and installation of space boilers,
warm air furnaces and distribution systems therein, using electricity as the
only source of fuel. No work of installation, alteration or servicing of the
electrical element component shall be done, except by persons licensed in
accordance with article XII of this chapter.
      (7)   Coal fired equipment: 
         a.   Class A coal fired equipment, limited to input equivalent of
400,000 B.T.U. capacity per hour, per unit.
         b.   Class B coal fired equipment, with unlimited capacity.
      (8)   Sheet metal work only. The installation and/or alteration of all
types of sheet metal for all purposes.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-695. - Issuance, insurance; refusal.
   (a)   Upon receipt by the department of the report of the board of
examiners, if such report recommends the granting of a license, the director
shall immediately certify to the city clerk that the applicant is entitled to a
license of the classification recommended, and the clerk shall thereupon issue
such a license.
   (b)   If the report from the board of examiners recommends a refusal to
issue a license, the director shall immediately notify the applicant in writing
of such refusal.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-696. - Insurance required for permits.
   Before a permit will issue for the repair, alteration or installation of any
heating, ventilating or air conditioning systems in the city, the permittee
shall file with the city clerk a certificate of insurance, or evidence of
insurance, issued by an insurance company authorized to do business in this
state insuring such permittee against claims for loss, injury or damage to
persons and property by reason of installation of any equipment being installed
by such permittee, all of which insurance shall cover public liability damage
for amounts of $10,000.00 for each person, $20,000.00 for each accident and
$10,000.00 property damage per accident. Every such certificate of insurance,
as above specified, shall contain a provision that before such insurance is
cancelled, a notice shall be given by the insurer to the city clerk of the
insurer's intention to cancel such policy not less than ten days after the
receipt of such notice.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-697. - Registration.
   Upon issuance of any license under this division, the name, business address
and classification of the licensee shall be entered on a register kept for that
purpose in the office of the city clerk, and such register shall be open for
public inspection at all reasonable hours.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-698. - Term of license.
   All licenses issued under this article shall expire at 12:00 midnight on
December 31 of each year and shall be renewable within 60 days thereafter.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-699. - Suspension or revocation of license.
   No license issued under this division shall be revoked except for cause upon
proof of charges filed with the department by the inspector, specifying with
reasonable detail the facts showing carelessness or negligence in the
performance of the licensee's duties in connection with his work, showing that
such licensee has violated or permitted a violation of this article, or that
this article has been violated in connection with work for which the licensee
was responsible and of which the licensee was aware or in the exercise of
reasonable diligence should have been aware that such violation had occurred.
Upon the filing of such charges, the director shall forthwith suspend the
license involved, and shall give to such licensee notice of a hearing upon such
charges, which hearing shall be held by the board of appeals not less than ten
days after the date of such notice unless an earlier date is agreed upon in
writing by the licensee affected. Such notice shall be by personal service or
registered mail and shall state the time and place of such hearing and shall
contain a copy of the charges. If such charges are sustained by the board of
appeals, the director shall immediately revoke the license involved and shall
notify the licensee in writing of such revocation.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-700. - Unlawful use of licenses.
   No person having procured a license under this division shall permit or
allow the use of his name by any other person, directly or indirectly, for the
purpose of obtaining a permit to do any installation, alteration, replacement
or repair of heating, air conditioning, ventilating, oil burner, gas burner or
stoker equipment in the city.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-701. - Unlawful display of signs.
   No person other than a licensed contractor shall engage in the business of
installing, altering, replacing or repairing heating, air conditioning,
ventilating, gas burner, oil burner or stoker equipment in the city, and no
person shall expose the sign of such licensed contractor or make any
advertisement pertaining thereto unless he shall have been first duly licensed
in accordance with the provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-702. - Termination of services of supervisory employee.
   Should the qualified supervisory employee's services terminate, the
installation and service operations of the employer shall cease, and it shall
be unlawful to continue such operations until another supervisory employee is
certified for the employer by the board of examiners, provided that a ten-day
period may be allowed for the employer, with the approval of the examining
board, to replace him by a qualified supervisory employee. The department shall
be notified in writing by both the employee and the employer when such change
takes place, and the new supervisory employee's name shall be entered on the
current license and application.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-703. - Reciprocal licenses.
   The city shall permit contractors engaged in the business of installing,
altering, repairing, servicing or contracting to install, alter, repair or
service heating, air conditioning, ventilating, oil burner, gas burner or
stoker equipment who are legally licensed by other municipalities of the state
to engage in the business of installing, altering, repairing or servicing or
contracting to install, alter, repair or service heating, air conditioning,
ventilating, oil burner, gas burner or stoker equipment within the corporate
limits of this city upon registration with the department and the payment of
the registration fee; provided that the municipality in which such contractors
are licensed reciprocates in recognizing contractors duly licensed under the
provisions of this division by granting them the same privileges and charging
the same license and registration fees; provided further, that the licensing,
ordinance, examination and examination procedures of such municipalities having
a desire to participate in reciprocal licensing shall be substantially equal to
the requirements set forth in this article, and their regulations governing the
installation, alteration, repairing and servicing of heating, air conditioning,
ventilating, oil burner, gas burner or stoker equipment shall meet recognized
standards acceptable to the department. No contractor's license shall be
recognized for the purpose of registration by the city which has been issued by
a municipality which has failed to approve by affirmative action of its
legislative body the reciprocal licensing provisions contained in this article.
A contractor shall obtain his license in the municipality wherein such
contractor maintains his principal place of business.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.21, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-704—5-720. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - BOARD OF SAFETY ENGINEERS **
Sec. 5-721. - Compensation.
   Each member of the board of safety engineers, excepting the director and the
inspector, shall receive such compensation as shall be fixed and determined by
proper resolution of the city council for each examination or board of appeals
session attended by such member; provided, however, that such member shall not
be paid for attending more than 12 sessions in any one calendar year.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-722. - Quorum.
   Four members of the board of safety engineers shall constitute a quorum to
conduct any examination or to transact any business of the board.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-723. - Rules and regulations.
   The board of safety engineers shall have the power to make all necessary and
reasonable rules and regulations setting up standards as to qualifications of
applicants and for the conducting of examinations.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-724. - Duties.
   The duties of the board of safety engineers shall be to determine by
examination of such a kind as it may require, the qualifications and ability of
applicants for licenses. Such examinations shall consist of oral, written and
practical tests and shall cover the theory and practice of heating construction
and engineering and the interpretation of charts, blueprints and plans for
heating installations. The board shall file with the department a written
report of its findings and recommendations in each case. 
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-725. - Examination papers to be filed.
   All examinations and examination papers shall be open to persons holding
licenses of the classification for which the examination is being held, and all
written examination papers shall be kept on file in the department for a period
of not less than 60 days after the examination has been taken by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-726. - Time for holding examination.
   Examinations for a license under this division shall be held on the second
Friday of each month except when such Friday is a holiday, in which case it
shall be held on the following Monday. No sessions of the board of examiners
shall be held unless there are at least two applicants for examination. Special
sessions of the board of examiners may be called by the director when in his
discretion necessity may require it.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.9, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-727—5-745. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 4. - FEES **
Sec. 5-746. - Enumerated.
   The fees for examinations, licenses and registrations under this article
shall be as follows:
 
 Fee
 
      (1)   Examination or reexamination ..... $ 5.00
      (2)   Contractor's license ..... 25.00
      (3)   Contractor's license registration ..... 10.00
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-747. - Renewal.
   The renewal fees for all licenses and registrations under this article shall
be the same as the original license or registration fees provided for in
section
5-746.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 2.19, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-748—5-765. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - BOARD OF APPEALS **
Sec. 5-766. - Creation.
   There is hereby created a board of appeals, referred to in this division as
the board, which shall consist of the chairman of the board of examiners,
referred to in division 3 of this article, the chief of the fire department,
the corporation counsel, the director of building and safety and a heating
inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 3.1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-767. - Organization.
   The director of building and safety shall be the chairman of the board and
shall preside at all meetings thereof; if at any time the chairman is not
present at any meeting of the board, if a quorum is present, such board shall
appoint a temporary chairman to act in their place. The director shall appoint
as permanent secretary to the board a qualified person from the department who
shall keep a record of all the minutes and proceedings of the board and be in
attendance at all of its meetings in so far as it is possible, send out any
necessary notices and perform such other duties as the board may delegate to
him.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 3.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Sec. 5-768. - Powers and duties.
   The board is hereby authorized and empowered:
      (1)   When it is impossible for a licensee under this article or an owner
to obtain the material specified for use in this article because of any
national emergency, or when it is undesirable to use the materials specified
because of improvements or new discoveries made, or when it is impractical or
undesirable for a licensee to follow the method of procedure prescribed by this
article, the board in its discretion may approve any material proposed as a
substitute for those mentioned in this article, or may in its discretion,
approve any method of procedure as a substitute for that herein prescribed, and
when such approval is given it shall have the force and effect of law.
      (2)   To hear and conduct appeals from rulings or decisions of the
inspector as specified in this article.
      (3)   To conduct investigations on any matters pertaining to the
effective operation and application of this article to the various matters
covered thereby.
      (4)   To make findings that shall be conclusive on all questions of fact,
whether arising from such investigations, appeals or otherwise.
      (5)   To make rules and regulations for carrying out the provisions of
this division.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 3.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-769. - Procedure on appeal.
   If any person desires to appeal to the board from any decision or ruling of
the inspector on any matter under this article, such appeal shall be made in
writing and filed with the secretary of the board. Where giving notice of
hearing on an appeal is not otherwise provided for in this article, the
secretary of the board shall give such notice to all the interested parties at
least ten days before the date of such hearing, either by personal service or
registered mail, and the hearing shall be held at such time and place in the
city as shall be therein stated. Proof of service of giving such notice shall
be made and filed with the board prior to the hearing.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 3.4, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-770—5-785. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 6. - INSPECTOR **
Sec. 5-786. - Qualifications.
   In addition to the qualifications specified by the civil service rules of
the city for the classification of inspector, every person to be qualified for
such position under this article shall carry an unlimited journeyman's license,
issued under the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-787. - Supervision of work.
   All construction, installation, alteration, replacement and repair work
within the city involving heating, ventilating, refrigeration and air
conditioning plants and equipment, subject to regulation by the provisions of
this article, in and for buildings of all classes shall be done under the
supervision and subject to the inspection and approval of the inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-788. - Enforcement; removal of construction.
   It shall be the duty of the inspector and his regularly authorized assistant
to enforce or cause to be enforced the provisions of this article; to supervise
all necessary tests and to make all necessary inspection of heating,
ventilating or air conditioning plants and equipment installed under this
article; to require such tests to be made as may be necessary to determine the
tightness and safety of any steam or hot water heating installation, or repair
or replacement of any portion thereof, or of any sheet metal ducts or heating
pipes connected therewith, or of oil or gas piping and equipment; and to
require the immediate removal of any material or construction found to have
been installed so as to conceal or cover up before its inspection and approval
by the inspector any newly installed portion of any heating, ventilating or air
conditioning system or plant.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-789. - Authority to stop construction.
   If the inspector or his assistant at any time discover that any work is
being done on any building or structures in the city, contrary to the
provisions of this article, such inspector or his assistant is hereby
authorized and directed to issue a stop work order as to such illegal or
improper construction, and to post a notice thereof on such improper work, and
if such work is being carried on contrary to the provisions of this article,
the person doing or performing such work shall be subject to prosecution for
such violation under the terms hereof, it being hereby intended that such stop
work order shall not in any way exonerate the wrongdoer from his criminal
responsibility under this section. After a stop work order has been issued, it
shall be unlawful for any work to be done by the person on the job until the
illegal or improper construction has been corrected and the stop work order
removed by the inspector or his assistant. It shall be unlawful for any person,
other than the inspector or his assistant, to remove such stop work notice
posted as provided in this section.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-790. - Determination of rating.
   The inspector shall determine the rating or capacity of any second-hand
boiler, furnace or device which is no longer manufactured, which is to be used
in connection with any heating or airconditioning system or plant, and for
which the above required test data, measurements, rating or capacity are not
available, as required by this article.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-791. - Request for inspection; concealment restricted.
   The heating, ventilating, refrigerating and air conditioning contractor
shall immediately notify the inspector upon the completion of the installation
or other work under this article that the work for which a permit had been
issued is ready for inspection and test in the case of a steam, hot water,
ventilating or air conditioning installation, or for inspection in the case of
warm air, oil burner, gas burner or stoker installation or other work under
this article, by registering the number of the permit and the address at which
is located the work to be inspected in the inspection register kept for that
purpose in the office of the department. It shall be unlawful for any
contractor, owner or his employees to cover up any work for which a permit has
been issued under this article until after such work has been inspected or
tested, or both.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 4.6, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-792—5-810. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 7. - PERMITS **
Sec. 5-811. - Required, application; exceptions.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to construct, install, alter,
replace or repair any heating, ventilating or air conditioning plant or
equipment, oil burner, gas burner or stoker, or to begin such work, which is
subject to regulation by the provisions of this article, in or for any building
in the city without first having a permit issued therefor. Applications for
such permit shall be made in writing by such person and a permit issued
pursuant thereto by the department prior to beginning any work governed by the
provisions of this article. It shall be unlawful to fail or neglect to comply
with such provisions or of the permit issued pursuant thereto.
   (b)   Any person, when applying for any such permit, shall, upon demand of
the inspector, furnish all necessary plans in duplicate for such proposed
construction, installation, alteration, replacement or repair and use, all
proper and sufficient information relating thereto, and shall secure the
inspector's approval of such plans before such permit shall be issued.
   (c)   The department may waive the above requirement of a permit in the case
of alterations, replacements or repairs, anything in this article to the
contrary notwithstanding, to any existing heating, ventilating, air
conditioning plant or equipment where the estimated cost of such alteration,
replacement or repair, both as to labor and material, will not exceed $50.00,
if such alteration, replacement or repairs will not add to the required
capacity of such heating, ventilating or air conditioning plant or equipment
and will not, in the opinion of the inspector, be of such a nature as to render
an inspection of same necessary. No permit shall be required for repair,
replacement or alteration of any existing gravity warm air heating system, the
cost of which both as to material and labor shall not exceed $25.00.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-812. - Test data, measurements, ratings, capacities.
   Before a permit shall be issued by the department for the installation,
alteration, replacement or repair of any steam or hot water boiler, warm air
furnace or any device performing some specific service in connection with any
heating, ventilating or air conditioning system or plant, the capacity of which
device might affect in whole or in part the efficiency of the system or plant,
or produce a dangerous condition on the premises, the contractor installing,
altering, replacing or repairing such boiler, furnace or device or the
manufacturer of same, shall furnish the inspector with such test data,
measurements, ratings, capacities or other information as may be required by
the inspector for the purpose of determining ratings or capacities of such
boiler, furnace or device in accordance with the engineering provisions of this
article.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-813. - Certificate required.
   All test data, measurements, ratings or capacities submitted to the
inspector, as required in section
5-812, shall be accompanied by an engineer's certificate as to the correctness
of the same; such certificate to be made by an engineer employed by the
manufacturer of the boiler, furnace or device for which the test data
measurements, ratings or capacities are submitted.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-814. - Issuance restricted.
   No permit for the construction, installation, alteration, replacement or
repair of any oil burner, gas burner, stoker, heating, ventilating or air
conditioning plant or equipment shall be issued by the department to any person
unless he is duly licensed as required by this article to do such work.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-815. - Owner's privilege.
   Nothing contained in this division shall prohibit any bona fide owner from
personally installing, altering, replacing or repairing any heating,
ventilating or air conditioning plant or equipment in a one-family dwelling in
which he lives or plans to live, if a permit to do so is issued by the
department; provided, however, before such permit will issue, the owner shall
file an application in writing, signed and sworn to by such owner personally,
upon a form of application prescribed by the department of building and safety,
and shall pass an examination in a satisfactory manner prescribed by the
heating board of appeals, which examination shall show that such owner is able
and competent by experience and training to install, alter, replace or repair
such equipment in a safe manner and without the likelihood of injury to the
public.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-816. - Fees.
   (a)   The department shall, before issuing any permit under this article,
require the payment by the applicant for such permit of a permit fee in the
amount set forth in this section and for the purpose herein provided:
      (1)   Power plants generally. For any permit for the installation or
construction of a power plant or a boiler, or furnace and boiler, in connection
with any such plant, for each such boiler, or boiler and furnace or power plant
to be constructed or installed therein, where the cost of the proposed work
does not exceed $300.00, a fee of $3.00; for each additional $50.00 cost, an
additional fee of $1.00 will be required.
      (2)   Power plants, alterations of. For any permit for alterations,
replacements or repairs to any existing power plant, or boiler, or furnace and
boiler in connection with a power plant, required by the terms of this article,
a fee of $2.00.
      (3)   Gravity warm air heating systems. For any permit for the
installation of a gravity warm air heating system, $4.00. For any permit for
alterations, replacements or repairs to any existing gravity warm air heating
system or furnace in connection with such system, $2.00.
      (4)   Mechanical warm air heating or air conditioning system. For any
permit for the installation of a mechanical warm air heating system and each
such heating system to be installed, $5.00. For any permit for the installation
of a mechanical warm air heating system and the duct work and equipment of an
air conditioning system in connection therewith, for each such heating and air
conditioning system to be installed thereunder, $5.00.
      (5)   Mechanical warm air heating, etc., alterations. For any permit for
alteration, replacement or repairs to any existing mechanical warm air heating
system or duct work and equipment in any existing air conditioning system,
$3.00.
      (6)   Steam or hot water heating systems. For any permit for the
installation of a steam or hot water heating system or for the installation for
use in connection with fan heating system of a steam or hot water heating
plant, where the cost of the proposed work does not exceed $1,000.00, $5.00,
and $1.00 for each additional $1,000.00 cost.
         a.   For any permit for the installation of a steam or hot water
boiler in connection with any existing heating system or plant, $3.00.
         b.   For each sheet metal duct work in connection with cooling,
ventilating or any other type of system, a permit fee of $5.00, where the cost
of the proposed work does not exceed $10,000.00; and $1.00 for each additional
$5,000.00 cost or fraction thereof.
      (7)   Cooling piping and equipment. For any permit for the installation
of pipe duct work and equipment designed to accomplish the required cooling in
connection with the ventilating or summer air conditioning of buildings or
spaces therein, for the first 10,000 square feet of floor area, $5.00; and
$1.00 for each additional 1,000 square feet of floor area. Any permit for
alterations or repairs to any such cooling piping or equipment, $3.00.
      (8)   Stokers and powdered fuel burners. For any permit for the
installation, alteration, replacement or repair of a stoker or stokers, for
each stoker included in such permit, or for the equipment therewith, the
required fee shall be $3.00.
      (9)   Gas burners. For any permit for installing, altering, replacing or
repairing gas burners, or gas burning equipment for use in connection with the
heating system, the fee charged shall be $3.00 for each gas burner or its
equipment included in such permit.
      (10)   Gas fired unit heaters. For any permit for the installation of gas
or oil unit heaters, for each such heater separately metered, $3.00.
      (11)   Gas water radiators. For any permit for installing gas water
radiators the fee charged shall be $2.00 for each such device included in the
permit.
      (12)   Oil burners for heating systems. For any permit for the
installation of an oil burner, $3.00. For replacement or repair of an oil
burner or oil burner equipment, $2.00.
      (13)   Fuel oil storage tanks. For fuel oil storage tanks up to and
including 275 gallon capacity, the permit fee shall be $2.00 for storage or
auxiliary tanks over 275 gallon capacity and not exceeding 600 gallons, the
additional permit fee shall be $2.00 for each tank. For outside storage tanks,
the permit fee shall be $5.00 for each tank.
   (b)   However, when an inspector is required to make over three inspection
calls on any one job, an additional inspection fee of $3.00 per call will be
required.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 5.6, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-817—5-835. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 8. - BOILERS **
Sec. 5-836. - Foundations.
   Low pressure steam boilers, hot water furnaces, and hot water heaters shall
be supported upon concrete or other fireproof floors, but if not brick set, may
be supported on wood floors if protected below with four inches of brick, tile
or concrete laid over one-eighth inch plate turned up one inch on all sides,
such protection to extend four feet beyond the front of apparatus and two feet
beyond sides and back.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-837. - Protection of objects near boilers.
   All wood lath and plaster and other combustible ceilings and beams over and
for a minimum distance of four feet on all sides from such boiler and not less
than three feet from the top of the boiler to the ceiling shall be shielded
with approved metal or other fire-resistive materials. The material to be
applied shall leave an air space of not less than one-half inch between the
material and the ceilings or beams. The sides as well as the bottom of beams,
shall be protected. The distance from the top of the boiler to such shield
shall be not less than 12 inches. No combustible partition shall be within
three feet of the sides and back and five feet from the front of any boiler,
unless such partition shall be covered with fire-resistive material to a height
of at least three feet above the floor, and the fire-resistive material shall
extend from the end or the back of the boiler to at least four feet in front of
it; in which case the distance shall not be less than two feet in front of the
sides and four feet from the front of the boiler. If the above requirements for
clearance cannot be complied with, when required by the inspector, boiler rooms
shall be enclosed with incombustible walls or partitions and ceilings in such
manner as may be required by the building code of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-838. - Low pressure boilers.
   (a)   Low pressure boilers are hereby determined to include all boilers
carrying a pressure of not more than 15 pounds per square inch of steam
pressure and not more than 30 pounds per square inch of water pressure.
   (b)   Ratings for all low pressure cast iron and steel boilers shall be
selected in accordance with the recommendations for low pressure boilers as
determined by the Heating, Piping and Air Conditioning Contractor's National
Association, Engineering Standards, and all rules contained therein, and
amendments thereto, shall apply to all boilers governed by the provisions of
this article; provided however, that any low pressure boiler having an approved
rating from the American Society of Mechanical Engineers shall be acceptable
under this article.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-839. - Grate area.
   All boilers used for heating shall have grate area and evaporating capacity
sufficient for the amount of radiation served in accordance with the Net Load
Recommendations for Heating Boilers as published by the Heating, Piping and Air
Conditioning Contractor's National Association, except that no round cast iron
boiler with grate diameter less than 17 inches and containing less than five
sections, ash pit, fire pot, two intermediate sections and dome, shall be
permitted.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-840. - Boiler trimmings—Steam, vacuum and vapor.
   Every low pressure steam heating boiler shall be equipped with the
following:
      (1)   A safety valve of approved type with lever handle set at 15 pounds
and of sufficient size to dissipate all steam which can be generated in the
boiler without permitting the pressure in same to exceed 15 pounds per square
inch.
      (2)   Water column with try cocks and gauge glass connected directly to
the boiler independent of other connections.
      (3)   Steam pressure gauge of approved type with brass syphon loop
mounted at top of water column or, if placed more than five feet from water
column connection, shall be of approved size. No connections of any kind except
water column, blow-down, automatic feeder or low water cutoff connections shall
be permitted from steam or water connections from boiler to gauge glass or
pressure gauge.
      (4)   A permanent makeup or feed water connection of size approved by the
inspector, but in no case smaller than one-half inch, with globe valve placed
in same within easy reach of the floor with an approved type check valve
between shutoff valve and boiler shall be made to each boiler.
      (5)   Connection not less than one inch in size, equipped with hose end
or connected to blow-off piping to permit complete drainage of boiler.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-841. - Same—Water.
   Every low pressure hot water heating boiler shall be equipped with the
following:
      (1)   Water relief valve of approved make with lever handle, side outlet
not less than one inch in size, set to open at 30 pounds per square inch
pressure.
      (2)   Altitude gauge of approved make.
      (3)   Thermometer of approved make.
      (4)   Boiler feed connections. A permanent makeup or automatic feed water
connection of proper size, but in no case smaller than one-half inch, with
globe valve placed in same within reach of floor, shall be made to each boiler.
      (5)   Drain connection shall be not less than three-fourths inches in
size, equipped with hose end or connected to blow-off piping to permit complete
drainage of boiler.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-842. - Smoke pipes—Clearances.
   The clear distance between a smoke pipe or metal breaching and combustible
material or construction, including plaster or wood lath, shall be not less
than 24 inches; provided that such clearances may be reduced to 12 inches when
all combustible materials are protected with not less than one-quarter inch of
asbestos millboard placed at least one inch from the surface, to be protected
and extending the full length of the smoke pipe, and not less than 12 inches
beyond it on both sides, or such combustible material or construction may be
protected by some covering of equivalent safety placed at least one inch from
the surface to be protected and extending the full length and on both sides of
the smoke pipe, as above set forth.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-843. - Same—Through roof.
   No metal or crock smoke pipe shall pass through the roof or wall of any
building not wholly fireproofed, except in the case of a gas heater, a fume or
smoke pipe therefrom may be passed through the roof, in which case a special
permit shall be first obtained from the department; provided, however, the
foregoing requirement shall not prevent the issuing of, and the department is
hereby authorized to issue, a special permit for a period of not to exceed 90
days to allow a smoke pipe through the wall or roof of a construction shanty
designed to house workmen during the progress of any construction work. If a
permit is granted to pass such a pipe through a roof which is not wholly
fireproofed, the smoke pipe shall be protected in the following manner: A
galvanized iron ventilating thimble of the dimensions hereinafter stated shall
be installed: in the case of a smoke pipe, the diameter of the outside guard
shall be not less than 12 inches and the diameter of the inner guard shall be
not less than eight inches larger than the smoke pipe; and for all furnaces, or
where similar large hot fires are used, the diameter of the outside guard shall
be not less than 18 inches and the diameter of the inner guard shall not be
less than 12 inches larger in diameter than the pipe. The smoke pipe thimbles
shall extend from the under side of the ceiling or roof beams to at least nine
inches above the roof, and they shall have openings for ventilation at the
lower end where the smoke pipes enter, and at the top of the guards above the
roof. When a smoke pipe of a boiler passes through a roof, it shall be guarded
by a double ventilating thimble, as above specified, with outside and inside
guards 36 inches and 24 inches, respectively, larger than the diameter of the
smoke pipe of the boiler. This shall not be taken to apply to reinforced
concrete roof, or other roof which is wholly fireproofed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-844. - Same—Construction.
   Smoke pipes from heating boilers and furnaces, except domestic heating
boilers and furnaces, shall be constructed of iron or steel not lighter than
No. 20 gauge, or of equally safe material, and shall be extended full size
without restriction from smoke connection on boiler or furnace to the chimney.
Smoke pipes from domestic heating boilers and furnaces shall be constructed of
iron or steel not lighter than No. 24 gauge, or of equally safe material. All
smoke pipes shall be fitted with dampers of approved design.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-845. - Same—Connections prohibited.
   No smoke pipe or vent from any oil or gas fired boiler shall be connected
into the breeching or smoke pipe from a coal burning boiler or furnace, but
shall be provided with separate connection entirely, nor shall any horizontal
flue from a gas fired boiler be connected to any chimney flue which takes gases
from any other heating unit of any nature whatsoever.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-846. - Same—Connection required.
   Every furnace or boiler shall have suitable connection to an adequate
chimney or smoke stack which shall conform to the requirements of the building
code.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 6.11, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-847—5-865. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 9. - HEATING SYSTEM **
Sec. 5-866. - Heat loss.
   For the purpose of this division, the method of computing heat losses shall
be based on approved engineering practice using the British thermal unit system
of computation, as set forth by the American Society of Heating and Ventilating
Engineers, or similar methods as approved by the inspector. In addition to
actual heat loss through building construction, sufficient allowance shall be
made for ventilation requirements either on the basis of air changes per hour,
as set forth in section
5-877, or on a basis of infiltration.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-867. - Radiation—Generally.
   Any form of radiation approved by the inspector, after a test has been made
as to safety and quality of material, may be used on any heating system, except
that no radiators, either direct or indirect, carrying a pressure of more than
15 pounds per square inch shall be used in any building defined in the building
code as a public or residence building. No cast iron direct radiator shall in
any case be operated under a steam pressure exceeding ten pounds per square
inch or water pressure in excess of 30 pounds per square inch.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-868. - Same—Table of heat emissions.
   The heat output of direct steam radiators shall be figured not to exceed the
following emissions per square foot per hour with steam at two pounds pressure
and air temperature at 70 degrees Fahrenheit.
 
                         British Thermal Steam units British Thermal Hot Water
                                                     units
Cast iron tube radiators 240                         160
.....
Cast iron wall radiators 265                         175
.....
Single tier pipe coils   300                         200
.....
 
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-869. - Same—Necessity to convert into equivalent of BTU.
   In selecting boiler sizes, all radiation to be served shall be converted
into equivalent direct radiation figures based on 240 British thermal units per
square foot emission for steam, and 160 British thermal units for water.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-870. - Same—Equivalent for unit heaters.
   Equivalent direct radiation for unit heaters, indirect heaters, unit
ventilators and stack heaters shall be computed from manufacturer's data either
by dividing British thermal units output by 240, or pounds condensation per
hour by 4.0 in the case of steam, and in the case of hot water by dividing
British thermal units by 160.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-871. - Welding.
   All gas and electric arc-welding on gravity forced hot water, low pressure
heating systems shall be tested to meet the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-872. - Gas radiators and heaters.
   All gas radiators and heaters shall be of an approved, enclosed, vented
type, bearing the seal of the American Gas Association and shall be
automatically controlled in such a manner that the valve is completely shut off
upon failure of gas supply. Such radiators or heaters shall have legs not less
than six inches high, and the distance from the radiator or heater to the wall
shall be not less than five inches.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-873. - Steam heating—Piping.
   (a)   Black standard steel or wrought iron pipe with steam pattern cast iron
fittings shall be used on all steam heating systems except under special
conditions when, if approved by the inspector, other equally safe material may
be used.
   (b)   In general, piping shall be arranged to pitch in the direction of flow
of steam or condensate and shall be adequately dripped and vented. Maximum
pressure drop shall not exceed one-half pound total.
   (c)   As far as possible, boilers shall be located to permit the return of
condensate by gravity to the boiler and on such gravity systems, a check valve
or Hartford loop shall be installed in the main return to the boiler. On cast
iron boilers of the exterior return drum type, the main return shall be
branched at the boiler to connect to each such drum.
   (d)   Equalizer of the size, at least one-half the diameter of the boiler
tappings, of the main steam load shall be provided from the main supply of the
boiler to the wet return connection at the boiler in each case, but in no case
shall such equalizer be less than two inches in diameter.
   (e)   In one or two pipe gravity steam heating systems, the low point of the
steam main or "dry" return shall be at an elevation not less than 27 inches
above the normal boiler water line.
   (f)   No piping shall be laid in any coal bin unless protected by suitable
tile or other approved material to keep piping from direct contact with coal.
   (g)   No steam or return piping shall be buried directly in concrete without
protection by tile pipe and waterproofed covering with drain at end of the
crock pipe, nor shall wet return piping other than threaded cast iron pipe or
standard brass pipe having not less than 85 percent copper content be buried
below or in concrete floors. All trapped returns must have a full size plugged
tee or drain cock at lowest point.
   (h)   In building of frame construction where steam pipes are installed with
two inches of wood joints, studs, flooring or other combustible construction,
they shall be protected by asbestos or other insulation material not less than
three-fourths inch in thickness.
   (i)   Steam and return piping shall be run to permit expansion and
contraction without putting any undue strain on pipe or fittings using swing
joints or expansion joints to accomplish the above.
   (j)   No cutting of girders, beams, joists, studs or other structural
members to permit passage of heating pipes will be permitted, except as
approved by the building inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-874. - Same—Temperature control valves.
   No thermostatically operated temperature control valve or trap shall be
installed on steam mains or returns, unless adequate provision, subject to
approval of the inspector, is made to prevent the retaining of water in the
system and its proper return to the boiler.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-875. - Hot water heating—Piping.
   (a)   Brass, copper, black standard steel or wrought iron pipes and fittings
shall be used on all hot water heating systems except under special conditions
when, if approved by the heating board of appeals, other safe material may be
used.
   (b)   No part of the piping on a hot water heating system shall be laid in
any coal bin unless protected by suitable removable tile or other approved
material to keep piping from direct contact with coal and to permit
examination.
   (c)   Hot water piping, used for under the floor space heating, commonly
known as radiant heating, shall be buried in concrete of sufficient strength
and thickness to carry the floor load as provided for in the building code,
with a minimum thickness of three inches with at least two inches of concrete
over such piping and shall be laid level on a solid foundation over a four-inch
gravel fill, as recommended by the manufacturer's specifications, to eliminate
any possibility of air pockets in the system, with provisions made for drainage
at one or more points. Radiant heat piping shall be made of wrought iron,
copper, or brass with welded, brazed or soldered joints. All copper radiant
heat piping shall be tested by the installer with water, air, or gas at 60
pounds per square inch for a period of 30 minutes without any drop in pressure,
to the satisfaction of the heating inspector. Wrought iron and brass radiant
heat piping shall be tested by the installer with water, air or gas at 200
pounds per square inch for 30 minutes without any drop in pressure to the
satisfaction of the heating inspector. Hot water heat piping installed in
floors of dwellings which are built directly on the ground, at grade level,
shall be installed on a solid slab of cement concrete at least one inch in
thickness over a four-inch gravel fill or on a solid slab of zonolite concrete
or its equivalent at least one inch in thickness, over a four-inch gravel fill
in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications. A vapor barrier of
asphalt-saturated building paper equal to a 30-pound felt with a four-inch lap,
shall be installed over the zonolite or cement concrete base under the piping.
One inch asphalt insulation must be installed along the outer edge of the floor
slab and extend two feet under the floor as a border insulation to be placed
over the moisture barrier, in accordance with Sketch No. 1 shown herewith.
   (d)   Piping installed in the ceiling of dwellings for space heating shall
be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications with proper
insulation to prevent undue heat loss or the accumulation of moisture on the
ceiling.
   (e)   All supply and return piping run in exterior walls, except in cases
opening directly to rooms through which they pass, shall be insulated with
asbestos or other approved covering at least three-fourths inch thick.
   (f)   All low points in any hot water heating system shall be provided with
means for drainage.
   (g)   All hot water heating pipes shall be run to permit expansion and
contraction without undue strain on the pipe or fittings, using swing joints or
expansion joints to accomplish the above.
   (h)   No cutting of girders, beams joists, studs or other structural members
to permit passage of hot water heating pipes will be permitted, except as
approved by the building inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-876. - Same—Expansion tanks.
   (a)   Each hot water heating system shall be provided with an expansion tank
of sufficient capacity to allow for expansion of all water in the system from
50 degrees Fahrenheit to 220 degrees Fahrenheit.
   (b)   In open systems the expansion tank shall be installed above the
highest radiator served and shall be connected directly to the boiler with one-
inch pipe, with no valve of any description in this line between boiler and
tank.
   (c)   Each such tank shall be equipped with open vent at top terminated
within the walls of the building. An overflow pipe not less than three-fourths
inch in size shall also be provided, terminated in basement or other approved
location over sink or floor drain. No valves of any description may be placed
in vent or overflow pipes from open system expansion tanks.
   (d)   In closed systems an approved water relief valve with threaded side
outlet and lever handle for testing shall be provided on each closed expansion
tank with outlet extended to floor or other approved location.
   (e)   In all closed systems there shall be installed an automatic boiler
feed valve set for a maximum pressure of 18 pounds, to be not less than one-
half inch in size.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.11, 11-4-81)

Sec. 5-878. - Minimum requirements in determining radiating surface.
   The following are minimum requirements for determination of amount of direct
steam or hot water radiating surface to be installed in steam and hot water
heating systems:
      (1)   The amount of equivalent direct radiation to be installed in a
given room, where unenclosed radiators are to be employed, shall be as
determined by the following formulae:
 
    H
S = 240 (for steam) (1)
    H
S = 150 (for gravity hot water) (2)
    H
S = 220 (for forced hot water system) (3)
 
   Where:
H = heat loss of the room in BTU per hour, as determined by the methods herein
provided, and
S = equivalent direct radiating surface in square feet.
      (2)   For the purposes of this division, the equivalent direct radiation
in square feet for any unenclosed radiator shall be defined as the minimum
guaranteed heat emission of that radiator measured BTU per hour, divided by 240
for direct steam, 150 for gravity hot water radiation, 220 for forced hot water
heating.
      (3)   For various other water (or steam) temperatures, various emissions
per square feet are shown in the following table:
Temperature of Water  Heat Emission
in Radiator           Per Square Feet
