215 degrees .....     240 BTU per hour
225 degrees .....     260 BTU per hour
240 degrees .....     295 BTU per hour
Note: The above emissions are for a radiator in air at 70 degrees Fahrenheit
 
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-879. - Enclosed radiators.
   When direct radiator enclosures are to be used in the increase or decrease
of heat emission from the direct radiators, such radiators shall be governed by
provisions of the Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning Guide, as published by
American Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers, and amendments thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-880. - Convectors or concealed heaters.
   Ratings for convectors or concealed heaters shall be determined as set forth
in the Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning Guide, as published by American
Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers, and amendments thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-881. - Unit heaters.
   Coal, gas and oil fired unit heaters are to be installed according to the
engineering standards set forth by the Heating, Piping, and Air Conditioning
Contractors National Association, and amendments thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-882. - Gas or oil fired floor type furnaces.
   No furnace shall be installed in the floor of any auditorium, public hall,
public assembly room or commercial building, but such furnace may be installed
in single residences, subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth.
      (1)   The floor around the furnace shall be braced and double-headed with
a framework of material not lighter than the joists. The inside dimensions of
the framework shall be approximately one-half inch longer and wider than the
furnace to be installed.
      (2)   All floor furnaces, including those having single or dual wall
register outlets, shall be installed as approved without alterations,
extension, or changes of any kind in the furnace.
      (3)   No automatic pilot shutoff shall be installed on a floor furnace
that has not been approved for such equipment by the American Gas Association.
      (4)   All floor furnaces shall be equipped with a pressure regulator
approved by the American Gas Association.
      (5)   The bottom of the floor furnace shall have a clearance under it of
at least 12 inches above the bottom of the pit. The ground around the sides of
such furnace shall be excavated to form a "basinlike" pit having at least 24
inches on all sides of such furnace. This facilitates any servicing that may be
required, and allows ample air for proper combustion.
      (6)   Whenever such excavation exceeds 12 inches in depth or water
seepage is apparent under the house, a watertight pan shall be used. The pan
shall be made of not less than 24-gauge galvanized iron or 16-ounce copper. The
pan shall be suitably anchored in place, and the walls shall extend at least
six inches above the grade level, and shall have 24 inches clearance on all
sides.
      (7)   Adequate provisions shall be made for easy access to the furnace
under the house by means of an opening in the foundation wall at least four
inches by 24 inches.
      (8)   All flue pipes for floor furnaces and central heating furnaces
shall be connected to a masonry chimney or a properly designed vent flue.
      (9)   Every vent pipe or connection between the appliance and the chimney
or flue shall not be smaller than the size of the vent collar of the appliance,
and in no case shall the internal area be less than seven square inches (three-
inch pipe). Vent pipes leading from heating appliances for fuel other than gas,
when converted to gas fuel, may be reduced from original size on the basis of
one square inch of area for every 7500 BTU of fuel delivered to the appliance
burner.
      (10)   Where the appliance has more than one vent connection, or where
more than one appliance is connected to the same vent, the area of the vent
pipe shall equal the combined area of the vents for which it acts as a common
carrier to the flue. All connections to the lateral run shall be made with "Y"
connections.
      (11)   All vents shall extend through roof as near ridge as practicable
with laterals in the attic not less than 30 degrees from the horizontal.
      (12)   Height of the vent must be two feet above the highest portion of
any structure within 15 feet from the place where the vent extends above the
ridge.
      (13)   The installation of a cap or other device on the outlets of an
appliance vent, which in any way obstructs the free passage of the products of
combustion to the outside atmosphere, is prohibited.
      (14)   Vent pipes passing through any closet or other enclosed space used
for the storage of clothing, household goods, or other combustible materials
shall be Type "B" vents, as set forth in the engineering standards of the
Heating, Piping, and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association, and
amendments thereto, or shall be in a vitreous lined masonry chimney.
      (15)   Maximum length of lateral vents shall not be more than 75 percent
of vertical height of vent or chimney.
      (16)   All lateral vent pipes shall be supported at every joint by
perforated strap iron not less than 1/16 inch in thickness securely fastened to
the floor joists.
      (17)   Vent pipes shall not be closer than two inches to any combustible
material, and in all cases where vent pipes are less than four inches from any
combustible material, the same shall be protected with asbestos mill board of
not less than one-fourth inch thickness.
      (18)   Where said Type "B" vents are used, it shall not be necessary to
use the mill board as required in subsection (17) of this sectiion.
      (19)   In underfloor areas, the minimum pitch upward of lateral runs of
vents from the appliance must be at least one-half inch per foot.
      (20)   Floor furnaces shall be installed so that the connection from the
draft diverter to the flue can be made without the use of more than two 45-
degree elbows. The installation of 90-degree elbows in lateral vent piping is
prohibited.
      (21)   Floor furnaces shall not be vented to a masonry or metal flue
which has any side exposed to the weather, or to an unheated space for its
entire length.
      (22)   Connections of lateral vent pipes to transite or other Type "B"
vents must be made with fittings designed by the vent manufacturers for this
purpose.
      (23)   The installation of dampers or stops in the vent pipe attached to
any appliance equipped with a draft diverter is prohibited.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.16a, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-883. - Gravity warm air heating—Generally.
   Unless otherwise expressly stated, the following terms shall, for the
purpose of this division, be construed to have the meaning as herein defined:
      (1)   A warm air furnace shall consist of a direct fired heater, over the
exterior surface of which the air passes to be directly heated by the radiant
heat of combustion.
      (2)   A gravity warm air heating plant shall consist of one or more warm
air furnaces, enclosed within casings, together with necessary air or
recirculating pipes, ducts, boxes and fittings, smoke pipes and fittings,
dampers, registers, borders, faces and grilles, the same being intended for
heating the buildings in which they may be installed, the motive head producing
flow in such heating plant depending on the difference in weight between the
heated air leaving the casings and the cooler air entering the bottom of the
casing.
      (3)   The incorporation of a booster fan, blower or any power driven
device for the purpose of accelerating the air circulation in a gravity warm
air heating plant shall be construed as changing the classification of such
gravity system to a mechanical forced air heating system.
      (4)   The installation, alteration or repair of gravity warm air heating
systems shall be governed by the Standard Gravity Code, as published by the
National Warm Air Heating and Air Conditioning Association, and amendments
thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-884. - Same—Size of registers.
   All registers shall have a free area at least equal to the area of the
basement pipes to them, and shall be of the approximate width of the stacks or
fittings to which they are attached.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-885. - Same—Size of furnace.
   The required furnace size shall be determined according to the table as
hereinafter set forth, based upon the area of all heat pipes leading from the
furnace, as follows:
 
Size of furnace        Maximum total area of all pipes from furnace
18-inch fire pot ..... 250 square inches
20-inch fire pot ..... 350 square inches
22-inch fire pot ..... 450 square inches
24-inch fire pot ..... 525 square inches
26-inch fire pot ..... 600 square inches
28-inch fire pot ..... 700 square inches
 
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-886. - Same—Gas or oil fired furnaces.
   In the use of any gas or oil fired furnace with any gravity warm air heating
system, deviations from the requirements of this division shall be allowed only
in connection with the furnace itself, and such deviations shall be subject to
the approval of the inspector. The rating of each such gas or oil fired furnace
shall be determined in accordance with the best engineering practice.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-887. - Same—Furnaces; construction, installation of.
   The construction and installation of all warm air furnaces hereafter
installed in connection with gravity warm air heating plants in the city,
except as elsewhere in this division otherwise provided, shall comply with the
following requirements:
      (1)   The location of the furnace shall be such as to equalize the length
of warm air pipes as far as possible, yet give necessary preference to pipes
supplying rooms having unusual requirements.
      (2)   Furnace foundation of brick, cement, or other like incombustible
material shall be provided. Such foundation shall extend at least 36 inches in
front of furnace casing, and at least 15 inches at rear and sides of furnace
casing. Foundation shall be level.
      (3)   Where it is necessary to place a furnace on combustible floor, not
less than four inches of hollow tile shall be used in every instance, having
joints matched in such a way that air passage will be free from side to side,
so that at no time will the removal of ashes or the handling of coal close up
these openings. Such foundation shall be constructed upon and covered with
continuous sheet metal plates, of weight not less than No. 24 U.S. Standard
gauge, having all joints substantially riveted or double seamed and the bottom
sheet to have the edges turned up at least one inch. This floor covering shall
extend under the whole of the firebox and ash pit of the furnace and outwardly
not less than 12 inches on all sides and rear of casing or base ring, and 36
inches in front.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-888. - Mechanical warm air heating.
   The requirements of this section shall apply to the construction,
application and installation of air duct systems and self-contained units
employing mechanical means for the movement of air and used for forced air
heating systems.
      (1)   A mechanical warm air heating plant shall consist of one or more
warm air furnaces enclosed within casings, together with necessary
appurtenances thereto, consisting of warm air supply pipes and fittings, cold
air or recirculating pipes, ducts, boxes and fittings, smoke pipes and
fittings, dampers and registers, faces and grilles, fans or blowers, the same
being intended for heating the buildings in which they may be installed. The
circulation of air within such a system shall be dependent upon the motive
power furnished by a fan or blower, and the duct work in connection therewith
shall be designed especially for such system; provided, however, that the
incorporation of a booster fan, blower or any power driven device for the
purpose of accelerating the air circulation in a gravity warm air heating plant
shall be construed as changing the classification of such gravity system to a
mechanical system.
      (2)   The amount of air to be provided for each room or space to be
heated or conditioned shall be determined in accordance with the Technical Code
for the Design and Installation of Mechanical Warm Air Heating Systems, as
published by the National Warm Air Heating and Air Conditioning Association,
with amendments thereto.
      (3)   A warm air all year air conditioning system shall include a
mechanical warm air heating plant, such as defined in section
5-883(2), together with such other devices and such automatic controls as will
secure simultaneous control of the temperature, motion and humidity and a
reduction in the dust and odor content of the air employed in the ventilation
of rooms, but not provided with such devices and automatic controls as will
provide for cooling and dehumidifying in summer.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-889. - Wall stacks.
   Wall stacks for the purpose of conducting gravity warm air shall be
constructed and installed in accordance with the provisions of the building
code of the city, as amended.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 7.23, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-890—5-905. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 10. - VENTILATING AND AIR CONDITIONING **
Sec. 5-906. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Air conditioning shall mean provision for the simultaneous automatic control
of the temperature, motion, and humidity and a reduction in the dust content
and odors for air employed in the ventilation of rooms. The three
classifications of air conditioning which shall be recognized under this
division shall be as follows:
      (1)   Winter air conditioning, which shall include the proper
distribution of the cleaned, humidified and heated air to and within the spaces
to be conditioned.
      (2)   Summer air conditioning, which shall include the proper
distribution of the cleaned, dehumidified and cooled air to and within the
spaces to be conditioned.
      (3)   All year conditioning, which shall provide for all the services
enumerated in subsections (1) and (2) above.
   Partial cooling shall mean a device designed and employed to accomplish the
partial cooling of the air in a room or rooms, either by means of direct
expansion coils or water coils employing chilled water as a cooling medium, and
located either within the room or rooms to be so partially cooled, or
immediately adjacent thereto.
   Ventilation shall mean the process of supplying or removing air by natural
or mechanical means, to or from any space. Such air may or may not have been
conditioned.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-907. - Information to be submitted.
   (a)   The plans and specifications of all air conditioning or partial
cooling installations submitted for approval under this article shall set forth
the heat transmission coefficients for barriers and the amounts and sources of
heat loss and gain. The design temperatures and relative humidity shall be
recorded for air outside and inside, for condensing air or water, and for the
heat transferring medium.
   (b)   These governing design factors and temperatures shall be such as to
produce an effective result at least equal to those set forth by the Heating,
Ventilating, Air Conditioning Guide, as published by the American Society of
Heating and Ventilating Engineers, and amendments thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-908. - Air filters.
   (a)   Air filters shall be so installed as to be readily accessible for
inspection and removal for cleaning or replacement. Duct connections to and
from filters shall change size or shape gradually to insure even distribution
of air over entire filter area. Filters installed close to outside air inlet
shall be protected from the weather by suitable louvers, in front of which a
one-inch mesh wire screen shall be provided.
   (b)   The contractor installing such work should post in a conspicuous place
adjacent to the furnace a notice reading substantially as follows: "To insure
proper air delivery, the filter contained in this unit must be cleaned or
renewed at least once each year."
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-909. - Air washers.
   The following provisions shall govern the design, construction and
installation of air washers when incorporated as a part of any mechanical warm
air or air conditioning system:
      (1)   Air shall be uniformly distributed over washer inlet.
      (2)   Spray nozzles shall be so spaced and arranged that spray will
completely cover cross sectional area of washer above tank.
      (3)   Air velocity through washer shall not be less than 300 feet per
minute nor greater than 600 feet per minute.
      (4)   Provision shall be made to prevent entrained moisture being carried
past washer outlet.
      (5)   Drain and overflow connections from washer tank shall not be
directly connected to sewer or wash line, but shall, in all cases, drain to
open receptacle.
      (6)   Fresh water connection shall be so arranged that there will be no
possibility of tank water being drawn back into water supply line in the event
of lack of pressure in supply line.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-910. - Refrigerating equipment and refrigerants.
   All refrigerants, cooling equipment, piping and specialties installed and
used in connection with air conditioning shall be subject to the requirements
of the "American Standard Safety Code for Mechanical Refrigeration," as
approved by the American Standards Association, and as published by American
Engineering and Industrial Standards.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-911. - Recommendations of technical organizations.
   Except as otherwise specifically prescribed in this article or in duly
promulgated rules, the published recommendations of the following technical
organizations, recognized as authoritative in the field involved, shall be
deemed to be generally accepted as good practice in both heating, ventilating
and air conditioning work:
      (1)   Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning Guide, as published by
American Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers.
      (2)   American Standard Safety Code of Mechanical Refrigeration, as
approved by American Standards Association, and published by American
Engineering and Industrial Standards.
      (3)   Standards for the Installation of Air Conditioning, Warm Air
Heating, Air Cooling and Ventilating Systems, as recommended by National Fire
Protection Association.
      (4)   Technical Code for the Design and Installation of Mechanical Warm
Air Heating Systems, as published by National Warm Air Heating and Air
Conditioning Association.
      (5)   The Standard Gravity Code for the Design and Installation of
Gravity Air Heating and Air Conditioning Association.
      (6)   Heating, Piping and Air Conditioning Contractors National
Association Engineering Standards, as developed by the Committee on Standards
of the Heating, Piping and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
      (7)   Net Load Recommendations for Heating Boilers, as published by the
Heating, Piping and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-912. - Wall stacks.
   (a)   Wall stacks for the purpose of conducting forced air shall be
constructed and installed as provided in this section.
   (b)   All single wall stacks or wall pipes, heads, boots, ells, tees,
angles, and other connections shall be made of bright tin not lighter than IC,
or of galvanized iron not lighter than 26 U.S. Standard gauge; provided,
however, that aluminum with a sheet thickness of not less than .020 inch may be
used for forced air heating plans only; provided further that any aluminum duct
ten inches or larger shall be cross-broken and bracing angles installed. And
all transverse joint connections shall be of the aluminum sheet thickness
embracing as hereinafter indicated:

Sec. 5-913. - Ventilation of restaurant type cooking equipment.
   The following provisions shall apply to ventilation of restaurant type
cooking equipment:
      (1)   Hoods over such equipment shall be constructed of noncombustible
materials, with tight joints and have a clearance of at least 18 inches from
all unprotected combustible materials.
      (2)   Ducts from hoods over such equipment shall be constructed of No. 18
U.S. gauge or heavier steel, with tight joints and separated at least 18 inches
from all unprotected combustible material.
      (3)   The ducts shall constitute an independent system in no manner
connected with any other ventilating system.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-914. - Laboratory and factory hood vents.
   The following provisions shall apply to educational and industrial
establishments.
      (1)   Where fans are installed to remove acid fumes, corrosive gases or
other irritating gaseous products from hoods, kettles, drains or similar
devices used in educational or industrial establishments, the discharge from
such fans or blowers shall be carried up to the roof of the building and so
located as to preclude the possibility of constituting a nuisance or menace to
occupants of the building or adjacent structures.
      (2)   Unless specially constructed fireproof flues of acid-resisting
material and approved design are used, such exhaust fans shall be placed near
the roof of the building in which they are located so that all portions of the
duct work and vertical flues in the building passing through occupied spaces
shall be under suction.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-915. - Location and accessibility of fans.
   No fans with motors, pulleys, belts or other moving parts shall be installed
in such a manner as to make any of the bearings or moving parts inaccessible
for easy oiling, inspection and repair. All duct work enclosing bearings shall
be provided with access doors to permit inspection, and, if required by the
inspector, oil gauge glasses shall be brought out through such duct work.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-916. - Source of air for fan restricted.
   No fan used to force air to any parts of a building regularly occupied shall
take its air from any boiler room, open basement, garage or other location
where fire or noxious fumes are liable to be introduced to other parts of the
building through the system.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-917. - Fire dampers.
   Where ventilating ducts pass through fire-resistive walls or floors,
automatic fire dampers actuated by fusible link shall be provided as required
by the inspector. Such dampers shall be of design approved by the American
Society of Mechanical Engineers, and shall be provided with means for easy
resetting without dismantling duct work.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 8.12, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-918—5-935. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 11. - STOKERS **
Sec. 5-936. - Scope.
   Under this division is included any mechanically operated device which
introduces solid fuel into a furnace or boiler and has as part of its equipment
a mechanically operated fan or blower designed to force air for combustion
through such fuel bed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-937. - Combustion space.
   No stoker shall be installed unless sufficient combustion space is available
in the furnace to permit the device to operate at its full rated capacity
without producing smoke or excessive fly ash under normal conditions.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-938. - Draft.
   No stoker shall be installed in any boiler or heater where the stack or flue
is of insufficient size or height to take off all products of combustion
without building up positive pressure in the furnace at all firing periods.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-939. - Stoker controls.
   Every stoker operated by an electric motor shall be equipped with a low
voltage release device which, in case of current failure at the motor, will
prevent the restarting of the stoker automatically when the electric current is
again resumed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-940. - Stoker switch.
   Each mechanical stoker shall be equipped with an automatic stoker switch of
approved make installed in the smoke flue which will stop stoker when flue gas
temperature exceeds 650 degrees Fahrenheit, or starts when the temperature
drops below 200 degrees Fahrenheit.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-941. - Data to be given.
   Each application for stoker installation shall state the maximum firing rate
of the equipment in pounds per hour fired, the kind and quality of coal to be
fired and the cubic feet of combustion space available in the boiler or heater
in which the stoker is to be installed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-942. - Where prohibited.
   No mechanical stoker using forced draft will be permitted in any sheet iron
warm air furnace, unless lined with at least a two-inch thickness of fire
brick.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-943. - Undergrate blowers—Scope.
   Under sections
5-944 through
5-947 is included any mechanically operated fan or blower introducing air for
combustion into the ash pit of any furnace, heater, stove or boiler.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-944. - Same—Draft.
   No undergrate blower or fan shall be installed where the stack or flue is of
insufficient size to prevent the building up of a positive pressure in the
furnace at all firing periods.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-945. - Same—Stoker switch.
   Every undergrate blower shall be equipped with a stoker switch installed in
the smoke flue so wired as to shut off the blower when flue gas temperature
exceeds 650 degrees Fahrenheit.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-946. - Same—Data to be given.
   Each application for undergrate blower installation shall state the maximum
capacity of the blower or fan to be used, the size and type of heater or boiler
under which the blower is to be installed, and the kind of fuel to be burned.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-947. - Same—Where prohibited.
   No undergrate blower shall be installed in any sheet iron warm air furnace,
unless lined with at least two-inch fire brick.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 9.12, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-948—5-965. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 12. - OIL BURNERS **
Sec. 5-966. - Application of division.
   The construction, arrangement and manner of installation of all oil burners
and oil burner equipment installed for use in connection with heating systems,
and the alteration, replacement or repair of all oil burners and oil burner
equipment used or to be used in connection with heating systems, shall conform
to the provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-967. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Oil burner shall mean any device for use in connection with a heating
system, designed to burn fuel oil having a flash point of 130 degrees
Fahrenheit, or higher, as determined by the tag closed tester in accordance
with the method of test adopted by the American Society for Testing Materials
(A.S.T.M. Designation D-56-21), and having a fuel tank or container with a
capacity of more than ten gallons connected thereto.
   Oil burner equipment shall include oil burners and all tanks, piping, pumps,
control devices and accessories connected to the burners; provided, however,
this division shall not apply to portable burners not requiring connection to a
flue, such as oil stoves, oil heaters and oil lamps equipped with a wick or a
mechanical device, the movement of which is essential to flame adjustment.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-968. - Certificate of approval—Required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person or his agents, to install any oil burner
in the city until an application for approval of such make or type of burner,
on a form similar to that set forth immediately hereafter, shall have been
filed with the department and a certificate of approval of such burner issued
by the department. The inspector shall issue a certificate of approval or of
disapproval within 30 days after the filing of any such application.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-969. - Same—Application.
   The form of the application for a certificate of approval under this
division shall be as follows:
The undersigned hereby requests that a Certificate of Approval be issued for
the oil burner described below:
      1.   Address where burner will be installed _____
      2.   Name of burner _____
      3.   Type of burner _____
      4.   Name of manufacturer _____
      5.   Address of manufacturer _____
      6.   Kind of fuel recommended for burner _____
      7.   Length of time burner has been on market _____
      8.   List approvals by state, city or recognized laboratories:
   Name _____
   Date _____
      9.   Attach blue print of assembly drawing showing construction of
device, indicating moving parts, oil passages and air passage.
      10.   Application filed by ____________ at Dearborn, Michigan, this
____________ day of ____________ / ____________ / ____________ , 19
____________ .
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-970. - Same—Standards for approval.
   The inspector shall approve any oil burner listed by the Underwriters'
Laboratory or any other nationally recognized inspection board or laboratory.
Oil burners not listed by the Underwriters' Laboratory or any other nationally
recognized board or laboratory shall not be approved until they have been
inspected and tested by some recognized laboratory capable of making such a
test and inspection, and the certificate showing such inspection and test shall
be forwarded to the department. This inspection and test shall cover
arrangement of parts, suitability of material, strength of parts, electrical
control, thermostatic arrangement, reliability of automatic features,
positiveness of ignition and safeguards against flooding.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-971. - Installation of used oil burners.
   Any person licensed to install, alter, repair or replace oil burners in the
city shall install a used burner for use in connection with a heating system
only after he shall have furnished the inspector with a statement that such oil
burner has been put in first class operating condition, and a letter from the
purchaser acknowledging that such purchaser is buying a used oil burner.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-972. - Fuel oil—Specifications.
   The grade of fuel oil used with any burner shall be one which tests and
experience have shown to be suitable for use with that burner. The oil shall
have a flashpoint not less than 130 degrees Fahrenheit, and shall be free from
acid, grit, and fibrous or other foreign matter likely to clog or injure the
burners or valves.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-973. - Same—Commercial standards.
   The commercial standards (grades 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 for domestic and
industrial fuel oils, set up by the U.S. Government, Department of Commerce,
Bureau of Standards Bulletin CS 12-29, issued November 7, 1929) shall
constitute standard grades for fuel oil sold or delivered to oil burner plants
within the city. It is declared a violation of this division for any person to
deliver or put into the storage tank of an oil burner plant a grade of oil
inferior to that ordered by the purchaser.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-974. - Same—Approval tag required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to supply or deliver fuel oil to any
tank or container used in connection with or attached to a fuel oil burner
unless such fuel oil burner and equipment shall have been inspected and
approved by the inspector or his assistant and an approval tag securely
attached to the filler pipe of such tank or container.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-975. - Use of nonautomatic burners limited.
   Oil burners, which are not equipped with automatic means for preventing
abnormal discharge of oil at the burner, shall not be installed or operated in
any location where a competent attendant will not be constantly on duty at the
premises where the burner is located, while the burner is in operation.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-976. - Gravity feed to burners.
   Gravity feed shall be used only with burners arranged to prevent abnormal
discharge of oil at the burner by automatic means specifically approved for the
burner with which it is used.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-977. - Supply tanks capacity.
   (a)   Gravity supply tanks shall not exceed 275 gallons individual capacity.
Where more than one gravity supply tank is used, such tanks shall be connected
to the feed pipe leading to the burner through a manually operated, approved
three-way valve in such a way that only one tank can discharge its contents at
one time.
   (b)   On multiple tank installations, the fill pipe shall be so arranged
that both tanks will fill equally, and the vent pipe shall extend well above
cross connections between tanks to prevent air binding when filling.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-978. - Level device.
   Where oil is supplied to the burner by gravity and a constant level device
is not incorporated in the burner assembly or in an auxiliary tank used in
connection with an automatic pump, an approved constant level device shall be
installed in the oil feed line at the gravity tank or as close thereto as
practicable. The vent opening of such constant level device shall be connected
by piping or tubing to the gravity tank vent pipe.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-979. - Pressure feed.
   (a)   Pressure tank feed shall be used only with burners arranged to prevent
abnormal discharge of oil at the burner by automatic means specifically
approved for the burner with which it is used.
   (b)   Pressure tanks shall not exceed a capacity of 60 gallons, and shall
not be operated at pressures exceeding 50 pounds per square inch. They shall be
equipped with a reliable pressure gauge, approved by the A.S.M.E., and with an
automatic relief valve piped to discharge outside of buildings.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-980. - Underground tanks—Installation.
   Underground tanks shall be so buried as to have a cover of earth not less
than two feet thick, or shall be covered with not less than one foot of earth
on top of which shall be placed a slab of reinforced concrete not less than
four inches thick. The slab shall be set on a firm, well tamped earth
foundation and shall extend at least one foot beyond the tank in all
directions. Where tanks are buried underneath buildings, such a concrete slab
shall be provided in every instance.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-981. - Same—Foundations.
   Underground tanks shall be set on a firm foundation and surrounded with soft
earth or sand well tamped in place. Where necessary to prevent floating, they
shall be securely anchored or weighed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-982. - Oil tanks—Enclosure.
   Oil supply tanks, when located outside buildings and not buried underground,
must be totally enclosed, as provided in section
5-986.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-983. - Same—Installation inside buildings.
   Oil supply tanks larger than 60 gallons capacity shall not be located in
buildings above the lowest story, cellar or basement.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-984. - Same—Location.
   Unenclosed inside storage tanks and auxiliary tanks shall not be located
within five feet, horizontally, of any fire or flame.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-985. - Same—Storage.
   Inside storage and auxiliary tanks shall be securely supported by
substantial incombustible supports to prevent settling or sliding.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-986. - Same—Installation specifications.
   (a)   Oil supply tanks located inside buildings shall not exceed 275 gallons
individual capacity or 550 gallons aggregate capacity, in one building, unless
installed in an enclosure or casing constructed as follows:
      (1)   The walls of the enclosure shall be constructed of reinforced
concrete at least six inches thick or of brick at least eight inches thick, and
shall be bonded to the floor. The space between the tank and the enclosure
shall be completely filled with sand or well tamped earth.
      (2)   Where the floor or other construction immediately above the tank is
of fire-resistive construction capable of safely sustaining a load of 150
pounds per square foot, the walls of the enclosure shall be carried to a height
not less than one foot above the tank and the space filled with sand or well
tamped earth to the top; otherwise, the enclosure shall have a top of
reinforced concrete at least five inches thick or of equivalent construction.
   (b)   Instead of an enclosure as above described, the tank may be encased in
reinforced concrete not less than six inches in thickness, applied directly to
the tank so as to completely eliminate any air space.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-987. - Same—Capacity generally.
   In buildings of ordinary construction, the nominal gross capacity of oil
tanks shall not exceed 5,000 gallons.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-988. - Same—Capacity in fire-resistive structures.
   In fire-resistive buildings, the nominal gross capacity of oil tanks shall
not exceed 15,000 gallons.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.23, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-989. - Same—Gross capacity.
   In any building, if in a fire-resistive or detached room cut off vertically
and horizontally, in an approved manner, from other floors of the main
building, the nominal gross capacity of tanks shall not exceed 50,000 gallons,
with an individual tank capacity not exceeding 25,000 gallons.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.24, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-990. - Construction—Capacity.
   (a)   Underground tanks and tanks inside buildings shall be constructed of
steel or wrought iron of a minimum gauge (U.S. Standard) in accordance with the
following table, except that for tanks of 181 to 275 gallons capacity,
installed in buildings, and without masonry enclosures, the minimum gauge shall
be No. 14 steel, or wrought iron thinner than No. 7 gauge used in the
construction of underground and enclosed tanks shall be galvanized.

   (b)   If adequate internal bracing is provided, tanks of 12,001 to 30,000
gallons capacity may be built of one-fourth-inch plate; for tanks larger than
1,100 gallons capacity, having adequate internal bracing, a tolerance of ten
percent incapacity is permitted.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.25, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-991. - Same—Specifications.
   (a)   Joints shall be riveted and caulked, brazed, welded or made tight by
some equally satisfactory process. Tanks shall be tight and sufficiently strong
to bear without injury the most severe strains to which they may be subjected
in practice. Shells of tanks shall be properly reinforced where connections are
made. All connections to underground tanks, outside aboveground tanks, and
tanks inside buildings shall be made through the top of tank above the liquid
level, except that tanks of not over 275 gallons capacity may have one bottom
connection for gravity feed and one opening for an approved key stem gate valve
to facilitate cleaning or for a scavenging line to be run to the outside and
capped oiltight when not in use.
   (b)   Where tanks are located so that the top of the tank is above the level
of the suction inlet of the pump supplying oil to the burner or burner
assembly, a siphon breaking device consisting of an anti-siphon valve and
vacuum tank, Underwriter's vacuum siphon breaker, siphon breaking pump set, or
equivalent devices to prevent siphoning, shall be installed; provided, however,
that in the case of a single tank not exceeding 275 gallons capacity, or a
multiple tank installation so connected by means of an approved three-way tank
installation, so connected by means of an approved three-way valve that only
one tank may be drawn from at a time, the installation of the above-mentioned
antisiphon devices may be omitted. There must be separate valves on each
battery from the header.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.26, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-992. - Pressure tanks—Design.
   Pressure tanks shall be designed for at least six times the maximum working
pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.27, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-993. - Same—Outside coating.
   Tanks shall be thoroughly coated on the outside with tar, asphaltum or other
suitable rust-resisting paint. Where placed in corrosive soil special
protection may be required.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.28, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-994. - Same—For heavy oils.
   For fuel oil heavier than 35 degrees A.P.I., tanks may be made of concrete,
in accordance with the standards of the National Board of Fire Underwriters for
the construction of concrete fuel oil storage tanks, as recommended by the
National Fire Protection Association.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.29, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-995. - Tank vents.
   Storage tanks shall be equipped with an open vent or an approved
automatically operated vent, arranged to discharge to the open air. Vent
openings and vent pipes shall be of ample size to prevent abnormal pressure in
the tank during filling but not smaller than three-fourths-inch pipe size for
tanks up to 500-gallon capacity; one-inch pipe for tanks up to 1,000. The vent
from oil tanks shall be increased one-half inch in diameter for each 1,000
gallon capacity on oil tanks over 1,000 gallons in size.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.30, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-996. - Same—Draining.
   Vent pipes shall be arranged to drain to the tank. The lower end of the vent
pipe shall not extend through the top into the tank for a distance of more than
one inch.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.31, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-997. - Same—Termination.
   Vent pipes shall terminate outside of buildings at a point not less than two
feet measured vertically or horizontally from any window or other building
opening and not less than one foot above fill cap, nor less than eight feet
above the ground. Outer ends of vent pipes shall be provided with a
weatherproof hood or return bend. Vent pipes of tanks containing heaters shall
be extended to such a height that oil vapors discharging from the vent will be
readily diffused without danger of ignition.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.32, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-998. - Same—Cross connections prohibited.
   Vent pipes shall not be cross connected with fill pipes or return lines from
burners.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.33, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-999. - Vent and fill pipes.
   Fill and vent pipes shall not be run through windows or coal-chutes unless
such openings are totally enclosed with masonry to prevent oil from entering
building during filling operation.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.34, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1000. - Tank fill and overflow pipes.
   Underground tanks and storage tanks inside buildings shall be filled only
through fill pipes terminating outside of buildings at a point at least two
feet from any building opening at the same or lower level. Fill terminals shall
be closed tight, when not in use, by a metal cover designed to prevent
tampering.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.35, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1001. - Auxiliary tanks—Filling.
   Auxiliary tanks shall be filled by pumping from storage tanks.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.36, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1002. - Same—Overflow equipment.
   Auxiliary tanks other than vacuum tanks shall be equipped with an overflow
pipe draining to the storage tank, at least one size larger than the supply
pipe.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.37, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1003. - Same—Gravity and pressure.
   Overflow pipes of auxiliary gravity tanks shall have no valve or
obstructions. Overflow pipes of auxiliary pressure tanks shall be provided with
interconnected valves or other means for automatically venting the tank during
filling.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.38, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1004. - Oil gauging.
   All tanks in which a constant oil level is not maintained by an automatic
pump shall be equipped with an approved method of determining the oil level.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.39, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1005. - Test wells.
   Test wells shall not be installed inside buildings and, where permitted for
outside services, shall be closed tight when not in use by a metal cover
designed to prevent tampering.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.40, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1006. - Gauging devices.
   Gauging devices such as liquid level indicators or signals shall be
installed so that oil or vapor will not be discharged into the building from
the fuel supply system.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.41, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1007. - Gauges, kinds not in use.
   No glass gauge, or any gauge, the breaking of which will permit oil to
escape from the tank, shall be used.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.42, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1008. - Oil pumps—Specifications.
   Oil pumps shall be of approved type, secure against leaks, and shall be
rigidly fastened in place.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.43, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1009. - Same—Automatic.
   Automatic pumps not an integral part of the burner shall be arranged to stop
automatically in case of total breakage of the supply line to the burner.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.44, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1010. - Same—Duplicate pumps.
   In isolated locations, where fire protection equipment is dependent upon a
heating plant fired by an oil burner, oil pumps supplying the burner shall be
installed in duplicate.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.45, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1011. - Piping—Minimum specifications.
   All piping shall be standard full weight wrought iron, steel, or brass pipe
with standard fittings or approved brass or copper tubing with approved
fittings.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.46, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1012. - Same—Sizes.
   Pipe used in the installation of domestic type burners shall not be smaller
than 3/8 -inch iron pipe size; pipe used in the installation of industrial type
burners shall not be smaller than ½-inch iron pipe size. Copper or brass tubing
used in the installation of domestic type burners where the oil flows by
gravity from the tank to the burners shall not be smaller in size than 3/8 -
inch outside diameter, .049-inch wall thickness tubing. For other than domestic
installations such copper or brass tubing shall not be smaller than 3/8 -inch
inside diameter, .049-inch wall thickness tubing. For industrial type burners
such copper or brass tubing shall not be smaller in size than the equivalent of
the iron pipe size mentioned above, with wall thickness not less than .049-
inch.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.47, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1013. - Same—Installation.
   Piping shall be rigidly secured in place and protected from injury in a
workmanlike manner, and where necessary shall be protected against corrosion.
Where practicable, oil piping shall be buried underground or in a concrete
floor or placed in a metal-covered pipe trench.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.48, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1014. - Same—Connections.
   Pipe joints and connections shall be made tight in a workmanlike manner.
Union and tubing fittings shall be made of approved standard type. Unions
requiring gaskets or packing, and right and left couplings, shall not be used
in oil lines.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.49, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1015. - Same—Allowances.
   Proper allowances shall be made for expansion, contraction, jarring and
vibration. Pipe lines, other than tubing, connected to underground tanks,
except fill lines and test wells, shall be provided with double swing joints
arranged to permit the tank to settle without impairing the efficiency of the
pipe connections.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.50, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1016. - Same—Strainers.
   Oil supply lines to burners shall be provided with approved strainers.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.51, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1017. - Valves—Installation.
   Readily accessible shutoff valves of approved type shall be installed in oil
supply lines near each burner and close to gravity and pressure supply tanks.
Shutoff valves of approved type shall be installed on each side of oil
strainers which are not a part of the oil burner unit and on the discharge and
suction side of oil pumps which pump directly to the burner but which are not a
part of the burner unit.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.52, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1018. - Same—When relief needed.
   Where a shutoff valve is installed in the discharge line of an oil pump, an
approved pressure relief valve shall be connected into the discharge line
between the pump and the shutoff valve and arranged to return surplus oil to
the storage tank or to bypass it around the pump.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.53, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1019. - Same—Control.
   Control valves shall be provided with stuffing box of liberal size,
containing a removable cupped gland designed to compress the packing against
the valve stem and arranged so as to facilitate removal. Valves shall be
designed to close against the supply, and prevent withdrawal of stem by
continued operation of the handwheel. Packing affected by the oil or by heat
shall not be used.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.54, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1020. - Preheating of oil.
   Preheating of oil, where necessary, shall be done by steam, hot water or
approved electric heaters. Heaters shall be substantially constructed with all
joints made oil tight. Thermometers shall be installed at suitable locations to
indicate the temperature of the heated oil. Heaters shall be by-passed or
provided with suitable means to prevent abnormal pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.55, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1021. - Tests of covered tanks and piping.
   After installation and before being covered, tanks of 1,000 gallons capacity
or more, and piping, shall be tested hydrostatically, or with equivalent air
pressure at a pressure not less than 1½ times the maximum working pressure but
not less than five pounds per square inch at the highest point of the system.
Instead of a pressure test, suction lines may be tested under a vacuum of not
less than 20 inches of mercury. Such tests shall be made by the installer, in
the presence of the inspector, and shall continue for at least 30 minutes
without a noticeable drop in pressure or vacuum.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.56, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1022. - Oil burner controls.
   Oil burner equipment shall be provided with some means for manually stopping
the flow of the oil to the burner, from a conveniently located point at a safe
distance from the burner. With electrically driven equipment this may be
accomplished by a switch in the motor supply circuit, placed near the entrance
to the room where the burner is located. A quick-closing valve in the oil
supply line may be used.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.57, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1023. - Automatic shut down devices.
   Automatically operated oil burners used in connection with vapor, hot water,
steam or warm air heating systems shall be equipped with approved automatic
device to shut down the burner in the event of undue pressure in a steam boiler
or overheating within a hot water boiler or warm air furnace. Each steam boiler
shall be equipped with a low water cut-off.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.58, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1024. - Atomizing supply, cutoff.
   In systems where steam or air used for atomizing the oil, the equipment
shall be so arranged that in case of interruption of the atomizing supply, the
oil supply will immediately shut off.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.59, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1025. - Automatic shut-off on failure of ignition.
   All oil burners shall be equipped with an approved automatic device for the
control or shutoff of the flow of oil in case of failure of the oil in the
combustion chamber to ignite.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.60, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1026. - Installation of controls.
   On all installations where operation of burner is controlled by an aquastat,
pressurestat or furnacestat, a second control either aquastat, pressurestat or
furnacestat, shall be installed in the 110-volt line ahead of all other
controls, as a high limit or safety control.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.61, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1027. - Installation of burner.
   Oil burners shall be securely installed in a workmanlike manner, in
accordance with the instructions of the manufacturer, by qualified mechanics
experienced in making such installations.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.62, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1028. - Conversion from coal; installation.
   Where oil burners are installed in furnaces originally designed for solid
fuel, the ash door of the furnace shall be removed or bottom ventilation
otherwise provided to prevent the accumulation of vapors in the ash pit, unless
the burner is of a type which mechanically purges the ash pit.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.63, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1029. - Oil burners in boilers and furnaces.
   Boilers and furnaces in which oil burners are installed shall be connected
to flues having sufficient draft at all times to assure safe operation of the
burner. Smoke pipe dampers, if any, shall be removed or locked in the desired
position and shall be such that they cannot close off more than 80 percent of
the internal cross section area of the smoke pipe. All check drafts must be
kept closed at all times.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.64, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1030. - Rooms for oil burners—Adequate air supply.
   Rooms in which oil burners are located shall be provided with adequate
ventilation to assure continuous complete combustion of the oil.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.65, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1031. - Same—Instructions posted.
   Complete instructions for the care and operation of the oil burner equipment
shall be conspicuously posted near the oil burner and shall be maintained in
readable condition by user, and there shall be displayed, near the heating
plant, a card which shall read as follows:
   NOTICE: The heating code requires that pipe dampers shall be removed or
locked in the desired position and no damper closing off more than 80 percent
of the pipe area shall be allowed. All check drafts must be kept closed at all
times.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.66, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1032. - Industrial oil burners, plans furnished and posted.
   Contractors installing industrial oil burner systems shall furnish diagrams
showing the main lines and controlling valves, one of which shall be posted
near the oil burner equipment and another at some point which will be
accessible in the case of fire at the burners.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.67, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1033. - Modifications.
   Where the circumstances or conditions of any particular installation are
unusual and such as to render the strict application of this division
impracticable, the inspector may permit such modifications as will provide a
substantially equivalent degree of safety.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.68, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1034. - Fireproofing.
   It shall be the duty of each licensed installer, when installing an oil
burner in connection with a heating plant, to install such fireproofing,
adjacent to the smoke pipe thereof, as may be required to comply with the
following provisions:
      (1)   No metal smoke pipe shall pass through any floor or be nearer than
12 inches to any wood or other combustible portion of the building except as
noted below. All combustible material within 18 inches shall be covered with a
metal or asbestos shield extending at least one foot on each side of the smoke
pipe, and in the case of smoke pipes of a greater diameter than 12 inches and
of less area than six square feet shall be kept at least 16 inches away from
any woodwork. Such woodwork shall be protected as before specified for the
smaller smoke pipes, a distance of three feet on each side of such smoke pipes.
      (2)   Where metal smoke pipes of 12 inches or less in diameter pass
through a wood or plastered stud partition, they shall be surrounded either by
a body of brick, hollow tile, or other incombustible fireproof material of a
thickness of at least four inches around such smoke pipes; or they shall be
surrounded by a sheet metal thimble of two concentric rings at least two inches
apart, and the entire thimble so constructed that there will be a free
circulation of air between the two rings forming the same. Smoke pipes of a
diameter of six inches or less may have thimbles with one inch air space.
      (3)   Where a new smoke pipe is installed, it shall be lockseamed or
riveted, with all joints lapped not less than 1½ inches and rigidly secured,
and shall have a proper thimble for making tight connection to the chimney
flue.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.69, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1035. - Request for inspection, concealment of work.
   Immediately upon the installation of the tanks and concealed piping of an
oil burner installation, the installer thereof shall notify the inspector that
such tanks and piping are ready for inspection by registering the number of the
permit and the location of the work in the inspection register book kept for
that purpose in the office of the inspector. It shall be unlawful for any
person to cover up any such tanks or piping until the same shall have been
inspected and approved by such inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.70, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1036. - Pilot light.
   Gas pilot, acetylene or any other gas possessing a wider range of
explosiveness in a mixture with air and coal gas, or water gas, is prohibited
for use in the gas pilot of any fuel oil burner.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.71, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1037. - Fire extinguisher required.
   In the single residences, every oil burner installation shall have near the
entrance to the furnace room, and readily accessible for convenient use in
emergency, a hand fire extinguisher of at least a quart capacity, approved by
the National Board of Fire Underwriters for extinguishing combustible oil
fires; provided, however, that installations of oil burning equipment in
multiple dwellings, commercial establishments of any kind or description where
the public congregates or persons are permitted to be present on invitation or
otherwise, such installations shall have accessible in the furnace room for
immediate and convenient use in emergency, a fire extinguisher of at least 2½-
gallon capacity, approved by the National Board of Fire Underwriters, and which
shall be foam type or its equivalent; provided further, that in case of great
hazard or danger to the public, the chief of the fire department may, in
writing, require further or additional fire extinguishing apparatus in order to
safeguard public property and life.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 10.72, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-1038—5-1055. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 13. - GAS BURNER INSTALLATIONS **
Sec. 5-1056. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Gas burner shall mean a device for the final conveyance of the gas, or a
mixture of gas and air, to the combustion zone of a conversion gas burner, gas
fired unit heater or water radiator, gas fired boiler, heater or furnace used
in connection with a space heating system.
   Gas burner equipment shall include gas burners and all piping including
supply piping from meter to appliance shutoff valve, blowers, control device
and accessories connected to the burners.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.2, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-1057. - Conformity required.
   The construction, arrangement and manner of installation of all gas burners
and gas burner equipment hereafter installed for use in connection with heating
systems, and the alteration and repair hereafter of all gas burners and gas
burner equipment used or to be used in connection with heating systems, shall
conform to the provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1058. - Permit required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person or his agents to install any gas burner
until an application for a permit shall have been filed with and a permit
issued by the department of building and safety.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1059. - Application for permit.
   The application for a permit to install a burner under the provisions of
this division shall be in the following form:
The undersigned hereby requests that a permit be issued to install the gas
burner described below:
      1.   Address where installation is to be made _____
      2.   Name of burner _____
      3.   Type of burner _____
      4.   B.T.U. input _____
      5.   Name of manufacturer _____
      6.   Address of manufacturer _____
      7.   Kind of fuel recommended for burner _____
      8.   Length of time burner has been on market _____
      9.   Name of approving laboratory and the certificate number _____
      10.   Application filed by _____
      11.   at Dearborn, Michigan, this ____________ day of ____________ /
____________ / ____________ , 19 ____________ .
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1060. - Approval of permit application.
   (a)   The department shall issue a permit for installing any gas designed
furnace or boiler which has been approved by the American Gas Association. It
shall be unlawful to install or cause to be installed in the city any such
furnace or boiler which has not first been approved by the American Gas
Association.
   (b)   A list of all conversion type gas burners shall be maintained by this
department, which, through the arrangement of parts, suitability of materials,
strength of parts, electric or other control, thermostatic arrangement,
sensitivity of automatic features, positiveness of ignition, and possibility of
explosion, have been found, by best or acceptable proof from the American Gas
Association or some equally competent laboratory, to be acceptable to the
heating board of appeals and this department for use in the city under the
provisions of this division.
   (c)   Before a permit will be issued for a conversion type gas fired burner,
each applicant for the installation of such burners must furnish the department
with a photostatic copy or other suitable evidence of the approval or the
official certification by the American Gas Association; provided, however, that
if a particular trade name of burner is listed for the current year in the
Directory of Approved Gas Appliances and listed Accessories, or a supplement
thereto, as published by the American Gas Association Testing Laboratories,
evidence of further approval or certification will not need to be furnished by
the applicant.
   (d)   In addition to the approval or certification by the American Gas
Association, as hereinabove required for conversion type burners, such
conversion type burner must meet the two following requirements:
      (1)   If the burner is of the single port spreader flame type, the main
body of the burner including mixer head and mixer tube shall be of wrought iron
or wrought steel construction. The burner head shall be of wrought iron, alloy
cast iron, or other heat resisting alloys. The spreader plate shall have a
thickness of one-fourth inch if it is constructed of wrought iron, alloy
wrought iron, other heat resisting alloys, or ceramic material, but if the
spreader is made of metal containing at least 25 percent of nickel or chrome
alloy, or some other equally heat resisting metal, the spreader need not be
more than one-eighth inch thick.
      (2)   If the burner is a drilled multiple port type, the cast iron burner
heads with raised drill ports shall be installed without baffles.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1061. - Installation of used gas burners, procedure required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, licensed to install, alter, repair or
replace gas burners within the city, to install any used gas burner or for the
inspector to issue any permit authorizing him so to do, until such licensee
shall have first submitted with his application for such permit a copy of the
purchase order describing the used burner that is to be installed and a
statement by the purchaser acknowledging that to be the case, together with a
statement by such licensee that such burner has been properly reconditioned and
will comply in every way with code requirements for new equipment as to
operation, safety standards and adjustments.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1062. - Ventilation.
   Gas burners shall not be installed in an appliance located in a room where
the normal facilities for ventilation do not permit proper combustion of gas,
unless special provision is made for supplying sufficient air for complete
combustion.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1063. - Flues—Generally.
   All appliance flues through which flue gases are conducted shall be
thoroughly cleaned and examined for leaks and draft conditions before
installation is to be made.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1064. - Same—Installation.
   Means shall be employed which will prevent the flue pipe from entering
beyond the inner wall of the chimney flue. Flue pipe shall be cemented to the
chimney wall so as to prevent infiltration of cold air.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1065. - Same—Corrosive-resistant materials.
   Material used for flue pipe shall be such as to resist the corrosive action
of flue gases.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1066. - Same—Support, location.
   Flue pipe shall be well supported to prevent sagging, shall be adequately
insulated from and in no case shall be located closer than four inches to
combustible building materials.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1067. - Same—Relocation.
   Flue pipe shall be relocated, where necessary, to avoid sharp turns or other
constructional features which would create excessive resistance to the flow of
the flue gases.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1068. - Same—Replacement.
   Where flue pipes are rusted or burned out, they shall be replaced by new
pipe.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1069. - Same—Adjustable damper.
   The proportioned section at the flue outlet of the appliance eliminates the
necessity of using an adjustable damper in the flue pipe.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1070. - Same—Dampers permanently kept open.
   Where dampers are an integral part of the boiler or furnace, they shall be
removed or permanently secured in the wide open position, except such dampers
the function of which is to alter the passage of flue gases through the
appliances, which shall be locked in such a position as not to interfere with
the normal operation of the burners.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1071. - Draft hood—Installation.
   (a)   A draft hood or its equivalent should be installed which is designed
to:
      (1)   Insure the ready escape of the products of combustion in the event
of no draft, backdraft or stoppage beyond the appliance.
      (2)   Prevent a backdraft from entering the appliance.
      (3)   Neutralize the effect of stack action of the flue upon the
operation of the appliance or in the appliance itself.
   (b)   Such device must be approved by the American Gas Association, together
with the appliances and appurtenances thereto.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1072. - Same—Location.
   The draft hood shall be located at a point not lower than the top of the
highest flue passage in the appliance.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1073. - Same—Alternate location.
   The draft hood should ordinarily be located adjacent to the appliance. In
cases where it appears desirable to place the draft hood at a distance from the
appliance, the size of the restricted section may be modified according to the
length and rise of the flue pipe.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1074. - Same—Revertible type.
   Appliances of the revertible flue type shall have the draft hood located at
least one foot higher than the top of the highest flue passage. In all boilers
or furnaces of the revertible flue type, not specifically designed for the use
of gas fuel, proper provision shall be made to prevent the accumulation of gas
in any part thereof, subject to the approval of the inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1075. - Area of flue pipe, draft hood.
   (a)   The internal cross sectional area of the section of the flue pipe
between the outlet of the appliance and the draft hood shall be such as to
provide not less than one square inch of flue area per 7,500 hourly BTU input.
In no case shall this section of flue pipe be less than three inches in
diameter, and it shall not be larger than the next integral inch diameter above
the size given in the following table:
   Minimum Permissible Flue Sizes for Gas Burner Installations

Pipe—Inches�Outlet—Sq. In.Pipe—Inches

147,000       19.6            5

288,750       38.5            7
