477,000       63.3            9
 
   Based on 1 sq. in. flue area per 7,500 B.T.U. per hour input.
   (b)   In cases where the outlet from the appliance is larger than the above
indicated size, an orifice plate may be inserted or a section of the flue pipe
restricted to the size indicated.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1076. - Baffles not to be used.
   No baffles shall be applied which will interfere with the proper combustion
of the gas.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1077. - Heating surfaces.
   The heating surfaces shall be thoroughly cleaned before burners are
installed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1078. - Gastight.
   The combustion chamber and all flue gas passages shall be gastight.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1079. - Doors.
   In converted burners, the fuel door of the heating appliance must be
arranged to relieve pressure due to puffs or backfire caused by delayed
ignition.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.23, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1080. - Installation—Generally.
   Gas burners of all types shall consist of factory assembled and tested units
and shall be accompanied by complete and comprehensive installation and
operation instructions.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.24, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1081. - Same—Location.
   The burner or burners shall be located according to the manufacturer's
instructions and shall be securely fastened in place to prevent twisting,
sliding or dropping out of position.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.25, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1082. - Same—Accessible for cleaning.
   The burners shall be so installed as to be readily accessible for cleaning
and inspection.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.26, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1083. - Same—Combustion control.
   The burner or burners shall be so installed that no part of the flames
impinge so as to cause incomplete combustion.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.27, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1084. - Same—Air shutter adjustment.
   Air shutters shall be adjusted to produce a good flame at the prevailing gas
pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.28, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1085. - Same—Secondary air openings.
   Where secondary air is necessary, secondary air opening or openings shall be
provided of sufficient area to supply an adequate amount of air for complete
combustion.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.29, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1086. - Same—Controls.
   Where an automatic secondary air control is provided, the construction shall
be such that in case the control fails in any way, either the gas will be shut
off or the secondary air door will remain open.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.30, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1087. - Pilots—Required.
   Either a thermostatic pilot, so constructed and adjusted that no gas can
flow through the main burner unless the pilot flame is burning, or some other
similar type of safety device serving this same end shall be employed. The
operation of this safety device shall not depend on the closing of an electric
circuit to shut off the main gas supply.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.31, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1088. - Same—Fixed in stationary position.
   Pilot burners shall be supported in such a manner that their position
relative to the main burner or burners will be fixed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.32, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1089. - Same—Accessible.
   Pilot burner or burners shall be so placed that they can be safely lighted,
and they shall be readily accessible or removable for cleaning.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.33, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1090. - Same—Connection of lines.
   Pilot lines shall be connected to vertical main gas supply lines or to the
side or top of horizontal lines ahead of all controls, except pressure
regulators, and shall be susceptible to independent control.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.34, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1091. - Same—Thermostatic safety.
   Thermostatic safety pilots shall be so adjusted that main gas supply will be
shut off within three minutes after flame has been extinguished.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.35, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1092. - Shut-off valve—Required.
   A manually operated shutoff valve shall be installed at each appliance to
shut off the entire gas supply to the appliance in cases of emergency.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.36, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1093. - Same—Location.
   The shutoff valve shall be so located that it is readily accessible and
shall clearly indicate the "on" and "off" positions or direction of rotation to
open or close.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.37, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1094. - Electric control valves.
   Electric control valves shall be installed according to the instructions
furnished by the manufacturer and comply with article XII of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.38, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1095. - Gas pressure regulators.
   A gas pressure regulator shall be installed on all gas burner installations
for heating purposes.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.39, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1096. - Safety devices—Required.
   The boiler or furnace shall be equipped with safety devices arranged to
limit high steam pressures or water temperatures, as well as high air
temperatures in warm air furnaces.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.40, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1097. - Same—Independent of shut-off main gas supply.
   Safety devices operated electrically shall not depend upon the closing of a
circuit to shut off the main gas supply. This requirement shall not be
construed as prohibiting the use of electrical regulating devices, provided the
required safety devices are also installed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.41, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1098. - Low water cutoff.
   Each gas fired steam boiler shall be equipped with a low water cutoff.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.42, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1099. - Forced primary air control.
   When air under pressure is used in connection with gas supply, effective
means shall be provided to prevent the air from going back into the gas piping.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.43, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1100. - Piping in line direct from meter.
   All gas piping installed for the service of the gas burners to be used in
connection with any heating system shall be supplied by an independent line
direct from the meter.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.44, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1101. - Adjustment of pilot and burners.
   After the piping has been thoroughly purged, the pilot burner shall be
lighted and adjusted and the burners put into operation in accordance with the
manufacturer's instructions.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.45, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1102. - Pilot operation—Generally.
   Pilot flames shall effectively ignite the gas at the main burner or burners
and shall be adequately protected from drafts. A device which is at least equal
in performance to the draft hood shall be interpreted as fulfilling the second
part of this requirement as far as chimney drafts are concerned.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.46, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1103. - Same—Flames not to be extinguished.
   Pilot flames shall not become extinguished when the main burner or burners
are turned on or off in a normal manner, either manually or by automatic
controls.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.47, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1104. - Same—Luminous flame.
   Luminous flame pilots shall be adjusted so as not to show carbon deposits.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.48, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1105. - Electrical devices, approval.
   All automatic or electrical devices used in connection with the operation
and repair of gas burners must be approved by the American Gas Association or
some other nationally recognized board before a permit will be issued therefor
to install such device.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.49, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1106. - Summer cooling.
   Gas burners equipped with summer switches for cooling purposes must have a
key type switch installed.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.50, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1107. - Flame—Regulation.
   The flames from each burner shall freely ignite the gas from adjacent
burners or from each constant burning pilot when operating at the prevailing
gas pressure or when the main control valve is regulated to deliver about one-
third the full gas rate, except where additional pilots are provided.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.51, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1108. - Same—Not to flash.
   When ignition is made in a normal manner, the flames shall not flash outside
the appliance.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.52, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1109. - Same—Not to burn in mixer.
   Burners shall not expel gas through air openings in mixer faces when
operating at the prevailing pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.53, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1110. - Appliance operation, oxygen concentration pressure.
   The concentration of oxygen in the flue products shall in no case be less
than four percent, nor more than ten percent. The rate of flow of the gas shall
be adjusted to within plus or minus five percent of the required hourly BTU
input rating at the manifold pressure specified by the manufacturer. When the
prevailing pressure is less than the manifold pressure specified, the gas rate
shall be adjusted to the prevailing pressure.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.54, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1111. - Appliance—Method of test.
   The appliance shall be allowed to operate until the stack temperature
becomes stabilized, after which a sample of the flue products shall be taken at
a point in the flue after the outlet of the appliance but ahead of the draft
hood and analyzed for carbon dioxide and oxygen.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.55, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1112. - Same—Checked by inspector and installer.
   The various controls of the appliance shall be checked by both inspector and
installer to insure their proper operation.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.56, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1113. - Instructions to the customer—Required.
   The customer shall be thoroughly instructed by the installer as to the
proper and safe operation of the appliance before it is placed in continuous
service.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.57, 11-4-81)
Sec. 5-1114. - Same—Printed and posted.
   Suitable printed instructions shall be supplied by the installer and posted
in a prominent position near the appliance.
(Ord. No. 81-65, § 11.58, 11-4-81)
Secs. 5-1115—5-1129. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE X. - ELECTRICAL CODE ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-1130. - Adopted.
   There is hereby adopted by reference the National Electrical Code, 1999, as
amended, with current Michigan amendments added by the state electrical board.
A copy of such code shall be available in the city clerk's office.
(Ord. No. 97-704, 5-20-97; Ord. No. 00-817, 4-18-00)
Sec. 5-1131. - Short title.
   The short title of this article shall be the Electrical Code of the City of
Dearborn, Michigan.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 1.1, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1132. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Department shall mean the department of building and safety in the city.
   Director shall mean the director of building and safety in the city.
   Inspector shall mean the electrical inspector whose duties are defined and
set forth in this article, and such word shall include in its meaning all
assistants, agents or persons authorized to assist or carry on the work of
electrical inspection under the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 1.2, 2-13-91; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 5-1133. - Exceptions.
   The provisions of this article shall not apply to the following, anything in
this article to the contrary notwithstanding.
      (1)   The installing of radio receiving sets and equipment; provided,
however, the installation of convenience outlets for power to supply such radio
set shall be governed by the provisions of this article.
      (2)   Minor repair work, the replacement of lamps, or the connection of
portable devices to suitable receptacles which have been permanently installed.
      (3)   The installation, alteration or repair of equipment for the
operation of signals, or the transmission of intelligence where such work is an
integral part of the communication system owned and operated by a telephone
company in rendering its duly authorized service as such company, where such
person or company is subject to the jurisdiction of the state public service
commission.
      (4)   The repairing or maintaining of household electrical apparatus or
appliances.
      (5)   The installation, alteration or repair of electric wiring for the
generation and primary distribution of electric current, or the secondary
distribution system up to and including the meters where such work is an
integral part of the system owned and operated by an electric light and power
company in rendering its duly authorized service, where such company is subject
to the jurisdiction of the state public service commission.
      (6)   Any work involved in the manufacture, test or repair of electrical
apparatus, appliances or equipment in a manufacturer's plant but not including
any permanent wiring other than that which is a part of the testing equipment.
      (7)   Any wiring in or on a home and accompanying outbuildings owned,
occupied or to be occupied by the person performing the installation,
alteration or repair of wiring devices, appliances and appurtenances, providing
the inspector deems such person qualified to perform such work, and such person
obtains a permit as required by this article.
      (8)   Any work involved in the manufacture, installation, test or repair
of electrical apparatus, appliance or equipment in conjunction with the
operation of elevators, escalators, dumbwaiters, hoisting machinery, or other
similar electrical equipment, where such work is done on wiring or beyond the
final switch, fuse or circuit breaker on the circuit supplying such equipment.
      (9)   Any work involved in the operating, maintenance, servicing or
repairing of theatrical equipment such as motion picture equipment,
stereopticons, public address systems, spotlights, or other electrical stage
equipment connected or attached to existing permanently installed wiring for
which a permit has been obtained and the installation approved.
      (10)   Any installation of electric wiring and equipment in connection
with carnivals, circuses or other commercial amusements of a temporary and
transient character, provided the person applying for the permit satisfactorily
identifies himself to the inspector that he is a regularly employed electrician
with such carnival, circus or commercial amusement, obtains the necessary
permit therefor and pays the fee required by this article; provided, however,
that the issuance of a permit is subject to the right and authority in the
inspector to prevent the supplying, or to cut off or order cutting off of
electric power, if the provisions of this article as to installation have not
been complied with.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 1.3, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1134. - Enforcement officers.
   (a)   The inspector and any agents designated by the director are hereby
empowered to perform the duties and functions and are hereby given like
authority of regularly authorized and appointed police officers of the city in
the enforcement of the provisions of this article.
   (b)   In addition to the qualifications specified by the civil service rules
of the city for the classification of inspector, every person to be qualified
for such position under this article shall carry an electrical journeyman's
license, issued under the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 1.4, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1135. - Responsibility.
   This electrical code shall not be construed to lessen the liability of any
person owning, operating, controlling or installing any electric wiring,
apparatus, or equipment for damages to the person or property caused by any
defect therein, and shall not be construed so as to impose any liability upon
the city by reason of the requirements for inspection, as set forth in this
article.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 7.3, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1136. - Ohm's law.
   Electrical Formulas
   Ohm's Law Made Easy

Secs. 5-1156—5-1162. - Reserved.
Sec. 5-1163. - Duties of inspector.
   There shall be employed in the department an electrical inspector who shall
be appointed by the director in accordance with the civil service provisions of
the charter. Such inspector shall be directly responsible to the director. The
inspector shall have the following duties:
      (1)   He shall carry out and enforce the terms and provisions of this
article.
      (2)   He shall approve all plans and specifications before permits are
issued under this article covering any work or operations governed by this
article involving the construction, installation, alteration, maintenance or
repair of electrical equipment, wiring, apparatus or devices. If any of such
proposed work or operations do not conform to the requirements of this article,
such permit shall be refused until compliance with this article is made.
      (3)   He shall prepare, subject to the supervision and approval of the
board of review, the examination questions and the acceptable answers thereto
of applicants for licenses under this article, and he shall hear and conduct
all such examinations and correct the examination papers, except as herein
otherwise provided, which examinations may consist of written questions and
answers, oral questions and answers, or practical demonstrations or any
combination of such written and oral questions and demonstrations, which shall
be sufficient to prove the competency of the applicant for the license applied
for. All oral questions and answers shall be reported stenographically and the
transcript thereof made a part of the examination records of the applicant. All
such examination questions shall be kept in the personal files or possession of
the inspector and shall not be left or remain in the general files in the
department; provided, however, that all such answers to the examinations shall
be regarded as confidential and shall be open to inspection only by the members
of the board of appeals, its secretary, or by the applicant himself. After the
electrical inspector has conducted the examinations provided for in this
section and has corrected the written examination papers, as well as the
transcript of the oral examination, and determined the grade or score thereon,
such papers shall be delivered to the board of review for review and approval
or disapproval by it, after which such papers shall be filed with the secretary
of the board.
      (4)   He is hereby authorized to file proceedings to suspend the license
of any person holding a license under this article with the secretary of the
board of review, or to file such proceedings with such secretary to suspend the
permit of any person to whom a permit has been issued under this article for
any of the following reasons:
         a.   Violating the provisions of this article or any law applicable to
the work or operation being performed by such licensee or employee under his
direction, or violating or failing to obey any order of the inspector which he
is authorized under this article to make.
         b.   Making any false statement or representation of material fact in
any application for license or permit to be issued under this article.
         c.   For a master electrician licensee to serve or attempt to serve
under more than one licensed electrical contractor at the same time.
         d.   For a master electrician licensee to fail to notify in writing
the department within 72 hours of the change of employment of such licensee,
where such employment was necessary to qualify his employer as an electrical
contractor.
         e.   For an electrical contractor licensee to take out a permit for
the benefit of another person who is not a licensee of this city to enable such
other person to evade the requirements of the licensing provisions of this
article, or to allow other persons to apply for permits on such license.
         f.   For an electrical contractor licensee not to be or not to have in
his employ a master electrician licensee.
      (5)   He shall be and he is hereby authorized to withdraw the proceedings
to suspend any license or permit without the necessity of a hearing before the
board of appeals, if and when the work or operation in violation of this
article has been made to conform to the provisions of this article or changed
so that it will not be a menace to the public safety.
      (6)   He shall inspect, and if satisfactory, approve all construction,
installation, alteration, replacement or repair work hereafter made or
operations carried on within the city involving any wiring, apparatus,
material, equipment, or device subject to regulations by the provisions of this
article in buildings or structures of all classes in the city.
      (7)   He shall make all necessary tests and inspections of apparatus and
equipment governed by the provisions of this article to determine that such
apparatus or equipment will not be injurious to public safety and will not
create a fire hazard. If such test or inspection shows that any apparatus or
equipment is likely to be injurious to the public safety, he shall not permit
such apparatus or equipment to be installed.
      (8)   He may, in his discretion, and he is hereby authorized to order the
immediate removal of any covering, wiring, construction, alteration or repairs
found to have been installed and concealed or covered up before its inspection
and approval, which wiring, construction, apparatus or equipment is governed by
the provisions of this article.
      (9)   If the inspector at any time discovers that any work or
construction is being done on any buildings or structures in the city, contrary
to the provisions of this article, or any statute now existing or hereafter
adopted, such inspector is hereby authorized and directed to issue a stop work
order as to such electrical work or construction, and to post a notice thereof
on such improper work.
         a.   If such work or construction is being carried on contrary to the
provisions of this article or any such statute, the person doing or performing
such work shall be subject to prosecution for such violation under the terms
hereof, it being hereby intended that such stop work order shall not in any way
exonerate the wrongdoer from his criminal responsibility thereunder.
         b.   After a stop work order has been issued, it shall be unlawful for
any work or construction to be done by any person or persons until the illegal
or improper installation, alteration, repairs or construction has been
corrected and the stop work order removed by the inspector.
         c.   It shall be unlawful for any person other than the inspector to
remove such stop work notice posted as provided in subsection (a) of this
section. If a stop work order is issued by the inspector, he may in his
discretion take into his possession the permit for the construction,
installation or alteration of any electrical wiring, materials or equipment
covered thereby.
      (10)   He shall prepare such forms of applications for permits or
licenses, as required by the provisions of this article.
      (11)   He shall approve the application for electrical contractor's
license and for licenses issued under the provisions of section 5-1193, when
such applicant has complied with all the provisions of this article.
      (12)   He is hereby authorized to give written orders to the clerks in
the department that, and when such orders have been given, no further permits
are to be issued to any licensee under this article when such licensee is
violating the provisions of this article in any way.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 2.8, 2-13-91)
Secs. 5-1164, 5-1165. - Reserved.
Sec. 5-1166. - Right of entry; turning off power.
   The inspector shall have the right during reasonable hours to enter any
buildings or structures covered by the provisions of this article in connection
with which a permit has been requested, or has issued at any time previously
thereto, in the discharge of his official duties, or for the purpose of making
any inspection or test of the installation of electric wiring, material,
equipment or devices therein or thereon. He shall have the authority to turn
off or cause the turning off of any and all electric power, or to cut or
disconnect in cases of emergency any wires where such electric power is
dangerous to life or property.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 2.11, 2-13-91)
Secs. 5-1167—5-1185. - Reserved.

** DIVISION 4. - PERMITS AND FEES **
Sec. 5-1216. - Required, application.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to do or make any electrical
construction, installation, alteration, wiring or repairs in or upon any
building, structure, fixtures or apparatus in the city requiring the use of
electric current, without exclusion for low voltage apparatus, without first
obtaining a permit therefor from the department. Applications for such permit
specifying the address where the work is to be done, the owner of the premises
at such address, and describing in detail the work to be done shall be made by
the licensee who will do the work. A blueprint or sketch of the proposed work
shall accompany the application, if requested by the inspector. The permit
shall be issued only to such applicant who must be a licensee, only after the
applicant has complied with all the provisions of this article, and after the
application therefor has been approved by the inspector. In the event of a
failure to make application for permit within 24 hours of the time work is
started, the fee shall be increased by 100 percent above the amount stated in
the schedule of fees hereinafter set forth or $100.00, whichever is greater.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.1, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1217. - Maintenance work excepted.
   It will be unnecessary for the owner who regularly employs electricians
licensed under this article to apply for a permit in order to perform
electrical maintenance or make repairs on the premises of such owner or
employer.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.2, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1218. - Homeowners.
   (a)   Permits will only be issued under this division to homeowners who are
occupying the one-family home and will continue to occupy the home for a period
of at least one year. No permits will be issued to persons who do not occupy
the home or will be selling the home within one year. An affidavit for the
homeowner to sign with these stipulations shall be a part of the application
form. If the owner intends to occupy the property once repairs are made, a
homeowner's permit may be issued with the approval of the inspector.
   (b)   The following procedure shall be followed in obtaining a homeowner's
permit:
      (1)   Homeowner must make application for permit with the building
department.
      (2)   At the time of application for the permit, the homeowner must
submit proof of ownership, i.e., deed, tax bill, land contract. They must also
provide proof of residency (i.e., driver's license, voter registration or three
pieces of mail which have been received addressed to them at the property).
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.1, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1219. - Voluntary revocation.
   After a permit has been issued under this division and if construction has
not been started pursuant to such division, permittee desiring a revocation of
such permit may, within a period of 90 days from the date of issuance, apply to
the department therefor, and after approval thereof by the inspector, and upon
surrender of such permit and receipt for fees paid, such permit shall thereupon
be revoked, and upon authorization in writing by the department, a refund of
such permit fee shall be made by the department of finance.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.1, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1220. - Fees.
   The fees required for permits under this division shall be paid to the city
treasurer prior to the time that a permit is issued for the work described in
the amount stated; provided, however, that if any permit issued by the
department does not describe all of the work which has been done or is being
done, the inspector is hereby empowered to order the permittee to obtain a
permit and pay the additional prescribed fee covering such work.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.3, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1221. - Inspection; connection.
   At various stages of installation or progress of the work, when an
inspection should be made, or upon the completion of the wiring of or
installation in any building or structure or part thereof, it shall be the duty
of the person performing such work to notify the inspector to inspect the
installation as soon as possible, and if such work is found to be fully in
compliance with the requirements of this article and does not constitute a
hazard to life or property, the inspector, upon application of the permittee,
may issue a certificate of inspection showing compliance with the provisions of
this article. Before any of the electric wiring, apparatus or equipment covered
by any permit issued under this division is connected up to the current and
used, the approval in writing by the inspector to put such electric wiring,
apparatus or equipment into use must be first obtained. In the case of new
installations and the issuance of a certificate of inspection upon final
completion of the job, it shall authorize the connection to the electric
current and the turning on for use. All wires which are to be hidden from view
shall be inspected before being concealed. Any person desiring an inspection as
herein required shall notify the inspector, giving him at least 24 hours within
which to make the required inspection.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.4, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1222. - Voiding of certificate of occupancy.
   If the approval in writing by the inspector to put the electric wiring,
apparatus or equipment covered by any permit into use has not been obtained, as
herein required, or if the owner, occupant or permittee has not requested that
a final inspection be made, or has not completed or caused such electrical work
to be completed in preparation for such final inspection, and if such
unapproved electric wiring, apparatus or equipment has been connected to the
electric current and is being used therewith, such failure to obtain the
written approval from the inspector before using such electric wiring,
apparatus or equipment shall be the basis of voiding and shall void the
certificate of occupancy issued or to be issued in accordance with the
provisions of this Code. The failure of the owner, occupant or permittee to
obtain such approval from the inspector before using such electric wiring,
apparatus or equipment, as required by this article shall also constitute a
violation of this article and shall be punishable as therein provided for any
violation thereof.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.5, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1223. - Reinspection; disconnect current.
   (a)   The inspector shall make periodically, without charge, a reinspection
of the electrical wiring, equipment or apparatus in buildings or other
structures which are installed in the city, and when any such wiring, equipment
or apparatus is found to be in a dangerous or unsafe condition, the person
owning, using or operating the same shall be notified and shall make the
necessary repairs or changes required to place such wiring, apparatus or
equipment in a safe condition within 15 days from the date of such notice. The
inspector is hereby empowered and authorized to disconnect or order the
discontinuance of electric power to such wiring, apparatus or equipment found
to be in a defective condition until such wiring, apparatus or equipment has
been made safe in accordance with the provisions of this article and as
directed by the inspector.
   (b)   If a reinspection is made necessary because inferior or illegal
workmanship or materials are used in connection with the work covered by any
permit issued under this article, a flat charge of $25.00 shall be made by the
city for each such reinspection against the permittee, and until such charge is
paid, such permittee shall not be entitled to take out or have issued to him
any other or additional permits by the department. Such failure to pay shall
constitute a violation of the provisions of this article by such permittee.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.6, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1224. - Prerequisites for issuing certificate of inspection.
   No certificate of inspection shall be issued unless the electrical
installation or construction is in strict conformity with the requirements of
this article and the statutes of the state. Approved methods of construction
for safety to persons and property as laid down in the National Electrical Code
and approved by the American Standards Association are hereby recommended as
good practice to be followed in the installation of electrical wiring.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 4.7, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1225. - Carnival and circus wiring, permit required.
   It shall be unlawful to install electrical wiring, apparatus or materials
for or by carnivals, circuses or other commercial amusements of a temporary or
transient character in the city, unless and until a permit has been issued as
specified in this article.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.8, 2-13-91)
Secs. 5-1226—5-1240. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR INSTALLATION **
Sec. 5-1241. - Approved materials.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful to install or use any electrical wiring, device,
apparatus or equipment designed for attachment to, or installation on, any
electrical circuit or system for heat, light or power that is not of good
design and construction and safe and adequate for its intended use. The
inspector shall have power to disapprove the use or installation of such
materials not fulfilling these requirements. Wiring, devices, apparatus or
equipment approved by such generally recognized authorities as United States
Bureau of Standards, Electrical Testing Laboratories of New York, or
Underwriters' Laboratories shall be held to have the approval of the inspector
unless explicitly disapproved by such inspector for reasons of faulty design
and poor construction involving danger to person or property.
   (b)   The inspector shall inspect devices, apparatus and equipment offered
to the public for use in installation to see that such items conform to the
above requirements when requested to do so.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.1, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1242. - Prerequisites for installation.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to install any wiring or electrical
devices in a building or structure previous to the roughing in of heating or
plumbing construction, or before the roof on such building or structure is
completed.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.2, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1243. - Presence of licensee may be required.
   The inspector reserves the right to require a representative of the
electrical contractor licensee to be on the job when final inspection is made.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.3, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1244. - Submission of plans and specifications.
   (a)   A detailed set of plans and specifications shall be submitted with the
application for a permit for any electrical installations, alterations,
repairs, or wiring in the following types of buildings or structures:
      (1)   Commercial.
      (2)   Manufacturing.
      (3)   Amusement.
      (4)   Religious.
      (5)   Educational.
   (b)   Such plans and specifications shall show the number of circuits, mains
and submain conductor sizes, wattage per outlet, and methods of construction
drawn with symbols of a standard form. Such plans and specifications shall be
prepared by a registered architect or engineer, and must be approved by the
inspector prior to the issuance of a permit for such work.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.4, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1245. - Blueprints available on job.
   Blueprints or plans, after being approved by the inspector, shall be
available for use by the inspector on the job at any time during the course of
construction.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.5, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1246. - Notice of inspection.
   Any notice of wiring inspection shall be posted in or on the job only by the
inspector.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.6, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1247. - Removal of violation notices.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to remove a violation notice from the
premises by anyone other than the inspector or his authorized agent.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 5.7, 2-13-91)
Secs. 5-1248—5-1265. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 6. - SPECIFIC CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS **
Sec. 5-1266. - Amendments to electrical code.
   The following sections of the National Electrical Code, 1990 Edition are
hereby revised as follows:
   (a)   Section 230. 
      (1)   Service equipment for residential occupancies of four units or
less. Single phase 100 amp service panel boards rated 125 ampere providing
space for 20 full size overcurrent devices with 100 amp main. Service cable
shall be armored type assembly enclosed by concentric neutral.
      (2)   Service equipment for multiple dwellings of over four occupancies.
One main service and disconnect means for necessary connected load. Unless all
current is through a bank of metering devices grouped in such a manner that
there will be a maximum of six disconnects, all such multiple dwellings must
have individual service disconnects. Where six or more two-wire branch circuits
are installed, 100 ampere service is necessary. All others the service
disconnecting means shall have a rating of not less than 60 amperes.
      (3)   In computing the maximum number of 15 or 20 ampere breakers per
bus-bar pole is based on ten amperes for each over current device (U. L. CTL
concept). Difficulties with subpanels and so-called half-size and duplex-type
circuit breakers replacing full size circuit breakers, on the basis of two
poles for one, leads to doubling the number of branch circuit over-current
devices, and resulting in overcrowding with wiring and overheated panel boards.
Where no physical means for installation of all overcurrent devices necessary
exists, anticipated seizure rating has to be increased.
      (4)   Service panel.
         a.   Panel not intended to be used as a junction box or for mounting
devices, bell transformers, handy boxes for receptacles.
         b.   Install service entrance cable perpendicularly (avoid unnecessary
outside horizontal run) directly from meter can to service panel.
         c.   Distribute conductors entering top of service panel (use knock-
outs provided) dissipation of heat and withdrawal of conductors without damage
to their insulation is not possible.
         d.   Mount service panel in vertical position.
         e.   Conductors other than service entrance cable shall not occupy
same entrance knockout in service panel.
         f.   A No. 6 service grounding electrode copper conductor shall be
bonded effectively to a cold water galvanized or copper pipe no smaller than
three-fourths inch trade size. Bond water meter.
         g.   Not more than one conductor shall be connected to the neutral and
grounding bar by a single (screw) pressure connector.
         h.   Two conductors on one circuit breaker or fuse device is
prohibited.
         i.   Provide grounding bar for grounding conductors.
      (5)   Existing main panels, sub-panels, fuse blocks, knob-tube platforms,
and associated hardware located in basement, garage or apartment hallways or
closets shall be removed. Enclosure in plastered wall can be used as a junction
box after removing devices or apparatus connected within.
   (b)   Article 220-32. Minimum size of conductors. 
      (1)   Residential occupancies, four dwelling units or less, each service
entrance conductor shall be minimum three-wire, copper, No. 2 A.W.G.
      (2)   In all other occupancies over four dwelling units demand factors
shall be permitted National Electrical Code article 220-32.
(Ord. No. 91-511, §§ 6.1, 6.2, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1267. - Service entrance conductors.
   (a)   Overhead. Overhead service entrance conductors on or in all buildings
of other than single and up to and including four-family dwellings shall be
installed in rigid conduit, electrical metallic tubing or busway, or other
similar approved means. A minimum vertical clearance abovegrade shall be 12
feet for service drop conductors to all buildings used for other than
residential purposes. For single and two-family services, see article 230
section 24. Service entrance cables extended horizontally along the exterior of
building shall be supported at least every three feet. Horizontal runs adjacent
to alleys or driveways shall be elevated at least eight feet abovegrade.
Service cable shall be equipped with service cable weatherhead above point of
attachment.
      (1)   Service entrance conductors underground shall have a depth of not
less than 30 inches measured from present surface of ground or final grade,
whichever is lower. Conductors entering a building shall be protected to the
point of entrance. Where the enclosure or raceway is subject to physical
damage, the conductors shall be installed in rigid metal conduit, schedule 80
rigid P.V.C.
      (2)   Service drops, supports or brackets shall not be attached to
chimneys or to fire or parapet walls extending above the roofline. A suitable
support shall be provided at all locations.
   (b)   Temporary service. All outdoor temporary service equipment must be
enclosed in a raintight enclosure or equipment approved for outdoor use with
suitable provision for locking. One-hundred- twenty-five volt, single-phase 15
or 20 ampere receptacles shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection
for personnel.
   (c)   Location. Service equipment shall not be located in coal bins,
bathrooms, lavatories or clothes closets. Where practicable, it should be
located in the basement or utility room. If installed in a finished wall in the
living area, it is recommended that provisions be made for addition of extra
circuits when reserve capacity exists. Recessing panelboards into plastered
walls or totally enclosed panelboards shall be avoided; accessibility and
working space are very necessary to provide easy access for maintenance,
circuit additions and heat transfer. In single- and two-family dwellings, this
equipment shall be at least four feet from the deck grade, shall not be subject
to mechanical injury or shall be provided with suitable protection. Sufficient
clearance and accessibility shall be provided when installed in basement near
laundry trays, oil tanks, or other permanently installed obstructions.
   (d)   Dead front requirement. Direct current 0-30 ampere and single phase 0-
125 ampere service equipment shall be dead front in residential occupancies up
to and including four-family occupancies and shall be designated service
equipment or suitable for use as service entrance equipment. Dead front
equipment is equipment having no live parts exposed whereby accidental contact
may be made.
   (e)   Two hundred ampere service. Consult local inspection authority when
service equipment is 200 ampere or larger.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.3, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1268. - Extension cords.
   (a)   Porcelain or metal shell sockets or any key socket on cord pendants
are not permissible within reach of grounded portion of building.
   (b)   Remove extension cords supplying laundry appliances and illegal light
fixtures. The use of an extension cord represents a conflict with requirements
of code in that it would serve as a substitute for laundry receptacle to be
located near the appliance. Extension cords are intended for temporary use with
portable appliances, tools, and similar equipment which are not normally used
at one specific location.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.4, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1269. - Bathrooms and laundry rooms.
   Bathrooms and laundry rooms require mechanical ventilation in accordance
with the BOCA National Mechanical Code, 1990. Metal duct and separate switch
shall be provided. Commercial locations shall be operated simultaneously with
the light on one switch.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.5, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1270. - Built-in exhaust fans.
   Duct work and wiring for exhaust fans must be completely installed before
calling for inspection. A permit shall be required for each fan to be
installed.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.6, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1271. - Cables.
   Steel, nonmetallic sheath or other cables terminating at lighting or other
outlets for fixtures or wiring devices shall be stripped, and all joints made
up before rough-in inspection.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.7, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1272. - Nonmetallic sheath cable.
   All grounding conductors must be parallel with nonmetallic sheath cable. All
outlets shall be grounded.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.8, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1273. - Types of wiring prohibited.
   Open conductors installed on exterior of buildings are prohibited except
secondary wiring for gas tube lighting, which may be installed with approved
cable. Overhead conductors between buildings to signs, floodlights, garages and
outbuildings are prohibited.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.9, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1274. - Underground wires and cables.
   (a)   When installed under concrete driveways, walks, floors or footings
shall be in conduit or other suitable raceways so they may be readily removed
or replaced. Vertically out of trench steel conduit (ells and riser) or
schedule 80 PVC shall be provided for physical protection.
   (b)   All direct burial cable or conductors or wiring in conduit shall be
installed a minimum of 18 inches belowgrade and shall be suitably protected
from mechanical injury.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.10, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1275. - Wire connectors.
   Wire connectors, U.L. approved, when used, shall be of a type having metal
conductors.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.11, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1276. - Maximum watts per circuit.
   The maximum allowable connected watts per circuit of No. 14 wire shall be
1200 watts, 80 watts per ampere.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.12, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1277. - Single phase motors.
   AC single phase motor of one-sixth horsepower or larger shall be on separate
circuit unless each motor is provided with running protection.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.13, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1278. - Minimum wattage requirements.
   The following minimum requirements for wattage shall be observed in
constructing, installing, altering or repairing residence lighting outlets;
      (1)   Living rooms, dining room, library, den, ceiling, 200 watts;
sidewalls, 75 watts.
      (2)   Sun parlor, bedroom, recreation room, ceiling, 100 watts;
sidewalls, 75 watts.
      (3)   Bathroom, kitchen, breakfast room, pullman diner, utility room,
ceiling, 100 watts; sidewalls, 50 watts.
      (4)   Basement, porch, pantry, vestibule, hallways, attic, closets,
toilets, 50 watts.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.14, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1279. - Wattage schedule.
   The following wattage schedule shall be observed in the constructing,
installing, altering or repairing of residence receptacle outlets.
      (1)   In living room, library, den, one outlet for each 12 linear feet of
wall space or major fraction thereof. Doors, arches, windows, mantles, and
including any wall space two feet or more in width or free-standing bar-type
counters, shall be included in measurement. Each outlet shall be 120 watts.
      (2)   In dining room, sun parlor, bedroom, first or second floor hall,
one outlet for each 12 linear feet of wall space or major fraction thereof.
Doors, arches, and windows shall be included in measurements. Each outlet shall
be 120 watts except bedroom, which shall be 80 watts.
      (3)   In kitchen, breakfast room or utility room, at least two 20-ampere
small appliance circuits, in addition to a separate 20 ampere circuit for the
refrigerator or freezer. Outlets installed within six feet of kitchen sink
above countertop surfaces shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter
protection for personnel, with a minimum of four outlets. Not more than six
outlets shall be connected to each circuit. Counter space wider than 12 inches
requires receptacle outlet.
      (4)   In bathroom or washroom at least one ground-fault circuit-
interrupter receptacle installed not less than 30 inches and not more than 48
inches above the floor adjacent to the wash basin and not more than four feet
from the basin, 120 watts. Extending G.F.C.I. receptacle device in series
outside of individual bathroom is not permitted. G.F.C.I. receptacle device is
required for each bathroom.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.15, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1280. - Residence special outlet wattage schedule.
   The following residence special outlet wattage schedule shall be observed in
constructing, installing, altering, or repairing of various rooms indicated:
      (1)   Bathroom built in heater, fireplace, laundry, motors for heating
furnaces and garage doors, according to rating of device, but shall be not less
than 1200 watts each.
      (2)   Transformers for control equipment shall be at least 100 watts
each. A separate transformer shall be provided for each of the following:
         a.   Gas heater control.
         b.   Heating plant control.
      (3)   Chime transformers shall be 50 watts each.
      (4)   Single-phase, 15-20 ampere receptacle shall be installed in a
basement, shall have ground-fault circuit, interrupter protection for
personnel, shall be rated 120 watts, in addition to any provided for laundry
equipment.
      (5)   Receptacle installed for the attachment of portable cords shall be
rated not less than 15 amperes, 125 volts, or 15 amperes, 250 volts, and shall
be mounted on vertical walls.
      (6)   At least one individual branch circuit of not less than 15 ampere
capacity shall be installed for the heating equipment. A readily accessible
disconnect switch shall be mounted on the exterior of the heating equipment or
on a surface adjacent to the heating equipment. Heating equipment which is not
readily accessible shall have an additional disconnect installed at the nearest
readily accessible location.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.16, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1281. - Minimum requirements for dwellings.
   The following minimum requirements must be observed in the constructing,
installing, altering, or repairing of single and multiple dwellings:
      (1)   No branch circuit shall be connected to serve more than one
apartment.
      (2)   Distribution panels shall be located in the apartment which they
serve or in a public space, and shall not be located in bathrooms.
      (3)   Stairways shall be provided with lighting outlet or outlets that
will adequately light each stair section.
      (4)   Unless served from a separate house meter, stairway outlets shall
be controlled from the circuit or apartment using same.
      (5)   Three-point switches shall be installed on all stairway lighting
outlets.
      (6)   Separate bell transformers shall be installed for each apartment,
unless a common transformer is connected to the house meter bell, chime or
enunciating system and contact switch required at residential entrances.
      (7)   Halls, corridors and passageways in all multiple dwellings and
motels shall have at least one light outlet every 20 feet or major fraction
thereof.
      (8)   Basements shall have one light outlet minimum for each 200 square
feet. Furnace, laundry and enclosed or partitioned area must be provided with a
light outlet.
      (9)   Clothes closets and storage spaces shall have at least one light
outlet installed therein. A wall switch control shall be provided at the
entrance to each clothes closet. Clearance between the fixture and a storage
area where combustible material may be stored is not less than 18 inches,
(fluorescent fixture six inches clearance). Recessed fixture shall have thermal
protection. Attics with scuttle holes must have a light near the opening and a
light required back of all knee-walls.
      (10)   Laundry washing machine receptacle outlet shall be a separate
circuit of 20 ampere capacity and shall be at height of the laundry trays and
within six feet of intended location of the equipment. The circuit must
terminate in an outlet box on the wall. Mechanical protection (E.M.T.) for
circuit below ceiling level must be provided. This receptacle shall be rated 20
ampere, grounding type 125 volts.
      (11)   A lighting outlet shall be placed over each set of laundry trays,
and may be connected to same circuit as that serving the laundry equipment.
      (12)   Bathrooms and washrooms shall have switches controlling all lights
therein. Mechanical fans shall be installed in all bathrooms and toilet rooms.
See sections
5-1270 and
5-1271.
      (13)   Wall switches shall be required for every habitable room; in
bathrooms, hallways, stairways, attached garages, and detached garages with
electric power, and outdoor entrances or exits.
      (14)   An approved grounding type receptacle within sight of equipment
and readily accessible at rear wall with a disconnecting means heavy duty 3-
wire No. 16 service cord shall be provided for residential food waste grinders.
A control switch above the counter mounted adjacent to the sink. Recess outlets
into walls. Separate 15 amp circuit shall be provided.
      (15)   A convenience outlet ground-fault circuit interrupter shall be
installed on front and one on rear of each dwelling. These must be on a
separate circuit, and each outlet must be separately switched. Switches must be
separated from each other.
      (16)   A spotlight shall be installed on the rear of each residence at a
height sufficient to provide lighting for rear yard; must be switched at or
near side door if one is provided. Fixture must be directional so light can be
adjusted not to trespass property boundaries.
      (17)   Multiple dwellings and motels which do not have a central air-
conditioning system must provide at least one 220-volt convenience outlet in
close proximity to an outside window in each dwelling unit.
      (18)   Halls, corridors, and passageways in multiple dwelling and motels
shall have at least one convenience outlet installed, spaced so no electrical
cord will require to reach over 30 feet.
      (19)   A 20 ampere 120 volt No. 12 A.W.G. conductor shall be largest size
branch circuit permitted in attached and detached residential garages. All
overcurrent devices must be located at service panel; when more than one
circuit is provided, a potential of 120 volts must be maintained. All circuits
are to originate from same bus at service panel board. Garage branch circuits
shall serve garage only.
      (20)   Every newly constructed single or multiple dwelling unit shall be
provided with smoke detectors. The detectors shall be approved or listed by a
recognized independent testing laboratory and, when actuated, shall provide an
alarm suitable to warn the occupants within the individual dwelling unit. A
minimum of one smoke detector shall be located in each of the following areas:
         a.   In each apartment, suite or sleeping area.
         b.   In the basement at the head of the landing leading to the ground
level floor.
         c.   Any other areas of the dwelling which, by reason of the dwelling
layout, would not be protected by detectors located in subsection a. or b.
above. Each detector shall be interlocked and electrically wired and connected
to any lighting circuit.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.17, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1282. - Commercial requirements.
   (a)   The following specifications must be complied with in the
constructing, installing, altering or repairing of commercial buildings or
structures.
      (1)   Distribution panels shall be located in the office, offices, store
or stores, which they serve or in a readily accessible place and shall not be
located in washrooms or toilets. Service entrance conductors for all buildings
used for other than residential purposes shall be installed in rigid conduit or
electrical metallic tubing.
      (2)   Service equipment. Minimum 100 ampere service equipment with No. 2
A.W.G. CU type RH., or equal wire, shall be provided for stores, apartment
houses, industrial plants, machine shops, service garages or occupancies
greater than four units, operating on a voltage of less than 300 volts to
ground and less than 1,200 amperes capacity shall be required for connected
load and floor area of more than 300 square feet. A main switch with four
wires, three blades solid neutral, or one three wire, three blade switch for
power and one three wire, two blade solid neutral for lighting shall be
required. Where the voltage to ground of service exceeds 300 volts, the current
issue of the National Electric Code, as adopted by the state, shall be
followed. Service to be protected from mechanical injury, where abutting an
alley or driveway, to a minimum height of at least six feet above the earth.
All commercial services must be installed either in rigid steel conduit,
approved for outside use, or of designed copper bus service, suitable for type
of occupancy of building.
      (3)   Coil cabinet (ct's used for metering over 200 amp services) shall
not be used as junction box, raceway or distribution center. Conductors of size
1/0 or larger shall be permitted to be connected in parallel, electrically
joined at both ends to form a single conductor, and terminate at a bus,
disconnect or auxiliary gutter.
      (4)   No. 12 wire shall be the minimum size conductor permitted and have
over current protection of 15 amperes for maximum 1,200 watts connected
lighting load. Rigid conduit or E.M.T. or flexible conduit must be used.
Exception-conduit shall have wire fill marked for inspection if conductors are
counted, when applying the provisions of National Electrical Code Note 8 of
Table 310-16.
      (5)   Receptacle plug outlets in industrial plants, machine shops,
service garages or similar occupancies, shall be limited to four per circuit.
      (6)   Special outlets, store type buildings, in addition to other code
requirements, at least one three-fourth-inch rigid metal conduit or E.M.T.
shall be provided from the distribution panel to a point approximately midway
on each longitudinal wall and at least one receptacle outlet shall be installed
thereto. These outlet boxes to be flush with facing of finish wall. This
requirement is for first floor only unless specifically omitted in approved
electrical plan.
      (7)   Receptacle plug outlets shall not be on a circuit with lighting
outlets except in residences or residential portions of other buildings.
      (8)   Exit and emergency light requirements shall be installed in a
three-fourths-inch conduit with no other wiring. Duo-voltage unit equipment
shall originate from the same panelboard as that of the normal lighting
circuits and is provided with a circuit breaker with a lock-on feature.
Emergency illumination shall include all required means of egress lighting,
illuminated exit signs and all other lights as necessary to provide required
illumination.
      (9)   When a drain is installed in a transformer room, such a drain must
have a liquid seal of not less than three inches in depth. This seal may be
supplied by water which is permitted to bypass into the trap from a water
supply connection to a basin fountain or similar fixture or such seal may be
made of a nonexplosive liquid such as a low grade engine oil.
      (10)   Elevator escalator machine rooms shall be wired for at least one
lighting and one convenience outlet.
      (11)   A sign outlet rated at 1,500 watts consisting of an approved
fitting with blank cover shall be provided for each store section or new or
remodeled buildings with new fronts, located at least ten feet above sidewalk
on front wall, connected with three-fourths inch minimum size conduit. Sign
conduit to be rigid or E.M.T., where practical, and installed independent of
other outlets or conductors. At least one circuit of No. 12 wires with 20
ampere double pole lock type switch shall be installed for each out-of-door
sign outlet.
      (12)   A 125-volt, single-phase receptacle outlet ground-fault circuit-
interrupter protection for personnel shall be located on the same level and
within 20 feet of rooftop heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration
equipment. Receptacle outlet shall not be connected to load side of equipment
disconnecting means. Install disconnect on outer surface or within six feet of
each unit, easily located during emergency. Each office or commercial building
to have one 220 volt receptacle outlet, preferably near an outside window for
air-conditioning, unless building has an overall air-conditioning unit.
      (13)   All alarm wiring be installed in a separate conduit. This wiring
must be an approved system and installed in strict accordance with
manufacturers recommendations and Life and Safety Code 101 and N.F.P.A. 72.
      (14)   The minimum size of commercial service shall be four No. 2 copper
conductors, three phase required.
      (15)   Masonry walls must have proper channels for conduit or conduits to
be installed in walls when constructed.
      (16)   No installation of plumbing equipment, refrigeration equipment,
space heating equipment, duct work, cabinet partitions, or materials shall be
made which will render the wiring in any electrical service equipment,
distribution panel, outlet, splice, junction box or pull box inaccessible.
Minimum clearance of three feet (horizontal) must be maintained from electrical
equipment.
      (17)   Bathroom and washrooms in commercial building shall have wall
switches controlling all lights therein. Mechanical fans shall be installed in
all bathrooms and toilet rooms. See sections
5-1270 and
5-1271. Receptacles shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection.
      (18)   All raceways underground or in concrete to equipment located
outside the building in gasoline dispensing stations or similar properties
shall be rigid metal conduit, galvanized or sheradized and not smaller than
three-fourths inch. Raceways shall be run to each pump on the islands with a
sealoff at the pump and another at first opening on supply end.
      (19)   Type AC cable is a fabricated assembly of insulated conductors in
a flexible metallic enclosure. A green grounding conductor shall be included.
      (20)   Flexible metal conduit shall be one-half inch minimum; a green
grounding conductor shall be included and properly terminated. Exception:
three-eighths inch permitted for furnace and boiler wiring.
      (21)   Electrical equipment, conduit or devices shall not be mounted
directly on roof or parapet walls. Maintenance coating applied to roofs and
parapets coat and seal electrical equipment preventing safe operation and
access having a deteriorating effect. Coated and concealed conduits are very
hazardous.
      (22)   A detailed set of plans and specifications shall be submitted with
the application for building permit for any wiring or alteration to the
electrical system.
   (b)   The electrical drawing must include such details as lighting layouts,
circuiting, switching, copper conductor and conduit sizes. Also, wattage,
schedule, panel schedule, service location, riser diagram, calculations and
proposed method of construction drawn with symbols of a standard form.
Designer's responsibility is to comply with National Electrical Code and this
article.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.18, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1283. - Gas-tube lighting exceeding 600 volts.
   The following minimum requirements shall govern the constructing,
installing, altering or repairing of gas-tube lighting exceeding 600 volts:
      (1)   All wiring and accessories used in the fabrication of gas-tube
lighting systems shall be of approved material.
      (2)   Transformers shall be of the enclosed type and shall be installed
so as to be accessible at all times. Secondary voltage rating shall not exceed
15,000 volts, 120 milliamperes.
      (3)   Transformers not incorporated in fixtures shall be equipped with
standard steel outlet boxes for primary connections.
      (4)   Transformers shall be equipped with approved housing for secondary
connections, PK's and quick connect connectors.
      (5)   Transformers in exposed show-windows or with inside wall signs
shall be equipped with externally operable switch mounted on transformer, which
shall open all primary conductors, switches shall be indicating type.
Mechanical protection facing or backing on gas-tubing at a height of less than
eight feet shall be provided.
      (6)   Gas-tube lighting fixtures using more than one transformer shall be
so connected that disconnecting switch controlling primary will de-energize all
conductors.
      (7)   Transformer shall be provided with center tap on secondary winding,
which shall be grounded to transformer case.
      (8)   All series connections shall be made with approved connectors,
using GTO 15 UL high-voltage cable, and where overall connecting cable is
installed in plenum walls, high voltage shield insulator incased in one-half
minimum greenfield shall be provided.
      (9)   Warning sign stating high voltage shall be posted at each
transformer visible to a service man.
      (10)   All transformer cases, outlet boxes and metal parts shall comply
with article 250 grounding, National Electrical Code.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.19, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1284. - Temporary light and power facilities.
   (a)   Where electric lighting for temporary barricades is used, it shall be
on independent circuits and arranged to burn continuously, lamps shall be
protected by suitable guards or by elevation.
   (b)   Branch circuits for construction purposes supplying energy for
temporary light and power outlets shall be not smaller than No. 12 A.W.G. for
distances less than 125 feet from source of supply. Circuits in excess of 125
feet shall be not less than No. 10 A.W.G. Receptacles shall be 125 volt, single
phase, 15 or 20 ampere, and it shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter
protection for personnel; not more than four such outlets per circuit. Lighting
outlets shall be limited to eight per circuit.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.20, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1285. - Theatres and places of assembly.
   (a)   National Electrical Code articles 518 and 520 and requirements of
section 8 NFPA 101 Life Safety Code Handbook shall be complied with for
theatres and places of assembly.
   (b)   Any portable electrical equipment employed by vaudeville, stock
companies or other shows shall be inspected.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.21, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1286. - Communication systems.
   (a)   Lighting conductors: a separation of five feet shall be maintained
between open conductors of communication systems on buildings and lighting
conductors.
   (b)   Grounding conductor: insulated No. 14 A.W.G. shall comply with article
800 National Electrical Code.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.22, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1287. - Community antenna television systems.
   (a)   The coaxial cable shall be permitted to deliver low-energy power to
equipment directly associated with the radio frequency distribution system, if
the voltage is not over 60 volts and if the current supply is from a
transformer or other device having energy-limiting characteristics.
   (b)   Bond CATV system coaxial cable sheath to the electrical power ground.
The earth ground shall not be used as an equipment grounding conductor or
bonding conductor, as it will not have the low-impedance path needed.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.23, 2-13-91)
Sec. 5-1288. - Mechanical execution of work.
   Electrical equipment shall be installed in a neat and workmanlike manner.
This article is not intended as a design specification nor an instruction
manual for untrained persons.
(Ord. No. 91-511, § 6.24, 2-13-91)
Secs. 5-1289—5-1305. - Reserved.
