Sec. 5-1331. Purpose.
   (a)   This article promotes safe, well-maintained, vibrant and attractive
residential and business districts while reasonably accommodating the need for
signs to function for the purposes for which they are intended. The regulations
contained in this article are written to directly address these purposes and
intents and to provide the least restrictive means to accomplish their ends.
   (b)   The regulations contained in this article recognize that the
individual's right to convey a message must be balanced against the public's
right to be free of signs which unreasonably compete with one another and
negatively impact traffic and safety. This article provides a consistent set of
sign regulations providing businesses and individuals with an opportunity to
attract the public, while providing uses that are substantially the same in
character with similar treatment.
   (c)   While this article recognizes that signs and outdoor advertising are
necessary to promote commerce, improve navigation and provide public
information, failure to require reasonable regulation of signs may lead to poor
identification of individual businesses, deterioration and blight, conflicts
between different types of land uses, and negative impacts on traffic safety.
Oversized, moving or improperly placed signs can, if not regulated, become a
nuisance, cause depreciation of property values, pedestrian and driver
confusion and distraction, and endanger the public health, safety and welfare.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18)
Sec. 5-1332. Intent.
   The intent of this article is to:
   (1)   Support the Master Plan's various character areas such as Great
Neighborhoods, Main Street Michigan Avenue, and Destination Commercial
Districts, as well as to support the purposes and recommendations of various
Area Specific Plans and special plans adopted in support of orderly development
of the city.
   (2)   Ensure that signs are located, designed, constructed, installed and
maintained in a way that protects public health, safety and welfare.
   (3)   Prohibit signs that are structurally unsafe, poorly maintained, and/or
cause unsafe traffic conditions by distracting motorists.
   (4)   Protect the aesthetic quality of neighborhoods and commercial
districts.
   (5)   Ensure that the constitutionally guaranteed right of free speech is
protected.
   (6)   Reduce conflict between public signs used for purposes of traffic
safety, identification of traffic controls, and other governmental purposes,
and private signs.
   (7)   Reinforce and support the desired character of each zoning district in
a manner that takes into consideration building scale and massing, lot size,
building setbacks, transparency, street dimensions, travel speed and pedestrian
presence so that signs contribute to the streetscape and aid in creating a
"sense of place."
   (8)   Allow for adequate and effective signs for business identification and
other appropriate commercial and non-commercial speech.
   (9)   Allow for the dissemination of public information as may be required
by law.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18)
Sec. 5-1333. Definitions.
   The words and phrases set forth below shall have the meaning stated when
used in this article, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:
   Awning shall mean a roof-like covering of canvas, or similar material, over
a door or window to provide protection against the sun, wind or rain
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6392.png]
 
   Banner shall mean a sign made of fabric, cloth, paper or other non-rigid
material that is typically not enclosed in a frame.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6394.png]
 
   Building sign shall mean a sign that identifies the building, rather than a
specific tenant of that building, commonly used in multi-tenant buildings to
identify strip commercial centers or office towers. In case of single tenant
buildings, the tenant and building sign may be the same sign.
   City shall mean the City of Dearborn.
   Department shall mean the Department of Economic Development.
   Director shall mean the director of the Department of Economic Development.
   Display area shall mean the gross area of the display panel or that area of
the wall or surface which is bounded by a series of straight lines which
enclose the complete sign unit, notwithstanding any physical separation between
parts.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6396.png]
 
   Electronic open sign means any electronic sign that is placed in a window or
affixed to a wall of a building, and which exclusively displays the word "open"
during the hours that the building or building unit is open to the public for
its usual business purpose.
   Electronic signs shall include electronic message boards and changeable
message centers, multimedia or computer-controlled variable message and display
signs, scrolling marquees, LED signs, and similar devices, whether standing
alone, incorporated within another sign, affixed to a building, or displayed in
a window so as to be visible from a roadway. The definition shall include
electronic open signs as defined in this article except as otherwise provided
in this article.
   Flag shall mean an item made of cloth, nylon, vinyl, or similar material,
varying in shape, size, color or design, usually attached at one end to a staff
or cord, used primarily as a symbol of a nation, state or organization.
   Ground sign shall mean any freestanding sign supported by and anchored
directly to the ground on privately owned property. Ground signs shall include
pole and monument signs.
   Glare shall mean any light emanating directly from a light source that has
the potential to create visual discomfort or momentary blindness when viewed.
   Historical signs and markers shall mean non-commercial plaques which tell
the story of some event, personality or a combination of the two of some
historical significance within the community.
   Message-casting (or projected) signs shall mean signs that are displayed by
"shooting", "casting", or "projecting" laser light, visible light beams, and/or
light images onto the ground, sidewalk, wall, or other visible surface, or into
the sky as part of a sign.
   Monument sign shall mean a ground sign mounted on a base directly to the
ground.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6398.png]
 
   Person shall mean a natural person, firm, co-partnership, corporation, or
voluntary association.
   Projecting sign shall mean any sign that extends beyond the building wall,
where the horizontal sign surface is not parallel to the building wall.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6400.png]
 
   Roof sign shall mean any sign mounted on or over the roof of a building.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/6d11f253bc485db6ae9c03eb2e030fa7490a0bbc/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6402.png]
   Sandwich board sign shall mean any sign that is constructed of two flat
pieces joined at the top with a hinge device so that the sign stands up as an
inverted "V."
   Sign shall mean any announcement, declaration, figure, billboard,
illustration, insignia or display (including bulbs and other lighting devices)
when designed and placed so as to attract general public attention. Such signs
shall be deemed to be a single sign whenever the proximity, design, content or
continuity reasonably suggests a single unit, notwithstanding any physical
separation between parts.
   Sign lighting shall mean any electric lighting element designed to
illuminate a sign to provide for its visibility in low-light or night time
conditions. This includes external lighting that reflects off the surface of
the sign and internal lighting that halos the sign, illuminates the sign face
from within and electronic message signs.
   Temporary sign shall mean any sign constructed of paper, cloth, canvas,
plastic, cardboard, wall board, inflatable material, plywood or other like
material without a permanent foundation or not otherwise permanently attached
to the ground, a structure, or a building and is not supported by a permanent
frame and which is intended to be displayed for a limited period of time.
   Temporary decoration shall mean an exterior decoration on private property
intended to be used for a limited period of time. Temporary decorations
include, but are not limited, to any streamer, pennant, lighting string,
inflatable, propeller, flag or any similar device of any type or kind whether
bearing lettering or not.
   Tenant sign shall mean an exclusive sign that is attached to the exterior
wall at the entrance of a building used for the purpose of identifying and
displaying the name of occupants engaged in professions or businesses on the
premises.
   Wall sign shall mean any sign attached to the exterior surface of any
building or wall, no portion of which projects more than 12 inches from the
surface. No wall sign shall be painted directly on the exterior surface of any
building, wall, fence or other structure, or on any window or door surface.
   Window cling shall mean a picture, design, message, label or decal made of
cloth, plastic or similar material, designed to adhere to or be transferred to
glass.
   Window sign shall mean any sign, including window clings, mounted or
arranged on the inside or outside of a building in a manner or position
intended primarily for viewing from the outside of the building on or through
windows or doors.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22;
Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1334. Permitting and maintenance of signs.
   (a)   Other codes applicable. In addition to the provisions of this article
all signs and structural reinforcement must also comply with all applicable
construction codes, ordinances, laws and regulations. No external braces, arms
or guys shall be permitted as reinforcement.
   (b)   Sign permits and licensing.
      (1)   Permit required. It shall be unlawful for any person to erect,
alter, relocate, re-assemble, repair, repaint or post any sign governed by the
provisions of this article within the city without first having obtained a
permit from the department, except as otherwise noted in this article.
      (2)   Sign erector license required. No person shall erect, alter,
relocate, reassemble or post in the city any sign governed by the provisions of
this article without first having obtained a license. It shall be unlawful to
obtain a permit without first obtaining an annual sign erector license from the
city clerk, in conformity with section
5-269. A sign erector license is not required for temporary signs, temporary
decorations or sandwich board signs.
   (c)   Sign maintenance.
      (1)   No sign shall be installed or maintained in a condition which is
structurally unsafe or constitutes a hazard to public health, safety and
welfare.
      (2)   All signs shall be maintained in good repair at all times and kept
free from bird harborage. Deterioration of paint or other surface treatment
that detracts from the appearance of a sign shall be considered a violation of
this article.
      (3)   All signs pertaining to the business or activity conducted on the
property shall be immediately removed from the premises by the owners when the
business or activity is discontinued. Cabinet or similar signs with changeable
faces may have a blank face installed to meet this requirement.
      (4)   Interval inspections. The condition and status of signs shall be
examined as part of the city-wide periodic inspection of all commercial and
industrial buildings and facilities, all multiple dwellings greater than two
units, all places of public assembly and all establishments open to the public,
as required per section
5-29, as amended. Signs shall be inspected for compliance with this article.
   (d)   Removal and abatement.
      (1)   Removal of unauthorized signs on public property. In addition to
any other remedies set forth herein pertaining to the enforcement of this
article, the department is hereby authorized and empowered to immediately
remove any unauthorized and/or unpermitted signs located on public property.
Any expense incurred by the city in the removal of such signs from public
property may be charged against the person(s) or entities which own or caused
the placement of the sign on public property. If the amount of such expense has
not been paid to the city within 30 days after a notice and invoice has been
served by ordinary mail, the city may invoke any and all collection remedies
allowed by law.
      (2)   Removal or abatement of signs on private property. All signs
located on private property which are unauthorized, unpermitted, blighted,
hazardous or in violation of any code, ordinance, law or regulation may be
ordered by the department to be removed and/or the violations corrected. Such
signs are also subject to the nuisance abatement procedure set forth in section
13-5, as amended.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18)
Sec. 5-1335. General requirements for all signs.
   (a)   Sign lighting.
      (1)   Glare/distractions. Sign lighting shall not create glare or
excessively illuminate the surrounding area. Sign illumination that distracts
motorists or creates a traffic hazard for either vehicles or pedestrians is
prohibited.
      (2)   Light sources. Sign lighting shall only be by steady, non-flashing,
stationary, shielded light sources using approved electrical devices. Exposed
bulbs are prohibited except when used in electronic signs as defined and
regulated in this article.
      (3)   Direction and shielding.
         a.   Lighting fixtures shall be carefully located, aimed and shielded
so that light is directed only onto the sign or building façade.
         b.   To the extent possible, fixtures shall be mounted and directed
downward (below the horizontal). Lighting fixtures shall not be directly
visible from or aimed at adjacent streets, roads or properties.
         c.   Raceways, conduits and piping for electrical sources shall not be
exposed to view and shall not exceed seven inches.
         d.   Back-lit, electronic, and internally- illuminated signs shall not
cause excessive glare or allow light to encroach onto surrounding properties.
         e.   Sign lighting shall be designed and installed so that the light
produced does not exceed 0.5 foot-candles at the nearest residential property
line.
      (4)   Timer control for non-residential uses in residential districts.
         a.   When an illuminated sign is permitted in a residential zoning
district for a permitted, non-residential use the illuminated sign shall be
equipped with an actively functioning timer control.
         b.   The control shall be set so that the sign is not illuminated
after 11:00 p.m. or one half hour following the close of the business,
whichever is earlier and further provided that no sign shall be illuminated
before 6:00 a.m. or one half hour prior to the opening of the business,
whichever is later.
         c.   Details of the design and operation of the timer control shall be
submitted with the sign permit application.
      (5)   Photometric study. The building official or the zoning
administrator may require a photometric study as part of site plan or permit
review to ensure compliance with applicable ordinances.
   (b)   Prohibited sign and decoration locations.
      (1)   Not to obstruct egress/openings. No sign or decoration may be
attached to a door, window casing or tree, nor placed in any other location
which may obstruct any fire escape, door, window, passageway or other opening
or means of egress from a building.
      (2)   Not to obstruct access for public safety personnel or otherwise
create a public hazard. No sign or decoration may be erected on any pole or
column on public property or located at a distance the horizontal projection of
which is less than ten feet from any fire hydrant, traffic light, fire or
police box or erected in any location where, in the discretion of the city, it
would imperil public safety or interfere with the duties of the police or fire
department.
      (3)   Not to obstruct sight lines along public roads. No sign or
decoration shall be permitted to be located within the unobstructed sight
triangles at intersections of roads and drives as required in the Zoning
Ordinance.
      (4)   Not to obstruct walks or parking. No sign or decoration may be
located such that it obstructs any parking spaces and maneuver aisles in
parking lots and public or private walkways.
   (c)   Prohibited signs.
      (1)   Off-premises signs. Any permanent sign approved under this article
shall pertain only to the use of the premises on which it is located or to the
business activity normally conducted therein.
      (2)   Billboards.
         a.   Billboards are hereby prohibited except as provided by the
Highway Advertising Act (Act 106 of 1972).
         b.   Exception for advertising on certain city-owned property.
Notwithstanding the provisions of this section, or any other section or
ordinance, the director of the Recreation Department may offer, subject to
certain conditions, sell, and contract to sell space for advertising signs,
painted logos, and banners at Dearborn Ice Skating Center, King Boring Field,
Dearborn Hills Golf Course, Mystic Creek Golf Course at Camp Dearborn, and the
Dearborn Dog Park. Such advertising shall comply with the following standards:
            1.   The subject matter of the advertisement, logo, and/or banner
must be limited to a proposed commercial transaction or corporate sponsorship.
For the purposes of this subsection, a proposed commercial transaction solicits
an exchange of property, goods, or services with intended customers that will
necessarily result in something of economic value to the advertiser.
            2.   The advertisement, logo, banner, or corporate sponsorship may
not:
               a.   Be false, misleading, or deceptive.
               b.   Relate to an activity or product that is prohibited under
applicable federal, state, or local laws and regulations. Advertise or depict,
by language or graphics, violence.
               c.   Advertise or depict language, gestures, conduct, or
graphical representations that are obscene, pornographic, sexually explicit,
vulgar, lewd, or profane.
               d.   Advertise or depict the use of tobacco, marijuana, smoking
or vaping products, firearms, adult entertainment products or services, or
adult entertainment establishments.
               e.   Advertise or depict material that violates a copyright or
trademark.
            3.   The primary purpose of allowing advertising, painted logos,
and banners under this subsection is to generate revenue.
      (3)   Bill posting (snipe signs).
         a.   No placard, poster, circular, show bill, handbill, card leaflet
or other signs shall be posted, pasted, nailed, placed, printed, painted,
stamped or in any way attached to any fence, wall, post, tree, sidewalk,
pavement, platform, pole tower, curbstone, or surface in or upon any public
property in the city; provided, however, nothing herein set forth shall prevent
official notices of the city from being posted on any public property deemed
appropriate by the city.
         b.   In any proceeding for violation of this section, the phone
number, e-mail address, or location of event displayed on the placard, poster,
circular, show bill, handbill, card leaflet or other advertising matter
whatsoever shall constitute in evidence a prima facie presumption that the
person or business to whom the phone number, e-mail address or event address
was assigned was the person or business who unlawfully displayed the
advertising matter.
      (4)   Roof signs. Roof signs shall not be permitted in the city. No sign,
including but not limited to temporary signs, shall be permitted to be mounted
above or extended over the roof of any building or structure whether supported
by such building or structure or mounted completely independent thereof.
      (5)   Signs with more than two faces. No sign shall have more than two
faces.
      (6)   Obscene matter. It shall be unlawful for any person to display upon
any sign or advertising structure any matter that the average person, applying
contemporary community standards, would find appeals to prurient interests,
depicts sexually explicit conduct, specifically defined by law, in a patently
offensive manner, and which matter, taken as a whole, lacks serious literary,
artistic, political or scientific value.
      (7)   Message-casting (or projected) signs. The use of message-casting
signs or displays shall be prohibited, except for use as temporary decorations
subject to the terms and conditions of this article, including, but not limited
to, sections
5-1336(d) and
5-1337(i).
   (d)   Nonconforming signs (including billboards).
      (1)   Applicability. Every permanently affixed sign which was legally
erected, constructed, installed, placed or located, and which lawfully existed
on the effective date of this article, but which does not conform to the type,
height, size, area, or location requirements of this article shall be deemed a
nonconforming sign. This status shall not be granted to any temporary sign,
banner, or placard, including those affixed to the interior or exterior of
windows.
      (2)   Expansion or extension prohibited. Nonconforming signs shall not be
expanded, enlarged, extended or structurally altered to create an additional
nonconformity or to increase the extent of the existing nonconformity. A
nonconforming sign may be lessened in size or dimension without jeopardizing
its nonconforming status.
      (3)   Maintenance. Nonconforming signs may be maintained and repaired to
continue the useful life of the sign.
         a.   Maintenance and repair includes re-facing, painting of chipped or
faded signs, replacement of faded or damaged surface panels, or repair or
replacement of electrical wiring or electrical devices. A sign permit shall be
required for sign re-facing, but is not required for normal repairs and
maintenance.
         b.   Excluding maintenance and repair, changes to nonconforming signs
shall be prohibited unless the signs are brought into conformance with this
article.
      (4)   Damage or destruction. If a nonconforming sign is damaged or
destroyed to an extent that its repair cost exceeds 50% of its replacement
cost, exclusive of the foundation, the sign shall not be restored or replaced
to its prior nonconforming status but shall conform to the requirements of this
article.
      (5)   Site redevelopment. Nonconforming signs shall be eliminated as part
of a zoning approval required by the zoning administrator, city planner,
planning commission or zoning board of appeals involving the redevelopment of a
site.
      (6)   Signs for nonconforming uses. A sign on a lot with a nonconforming
use may be erected in accordance with the sign regulations for the district in
which the property is located.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 17-1574, 3-21-17; Ord. No. 18-1612, 5-15-18;
Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1336. Permitted signs in residential zoning districts.
   (a)   Applicability. The regulations in this section shall apply to signs
for multi-family residential and nonresidential uses in all residential zoning
districts unless otherwise specified.
   (b)   Permanent signs.
      (1)   Wall signs.
         a.   Flush mounted wall signs.
            1.   Maximum number of signs: one per building. An additional sign
may be permitted for a corner building on the side of the building facing the
other street or on the back of a building where the rear faces a parking lot.
            2.   Maximum sign area: 10% of the building face the sign is
mounted on, maximum 100 square feet each.
            3.   Maximum height on the building: no wall sign or any portion
thereof may extend above the top of the wall upon which it is supported.
         b.   Projecting wall signs.
            1.   Maximum number of signs: one per building, an additional sign
may be permitted on the back of a building where the rear faces a parking lot.
            2.   Maximum sign depth: shall extend no more than 12 inches into
or over any public property or right-of-way.
            3.   Minimum sign height: shall be a minimum of 8.5 feet above
sidewalk grade, but not less than 14 feet above alley grade where they extend
over an alley.
            4.   Maximum height on the building: no wall sign or any portion
thereof shall extend above the top of the wall upon which it is supported.
      (2)   Ground signs.
         a.   Pole mounted signs. Pole mounted signs are prohibited in
residential zoning districts.
         b.   Monument signs.
            1.   Maximum number of signs: No lot or abutting parcels under
common ownership shall be permitted more than one monument sign.
            2.   Maximum sign area: 40 square feet.
            3.   Maximum sign height: Five feet.
      (3)   Electronic signs:
         a.   Non-residential uses in residential zoning districts are
permitted to have up to one double sided electronic sign. All electronic signs
shall comply with the rules and regulations set forth for electronic signs in
section
5-1337 of this article.
         b.   All electronic signs located in residential zoning districts
shall discontinue the display between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
   (c)   Temporary signs.
      (1)   Temporary signs for residential uses (other than temporary window
signs).
         a.   All residential dwellings, including but not limited to a single-
family house, two-family dwelling or a ground-level multiple family unit, shall
be permitted on-premise temporary ground signs.
         b.   Maximum sign size. Each sign shall not exceed nine square feet
per side.
         c.   Placement. Permitted signs shall not be located in public rights-
of-way and shall be set back at least three feet from the property line.
         d.   Illumination. Residential temporary signs shall not be
illuminated.
         e.   Duration. A temporary sign shall be permitted for no more than 60
consecutive days and be taken down no later than five days after the event it
pertains to is completed.
         f.   Permit. A sign permit is not required.
      (2)   Temporary signs for non-residential uses (religious institutions,
schools, day-care centers, etc.) in residential zoning districts (other than
temporary window signs).
         a.   Permitted number of signs:
            1.   Each property shall be limited to a total of six signs not to
exceed a total sign area of 48 square feet (e.g., 1 double sided 6'x4' sign, 2
double sided 3'x4' signs, etc.)
            2.   Exception: for properties with road frontage in excess of 400
linear feet, an additional 48 square feet of signage is permitted not to exceed
96 square feet in total sign area. This provision does not allow for an
increase in the total number of permitted signs.
         b.   Maximum size of individual signs:
            1.   Total sign area per face: 24 square feet.
            2.   Maximum height for ground mounted signs: 6 feet.
         c.   Location and setback: Temporary signs shall not be located in
public rights of way and shall be set back at least three feet from the
property line.
         d.   Installation: Temporary signs shall be securely attached to the
structure or securely anchored/ weighted to the ground.
         e.   Illumination: Signs shall not be illuminated.
         f.   Duration: a temporary sign shall be permitted for no more than 60
consecutive days and shall be taken down no later than five days after the
event to which it pertains to is completed.
         g.   A sign permit is not required.
   (d)   Temporary decorations.
      (1)   Temporary decorations, including message-casting (or projected)
signs, shall be permitted for a period of 60 consecutive days.
      (2)   Temporary decorations shall be securely attached and shall not
create a safety hazard of any kind.
      (3)   Temporary decorations shall not exceed the maximum allowable height
within the zoning district in which it is located.
      (4)   Temporary signs attached to temporary decorations shall be
permitted separately and in accordance with this section.
      (5)   City-sponsored temporary decorations on public property are exempt
from the requirements of the sign ordinance provided they are displayed for no
more than 60 days.
      (6)   Luminous tube, rope, neon, or fluorescent lighting shall be
prohibited in the front yard of lots located in residential zoning districts
unless it is a temporary display. A temporary display is permitted for 60
consecutive days and must be disassembled and removed from the structure within
that timeframe.
      (7)   Message-casting (or projected) signs as temporary decorations;
regulations.
         a.   Shall be carefully located, aimed and shielded so that light is
directed only onto the sign, building/structure façade, or ground.
         b.   Shall not create glare or excessively illuminate the surrounding
area, and shall not distract motorists or create a traffic hazard for either
vehicles or pedestrians.
         c.   Fixtures that produce message-casting or projected signs shall
not be aimed at adjacent streets, roads, or properties.
         d.   Shall not cause excessive glare or allow light to encroach into
surrounding properties.
         e.   Time limitation.
            1.   Message-casting signs shall discontinue display, and shall not
be illuminated between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
            2.   When a message-casting sign is being used as a temporary
decoration in a residential district for a permitted, non-residential use, the
message-casting sign shall be equipped with actively functioning timer control.
The control shall be set so that the sign is not illuminated after 11:00 p.m.
or one-half hour following the close of the business, whichever is earlier. No
message-casting sign used as a temporary decoration shall be illuminated or
projected before 6:00 a.m. or one-half hour prior to the opening of the
business, whichever is later.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1337. Permitted signs in commercial and industrial zoning districts.
   (a)   Applicability. The regulations in this section apply to signs in the
O-S, B-A, B-B, B-C, I-A, I-B, I-C, I-D, T-R and PUD zoning districts.
   (b)   Permanent signs.
      (1)   Wall signs.
         a.   Flush mounted wall signs.
            1.   Maximum total sign area: the total area of all signs shall not
exceed 15% of the building face the sign is mounted on.
            2.   Building signs:
               (i)   Maximum number of signs: one per building. An additional
sign may be permitted for a corner building on the side of the building facing
the other street or on the back of a building where the rear faces a parking
lot.
               (ii)   Maximum area per sign: 100 square feet each.
            3.   Tenant signs:
               (i)   Maximum number of signs: in addition to the building signs
noted above, one sign per elevation is permitted per commercial tenant if there
is more than one commercial tenant occupying the building, as long as the total
area of signs shall not exceed 15% of the total area of the building side the
sign is mounted on.
               (ii)   Maximum area per sign: 50 square feet each.
               (iii)   Maximum height on the building: no wall sign or any
portion thereof may extend above the top of the wall upon which it is
supported.
      (2)   Projecting wall signs.
         a.   Maximum number of signs: one per building. An additional sign may
be permitted on the back of a building where the rear faces a parking lot.
         b.   Maximum sign depth: may extend no more than 18 inches into or
over any public property or right-of-way.
         c.   Minimum sign height: shall be a minimum of 8.5 feet above
sidewalk grade, but not less than 14 feet above alley grade where they extend
over an alley.
         d.   Maximum height on the building: no wall sign or any portion
thereof may extend above the top of the wall upon which it is supported.
      (3)   Ground signs.
         a.   Pole mounted signs.
            1.   Maximum number of signs: No lot or abutting parcels under
common ownership shall be permitted more than one pole mounted sign.
            2.   Maximum sign area: 100 square feet.
            3.   Maximum sign height: 30 feet.
            4.   Minimum sign clearance (height to bottom of sign): 8.5 feet.
            5.   Minimum spacing between signs: 20 feet.
         b.   Monument signs.
            1.   Maximum number of signs: No lot or abutting parcels under
common ownership shall be permitted more than one monument sign.
            2.   Maximum sign area: 100 square feet.
            3.   Maximum sign height: 12 feet.
            4.   Minimum spacing between signs: 20 feet.
         c.   No lot or abutting parcels under common ownership shall have both
a pole and monument sign.
   (c)   Electronic signs.
      (1)   General requirements.
         a.   Electronic signs up to 24 square feet in area and electronic open
signs up to two square feet in area shall be permitted in nonresidential
districts subject to the regulations of this article, except in those districts
where prohibited by the Zoning Ordinance.
         b.   In zoning districts in which the Zoning Ordinance allows for
electronic signs, electronic signs shall comply with both the provisions of
this article and the applicable provisions of the Zoning Ordinance.
         c.   The permit requirements of this article shall not apply to
electronic open signs.
      (2)   Display requirements.
         a.   Scrolling or traveling of a message onto and/or off the
electronic sign display shall be allowed provided the message is coming from
one direction only and that no message shall take more than five seconds to be
displayed in its entirety. After a message has been displayed in its entirety,
the screen shall not change for 30 seconds, except for time/temperature signs,
which shall not change for five seconds.
         b.   The electronic sign display shall not, or shall not appear to,
flash, undulate, pulse or portray explosions, fireworks, flashes of light, or
blinking or chasing lights; the display shall not appear to move toward or away
from the viewer, expand or contract, bounce, rotate, spin, twist or make other
similar movements.
         c.   Electronic signs shall not be used to display animations, motion
pictures, television programming, movies, sporting events, or any similar live
or recorded broadcast.
         d.   Electronic signs shall only relate to the use of the premises on
which they are located or to the business activity normally conducted therein.
         e.   All electronic signs with the electronic display facing a
residential zoning district that is within 150 feet of that district shall
discontinue the display between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
      (3)   Light levels.
         a.   In order to prevent glare, electronic signs shall not operate at
a brightness level greater than the manufacturer's recommended levels. Light
levels emitted by electronic signs shall not exceed 0.5 foot-candles at the
property line of any adjacent residentially used or zoned parcel.
         b.   All electronic signs shall have installed ambient light monitors
and shall at all times allow such monitors to automatically adjust the
brightness level of the electronic sign based on ambient light conditions.
      (4)   Additional requirements.
         a.   No lots or abutting parcels under common ownership shall be
permitted more than one electronic sign. An electronic open sign shall not
count as the one electronic sign.
         b.   No individual unit of a building shall be permitted more than one
electronic open sign per public entrance, up to maximum of two.
         c.   Electronic sign permit applications shall include a copy of the
manufacturer's specifications for luminosity.
         d.   Electronic sign permit applications shall include certification
from the owner or operator of the sign stating that the sign shall be operated
in accordance with city codes and that the owner or operator shall provide
proof of such conformance upon request of the city.
         e.   Whether the electronic sign is programmed from the site or from a
remote location, the computer interface that programs the electronic sign shall
be available to city staff for inspection upon request at the site.
         f.   The surface area of electronic signs shall be included in
calculations of maximum allowable signage provided for in this article.
         g.   Any electronic sign found to not be in compliance with the
provisions of this article shall cease operation until the electronic sign is
brought into compliance with this article.
      (5)   Existing signs to conform. Any nonconforming electronic sign
lawfully existing under a variance previously granted by the building board of
appeals shall be made to comply with the requirements of this section within 30
days from the date this article takes effect. However, any existing electronic
sign that exceeds 24 square feet in area or any existing electronic open sign
that exceeds two square feet in area may continue as a nonconforming existing
sign until such time that the sign is removed, moved, or replaced.
   (d)   Awnings.
      (1)   Facades may be supplemented by awnings, which shall be straight
sheds with or without side flaps, not cubed or curved, or backlit. Awnings
shall be between 8.5 and 12 feet above sidewalk grade at the lower drip edge.
Awnings must avoid street trees and be set back at least two feet from the road
curb.
      (2)   The vertical drip edge of an awning may be stenciled with signage a
maximum of eight inches in height.
   (e)   Sandwich boards and similar signs.
      (1)   Each side of the sandwich board sign shall not exceed three feet in
height or two feet in width. A stanchion or support up to 12 inches in height
is permitted for the sandwich board sign.
      (2)   The bottom shall be weighted or anchored so that the sign is
stable, wind-proof, and not easily knocked down.
      (3)   Permits for sandwich board signs shall only be issued for the
period of April 1 through October 31. Sandwich board signs shall be prohibited
between November 1 and March 31. A new permit shall be applied for each year.
      (4)   All sandwich board signs must be stored indoors at the close of the
business each day.
      (5)   Sandwich board signs shall be placed on private property whenever
possible. In the event that placement on public property is necessary, the
applicant must obtain permission from the Director of the Department of
Economic Development, or their designee, to occupy the easement, right-of-way,
or other public area, which permission may be rescinded in the discretion of
the director.
      (6)   Sign owners, lessees, and manufacturers shall be liable for any and
all claims, injuries, or damages that arise from placement of a sandwich board
sign on public property.
      (7)   A permit for a sandwich board sign shall be revoked whenever the
sign becomes an eyesore, a nuisance, or is neglected.
      (8)   A temporary sign that meets the same height and width restrictions
as sandwich board signs under this subsection may also be used. Such temporary
signs shall be subject to the same terms and conditions as sandwich board signs
under this subsection, including, but not limited to, the requirement for a
permit, indoor storage during non-business hours, seasonal restrictions, and
permission from the Director of Economic Development, or their designee, to
place such sign on public property.
         a.   Temporary signs must be weighted or anchored so that the sign is
stable, wind-proof, and not easily knocked down.
   (f)   Light or utility pole mounted vertical banners on private property.
      (1)   Maximum size: vertical banners shall be no greater than of 30
inches wide by 94 inches tall with a two-inch hemmed sleeve at the top and
bottom.
      (2)   Minimum mounting height: vertical banners shall be mounted at least
12 feet above the sidewalk or parking lot surface.
      (3)   Minimum banner fabrication standards: A brass grommet shall be
installed at the top and bottom to secure the banner with nylon tie-wraps.
Banners shall be professionally constructed of suitable outdoor material
(vinyl, sunbrella, canvas, nylon, polyester) so as to guarantee durability for
the period of installation. Suitable wind slits must be provided.
      (4)   Minimum mounting hardware standards: Pole-mounted banners shall
only be installed on hardware sufficient to meet the requirements of the
applicable construction codes.
      (5)   Prohibited location: "Over-the-street banners" shall not be
permitted except as approved for special events by city council.   
   (g)   Window signs.
      (1)   Temporary window signs.
         a.   Maximum sign area per window: a maximum opaque coverage area of
30% shall be permitted per window.
         b.   Maximum number of signs per building: three.
         c.   Maximum time permitted per sign: 30 days or less.
         d.   Doors: such signs shall not be permitted on doors.
         e.   Sign permit: not required.
      (2)   Permanent/semi-permanent window signs.
         a.   Maximum sign area per window: a maximum opaque coverage area of
30% shall be permitted per window.
            1.   Permanent window or door signs/graphics (stenciled, etched,
silk screened, hand painted, vinyl letters/images, window clings, or similar)
are permitted with maximum coverage area of 100% provided the following
standards are met:
               (i)   Any coverage beyond 30% shall have a minimum of 70% visual
light transmission (VLT).
               (ii)   Approval by the Director of the Economic Development
Department or their designee.
         b.   Maximum number of signs per window: one.
         c.   Doors: such signs shall not be permitted on doors.
         d.   Sign permit: required.
         e.   Exception: the above regulations do not apply to street numbers,
hours of operation, menus and other small accessory signs less than one square
foot in area.
      (3)   Temporary and permanent/semi- permanent window signs shall not be
permitted to be displayed in the same window.
      (4)   Window signs that are blighted, deteriorated or obsolete shall be
removed immediately.
   (h)   Temporary signs (other than temporary window signs).
      (1)   Permitted number of signs:
         a.   Each property shall be limited to a total of six signs not to
exceed a total sign area of 48 square feet (e.g., 1 double sided 6'x4' sign, 2
double sided 3'x4' signs, etc.)
         b.   Exception: for properties with road frontage in excess of 400
linear feet, an additional 48 square feet of signage is permitted not to exceed
96 square feet in total sign area. This provision does not allow for an
increase in the total number of permitted signs.
      (2)   Maximum size of individual signs:
         a.   Total sign area per face: 24 square feet.
         b.   Maximum height for ground mounted signs: six feet.
      (3)   Location and setback: Temporary signs shall not be located in
public rights-of-way and shall be set back at least three feet from the
property line.
      (4)   Installation: Temporary signs shall be securely attached to the
structure or securely anchored/weighted to the ground.
      (5)   Illumination: Sign shall not be illuminated.
      (6)   Duration: A commercial temporary sign shall be permitted for 60
consecutive days and shall be taken down no later than five days after the
event it pertains to is completed.
      (7)   Permit: A sign permit is not required.
   (i)   Temporary decorations.
      (1)   Temporary decorations, including message-casting (or projected)
signs, shall be permitted for a period of 60 consecutive days.
      (2)   Temporary decorations shall be securely attached and shall not
create a safety hazard of any kind.
      (3)   Temporary decorations shall not exceed the maximum allowable height
within the zoning district in which it is located. This regulation shall not
apply to message-casting signs.
      (4)   Only one type of temporary inflatable shall be permitted at any
location at any time.
      (5)   Temporary signs attached to temporary decorations shall be
permitted separately and in accordance with this section.
      (6)   City-sponsored temporary decorations on public property are exempt
from the requirements of the sign ordinance provided they are displayed for no
more than 60 days.
      (7)   Message-casting (or projected) signs as temporary decorations;
regulations.
         a.   Shall be carefully located, aimed and shielded so that light is
directed only onto the sign, building/structure façade, or ground.
         b.   Shall not create glare or excessively illuminate the surrounding
area, and shall not distract motorists or create a traffic hazard for either
vehicles or pedestrians.
         c.   Fixtures that produce message-casting or projected signs shall
not be aimed at adjacent streets, roads, or properties.
         d.   Shall not cause excessive glare or allow light to encroach into
surrounding properties.
         e.   Time limitation.
            1.   All message-casting signs with the projected display facing a
residential zoning district, that is within 150 feet of that district, shall
discontinue the display and shall not be illuminated between the hours of 10:00
p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
            2.   Message-casting or projected signs being used as temporary
decorations shall be equipped with actively functioning timer control.
      (8)   Penalty for failure to remove. Failure to timely remove any
temporary sign or temporary decoration, or failure to obtain a permit, shall be
a civil infraction subject to a fine of $200.00. Second and subsequent
violations committed within two years of a previous conviction or finding of
responsibility shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed
$500.00, a term of imprisonment not to exceed 93 days, or both, in the
discretion of the court. Nothing set forth herein shall be construed as
limiting the ability of the city to abate as provided in this article.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1338. Other signs.
   (a)   Flags.
      (1)   Flags may either be attached to a ground-mounted flagpole or
affixed to a building. Flagpoles may not exceed the height of buildings
permitted in the zoning district.
      (2)   Flags, whether ground mounted or wall mounted, shall be grouped in
a single area of the site or building.
   (b)   Historic markers. Historical signs and markers shall be aesthetically
attractive and recognizable by the citizenry as associated with historical
subject matter. Signs and markers shall be at least 18 inches wide and 24
inches high and rectangular in shape. Larger sizes shall be permitted depending
on the text and location. All signs and markers shall be made of metal to
ensure a long life and shall be metal post mounted or wall mounted. All signs
and markers, with the exception of approved bronze plaques, shall be enameled
or vinyl coated a deep brown color. Lettering shall be in a cream or black
color. Uniformity of size, material and color are desirable characteristics to
be considered by the Historical Commission in reviewing applications hereunder.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18)
Sec. 5-1339. Banners on rights-of-way.
   (a)   Purpose. The purpose of this section is to allow the city and city
authorities permitted by law, including but not limited to the Downtown
Development Authority (DDA) and Warren and Dix-Vernor Corridor Authority, to
promote city and authority sponsored events or activities.
   (b)   Eligibility. Banners may display corporate logos or similar
endorsements as long as they do not occupy a total of more than ten percent of
the banner size.
   (c)   Regulations. The Director of Public Works, or his designee, may
regulate the installation and maintenance the banners, and impose any other
conditions in the interest of the appearance of the street, as well as traffic
and pedestrian safety, that are consistent with this article and the city’s
Code of Ordinances and Zoning Ordinance.
   (d)   Banner requirements. Vertical (utility pole) mounted banners shall
conform to the city's existing brackets and shall have a dimension of 30 inches
wide by 94 inches tall with a two inch hemmed sleeve at the top and bottom. A
brass grommet shall be installed at the top and bottom to secure the banner
with nylon tie-wraps. Banners shall be professionally constructed of suitable
outdoor material (vinyl, sunbrella, canvas, nylon, polyester) so as to
guarantee durability for the period installation. Suitable wind slits must be
provided. Banners must not interfere with any traffic control devices,
streetlights or streetlight controls and shall be mounted at least 12 feet
above the sidewalk surface. Banners proposed for installation on bridge/
overpass railings will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
   (e)   Installation requirements. The permittee shall be solely responsible
for the installation, maintenance and removal of the banners. To guarantee
safety and minimize interference with traffic flow, all installation work shall
be performed between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, or during daylight
hours on weekends. Pole-mounted banners may only be installed on fiberglass
banner rods attached to poles by metal brackets. Only a contractor that is
licensed and bonded to work in the city right-of-way may perform installations.
Proper safety procedures and temporary traffic control devices must be used
during the installation. A detailed schedule of banner installation must be
submitted to the Director of Public Works at least seven days in advance of the
proposed installation date. The director may require revisions to the schedule
for purposes of safety, traffic flow or other reasons. After approval of the
schedule by the director, any changes proposed by the permittee must be
communicated immediately to the director and shall not be implemented until
further approvals are obtained.
   The city will not install, maintain or remove banners except that if the
permittee fails to comply with the requirements of this section, the city may
abate any non-compliant banners and impose costs and fees as provided in
subsection (n). In addition, the permittee will not be allowed to apply for
banner permits in the future.
   The city will not provide any facilities for the storage of banners awaiting
installation, or for equipment used in the installation process.
   (f)   Utility pole/streetlight damage liability. The permittee shall be
responsible for all costs to repair damage to utility poles, streetlights or
other facilities, caused during installation, occupancy or removal of banners.
   (g)   Duration of banner installations. Permits will not be issued for
installation of banners for periods in excess of 90 days. Banners promoting
events or activities must be removed within seven days of the conclusion of the
event or activity.
   (h)   Insurance. The permittee shall furnish insurance as specified. An
insurance carrier must be licensed to do business in the State of Michigan.
Insurance must be provided on a comprehensive form to include the following:
      (1)   General liability insurance: Occurrence policy with a limit of not
less than $1,000,000.00 per occurrence and $2,000,000.00 aggregate. The
following endorsements must be included:
         a.   Products/completed operations.
         b.   Contractual liability.
         c.   Personal injury.
      (2)   Workers compensation insurance as required by State of Michigan
law.
         a.   Michigan Statutory coverage.
         b.   Employers Liability: $500,000.00.
      (3)   Auto liability coverage of $1,000,000.00 for all owned, scheduled,
hired or non-owned vehicles.
   (i)   Application deadlines. All permit applications must be submitted at
least 60 days prior to the desired date of installation of the banners. This
period is necessary to complete coordination efforts between the city and other
affected organizations, such as the Michigan Department of Transportation
(MDOT), Wayne County and utility companies.
   (j)   Application procedures. The applicant must complete the city's banner
application and submit it to the Director of Public Works. The application
requires certain information, including:
      (1)   The purpose of the organization, as well as the event or activity;
      (2)   Dates and times during which the banners will be installed,
displayed and removed;
      (3)   Dates and times of the event or activity (if applicable);
      (4)   Location and number of banners with specific utility pole/street
light pole locations;
      (5)   Color sample of the banner's design and content, as well as details
of construction and materials;
      (6)   Deposit in the form of a check payable to the City of Dearborn (see
subsection (l)).
   (k)   Application processing. Applications will be accepted on a "first-
come, first-served" basis. In the event of dual and competing requests, the
application with the earliest postmark shall be given priority, unless one of
the applicants has received prior approval from the city, in which case that
applicant will retain the first right of refusal. The city reserves the right
to deny applications that are incomplete, do not meet the requirements of this
policy, or represent an unreasonable burden on the city's resources.
   (l)   Deposit. Upon submission of the permit application, the permittee
shall provide a refundable deposit of $300 to cover costs to the city in the
event of the permittee's non-compliance with this policy. The deposit will be
refunded if the permit request is denied, the permittee has complied with all
requirements of this policy, including removal of the banners by the stated
removal date and after inspection by the city determines that no significant
damages to poles, brackets, rods or other facilities has occurred as a result
of the banner installation, occupancy and removal, or the permittee does not
proceed with installation of the banners.
   (m)   Fees. Within seven days of permit approval, the permittee shall
provide to the city a fee of $100, plus $10 per banner. Such fees shall only
cover the period for which the banner permits is granted and shall not be
applied to any subsequent permits or permit renewals. The program fee is
required to cover the costs of administering the banner permit program, minor
maintenance, and repair to facilities resulting from the installation,
occupancy and removal of the banners. If, after approval of the permit
application, the permittee does not proceed with the banner installation, the
program fee shall be refunded, less $50, to cover the city's administrative
costs.
   (n)   Maintenance. Throughout the display period, the permittee shall
inspect the banners and brackets and make repairs or adjustments as required to
guarantee safety and proper appearance. If the city notifies the permittee of a
maintenance requirement, the permittee shall complete the necessary repairs or
adjustments within 24 hours. Failure to complete such corrective action within
the 24-hour period shall result in the city initiating action to perform the
corrections and billing all costs, plus an administrative fee of $500, to the
permittee.
   (o)   Permits and requirements of other agencies and utilities. The majority
of the utility and streetlight poles located in the city are located within the
rights-of-way of MDOT and Wayne County. In addition, DTE Entergy, MDOT or the
county owns most of these facilities. Each of these organizations requires
specific permits to occupy the rights-of-way and to attach to their facilities.
These organizations will not issue banner permits to individuals or
organizations, only to the local unit of government (city). These requirements
place specific burdens on the city in terms of coordination, application
processes and liability. The city may require that the banner permittee pay for
costs associated with these efforts. Such costs shall be determined by the city
in advance of approval of the permit application. The applicant may withdraw
the application if these costs are not acceptable. In such cases, the
applicant's deposit and the program fee shall be refunded.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1340. Penalties for violation.
   (a)   Penalties.
      (1)   Violation of any provision of this article by any person, firm,
corporation, partnership, owner, agent or lessee shall be a civil infraction
punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.00, plus any costs imposed by the
court, except where a specific penalty is otherwise provided. Increased fines
shall be imposed for repeat violations of this section by any person, agent,
partnership, corporation, association, company, or business.
         a.   As used in this section, repeat violation means a violation
committed within six (6) months of an admission or determination of
responsibility for a violation of this article committed by the same person,
agent, partnership, corporation, association, company, or business.
         b.   The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall be a civil
fine of $1,000.00, plus any costs imposed by the court.
      (2)   In addition to the penalties provided under this section, any
condition caused or permitted to exist in violation of any of the provisions of
this article shall be deemed to be a new and separate offense for each day that
the condition continues to exist.
      (3)   In addition to any penalty provided under this section, the city
may seek injunctive relief, abate the condition as a nuisance, revoke any
permit or license, and/or seek any other available remedy provided by law.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22;
Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1341.   Appeals.
   (a)   Any person aggrieved by any decision, ruling, interpretation or order
regarding this Article may appeal to the Building Board of Appeals, which board
is hereby empowered and authorized to hear and consider such an appeal. Such
appeal shall be taken within ten days after the decision, ruling interpretation
or order complained of by filing with the Director of the Department of
Economic Development, or their designee, a written notice of appeal directed to
the board, specifying the grounds thereof and the relief prayed for. The
director shall transmit to the board all papers constituting the record upon
which the decision, ruling, interpretation or order appealed from has been
taken.
   (b)   The appeal procedure in this article is intended to provide limited
relief from the requirements of this article in cases where a strict
application of a particular requirement shall create an unnecessary hardship
affecting a substantial property right. This procedure is intended to address
extraordinary, exceptional or unique situations that were not caused by an act
or omission of the applicant or the applicant's predecessor in title, employee,
or agent. Relief is not to be granted merely on the basis of inconvenience or
financial burden.
   (c)   Variances. A variance from the requirements of this article may be
allowed only in cases where there is evidence of practical difficulty. In this
case all of the following criteria shall be met. Increased costs in complying
with the requirements of this article shall not be considered a basis for
granting a variance.
      (1)   Exceptional circumstances or conditions: There are exceptional or
extraordinary circumstances or conditions applying to the property that do not
generally apply to other properties in the same zoning district or neighboring
area, such as lot shape, abutting property issues, motorist safety or scale of
building or lot frontage;
      (2)   Substantial property right: A variance is necessary to preserve a
substantial property right similar to that possessed by other properties in the
same zoning district;
      (3)   Not self-created: The immediate practical difficulty causing the
need for the variance was not created by the applicant or any other person
having an interest in the sign, sign structure, or property;
      (4)   No substantial detriment: Granting the variance will not be
detrimental to the public welfare, be injurious to other properties or
improvements, endanger public safety or substantially impair property values in
the area;
      (5)   Master Plan, zoning ordinance or this article: A variance will be
consistent with, and will not materially impair, the spirit and intent of the
City Master Plan, zoning ordinance, or this article.
   (d)   The Building Board of Appeals shall hear and decide appeals where it
is alleged there is an error in any interpretation, requirement, decision or
determination in the enforcement or administration of this article.
(Ord. No. 17-1569, - -17; Ord. No. 18-1621, 7-17-18; Ord. No. 22-1733, 1-25-22;
Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)
Sec. 5-1342.   Severability.
   Should any word, phrase, sentence, paragraph, or section of this article be
held invalid or unconstitutional, the remaining provisions of the article shall
remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. No. 23-1804, 1-9-24)

*** ARTICLE XIII. - FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 5-1356. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Appeal means a request for review of the director of building and safety's
interpretation of any provision of this article or a request for a variance
from the provisions.
   Applicant means the owner, agent or legal representatives of property for
which and by whom an application for a development permit is made.
   Area of shallow flooding means a designed AO zone on the flood insurance
rate map (FIRM). In this area, the base flood depths range from one to three
feet; a clearly defined channel does not exist; the path of flooding is
unpredictable and indeterminate; and velocity flow may be evident.
   Area of special flood hazard means the land in the floodplain subject to a
one percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year as determined by
the flood insurance study, or as may be determined in flood hazard studies
conducted subsequent to the flood insurance study.
   Base flood means the flood having a one percent chance of being equaled or
exceeded in any given year as determined by the flood insurance study, or as
may be determined in flood hazard studies conducted subsequent to the flood
insurance study. For the purposes of this article, this shall be considered the
"100 year flood."
   Development means any manmade change to improved or unimproved real estate
within an area of special flood hazard, including, but not limited to,
buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving,
excavation or drilling operations.
   Existing manufactured home park or subdivision means a manufactured home
park for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lot on which
the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including, at a minimum, the
installation of utilities, either final site grading or the pouring of concrete
pads, and the construction of streets) are completed before the effective date
of floodplain management regulations adopted May 6, 1996.
   Expansion to an existing manufactured home park or subdivision means the
preparation of additional sites by the construction of facilities for servicing
the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including the
installation of utilities, either final site grading or pouring of concrete
pads, or the construction of streets).
   Flood or flooding means a general and temporary condition of partial or
complete inundation of normally dry land areas from the overflow of inland
waters and/or the unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters
from any source.
   Flood hazard boundary map (FHBM) means the official map on which the federal
insurance administration has delineated the areas of special flood hazards.
   Flood insurance rate map (FIRM) means the official map on which the federal
insurance administration has delineated both the areas of special flood hazards
and the risk premium zones applicable to the city.
   Flood insurance study means the official report provided by the Federal
Insurance Administration that contains flood profiles, as well as the flood
hazard boundary-floodway map and the water surface elevation of the base flood
applicable to the city.
   Floodway means the channel of a river or other watercourse and the adjacent
land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without
cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation to more than one-tenth
foot.
   Habitable floor means any floor usable for living purposes, which includes
working, sleeping, eating, cooking or recreation, or a combination thereof. A
floor used only for storage purposes shall be excluded from this definition.
   Manufactured home means a structure, transportable in one or more sections,
which is built on a permanent chassis and is designed for use with or without a
permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities. For floodplain
management purposes the term manufactured home also includes park trailers,
travel trailers, and other similar vehicles placed on a site for greater than
180 consecutive days. For insurance purposes, the term manufactured home does
not include park trailers, travel trailers and other similar vehicles.
   Manufactured home park or subdivision means a parcel (or contiguous parcels)
or land divided into two or more manufactured home lots for rent or sale.
   New construction means structures for which the "start of construction"
commenced on or after the effective date of this article.
   Openings in enclosures below a structure's lowest floor for all new
construction and substantial improvement, fully enclosed areas below the lowest
floor that are subject to flooding shall be designed to automatically equalize
hydrostatic flood forces on exterior walls by allowing for the entry and exit
of floodwaters. Designs for meeting this requirement must either be certified
by a registered professional engineer or architect or must meet or exceed the
following minimum criteria: A minimum of two openings having a total net area
of not less than one square inch for every square foot of enclosed area subject
to flooding shall be provided. The bottom of all openings shall be no higher
than one foot above grade. Openings may be equipped with screens, louvers, or
other coverings or devices provided that they permit the automatic entry and
exit of floodwaters.
   Start of construction means the date the building permit was issued,
provided the actual start of construction, repair, reconstruction, placement or
other improvement was within 180 days of the permit date. The actual start
means either the first placement of permanent construction of a structure on a
site, such as the pouring of slab or footings, the installation of piles, the
construction of columns, or any work beyond the state of excavation; or the
placement of a manufactured home on a foundation. Permanent construction does
not include land preparation, such as clearing, grading and filling; nor does
it include the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does it include
excavation for a basement, footings, piers or foundations or the erection of
temporary forms; nor does it include the installation on the property of
accessory buildings, such as garages, or sheds not occupied as dwelling units
or not par of the main structure.
   Structure means anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires
location on the ground or attachment to something having location on the
ground.
   Substantial improvement means any repair, reconstruction or improvement of
the structure, the cost of which equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market
value of the structure, either before the improvement or repair is started, or,
if the structure has been damaged and is being restored, before the damage
occurred. For the purposes of this definition "substantial improvement" is
considered to occur when the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor or
other structural part of the building commences, whether or not the alteration
affects the external dimensions of the structure. The term does not, however,
include either any project or improvement of a structure to comply with
existing state or local health, sanitary or safety code specifications which
are solely necessary to assure safe living conditions; nor any alteration of a
structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places or a state or
local inventory of historic places.
   Variance means a grant of relief from the requirements of this article which
permits construction in a manner which would otherwise be prohibited by this
article.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1357. - Rules of construction.
   The following rules of construction apply to the provisions of this article:
      (1)   The particular shall control the general.
      (2)   A "building" or "structure" includes any part thereof.
      (3)   The phrase "used for" may include "arranged for," "designed for,"
"intended for," "maintained for," or "occupied for."
      (4)   Unless the context clearly indicates the contrary, where regulation
involves two or more items, conditions, provisions or events connected by the
conjunction "and," "or," "either … or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as
follows:
         a.   "And" indicates that all the connected items, conditions,
provisions or events shall apply.
         b.   "Or" indicates that the connected items, conditions, provisions
or events may apply singly or in any combination.
         c.   "Either … or" indicates that the connected items, conditions,
provisions or events shall apply single but not in combination.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1358. - Statutory authorization.
   This article is adopted to secure the public health, welfare and safety
under the combined authority of Act No. 279 of the Public Acts of Michigan of
1909 (Home Rule Cities; MCL 117.1 et seq., MSA 5.2071 et seq.), as amended; Act
No. 167 of the Public Acts of Michigan of 1968 (Flood Plain Control Act), an
amendment to Act No. 245 of the Public Acts of Michigan of 1929 (Water Resource
Commission Act; MCL 323.1 et seq., MSA 3.521 et seq.); The National Flood
Insurance Act of 1968, as amended; and the Flood Disaster Protection Act of
1973.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1358.5. - Code appendix enforced.
   Pursuant to the provisions of the state construction code, in accordance
with Section 8b(6) of Act 230, of the Public Acts of 1972, as amended, Appendix
G of the Michigan Building Code shall be enforced within the City of Dearborn
by the city engineer.
(Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
Sec. 5-1359. - Findings of fact.
   (a)   The flood hazard areas of the city may be subject to periodic
inundation which results in the potential loss of life and property, health and
safety hazards, disruption of commerce and governmental services, extraordinary
public expenditures for flood protection and relief and impairment of the tax
base, all of which adversely affect the public health, safety and general
welfare.
   (b)   These potential flood losses are caused by the cumulative effect of
obstructions in floodplains and floodways causing increases in flood heights
and velocities, and when inadequately anchored, damages land uses in other
areas. Uses that are inadequately floodproofed, elevated or otherwise protected
from flood damage also contribute to the flood loss.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1360. - Purpose.
   It is the purpose of this article to promote the public health, safety and
general welfare to minimize public and private losses due to flood conditions
in specific areas by provisions designed to:
      (1)   Protect human life and health;
      (2)   Minimize expenditure of public money for costly flood control
projects;
      (3)   Minimize the need for rescue and relief efforts associated with
flooding and generally undertaken at the expense of the general public;
      (4)   Minimize prolonged business interruptions;
      (5)   Minimize damage to public facilities and utilities such as water
and gas mains, electric, telephone and sewer lines, streets and bridges located
in areas of specific flood hazard;
      (6)   Ensure that the public has access to information indicating the
location of land areas which may be subject to periodic flooding;
      (7)   Ensure that those who occupy the areas of special flood hazard
assume responsibility for their actions;
      (8)   Help maintain a stable tax base by providing for the sound use and
development of flood-prone areas in such a manner as to minimize future blight
areas;
      (9)   Preserve the ability of floodplains to carry and discharge a base
flood; and
      (10)   Preserve and protect the natural resources and wildlife of the
floodplain, and to enhance the recreational, educational and aesthetic values
of the floodplain.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1361. - Methods of reducing flood losses.
   In order to accomplish its purpose, this article encourages methods of
providing for:
      (1)   Restricting or prohibiting uses which are dangerous to health,
safety and property due to water and erosion hazards, or which result in
damaging increases in erosion or in flood heights or velocities;
      (2)   Requiring that uses vulnerable to floods, including facilities
which serve such uses, be protected against flood damage at the time of initial
construction;
      (3)   Controlling the alteration of natural floodplains, stream channels
and natural protective barriers, which help accommodate or channel floodwaters;
      (4)   Controlling filling, grading, dredging and other development which
may increase flood damage; and
      (5)   Preventing or regulating the construction of flood barriers which
will unnaturally divert floodwaters or which may increase flood hazards in
other areas.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1362. - Lands to which this article applies.
   This article shall apply to all areas of special flood hazards within the
jurisdiction of the city.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1363. - Designation of regulated flood prone areas.
   (a)   The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Flood Insurance Study
(FIS) Entitled "Wayne County, Michigan (All Jurisdictions)" and dated October
21, 2021, and the Flood Insurance Rate Map(s) (FIRMS) panel number(s) of
26163C0233E, 26163C0234E, 26163C0241E, 26163C0242E, 26163C0253E, 26163C0255E,
26163C0261E, 26163C0262E, 26163C0263E, 26163C0264E, effective February 2, 2012,
and 26163CIND1C, and 26163C0270G, effective October 21, 2021, are adopted by
reference for administration of the Michigan Construction Code, and declared to
be a part of this article, of Section 1612.3 of the Michigan Building Code, and
to provide the content of the "Flood Hazards" section of Table R301.2(1) of the
Michigan Residential Code. The flood insurance study is on file at the city
clerk's office, and is available for inspection by the public at all times
during normal business hours.
   (b)   Flood hazard areas additional to those areas described in the flood
insurance study may exist in the city. The location of these areas shall be
designated by the city engineer using the best available floodplain data.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12; Ord. No. 21-1717, 9-14-21)
Sec. 5-1364. - Compliance.
   No structure or land shall hereafter be located, extended, converted or
structurally altered without full compliance with the terms of this article and
other applicable regulations.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1365. - Abrogation and greater restrictions.
   This article is not intended to repeal, abrogate or impair any existing
easements, covenants or deed restrictions. However, where this chapter and
another Code provision conflict or overlap, whichever imposes the more
stringent restriction shall prevail.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1366. - Warning and disclaimer of liability.
   The degree of flood protection required by this article is considered
reasonable for regulatory purposes and is based on scientific and engineering
considerations. Larger floods can and will occur on rare occasions. Flood
heights may be increased by manmade or natural causes. This article does not
imply that land outside the areas of special flood hazard or uses permitted
within such areas will be free from flooding or flood damages. This article
shall not create liability on the part of the city or by any officer or
employee thereof for any flood damages that result from reliance on this
article or any administrative decision lawfully made thereunder.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
** DIVISION 2. - ADMINISTRATION **
Sec. 5-1367. - Administrator designated.
   Pursuant to the provisions of the state construction code, in accordance
with Section 8b(6) of Act 230, of the Public Acts of 1972, as amended, the City
of Dearborn, by its city engineer, is hereby designated as the enforcing agency
to discharge the responsibility of the City of Dearborn under Act 230, of the
Public Acts of 1972, as amended, State of Michigan. The City of Dearborn
assumes responsibility for the administration and enforcement of said Act
through out the corporate limits of the community adopting this ordinance.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
Sec. 5-1368. - Duties and responsibilities.
   Duties of the city engineer shall include but not be limited to those given
in this section. The city engineer shall:
      (1)   Review all permits to assure that the permit requirements of this
article have been satisfied.
      (2)   Advise permittees that additional federal or state permits may be
required, and if specific federal or state permits are known, require that
copies of such permits be provided and maintained on file with the development
permit.
      (3)   Notify adjacent communities and the state flood control coordinator
at the state development office prior to any alteration or relocation of a
watercourse, and submit evidence of such notification to the Federal Insurance
Administration.
      (4)   Assure that maintenance is provided within the altered or relocated
portion of the watercourse so that the flood-carrying capacity is not
diminished.
      (5)   Verify and record the actual elevation, in relation to National
Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) of the lowest floor, including basement, of all
new or substantially improved structures.
      (6)   Verify and record the actual elevation, in relation to National
Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) to which the new or substantially improved
structures have been floodproofed.
      (7)   When floodproofing is utilized for a particular structure, obtain
