design certification from a registered professional engineer or architect to
verify such floodproofing design.
      (8)   Where interpretation is needed as to the exact location of the
boundaries of the areas of special flood hazard (for example, where there
appears to be a conflict between a mapped boundary and actual field
conditions), make the necessary interpretation. The person contesting the
location of the boundary shall be given a reasonable opportunity to appeal the
interpretation as provided in this article.
      (9)   Maintain all records pertaining to the provisions of this article,
which shall be maintained in his office, and shall be open for public
inspection.
      (10)   Promulgate other such administrative procedures as is required to
fully implement the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
Sec. 5-1369. - Establishment of development permit.
   (a)   A flood hazard area development permit shall be required in
conformance with the provisions of this article. Application of such permit
shall be on forms furnished by the city engineer. The application shall supply
all information required on the form. In addition to the aforestated, the
following information shall be provided on a site plan for the subject
property. Such site plan shall accompany the application form.
      (1)   The elevation in relation to the National Geodetic Vertical Datum
(NGVD) of the lowest floor, including basement, of all structures.
      (2)   The elevation in relation to National Geodetic Vertical Datum
(NGVD) to which the structure has been floodproofed.
      (3)   Certification by a registered professional engineer or architect
that the floodproofing methods for any nonresidential structure meet the
floodproofing criteria established in this article.
      (4)   The description of the extent to which any watercourse will be
altered or relocated as a result of the proposed development.
   (b)   In addition, application for a permit to occupy or alter the
floodplain or channel of a watercourse must be submitted to and approved by the
department of natural resources as required by Act No. 245 of the Public Acts
of Michigan of 1929 (MCL 323.1 et seq., MSA 3.521 et seq.), as amended. Any
proposed stream modifications require approval from the department of natural
resources as well as the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers under a joint permit
required by Act No. 346 of the Public Acts of Michigan of 1972 (MCL 281.951 et
seq., MSA 11.475(1) et seq.), as amended, and Section 404 or Public Law 92-500.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
Sec. 5-1370. - Fees.
   All necessary permit application required by this article shall be
accompanied by an application fee. Such fees shall be established or modified
by the city engineer.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
** DIVISION 3. - STANDARDS **
Sec. 5-1371. - General standards.
   In all areas of special flood hazard, the following provisions are required:
      (1)   All new construction and substantial improvements shall be anchored
to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement of the structure.
      (2)   All new construction and substantial improvements shall be
constructed with materials and utility equipment resistant to flood damage.
      (3)   All new construction or substantial improvements shall be
constructed by methods and practices that minimize flood damage.
      (4)   All new and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to
minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the system.
      (5)   New and replacement sanitary sewer systems shall be designed to
minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the systems and
discharges from the systems into floodwaters.
      (6)   On-site waste disposal systems shall be located to avoid impairment
to them or contamination from them during flooding.
      (7)   Any substantial improvement to a structure on which the start of
construction was begun after the effective date of this article shall meet the
requirements of the flood damage prevention program.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1372. - Residential construction.
   New construction or substantial improvement of any residential structure in
all areas of special flood hazard shall either have the lowest floor, including
the basement, elevated to or above the level of the base flood elevation or be
floodproofed so that the structure is watertight and capable of resisting
hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and effects of buoyancy. Certification by a
registered professional engineer or architect that the standards of this
subsection are satisfied may be required.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1373. - Nonresidential construction.
   New construction or substantial improvement of any commercial, industrial or
other nonresidential structure in all areas of special flood hazard shall
either have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above the
level of the base flood elevation or, together with attendant utility and
sanitary facilities, be floodproofed so that the structure is watertight with
walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water and with structural
components have the capability of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads
and effects of buoyancy. A registered professional engineer or architect shall
certify that the standards of this subsection are satisfied. Such certification
shall be provided to the director of building and safety.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1374. - Manufactured homes.
   (a)   All manufactured homes to be placed or substantially improved with R-
A and R-B districts shall be elevated on a permanent foundation such that the
lowest floor of the manufactured home is at or above the base flood elevation
and be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation system in
accordance with the provisions of paragraph (b) of this section.
   (b)   All manufactured homes shall be anchored to resist flotation, collapse
or lateral movement by providing over-the-top and frame ties to ground anchors.
Specific requirements shall be that:
      (1)   Over-the-top ties be provided at each of the four corners of the
manufactured home, with two additional ties per side at intermediate locations.
Mobile homes less than 50 feet long require one additional tie per side;
      (2)   Frame ties be provided at each corner of the home with five
additional ties per side at intermediate points and manufactured homes less
than 50 feet long requiring four additional ties per side;
      (3)   All components of the anchoring system be capable of carrying a
force of 4,800 pounds; and
      (4)   Any additions to the manufactured home be similarly anchored.
   (c)   New manufactured home parks and subdivisions; expansions to existing
manufactured home parks and subdivisions; existing manufactured home parks and
subdivisions where the repair, reconstruction or improvement of the streets,
utilities and pads equals or exceeds 50 percent of value of the streets,
utilities and pads before the repair, reconstruction or improvement has
commenced; and manufactured homes not placed in a manufactured home park or
subdivision require:
      (1)   All manufactured homes placed on stands or lots elevated on
compacted fill or on pilings so that the lowest floor of the manufactured home
will be above the base flood level;
      (2)   Provision of adequate surface drainage and access for a hauler; and
      (3)   In the instance of elevation on pilings, lots large enough to
permit steps, piling foundations placed in stable soil no more than ten feet
apart, and reinforcement provided for pilings more than six feet above the
ground level.
      (4)   This paragraph applies to manufactured homes to be placed or
substantially improved in an expansion to an existing manufactured home park or
subdivision. This paragraph does not apply to manufactured homes to be placed
or substantially improved in an existing manufactured home park of subdivision
except where the repair, reconstruction or improvement of the streets,
utilities and pads equals or exceeds 50 percent of the value of the streets,
utilities and pads before the repair, construction or improvement has
commenced.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1375. - Floodways.
   Located within areas of special flood hazard are areas designated as
floodways. Since the floodway is an extremely hazardous area due to the
velocity of floodwaters which carry debris, potential projectiles and erosion
potential, the following provisions shall apply:
      (1)   Encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial
improvements and other developments shall be prohibited unless certification by
a registered professional engineer or architect is provided demonstrating that
encroachments shall not result in any increase in flood levels during
occurrence of the base flood discharge.
      (2)   If subsection (1) above is satisfied, then all new construction and
substantial improvements shall comply with all applicable flood hazard
reduction provisions of this article.
      (3)   The placement of any manufactured homes, except in an existing
manufactured home park, shall be prohibited.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1376. - Subdivision proposals.
   (a)   All subdivision proposals shall be consistent with the need to
minimize flood damage.
   (b)   All subdivision proposals shall have public utilities and facilities
such as sewer, gas, electrical and water systems located and constructed to
minimize flood damage.
   (c)   All subdivision proposals shall have adequate drainage provided to
reduce exposure to flood hazards.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1377. - Accessory structures and uses.
   (a)   Within the flood hazard area, no accessory structure shall be used
except for one or more of the following uses and only in a manner consistent
with the requirements of permitted uses and accessory structures in the
underlying district, and with those that follow.
   (b)   Within the special flood hazard area, the following accessory
structures may be constructed below the base flood elevation:
      (1)   Garages, sheds, swimming pools, outdoor play equipment and
aboveground patios, providing each of the following are met:
         a.   The structure would not cause an increase in water surface
elevation, obstruct flow or reduce the impoundment capacity of floodplain.
         b.   No structure shall be constructed within the floodway.
         c.   All equipment and structures shall be anchored to prevent
flotation and lateral movement.
         d.   All equipment and structures shall be constructed with materials
resistant to flood damage.
         e.   All structures shall be constructed to minimize flood damage.
         f.   Electrical, heating, ventilation, plumbing and air-conditioning
equipment and other service facilities shall be designated and/or located so as
to prevent water from entering or accumulating within the components during
conditions of flooding.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
** DIVISION 4. - VARIANCE PROCEDURE **
Sec. 5-1378. - Appeal board and jurisdiction.
   (a)   The building board of appeals shall hear and decide appeals and
request for variances from the requirements of this article.
   (b)   The building board of appeals shall hear and decide appeals where it
is alleged there is an error in any requirement, decision or determination made
by the director of building and safety in the enforcement or administration of
this article.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1379. - Relevant factors and standards.
   The building board of appeals, when considering an appeal or request for
variance, shall consider all technical evaluations, all relevant factors,
standards specified in this article, state and federal requirements, and:
      (1)   The danger that materials may be swept onto other lands to the
injury of others;
      (2)   The danger to life and property due to flooding or erosion damage;
      (3)   The susceptibility of the proposed facility and its contents to
flood damage and the effect of such damage on the individual owner;
      (4)   The importance of the services provided by the proposed facility to
the community;
      (5)   The necessity to the facility of a waterfront location, where
applicable;
      (6)   The availability of alternative locations, not subject to flooding
or erosion damage, for the proposed use;
      (7)   The compatibility of the proposed use with existing and anticipated
development;
      (8)   The relationship of the proposed use to the comprehensive plan and
floodplain management program for that area;
      (9)   The safety of access to the property in times of flood for ordinary
and emergency vehicles;
      (10)   The expected heights, velocity, duration, rate of rise and
sediment transport of the floodwaters and the effects of wave action, if
applicable, expected at the site; and
      (11)   The costs of providing governmental service during and after flood
conditions, including maintenance and repair of public utilities and facilities
such as sewer gas, electrical and water systems, and streets and bridges.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96)
Sec. 5-1380. - Record of appeal actions.
   The city engineer shall maintain the records of appeal actions and report
any variances to the Federal Insurance Administration upon request.
(Ord. No. 96-680, 8-7-96; Ord. No. 12-1347, 1-24-12)
*** ARTICLE XIV. - PROPERTY MAINTENANCE CODE ***
Sec. 5-1381. - Adoption of the International Property Maintenance Code.
   A certain document, a copy of which is on file in the office of the City
Clerk of the City of Dearborn, being marked and designated as the International
Property Maintenance Code, 2006 edition, is hereby adopted in its entirety
along with any subsequent amendments as the property maintenance code for the
city for the control of nonresidential buildings and structures, and each and
all of the regulations, provisions, penalties, conditions and terms of the
above are hereby referred to, adopted, and made a part hereof, as if fully set
out in this article.
(Ord. No. 10-1289, 9-7-10)
Sec. 5-1382. - Additions, insertions, and changes.
   The International Property Maintenance Code as adopted in section
5-1381 is hereby changed and amended as follows:
      (1)   Section 101.1. Title. These regulations shall be known as the
Property Maintenance Code of the City of Dearborn, hereinafter referred to as
"this code."
      (2)   Section 103.1. General. The director of economic and community
development, or his or her designee, is designated as the enforcing agent
(hereinafter "code official") to discharge the responsibilities and enforce the
provisions of this code.
      (3)   Section 103.5. Fees. The fees for activities and services provided
by the department in carrying out its responsibilities under this code shall be
established by resolution of the city council.
      (4)   Section 106.4. Violation penalties. 
   Section 106.4.1. Civil infraction. Each of the first three (3) violations of
any provision of Section
5-1381 is a civil infraction that shall result in the assessment of fines as
follows:
   (a)   The fine for any first violation shall be not less than one hundred
dollars ($100.00) per violation, plus costs and sanctions.
   (b)   The fine for any violation which the violator has, within the past two
years, been found in violation of once before, shall be not less than two
hundred dollars ($200.00) per violation, plus costs and sanctions.
   (c)   The fine for any violation which the violator has, within the past two
years, been found in violation of twice before, shall be not less than three
hundred dollars ($300.00) per violation, plus costs and sanctions.
   Section 106.4.2. Misdemeanor. For any violation which the violator has,
within the past two years, been found in violation of at least three or more
times before, the violation shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not
less than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisonment for not more than
ninety (90) days per violation, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the
discretion of the court.
   Section 106.4.2. Separate violation for each day. A separate violation shall
be deemed committed upon each day during or when a violation occurs or
continues.
      (5)   Sections 110.1 through 110.4 , inclusive, are hereby deleted in
their entirety and the following new section 110.1 is added:
      (6)   Section 110.1. Demolition. It is unlawful for any owner or agent
thereof to keep or maintain any non-residential or residential dwelling,
building, structure, or part thereof that is a "dangerous building" as defined
in section
5-27(21) of this code of ordinances. Proceedings regarding "dangerous
buildings" and demolition shall follow the procedures set forth in section
5-27(21) through
5-27(27), inclusive, of this code of ordinances.
      (7)   Section 111.1. Application for appeal. Any person directly affected
by a decision of the code official, or a notice or order issued under this
code, shall have the right to appeal to the City of Dearborn Building Board of
Appeals, provided that a written application for appeal is filed within 20 days
after the day of the decision, notice or order was served. An application for
appeal shall be based on a claim of one or more of the following: 1) that the
true intent of this code, or the rules legally adopted thereunder, have been
incorrectly interpreted; 2) that the provisions of this code do not fully
apply; 3) that the requirements of this code are adequately satisfied by other
means; 4) that the strict application of any requirement of this code would
cause an undue hardship; or 5) that the applicant is aged and indigent, without
the resources to comply, and that failure to correct the ordered corrections or
repairs immediately does not pose an imminent danger to the health or safety of
the occupant(s).
      (8)   Section 111.2 through 111.2.5, inclusive, are hereby deleted in
their entirety and a new section 111.2 is added to read as follows:
   Section 111.2. Membership of board. The City of Dearborn Building Board of
Appeals shall act as the appeal body under this code and shall hear all appeals
under this code, with the exception of appeals relating to dangerous buildings
and demolition, which shall be appealed to the City of Dearborn Demolition
Board of Appeals. Membership of the City of Dearborn Building Board of Appeals
shall be controlled by sections 5-27(9) and 5-27(10) of this code of
ordinances. Membership of the City of Dearborn Demolition Board of Appeals
shall be controlled by section
5-27(26) of this Code of Ordinances.
      (9)   Section 111.5. Postponed hearing. When there are not at least three
(3) members present to hear an appeal, either the appellant or the appellant's
representative shall have the right to request a postponement of the hearing.
      (10)   Section 111.6. Board decision. The board shall modify or reverse
the decision of the code official only by a concurring vote of not less than
three members.
      (11)   Section 111.7. Court review. Any person aggrieved by a decision of
the board may apply to the appropriate court for a review of such decision.
Application for review shall be made to the circuit court within 20 days after
the filing of the board's decision in the office of the code official.
      (12)   Section 302.4 is hereby amended by inserting "six (6) inches" in
the first sentence.
      (13)   Section 304.14 is hereby deleted in its entirety. (See section
11-103 of this Code of Ordinances.)
      (14)   Section 602.3 is hereby deleted in its entirety. (See section
11-101 of this Code of Ordinances.)
      (15)   Section 602.4 is hereby amended by inserting the dates "October 1
to May 1."
(Ord. No. 10-1289, 9-7-10)
Sec. 5-1383. - Construction.
   The provisions of this article shall be construed, if possible, in such
manner as to make such provisions consistent with all other ordinances of the
city, including all future ordinances of the city, and all amendments thereto;
provided, however, that where any inconsistency or conflict cannot be avoided,
then the most restrictive of such inconsistent or conflicting provision shall
control and prevail.
(Ord. No. 10-1289, 9-7-10)
*** ARTICLE XV. MEDICAL AND RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA CULTIVATION AND POSSESSION
***
Sec. 5-1384. Purpose and intent.
   (a)   The purpose of this article is to exercise the police, regulatory, and
land use powers of the city by regulating standards for the growth,
cultivation, extraction, manufacture, processing, and storage of marijuana to
the extent permissible under state and federal laws and regulations, and to
protect the public health, safety, and welfare of the residents of the city. As
such this article constitutes a public purpose.
   (b)   The city finds that the activities associated with the growing,
cultivation, extraction, manufacture, processing, and storage of marijuana are
significantly connected to the public health, safety, security, and welfare of
its citizens and it is therefore necessary to regulate and enforce building,
safety, security, fire, police, health, environmental, and sanitation practices
related to such activities and also to provide a method to defray
administrative costs incurred by such regulation and enforcement.
   (c)   It is determined necessary for the health, safety, and welfare of the
city and its residents to establish standards and regulations for the growth,
cultivation, extraction, manufacture, processing, and storage of marijuana in
the city.
   (d)   Except as may be required or permitted by law or regulation, it is not
the intent of this article to diminish, abrogate, or restrict the protections
for the use of marijuana found in either the Michigan Medical Marihuana Act,
MCL 333.26421 et seq. (MMMA) or the Michigan Regulation and Taxation of
Marihuana Act, MCL 333.27951et seq. (MRTMA)
   (e)   Nothing in this article, or in any companion regulatory provision
adopted in the city's Code of Ordinances or zoning regulations, is intended to
grant, nor shall they be construed as granting, immunity from criminal
prosecution for the growth, cultivation, sale, consumption, use, distribution,
or possession of marijuana that is not in strict compliance with the MMMA or
MRTMA, applicable state and federal laws, this article, the zoning regulations,
or the City Code.
   (f)   By adopting this article and the companion regulatory provisions found
in the city's Code of Ordinance and zoning regulations, the city is not opting
into either the Michigan Medical Marihuana Facilities Licensing Act, MCL
333.2701 et seq., (MMMFLA), or the Michigan Regulation and Taxation of
Marihuana Act, MCL 333.27951 et seq. (MRTMA).
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1385. Definitions, interpretation, and conflicts.
   The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except when the context
clearly indicates a different meaning. Any term defined by MMMA or MRTMA
(collectively referred to as “the Acts”) shall have the definition given in
that particular statute. If the definition of a word or phrase set forth in
this article conflicts with the definition for the same word or phrase in the
Acts, or if a term is not defined in this article but is defined in the Acts,
then the definition in the Acts shall apply.
   Acts. Unless otherwise stated, collectively means the Michigan Medical
Marihuana Act, MCL 333.26421 et seq., the Michigan Regulation and Taxation of
Marihuana Act, MCL 333.27951 et seq., and Michigan Administrative Rules, R
333.101, et seq.
   Adult-use participant. Means an individual 21 years of age or older that
possesses, stores, and/or processes marijuana pursuant and subject to the
Michigan Regulation and Taxation of Marihuana Act, MCL 333.27951et seq.
   Collective growing operations. Means medical marijuana operations where a
caregiver has possession over marijuana plants that are not connected to the
caregiver or the qualifying patients that are registered to that particular
caregiver through the Department's registration process. Collective growing is
not allowed under the Act pursuant to People v. Bylsma, 493 Mich 17; 825 NW2d
543 (2012).
   Department. Means the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory
Affairs.
   Distribution. Means the physical transfer of any amount of marijuana in any
form by one person to any other person or persons, whether or not any
consideration is paid or received. At no time shall distribution include
marijuana that has been altered or combined with another controlled substance.
   Distributor. Means any person, including but not limited to a caregiver,
patient or any other person, who engages in any one or more acts of
distribution.
   Enclosed, locked facility. Means a closet, room, or other comparable,
stationary, and fully enclosed area equipped with secured locks or other
functioning security devices that permit access only by a registered caregiver
or registered qualifying patient. Enclosed, locked facility includes a motor
vehicle if both of the following conditions are met:
      (1)   The vehicle is being used temporarily to transport living marijuana
plants from one location to another with the intent to permanently retain those
plants at the second location.
      (2)   An individual is not inside the vehicle unless he or she is either
the registered qualifying patient to whom the living marijuana plants belong or
the individual designated through the departmental registration process as the
primary caregiver for the registered qualifying patient.
   Marijuana. Means all the parts of the plant genus cannabis, growing or not;
the seeds of the plant; the resin extracted from any part of the plant; and
every compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of the
plant or its seeds or resin, including marijuana concentrate and marijuana-
infused products. For the purposes of this article, marijuana does not include:
      (1)   The mature stalks of the plant, fiber produced from the stalks, oil
or cake made from the seeds of the plant, any other compound, manufacture,
salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of the mature stalks, except the
resin extracted from those stalks, fiber, oil, or cake, or any sterilized seed
of the plant that is incapable of germination;
      (2)   Industrial hemp; or
       (3)   Any other ingredient combined with marijuana to prepare topical or
oral administrations, food, drink, or other products.
   Marijuana concentrate. Means the resin extracted from any part of the plant
of the genus cannabis.
   Medical Marijuana Caregiver Facility (“Caregiver Facility”). Means a non-
residential caregiver facility as authorized by Ord. No. 20-1682, where
registered caregivers grow, cultivate, manufacture, extract, process, store,
distribute, assist an associated qualifying patient with his or her medical use
of marijuana, and otherwise engage in the activities allowed under this
article, the city's zoning regulations, and the Act.
   Medical use of marijuana. Means the acquisition, possession, cultivation,
manufacture, extraction, use, internal possession, delivery, transfer, or
transportation of marijuana, marijuana-infused products, or paraphernalia
relating to the administration of marijuana to treat or alleviate a registered
qualifying patient's debilitating medical condition or symptoms associated with
the debilitating medical condition, as defined in the Act, MCL 333.26423(h).
   Primary caregiver or caregiver. Means a person who is at least 21 years old
and who has agreed to assist with a patient's medical use of marijuana defined
under MCL 333.26423(k) of the Act, and who has been issued and possesses a
valid registry identification card under the Act.
   Principal residence. Means the one place where an owner of the property has
his or her true, fixed, and permanent home to which, whenever absent, he or she
intends to return and that shall continue as a principal residence until
another principal residence is established, pursuant to MCL 211.7dd(c).
   Qualifying patient or patient. Means a person who has been diagnosed by a
physician as having a debilitating medical condition, as defined under MCL
333.26423(l) of the Act.
   Registry identification card. Means the document issued by the Department
that identifies a person as a registered qualifying patient or registered
primary caregiver, as defined by the Act, MCL 333.26423(m).
   Transfer.  Means to convey, sell, give, deliver, or allow the possession by
another person or entity.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1386. General requirements for qualifying patients, primary caregivers,
and adult-use participants; general requirements for caregiver facilities;
common regulations.
   (a)   Qualifying patients. A person who has been issued and possesses a
lawful registry identification card as a qualifying patient as set forth in the
Michigan Medical Marihuana Act, MCL 333.26421 et seq. (hereinafter “MMMA”),
shall comply with the following requirements:
      (1)   Registry identification card for qualifying patients; personal
possession limits for qualifying patients. A qualifying patient who has been
issued and possesses a registry identification card, shall not be subject to
arrest, prosecution, or penalty for the use of marijuana in accordance with
state law, subject to the following:
         a.   Qualifying patients. The qualifying patient who has been issued
and possess a registry identification card may possess an amount of marijuana
that does not exceed 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana and marijuana equivalents,
and, if the qualifying patient has not specified that a primary caregiver be
allowed under state law to cultivate marijuana for the qualifying patient, 12
marijuana plants kept in an enclosed, locked facility pursuant to this article.
Any incidental amount of seeds, stalks, and unusable roots shall also be
allowed and shall not be included in this amount.
      (2)   Storage, growing, and processing of medical marijuana. Storage,
growing, and processing of medical marijuana by a qualifying patient shall only
occur within one enclosed, locked facility at the primary residence of the
qualifying patient or in another location specifically permitted by law or
ordinance so that storage, growing, and/or processing does not occur in
multiple locations. If the primary residence is being rented or leased by the
qualifying patient, the owner of the property may prohibit the smoking or
cultivation of marijuana if such prohibition is in the written lease.
         a.   The location of the enclosed, locked facility shall not be in an
area of the dwelling/premises where utilities are located that may be accessed
by someone other than the qualified patient.
       (3)   Access to medical marijuana limited. No person other than the
qualifying patient shall be engaged or involved in the growing, processing, or
handling of medical marijuana, except as permitted by law or ordinance for
primary caregivers.
   (b)   Primary caregivers. A person who has been issued and possesses a
lawful registry identification card as a primary caregiver as set forth in the
MMMA shall comply with the following requirements:
      (1)   Registry identification card for primary caregivers; possession
limits. A primary caregiver who has been issued and possesses a registry
identification card shall not be subject to arrest, prosecution, or penalty for
assisting a qualifying patient to whom he or she is connected through the
state's registration process with the medical use of marijuana in accordance
with state law. The privilege from arrest under this subsection applies only if
the primary caregiver presents both their registry identification card and a
valid operator's license or government-issued identification card that bears a
photographic image of the primary caregiver. This subsection applies only if
the primary caregiver possesses an amount of marijuana that does not exceed:
         a.   2.5 ounces of usable marijuana for each qualifying patient to
whom they are connected through the state's registration process; and
         b.   For each registered qualifying patient who has specified that the
primary caregiver will be allowed under state law to cultivate marijuana for
the qualifying patient, 12 marijuana plants kept in an enclosed, locked
facility; and
         c.   A primary caregiver may assist a maximum of five qualified
patients, plus the caregiver themselves, and may cultivate no more than 72
total marijuana plants; and
         d.   Any incidental amount of seeds, stalks, and unusable roots.
      (2)   Storage, growing, and processing of medical marijuana. A primary
caregiver may grow, process, and otherwise assist in the medical use of medical
marijuana in compliance with the MMMA in one enclosed, locked facility within
or upon an owner-occupied, detached single-family residential dwelling/premises
where the primary caregiver lives and which is the primary caregiver’s
principal residence pursuant to Michigan law, or in another location
specifically permitted by law or ordinance, so that storage, growing, and
processing does not occur in multiple locations.
         a.   The location of the enclosed, locked facility shall not be in an
area of the dwelling/premises where a utility or access to a utility is located
that may be accessed by someone other than the registered primary caregiver.
      (3)   Access to medical marijuana limited. No person other than the
primary caregiver shall be engaged or involved in the growing, processing,
dispensing, delivery, or handling of marijuana, except to the extent that the
primary caregiver lawfully transfers medical marijuana to a qualifying patient
to whom the primary caregiver is linked through the state registration system.
      (4)   Limits on primary caregivers and qualifying patients. No qualifying
patient shall visit, come to, or be present at the primary caregiver’s
residence to purchase, smoke, consume, obtain, or receive possession of any
marijuana. Rather, the primary caregiver must personally deliver the marijuana
to their qualifying patient. No person may deliver medical marijuana to a
qualifying patient other than the primary caregiver linked through the state
registry system to that qualifying patient.
      (5)   Other commodities, products, or services prohibited; joint
operations prohibited. The residential premises upon which a primary caregiver
cultivates medical marijuana shall not be a location at which any other
commodity, product, or service is also sold, distributed, or otherwise
available. It shall be a violation of this article for any person to
participate as a primary caregiver in a jointly operated facility where primary
caregivers jointly share building space which is used in common to dispense
medical marijuana to qualifying patients or assist qualifying patients with the
medical use of marijuana.
      (6)   Dispensaries and cooperatives prohibited. Medical marijuana
dispensaries and cooperatives are prohibited.
      (7)   Location. The proposed location for a primary caregiver must comply
with the locational requirements of the Zoning Ordinance.
   (c)   Adult-use participants. A person 21 years or older that possesses,
stores, and/or processes marijuana in accordance with the Michigan Regulation
and Taxation of Marihuana Act, MCL 333.27951et seq. (hereinafter “MRTMA”),
shall comply with the following requirements:
      (1)   Storage, growing, and processing of marijuana. An adult-use
participant may store, grow, and process not more than ten ounces of marijuana
and any marijuana produced by marijuana plants cultivated on their residential
premises. They may also cultivate not more than 12 marijuana plants for
personal use, provided that no more than 12 marijuana plants are possessed,
cultivated, or processed on the premises at once.
      (2)   Access to marijuana limited. Any marijuana in excess of 2.5 ounces
within the person's place of residence must be stored in a container or area
equipped with locks or other functioning security devices that restrict access
to the contents of the container or area. In addition, marijuana plants must be
cultivated in an enclosed area equipped with locks or other functioning devices
that restrict access to the area.
   (d)   Caregiver facilities; new facilities prohibited; permit and
certificate of occupancy required.
      (1)   New facilities prohibited. On the effective date of this article,
no new facilities will be allowed to operate pursuant to this subsection, and
no facilities may move their location within the city or expand their
operations. Only those facilities that have been issued a permit pursuant to
this subsection or its precursor ordinance (Ord. No. 20-1682) on the effective
date of this article will be allowed to operate pursuant to the terms and
conditions of this article, and shall be considered legal non- conformities
that must adhere to the applicable regulations for non- conforming structures
found in the City's Zoning Ordinance.
      This subsection does not prohibit registered primary caregivers from
cultivating medical marijuana in accordance with the MMMA and the provisions of
this article and Zoning Ordinance Sec.
7.03.
      (2)   Permit and certificate of occupancy required. Only primary
caregivers with a valid state-issued registry identification card may assist
with a qualifying patient's medical use of marijuana in the city, and no
registered caregivers shall be allowed to assist with a qualified patient's
medical use of marijuana pursuant to this subsection without first obtaining
the necessary inspections, paying the required fees, and obtaining the needed
permit(s), and certificate(s) of occupancy as provided in this subsection, the
Code of Ordinances, and the Zoning Ordinance.
      (3)   Inspections. Each caregiver facility is required to submit to an
annual inspection by the building official or their designee, fire department,
and any other applicable local and/or state officials. In addition,
intermediate inspections may occur if deemed necessary by the building
official, fire department, or their designees, and fees for annual or
intermediate inspections shall be assessed as provided in the city's Code of
Ordinances.
      (4)   A primary caregiver may only grow, cultivate, extract, manufacture,
process, store, distribute, and/or otherwise assist a connected qualifying
patient with his or her medical use of marijuana in an industrial district for
not more than five qualifying patients and the primary caregiver only, subject
to the following general conditions:
         a.   A primary caregiver under this subsection may only grow,
cultivate, extract, manufacture, process, store, distribute, and/or otherwise
assist an associated qualifying patient with their medical use of marijuana
pursuant to this subsection and the applicable zoning regulations;
         b.   No marijuana may be sold or offered for sale on the premises,
except as is produced on the premises by the primary caregiver for the
qualifying patient or patients only;
         c.   The activity shall not generate noise or odors offensive to the
surrounding area;
      (5)   Change of information and duty to inform. The owner of a caregiver
facility is responsible for notifying the director of the department of
economic development, or their designee, [or the building official or their
designee] if there is a change of information regarding any of the following:
         a.   The number of registered caregivers at a particular facility
changes from the information provided in the application for a caregiver
certificate or application for renewal.
         b.   There is a change in the configuration of the facility that would
require a commercial renovation or re-occupancy permit.
         c.   Notice of a change of information must be provided in writing, by
either first-class mail or hand-delivery, to the Director of the Department of
Economic Development within ten (10) business days of becoming known.
      (6)   Leases. All lease or rental agreements between the owner of a
building, structure, facility, or premises being used for the activities
authorized under this article and a lessee, and/or between the owner or lessor
and the registered caregivers engaged in the activities authorized under this
article within that building, structure, facility, or premises, shall include a
provision in the lease or rental agreement that prohibits “collective growing
operations” as that term is defined in this article.
         a.   Copies of these lease agreements shall be provided to the
director of the department of economic development, the city's zoning
administrator, and the city's corporation counsel within ten days of the lease
or agreement being signed by all parties to the agreement.
         b.   No assistance with the medical use of marijuana may take place in
any building, facility, or premises in the city where a lease or rental
agreement is in effect unless and until a copy of the agreement is provided to
the city under the terms of this article.
         c.   If any changes are made to the terms of an existing lease or
agreement, a copy of the amended lease or agreement must be provided to the
city's corporation counsel within ten days of the amended lease or agreement
being signed by all parties to the agreement.
         d.   Failure to comply with the provisions of this subsection is a
violation of this article, and may result in the suspension or revocation of
all applicable permits and certificates of occupancy, in addition to all other
penalties permitted under this article.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1387. Common regulations for qualifying patients, primary caregivers,
adult-use participants, and caregiver facilities.
   In addition to these common regulations, site development standards for
marijuana and medical marijuana home occupations can be found in Section
7.03 of the City's Zoning Ordinance.
   (a)   Modification of residential dwelling for marijuana related purposes.
Any modifications to the dwelling made for the purpose of cultivating medical
marijuana shall comply with all applicable building, electrical, mechanical,
and fire safety code requirements, including all requisite permit applications
and related inspections.
   (b)   Enclosed, locked facility. All medical marijuana cultivation, growing,
and manufacturing, must occur within an enclosed, locked facility permitted
under this article, the Code of Ordinances, and the City's zoning regulations,
and such activities, with the exception of transportation as allowed in this
article the Act, can occur only in locations not visible to the public and
adjoining uses.
   (c)   Collective growing prohibited. A primary caregiver may only grow,
cultivate, manufacture, extract, deliver, transfer, store, distribute, and/or
otherwise assist an associated qualifying patient with his or her medical use
of marijuana within an “enclosed, locked facility,” as that term is defined in
this article and the MMMA. If more than one caregiver will be growing, storing,
manufacturing, cultivating, distributing, or otherwise assisting an associated
qualifying patient with their medical use of marijuana in a single building,
collective growing operations are strictly prohibited. To avoid collective
growing operations each primary caregiver may only engage in the medical use of
marijuana described in the MMMA and this article in a separate enclosed and
locked sub-facility within the overall building or facility that is equipped
with security features that make it accessible only by a single, particular
primary caregiver or the qualifying patients connected to that particular
caregiver.
   (d)   Signs not allowed. No sign in the form of a device, structure,
fixture, or placard using graphics, symbols, and/or written copy designed
specifically for the purpose of advertising or identifying a particular
dwelling or property as being associated with the use or cultivation of medical
marijuana.
   (e)   Noise, vibration, glare, light, fumes, odor, and electrical
interference. No equipment or process shall be used in growing, processing, or
handling marijuana which creates noise, vibration, glare, light, fumes, or
electrical interference detectable to the normal senses at or beyond the
property line of the qualifying patient's or adult-use participant's
residential property. In the case of electrical interference, no equipment or
process shall be used which creates visual or audible interference with any
radio, television, or similar receiver off the premises or causes fluctuation
of line voltage off the premises.
   (f)   Odor control measures. If it is determined by the city upon inspection
or complaint that odors related to the growth, cultivation, storage,
processing, extraction, or manufacture of marijuana are escaping unabated
beyond the property line of the premises, the owner or occupant of the
residential dwelling or structure shall install a ventilation system or unit(s)
designed to prevent such emission of odors beyond the property line. Such
system must comply with all relevant code regulations and shall be subject to
review, inspection and approval by the relevant city department(s) as
determined by the building official or their designee.
      (1)   Ventilation controls required for caregiver facilities. All
caregiver facilities within the city must have a ventilation system or unit(s)
to prevent the emission of odors from escaping beyond the property line of the
facility or premises. Such system must comply with all relevant code
regulations and shall be subject to inspection and approval by the relevant
city department as determined by the building official or their designee.
   (g)   Compliance for medical use of marijuana. The medical use of marijuana
shall comply at all times and in all circumstances with the Michigan Medical
Marihuana Act, MCL 333.26421 et seq., the Administrative Rules, R 333.101 et
seq., and this article.
   (h)   Inspections and permits. All necessary inspections and permits must be
obtained for any alterations of any portion of the building in support of or in
association with the cultivation of marijuana.
      (1)   A primary caregiver assisting with the medical use of marijuana
under the provision of this article and the MMMA must present their valid
state-issued registry identification card during any inspection upon request.
   (i)   Storage of chemicals. The storage of any chemicals such as herbicides,
pesticides, and fertilizers, are subject to inspection and approval by the fire
department, the building official, their designees, and/or other applicable
local and/or state officials.
   (j)   Modifications. Any modifications to the dwelling unit made for the
purpose of cultivating marijuana must comply with all applicable building,
electrical, mechanical, and fire safety code requirements, including all
requisite permit applications and related inspections.
   (k)   Butane extraction prohibited. The separation of plant resin from a
marijuana plant by butane extraction or any other method that utilizes a
substance with a flashpoint below 100 degrees Fahrenheit in any public place, a
motor vehicle, inside a residential dwelling, or the curtilage of a residential
dwelling is prohibited.
   (l)   Compliance for existing growers. Residential properties within the
city that are being utilized for growing, cultivating, harvesting, and/or
storing of marijuana on the effective date of this section must come into
compliance with the provisions of this article, the City's Zoning Ordinance,
and all applicable code requirements within 180 days of the effective date of
this article.
   (m)   Medical marijuana presumption. There shall be a presumption that a
qualifying patient or primary caregiver is engaged in the medical use of
marijuana in accordance with the MMMA and this article if the qualifying
patient or primary caregiver:
      (1)   Is in possession of a registry identification card; and
      (2)   Is in possession of an amount of marijuana that does not exceed the
amount allowed under the MMMA or this section. The presumption may be rebutted
by evidence that conduct related to marijuana was not for the purpose of
alleviating the qualifying patient's debilitating medical condition or symptoms
associated with the debilitating medical condition, in accordance with this
article.
   (n)   Presumed responsible party. The owner of the property, as identified
by the city's property tax rolls, shall be presumed to be the party responsible
for compliance with the registration and regulatory requirements of this
article.
   (o)   Compliance with state law. All individuals engaged in the lawful
possession of marijuana pursuant to the provisions of this article shall also
comply with all applicable provisions of state law, including the MMMA and
MRTMA.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1388. Location registration; certificate of occupancy required;
application; de factor status for existing caregiver facilities; inspection;
other requirements; disqualification, suspension, or revocation; reservation of
authority.
   (a)   Registration required; certificate of occupancy. No cultivation,
manufacture, extraction, growing, or cultivation of medical marijuana shall be
lawful at a location within the city until the location has been registered
under this article and issued a certificate of occupancy. Once a certificate of
occupancy has been issued the property shall be added to a registry list.
      (1)   Exception. Registration is not required for the principal residence
or homestead of a qualifying patient or adult-use participant where marijuana
is cultivated for such patient's or participant's personal use.
   (b)   De facto registration for caregiver facilities; responsibility of
facility owner. Facilities that have been issued a permit pursuant to this
article or its precursor ordinance (Ord. No. 20-1682) on the effective date of
this article, and otherwise meet the requirements to operate under this
article, will be considered registered pursuant to this article. The
registration fee required under this subsection shall be waived.
      (1)   As a condition of their de facto registration status, and in
addition to the responsibilities of previously noted in this article, a
facility owner shall have a continuing responsibility under this article to
ensure that any primary caregiver assisting with the medical use of marijuana
within the owner's facility has a valid state-issued registry identification
card.
   (c)   Effect of registration.
      (1)   Registration does not prohibit prosecution by the city, state, or
federal government for violations of applicable ordinances, laws, or statutes.
      (2)   Compliance with city ordinances and state statutes, including the
MMMA and MRTMA, if applicable, is a condition of acceptance and maintenance of
registration status, and a registration may be suspended for cause pursuant to
the provisions of this article.
       (3)   Suspension of a certificate of compliance is not an exclusive
remedy and nothing contained herein is intended to limit the city's ability to
prosecute code violations that may have been the cause of the suspension or any
other code violations not protected by the Act.
   (d)   Application for registration for caregivers in residential dwellings.
Subject to the exceptions in this section, the owner of a residential dwelling
being used for the medical use of marijuana shall submit a registration form to
the director of the department of economic development or their designee. The
registration form shall be on a form approved by the director, and shall
require the emergency and non-emergency contact information for the owner of
the property and a proxy in the event of the owner's lack of availability
during an emergency. The completed registration form must be accompanied by the
following:
      (1)   A photocopy of the front of the current and valid caregiver
registry card issued by the state to the person who is permitted to grow,
cultivate, harvest, and store medical marijuana and who will be doing so at the
registered location. Upon expiration of the card, the registration form shall
be updated and a new copy of the renewed card shall be provided to the director
of the department of economic development, or their designee.
      (2)   A floor plan, with dimensions, illustrating the enclosed and locked
location in the building where marijuana will be grown, cultivated, harvested,
processed, and stored, and detailing the security measures related to that
location and the building.
      (3)   Specification of the number of qualifying patients for whom
marijuana will or may be grown, cultivated, harvested, and stored.
      (4)   Details regarding electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and any other
code- related improvements and installations or facilities that will be used
for growing, cultivating, harvesting, and storing the marijuana.
      (5)   Any additional information that the fire marshal, building
official, or their designees deem necessary for evaluating code compliance and
public safety associated with the proposed growing, cultivating, harvesting,
and storing of marijuana at the registered location in the manner proposed in
the registration materials.
      (6)   Payment of a non-refundable registration fee of $250.
   (e)   Review. Upon receipt of all required documents, information, and
payment, the director of the department of economic development, or their
designee, shall circulate the documents and information to the building
official, fire marshal, or their designees, for review. If, after review, the
building official and/or fire marshal, or their designees, require any
additional information relating to security measures, fire safety, code
compliance, or compliance with this article, the property owners shall be
advised in writing of the additional information required and the owner shall
provide such information before any growing, cultivation, harvesting, or
storage of marijuana may occur at the proposed location.
   (f)   List of registered properties; notice of approval. The director of the
department of economic development, or their designee, shall maintain a list of
approved registered caregiver properties, and will provide a copy of this list,
along with any updated lists, to the chief of police and any other department
that is deemed appropriate by the director.
   (g)   Annual inspection; certificate of compliance renewal; qualified
patient list; entry for inspection; duty to update information.
      (1)   Annual inspection. Each caregiver and caregiver facility is
required to submit to an annual inspection of their property and caregiving
location by the building official, fire marshal, and/or their designees, or
more frequently if determined to be necessary. Upon successful completion of
all inspections and the issuance of all required Permits, the director of the
department of economic development, or their designee, shall issue a
registration certificate for the property, which shall be prominently and
conspicuously displayed on or within the enclosed, locked facility approved
during the review process and where medical marijuana will be grown,
cultivated, harvested, and/or stored.
      (2)   Annual renewal and re-inspection. Annual inspections are required
for a renewal of a certificate of compliance.
      (3)   Qualified patient list. A primary caregiver must maintain a list of
their qualifying patients by registration number with the state. This list is
subject to inspection during inspections conducted pursuant to this article. At
no time shall the city copy or retain a copy of this list.
      (4)   Entry for inspection. Nothing in this article shall prohibit the
owner of a residential dwelling or structure, or a caregiver facility, from
denying entry. However, nothing shall prevent the fire marshal, building
official, or their designees from asking permission from an owner for
permission to inspect.
         a.   In the event an owner denies entry for an inspection, nothing in
this article shall prohibit the fire marshal, building official, or their
designees from seeking an administrative search warrant based on probable cause
to conduct an inspection pursuant to this article or the Acts.
         b.   Refusal to allow an inspection under this subsection is
considered a violation of this article if an inspection is refused after an
administrative search warrant is obtained.
   (h)   Change of information and duty to inform. A registered caregiver is
responsible for notifying the director of the department of economic
development, or their designee, [or the building official or their designee] if
there is a change of information regarding any of the following:
      (1)   Validity of registry identification card as a primary caregiver.
      (2)   The number of qualifying patients for whom marijuana will or may be
grown, cultivated, harvested, and stored.
      (3)   Change in the configuration of the enclosed, locked facility on the
premises where marijuana is being grown, cultivated, harvested, and stored.
      (4)   Any information contained in the registration application.
      (5)   Notice of a change of information must be provided in writing, by
either first-class mail or hand-delivery, to the director of the department of
economic development within ten business days of becoming known.
   (i)   Grounds for suspension or revocation of registry status. The director
of the department of economic development may issue a written notice of
suspension or revocation of registry status if any of the following occur:
      (1)   The applicant has knowingly or recklessly allowed two or more
violations of the regulations of this article or the applicable regulations in
Chapter 13 of this Code in the preceding 12-month period and the violations
have been adjudicated;
      (2)   The applicant has knowingly or recklessly allowed a nuisance, as
defined under the Revised Judicature Act of 1961, MCL 600.3801, to be
maintained upon the premises;
      (3)   The subject premises has existing violations of building, zoning,
plumbing, mechanical, electrical, health, nuisance, or fire prevention codes;
      (4)   The applicant has knowingly or recklessly operated the facility
during a period of time when the certificate was suspended; and/or
      (5)   The applicant has knowingly or recklessly engaged in illegal
activity or allowed any illegal activity to occur in or on the certified
premises that violate the regulations of this article, the Zoning Ordinance,
state or local law, or applicable code requirement.
   (j)   Effect of appeal of conviction. The fact that any relevant conviction
in violation of this article is being appealed shall have no effect on the
revocation or suspension.
   (k)   Reservation of authority. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in
this article, no applicant has a right to the issuance of a certificate of
occupancy or a certificate of compliance. The city hereby reserves the right to
determine who, if anyone, shall be entitled to such a certificate, based on the
objective criteria listed in this article and the Zoning Ordinance which
relates to concerns for public health, safety, and welfare as identified
herein.
   (l)   Confidentiality. Information treated as confidential under the MMMA
that is received by the city, including all information provided to the city
pursuant to this section, shall be deemed confidential due to the
confidentiality requirements of the MMMA. It shall not be distributed or
otherwise made available to the public unless required by law or court order.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1389. Enforcement.
   (a)   Notice of violation. If a violation or condition(s) causing or
contributing to a violation of this article is discovered, a notice of
violation shall be issued. Such notice shall inform the owner or occupant of
the nature of the violation, and require the owner or operator of the facility
to eliminate and correct the violation or condition(s) causing or contributing
to the violation within 14 days of notification.
   (b)   Violation and penalty. Failure to correct a violation within the time
permitted after receiving notice under subsection (a) of this section shall
constitute a violation of this article. Unless another penalty found in local,
state, or federal law applies to the particular violation, a person who
violates this article is responsible for a civil infraction punishable by a
fine of $1,000.00, plus any additional conditions imposed by a court of
competent jurisdiction.
   (c)   Repeat violation. An increased fine schedule shall be imposed for
repeat violations of this article. As used in this section, “repeat violation”
means a violation committed within 90 days of an admission or determination of
responsibility for a violation of this article occurring upon the same
property. The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall be a civil fine of
$2,500.00, plus any additional costs and/or conditions imposed by the court.
   (d)   Other penalties. Nothing in this article shall be deemed to prohibit
the city from imposing other penalties authorized by the City's Code of
Ordinances, including nuisance violations and any other legal action in a court
of competent jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1390. Appeals.
   (a)   Appeals of administrative interpretations and decisions from
regulations within the Code of Ordinances or this article shall be made to the
building board of appeals.
      (1)   Exceptions. The following are exempt from the appeal provisions
outlined in this section:
         a.   Any provision or regulation found in this article that is also
contained in the MMMA and/or MRTMA cannot be appealed.
         b.   Any appeal from the requirements of the Zoning Ordinance,
including any regulations found in this article that are also found in the
Zoning Ordinance, shall be heard by the Zoning Board of Appeals pursuant to
Section
32.05 of the Zoning Ordinance.
   (b)   Application for appeal. An application for appeal shall be made within
20 days after the decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order complained
of by filing with the Building Official and the board a written notice of
appeal specifying the grounds of the appeal and the relief sought, and paying a
filing fee. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim of one or more
of the following:
      (1)   That the true intent of the regulations within the Code of
Ordinances or this article have been incorrectly interpreted;
      (2)   That the provisions of the regulations within the Code of
Ordinances or this article do not fully apply;
      (3)   That the requirements of the Code of Ordinances or this article are
adequately satisfied by other means;
      (4)   That the strict application of any requirements of the Code of
Ordinances or this article would cause an undue hardship; or
      (5)   That the applicant is aged and indigent, without the resources to
comply, and that failure to correct the ordered corrections or repairs
immediately does not pose an imminent danger to the health or safety of the
occupant(s).
   (c)   Scope and procedure of appeal; variances. The appeal procedure is
intended to provide limited relief from the requirements of this article in
cases where a strict application of a particular requirement shall create an
unnecessary hardship affecting a substantial property right. This procedure is
intended to address extraordinary, exceptional, or unique situations that were
not caused by an act or omission of the applicant or the applicant's
predecessor in title, employee, or agent. Relief is not to be granted merely on
the basis of inconvenience or financial burden.
   Subject to the exceptions found in this section, a variance from the
requirements of this article may be allowed only in cases where there is
evidence of practical difficulty. Increased costs in complying with the
requirements of this article shall not be considered a basis for granting a
variance. In this case, all of the following criteria shall be met:
      (1)   Exceptional circumstances or conditions. There are exceptional or
extraordinary circumstances or conditions applying to the property that do not
generally apply to other properties in the same zoning district or neighboring
area, such as lot shape, abutting property issues, motorist safety, or scale of
building or lot frontage.
      (2)   Substantial property right. A variance is necessary to preserve a
substantial property right similar to that possessed by other properties in the
same zoning district.
      (3)   Not self-created. The immediate practical difficulty causing the
need for the variance was not created by the applicant or any other person
having an interest in the sign, sign structure, or property.
      (4)   No substantial detriment. Granting the variance will not be
detrimental to the public welfare, be injurious to other properties or
improvements, endanger public safety or substantially impair property values in
the area.
      (5)   Master Plan, zoning ordinance, or this article. A variance will be
consistent with, and will not materially impair, the spirit and intent of the
City Master Plan, zoning ordinance, or this article.
   (d)   Hearing before the Building Board of Appeals. At the hearing the
petitioner shall be given an opportunity to be heard and to show why such
decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order should be modified or
withdrawn.
   (e)   Action by Building Board of Appeals. After hearing, the building board
of appeals shall sustain, modify, or withdraw the decision, ruling,
interpretation, notice, or order, depending upon its findings to whether the
provisions of this article and of the rules and regulations adopted pursuant
thereto have been complied with. If the board sustains or modifies such
decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order, it shall be deemed to be an
order.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Sec. 5-1391. No vested rights.
   A property owner shall not be deemed to have any vested rights or
nonconforming use rights that would serve as a basis for failing to comply with
the requirements of this article.
(Ord. No. 22-1782, 12-14-22)
Chapter 6 - CABLE TELECOMMUNICATIONS[1] 
Footnotes:
