*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 6-1. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Cable television or cable communications shall mean any communications
system which distributes cablecast or broadcast programs, pay programs or other
services by means of coaxial cable or other state-of-the-art equipment
installed on, over or under the public right-of-way.
   Commission shall mean the Dearborn Telecommunications Commission.
   Premium television shall mean a show, channel or service for which a
separate fee is charged such as pay television, or security service.
   Upstream shall mean signals travelling from subscribers to the headend or
electronic control center.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.2, 4-7-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 6-2. - Exception.
   This chapter shall not apply to any cable communications system in operation
in the city on April 7, 1981.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 5.1, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-3. - Franchise required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to own or operate a cable television or
cable communications system within the city, unless authorized by a valid grant
of franchise.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.3, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-4. - Manner of issuance of franchise.
   No grant of franchise shall be valid unless authorized by ordinance adopted
by the city council and until a franchise agreement has been executed by the
mayor and filed with the city clerk. The council may, by resolutions, authorize
the mayor to execute agreements to extend a franchise for periods of less than
one year.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.4, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-5. - Suspension, revocation of franchise.
   (a)   The city council may suspend or revoke the franchise of any cable
television or cable communications system for violation of any of the
provisions of this chapter, upon the recommendation of the commission.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any cable television
or cable communication system in the city to collect subscriber fees for any
period of time when the franchise has been suspended or revoked by the city
council. The city may bring action on behalf of itself or subscribers to
recover any such fees collected.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 4, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-6. - Local representative, telephone required.
   All persons owning or operating a cable television or cable communications
system within the city shall designate a local representative, operate a local
business office within the corporate limits of the city and shall have a
publicly listed telephone.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.5, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-7. - Emergency override system.
   All cable television or cable communications systems operated within the
city shall include emergency override operation which shall permit the mayor or
his designee to override all audio and visual signals simultaneously in the
case of emergencies, as determined by the mayor. The city shall conduct monthly
tests of the emergency override operation.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.6, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-8. - Conflict of interest.
   Any person owning or operating a franchised cable television or cable
communications system in the city is specifically prohibited from recommending
a particular manufacturer, sales or service establishment, or engaging in the
sale, service, rental, leasing of television receivers, radio receivers, or
television or radio receiver related parts and accessories anywhere in Wayne,
Oakland or Macomb counties. Such owner or operator shall prohibit its officers,
agents, and employees from violating the terms of this section, whether in the
performance of cable system duties or otherwise.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.7, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-9. - Protection of subscriber's privacy.
   All subscriber information shall be deemed private. It shall be unlawful for
any person owning or operating any cable television or cable communication
system in the city to publish, sell, distribute, trade or in any way
disseminate subscriber names, addresses, phone numbers, cable services or any
other subscriber information without the express written consent of the
subscriber. Such consent shall be obtained separately from any other document,
shall be effective no longer than one year, and shall describe the specific
intended use for which the consent is solicited.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.8, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-10. - Monitoring, etc., device restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any cable television or
cable communications systems in the city to install any monitoring device,
polling device or reverse (upstream) transmission device without the written
consent of the subscriber.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.9, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-11. - Map, plats of system to be filed.
   The owner or operator of all franchise cable television or cable
communications systems operating in the city shall file with the city engineer
and the department of communications, annually, during construction years, and
every two years thereafter, a current map and subsidiary plats showing the
exact location of the transmission and distribution facilities and equipment of
the system.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.10, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-12. - Services to be offered without discrimination.
   Every cable television or cable communications system operated in the city
shall offer service to all subscribers without discrimination as to rates,
policies, facilities or service within subscriber classifications. This section
shall not prohibit promotional campaigns, prepayment discounts, bona fide
system employee discounts, or service without charge to educational and
governmental facilities and buildings. This section shall not prohibit
classification discounts permitted by a franchise ordinance.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.11, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-13. - Disconnection fees prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for the owners or operators of cable television or
cable communication systems within the city to charge any fee for the
disconnection of service.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.12, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-14. - Maintenance of facilities, equipment.
   All facilities and equipment of any franchised cable television or cable
communications system operating in the city shall be constructed and maintained
at a state-of-the-art level in accordance with the requirements and
specifications of the National Electrical Code, the rules and regulations of
the Federal Communication Commission, the standards of the National Association
of Broadcasters, the standards of the National Association of Cable Television
Broadcasters and all other pertinent ordinances and codes of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 1.13, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-15. - Discontinuance of nonpremium service restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any cable television or
communications system in the city to discontinue nonpremium service for a
subscriber arrearage of less than two months duration without the consent of
the subscriber, the commission, or without first securing a judgment against
the subscriber.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.1, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-16. - Entry on private property restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any cable television or
communications systems in the city to enter upon private land or buildings
without due process of law, including hearing, or without the consent of the
owner or holder. Consent for entry shall not be elicited as part of any
subscription agreement or application.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.2, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-17. - Defense against suit for collection of subscriber fees.
   Violation by a franchisee of one or more of the provisions of this chapter
shall be a lawful defense to any suit by the franchisee for the collection of
unpaid subscriber fees.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.3, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-18. - Record of complaints, etc.
   All complaints, service requests and subscriber inquiries regarding the
accuracy, fairness or legality of billings shall be recorded in written or
printed form by the operator of all cable television or cable communication
systems operating within the city. Such records shall include the date and time
received and the date and time completed along with all service, corrective
action or other disposition actions.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.4, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-19. - Retention of records.
   All billing, revenue, service and complaint records of all cable television
or cable communication systems operating within the city shall be maintained by
such operators for no less than five years after the year of origin, shall be
made available to the city for inspection at a place within the city and for
such time as the city shall request.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.5, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-20. - Copies of complaints, pleadings.
   All franchised cable television and cable communications owners or operators
shall submit, within 30 days of filing, a copy of all complaints and all
pleadings filed by such owner or operator in every suit or action arising from
operation of any system in the city to the commission.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.6, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-21. - Unauthorized connections to system.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to make any physical connection to any
franchised cable television or cable communication system operating in the city
that is not authorized by the operator of such system.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.7, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-22. - Interference with system.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to wilfully damage, destroy, remove,
obstruct or interfere with any part of any franchise cable television or cable
communication system operating in the city.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.8, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-23. - Prohibited modification of equipment.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to make any modification to system
equipment or to any system-connected equipment so as to induce any
uncompensated franchised cable television or cable communications system
service or level of service for which the operator has established compensation
rates.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 3.9, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-24. - Cable television rate regulations.
   (a)   The city adopts by reference rules of the Federal Communications
Commission set forth in Subpart N (Cable Rate Regulation) of Part 76 (Cable
Television Service) of chapter I of Title 47 of the Code of Federal Regulations
regarding the regulation of cable television rates for basic service and
associated equipment, as amended.
   (b)   After a cable operator has submitted for review its existing rates for
the basic service tier and associated equipment costs or a proposed increase in
these rates, the city clerk shall publish a public notice of the rates and
costs giving interested parties, including the cable operator, a reasonable
opportunity to file written comments which shall be available in the office of
the city clerk for public inspection and copying during normal business hours.
   (c)   The city adopts by reference procedures set forth in 47 CFR § 0.459
regarding confidential business information submitted by a cable operator in a
rate regulations proceeding.
   (d)   A cable operator which willfully or repeatedly fails to comply with a
rate decision or refund order directed specifically at the cable operator shall
be subject to a monetary forfeiture not to exceed $25,000.00 for each violation
of each day of a continuing violation not to exceed $250,000.00, as determined
by the city following the procedures set forth in 47 USC §§ 503(2)(D), (3)(A)
and (B), (4)(A), (B) and (C) which the city adopts by reference.
   (e)   A copy of the rules and procedures adopted by reference in this
section shall be available in the office of the city clerk for public
inspection and copying during normal business hours.
   (f)   In the event of a conflict between this section and a cable television
franchise, the provisions of this section shall prevail.
(Ord. No. 93-573, §§ 1—6, 11-3-93)
Secs. 6-25—6-45. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - COMMISSION ***
Sec. 6-46. - Established.
   There is hereby established the Dearborn Telecommunications Commission which
shall consist of nine members appointed by the mayor and confirmed by the city
council for a term of three years. The first appointments to the commission
shall be three commissioners each for one-year, two-year and three-year terms,
as designated by the mayor. One person appointed to the commission shall have
technical television or communications experience, and one person appointed to
the commission shall have television programming experience.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.1, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-47. - Quorum.
   A majority of the appointed members of the commission shall constitute a
quorum. Five votes shall be required for commission action.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.2, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-48. - Staff support, administration.
   The director of the research and information department shall provide staff
support and shall be charged with the day-to-day administration of the business
of the commission.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.3, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-49. - Meetings, rules.
   The commission shall adopt a schedule of meetings, shall adopt rules for the
orderly conduct of business and shall annually elect officers.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.4, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-50. - Powers, duties generally.
   The commission shall administer all cable television and cable
communications franchises on behalf of the city; shall establish operational
standards; shall review and make recommendation after public hearing upon any
application for increase in cable system fees or charges; shall review and make
recommendation upon any proposal for any new franchise, for the renewal of any
franchise, and for any new cable system services. The commission shall also
establish and/or review and approve all rules governing local access, content
and programming, and shall approve franchise system policies.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.5, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-51. - Recommendations.
   Recommendations of the commission shall be addressed to the mayor and city
council and shall be filed with the city clerk. Recommendations for new
franchises, renewals or extensions of existing franchises, and proposals for
new services for which a subscriber fee is charged shall require council
action.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.6, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-52. - Manner of granting, extending franchise.
   The city council shall grant or award franchises and renewals thereof by
ordinance. Extensions of franchises for periods of less than one year may be
authorized by resolution. Proposals for any new cable system services may be
approved by resolution authorizing the mayor to execute an addendum to the
franchise agreement.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.7, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-53. - Rate, fee increases.
   Recommendations for the grant or denial of any cable system rate or fee
increase shall only be made after public hearing by the commission upon the
application for rate increase. Such recommendations will be automatically
adopted 60 days after the filing of the recommendation with the city clerk.
Such recommendations shall be final unless a new public hearing before the city
council upon the rate or fee increase is requested by the franchisee, the mayor
or two members of the city council. If such hearing is requested, the increase
shall not automatically be effective but shall abide council action. At public
hearing before the city council, the council may adopt or reverse the
recommendation of the commission, in whole or in part, or may remand, in whole
or in part, to the commission for rehearing or reconsideration.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.8, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-54. - Appeal from commission action.
   The commission's decisions, rulings or adoptions of operational standards;
rules governing local access, content, and programming; and franchise policies
may be appealed to the city council by any party or person aggrieved thereby.
The council may uphold or reverse the ruling or decision or may remand to the
commission for rehearing or reconsideration.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.9, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-55. - Furtherance of local interests.
   The commission is authorized in the name of the city, with the approval of
the city council, to administer gifts, grants, trusts, scholarships and
donations; to allocate funds for local programming, educational and
governmental cable applications, and for related purposes fostering community
origination, local programming and training.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.10, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-56. - Franchisee participation at meetings.
   At the request of the commission, the designated local representative of any
franchised cable system shall attend and respond at any meeting of the
commission. All franchised cable systems shall also submit a written annual
report to the commission, including such topics as programming finances,
technical matters and future directions of the company.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.11, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-57. - Annual report.
   The commission shall submit an annual, written report to the mayor and to
the city council.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.12, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-58. - Annual budget.
   The commission shall submit an annual, written budget to the mayor and city
council.
(Ord. No. 81-17, § 2.13, 4-7-81)
Sec. 6-59. - Sanctions, penalties.
   (a)   The city council may suspend or revoke the franchise of any cable
television or cable communications system for violation of any of the
provisions of this chapter upon the recommendation of the city
telecommunications commission.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any cable television
or cable communication system in the city to collect subscriber fees for any
period of time when the franchise has been suspended or revoked by the city
council. The city may bring action on behalf of itself or subscribers to
recover any such fees collected.
   (c)   Violation of any provision of this chapter shall be a misdemeanor
punishable as prescribed in section
1-9 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 81-17, §§ 4.1—4.3, 4-7-81)
Secs. 6-60—6-70. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - FRANCHISE REGULATIONS ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 6-71. - Short title.
   This article shall be known and may be cited as the Dearborn
Telecommunications Systems Regulatory Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.1, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.1, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.1, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-72. - Definitions.
   Unless otherwise stated, the following definitions of terms shall apply
throughout this article:
   Cable service means the one-way transmission to customers of (i) video
programming, or (ii) other programming service, and customer interaction, if
any, which is required for the selection or use of such video programming or
other programming service. The definition of cable service contained in section
602 of the Cable Act is incorporated by reference. Any service to residential
customers shall be subject to council approval, which shall not be unreasonably
withheld or delayed. Specifically excluded are common carrier or other non-
cable television telecommunications services and any leasing of system capacity
to users who provide telecommunications services directly or indirectly to
customers.
   Cable system shall mean a facility, consisting of a set of closed
transmission paths and associated signal generation, reception, and control
equipment that is designed to provide cable service which includes video
programming and which is provided to multiple customers within a community and
used to provide cable service pursuant to and in accordance with a franchise,
including all network facilities such as cables, conduits, access manholes,
rights-of-way, equipment, devices and appurtenances to be used by grantee to
make the cable system network fully operational. The definition of cable system
contained in section 602 of the Cable Act is incorporated by reference.
Specifically excluded are non-cable television telecommunications systems and
any leasing of system capacity or fibers to users who provide
telecommunications services directly or indirectly to customers.
   City shall mean the City of Dearborn.
   Council shall mean the City Council of the City of Dearborn.
   Customer is any person who contracts with a grantee for, or is in any manner
provided with telecommunications service or cable service.
   Franchise is a non-exclusive, limited authorization awarded by ordinance for
the construction, maintenance and operation of a telecommunications system or
cable system on, under, over or across the public ways of the city and/or to
transact local telecommunications or cable television business therein.
   Grantee is any holder of a telecommunications system franchise granted
pursuant to this article. Telecommunications systems franchises for cable
systems and services and/or telecommunications systems and services, as defined
in this article may be granted under this article.
   Person shall mean any individual, corporation, partnership or any other
entity.
   Telecommunications service means the provision or offering of
telecommunications service (either directly or as a carrier for others) to
persons within the city by means of the telecommunications system. Specifically
excluded are telecommunications services or cable services subject to
regulation under the Cable Act of 1984, 47 U.S.C. S 521, et seq. as amended
("Cable Act"). Any service to residential customers shall be subject to council
approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
   Telecommunications system means the telecommunications network to be
constructed and installed by grantee and used to provide telecommunications
service pursuant to and in accordance with a franchise, including all network
facilities such as cables, conduits, access manholes, rights-of-way, equipment,
devices and appurtenances to be used by grantee to make the telecommunications
network fully operational. Specifically excluded are telecommunications systems
or cable systems subject to regulation under the Cable Act.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.2, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.2, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.2, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-73. - Franchise required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to own, service, use, transmit over or
operate a telecommunications system or cable system within the city unless
authorized by a valid grant of franchise.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.3, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.3, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.3, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-74. - Granting of franchises.
   The city may grant one or more franchises for telecommunications systems or
cable systems in the city subject to this article. The city specifically
reserves the right to grant, at any time, such additional franchises for a
telecommunications system or cable system as it deems appropriate. Additional
franchises shall not be deemed to modify, revoke, terminate or damage any
rights previously granted to any other grantee.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.4, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.4, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.4, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-75. - Authorization by ordinance.
   No grant of franchise shall be valid unless authorized by ordinance adopted
by the council and until a franchise agreement has been executed by the mayor
and filed with the city clerk. The mayor is authorized to execute agreements to
extend a franchise for a period of one year or less.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.5, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.5, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.5, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-76. - Business office.
   All persons owning or operating a telecommunications system or cable system
within the city shall designate a local representative, operate a local
business office within the greater Detroit Metropolitan area, and shall have a
publicly-listed telephone.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.6, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.6, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.6, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-77. - Filing of current map and subsidiary plats.
   The owner(s) or operator(s) of all franchised telecommunications systems or
cable systems operating in the city shall file with the city engineer and the
department of communications annually during a construction year and every two
years thereafter, a current map and subsidiary plats showing the exact location
of the transmission and distribution facilities and equipment of the system in
the public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.7, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.7, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.7, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-78. - Construction and maintenance of equipment.
   All facilities and equipment of any franchised telecommunications system or
cable system operating in the city shall be constructed and maintained at a
state-of-the-art level in accordance with the applicable requirements and
specifications of the National Electrical Code as adopted by the City of
Dearborn, the applicable rules and regulations of the Federal Communication
Commission, and all other pertinent ordinances and codes of the city.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.8, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.8, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.8, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-79. - Compensation to city.
   The franchise agreement required by section
6-75 may contain such terms and conditions, including, without limitation,
compensation to the city for use of rights-of-way and provision by the grantee
of telecommunications or cable services and facilities to the city, as public
interest may require, subject to the limitations of any applicable federal,
state or local law.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.9, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.9, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.9, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-80. - Franchise fee.
   In recognition of the unique character of telecommunications franchises, a
franchise fee shall be determined through a negotiated franchise fee procedure
based upon the value of services for similar agreements and other pertinent
factors.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.10, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.10, 8-1-95; Ord. No.
97-696, § 1.10, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-81. - Transfer of franchise.
   Any franchise granted by the city hereunder is to be held in personal trust
by the grantee and may not be sold, transferred, assumed or assigned in any
manner either directly or indirectly, without the prior written consent of the
council.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 1.11, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 1.11, 8-1-95; Ord. No.
97-696, § 1.11, 2-18-97)
Secs. 6-82—6-90. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - DEPARTMENT OF COMMUNICATIONS **
Sec. 6-91. - Administration and review of franchises.
   The Dearborn Department of Communications (the "department of
communications") shall administer all telecommunications and cable television
franchises on behalf of the city; shall review and make recommendations upon
any proposal for any amendment of an existing franchise, any new franchise and
for the renewal of any franchise.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 2.1, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 2.1, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 2.1, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-92. - Recommendations.
   Recommendations of the department of communications shall be addressed to
the mayor and council and shall be filed with the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 2.2, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 2.2, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 2.2, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-93. - Appeal of rulings.
   The department of communications decisions, rulings or adoptions of
operational standards and franchise policies may be appealed to the council by
any party or person aggrieved thereby. The council may uphold or reverse the
ruling or decision or may remand to the department of communications for
rehearing or reconsideration.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 2.3, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 2.3, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 2.3, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-94. - Local representative.
   At the request of the department of communications, the designated local
representative of any franchised telecommunications system or cable system
shall attend and respond at any meeting called by the department of
communications provided, however, that such representative is given reasonable
notice prior to the meeting.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 2.4, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 2.4, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 2.4, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-95. - Advisory commission.
   The mayor shall appoint an advisory commission (Dearborn Telecommunications
Commission) to advise the city and council on matters related to
telecommunications systems franchises. The commission shall be organized as
follows:
      (1)   The commission shall be made up of seven members, appointed by the
mayor and confirmed by the council.
      (2)   The term of office for each commissioner shall be two years. For
the first appointments, the term of office for three commissioners shall be one
year and the term of office for the remaining four commissioners shall be two
years.
      (3)   The purpose of the commission will be to advise the mayor and
council and hold public hearings on issues including rate setting proceedings,
revocation proceedings, renewal proceedings and any other purposes as
designated by the mayor.
(Ord. No. 97-696, § 2.5, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-96. - Administer gifts, grants, etc.
   The Dearborn Telecommunications Commission is authorized in the name of the
city, with the approval of the city council, to administer gifts, grants,
trusts, scholarships and donations for local programming, educational and
governmental cable applications and for related purposes fostering community
origination, local programming and training.
(Ord. No. 97-696, § 2.5, 2-18-97)
Secs. 6-97—6-100. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - SANCTIONS AND PENALTIES **
Sec. 6-101. - Suspension or revocation.
   The council may revoke any franchise of any telecommunications system or
cable system for violation of any of the material provisions of this article
and/or any telecommunications systems franchise ordinance upon the
recommendation of the department of communications, provided, however, that
grantee is given written notice of the violation and a reasonable opportunity
to cure the same. The time for cure shall be for such period as may be
reasonably necessary to correct the violation as determined by the department
of communications.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 3.1, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 3.1, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 1.1, 2-18-97; Ord. No. 97-696, § 3.1, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-102. - Collection of fees when franchise suspended or revoked.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any telecommunications
system or cable system in the city to collect customer fees for any period of
time when its franchise has been revoked by the council. The city may bring
action on behalf of itself or customers to recover any such fees collected.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 3.2, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 3.2, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 3.2, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-103. - Entering private land or buildings.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of any telecommunications
system or cable system in the city to enter upon private land or buildings
without due process of law including notice and hearing or without the consent
of the owner or possessor except as allowed by applicable state and federal
laws.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 3.3, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 3.3, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 3.3, 2-18-97)
Sec. 6-104. - Violation.
   Violation of any provisions of this article and/or any Telecommunications
Systems Franchise Ordinance shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not
more than $500.00 or by imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both such
fine and imprisonment. Each day of a continuing violation may be charged and
punished as a separate and distinct offense.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § 3.4, 8-16-94; Ord. No. 95-644, § 3.4, 8-1-95; Ord. No. 97-
696, § 3.4, 2-18-97)
Secs. 6-105—6-120. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE IV. - METROPOLITAN FIBER SYSTEMS OF DETROIT, INC. FRANCHISE ***
Sec. 6-121. - Granting of franchise.
   (a)   The City of Dearborn grants Metropolitan Fiber Systems of Detroit,
Inc, hereafter called MFS, a nonexclusive franchise to construct, operate and
maintain a telecommunications system within the corporate boundaries of the
City of Dearborn for a term of 15 years from the date of execution of this
franchise agreement.
   (b)   Any franchise and the rights, privileges, authority, and
responsibilities established shall take effect and be in force from the date of
execution of this franchise agreement only if within 30 days after the date of
the granting of the franchise, MFS files with the Mayor of the City of Dearborn
its acceptance of the franchise terms, all required letters of credit,
construction bonds and insurance certificates, and pays to the city clerk all
reasonable costs incurred by the city in preparing, considering and awarding
this franchise, including legal, engineering, technical, publication and other
expenses, said costs not to exceed $2,500.00. If MFS fails to timely comply
with this section, it shall acquire no rights, privileges, or authority
whatsoever.
   (c)   This franchise is subject to all of the provisions of the Dearborn
Telecommunications Systems Regulatory Ordinance.
   (d)   Unless otherwise stated, the following definitions of terms shall
apply throughout this article:
   City means the City of Dearborn.
   Council means the City Council of the City of Dearborn.
   Customer means any person who contracts with MFS for, or is in any manner
provided with telecommunications system service.
   Department of communications means the City of Dearborn Department of
Communications.
   Franchise means a nonexclusive, limited authorization awarded by ordinance
for the construction, maintenance and operation of a telecommunications system
on, under, over or across the public ways of the city and/or to transact local
telecommunications business therein.
   Gross revenues means all of the revenue, as determined in accordance with
generally accepted accounting principles, that is derived from the installation
and operation of the telecommunications system within the city.
   Person means any individual, corporation, partnership or any other entity.
   Service means the provision or offering of special access or private line
telecommunications service (either directly or as a carrier for others) to
persons within the city by means of the telecommunications system. Specifically
excluded are telecommunications services subject to regulation under the Cable
Act of 1984, 47 U.S.C. § 521 et seq. as amended ("Cable Act") as well as home
residential service. Any expansion of service to residential customers shall be
subject to council approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or
delayed.
   Telecommunications system means the telecommunications network to be
constructed and installed by MFS and used to provide service pursuant to and in
accordance with this franchise, including all network facilities such as
cables, conduits, access manholes, rights-of-way, equipment, devices and
appurtenances to be used by MFS to make the telecommunications network fully
operational. Specifically excluded are telecommunications systems subject to
regulation under the Cable Act.
   (e)   No installation of any telecommunications system facility shall be
performed or conducted in the city unless plans therefor shall have been first
submitted to the city engineer and a construction permit issued therefor.
Within nine months after the date MFS accepts the terms of this franchise, MFS
shall complete construction of the backbone route for the telecommunications
system. MFS shall have the ability to perform lateral construction in order to
provide service to additional buildings any time during the term of this
franchise.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § I, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-122. - Franchise fee payments.
   (a)   MFS shall annually pay to the city a franchise fee in an amount equal
to three percent of the gross revenues received by MFS. Payments due the city
under the terms of this section shall be paid quarterly on or before the last
day of January, April, July and October of each year.
   (b)   The city shall be furnished a certificate with each payment reflecting
the computations for the period covered by the payment. Any payment shall bear
interest at the prime rate plus one percent after the due date. The estimated
initial payment shall be $3,000.00 for the franchise.
   (c)   Franchise fees shall be in addition to any other tax, charge, fee, or
payment due the city by MFS which are imposed on all businesses operating in
the city.
   (d)   Not less than annually, MFS shall provide the city with an opinion as
to the accuracy of the franchise fee payments paid within the preceding 12
months. Said certifications shall be prepared internally by MFS in accordance
with generally accepted accounting standards as established by the financial
accounting standards board (FASB) and shall be kept confidential by the city.
The city reserves the right, upon reasonable notice to MFS, to audit all books
and records of MFS necessary to determine compliance with the terms of this
franchise at least three times during the term. The city shall pay for all
costs and expenses associated with any such audit.
   (e)   In the event that MFS is granted rights to place fiber optic cable in
and upon public roads, rights-of-way and easements of, and/or to transact local
telecommunications business in, another municipality with less than 500,000
people within the tri-county area of Wayne, Macomb and Oakland Counties,
pursuant to compensation terms which would, if applied to the city, result in
MFS paying a higher percentage of revenue than required under this franchise,
the city shall have the option to replace the percentage of revenue payable
hereunder with the percentage applicable to MFS in that municipality. The city
shall notify MFS in writing of its election to accept such alternative terms.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, the city shall retain all rights available to it
under law.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § II, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-123. - New developments.
   (a)   The city may amend this article from time to time, to allow MFS to
innovate and implement new services and expansion of its telecommunications
system backbone network or to impose any terms allowed by law which are applied
uniformly to all telecommunication carriers.
   (b)   The department of communications may require interconnection to the
telecommunications system or services for emergency communications.
   (c)   In addition to those matters required in this franchise, MFS shall
make the following express representations:
      (1)   MFS shall have no recourse whatsoever against the city for any
loss, cost, expense or damage arising out of any of the lawful provisions or
requirements of this article or because of the enforcement thereof by city,
unless caused by the gross negligence or willful or intentional misconduct of
the city or its agents, employees or representatives. MFS expressly
acknowledges that on accepting a franchise it did so relying on its own
investigation and understanding of the power and authority of the city.
   By acceptance of a franchise, MFS acknowledges that it has not been induced
to enter into a franchise by any understanding or promise or other statement,
whether verbal or written, by or on behalf of city or by any other third person
concerning any term or condition of this franchise not expressed in this
article.
      (2)   MFS further acknowledges by the acceptance of this franchise that
it has carefully read the terms and conditions herein, and is willing to and
does accept all of the risks of the meanings of such terms and conditions.
   (d)   MFS shall at all times comply with all laws and regulations of the
state and federal government or any administrative agency. However, if any such
state or federal law or regulation shall require MFS to perform any service, or
shall permit MFS to perform any service, or shall prohibit MFS from performing
any service, in conflict with the terms of this franchise or of any law or
regulation of the city then as soon as possible, MFS shall notify the city of
the point of conflict believed to exist between such regulation or law and the
laws and regulations of the city or the franchise.
   (e)   If any provision of this franchise is held by any court of competent
jurisdiction to be invalid as conflicting with any federal or state law, rule
or regulation now or hereafter in effect, or is held by such court to be
modified in any way in order to conform to the requirements of any law, rule or
regulation, said provision may be considered a separate, distinct and
independent part of the franchise, and such holding shall not affect the
validity and enforceability of all other provisions. In the event that such
law, rule or regulation is subsequently repealed, rescinded, amended or
otherwise changed, so that the provision which had been held invalid or
modified is no longer in conflict with the law, rules or regulations, said
provision shall return to full force and effect and shall be binding on the
parties.
   (f)   If a material provision of this franchise is affected by action of a
court or of the state or federal government, it may be modified to such
reasonable extent as may be necessary to carry out the full intent and purpose
of this franchise provided the intent and purpose of the franchise is not
contravention of any law, regulation or order of a court.
   (g)   MFS agrees not to unreasonably oppose intervention by the city in any
suit or proceeding related to this article to which MFS is a party. MFS agrees
to abide by all provisions of this article and its franchise and further agrees
that it shall not make any claim against the city that the provisions of this
article or franchise are unreasonable, arbitrary or void, without having a
reasonable basis in the law.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § III, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-124. - Liability.
   (a)   MFS shall defend, indemnify, protect and hold harmless the city, its
officers, agents, employees, departments and boards from any and all claims,
losses, liabilities, causes of action demands, judgments, decrees, proceedings,
and expenses of any nature (including without limitation reasonable attorneys
fees) arising out of, or resulting from the acts or omission of MFS, its
officers, agents, employees, contractors, successors or assignees, unless such
claims are caused by the gross negligence or intentional or willful misconduct
of the city.
   (b)   MFS shall carry worker's compensation insurance with statutory limits
and employer's liability insurance with limits of no less than $100,000.00
which shall cover all operations to be performed for construction, maintenance
and operation of the telecommunications system.
   (c)   MFS shall carry comprehensive general liability, including completed
operations, independent contractors, and contractual liability coverage, and
comprehensive automobile liability insurance with bodily injury limits of not
less than $500,000.00 per person and $1,000,000.00 per occurrence which shall
cover all operations. MFS shall also carry property damage liability insurance
with limits of not less than $500,000.00.
   (d)   MFS shall furnish certificates of such insurance to the city. The
certificates shall be approved by the corporation counsel of the city, shall
list the city as an additional insured, and shall provide that the insurance
shall not be canceled or materially changed unless 30 days prior written notice
shall be given to the city.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § IV, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-125. - General capability.
   (a)   In furtherance of the general policy that the services provided be
innovative and modern, MFS, in the exercise of its reasonable business
judgment, will actively pursue a continuous policy of incorporating new
technical developments into the system to reflect the "state of the art." City
may waive this requirement at its discretion.
   (b)   MFS shall provide four fibers ("city's fibers") for the use of the
city throughout its entire telecommunications system in the city and shall
provide 10,000 feet of four fiber cable to the city. This fiber and cable shall
become the property of the city and remain so throughout the duration of this
franchise. Upon expiration of this franchise, said fiber and cable shall remain
the property of the city. MFS shall connect up to four fibers to the city's
fibers at up to a maximum of six splice locations. The city's use of these
fibers shall be limited to its exclusive, internal telecommunications use and
shall not be sold, assigned, or transferred to or by third parties.
   (c)   In the event that the city wishes to utilize any services of the
telecommunications system, MFS agrees to provide those services to the city at
the lowest rate that it charges any of its commercial customers for comparable
services.
   (d)   During construction of any part of the telecommunications system, if
MFS installs conduit in the public right-of-way within the city, then MFS
shall, at the same time, install one 1¼-inch conduit for the use of the city,
provided, however that such use shall be limited to the city's exclusive,
internal telecommunications use and shall not be sold, assigned, or transferred
to or by third parties.
   (e)   In the event of an emergency or other urgent community need, MFS
shall, upon request of the city, make available its facilities to the city for
the duration of the emergency at no charge.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § V, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-126. - Conditions of street occupancy.
   (a)   The poles, wires, and appurtenances of MFS' system shall be located,
erected, and maintained upon existing utility facilities wherever reasonable
and feasible. MFS shall use underground equipment in all cases where all other
utilities are required to use underground equipment and in all cases where city
ordinance requires underground installation.
   (b)   MFS shall be allowed, subject to appropriate regulation, to set its
own poles, anchors, guys, and similar facilities within public rights-of-way
within the city when necessary and upon the securing of permits from the city.
   (c)   All facilities erected by MFS within the city shall be so located as
to cause minimum interference with the proper use of public rights-of-way and
public places and to cause minimum interference with the rights and convenience
of adjoining property owners.
   (d)   In case of disturbance or damage to any street, sidewalk, alley,
public way, street sign or other public property, MFS shall at its own expense
promptly and in a manner acceptable to the city, replace, repair, and otherwise
restore such disturbance or damage.
   (e)   MFS shall act diligently and without delay to repair, regardless of
time of day, any safety hazard that occurs involving MFS' equipment and plant.
   (f)   If, at any time during the term of this franchise, the city shall
properly elect to undertake public building or construction, altering the
grade, alignment, or location of any street, sidewalk, alley, or public way MFS
promptly shall, upon reasonable written notice from the city, remove and
relocate its facilities at MFS' expense in a manner reasonably acceptable to
the city. The city shall use its best efforts to find MFS a suitable relocation
for its facilities. In the event of emergency, the city may sever, disrupt,
dig-up or otherwise destroy facilities of MFS using its best efforts to notify
MFS prior to performing such work whenever practicable. Repairs to MFS'
equipment and facilities shall be done at MFS' expense.
   (g)   MFS shall at all times employ ordinary care and shall install and
maintain industry standards and services for preventing failures and accidents
which would cause damage, injuries, or nuisance to the public.
   (h)   Prior to the installation of any portion of the telecommunications
system, MFS is responsible for obtaining all applicable permits and approvals
from the city, Wayne County, State of Michigan and any other parties with
control of that portion of the right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § VI, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-127. - Technical and construction standards.
   (a)   MFS shall construct, install and maintain its telecommunications
system in a manner consistent and in compliance with all applicable laws,
ordinances, construction standards, governmental requirements, and technical
standards established by the Federal Communications Commission or state agency.
Upon request by the city, MFS shall provide to the city written reports of MFS'
performance tests conducted pursuant to such state or federal standards and
requirements.
   (b)   MFS shall at all times comply with the National Electrical Safety Code
(National Bureau of Standards); National Electrical Code (National Bureau of
Fire Underwriters); applicable federal, state and local regulations; and other
applicable codes and ordinances of the city.
   (c)   In any event, the telecommunications system shall not endanger or
interfere with the safety of persons or property within the city or other areas
where MFS may have equipment located.
   (d)   All working facilities, conditions, and procedures, used or occurring
during construction of the telecommunications system shall comply with the
standards of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.
   (e)   Construction, installation and maintenance of a telecommunications
system shall be performed in an orderly and workmanlike manner, and in close
coordination with public and private utilities serving the city following
accepted industry construction procedures and practices and working through
existing committees and organizations.
   (f)   All cable and wires shall be installed, where possible, parallel with
electric and telephone lines, and multiple cable configurations shall be
arranged in parallel and bundled with due respect for engineering
consideration.
   (g)   MFS shall develop an adequate preventive maintenance policy and shall
file it with the department of communications.
   (h)   MFS shall develop an adequate customer service policy and repair/
maintenance standards and shall file it with the department of communications.
   (i)   MFS shall immediately join the Miss Dig Program.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § VII, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-128. - Maps, records and reports.
   (a)   MFS shall provide to the city, prior to start of construction,
complete plans for the initial build out of the telecommunications system for
approval by the appropriate city departments.
   (b)   MFS annually shall file with the city clerk a copy of its annual
financial reports when such reports are completed by MFS and ready for
distribution.
   (c)   MFS shall submit to the city such other information reports either
electronically or in such other form and at such times as the city may
reasonably request.
   (d)   Subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations, MFS shall
keep open books and records. The city shall have the right to inspect at any
time during normal business hours all books, records, maps, plans, performance
test results and other like materials of MFS which relate to the operation of
the telecommunications system. All requested books or records, or copies
thereof, shall be provided to the city at the department of communications
within a reasonable time after the initial request.
   (e)   MFS shall allow the city to make inspections of any of MFS' facilities
and equipment at any time upon receiving prior written notice.
   (f)   All records, reports required under this section, except as otherwise
provided, to be provided to the city shall be available for public inspection
in the city clerk's office during normal business hours.
   (g)   The refusal, failure, or neglect of MFS to file any of the records or
reports required to be provided to the city under this section shall be deemed
a material breach of this franchise, and shall subject MFS to all penalties and
remedies, legal or equitable, which are available to the city.
   (h)   Any material false or misleading statement or representation knowingly
made by MFS in any report shall be deemed a material breach of this franchise,
and shall subject MFS to all penalties and remedies, legal or equitable, which
are available to the city.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § VIII, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-129. - Transfer of rights.
   (a)   Neither the franchise nor any rights or obligations of MFS pursuant to
this franchise or the ordinance nor any of MFS's controlling interest in the
telecommunications system shall be assigned, transferred, sold, leased or
sublet in any manner, to any person, without the prior consent of the council,
which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or unduly delayed. Nothing
herein shall prevent MFS from assigning its rights and obligations to a parent,
affiliate or subsidiary of MFS upon notice to the city. Further, nothing herein
shall prevent or prohibit MFS, or any of its parents, subsidiaries or
affiliates, from granting a security interest in any of MFS' or any of its
parents', subsidiaries' or affiliates' financing transactions. The grant or
waiver of any one or more of said consents shall not render unnecessary any
subsequent consent or consents, nor shall the grant of any said consent
constitute a waiver of any other rights of the city.
   (b)   No franchise nor any part or portion thereof granted hereunder may be
sold, transferred or assigned until the initial build out of the
telecommunications system which MFS has proposed to provide and install
pursuant to this franchise is 100 percent completed and operational for a
period of one year except as may be mutually agreed to by MFS and the city.
   (c)   MFS shall not transfer, sell or assign any portion of its interest in
this franchise or in its telecommunications system without prior approval of
the council. MFS shall have the responsibility:
      (1)   To show to the reasonable satisfaction of the city whether the
proposed purchaser, transferee, or assignee (the "proposed transferees"),
which, in the case of a corporation, shall include all officers, directors,
employees and all persons having a legal or equitable interest in five percent
or more of its voting stock, or any of the proposed transferee's principals:
         a.   Has ever been convicted or held liable for acts involving moral
turpitude (including, but not limited to, fraud, misrepresentation to any
federal or state agency, violation of any securities law), or is presently
under an indictment, investigation, or complaint charging such acts.
         b.   Has ever had a judgment in an action for fraud, deceit or
misrepresentation entered against it, her, him, or them by any court of
competent jurisdiction.
         c.   Has pending any legal claim, law suit or administrative
proceeding arising out of or involving a telecommunications system.
      (2)   To establish to the reasonable satisfaction of the city the
financial solvency of the proposed transferee by submitting all current
financial data for the proposed transferee and such other data as the city may
request.
      (3)   To establish to the reasonable satisfaction of the city that the
financial standing of the proposed transferee is such that the proposed
transferee shall be able to maintain and operate the telecommunications system
for the remaining term of the franchise.
   (c)   Any proposed transferee shall execute an agreement, in a form and
containing conditions approved by the council, that it will assume and be bound
by all of the provisions, terms and conditions of this franchise and all
applicable federal, state and local laws and further, that the transferee shall
be primarily liable and obligated under said documents without, however
relieving MFS from its obligations to the city under this franchise.
   (d)   Nothing in any approval by the city of an authorization of any
transfer or assignment of any ownership interest shall be construed to waive or
release any rights of the city in and to the streets, public ways and public
places of the city, or as a release of any of the city's police powers, or as
an exercise of eminent domain.
   (e)   The occurrence of any event which constitutes either in act of
bankruptcy by MFS as defined in the Federal Bankruptcy Act; or placement of MFS
into receivership or the issuance of any order to MFS or any of its
stockholders by a government agency or court of competent jurisdiction to
divest any interest related to the telecommunications system or the entry of
any judgment against MFS which, in the opinion of the city, impairs MFS'
credits or MFS' failure to meet its financial obligations on a continuing
basis, shall be deemed an unauthorized transfer and assignment under the
provisions of this subsection and shall:
      (1)   Be deemed a material breach and default of this franchise; and
      (2)   Subject MFS to all penalties and remedies prescribed in this
franchise and to all other remedies, legal and equitable, which are available
to the city.
   (f)   The occurrence of an unauthorized transfer or assignment may, at the
option of the city, terminate this franchise and accelerate all of the
obligations and rights thereunder. MFS shall notify the city of any occurrence
which constitutes an unauthorized transfer and of the entry of any judgment
against it within 24 hours of knowledge of such occurrence or of when MFS
should have had knowledge of such occurrence. From and after any notification
of an unauthorized occurrence, MFS shall not make, execute or enter into any
deed, deed of trust, mortgage, conditional sales contract or any loan, pledge,
sale, pole agreement or any other agreement or hypothecation concerning any of
the facilities or property, real or personal, of MFS without the written
approval of the city, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld.
   (g)   In the event of an express conflict between a provision in this
article and a provision in the telecommunications systems regulatory ordinance,
the provision in this article shall control.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § IX, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-130. - Construction and performance guarantee and letter of credit.
   MFS shall, within 30 days of the execution of this franchise, file with the
city clerk, a cash bond in the amount of $100,000.00, provided, however, that
such bond shall be reduced to $50,000.00 upon completion of construction and
further reduced to $10,000.00 one year after construction. The purpose of the
bond is to guarantee the timely construction and operation of the
telecommunications system. The bond shall be for the purpose of allowing
recovery by the city of any and all damages, loss or costs suffered by the city
resulting from the failure of MFS to satisfactorily complete and fully activate
and maintain the telecommunications system throughout the city.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § X, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-131. - Termination.
   (a)   In addition to all other rights and powers reserved or pertaining to
the city, the city reserves as an additional and as a separate and distinct
remedy the right to terminate this franchise and all rights and privileges of
mfs thereunder in any of the following events or for any of the following
reasons:
      (1)   MFS fails after 30 days prior written notice to comply with any of
the provisions of this franchise or has, by act or omission, violated any term
of condition provided, however, that such period shall be extended for a period
of time as may be reasonably necessary to correct such noncompliance or
violation; or
      (2)   MFS becomes insolvent, unable or unwilling to pay its debts, or is
adjudged a bankrupt; or
      (3)   MFS attempts to or does practice any fraud or deceit in its conduct
or relations with the city under this franchise; or
      (4)   City condemns substantially all of the property of MFS within the
city by the lawful exercise of eminent domain.
   (b)   No termination, except for reason of condemnation and revocation at
will, shall be effective unless or until the city shall have adopted a
resolution setting forth the cause and reason for the revocation and the
effective date, which resolution shall not be adopted without 30 days prior
notice to MFS and an opportunity for MFS to be heard on the proposed
resolution. If the revocation depends on a finding of fact, such finding of
fact made by the city after the hearing provided for, if requested by MFS,
shall be conclusive.
   (c)   Upon the expiration or termination of this franchise, MFS shall have
the option to, without expense to the city and within such time as the city may
reasonably require, remove its telecommunications system and restore the
premises hereby authorized to be used and occupied to a condition reasonably
satisfactory to the city, or to abandon said telecommunications system. In the
event MFS chooses to abandon said telecommunications system, the city, after 30
days prior written notice, shall be allowed to take over said
telecommunications system located within the public ways of the city, as
property of the city, without compensation, and in no event shall MFS have any
claim for damages against the city or account of the taking over of said
telecommunications system, nor shall MFS have any obligation to the city or any
third party for the abandonment of said telecommunications system.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XI, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-132. - Acceptance of agreement and incorporation of ordinance by
reference.
   Upon execution of this franchise by MFS, MFS agrees to be bound by all of
its terms and conditions. In addition, MFS specifically agrees that this
ordinance of the city is incorporated by reference and made a part of the
permit of franchise.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XII, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-133. - Severability.
   (a)   If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase or word of this
franchise is for any reason held invalid or unconstitutional by any court of
competent jurisdiction by action of MFS, such portion shall be deemed a
separate, distinct and independent provision, and such holding shall not render
invalid or terminate this franchise.
   (b)   The headings incorporated by this article are or organizational
purposes only and shall not be deemed part of the franchise granted to MFS.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XIII, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-134. - Tampering with telecommunications system.
   (a)   A person who willfully or maliciously damages, or causes to be
damaged, any wire, cable, conduit, apparatus or equipment of either party, or
who commits any act with intent to cause damage to any fiber, wire, cable,
conduit, apparatus or equipment of either party, or who taps, tampers with, or
connects any fiber or wire or device to a fiber, wire, cable, conduit or
equipment of either party with intent to obtain a signal or impulse therefrom
without authorization, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
   (b)   This section shall not prevent MFS from removing, disconnecting or
otherwise rendering inoperable any of its apparatus or equipment attached or in
any way connected to such person's facilities, if done for reasonable cause.
   (c)   The prohibitions, penalties and remedies set forth in this section are
in addition to any penalties and remedies for theft, fraud or destruction of
property provided by state, local or federal law.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XIV, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-135. - Notices.
   All notices shall be in writing, and shall be deemed delivered to the
addressee thereof two days after deposit at a main or branch United States Post
Office, and shall be certified or registered mail, return receipt requested,
postage prepaid or sent by overnight delivery or telefacsimile, properly
addressed to the parties, respectively, as follows:
   For notices and communications to MFS:
      Metropolitan Fiber Systems of Detroit, Inc.
      c/o MFS Telecom, Inc.
      One Tower Lane, Suite 1600
      Oakbrook Terrace, Illinois 60181
      Attn: General Counsel
   Invoices to MFS shall be sent to "accounts payable" at the above address.
   For notices and communications to the city:
      City of Dearborn
      13615 Michigan Avenue
      Dearborn, Michigan 48126
      Attn: City Clerk
   By notice complying with the foregoing requirements of this section, each
party shall have the right to change the address or addressee or both for all
future notices and communications to such party, but no notice of a change of
address shall be effective until actually received.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XV, 8-16-94)
Sec. 6-136. - Amendments.
   This franchise may be amended only by written agreement of both parties.
(Ord. No. 94-605, § XVI, 8-16-94)

*** ARTICLE II. DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT[2]  ***
Footnotes:
--- (2) ---
Editor's note— Ord. No. 09-1226, adopted June 1, 2009, amended Art. II in its
entirety and enacted similar provisions as set out herein. The former Art. II
derived from Ord. No. 81-122, §§ 1—3, adopted Nov. 4, 1981.
Sec. 7-26. - Established.
   (a)   There is hereby created and established in and for the city a
department in the city government to be known as the Department of Economic
Development which shall be under the supervision of a director, who shall be
appointed by the mayor in accordance with the Charter provisions pertaining to
the directors of departments, and shall receive such compensation as shall be
fixed by the council.
   (b)   The city council shall provide the necessary appropriations annually
to provide suitable office space, facilities, equipment and personnel to carry
on the work of the Department of Economic Development.
   (c)   The director shall be the appointing authority for all employees who
may be required to operate the department.
(Ord. No. 09-1226, 6-1-09; Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Sec. 7-27. - Functions and duties.
   The director of the Department of Economic Development shall supervise and
control the department. Functions and duties of the director shall include, but
not be limited to, the following:
   (1)   To be responsible for helping maintain and expand existing businesses
and industries, attracting new business and industry to the city, as well as
develop new programs beneficial to the general development of the city.
   (2)   Planning and coordinating the activities of the city and private
business in connection with the improvement and beautification of the business
districts within the community.
   (3)   Planning and coordinating the activities of the city and private
industry in connection with the improvement and beautification of the
industrial districts within the community.
   (4)   To serve as the administrative liaison and provide supportive staff
for the East Dearborn Downtown Development Authority, West Dearborn Downtown
Development Authority, East Dearborn Development Area Citizens Council, West
Dearborn Development Area Citizens Council, commercial corridor improvement
authorities, economic development corporation, Brownfield Redevelopment
Authority, and zoning board of appeals.
   (5)   To coordinate the economic and community development department's
activities with related planning activities of other departments or
subdivisions of the government and with those of other state, local and federal
governmental agencies.
   (6)   To serve as the city representative in connection with the state and
federal programs relative to community improvement, education and job training,
and other similar matters.
   (7)   To prepare annual application, administer the day-to-day operation, to
prepare annual reports and to otherwise be the administrative officer in charge
of the city's participation under the community development block grant
program.
   (8)   To administer the functions and duties of the Property Maintenance and
Buildings Division, as explained in Secs.
7-35 to
7-37 of this Code.
   (9)   To coordinate the review of plans for commercial, industrial, and
residential development with appropriate city agencies.
(Ord. No. 09-1226, 6-1-09; Ord. No. 14-1443, 11-12-14; Ord. No. 16-1522, 2-9-
16; Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Sec. 7-28. - Assignment of duties and responsibilities.
   Any reference in the building, zoning, nuisance and other applicable codes
to the department of building and safety, as previously constituted and/or the
director of building and safety or property maintenance and development
services, insofar as they relate to the construction, authorization,
inspection, or repair of commercial and industrial buildings or other
appurtenant structures, shall be applicable instead to the Department of
Economic Development and its director, or their designee, respectively.
(Ord. No. 09-1226, 6-1-09; Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Sec. 7-29. Planning director - Appointment and vacancy.
   The director of the Department of Economic Development shall be the
appointing authority of the planning director, who may be a part-time,
contractual employee, and who shall assume all the duties and responsibilities
of the planning director and exercise all the powers granted to the planning
director, as requested by the director.
(Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Sec. 7-30. Same - Authority Generally.
   The director of the Department of Economic Development shall be the
appointing authority of all members of the planning staff and shall assist the
city planning commission in carrying out its powers and duties, as prescribed
by the charter.
(Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Sec. 7-31. Urban renewal.
   In addition to any and all duties of the planning director, they may be
charged with planning and coordinating the activities of the city in connection
with residential and commercial renewal and establishing a program which will
qualify for federal assistance. In connection with such duties, the planning
director may also be responsible for formulating a program for the continued
prevention of blighted areas within the city and for removal of existing
blight.
(Ord. No. 22-1732, 1-25-22)
Secs. 7-32—7-34. Reserved.

director of economic and community development (insofar as they relate to the
construction, authorization, inspection, or repair of commercial, industrial
buildings or other appurtenant structures) and the director of the property
maintenance and development services department, shall be applicable instead to
the director of the Department of Economic Development, or their designee.
(Ord. No. 16-1523, 2-9-16; Ord. No. 22-1731, 1-25-22)
