*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 10-1. - Inspection for fire hazards.
   The fire chief shall have the power and authority, and it shall be his duty,
to order the inspection of all premises where he has reason to believe
combustible materials or defective heating devices exist to the danger of the
public. For this purpose duly authorized agents or employees of the city may go
upon private property; may demand and require admittance to any building within
the city, at any reasonable hour, and may require the removal, repair or
destruction of any defective and dangerous heating device or chimney, or other
connection or adjunct thereof, or the removal of combustible materials and
cleaning up or removal of rubbish or refuse matter wherever the same may be
dangerous to the safety of the public and capable of causing a fire or
increasing the danger of a fire.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-2. - Removal of fire hazards.
   Authorized employees in the fire department may inspect all stoves, furnaces
and heating apparatus in dwellings, buildings and structures within the city,
and where combustible or explosive substances are kept, and, if any place or
premises is found to be unsafe with respect to the danger of fire, such
employees shall order and require the source of such danger to be removed and
all places and premises be placed in a safe and proper condition. All such
orders shall be in writing signed by a duly authorized agent or employee of the
city and shall describe the condition ordered to be remedied, specifying the
thing or things to be done in order to remedy such condition and designating a
reasonable time within which such alterations must be made. Such notice shall
be served upon the owner or occupant of the premises involved. A duplicate copy
of such notice shall be kept and filed by the fire department and, if such
notice is not complied with within the time limitation allowed, it shall be the
duty of the fire department to make or cause to be made a complaint against the
person refusing to comply with such notice for the violation of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-3. - False alarms.
   It shall be unlawful for any person within the limits of the city to tamper
with, disturb, disarrange or in any manner interfere with any fire alarm box or
station, telephone reporting system or any signal apparatus of the signal
bureau or the fire department of the city; to ring or to give any false alarm
of fire; or in any manner disturb or obstruct the orderly working of the fire
department of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-4. - Interference with fire department.
   It shall be unlawful for any pedestrian or vehicle to obstruct, hinder or
retard the progress of any of the fire apparatus of the fire department when
going to or returning from a fire. Upon the approach of any vehicle of the fire
department, when on an emergency call, operators of other vehicles shall
immediately drive as closely as possible to the righthand curb and stop, and
shall not follow any vehicle or apparatus of the fire department until the same
shall be at least 500 feet away, or has stopped. No vehicle other than those of
the fire department or police department, except by direction of any authorized
employee of the fire department in charge, shall approach or park within 500
feet of any fire apparatus responding to a call after such fire apparatus shall
have reached the scene of the fire. No person shall drive a vehicle over, upon
or across any fire hose or other equipment in use by the fire department or at
any time obstruct free access to any fire hydrant within the limits of the
city.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-5. - Hydrant regulations.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to open, use or in any manner disturb or
interfere with any fire hydrant or other apparatus without having first
obtained permission therefor. Any person other than members of the fire
department desiring to make use of any fire hydrant shall apply to the chief of
the fire department for the permission to do so, setting forth the name,
residence and business address of the applicant and the use and length of time
for which permission is desired. All applicants shall deposit with the city
treasurer the sum of $25.00 and shall not use or interfere with any hydrant
except by the use of tools approved by the fire department and in accordance
with directions given the applicant by the fire department. Any damage
resulting from the use of such hydrant shall be charged to the applicant and
deducted from the sum deposited. Such deposit shall not be returned to the
applicant until the hydrant shall have been inspected, and the applicant shall
pay an inspection fee of $2.50 for this inspection, plus any fees for use of
water imposed by the division of water supply of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-6. - Protection of combustibles.
   No person shall have, put or keep any hay, cotton, wood shavings, hemp or
other such combustible materials without having first securely enclosed such
materials so as to protect them from flying sparks or fire, and no open flame
shall be used in proximity to such combustible storage. No person shall have or
place in any stove, grate or furnace or use in lighting or kindling fires in
any private house, store, hotel, shop or other such building, any gasoline,
benzine, naphtha or other highly explosive or flammable substance.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-7. - Open burning.
   (a)   This section applies to all outdoor burning and open burning within
the City of Dearborn.
   (b)   Exceptions. This section does not apply to:
      (1)   Grilling or cooking food using charcoal cookers, propane or natural
gas in cooking or filling appliances, braziers, hibachis, grills, outdoor
fireplaces or gas-fired stoves and similar semi-enclosed devices on the
premises of a one-family detached dwelling.
      (2)   Burning for the purpose of generating heat in a stove, furnace,
fireplace or other heating device within a building used for human or animal
habitation.
      (3)   The use of propane, acetylene, natural gas, gasoline or kerosene in
a device intended for heating, construction or maintenance activities.
      (4)   The use of non-ash producing fuels being used not less than 15 feet
from combustible materials, when used in metal containers for the heating of
building materials or for the warmth of workers.
      (5)   Open burning being used by the fire department in connection with
training and performance of its duties.
   (c)   Definitions. 
      (1)   Clean wood means natural wood which has not been painted, varnished
or coated with a similar material, has not been pressure treated with
preservatives, and does not contain resins or glues as in plywood or other
composite wood products.
      (2)   Construction and demolition waste means building waste materials,
including but not limited to waste shingles, insulation, lumber, treated wood,
painted wood, wiring, plastics, packaging, and rubble that results from
construction, remodeling, repair, and demolition operations on a house,
commercial or industrial building, or other structure.
      (3)   Open burning means kindling or maintaining a fire where the
products of combustion are emitted directly into the ambient air without
passing through a stack or a chimney.
      (4)   Outdoor burning means open burning or burning in a patio wood-
burning unit.
      (5)   Patio wood-burning unit means a portable fire pit, chimnea, patio
warmer, or other portable wood-burning device used for outdoor recreation and/
or heating. The unit must be enclosed with screening on all sides including the
top. The unit must be constructed of steel, concrete, clay or other non-
combustible material.
   (d)   General prohibition on open burning. Open burning, outdoor burning,
and burning in in-ground fire pits are prohibited unless specifically permitted
by this section.
   (e)   Open burning of refuse. Open burning of refuse is prohibited including
the burning of brush, leaves, and grass clippings.
   (f)   A patio wood-burning unit may be used in the City of Dearborn only in
accordance with all of the following provisions:
      (1)   The patio wood-burning unit shall not be used to burn refuse.
      (2)   The patio wood-burning unit shall burn only clean wood.
      (3)   The patio wood-burning unit shall be located in the rear yard only.
         a.   For the purpose of this section, on corner lots, the rear yard
shall be considered the yard opposite the street on which the front door of the
house faces.
         b.   This subsection shall be waived during the evening hours of
Halloween when a patio wood-burning unit may be placed in a location near the
public sidewalk to facilitate greeting trick-or-treaters.
         c.   This subsection shall be waived during a block party licensed by
the city. During the block party, a patio wood-burning unit may be placed in
the public street as part of the block party festivities.
         d.   This subsection may be waived with the permission of the fire
marshal.
      (4)   The patio wood-burning unit shall be located at least 15 feet from
the nearest structure which is not on the same property as the patio wood-
burning unit and at least 15 feet from the nearest structure on the same
property as the patio wood-burning unit.
      (5)   The patio wood-burning unit shall not cause a nuisance to
neighbors. Objectionable smoke shall be deemed a nuisance.
      (6)   Operational hours for any patio wood-burning unit shall be limited
to the time between 11:00 a.m. and 1:00 a.m.
      (7)   All fires shall be supervised by at least one person who is 18
years of age or older.
      (8)   There shall be a minimum of a garden hose connected to a reliable
water supply, one gallon bucket of water, or a 2a10BC rated fire extinguisher
within 20 feet of any patio wood-burning unit.
   (g)   The fire department and the police department are authorized to
enforce this section.
   (h)   Any person who violates any provision of this section shall be deemed
responsible for a civil infraction.
      (1)   A third offense within a 12-month period shall be a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.7, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 13-1394, 4-30-13)
Sec. 10-8. - Fireworks illegal.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to store, keep, sell, offer or keep for
sale, any fireworks or explosives within the city, except upon such conditions
as to time, place and manner of handling as the council may by resolution
determine.
(Ord. No. 81-96, § 1.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 10-9. - Private hydrant markings.
   (a)   All newly installed or relocated private hydrants shall be identified
as pressurized or nonpressurized. All pressurized hydrants over 80 p.s.i. are
to be painted red and all other hydrants are to be painted yellow with a two-
inch red band on the top of the dome. All hydrants must meet the city's color
code prior to acceptance.
   (b)   All mill water hydrants are to be painted purple (preferably
reflective).
   (c)   All existing private hydrants shall be cleaned and painted according
to the city's color code stated above.
   (d)   Any person who alters or tampers with a hydrant's required markings
shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 02-922, 11-19-02; Ord. No. 09-1197, 1-5-09)
Sec. 10-10. - Firewood in residential districts.
   (a)   Definition. Firewood means and includes cut logs, scrap wood, cut
brush and similar materials that can be burned or otherwise used as fuel.
   (b)   Storage requirements. It shall be unlawful for any person to store
firewood in a residential district in a manner not conforming with the
following:
      (1)   Location.
         a.   Firewood shall not be stored in any location other than the rear
yard, except that firewood may be stored on the front porch from October 1
through April 1 subject to the regulations of this section.
         b.   Where it is possible to place a firewood pile on the side of a
garage, accessory building, or behind the principal structure on the property,
the firewood pile shall be placed in one of those locations so as to minimize
the visual impact to neighboring property. If it is shown that placement in one
of these locations is not possible, the firewood may be stored behind a garage
or accessory structure, or along the property line.
      (2)   Dimensional requirements.
         a.   Firewood in the rear yard shall be stored in a rack or structure
that measures no more than five feet in height as measured from the ground and
two feet in depth. The width of a firewood pile may not exceed 25 percent of
the total width or depth of the rear yard, whichever is greater. Any firewood
pile stored on a surface other than concrete or pavers must be raised at least
nine inches above the ground.
         b.   Firewood on a front porch must be stored in a rack or structure
that measures no more than two feet in height, three feet in width, and two
feet in depth, or ten percent of the porch area, whichever is smaller. Firewood
on the front porch shall be stored so as not to impede ingress and egress to
and from the house, not to encroach on porch steps, and so as not to create a
trip hazard, regardless of the dimensions of the rack or structure.
         c.   The dimensional requirements of this section shall not apply to
storage of wood that is the product of a tree removed from the lot pursuant to
a permit issued by the city.
      (3)   No single lot shall be allowed more than one firewood pile.
      (4)   Storage of firewood is prohibited on vacant lots and in yards of
homes that are registered as vacant or qualify as vacant under chapter 11 of
this Code.
      (5)   No storage of firewood is permitted for use other than for the
dwelling contained on the lot or parcel.
      (6)   No firewood shall be stored that is rotting, infested with insects,
harboring animals, or otherwise causing a nuisance. A nuisance firewood pile
may be enforced against or abated as provided in this chapter or chapter 13 of
this Code.
(Ord. No. 11-1342, 12-12-11)
Secs. 10-11—10-35. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - FIRE PREVENTION CODE ***
Sec. 10-36. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this article is to provide for the city rules and regulations
to improve safety of the public by promoting the control of fire hazards;
regulating the installation, use and maintenance of equipment; the use of
structures, premises, and open areas; providing for the abatement of fire
hazards; and setting forth standards for compliance to achieve these
objectives.
(Ord. No. 77-1874, § 2, 10-4-77)
Sec. 10-37. - Enforcement.
   The chief of the fire department and any deputies, agents or inspectors
designated by him are hereby empowered to enforce the provisions of this
article.
(Ord. No. 77-1874, § 4, 10-4-77)
Sec. 10-38. - Adoption.
   Unless specifically provided for in other codes or ordinances of the city,
the standards developed under the procedures of the International Fire Code
(IFC), 2024, including appendices A through G, I, N and O, as amended, and the
2015 Michigan Building Code, as amended, shall apply. Chapter 10 of IFC 2024
and appendices H, J, K, L and M shall be excluded from adoption. The
International Fire Code, 2024 edition, including appendices A through G, I, N
and O, adopted and published by the International Code Council, Inc., and the
2015 Michigan Building Code are hereby incorporated by reference and made a
part hereof as if fully set out in this article. A complete copy of the
International Fire Code, 2024 edition, and appendices A through G, I, N and O,
and the 2015 Michigan Building Code,, are available for public use and
inspection at the office of the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 77-1874, § 5, 10-4-77; Ord. No. 95-647, 9-19-95; Ord. No. 99-763, 4-
14-99; Ord. No. 06-1070, 5-15-06; Ord. No. 08-1181, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 11-1336,
11-7-11; Ord. No. 14-1448, 12-9-14; Ord. No. 17-1578. 5-9-17; Ord. No. 24-1834,
1-14-25)
Sec. 10-38.1. - Additions, insertions, and changes.
   The following sections of the International Fire Code, 2024 Edition, adopted
in this article are hereby added or revised as follows:
   (a)   Section 1002. Definitions. Section 1002 is amended to add the
following definitions:
      BANQUET HALL: Any enclosed hall, building or portion of any building
available for rental, lease or loan, for the purpose of public or private
assemblies, whether or not a fee or other consideration is provided by the
renter for use of the building.
      The building must be designated as a banquet hall with a use group of A-2
      indicated on the certificate of occupancy. The occupant load card issued
for the building will have "BANQUET HALL" indicated on the occupant load card.
      OCCUPANT LOAD: The number of persons for which the means of egress of a
building or portion thereof is designed. The occupant load is indicated on the
certificate of occupancy and the provided occupant load card issued by the
building official and fire marshal through the Department of Economic
Development. When an occupant load established by the Zoning Board of Appeals
is lower than the occupant load established by the fire marshal/building
official, the Zoning Board of Appeals' occupant load shall prevail until all
issues identified by the Zoning Board of Appeals in support of the decreased
occupant load are mitigated.
      The established occupant load will be clearly indicated on the
certificate of occupancy and occupant load card.
      RENTER: Shall mean any individual, group or association that rents,
leases or borrows a banquet hall.
   (b)   Section 1004.3.1. Posting of occupant load. Every room or space that
is an assembly occupancy shall have the occupant load of the room or space
posted in a conspicuous place, near the main exit or exit access doorway from
the room or space. Posted signs are provided by the building official and fire
marshal through the Department of Economic Development and shall be maintained
by the owner or authorized agent.
      Section 1004.3.2. Disclosure of banquet hall occupant load in rental
agreement; liability of owner or operator and renter. The owner or operator of
a banquet hall must include a clause in its rental or lease agreement, or
provide a separate form to the banquet hall renter, that includes the
following:
         1.   A statement of the occupant load of the banquet hall or portion
of the banquet hall being occupied by the renter.
         2.   Notification to the renter that, if the occupant load is exceeded
during the renter's event, the City (police, fire marshal's office, or the
building official) may terminate the event and evacuate the banquet hall
pursuant to section 110.6 of this code.
         3.   Notification to the renter that both the owner or operator and
renter may be held responsible for violations of this code pursuant to section
110.5 of this code, and shall be held liable for a misdemeanor in the event
that the occupant load is exceeded in an unreasonable manner during the
renter's event.
         4.   The signature of the owner or operator and the renter.
(Ord. No. 11-1337, 11-7-11; Ord. No. 17-1578. 5-9-17; Ord. No. 24-1834, 1-14-
25)
Sec. 10-38.2. - Inspection, testing and maintenance reports.
   All inspections and maintenance reports required to be furnished to the fire
department by the fire code shall be electronically forwarded to the fire
department using the IROL system (InspectionReportsOnLine.net). Any company
doing inspection and maintenance shall be required to register with IROL.
(Ord. No. 14-1422, 3-18-14)
Sec. 10-39. - Violations.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to violate this article, to permit or
maintain such violation, to refuse to obey any provision thereof, or to fail or
refuse to comply with any provision or regulation, except as variation may be
allowed by action of the chief of the fire department in writing.
(Ord. No. 77-1874, § 6, 10-4-77)
Sec. 10-40. - State licensing requirements.
   Any individual or company that installs or maintains fire prevention, fire
suppression, or fire detection systems or equipment must comply with state
licensing requirements. Failure to do so shall constitute a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 06-1070, 5-15-06)
Sec. 10-41. - Fire Watch.
   (a)   Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following words and
phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed by this section. Words
and phrases not defined in this section shall have the meanings as defined in
the International Fire Code 2015, and any subsequent amendments:
      (1)   Fire watch. Means a temporary measure intended to ensure continuous
and systematic surveillance of a building, its premises, or portion thereof,
including the premises on which the building is located, by one or more
qualified individuals for the purposes of identifying and controlling fire
hazards, detecting early signs of unwanted fire, raising an alarm of fire and
notifying the fire department.
   (b)   Scope and authority. In addition to the provisions regarding fire
watch in International Fire Code 2015, and any subsequent amendments, this
section shall set forth the requirements of a fire watch when the Chief of the
Fire Department, or their designee, determines that a building or premises
presents a hazard to life or property as the result of a fire or other
emergency, or when it is determined that any fire protection equipment or
system is inoperable, defective, or has been taken out of service.
      (1)   Authority to require fire watch. The Chief of the Fire Department,
or their designee, may require implementation of a fire watch whenever it is
deemed necessary by the Chief or their designee to assure minimum fire and/or
life safety as regulated by this chapter. The Chief or their designee shall
specify the number of fire watch personnel and duties to be performed. Fire
watch duties shall be implemented immediately upon a determination by the Chief
or their designee.
      (2)   Authority of the Chief to assign department members; cost recovery.
Whenever the owner or person in charge of building and its premises does not
provide fire watch personnel as required, the Chief shall have the authority to
assign uniformed fire department personnel until such time as required fire
watch personnel are provided. If fire department personnel are assigned as fire
watch pursuant to this subsection, the owner, lessor, lessee, or operator of
the building or premises where such personnel are assigned shall be liable for
the costs of such assignment, which shall include labor, equipment usage, and
materials associated with fire watch responsibilities as determined by the fire
department.
       (3)   The provisions of this section are authorized by the International
Fire Code, 2015, and the Home Rule City Act, Public Act 279 of 1909, more
specifically but not limited to MCL 117.3(j).
    (c)   Fire watch maintained until safe. A fire watch shall be maintained
until such time that the Chief of the Fire Department, or their designee,
determines that the building or premises is safe from hazard to life or
property, or when fire protection equipment or systems are restored to service.
    (d)   Violation and penalty; repeat violation. It shall be unlawful for any
person to violate this section, to permit or maintain such violation, to refuse
to obey any provision thereof, or to fail or refuse to comply with any
provision or regulation, except as variation may be allowed by the Chief of the
Fire Department, or their designee, in writing. A violation of this section is
a civil infraction punishable by a fine of $2,500.00, plus any costs imposed by
the court.
      (1)   An increased fine schedule shall be imposed for repeat violations
of this section. As used in this section, “repeat violation” means a violation
committed within ninety (90) days of an admission or determination of
responsibility for a violation of this section occurring upon the same
property.
       (2)   The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall be a civil fine
of $5,000.00, plus any costs imposed by the court.
    (e)   Responsibility for instruction. The owner, manager, or person in
charge or control of the building or premises shall assign to the fire watch as
many personnel as deemed necessary by the Chief of the Fire Department, or
their designee, and subject to the duties as determined by the Chief or their
designee, shall instruct fire watch personnel as to:
       (1)   The procedure for notifying the Fire Department.
      (2)   The area to be patrolled.
      (3)   A method of alerting building occupants and an evacuation
procedure.
      (4)   A procedure shall be provided for reactivating sprinkler valves in
the event of fire when the sprinkler system has been taken out of service.
       (5)   Any other instruction deemed necessary by the Chief or their
designee.
   (f)   Log book. The owner, manager, or person in charge or control of the
premises shall provide a log book which contains a directory of names,
telephone numbers, and other information to assist in making emergency calls to
key management personnel, and which shall be used to record a history of patrol
rounds. The log book shall be maintained on the premises and be available for
inspection by the Fire Department.
    (g)   Specific duty and minimum requirements. Assigned fire watch personnel
shall:
       (1)   Be thoroughly familiar with the area they are patrolling;
      (2)   Perform patrol operations according to instructions from management
and the Chief of the Fire Department (or their designee);
      (3)   Patrol their designated area at least once each hour;
       (4)   Make reports and document the patrol as instructed;
       (5)   Maintain a record of the fire watch for inspection by the Fire
Department;
       (6)   Send a record of the fire watch to the Fire Department upon
request;
       (7)   Be trained in the use of a fire extinguisher and have one
accessible at all times;
       (8)   Be capable of communicating with building and/or premises
occupants and the Fire Department to notify them about fires or other
emergencies; and
      (9)   Any other requirements deemed necessary by the Chief of the Fire
Department or their designee. (Ord. No. 22-1763, 8-23-22)
Secs. 10-42—10-60. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - SMOKING AND USE OF FIRE ***
Sec. 10-61. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Combustible material shall mean any material which will burn when a fire is
applied thereto. It shall include cloth, paper and wood in all its various
forms and combinations, and hydrocarbons, but shall not be limited to these
materials.
   Retail store shall mean a place or building in which goods, wares or
merchandise is sold directly to the consumer or his agent.
   Smoke or smoking shall mean the use of cigarettes, cigars, pipes or tobacco
in any form after the tobacco is ignited.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 6, 9-19-50)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 10-62. - Enforcement.
   It shall be the duty of the fire marshal of the city to enforce the
provisions of this article and to see that proper notices are posted in those
buildings or portions of buildings where smoking is prohibited, and in those
buildings which have been designated by the fire marshal as not being dangerous
to life or property for smoking or other fire producing devices to be operated
therein; provided, however, that the failure to post any of the notices herein
required shall not excuse or suspend the operation of this article.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 5, 9-19-50)
Sec. 10-63. - Smoking prohibited in stores.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke in any retail store which is
designed or arranged to accommodate more than 50 persons in the city in which
combustible material is sold, or offered or exposed for sale; provided,
however, that smoking shall be permitted in smoking and restrooms, executive
offices, restaurants, beauty parlors and barbershops in such stores and in
areas specifically designed by the fire marshal by written authorization to the
owner having control or management thereof, when the fire marshal has
determined that smoking therein is not dangerous to life or property.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 1, 9-19-50)
Sec. 10-64. - Use of fire restricted.
   It shall be unlawful to use any spark, flame, match or other fire producing
device for purposes of demonstration in any retail store, building or section
of building in the city unless written authorization therefor has been first
given by the fire marshal after he has determined that the use of such fire
producing device is not dangerous to life or property.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 2, 9-19-50)
Sec. 10-65. - Unlawful to start fire while smoking.
   It shall be unlawful for any person in smoking or in attempting to light or
to smoke a cigarette, cigar, pipe or tobacco in any form for which a lighter or
matches are used, to set fire to any bed, bedding, furniture, curtains,
drapery, or household furniture in any hotel, roominghouse or public
lodginghouse.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 3, 9-19-50)
Sec. 10-66. - Smoking prohibited in theaters.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke in any theater in the
city. It shall be the duty of the owner or manager of the theater to see that
the provisions of this section are obeyed by the patrons, employees or other
persons in such theaters.
   (b)   For the purpose of this section, the word "theater" shall be deemed to
include and shall mean any assembly hall, auditorium, building or other
enclosed structure used for dramatic performances, vaudeville entertainments,
motion picture shows or other similar entertainment.
   (c)   It shall be the duty of the owner, operator and manager of any
theater, or either or any of them, to comply with the provisions of this
section and to enforce the observance thereof by patrons and employees or other
persons in such theater. It shall be a violation of this section for any
employee of the theater who has been authorized to enforce any part of this
section to refuse or neglect to observe the same or to enforce its observance
insofar as it may be within his power so to do.
   (d)   Smoking may be permitted in executive offices and in areas
specifically designated by written authorization of the fire marshal to persons
having control or management thereof, when the fire marshal has determined that
smoking therein is not dangerous to life or property.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 3-a, 9-19-50; Ord. No. 51-631, 5-15-51)
Sec. 10-67. - Smoking prohibited in schools.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke in any public or private
school building, school auditorium, or portions of buildings used for
instructional and educational purposes, or where an assembly of persons may
gather for educational purposes, regardless of the number.
   (b)   It shall be the duty of the persons having control or management
thereof to see that the provisions of this section are obeyed by the occupants,
employees or other persons in any such building.
   (c)   Smoking may be permitted in executive offices and in areas
specifically designated by written authorization of the fire marshal to persons
having control or management thereof, when such fire marshal has determined
that smoking therein is not dangerous to life or property.
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 3-b, 9-19-50; Ord. No. 51-631, 5-15-51)
Sec. 10-68. - Posting of notice required.
   The owner or manager of every retail store, building or section of building
affected by the prohibition of section
10-63 shall post in a conspicuous place, a notice or sign reading substantially
as follows:
"SMOKING PROHIBITED CITY ORDINANCE"
(Ord. No. 50-573, § 4, 9-19-50)

*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Secs. 11-1—11-25. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - MINIMUM HOUSING STANDARDS ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 11-26. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this article is to help protect the health, safety and
welfare of the citizens by attempting to prevent blight, avoid the creation and
maintenance of a nuisance and insure minimum maintenance of dwellings through
recognition of how the conditions set forth in this article can affect the
general well-being and property values of residents.
(Ord. No. 81-102, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 84-289, 2-21-84)
Sec. 11-27. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Basement shall mean a portion of a building located partly underground, but
having less than half its clear floor-to-ceiling height below the average grade
of the adjoining ground.
   Bedroom or room occupied for sleeping purposes shall mean a room
characterized by the following traits:
      (1)   A room not normally used for the preparation or consumption of
food.
      (2)   A room so arranged that it is not necessary to go through this room
in order to gain access to the principal bathroom of the dwelling unit or any
other room with the exception of a secondary bath or toilet room serving that
sleeping room only.
      (3)   A room with solid swing-type door with stop mouldings to afford
privacy.
      (4)   A room with adequate ventilation.
      (5)   A room normally with a closet.
   Cellar shall mean a portion of a building located partly or wholly
underground, and having half or more than half of its clear floor-to-ceiling
height below the average grade of the adjoining ground.
   Dwelling shall mean any building which is wholly or partly used, or intended
to be used, for living or sleeping by human occupants; provided that temporary
housing shall not be regarded as a dwelling.
   Dwelling unit shall mean any room or group of rooms located within a
dwelling and forming a single habitable unit with facilities which are used or
intended to be used for living, sleeping, cooking and eating.
   Extermination shall mean the control and elimination of insects, rodents or
other pests by eliminating their harborage places; by removing or making
inaccessible materials that may serve as their food, by poisoning, spraying,
fumigating, trapping; or by any other recognized and legal pest elimination
methods approved by the health officer.
   Garbage shall mean the animal and vegetable waste resulting from the
handling, preparation, cooking and consumption of food.
   Habitable room shall mean a room or enclosed floor space used or intended to
be used for living, sleeping, cooking or eating purposes, excluding bathrooms,
water closet compartments, laundries, pantries, foyers or communicating
corridors, closets and storage spaces.
   Infestation shall mean the presence, within or around a dwelling, of any
insects, rodents or other pests.
   Multiple dwelling shall mean any dwelling containing more than two dwelling
units.
   Occupant shall mean any person, over one year of age, living, sleeping,
cooking or eating in, or having actual possession of, a dwelling unit or
rooming unit.
   Operator shall mean any person who has charge, possession or control of a
building, or part thereof, in which dwelling units or rooming units are let.
   Ordinary minimum winter conditions shall mean the temperature 15 degrees
Fahrenheit above the lowest recorded temperature for the previous ten-year
period.
   Owner shall mean any person who, alone or jointly or severally with others:
      (1)   Shall have legal title to any dwelling or dwelling unit, with or
without accompanying actual possession thereof; or
      (2)   Shall have charge, possession or control of any dwelling or
dwelling unit, as owner or agent of the owner, or as executor, executrix,
administrator, administratrix, trustee or guardian of the estate of the owner.
Any such person thus representing the actual owner shall be bound to comply
with the provisions of this article, and of rules and regulations adopted
pursuant thereto, to the same extent as if he were the owner.
   Plumbing shall mean and include, but not be limited to, the following
supplied facilities and equipment: gas pipes, gas burning equipment, water
pipes, garbage disposal units, water pipes, water closets, sinks, installed
dishwashers, lavatories, bathtubs, shower baths, installed clothes-washing
machines, catch basins, drains, vents and any other similar supplied fixtures,
together with all connections to water, sewer or gas lines.
   Rooming house shall mean any dwelling or that part thereof containing one or
more rooming units in which space is let by the owner or operator to three or
more persons who are not husband and wife, son or daughter, mother or father,
or sister or brother to the owner or operator.
   Rooming unit shall mean any room or group of rooms forming a single
habitable unit used or intended to be used for living and sleeping, but not for
cooking or eating purposes.
   Rubbish shall mean combustible and noncombustible waste materials, except
garbage; and the term shall include the residue from the burning of wood, coal,
coke and other combustible materials, paper, rags, cartons, boxes, wood
excelsior, rubber, leather, tree branches, yard trimmings, tin cans, metals,
mineral matter, glass crockery and dust.
   Supplied shall mean paid for, furnished or provided by or under the control
of the owner or operator.
   Temporary housing shall mean any tent, trailer or other structure used for
human shelter which is designed to be transportable and which is not attached
to the ground, to another structure, or to any utilities system on the same
premises for more than 30 consecutive days.
   Whenever the words "dwelling," "dwelling unit," "roominghouse," "premises,"
are used in this article, they shall be construed as though they were followed
by the words "or any part thereof."
(Ord. No. 81-102, §§ 1.1—1.25, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 11-28. - Conflict with other ordinances and laws.
   When a provision of this article is found to be in conflict with a provision
of any state statute or any zoning, building, fire, safety or health ordinance
or code of the city, the provision which establishes the higher standard for
the promotion and protection of the health and safety of the people shall
prevail. If a provision of this article is found to be in conflict with a
provision of a state statute or any other ordinance or code of the city which
establishes a lower standard for the promotion and protection of the health and
safety of the people, the provisions of this article shall be deemed to
prevail.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 14.1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 84-289, 2-21-84)
Secs. 11-29—11-40. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - INSPECTION **
Sec. 11-41. - Right of entry, access.
   (a)   The Department of Economic Development director or their designee is
hereby authorized and directed to make inspections to determine the conditions
of all existing residential and nonresidential structures and all existing
premises located within the city. These inspections are performed either to
fulfill the requirements of this chapter or code, upon identifiable external
violations documented by the director or their designee, upon inspection, or
set forth in complaints registered by area residents and/or neighborhood
associations, if such inspections are needed to correct violations heretofore
enumerated in this code.
   (b)   For the purpose of making such inspections, the director or their
designee, is hereby authorized to enter, examine and survey at any reasonable
time all existing residential and nonresidential structures and all existing
premises. The owner or occupant of every residential and nonresidential
structure, or the person in charge thereof, shall give free access to such
residential and nonresidential structure and its premises, at any reasonable
time, for the purpose of such inspection, examination and survey.
   (c)   Every occupant of a residential or nonresidential structure shall give
the owner thereof, or their agent or employee, access to any part of such
residential or nonresidential structure, or its premises, at any reasonable
time, for the purpose of making such repairs or alterations as are necessary to
effect compliance with the provisions of this article or with any lawful rule
or regulation adopted or any lawful order issued pursuant to the provisions of
this article.
   (d)   Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the owner, lessee, tenant, or
business owner in charge of the property from denying entry. However, nothing
shall prevent the director from asking permission from an owner, lessee, or
business owner in charge of the property for permission to inspect.
      (1)   In the event an owner, lessee, tenant, or business owner denies
entry for an inspection, nothing in this article shall prohibit the director
from seeking an administrative search warrant based on probable cause to
conduct an inspection.
      (2)   Refusal to allow an inspection under this chapter is considered a
violation under this chapter if an inspection is refused after an
administrative search warrant is obtained.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1037, 5-2-05; Ord. No. 10-1271, 5-
3-10; Ord. No. 22-1735, 1-25-22)
Sec. 11-42. - Inspection and occupancy requirements.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for anyone, including, but not limited to, the
owner, attorney, representative, lending institution, title company, real-
estate firm, broker, or salesman to assist in consummating a sale or transfer,
including installment sales such as land contracts or other transaction
involving real property in the city regardless of where the closing of the sale
occurs, without first presenting the prospective purchaser or grantee with a
certificate of occupancy issued by the Department of Economic Development.
   For closing purposes, the certificate of occupancy shall expire six months
after the date on which the real property was approved for occupancy. In the
event that the real property is not transferred or conveyed within such six-
month period, a new inspection is required.
   Exceptions:
      (1)   In the event that the real property has not been approved for
occupancy (i.e. is sold without a certificate of occupancy), then the purchaser
must sign a compliance agreement agreeing to correct all violations shown on an
inspection report prepared by the Department of Economic Development based upon
an inspection occurring not more than 12 months prior to the date of sale or
transfer.
      (2)   In the event the real property is sold or transferred at a
sheriff's sale, court-ordered auction, or through another means whereby an
inspection could not be performed prior to the sale or transfer, the purchaser
shall apply in writing to the director of the Department of Economic
Development within 30 days after the date of sale or transfer and pay the fee
for an inspection of the property and will enter into and pay the fee for a
compliance agreement referred to above. If there are no violations shown on the
inspection report, then the purchaser will be refunded the fee for the
compliance agreement.
      (3)   This section does not apply to the individual transfer of property
through inheritance where no bona fide sale is intended and the property has
been and continues to be occupied by the person or persons receiving the
inheritance.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to occupy or for any owner or
agent thereof to permit the occupation of any building or addition thereto, or
part thereof, for any purpose, until occupancy has been approved by the
Department of Economic Development.
      (1)   A certificate of occupancy is issued when all violations noted on
the inspection report issued by the Department of Economic Development have
been corrected and required repairs have been made.
      (2)   In the event an owner, prospective purchaser, or transferee
requests that occupancy be permitted prior to correction of all violations
noted on the inspection report, and if the absence of such complete conformance
does not, in the judgment of the Department of Economic Development, constitute
material health or safety hazards, conditional occupancy may be allowed upon
the condition that complete conformance be achieved within a reasonable time
specified by the Department of Economic Development, but in not more than 90
days.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 2.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1037, 5-2-05; Ord. No. 10-1271,
5-3-10; Ord. No. 14-1430, 7-22-14; Ord. No. 22-1735, 1-25-22; Ord. No. 25-1852,
9-9-25)
Sec. 11-43. - Failure to comply.
   The penalty for any violation of this division by any person, firm and/or
corporation shall be a misdemeanor punishable as provided under section
1-9 of this Code. Each day that the violation continues shall constitute a
separate and distinct violation.
   Nothing in this division constitutes a waiver of the city's right to
petition the circuit court for the right to take action to prevent occupancy of
a property.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 2.3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 97-707, 7-1-97; Ord. No. 02-898, 5-
21-02; Ord. No. 05-1037, 5-2-05; Ord. No. 10-1271, 5-3-10; Ord. No. 14-1430, 7-
22-14)
Secs. 11-44—11-55. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - ENFORCEMENT **
Sec. 11-56. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 05-1037, adopted May 2, 2005, delete §
11-56 in its entirety. Former §
11-56 pertained to notice of violation and derived from Ord. No. 81-102, § 3.1,
adopted Nov. 4, 1981.
Sec. 11-57. - Hearing.
   Any person affected by any notice which has been issued in connection with
the enforcement of any provision of this article, or of any rule or regulation
adopted pursuant thereto that cannot be resolved by departmental appeal
procedures, may request and shall be granted a hearing on the matter before the
building board of appeals; provided that such person shall file to the
Department of Economic Development a written petition requesting such hearing
and setting forth a brief statement of the grounds therefor within ten days
after the day the notice was served. Upon receipt of such petition, the
building board of appeals shall set a time and place for such hearing and shall
give the petitioner written notice thereof. At such hearing the petitioner
shall be given an opportunity to be heard and to show why such notice should be
modified or withdrawn. The hearing shall be held at the next scheduled building
board of appeals meeting or at a special meeting of the building board of
appeals, not later than 30 days after the day on which the petition was filed;
provided that upon application of the petitioner, the building board of appeals
may postpone the date of the hearing for a reasonable time beyond such 30-day
period, if in the judgment of the board the petitioner has submitted a good and
sufficient reason for such postponement.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 3.2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1037, 5-2-05; Ord. No. 22-1735,
1-25-22)
Sec. 11-58. - Action by appeal board.
   After hearing, the building board of appeals shall sustain, modify or
withdraw the notice, depending upon its findings to whether the provisions of
this article and of the rules and regulations adopted pursuant thereto have
been complied with. If the board sustains or modifies such notice, it shall be
deemed to be an order.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 3.3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1037, 5-2-05)
Sec. 11-59. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 05-1037, adopted May 2, 2005, deleted §
11-59 in its entirety. Former §
11-59 pertained to records and derived from Ord. No. 81-102, § 3.4, adopted
Nov. 4, 1981.
Sec. 11-60. - Emergency measures.
   Whenever the health officer or director finds that an emergency exists which
requires immediate action to protect the public health, he may, without notice
or hearing, issue an order reciting the existence of such an emergency and
requiring that such action be taken as he deems necessary to meet the
emergency. Notwithstanding the other provisions of this article, such order
shall be effective immediately. Any person to whom such order is directed shall
comply therewith immediately, but upon petition to the corporation counsel
shall be afforded a hearing as soon as possible. After such hearing, depending
upon the finding as to whether the provisions of this article and of the rules
and regulations adopted pursuant thereto have been complied with, such order
shall be continued or may be modified or revoked.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 3.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-61. - Enforcement officer.
   The director of the Department of Economic Development (or designee) shall
serve as an ordinance officer for purposes of enforcement of the provisions of
this article. The director of the Department of Public Works and Facilities (or
designee) shall be authorized to issue notices of violation and/or appearance
tickets requiring that corrective action be taken by the owner or occupant of
any dwelling and/or requiring the owner or occupant of any dwelling to appear
in court to answer for violations of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 13.1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1735, 1-25-22)

** DIVISION 4. - MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR BASIC EQUIPMENT AND FACILITIES **
Sec. 11-76. - Compliance required.
   No person shall occupy as owner-occupant or let to another for occupancy any
dwelling or dwelling unit, for the purpose of living, sleeping, cooking or
eating therein, which does not comply with the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-77. - Kitchen required.
   Every dwelling unit shall contain a kitchen with a properly installed
kitchen sink, a refrigerator in good working condition, and a properly
installed cooking range. The refrigerator and cooking range may be the personal
equipment of the tenant.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-78. - Bathroom required.
   Every dwelling unit shall contain a room which affords privacy to a person
within such room and which is equipped with a flush water closet, a stall
shower or bathtub, a lavatory basin and either a mechanical exhaust fan in good
working condition or an operable window meeting the requirements of section
11-98.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-79. - Laundry facilities.
   Every dwelling unit shall contain a properly installed laundry tray or other
facilities for laundering approved by the director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-80. - Plumbing generally.
   Every kitchen sink, lavatory basin, laundry tray and tub or shower required
under the provisions of sections
11-77,
11-78 and
11-79 shall be properly connected with both hot and cold water lines and all
plumbing fixtures within every dwelling unit shall be properly connected to a
water and sewer system approved by the director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-81. - Rubbish storage.
   Every dwelling unit shall be supplied with adequate rubbish storage
facilities, the type and location of which are approved by the director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-82. - Garbage disposal.
   Every dwelling unit shall have a properly installed garbage disposal unit
installed in the waste line of the kitchen sink in a manner approved by the
director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-83. - Water-heating facilities.
   Every dwelling shall have supplied water-heating facilities which are
properly installed, maintained in safe and good working condition, properly
connected with the hot water lines required under the provisions of section
11-80, and capable of heating water to such a temperature as to permit an
adequate amount of water to be drawn at every required kitchen sink, lavatory
basin, bathtub or shower at a temperature of not less than 120 degrees
Fahrenheit. Such supplied water-heating facilities shall be capable of meeting
the requirements of this subsection when the dwelling or dwelling unit heating
facilities required under the provisions of section
11-101 are not in operation.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-84. - Egress.
   Every dwelling unit shall have safe, unobstructed means of egress leading to
safe and open space at ground level, as required by the laws of this state and
the city.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-85. - Smoke detectors.
   Each apartment, suite or sleeping area of every single or multiple dwelling
unit shall be provided with a minimum of one smoke detector capable of sensing
visible or invisible products of combustion. The detector shall be approved or
listed by a recognized independent testing laboratory and, when actuated, shall
provide an alarm suitable to warn the occupants within the individual dwelling
unit. A minimum of one smoke detector shall be located in the immediate area of
all sleeping quarters.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 4.9, 11-4-81)
Secs. 11-86—11-95. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR LIGHT, VENTILATION AND HEATING **
Sec. 11-96. - Compliance.
   No person shall occupy as owner-occupant or let to another for occupancy any
dwelling or dwelling unit, for the purpose of living therein, which does not
comply with the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-97. - Windows.
   Every habitable room shall have at least one window or skylight facing
directly outdoors. The minimum total window area measured between stops, for
every habitable room, shall be 12½ percent of the floor area of such room.
Whenever walls or other portions of structures face a window of any such room
and such light obstruction structures are located less than three feet from the
window and extend to a level above that of the ceiling of the room, such a
window shall not be deemed to face directly outdoors and shall not be included
as contributing to the required minimum total window area. Whenever the only
window in a room is a skylight-type window in the top of such room, the total
window area of such skylight shall equal at least 15 percent of the total floor
area of such room.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-98. - Ventilation.
   Every habitable room shall have at least one window or skylight which can
easily be opened, or such other device as will adequately ventilate the room.
The total of openable window area in every habitable room shall be equal to at
least 60 percent of the minimum window area size or minimum skylight-type
window size, as required under section
11-96, except where there is supplied some other device affording adequate
ventilation and approved by the director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-99. - Electric service panel.
   Every one-bedroom dwelling unit shall be supplied with a minimum 60 ampere
electric service panel, and every dwelling unit containing more than one
bedroom shall be supplied with a minimum 100 ampere electric service panel. All
connected loads to such panels shall be protected with fuses or circuit
breakers.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-100. - Electrical outlets, fixtures.
   Every habitable room of every dwelling unit shall contain at least two
separate wall type electric convenience outlets and one wall switched ceiling
light fixture or outlet plug. Every water closet compartment or bathroom shall
contain at least one wall type electric convenience outlet and one wall
switched light fixture. Laundry rooms, furnace rooms, and other such rooms
shall be provided with adequate electric outlets for their purpose. Every such
outlet and fixture shall be properly installed, shall be maintained in good and
safe working condition, and shall be connected to the electric service panel in
a safe manner.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-101. - Minimum heating standards.
   (a)   It shall be the duty of every person who shall have contracted or
undertaken or who shall be bound to heat or to furnish heat for any occupied
dwelling, in the absence of a contract or agreement to the contrary, to furnish
sufficient heat for any occupied part thereof from October 1 of each year to
May 1 of the succeeding year, so as to maintain in such occupied premises a
minimum temperature of at least 60 degrees Fahrenheit from 10:30 p.m. until 6:
30 a.m., 65 degrees Fahrenheit at 7:30 a.m., and 68 degrees Fahrenheit at 8:30
a.m. and thereafter until 10:30 p.m., whenever the outer or street temperature
shall fall below 55 degrees Fahrenheit; provided, however, that failure to
provide the heat required shall not constitute an offense when it is due to any
act or acts of the occupant thereof or any cause beyond the control of the
person so required to furnish. The term "contracted" shall mean a written or
oral contract or agreement which has been entered into.
   (b)   It shall be the duty of the health officer or his authorized agent in
the department of health to receive, investigate and report all violations of
this section and to appear in court after complaint has been made by the party
aggrieved, for the purpose of furnishing testimony, and the health officer is
hereby authorized to adopt such methods of procedure and to make such rules and
regulations, subject to charter provisions as may be necessary, to accomplish
the intent of this section.
(Ord. No. 81-72, §§ 1, 2, 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-102. - Lighting of halls, stairways.
   Every public hall and stairway in every multiple dwelling containing five or
more dwelling units shall be adequately lighted at all times. Every public hall
and stairway in structures devoted solely to dwelling occupancy and containing
not more than four dwelling units may be supplied with conveniently located
light switches, controlling an adequate lighting system which may be turned on
when needed, instead of fulltime lighting.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-103. - Screening—Protection against mosquitoes, flies, etc.
   During that portion of each year when the health officer deems it necessary
for protection against mosquitoes, flies, and other insects, every door opening
directly from a dwelling unit to out-door space shall have supplied screens and
a self-closing device, and every window or other device with openings to
outdoor space, used or intended to be used for ventilation, shall likewise be
supplied with screens; provided that such screens shall not be required during
such period in rooms deemed by the health officer to be located high enough in
the upper stories of buildings as to be free from such insects, and in rooms
located in areas of the city which are deemed by the health officer to have so
few such insects as to render screens unnecessary.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-104. - Same—Rodent control.
   Every basement or cellar window used or intended to be used for ventilation,
and every other opening to a basement which might provide an entry for rodents,
shall be supplied with a screen or such other device as will effectively
prevent their entrance.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 5.8, 11-4-81)
Secs. 11-105—11-115. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 6. - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO THE SAFE AND SANITARY
MAINTENANCE OF PARTS OF DWELLINGS AND DWELLING UNITS **
Sec. 11-116. - Compliance.
   No person shall occupy as owner-occupant or let to another for occupancy any
dwelling or dwelling unit, for the purpose of living therein, which does not
comply with the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-117. - Foundations, floors, etc.
   Every foundation, floor, wall, ceiling and roof shall be reasonably
weathertight, watertight and rodentproof; shall be capable of affording
privacy; and shall be kept in good repair.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-118. - Windows, doors, etc.
   Every window, exterior door and basement hatchway shall be reasonably
weathertight, watertight and rodentproof; and shall be kept in sound working
condition and good repair.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-119. - Stairs, porches, etc.
   Every inside and outside stair, and every porch and every appurtenance
thereto, shall be so constructed as to be safe to use, and capable of
supporting the load that normal use may cause to be placed thereon, and shall
be kept in sound condition and good repair.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-120. - Plumbing installations.
   Every plumbing fixture and water and waste pipe shall be properly installed
and maintained in good sanitary working condition, free from defects, leaks and
obstructions.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-121. - Bathroom floors.
   Every water closet compartment floor surface and bathroom floor surface
shall be constructed and maintained so as to be reasonably impervious to water
and so as to permit such floor to be easily kept in a clean and sanitary
condition.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-122. - Other facilities, equipment.
   Every supplied facility, piece of equipment or utility which is required
under this article shall be so constructed or installed that it will function
safely and effectively, and shall be maintained in satisfactory working
condition.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-123. - Disconnection of services.
   No owner, operator or occupant shall cause any service, facility, equipment
or utility which is required under this article to be removed from, shut off
from or discontinued for any occupied dwelling let or occupied by him, except
for such temporary interruption as may be necessary while actual repairs or
alterations are in process, or during temporary emergencies when discontinuance
of service is approved by the director.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-124. - Condition of vacant units.
   No owner shall occupy or let to any other occupant any vacant dwelling unit
unless it is clean, sanitary and fit for human occupancy.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 6.8, 11-4-81)
Secs. 11-125. - Residential concrete driveway reinforcement.
   All residential concrete driveways with a depth of four inches or more shall
be constructed with a minimum of six-inch by six-inch (6 x 6) welded wire mesh
reinforcement. An alternative equivalent may be used if reviewed and approved
by the city's building official. This requirement shall apply to all new
driveway installations and to any driveway section replacement.
(Ord. No. 25-1854, 9-23-25)
* Secs. 11-126—11-135. - Reserved. *
** DIVISION 7. - MINIMUM SPACE, USE AND LOCATION REQUIREMENTS **
Sec. 11-136. - Compliance.
   No person shall occupy or let to another for occupancy any dwelling or
dwelling unit, for the purpose of living therein, which does not comply with
the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-137. - Minimum floor space—Dwelling unit.
   Every dwelling unit shall contain at least 250 square feet of floor space
for the first occupant thereof and at least 100 additional square feet of floor
space for every additional occupant thereof, the floor space to be calculated
on the basis of total habitable room area.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-138. - Same—Sleeping rooms.
   In every dwelling unit of two or more rooms, every room occupied for
sleeping purposes by one occupant shall contain at least 100 square feet of
floor space, and every room occupied for sleeping purposes by more than one
occupant shall contain at least 50 square feet of floor space for each occupant
thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-139. - Access to bathroom.
   No dwelling or dwelling unit containing two or more sleeping rooms shall
have such room arrangements that access to a bathroom or water closet
compartment, intended for use by occupants of more than one sleeping room, can
be had only by going through another sleeping room; nor shall room arrangements
be such that access to a sleeping room can be had only by going through another
sleeping room, bathroom or water closet compartment.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-140. - Ceiling height.
   At least one-half of the floor area of every second floor habitable room
shall have a ceiling height of at least seven feet, six inches, and the floor
area of that part of any room where the ceiling height is less than five feet
shall not be considered as part of the floor area in computing the total floor
area of the room for the purpose of determining the maximum permissible
occupancy thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-141. - Use of cellar, basement restricted.
   No cellar or basement space shall be used as a bedroom or dwelling unit.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 7.5, 11-4-81)
Secs. 11-142—11-150. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 8. - RESPONSIBILITIES OF OWNERS AND OCCUPANTS **
Sec. 11-151. - Shared public areas.
   Every owner of a dwelling containing two or more dwelling units shall be
responsible for maintaining in a clean and sanitary condition the shared or
public areas of the dwelling and premises thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-152. - Individual responsibility of occupant.
   Every occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall keep in a clean and
sanitary condition that part of the dwelling, dwelling unit, and premises
thereof which he occupies and controls.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-153. - Disposal of rubbish.
   Every occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall dispose of all his
rubbish in a clean and sanitary manner by placing it in the rubbish containers
required by section
11-81.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-154. - Disposal of garbage.
   Every occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall dispose of all his
garbage and any other organic waste which might provide food for rodents, in a
clean and sanitary manner; by placing it in the garbage disposal facilities or
garbage storage containers required by section
11-82. It shall be the responsibility of the owner to supply such facilities or
containers for all dwelling units in a dwelling containing more than four
dwelling units and for all dwelling units located on premises where more than
four dwelling units share the same premises. In all other cases it shall be the
responsibility of the occupant to furnish such facilities or containers.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-155. - Screens, storm doors and windows.
   Every occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall be responsible for
hanging all screens and double or storm doors and windows whenever the same are
required under the provisions of this article or of any rule or regulation
adopted pursuant thereto, except where the owner has agreed to supply such
service.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-156. - Pest control.
   Every occupant of a dwelling containing a single dwelling unit shall be
responsible for the extermination of any insects, rodents or other pests
therein or on the premises; and every occupant of a dwelling unit in a dwelling
containing more than one dwelling unit shall be responsible for such
extermination whenever his dwelling unit is the only one infested.
Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this section, whenever infestation
is caused by failure of the owner to maintain a dwelling in a ratproof or
reasonably insectproof condition, extermination shall be the responsibility of
the owner. Whenever infestation exists in two or more of the dwelling units in
any dwelling, or in the shared or public parts of any dwelling containing two
or more dwelling units, extermination thereof shall be the responsibility of
the owner.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-157. - Plumbing fixtures.
   Every occupant of a dwelling unit shall keep all plumbing fixtures therein
in a clean and sanitary condition and shall be responsible for the exercise of
reasonable care in the proper use and operation thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-158. - Maintenance of exterior.
   Every owner or occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall be responsible
for maintaining the exterior of the building. Such maintenance shall include,
but is not limited to:
      (1)   Maintaining lawn so as to prevent tall grass, vegetation and weeds
in the front yard, side yard, rear yard, adjacent rights-of-way and easements.
Six inches or more in length shall constitute a violation of this article.
      (2)   Maintaining any structure, garages, deck, shed, fence and/or pool
including but not limited to preventing peeling paint, broken, damaged or
missing steps, handrails, guardrails and/or porches, detached or loose gutters,
fascia, siding, flashing and/or shingles, broken doors and windows, sagging
roofs and torn, damaged or missing screens.
      (3)   Disposing of any accumulation of debris in yards and easements.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 8.8, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 84-289, 2-21-84; Ord. No. 06-1072,
5-15-06)
Secs. 11-159—11-170. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 9. - ROOMINGHOUSES **
Sec. 11-171. - Compliance.
   No person shall operate a roominghouse, or shall occupy or let to another
for occupancy any rooming unit in any roominghouse except in compliance with
the requirements of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-172. - Application to hotels.
   Every provision of this article which applies to roominghouses shall also
apply to hotels, except to the extent that any such provision may conflict with
the laws of this state or with the lawful regulation of any state board or
agency.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-173. - Notice of violation, procedures.
   Whenever upon inspection of any roominghouse, the health officer finds that
conditions or practices exist which are in violation of any provision of this
article or of any rule or regulation adopted pursuant thereto, the health
officer shall give notice in writing to the operator of such roominghouse
unless such conditions or practices are corrected within a reasonable period,
to be determined by the corporation counsel, the operator's roominghouse permit
will be suspended. At the end of such period, the health officer shall
reinspect such roominghouse, and if he finds that such conditions or practices
have not been corrected, he shall give notice in writing to the operator that
the latter's permit has been suspended. Upon receipt of notice of suspension,
such operator shall immediately cease operation of such roominghouse, and no
person shall occupy for sleeping or living purposes any rooming unit therein.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-174. - Suspension, revocation; hearing.
   Any person whose permit to operate a roominghouse has been suspended, or who
has received notice from the health officer that his permit is to be suspended
unless existing conditions or practices at his rooming house are corrected, may
request and shall be granted a hearing on the matter before the corporation
counsel under the procedure provided by section
11-57; provided that if no petition for such hearing is filed within ten days
following the day on which such permit was suspended, such permit shall be
deemed to have been automatically revoked.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-175. - Bathroom facilities.
   At least one flush water closet, lavatory basin, and bathtub or shower
properly connected to a water and sewer system, approved by the health officer,
and in good working condition, shall be supplied for each eight persons or
fraction thereof residing within a roominghouse, including members of the
operator's family wherever they share the use of the facilities; provided that
in a rooming house where rooms are let only to males, flush urinals may be
substituted for not more than one-half the required number of water closets.
All such facilities shall be so located within the dwelling as to be reasonably
accessible from a common hall or passageway to all persons sharing such
facilities. Every lavatory basin and bathtub or shower shall be supplied with
hot water at all times. No such facilities shall be located in a basement
except by written approval of the health officer.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-176. - Linens.
   The operator of every roominghouse shall change supplied bed linen and
towels therein at least once each week, and prior to the letting of any room to
any occupant. The operator shall be responsible for the maintenance of all
supplied bedding in a clean and sanitary manner.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-177. - Minimum area for sleeping rooms.
   Every room occupied for sleeping purposes by one person shall contain at
least 100 square feet of floor space, and every room occupied for sleeping
purposes by more than one person shall contain at least 50 square feet of floor
space for each occupant thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-178. - Egress.
   Every rooming unit shall have safe, unobstructed means of egress leading to
safe and open space at ground level, as required by the laws of this state and
the city.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 11-179. - Sanitary maintenance of walls, etc.
   The operator of every roominghouse shall be responsible for the sanitary
maintenance of all walls, floors, and ceilings, and for maintenance of a
sanitary condition in every other part of the roominghouse; and he shall be
further responsible for the sanitary maintenance of the entire premises, where
the entire structure or building is leased or occupied by the operator.
(Ord. No. 81-102, § 9.7, 11-4-81)
Secs. 11-180—11-190. - Reserved.
