MCL 289.1111 and MCL 289.6137).
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24; Ord. No. 25-1842, 5-20-25)
Sec. 12-251. - License required; compliance and scope of article.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any food truck to operate in the City of
Dearborn without first obtaining a food truck license from the city clerk and
pursuant to the provisions of this article.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to assist or help any person with
the operation of a food truck in the City of Dearborn except as provided by
this article.
   (c)   The provisions of this article shall apply to food trucks operating in
the city pursuant to the terms and conditions in this article.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24)
Sec. 12-252. - Application, review, and inspection; reservation of location not
guaranteed; application on behalf of food trucks at events.
   (a)   Application. The application for a food truck license shall be on
forms approved by the city clerk and shall include the following information:
      (1)   Name of the applicant; name of the business; applicant’s signature;
phone number, email contact, and business address of the applicant.
      (2)   If the owner of the business is different than the applicant, name
of the business owner; owner’s signature; phone number, email contact, and
business address of the owner.
      (3)   Information on the food truck, including the year, make and model
of the vehicle or unit and its dimensions.
      (4)   A statement of the status of monies owed to the city including, but
not limited to, water bills, real property taxes, personal property taxes, and
miscellaneous fees. An applicant with any unpaid fees owed to the city shall
not be eligible for a license under this article.
      (5)   a.   Copies of all necessary licenses or permits issued by the
Wayne County Health Department, another county health department in the State
of Michigan, and/or the State of Michigan, including but not limited to a copy
of the food service establishment license issued by the State of Michigan,
Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, or successor agency.
         b.   Retention of state license. The clerk shall keep a copy of the
type of state license (e.g., mobile food establishment or special transitory
food unit) that each licensee under this article has for the duration of their
local license.
      (6)   A signed statement that the licensee shall hold harmless and
indemnify the city, their officers, and employees for any claims for damage to
property or injury to persons which may occur as a result of any activity
carried on under the terms of the license.
      (7)   Proof of insurance coverage as follows:
         a.   Proof of commercial general liability policy with limits of no
less than $1,000,000.00 per occurrence with a $2,000,000.00 general aggregate
including products liability issued by an insurer licensed to do business in
the State of Michigan.
         b.   For food trucks operating on city-owned public property,
insurance coverage naming the city as an additional insured is required.
         c.   Proof of liability and property damage motor vehicle policy with
limits of no less than $1,000,000.00 used by an insurer licensed to do business
in the State of Michigan.
   (b)   Fee. Payment of the non-refundable fee listed in
Chapter 12, Section
12-6 of the Code of Ordinances shall be submitted with the application.
   (c)   Code compliance. In addition to the application requirements under
this subsection, each applicant must successfully pass review and inspection to
ensure that they are in compliance with all relevant requirements of the Fire
Prevention Code.
   (d)   Inspection requirements; proof of inspection. The following inspection
requirements shall apply:
      (1)   Consent to inspection. The filing of an application for a food
truck license shall constitute consent to inspection by the city’s fire
department for the purpose of ensuring compliance with the specific regulations
of this article, the city’s Code of Ordinances, and applicable law. This
subsection shall be narrowly construed by the city to authorize reasonable
inspections of the food truck pursuant to this article.
      (2)   Scheduling and scope of inspection. Upon the filing of a completed
application, the city clerk shall forward a copy of the application to the
Dearborn fire department to schedule an inspection. Inspections will occur
during normal city business hours or at another mutually agreeable time, and
the applicant shall allow representatives of the fire department into the food
truck to complete inspection. Inspections of the food truck shall be for the
following:
         a.   Compliance with the city’s Fire Prevention Code, Section
10-38 of the Code of Ordinances, including but not limited to code requirements
related to propane use and storage, as referenced in Section
12-255 of this article;
         b.   Inspection of the food truck for compliance with generator noise
decibel levels. Per Section
12-255 below, all generators must operate at a level of 80 decibels or lower,
exclusive of any other noise, when measured from a distance of 15 feet; and
         c.   An inspection to confirm that exhaust from the food truck is
directed away from the service side of the vehicle; and
      (3)   Alternative inspection. Proof from the Western Wayne County Fire
Department Mutual Aid Association that the applicant’s food truck complies with
the fire safety, propane, generator noise decibel, and exhaust requirements of
this article is sufficient if proof of such compliance is provided to the
Dearborn fire marshal for verification.
   (e)   Location disclaimer. Application under this section does not guarantee
access to city-approved locations for operation of a licensee’s food truck.
Licensees interested in accessing approved locations must seek and receive
approval as indicated in Section
12-255  of this article.
   (f)   License validity. A license issued under this article is valid for a
food truck and its employees.
   (g)   Non-transferable. A license issued under this article shall not be
transferable from one food truck to another.
   (h)   Third-party application for events. For events with 2 or more food
trucks, the event organizer may apply for a food truck license on behalf of the
participating food trucks subject to compliance with all requirements for
licensure under this article.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-
22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-24; Ord. No. 25-1842, 5-20-25)
Sec. 12-253. - License renewal and expiration.
   Food truck licenses must be renewed annually by submitting an application
pursuant to the terms and requirements of this article. Licenses issued under
this article shall expire annually on April 30. Food trucks that have a valid
license on the effective date of the amendments to this section, and whose
license is scheduled to expire on December 1, 2024, are hereby granted an
extension of their license until April 30, 2025.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24)
Sec. 12-254. - Display of license.
   The license issued to a food truck owner/operator by the city clerk shall be
displayed in a conspicuous location whenever the food truck is open for
business in the City of Dearborn. In addition, food trucks shall be ready to
provide visual proof of the city license and all necessary county health
department and/or State of Michigan permits and licenses at all times.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24)
Sec. 12-255. - Rules, guidelines, and restrictions; authorized locations and
reserving space; block parties.
   (a)   Rules, guidelines, and restrictions.
      (1)   Hours of operation. Hours of operation in designated park locations
shall be between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m., unless otherwise allowed
in writing by the Director of Recreation.
      (2)   Interference with adjacent buildings prohibited. Food trucks shall
not impede access to the entrance or driveway of any adjacent building.
      (3)   Trash collection by operator. All trash or debris accumulating
within 20 feet of any food truck shall be collected by the operator and
deposited in a trash container. All food truck operators must provide trash
receptacles adjacent to or as a part of their truck. Operators may also rent
trash receptacles from the city at an additional cost. It shall be unlawful for
any food truck operator, or anyone aiding or assisting in the operation of a
food truck, to throw or deposit any goods, merchandise, packaging, containers,
fat, grease, paper, or other liquid waste upon any alley, street or sidewalk,
or in any sewer, in the city.
      (4)   Waste disposal by operator. All waste originating from the food
truck, and not from customers, shall be collected and disposed of off-site by
the food truck operator each day. Spills of food or food by-products shall be
cleaned up and no dumping of greywater on the street or in parks and storm
drains is allowed. Food truck operators should take appropriate precautions to
prevent spills or other damages to the public property as a result of their
operation. Food trucks are responsible for all greywater, grease, and other
food waste, which shall NOT be dumped or disposed of on or into public
property, including but not limited to drains and public trash receptacles.
      (5)   Noise and generators. No food truck operator shall make or cause
any unreasonable or excessive noise. No loud music or amplified announcements
or noise is permitted. In addition, all generators must operate at a level of
80 decibels or lower when measured from a distance of 15 feet. Initial
inspection by the fire department shall include generator compliance.
      (6)   Propane usage. Food trucks that utilize propane must comply with
all relevant requirements under law, including but not limited to the city’s
Fire Code (See Code of Ordinances, Section
10-38), and pass Fire Code inspection.
         a.   Propane canisters must be securely mounted to the food truck or
placed within a ventilated compartment;
         b.   A ventilated compartment must provide for the natural or
mechanical process of supplying conditioned or unconditioned air to, or
removing such air from, the location of the propane canister being used, in
conformity with the definition of “ventilation” found in Sec. 202 of IFC 2024;
and
         c.   Propane canister must not be stored or placed on the ground.
      (7)   Exhaust. All food trucks shall direct exhaust away from the service
side of the vehicle. Initial inspection by the fire department shall include
exhaust compliance.
      (8)   Nuisance prohibited. Except as otherwise stated in this article,
food truck operators shall be subject to the provisions of
Chapter 13 of the city’s Code of Ordinances regarding nuisances, including but
not limited to regulations regarding noise, smoke, and noxious odors.
      (9)   Traffic obstruction prohibited. No food truck operator shall
conduct business in such a way as would increase traffic congestion or delay,
constitute a hazard to life or property, interfere with an abutting property
owner, or obstruct access to emergency vehicles.
      (10)   Public rights-of-way. Food truck operators shall operate in
compliance with all provisions of the city’s Code of Ordinances and Zoning
Ordinance that govern sidewalks and other public places, traffic, and motor
vehicles.
      (11)   Code compliance. Food truck operators shall be subject to all
applicable building, electrical, mechanical, and fire safety code requirements,
including any permit or inspection requirements deemed necessary by the
building official.
      (12)   Signs. Signage shall be placed on the food truck. Separate free-
standing signs are permitted in accordance with the city’s existing
encroachment regulations and sign ordinance (See Dearborn Code of Ordinances
Chapter 4, Article XII).
      (13)   Lights. All exterior lights more than 60 watts are subject to the
following regulations:
         a.   Lighting and/or illumination shall not create glare or
excessively illuminate the surrounding area;
         b.   Lighting and/or illumination that distracts motorists or creates
a traffic hazard for either vehicles or pedestrians is prohibited;
         c.   No flashing, blinking, or strobe lights are allowed when the food
truck is parked, in-service, or in motion within the city; and
         d.   All exterior lights shall be located and directed downward (below
the horizontal), and shall not be directly visible from or aimed at adjacent
streets, roads, or properties.
      (14)   Power supply. Power required for a food truck shall be self-
contained and self-provided. However, a food truck may request authorization
from the building official to utilize public utilities where available. No
power cable shall be extended on or across any city street or sidewalk except
in a safe, concealed manner designed to prevent tripping if reviewed and
approved by the building official or their designee.
      (15)   Proximity to fire hydrants. No food truck is allowed within 20
feet of a fire hydrant.
   (b)   Authorized locations to operate food trucks in the city; city park
food truck permit required.
      (1)   Public parks and park property. In addition to the licensing
requirements under this article, food truck operators must also obtain a
recreation food truck permit from the director of the department of recreation,
or their designee, before operating a food truck in designated locations as
identified below. Applicants must be licensed pursuant to the terms and
conditions of this article, and their license must remain in good standing at
all times they are in operation.
      (2)   Application process.
         a.   Before applying for a recreation food truck permit to operate at
a designated location, applicants must have a valid food truck license.
         b.   Applicants must file a complete application with the recreation
department on forms approved by the director of the department of recreation,
or their designee.
         c.   A fee determined by the director of the department of recreation
is due at the time of application. The fee shall be non-refundable except as
otherwise stated in this article.
         d.   Complete applications will be taken on a first-come, first-serve
basis.
      (3)   Rental fee. A non-refundable administrative rental fee determined
by the director of the department of recreation will be charged in addition to
the application fee under this subsection. Such fee will be based on the
duration that designated locations will be rented, with the following tiers:
         a.   Daily pass;
         b.   Weekly pass;
         c.   Weekend pass;
         d.   Monthly pass;
         e.   Season pass (no holidays); and
         f.   Premium pass (includes holidays and first priority for special
events).
      (4)   Designated locations. The director of the department of recreation
may designate areas at the following locations for the operation of food trucks
pursuant to the terms and conditions of this article:
         a.   Lapeer Park.
         b.   Hemlock Park.
         c.   Ford Woods Park.
         d.   Ford Field Park.
         e.   Levagood Park.
         f.   Crowley Park.
         g.   Ten Eyck Park.
         h.   Ford Center for the Performing Arts.
         i.   Other city parks as designated by the recreation director.
      (5)   Grounds for revocation of designated location. The recreation
director shall issue a written notice to revoke the recreation food truck
permit if the food truck license has been revoked by the city clerk.
      (6)   Appeals for park locations. Any person denied a location in a
designated location under this subsection (b) may appeal same as follows:
         a.   A person wishing to appeal pursuant to this subsection must first
file a written statement of the grounds for appeal and the relief requested
with the recreation director. Such appeal shall be filed with the director
within 14 days of notice of denial. The appeal shall be decided by the director
or their designee without hearing and within 14 days of receiving the appeal,
based on review of the written statement, any supporting documents or materials
submitted by the appellant, and any other papers, materials, and documents
associated with the decision.
         b   The decision of the director or designee may be appealed to city
council by filing a written statement of the grounds for appeal and the relief
requested with the council office. Such appeal shall be filed with the council
office within 14 days of notice of denial by the recreation director.
      (7)   Notice of appeal hearing. Upon receipt of a request for appeal, the
city council shall provide the appellant with notice and an opportunity to be
heard. The city council shall serve notice upon the licensee by certified mail
not less than 14 days prior to the hearing. The notice shall state:
         a.   The date, time and place of the hearing.
         b.   A statement that the licensee may present evidence and testimony,
and may be represented by an attorney.
         c.   The city council shall also notify the recreation director of the
date and time of the hearing and provide a complete copy of the appellant’s
written notice. The recreation director, or their designee, shall attend the
appeal hearing.
      (8)   Appeal hearing and decision. The hearing shall be conducted by the
city council and shall be open to the public. The city council shall, by
resolution, decide the appeal at the public hearing. The city council shall
only decide the following:
         a.   Whether to uphold or overturn the decision of the recreation
director;
         b   If the recreation director’s decision is upheld, the council’s
ruling shall be final;
         c.   If the recreation director’s decision is overturned, the council
shall then determine:
            (i)   Whether the appellant can have the park location they
originally applied for;
            (ii)   If that location is occupied by another food truck, whether
another location is available; or
            (iii)   If the appellant does not want another location whether to
refund the appellant’s application fee for a recreation food truck permit.
   (c)   Block parties. Food trucks may operate at block parties that receive a
valid permit under
Chapter 17 of the city’s Code of Ordinances, and must comply with all
requirements of this article, the the Code of Ordinances, and Zoning Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24; Ord. 25-1842, 5-20-25)
Sec. 12-256. - Suspension or revocation of license.
   Any license issued under this article may be suspended or revoked for any of
the following reasons:
   (1)   Fraud or misrepresentation in the application for the license.
   (2)   Fraud or misrepresentation in the course of conducting business.
   (3)   Conducting the business contrary to the conditions of the license,
this article, or applicable provisions of the city's Code of Ordinances or
Zoning Ordinance.
   (4)   Conducting the business of vending in such manner as to create a
public nuisance or constitute a danger to the public health, safety and
welfare.
   (5)   Conviction of any crime involving moral turpitude while holding a
vending license from the city.
   (6)   Intervention by the state department of health due to uncorrected
health or sanitation violations.
   Upon suspension or revocation, the city shall deliver written notice to the
license holder stating the action taken and the reasons supporting such action.
The written notice shall be delivered to the license holder's place of business
or mailed to the license holder's last known address.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24)
Sec. 12-257.   Appeals.
   Persons whose licenses under this article have been suspended or revoked, or
whose application for a license has been denied, may appeal by filing a written
notice of appeal with the city council.
(Ord. No. 18-1613, 6-12-18; Ord. No. 22-1743, 5-24-22; Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-
24)
Sec. 12-258.   Enforcement.
   The provisions of the article shall be enforced by the director of economic
development and any deputies, agents, or inspectors designated by him, any
officer of the police department, and the city clerk or their designee.
(Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-24)
Sec. 12-259.   Other permits, licenses, or authorizations.
   A license or permit obtained under this article shall not relieve any food
truck of the responsibility for obtaining any other permit or license or
authorization required by any other ordinance, statute, or administrative rule.
(Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-24)
Sec. 12-260.   Severability.
   Should any word, phrase, sentence, paragraph, or section of this article be
held invalid or unconstitutional, the remaining provisions of the article shall
remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. No. 23-1805, 1-9-24)
* Secs. 12-261—12-265. Reserved. *
*** ARTICLE VIII. - SOLICITING AND CANVASSING ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Secs. 12-266—12-274. - Reserved.
Sec. 12-275. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this article is to protect the health, safety and welfare of
the citizens of the city by protecting citizens from the possibility of crime
being committed by solicitors or canvassers or those posing as solicitors or
canvassers and by protecting the privacy rights of citizens in their homes.
(Ord. No. 88-416, § 1, 5-3-88)
** DIVISION 2. - COMMERCIAL SOLICITING **
Sec. 12-276. - Definition.
   For the purpose of this division, "soliciting" and "canvassing," as used in
this division, shall consist of any person, whether a resident of the city or
not, who by going from house to house solicits orders for merchandise of any
nature for future delivery; or orders for the installation or servicing of any
household equipment or appliances, including but not limited to, furnace or
boiler repair and maintenance, repair and servicing of washing machines,
incinerators, or the installation of storm windows and screens, awnings,
roofing and siding of buildings and the cleaning, painting or modernization of
buildings.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 2, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-277. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of soliciting
or canvassing without first obtaining a license therefor in compliance with the
provisions of this article. Such license shall be applied for and administered
pursuant to the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-278. - Application for license.
   Any person desiring a license under the provisions of this division must
make application to the city clerk on forms provided by him.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 4(a), 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-279. - License fees.
   (a)   No license shall be issued until the fee therefor shall have been paid
to the city clerk, as listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter. The annual fee to be paid by any firm, shall cover the
license cost of any and all of their agents, employees, distributors, dealers
or direct sales personnel. In cases where the distributors, dealers or direct
sales personnel act in an independent capacity in soliciting orders or in
selling for their own account, the firm whose products are being distributed or
sold may, at its option, elect to cover its distributors or direct sales
personnel by paying the annual charge, and nothing herein shall be construed as
establishing the relationship of employer and employee or principal and agent
between the person doing the distributing or selling and the company whose
products are being distributed or sold; provided, however, in all cases it will
be necessary for each individual subject to the provisions of this division to
make an individual application to the city clerk and secure an individual
license as herein provided. The annual license fee is for the purpose of
covering the cost of such licenses and does not waive the requirement that each
person engaged in soliciting or canvassing shall have his own individual
license.
   (b)   None of the license fees provided herein shall be so applied as to
occasion an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce. In any case where an
applicant engaged in interstate commerce believes the fee to constitute an
unreasonable burden on such commerce, he may apply to the city clerk for an
adjustment of the fee so that it shall not be discriminatory, unreasonable or
unfair as to such commerce. Such application may be made before, at or within
six months after payment of the required license fee. The applicant shall by
affidavit and supporting testimony show his business operations, the gross
volume or estimated gross volume of business and any other information that the
city clerk may deem necessary in order to determine the extent, if any, of such
unreasonable burden on such commerce. The city clerk shall then conduct an
investigation comparing the applicant's business with other businesses of like
nature and shall make a finding of fact from which he shall determine whether
the fee fixed by this division is unfair, unreasonable or discriminatory as to
the applicant's business, and shall fix as the license fee for the applicant an
amount that is fair, reasonable and nondiscriminatory. If the fee has already
been paid, the clerk shall order a re-fund of the amount over and above the fee
so fixed. In fixing the fee to be charged, the city clerk shall have the power
to base the fee upon a percentage of gross sales or any other method which will
assure that the fee assessed shall be uniform with that assessed on businesses
of like nature; provided, however, that the amount assessed shall not exceed in
any case the fees prescribed by this division. Should the city clerk determine
the gross sales measure of the fee to be a fair standard, he may require the
applicant to submit, either at the time of termination of the applicant's
business in the city or at the end of each three-month period, a sworn
statement of the gross sales and pay the amount of fee therefor; provided,
however, that no additional fee shall be required during any one calendar year
if the licensee shall have paid an amount equal to the annual license fee
provided in this division.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 4(b), 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 12-280. - Expiration of license.
   All annual licenses issued under the provisions of this division shall
expire one year from application date. Licenses, other than annual licenses,
shall expire on the date specified in the license.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-281. - Display of license; identification of organization.
   Licenses issued under the provisions of this division must be in the
possession of the licensee at all times and must be shown at the request of any
citizen or police officer of the city. All licensees must have the name and
address of their firm, partnership, corporation or association plainly lettered
on their business vehicles or equipment, with the exception of privately owned
passenger automobiles.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-282. - Prohibited hours of operation.
   A legally licensed solicitor or canvasser shall not solicit between the
hours of 9:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-283. - Reciprocal licensing.
   The city shall permit solicitors and canvassers legally licensed by other
governmental units within the county, or by the state, to engage in the
activities covered by this division upon registering with the city clerk;
provided, however, that no license issued by another governmental unit will be
recognized by the city unless such other governmental unit reciprocates in
recognizing the license issued by the city.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-284. - Orders.
   All orders taken by licensees under this division shall be in writing, in
duplicate, stating the name and address of both the solicitor or canvasser and
his employer, if applicable, the terms of the order, and description of the
goods, the amount of the down payment and one copy must be given to the
purchaser.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-285. - Access to premises restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to solicit or canvass upon any premises
if requested by anyone in control of the premises not to do so, or if there is
placed on such premises in a conspicuous position near the entrance thereof a
sign bearing the words "No Soliciting," "No Peddlers or Agents," "No
Canvassing," "No Agents" or any similar notice indicating in any manner that
the occupants of such premises do not desire to have solicitors or canvassers
call upon them.
(Ord. No. 81-100, § 8, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-286—12-295. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - NONCOMMERCIAL SOLICITING **
Sec. 12-296. - Definition.
   For the purpose of this division, "religious, political or charitable
soliciting" shall consist of any person or group, whether a resident of the
city or not, who, by going house to house without invitation, solicits money;
sells any merchandise for religious, political or charitable beliefs or
espouses charitable beliefs; and solicits a donation to further such beliefs.
(Ord. No. 88-416, § 2, 5-3-88; Ord. No. 04-1005, 6-15-04; Amend. of 5-25-07)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-297. - Hours of operation.
   A solicitor or a canvasser shall not solicit or canvass between the hours of
9:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m.
(Ord. No. 88-416, § 7, 5-3-88; Ord. No. 04-1005, 6-15-04; Ord. No. 25-1838, 3-
18-25)
Sec. 12-298. - Access to premises restricted. 
   It shall be unlawful for any person to solicit or canvass for religious,
political, charitable or public interest reasons upon any premises if requested
by anyone in control of the premises not to do so, or if there is placed on
such premises in a conspicuous position near the entrance thereof a sign
bearing the words "No Soliciting," "No Peddlers or Agents," "No Canvassing,"
"No Agents" or any similar notice indicating, in any manner, that the occupants
of such premises do not desire to have solicitors or canvassers call upon them.
(Ord. No. 88-416, § 8, 5-3-88; Ord. No. 04-1005, 6-15-04)
Secs. 12-299—12-324. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE IX. - TOBACCO PRODUCTS ***
Sec. 12-325. - Investigation prior to license application.
   All applications for a license hereunder shall be referred to the chief of
police or their designee for investigation as to the reputation, character and
police record of the applicant and whether such person is suitable to be
entrusted with the sale of articles mentioned in section
12-326, hereof, and upon a return of a favorable report thereof to the city
clerk and the payment of license fee as stated in section
12-6 to the treasurer, the clerk shall thereupon issue such license.
   In determining the applicant's reputation, character, and police record, the
following shall be considered:
   (a)   The following shall be considered a disqualifying criminal act and
result in the denial of an application for a license hereunder:
      (1)   Any of the following misdemeanor or felony offenses under any of
the following statutes, as amended, for which less than seven years has elapsed
since the date of conviction or the date of release from confinement for the
conviction, whichever is the later date:
         a.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter X, Arson and Burning;
         b.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XI, Assaults, except MCL 750.81(1)
and (2);
            1.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XVII, Bribery and Corruption;
         c.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXII, Compounding Offenses;
         d.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXVA, Criminal Enterprises;
         e.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXVIII, Disorderly Persons;
         f.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXXI, Embezzlement;
          g.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXXIII, Explosives, Bombs, Harmful
Devices;
         h.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XXXIV, Extortion;
         i.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XLIII, Frauds and Cheats;
         j.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XLIV, Gambling;
         k.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XLV, Homicide;
         l.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter XLVIII, Indecency and Immorality;
         m.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LVIII, Mayhem;
         n.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LXVII, Prostitution;
         o.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LXVIIA, Human Trafficking;
         p.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LXXVI, Sexual Conduct;
         q.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LXXVIII, Robbery;
         r.   Michigan Penal Code, Chapter LXXXIII-A, Michigan Anti-Terrorism
Act;
         s.   MCL, 333, Part 74, Controlled Substances Offense and Penalties;
         t.   MCL § 205.27, Taxation-Prohibited Acts, including tax evasion;
      (2)   Selling, giving, or furnishing a tobacco product, vapor product, or
alternative nicotine product to a minor in violation of MCL 722.641;
      (3)   Any attempt, solicitation, or conspiracy to commit one of the
foregoing offenses; or
      (4)   Any offense enumerated in the City's Code of Ordinances which
substantially corresponds to one of the foregoing state offenses; or
      (5)   Any offense in another jurisdiction that, had the predicate act(s)
been committed in Michigan, would have constituted any of the foregoing
offenses.
   (b)   In addition to subsection (a) above, the following shall also be
considered disqualifying acts that shall result in the denial of an application
for a license hereunder:
      (1)   Code compliance. The subject premises lacks a current certificate
of occupancy or does not comply with applicable building, zoning, plumbing,
electrical, mechanical, health, or fire prevention codes.
       (2)   Unpaid fees. Relevant city departments have indicated that there
are unpaid fees or incurred violations under their purview related to the
subject premises.
      (3)   Taxes. The treasury division has denied a real and/or personal
property tax clearance pertaining to the subject premises.
(Ord. No. 81-59, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1775, 10-25-22)
Sec. 12-326. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, furnish or give away, directly
or indirectly, cigarettes, cigars, tobaccos or the component parts thereof
without first obtaining a license.
(Ord. No. 81-59, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-327. - License application.
   Any person desiring to do any of the acts or things mentioned in section
12-326 shall make an application to the city clerk upon forms furnished by him,
setting forth the full name and place or places of business in which it is
proposed to carry on the business.
(Ord. No. 81-59, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-328. - Possession of tobacco products, vapor products, and alternative
nicotine products by minors.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any minor under the age of 21 years to have
in his possession any cigars, cigarettes, papers, wrappers or tobacco, and any
person furnishing such minors with any of the articles mentioned in section
12-326 or this section shall be deemed guilty of a violation of this article.
   (b)   A person shall not sell, give or furnish a tobacco product, vapor
product, or alternative nicotine product to a minor, including, but not limited
to, through a vending machine. A person who violates this subsection (b) or
subsection (f) is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine as follows:
      (1)   For a first offense, not more than $100.00.
      (2)   For a second or subsequent offense, not more than $500.00
   (c)   It is an affirmative defense to a charge under subsection (b) that the
defendant had in force at the time of arrest and continues to have in force a
written policy to prevent the sale of tobacco products, vapor products, or
alternative nicotine products, as applicable under this section and Public Act
31 of 1915, to persons under 21 years of age and that the defendant
enforced and continues to enforce the policy. A defendant who proposes to offer
evidence of the affirmative defense described in this subsection shall file
notice of the defense, in writing, with the court and serve a copy of the
notice on the prosecuting attorney. The defendant shall serve the notice not
less than 14 days before the date set for trial.
   (d)   A prosecuting attorney who proposes to offer testimony to rebut the
affirmative defense described in subsection (c) shall file a notice of
rebuttal, in writing, with the court and serve a copy of the notice on the
defendant. The prosecuting attorney shall serve the notice not less than seven
days before the date set for trial and shall include in the notice the name and
address of each rebuttal witness.
   (e)   Subsection (b) does not apply to the handling or transportation of a
tobacco product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine product by a minor
under the terms of the minor's employment.
   (f)   Before selling, offering for sale, giving, or furnishing a tobacco
product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine product to an individual, a
person shall verify that the individual is at least 21 years of age by doing
one of the following:
      (1)   If the individual appears to be under 27 years of age, examining a
government-issued photographic identification that establishes that the
individual is at least 21 years of age.
      (2)   For sales made by the internet or other remote sales method,
performing an age verification through an independent, third-party age
verification service that compares information available from a commercially
available database, or aggregate of databases, that are regularly used by
government agencies and businesses for the purpose of age and identity
verification to the personal information entered by the individual during the
ordering process that establishes that the individual is 21 years of age or
older.
   (g)   Minors and tobacco. Subject to subsection (l), a minor shall not do
any of the following:
      (1)   Purchase or attempt to purchase a tobacco product.
      (2)   Possess or attempt to possess a tobacco product.
      (3)   Use a tobacco product in a public place.
      (4)   Present or offer to an individual a purported proof of age that is
false, fraudulent, or not actually his or her own proof of age for the purpose
of purchasing, attempting to purchase, possessing, or attempting to possess a
tobacco product.
   (h)   An individual who violates subsection (g) is guilty of a misdemeanor
punishable by a fine of not more than $50.00 for each violation. Pursuant to a
probation order, the court may also require an individual who violates
subsection (1) to participate in a health promotion and risk reduction
assessment program, if available. In addition, an individual who violates
subsection (g) is subject to the following:
      (1)   For the first violation, the court may order the individual to do 1
of the following:
         a.   Perform not more than 16 hours of community service.
         b.   Participate in a health promotion and risk reduction assessment
program.
      (2)   For a second violation, in addition to participation in a health
promotion and risk reduction assessment program, the court may order the
individual to perform not more than 32 hours of community service.
      (3)   For a third or subsequent violation, in addition to participation
in a health promotion and risk reduction assessment program, the court may
order the individual to perform not more than 48 hours of community service.
   (i)   Minors and vapor products or alternative nicotine products. subject to
subsection (l), a minor shall not do any of the following:
      (1)   Purchase or attempt to purchase a vapor product or alternative
nicotine product.
      (2)   Possess or attempt to possess a vapor product or alternative
nicotine product.
      (3)   Use a vapor product or alternative nicotine product in a public
place.
      (4)   Present or offer to an individual a purported proof of age that is
false, fraudulent, or not actually his or her own proof of age for the purpose
of purchasing, attempting to purchase, possessing, or attempting to possess a
vapor product or alternative nicotine product.
   (j)   An individual who violates subsection (i) is responsible for a civil
infraction or guilty of a misdemeanor as follows:
      (1)   For the first violation, the individual is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be fined not more than $50.00. The court may order the
individual to participate in a health promotion and risk reduction assessment
program, if available. In addition, the court may order the individual to
perform not more than 16 hours of community service.
      (2)   For a second violation, the individual is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be fined not more than $50.00. The court may order the
individual to participate in a health promotion and risk reduction assessment
program, if available. In addition, the court may order the individual to
perform not more than 32 hours of community service.
      (3)   If a violation of subsection (j)(1) occurs after two or more prior
judgments, the individual is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of
not more than $50.00 for each violation. Pursuant to a probation order, the
court may also require the individual to participate in a health promotion and
risk reduction assessment program, if available. In addition, the court may
order the individual to perform not more than 48 hours of community service.
   (k)   An individual who is ordered to participate in a health promotion and
risk reduction assessment program under subsection (g) or (i) is responsible
for the costs of participating in the program.
   (l)   Subsections (g) and (i) do not apply to a minor participating in any
of the following:
      (1)   An undercover operation in which the minor purchases or receives a
tobacco product, a vapor product, or alternative nicotine product under the
direction of the minor's employer and with the prior approval of the local
prosecutor's office as part of an employer-sponsored internal enforcement
action.
      (2)   An undercover operation in which the minor purchases or receives a
tobacco product, a vapor product, or alternative nicotine product under the
direction of the state or local police agency as part of an enforcement action,
unless the initial or contemporaneous purchase or receipt of the tobacco
product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine product by the minor was not
under the direction of the state police or the local police agency and was not
part of the undercover operation.
      (3)   Compliance checks in which the minor attempts to purchase tobacco
products for the purpose of satisfying federal substance abuse block grant
youth tobacco access requirements, if the compliance checks are conducted under
the direction of a substance abuse disorder coordinating agency and with the
prior approval of the state or a local police agency.
   (m)   Subsections (g) and (i) do not apply to the handling or transportation
of a tobacco product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine product by a minor
under the terms of the minor's employment.
   (n)   This section does not prohibit an individual from being charged with,
convicted of, or sentenced for any other violation of law that arises out of
the violation of subsection (g) and (i).
   (o)   Definitions. the following words, terms, and phrases, when used in
this section, shall have the following meanings ascribed to them:
      (1)   “Alternative nicotine product” means a noncombustible product
containing nicotine that is intended for human consumption, whether chewed,
absorbed, dissolved, or ingested by any other means. Alternative nicotine
product does not include a tobacco product, a vapor product, food, or a product
regulated as a drug or device by the United States Food and Drug Administration
under 21 USC 351 to 360fff-7.
      (2)   “Minor” means an individual who is less than 21 years of age.
      (3)   “Person who sells vapor products or alternative products at retail"
means a person whose ordinary course of business consists, in whole or in part,
of the retail sale of vapor products or alternative nicotine products.
      (4)   “Person who sells tobacco products at retail” means a person whose
ordinary course of business consists, in whole or in part, of the retail sale
of tobacco products subject to state sales tax.
      (5)   “Public place” means a public street, sidewalk, or park or any area
open to the general public in a publicly owned or operated building or public
place of business.
      (6)   “Tobacco product” means a product that contains tobacco and is
intended for human consumption, including, but not limited to, a cigarette,
noncigarette smoking tobacco, or smokeless tobacco, as those terms are defined
in section 2 of the tobacco products tax act, 1993 PA 327, MCL 205.422, and a
cigar.
      (7)   “Use a tobacco product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine
product” means to smoke, chew, such, inhale, or otherwise consume a tobacco
product, vapor product, or alternative nicotine product.
      (8)   “Vapor product” means a noncombustible product that employs a
heating element, power source, electronic circuit, or other electronic,
chemical, or mechanical means, regardless of shape or size, that can be used to
produce vapor from nicotine or any other substance, and the use or inhalation
of which simulates smoking. Vapor product includes an electronic cigarette,
electronic cigar, electronic cigarillo, electronic pipe, or similar product or
device and a vapor cartridge or other container of nicotine or other substance
in a solution or other form that is intended to be used with or in an
electronic cigarette, electronic cigar, electronic cigarillo, electronic pipe,
or similar product or device. Vapor product does not include a product
regulated as a drug or device by the United States Food and Drug Administration
under 21 USC 351 to 360fff-7. (Ord. No. 81-59, § 4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19-1636,
1-29-19; Ord. No.19-1662, 9-24-19; Ord. No. 19-1669, 1-14- 20; Ord. No. 22-
1774, 10-25-22)
State law reference—MCL 722.641
Sec. 12-329. - Display of license.
   Every person procuring a license under this article shall obtain from the
city clerk a copy of this article and post it in a conspicuous place in his
place of business.
(Ord. No. 81-59, § 5, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-330—12-350. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE X. - USED AUTOMOBILE DEALERS ***
Sec. 12-351. - License required.
   No person shall engage in the business of keeping a secondhand electric or
motor-driven vehicle or used car store, place or lot within the city for buying
or selling secondhand electric or motor-driven vehicles, used cars or
accessories without a license from the city.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-352. - Issuance of license.
   The city clerk is authorized to issue a license to any person of good
character to engage in the business of keeping a secondhand automobile or used
car store, place or lot for the buying, taking in exchange or selling of
secondhand automobiles or used cars, upon payment into the city treasury the
sum that is as listed in Section
12-6 of this chapter. No license shall be issued unless the application is
accompanied by a certificate issued by the police department recommending the
issuance of such license and, in addition thereto, a certificate from the
department of building and safety stating that the location of the business
will not violate any of the terms of the zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 12-353. - Expiration of license.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this article shall expire one
year from the date of application. The applicant shall pay an annual renewal
fee in the same amount as the original application, as above provided.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-354. - Nontransferable.
   Licenses issued under this article shall not be transferable. Where the
licensee is a corporation, the transfer of the controlling interest in the
corporation shall be deemed a transfer of the business which will require the
issuing of a new license therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-355. - Licensed premises restricted.
   No person licensed under this article shall, by virtue of one license, keep
within the city more than one house, shop or place for the buying, receiving
and taking in exchange or selling secondhand automobiles or used cars and parts
and ac-cessories thereto of any description in any place other than his place
of business.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-356. - Record of purchases.
   Every person licensed under this article shall, at the place of business
named in such license, keep a book in which shall be written in ink at the time
of the purchase or sale of any secondhand or used automobile, or parts or
accessories, a description thereof, the name, age, address and personal
description of the person from whom such purchase was made or to whom such sale
is made; as well as the day and hour of such purchase or sale. Such book at all
times shall be open to the inspection of any authorized member of the police
department. No entry in such book shall be erased, obliterated, altered or
defaced.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-357. - Report to police.
   Every licensed dealer shall make out a report every day before 10:00 a.m. of
sales made and the cars received for sale or purchase on a blank form to be
furnished by the police department in accordance with the provisions of this
article; such report to give full details in accordance with this article, of
all transactions of the day previous and up to the time of making such report,
and such report shall be filed with the chief of police before 10:00 a.m. of
the next following business day.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-358. - Display of article.
   Every dealer licensed under this article shall post in a conspicuous place
in his place of business a copy of this article relating to the dealer's
license under the provision of this article, such copies to be furnished by the
police department.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-359. - Revocation.
   Any license issued under this division may be revoked by the mayor for cause
if the licensee shall violate this article or any other city ordinance or state
or federal laws, or if the zoning board of appeals shall fail to renew any
temporary certificate of compliance or occupancy previously granted to the
licensee.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-360. - Sunday sales prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of buying,
selling or exchanging new, used or secondhand motor vehicles, or offering to
buy, sell or exchange or participate in the negotiation thereof, or attempt to
buy, sell or exchange any motor vehicle or interest therein or of any written
instrument pertaining thereto in the city on the first day of the week,
commonly called Sunday; provided, however, that the provisions of this article
shall not be applicable to any person who conscientiously believes that the
seventh day of the week from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday should be
observed as the Sabbath and actually refrains from conducting or engaging in
the business of buying or selling or performing other secular business on that
day.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-361. - Barrier to be erected.
   Before a license will be issued covering any one house, shop or place which
will be used by a licensee under this article, the licensee shall construct or
cause to be constructed a barrier consisting of a solid masonry wall or curb,
or a steel or timber guardrail, not over 18 inches above the grade, as
established by the city, but of sufficient height to prevent motor vehicles
from being driven over them. Such barrier shall be maintained along the side or
sides of the parking area abutting one or more buildings owned by others, along
any abutting partition fence and along any part of the parking area which abuts
a public street or highway; provided, however, no such barrier shall be
required to be installed adjacent to a place where the curb has been cut and a
suitable concrete or other hard-surface approach to such area has been
installed.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 6-a, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-362. - Motor vehicle parts recycling license.
   Any licensee under the provisions of this article who deals primarily in the
sale of motor vehicle parts obtained by dismantling distressed motor vehicles
on the licensed premises shall, in addition to the used motor vehicle license,
also hold a motor vehicle parts recycling license. A motor vehicle parts
recycling license is distinguished and differs from a junk dealer's license in
that the former contemplates and shall permit the storage of distressed motor
vehicles on a temporary basis only, during which time the vehicle is completely
restored or dismantled by the licensee with all components therefrom suitable
for use on a registered motor vehicle stored on the premises in an orderly
fashion for resale to the general public. All nonusable parts or residue of the
distressed motor vehicle shall be stored on the premises on a temporary basis
only and shall be sold and removed from the premises as soon as practical.
Application and issuance of a motor vehicle parts recycling license shall be
governed by section
12-327, except that an additional surety bond shall not be required, and the
fee to be paid in connection with the issuance of a motor vehicle parts
recycling license in a fixed place in the city shall be the sum as listed in
Section
12-6 of this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 81-75, § 6-b, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22- 1724, 2-8-22)
Secs. 12-363—12-385. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XI. - SECONDHAND JEWELRY AND PRECIOUS METAL DEALERS[2]  ***
Footnotes:

Editor's note— Ord. No. 92-551, adopted Jan. 5, 1993, has been treated as
superseding the provisions of former art. XI, §§ 12-386—12-393, which pertained
to similar subject matter, and derived from Ord. No. 81-16, §§ 1—8, adopted
Feb. 17, 1981. Sections 1—9 of said Ord. No. 92-551 added a new art. XI, §§
12-386—
12-394, to read as herein set out.
State Law reference— Precious metal and gem dealer act, MCL 445.481 et seq.,
MSA 19.720(1) et seq.; secondhand watches, MCL 445.551 et seq., MSA 19.734 et
seq.
Sec. 12-386. - Definition.
   The term "secondhand dealer" as used in this article shall mean any person,
corporation or member or members of a co-partnership or firm whose principal
business is that of purchasing, storing, selling, exchanging and receiving
secondhand personal property of any kind or description.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 1, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-387. - License required.
   No person, corporation or firm shall engage in the business of buying or
selling any secondhand goods, secondhand jewelry, used silverware, or other
secondhand manufactured article composed wholly or in part of gold, silver,
platinum or other precious metal, nor shall any person engage in the business
of buying or selling gold, silver, platinum or other precious metal in the city
without having first procured a license from the city clerk for such purpose.
The license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 2, 1-5-93; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 12-388. - Separate license required for each place of business.
   No licensee under this article shall, by virtue of one license, maintain or
conduct more than one location for buying or selling the articles described in
12-387. A license shall be required where the activities or dealings described
in section
12-387 are carried on as an incident to an ordinary jewelry business or other
business.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 3, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-389. - Identification of seller; record to be kept by licensee.
   Every licensee under this article shall, at the time of each transaction of
any article described in section
12-387, require the buyer or seller of such article to produce a valid state
driver's license or equivalent photographic identification from which the
licensee shall record the name, driver's license number, age, address and
personal description of the customer. The licensee shall record this
information together with the signature of the customer, a detailed description
of the article purchased, the amount paid for each such article and the date
and hour of the transaction in a book which shall at all times be open to
inspection by any member of the police department. Such book shall be
substantially bound and of a size not less than 8½ by 11 inches in breadth and
in length. All entries in such book shall be in ink, legibly written and in the
English language. No entry in such book shall be erased, obliterated, altered
or defaced. Each entry shall be numbered consecutive commencing with the number
one and shall be initialed by the licensee. The record of transaction forms of
a dealer shall not be open to inspection by the general public.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 4, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-390. - Fingerprints of seller; to whom copies sent; nature of property
furnished to chief of police.
   At time same time any secondhand dealer shall acquire or purchase any
article of personal property, or other valuable thing, except new articles
purchased at wholesale from manufacturers, wholesale distributors or jobbers
for retail sales to customers, the dealer shall take in duplicate the legible
imprint of the right thumb of the person from whom such property was received,
or if that not be possible, of the left thumb or some other finger of such
person. Such fingerprint shall be taken under such rules and regulations
prescribed by the commissioner of the state police. One copy shall be forwarded
within 48 hours, together with a statement of the nature of the property
received, to the chief of police. The second copy shall be forwarded within 48
hours, together with a statement of the nature of the property received, to the
commission of the state police in East Lansing. This section shall not apply to
motor vehicles, old rags, waste paper, books, magazines, tapestries and antique
household furniture.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 5, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-391. - Daily report to police.
   Every licensee under this article shall prepare, in quadruplicate, every
business day before 12:00 noon, on a form to be provided by the Dearborn
Police, a legible and correct copy of the record required by the preceding
section containing the particulars of all purchases and sales the preceding
day, and shall forward this information within 48 hours to the chief of police
and to the commissioner of the state police in East Lansing. If the record of
the transaction form indicates that the customer resides outside the city, the
dealer shall also send a copy of the record of transaction form to the police
agency of the city, village or township in which the customer resides, or if
that city, village or township does not have a police agency, to the sheriff's
department of the county in which the customer resides as set forth on the
record of transaction.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 6, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-392. - Tags to be attached to purchased articles.
   Every licensee under this article shall, at the time of making any purchase,
attach a tag to each article purchased with a number written thereon to
correspond with the entry number recorded in the book described in section
12-389.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 7, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-393. - Certain purchases prohibited.
   No dealer shall purchase any article from a person under the age of 18 years
of age or any person known by the dealer or agent or employee of the dealer to
have been convicted of theft or receipt of stolen property within the preceding
five years, whether the person is acting in his or her own behalf or as the
agent of another.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 8, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-394. - Retention period of articles prior to disposal.
   Every licensee under this article shall retain, on the licensed premises,
each purchased article in its original condition for a period of time
immediately following the purchase. Jewelry, silverware and any type of
precious metals shall be retained by the dealer for nine calendar days after it
was received, without any form of alteration other than that required to make
an accurate appraisal of its value. All other secondhand articles shall be
retained for at least 15 days before disposing of them, in an accessible place
in the building where such articles are purchased and received. This section
shall not apply to old rags, waste paper and household goods except radios,
televisions, cameras, stereos, VCR's, record players and electrical appliances.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 9, 1-5-93)
Sec. 12-395. - Unlawful to permit unlicensed buying or selling on premises.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to knowingly
permit, on premises owned or operated by such person, firm or corporation, the
buying or selling of articles described in section
12-387 unless the persons so engaged in such activity shall first have procured
a license to do so in accordance with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 92-551, § 10, 1-5-93)
Secs. 12-396—12-415. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XII. - TRANSIENT MERCHANTS ***
Sec. 12-416. - Definition.
   For purposes of this article, a transient merchant shall mean any person who
has not paid taxes in the city upon his stock of goods or fixtures, and who
engages in the business of buying or selling any goods, wares or merchandise,
including but not limited to merchandise composed of gold, silver, platinum or
other precious metal, in the city and, for the purpose of carrying on such
business, rents, purchases or occupies premises for exhibition, delivery,
storage or sale of such goods, on a temporary basis. For purposes of this
definition, "temporary" shall mean a period of time less than 90 days in any
one calendar year and shall apply to any merchant who does not maintain a
permanent place of business within the city. No transient merchant shall be
exempted from the provisions of this article by reason of associating himself
temporarily with any local business.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 1, 4-21-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-417. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for a transient merchant to engage in business in the
city without first obtaining a license from the city clerk for such purpose.
The license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 2, 4-21-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 12-418. - Identification of seller; records.
   Every licensee under this article shall, at the time of purchase of any
article described in section
12-416, require the seller of such article to produce a valid state driver's
license or equivalent photographic identification from which the licensee shall
record the name, driver's license number, age, address and personal description
of the seller. The licensee shall record this information together with the
signature of the seller, a detailed description of the article purchased, the
amount paid for each such article and the date and hour of the purchase in a
book which shall at all times be open to inspection by any member of the police
department. Such book shall be substantially bound and of a size not less than
six inches in length and in breadth. All entries in such book shall be in ink,
legibly written and in the English language. No entry in such book shall be
erased, obliterated, altered or defaced. Each entry shall be numbered
consecutively commencing with the number one and shall be initialed by the
licensee.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 3, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-419. - Daily report to police.
   Every licensee purchasing merchandise under this article shall prepare,
every business day before 12:00 noon, on a form to be provided by the police
department, a legible and correct copy of the record required by section
12-418 containing the particulars of all purchases the preceding day, and shall
make such record available to any member of the police department.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 4, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-420. - Identification tags.
   Every licensee under this article shall, at the time of making any purchase,
attach a tag to each article purchased with a number written thereon to
correspond with the entry number recorded in the book described in section
12-418.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 5, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-421. - Purchases from minors.
   No licensee under this article shall purchase any article from a person
under the age of 18 years of age.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 6, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-422. - Retention period.
   Every licensee under this article shall retain, on the licensed premises,
each purchased article in its original condition for a period of time not less
than 96 hours, except for precious items as defined in state law which shall be
kept for nine days, immediately following the purchase.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 7, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-423. - Record at termination of business.
   A licensee under this article who intends to engage in the business of
buying of articles described in section
12-416, in the city, shall be required to deliver to the chief of police or his
designated representative a complete record, as described in section
12-419, no later than 24 hours after such licensee has ceased doing business in
the city. Such licensee shall not sell or otherwise dispose of any purchased
articles until such record has been delivered to the chief or his
representative.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 8, 4-21-81)
Sec. 12-424. - Unlicensed purchases, sales.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the buying or selling of
articles described in section
12-416, unless the persons so engaged in such activity shall first have
procured a license to do so in accordance with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-20, § 9, 4-21-81)
Secs. 12-425—12-445. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XIII. - GASOLINE STATIONS ***
Sec. 12-446. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Full service shall mean the availability of one or more gasoline dispensing
pumps from which an owner, employee or agent of a gasoline service station or
gasoline self service station will dispense gasoline or other motor vehicle
fuel directly into a customer's motor vehicle.
   Gasoline self service station shall mean a gasoline service station which
provides one or more gasoline dispensing pumps which customers are required to
operate themselves in order to fuel such customers' motor vehicles.
   Gasoline service station shall mean any building, structure, lot, premises
or parcel of land where gasoline, lubricating oil or other vehicle fuel are
sold to the public; provided, however, that where any such petroleum products
are sold in factory sealed containers, the seal of which is not broken and the
contents thereof not dispensed on the premises, such products shall not be
regarded as being sold from a gasoline service station and shall not be deemed
to be subject to the regulation of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 1, 6-2-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-447. - License required for stations.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to maintain any gasoline service station
or self-service gasoline station without first having obtained a license to do
so in accordance with the provisions of this article. The license fee for such
stations shall be listed in section
12-6 under the business heading of "motor supply station," and the license
shall indicate whether the service station is authorized to engage in full
service and/or self-service activities. No additional self-service licenses
shall be issued without the prior approval of the city council. The licensee
shall comply with the applicable building, fire and weights and measures code
provisions.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 2, 6-2-81)
Sec. 12-448. - License required for deliveries.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to make deliveries by truck of gasoline
or other vehicle fuel governed by the provisions of this article within the
city without first having obtained a license to do so in accordance with the
provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 2, 6-2-81; Ord. No. 82-213, 6-15-82)
Sec. 12-449. - Application, inspection.
   Application for a self-service license shall be made to the city clerk who
shall immediately refer the application to the city council for approval/denial
of the operation of a self-service motor supply station at the location
requested. The city clerk shall also immediately refer the application to the
fire marshal, building and safety department and weights and measures division
to insure compliance with applicable codes. The city clerk shall issue a self-
service license only after approval by the city council and reports from the
administrative departments indicating compliance with applicable codes.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 2, 6-2-81)
Sec. 12-450. - Smoking, fires prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke or light any fires while
operating any gasoline dispensing pump.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 3, 6-2-81)
Sec. 12-451. - Unlawful to run engine; pump cover required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit the engine of a motor vehicle
to run while such vehicle is being fueled from a gasoline dispensing pump. All
gasoline pumps shall be equipped with a cover on the nozzle designed to reduce
and minimize the escape of gas fumes when pumping gas or other motor fuel.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 4, 6-2-81)
Sec. 12-452. - Signs.
   (a)   Every person who maintains a gasoline service station abutting or
adjacent to a street or highway, and advertises any grade of gasoline or other
motor fuel, shall post, or cause to be posted or displayed, maintain and keep
current at the station signs, which are clearly visible from all traffic lanes
in each direction on such street or highway, and each sign shall accurately
indicate thereon the actual price per gallon, including all taxes and minimum
and maximum limits, if any of the grade of gasoline and the method of service
which will be sold at such station to any one purchaser at any one time for use
in a motor vehicle.
   (b)   Whenever any gasoline service station has more than one method of
pricing, such as full service and self-service or full service and mini-
service, or any such combination, by any name, the islands or pumps where each
particular method of pricing is being used shall be identified as such: full
service, self-service, mini-service or any such name.
   (c)   No changes shall be made in the actual price per gallon including all
taxes and minimum and maximum limits, if any, at which each grade of gasoline
or other motor fuel is to be sold, without such change or changes being first
shown on such posted sign. Posted prices shall be identical to pump prices.
   (d)   Each sign posted pursuant to the requirements of this section shall
not be inconsistent with the provisions of the sign ordinance.
   (e)   Each and all letters, words, figures and numerals used on any such
sign shall be uniform in size and clearly visible.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 5, 6-2-81; Ord. No. 82-213, 6-15-82)
Sec. 12-453. - Flammable liquids regulations; MIOSHA; fire blanket.
   (a)   Every gasoline service station and gasoline self-service station shall
comply with all applicable provisions of the Michigan Flammable Liquids
Regulations Promulgated by Authority of Act No. 207 of the Public Acts of 1941,
as amended, specifically but not limited to Rule 110 of such regulations, as
well as any applicable standards promulgated under the Michigan Occupational
and Safety Hazards Act.
   (b)   Every gasoline service station and gasoline self-service station shall
be equipped with at least one fire blanket installed at a location or locations
to be designated by the fire chief or his authorized representative.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 6, 6-2-81)
Sec. 12-454. - Emergency controls.
   Every gasoline self-service station shall install approved emergency
controls at a location no more than 100 feet from a dispenser. The attendant or
supervisor shall remain within arms length of the emergency controls during the
dispensing of a Class I liquid. All dispenser-metered computations shall be
legible from the emergency controls position, or duplicate readings shall be
provided by approved equipment installed at the emergency controls position.
(Ord. No. 81-26, § 6, 6-2-81; Ord. No. 82-213, 6-15-82)
Sec. 12-455. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 06-1083, adopted June 12, 2006, repealed §
12-455 in its entirety. Former §
12-455 pertained to Air and derived from Ord. No. 81-26, § 7, adopted June 2,
1981.
Secs. 12-456—12-475. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XIV. - AMUSEMENTS AND ENTERTAINMENTS[3]  ***
Footnotes:
--- (3) ---
State Law reference— Crimes relating to public exhibitions and entertainments,
MCL 750.463 et seq., MSA 28.718 et seq.
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 12-476. - License required.
   No person shall exhibit or maintain in the city any circus, menagerie, play,
game or theatrical exhibit; or give any concert, vocal or instrumental,
lecture, sermon, speech or debate; or exhibit any natural or artificial
curiosity or give a show of any kind for which pay is demanded, received or
collected until a license therefor has been obtained from the city council.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-477. - Exceptions.
   This article shall not extend to any exhibition by the pupils of any private
or public school; to any musical entertainment given by the members and for the
benefit of any resident musical society; to any exhibition of painting,
engraving, sculpture or fine art, executed by a citizen of the city; to any
concert or musical entertainment, fair, festival or lecture for the benefit of
any church or benevolent object; to any game of cricket, lacrosse, football; to
any exhibit of archery; or to any race, contest of military exhibition given or
managed by any resident association, club or company.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-478. - Application for licenses.
   Applications for licenses shall be filed with the city clerk for
presentation to the council. Applications shall set forth the full name of the
applicant and of every person interested in the issue of the license applied
for, together with the business and residence addresses of such persons. If the
applicant shall be a corporation, this provision shall apply to the officers
and directors of such corporation only. Such application shall also set forth
the place or places where it is proposed to establish, maintain or operate the
amusement for which a license is asked and the number of amusements to be so
established, maintained or operated.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-479. - Council consideration.
   The city clerk shall keep a record of all applications and the action taken
thereon by the council in a book to be provided for the purpose by the council,
and shall present all applications at the next meeting of the council after
they shall have been filed with him. If the council, upon examination of the
matter, shall deem the issuing of a license consistent with the safety and good
government of the city and the welfare of its inhabitants, the clerk may be
directed to issue the license upon the payment of the fee or fees provided for
in section
12-480.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-480. - License fee.
   Before any license shall be issued under the terms of this article, the
applicant or applicants shall pay to the city treasurer a license fee for
establishing, maintaining or operating such exhibitions or entertainments, as
prescribed in section
12-6 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-481. - Disorderly conduct.
   No person or company receiving a license under this article shall permit any
disorderly conduct or the use of any immoral, profane, or indecent language, or
permit such place of amusement or exhibition to become and be a place of resort
of thieves, prostitutes or other disorderly persons.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-482. - Street carnivals restricted.
   No person shall conduct or cause to be conducted in the city any so-called
"street carnival," unless the same is composed of local talent and operated by
local fraternities, groups or clubs. In no event shall any street carnival be
permitted to operate within the limits of the city unless a petition requesting
the same is first filed with the city clerk, signed by at least 51 percent of
the people living within a radius of 500 feet of the location proposed to be
used for such street carnival. The word "people" in this article is defined to
mean any person of the age of 21 years and upwards.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-483. - Permit required.
   No person shall conduct or cause to be conducted in the city any
entertainment or amusement whether the same is sponsored, operated by or
conducted under the auspices of local fraternities, religious groups, societies
or clubs or composed of local talent, unless application is made to and a
permit therefor obtained from the city council.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 9.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-484. - Application for permit.
   Before any permit shall be issued by the council for the conduct of any
entertainment or amusement, an application shall be made which shall fully and
completely give the following information, which shall be sworn to by an
authorized person as true and correct in every detail:
      (1)   A sketch shall be prepared and submitted showing the proposed
premises to be occupied; the lay-out of the carnival or amusements with respect
to location of amusements, concessions and devices; and space or spaces to be
occupied by the public and operators of such amusements and devices; all fire
extinguisher locations, type and size of fire escapes and exits and entrances,
all of which shall be approved by the chief of fire department before such
entertainment is opened for public admission. Failure to maintain fire exits
and extinguishers in a safe and workable condition at all times will be
sufficient grounds for the chief of the fire department to close such amusement
or entertainment.
      (2)   The name and description of the operation and conduct of the game,
device or amusement in such entertainment or amusement shall be specifically
enumerated in detail, together with the number, type, or variation of such
games, devices or amusements, as hereinbefore defined, and the prizes, gifts,
or rewards, if any, to be distributed.
      (3)   The percentage of profits and division of cost of operating such
carnival, where the same is conducted by persons skilled in the conduct of such
entertainments or amusements, or operating the same for hire or a percentage of
profits thereof, shall be given with the names and addresses of such persons.
      (4)   Each applicant for a permit, at least 30 days prior to the issuance
of such permit, as herein provided for, shall submit a full and complete list
of all towns, cities and villages, together with the names and addresses of any
person under whose auspices such carnival and/or amusement was sponsored and
operated during the period of two years next preceding the date of making such
application.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 9.2, 11-4-81)
