Sec. 12-485. - Approval of sanitary facilities.
   Where food and/or beverages of any description are to be dispensed in
conjunction with the operation of such entertainment or amusement, the
approval, in writing, of the department of health shall be obtained as to the
proposed sanitary facilities to be furnished in the dispensing and handling of
all such foods or beverages.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 9.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-486. - Approval of electrical fixtures and wiring.
   Before and at any time during the operation of any enterprise or undertaking
coming under this article, all electrical fixtures and wiring, where
temporarily installed for the particular amusement or entertainment, shall be
inspected and approved by the electrical inspector, and if found improper, the
same shall be remedied forthwith. Failure to so comply shall cause a revocation
of such license.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 9.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-487. - Authority of commission of safety.
   All amusements coming under this article shall be at all times subject to
the inspection and proper control of the commission of safety and shall comply
with any orders issued by the commission of safety intended to protect life and
property from fire hazards.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-488. - Expiration of license.
   All annual licenses granted under this division shall expire on the first
Tuesday in May after the date of their issuance.
(Ord. No. 81-56, § 11, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-489—12-500. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - AMUSEMENT DEVICES **
Sec. 12-501. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this division is for the preservation of the public peace,
health, safety and welfare as it is necessary to regulate amusement devices, as
the use and placement of such devices in the city is increasing in a manner
which will, absent regulation, have an adverse impact on the city.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 1, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-502. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Amusement device shall mean any machine or contrivance which, upon the
insertion of a coin, slug, token, plate or disc, or the payment of a price, may
be operated by the public generally for use as a game, entertainment or
amusement, whether or not registering a score and whether operated by hand,
electricity or any other form of power. It shall include such devices as marble
machines, pinball machines, skill ball machines, mechanical grab machines,
coin-operated bowling alleys, shuffleboard game machines or devices, whether
played with discs, weights, pucks or balls, mechanical guns, coin-operated
motion picture machines, any so-called claw, crane or digger machine,
electronic video devices or any other games, devices, operations or
transactions similar thereto, under whatever name they may be indicted, which,
when operated, do not deliver as a result of the application of an element of
chance, any money or property, or by the operation of which a person may not be
entitled to receive as a result of the application of an element of chance, any
money or property. It shall not include any machine or mechanical device
designed or manufactured primarily for use at a race track in connection with
pari-mutuel betting and shall not include billiard or pool tables.
   Distributor shall mean any person who owns or has control of any amusement
device and who contracts or permits any such amusement device to be installed
or operated in other than his own place of business.
   Exhibitor shall mean any person who operates a business establishment and
displays for public patronage or keeps for operation therein, either as lessee,
bailee, owner or otherwise, three or more amusement devices.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 2, 3-16-82; Ord. No. 06-1109, 12-4-06)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-503. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or cause to be operated, or
to carry on, in the city, any of the business activities of an exhibitor or
distributor without first having obtained a license in conformance with the
regulations set forth in this division. It shall be further unlawful for any
exhibitor to operate, or cause to be operated, any amusement device without
obtaining a license for each such device.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 3, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-504. - Application for license.
   Each person desiring to exhibit or distribute any amusement device shall
first make application to the city clerk for a license therefor. Such
applications shall contain the following information:
      (1)   Generally: 
         a.   The name and address of the applicant, if an individual,
including the street and number, together with the date and place of birth; if
a copartnership, the names and addresses including street and number, of such
copartners and their respective dates and places of birth; if a corporation or
voluntary association, the names and addresses, including street and number, of
the several officers and resident agent thereof, and their respective dates and
places of birth.
         b.   Kind of license being applied for, whether as exhibitor or
distributor, or for one or more amusement devices.
         c.   List any prior convictions for violations of any ordinances or
statutes of any kind by the applicant, if an individual, by any of the
copartners of a copartnership, or by the officers, if a corporation, setting
forth the name of the court, the charge, and the date of conviction, if any.
         d.   The fingerprints of the applicant and if the applicant is a
copartnership, corporation or association, the application shall be accompanied
by the fingerprints of the officers of such copartnership, corporation or
association.
         e.   Application shall be sworn to by the person signing it.
         f.   If the person signing the application does so in a representative
capacity, indicate what that capacity is.
      (2)   Distributor. In addition to the requirements of subsection (1) of
this section, a person applying for a distributor license shall provide the
address, including street and number, from which the applicant's business is
conducted, and type of business, whether rentals or sales of amusement devices,
or both.
      (3)   Exhibitor. In addition to the requirements of subsection (1) of
this section, a person applying for an exhibitor's license shall provide:
         a.   Each location where an amusement device is to be displayed or
operated and the type of business conducted at such location.
         b.   The total number of amusement devices.
         c.   A statement whether the devices are owned by applicant, rented or
being purchased on contract. If rented, the name of the owner shall be shown,
or if being purchased on contract or owned, the name and address of seller.
         d.   A floor plan drawing of the location showing all exits and the
proposed location of each amusement device.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 4(a—c), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-505. - Minimum age of applicant.
   No license shall be issued under this division to any applicant unless the
applicant is 21 years of age or older.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 4(d), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-506. - Approval of application.
   Every application for license required by this division shall be referred by
the city clerk to the departments hereinafter set forth. No license shall be
issued by the city clerk until each such department investigation and approval
has been received.
      (1)   Police department. The police department shall cause an
investigation to be made as to the character of the applicant, the officers of
the club, society or corporation, the persons who are to have general
management of the business and of the type of amusement devices to be used. The
applicant shall be rejected if the police department shall find any of the
persons named in the applications not of good moral character, as defined in
section
12-4 of this chapter; that any of such persons have previously been connected
with any amusement device operation where the license has been revoked; where
any of the provisions of this division or any other city ordinance with
reference to amusement devices have been violated, or if the premises in which
the amusement devices are to be operated do not conform in every way with the
regulations, ordinances and rules applicable thereto. No application shall be
approved until the types of amusement devices to be used are approved by the
police department.
      (2)   Fire department. The fire department shall cause an investigation
to be made of the premises where an amusement device is to be operated to
determine whether or not such premises and any electrical equipment proposed to
be used therein comply with all of the fire codes, ordinances and rules and
regulations of the city, and the application shall be rejected if the fire
department shall find any existing violation or threat of a probable future
violation of any such code, ordinance, rule or regulation.
      (3)   Building and safety department. The building and safety department
shall cause an investigation to be made of the premises where an amusement
device is to be operated to determine whether or not the building involved
meets all of the requirements of the building code and other applicable city
ordinances, whether or not the proposed use is a permissible one under the
provisions of the zoning ordinance of the city, whether or not the off-street
parking requirements of the zoning ordinance and other applicable city
ordinances are met, and the application shall be rejected if the building
department shall find that the proposed use violates any of the provisions of
the building code, the zoning ordinance or any other applicable city ordinance.
      (4)   Treasurer. A certificate indicating that all personal property
taxes levied and assessed against the applicant for licenses have been paid in
full.
      (5)   In addition to the requirements of subsections (1) through (4) of
this section, the city clerk shall refer any application for an amusement
device to the city council. Such referral shall take place only after receipt
of all reports pursuant to subsections (1) through (4) of this section. In
granting or denying the application, the council shall consider the following:
         a.   Will the proposed use alter the surrounding business area or its
environment?
         b.   Will the proposed use adversely affect the quiet enjoyment of the
property in the immediate area?
         c.   Will the proposed use adversely affect traffic conditions so as
to create a nuisance?
         d.   Will the proposed use create a safety hazard for individuals in
the surrounding area?
         e.   Will the proposed use be in violation of any city ordinance?
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 5, 3-16-82; Ord. No. 82-234, 6-15-82)
Sec. 12-507. - License fees.
   The annual license fee for an exhibitor or distributor shall be as
prescribed by section
12-6, as amended. In addition there shall be an annual fee for each amusement
device operated or caused to be operated by any exhibitor, as prescribed by
section
12-6, as amended. No license shall be issued until the proper fee has been paid
to the city.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 6, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-508. - Display.
   Every license granted under this division shall be displayed at all times by
the licensee in a conspicuous place in the premises. Every device required to
be licensed under this division shall contain thereon legible identifying data
showing the name and address of the distributor if the device is not owned by
the exhibitor.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 7, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-509. - Nontransferable.
   Any license issued under this division shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 7, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-510. - Expiration of license.
   All licenses granted under the provisions of this division shall expire on
December 1 of each year.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 7, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-511. - Enforcing officers; inspection.
   The police department, the department of building and safety and/or other
city departments for the purpose of enforcing this division or any other
ordinance relating to the health, safety and welfare of the public shall have
the right to enter the place of business of any licensee under this division at
any reasonable hour for the purpose of making an inspection and survey of the
premises and the equipment therein. It shall be unlawful for any person to
resist or attempt to prevent any of the above named officers or employees from
carrying out the purposes herein set forth.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 8, 3-16-82; Ord. No. 06-1109, 12-4-06)
Sec. 12-512. - Automatic revocation of license.
   If any licensee, owner or agent, servant or employee thereof, is convicted
of a violation of this division, the license of the amusement device, exhibitor
or distributor on or about which the violation occurred shall be automatically
revoked forthwith. Any license so revoked shall not be reissued to the same
person for a period of one year from the date of revocation.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 9, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-513. - Gambling devices.
   Nothing in this division shall in any way be construed to authorize, license
or permit any gambling devices whatsoever, or any mechanism that has been
judicially determined to be a gambling device, or in any way contrary to law.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(a), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-514. - Giving of prizes, awards, etc.; gambling prohibited.
   No person by himself, another or otherwise, shall give any prize, award,
merchandise, gift or anything of value to any player or any operator of any
such amusement device or to any contestant for any score made on such device,
or by any reason of the playing of such amusement device; provided that
trophies and scholarships may be awarded to players or teams for league or
tournament play. No form of gambling shall be permitted in connection with the
operation of any amusement device.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(b), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-515. - Hours of operation.
   No person shall operate or cause to be operated in the city any amusement
device between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. of the official time of the
city.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(c), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-516. - Use of devices by minors.
   No person shall permit any amusement device regulated by this division to be
played, in any commercial establishment, by any minor under the age of 16
years, except when such minor shall be accompanied by his parent or legal
guardian.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(c), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-517. - Conduct on premises.
   (a)   No person, licensee, owner or operator of any amusement device or any
servant, agent or employee of a licensee or owner of an amusement device shall
permit upon the premises housing an amusement device:
      (1)   Any indecent, illegal or profane language, or indecent, illegal or
disorderly conduct, or to become a resort for disorderly persons of any type.
      (2)   Gambling or the use, possession or presence of gambling
paraphernalia on the premises.
      (3)   Intoxicated persons to loiter on the premises.
      (4)   The possession or use of any alcoholic liquor on the premises, nor
shall the licensed premises be accessible in any way with any place where
alcoholic liquor is kept, sold, distributed or given away. This prohibition
shall not apply while a state liquor control commission license is in effect at
the licensed premises.
      (5)   The possession or use of any drug, narcotic or controlled
substance, including marijuana on the premises.
      (6)   Noise or music to emanate from the licensed premises which is
disturbing to the surrounding areas.
      (7)   Acceptance or receipt of anything of value other than cash as
consideration for the use or operation of any amusement device on the licensed
premises.
   (b)   Any licensee, owner or servant, agent or employee thereof shall
presumptively be deemed to have permitted the conduct enumerated above if it
occurs on the premises housing an amusement device.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(d), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-518. - Supervision of use of devices.
   No amusement device shall be operated, caused to be operated or played
unless a person 21 years of age or older is present and in control of the
premises.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(e), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-519. - Security required.
   (a)   In addition to the regulations set forth in sections
12-513 through
12-518, a location consisting of ten or more, but less than 20 amusement
devices shall not be open for business between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 2:00
a.m. on weekdays and all hours of operation of Saturday, Sunday and holidays
without an adult supervisor, 21 years of age or older, present on the premises.
This supervision is in addition to the one required by section
12-518.
   (b)   If the location consists of 20 or more amusement devices, then a
licensed security guard shall be employed, and on the premises, in addition to
the two adult supervisors, during the hours mentioned in subsection (a) of this
section. An additional licensed security guard and adult supervisor shall be
required for each additional increment of 15 amusement devices over 20.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 10(f), 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-520. - Confiscation of unlawful devices.
   Any machine, apparatus, contrivance or device, which shall have been made
use of in violation of the terms of this division, may be seized and destroyed
in compliance with the terms and provisions of the statutes of the state
relating to gambling devices; provided, however, the owner may reclaim such
device upon payment of any fees owing plus $50.00 for cost of confiscation.
However, property taken for violation of gambling laws may not be returned to
the owner except by court order.
(Ord. No. 82-212, § 11, 3-16-82)
Sec. 12-521. - Reserved.
Editor's note— The provisions of §
12-521, which pertained to location restrictions, has been deleted as being
superseded by the provisions of the zoning ordinance, which is on file in the
offices of the city.
Secs. 12-522—12-530. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - BOWLING ALLEYS, POOL HALLS **
Sec. 12-531. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Billiard room shall mean a room or rooms wherein the several games are
played on a table known as a billiard or pool table, surrounded by an elastic
ledge or cushion, with or without pockets, with balls which are driven by a cue
and which shall include all forms of the game known as carom billiards, pocket
billiards, three cushion billiards and English billiards, as well as all other
games played on a billiard table, and shall include the games known as 15-ball
pool, eight-ball pool, bottle pool, pea-pool and all other games played on a
so-called pool table and all games played on a so-called pigeon-hole table.
   Room containing bowling alleys shall mean a place or room where any of the
several games are played on a wooden surface or alley where balls are thrown or
rolled by hand along a lane towards wooden pins, and shall include all forms of
the game known as ten pins, nine pins, duck pins or any other game played with
wooden pins and balls rolled in lanes.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 2, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-532. - Enforcement.
   (a)   The health officer or his authorized representative shall enforce the
provisions of this division which relate to the public health, and the police
department shall enforce all other provisions of this division, except those
expressly assigned to some other department to enforce. The department of
public works shall enforce all the ordinances of the city involving such
licensed premises, which it is authorized to enforce.
   (b)   All officers or employees of the city who are charged with the
enforcement of this division shall at all reasonable times have access to every
part of the premises licensed under this division.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-533. - License required.
   No person shall open or cause to be opened, or conduct, maintain, establish
or operate any commercial billiard room, or room containing bowling alleys
within the city, without first having obtained a license therefor; provided,
however, that this division shall not apply to or control private residences,
schools, churches, fraternal societies or municipal institutions.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-534. - Application for license.
   (a)   Each person desiring to open or maintain a commercial billiard room or
room containing bowling alleys shall first make application for a license to
carry on such activity. Such application shall be filed with the city clerk,
and, upon the filing thereof the applicant shall pay an annual license fee, as
prescribed in section
12-6. Upon receipt of such application, it shall be referred to the police
department, department of health, and the department of building and safety for
investigation and report.
   (b)   The application for the license shall contain the full name and
residence address of the applicant, if he is a single owner; or if a
copartnership, the names and residence addresses of all of the copartners; or
if a society, club, firm, association or corporation, the full names and
residence addresses of all of the principal officers of such applicant. If the
applicant is a corporation, the application shall further show the state in
which such corporation was organized. If the applicant is a society, club,
firm, or copartnership, association or corporation, the application shall
further designate the name and residence address of its manager or the person
who will be in charge of such billiard room or room containing bowling alleys.
   (c)   Before the police department will issue a license for a commercial
billiard room, the applicant, if an individual owner; all of the copartners, if
a copartnership; or all of the principal officers, including the manager, if
the applicant is a society, club, firm, association, copartnership or
corporation, shall submit and file their individual fingerprints with the
police department.
   (d)   The application shall further set forth:
      (1)   The street address where such commercial billiard room or room
containing bowling alleys is to be conducted, indicating whether such room is
in the basement, the ground floor, or the number of the floor above the ground
level, the number of rooms to be used, and the approximate floor area of such
room or rooms.
      (2)   The age of the applicant, if an individual, and the respective ages
of the copartners, if a copartnership, or of the officers and manager, if a
society, club, firm, association or corporation.
      (3)   Whether the applicant, owners or officers, including the manager,
are citizens of the United States or have declared their intention to become
citizens.
      (4)   Whether the applicant, if an individual, or if a copartnership, the
copartners, or if a society, club, firm, association or corporation, the
principal officers, including the manager, has ever been engaged in operating a
billiard room or room containing bowling alleys; and if so, when, where and how
long in each place within the last five years prior to filing such application;
and whether or not the applicant or any of its officers or manager has ever had
a license to operate a billiard room or room containing bowling alleys
suspended or revoked; and if so, when, where and who had such experience.
      (5)   Whether the applicant, if an individual, or the copartners, if a
copartnership, or any officers of the abovenamed groups, including the manager,
has ever been convicted of violating any ordinance of the city or of any other
city in the United States, or convicted of violating any law of the state or
any other state in the United States, or of any law of the United States of
America; and if so, when, what law and where.
      (6)   The name of the owner of the premises in which such commercial
billiard room or room containing bowling alleys is located, and the residence
address of such owner.
      (7)   The application shall be signed by the applicant, if an individual,
or by all of the copartners, if a copartnership, or by all of the officers, if
the applicant is a society, club, firm, association or corporation, together
with the signatures of the manager thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-535. - Investigation of applicant.
   (a)   The city clerk, upon receipt of the application and petition for a
license required by this division, shall refer them to the police department,
department of building and safety, the department of health, the fire
department, and the treasurer for investigation of the facts therein set forth.
If any of such departments upon investigation find that any of the facts
therein set forth have been misrepresented, falsified or only partially set
forth where a more detailed statement should have been made in order to give a
full and complete answer to the questions in such application, the application
shall be denied forthwith.
   (b)   The department of health shall also make an investigation of the
premises proposed to be licensed as to the cleanliness and suitability thereof
for the use requested by the applicant, and, if such premises comply with all
of the provisions of the several ordinances of the city, the laws of the state
and of the United States, relative to public health and are otherwise suitable,
the department of health shall approve such application for the issuance of a
license.
   (c)   The department of building and safety in its investigation shall
determine if all of the city ordinances enforced by its department are being
complied with before it shall approve such application.
   (d)   If such departments shall find all of the facts in such application to
be correct and the questions completely answered, and shall find that the
applicant or the officers and manager of such applicant are persons of good
moral character and are complying with all of the laws and ordinances of the
city, the state and of the United States, such departments shall approve the
issuing of such license and shall forward such approval to the city clerk, who
will issue such license; provided, however, that no license or renewal thereof
shall be issued to any person under this division unless and until a
certificate has been obtained from the city treasurer to the effect that all
personal property taxes levied and assessed against such applicant for license
have been paid in full.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-536. - Location restricted.
   No license to operate a commercial billiard room shall be issued for a
location within 500 feet of any church or school, and no license to operate a
commercial bowling alley shall be issued for a location within 300 feet of a
church or school.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-537. - Periodic inspection.
   It shall be the duty of the police department, the department of building
and safety and the department of health, together with their authorized
officers and employees, to visit any and all commercial billiard rooms and
rooms containing bowling alleys as frequently as may be necessary for the
purpose of investigating such premises to determine that all of the provisions
of city ordinances, the state and national laws are complied with.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-538. - Nontransferable.
   Each license issued under this division shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-539. - Display.
   Every license issued under this division shall be conspicuously displayed at
all times by the licensee inside and near the front entrance of such premises.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-540. - Expiration.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this division shall expire one
year from application unless sooner terminated by operation of law.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-541. - Renewal.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this article may be renewed upon
filing the application and paying the license fee as specified in section
12-6 for the original license.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-542. - Hours of operation.
   (a)   No licensee shall operate or cause to be operated in the city any
commercial billiard room or any room where billiard tables are kept, between
the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., except on the day preceding a legal
holiday when the prohibited hours shall be between 1:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. No
licensee shall operate or cause to be operated in the city any room containing
bowling alleys between the hours of 3:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. No licensee shall
harbor or permit any person, except regular employees who are performing the
necessary work within the premises, to be or remain in any such licensed room
or place any day of the week or times during which such licensed premises are
prohibited from operation.
   (b)   The foregoing hours shall apply to the operations licensed under this
division, even though a restaurant, licensed beverage place, cafe or other
place of business might be operating in conjunction with such licensed billiard
room or room containing bowling alleys or might be located in the same building
with such licensed billiard room or room containing bowling alleys.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-543. - Presence of minors.
   No person shall be permitted to play billiards in any commercial billiard
parlor, or to be or remain in such parlor for any purpose whatsoever, if he is
under the age of 14 years, unless accompanied by a parent or guardian. It shall
be unlawful for any person to misrepresent himself or herself to have reached
the age of 14 years in order to obtain admittance to such commercial billiard
parlor. It is hereby made the duty of all proprietors, owners, managers,
licensees or anyone connected with the licensed business of operating or
maintaining any commercial billiard parlor to ascertain the correct age of any
person subject to regulation by this section. A violation by a licensee of this
requirement shall be the basis for a suspension and revocation of his license.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-544. - Certain games prohibited.
   No dice shall be thrown, no pea ball or shake ball shall be used, and no
cards, raffles or other games of chance or other form of gambling shall be
permitted in any licensed billiard room or room containing bowling alleys in
the city, or in any room in which billiard tables are located, or at any cigar
stand or any other place in which any business licensed under this division is
carried on, whether or not such room is divided by a partition.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-545. - Prizes, rewards restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for any checks to be given which can be redeemed for
merchandise or cash; provided, however, such prohibition shall not be construed
to prevent the giving of cash or merchandise as prizes to billiard players or
to bowlers in tournament, league or any other competitive play.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-546. - Obstruction, access.
   (a)   No screens or other obstructions shall be placed in the doors or
windows of any licensed billiard room or room containing bowling alleys, but
all such doors and windows must at all times be kept free and clear of screens
or other obstructions so as to permit an unobstructed view into such billiard
room or bowling alley from the street.
   (b)   Both front and rear doors of all rooms where the operations licensed
under this division are carried on shall be kept unlocked at all times while
such licensed operations are being carried on.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-547. - Certain persons prohibited.
   After a warning given by any member of the police department, it shall be
unlawful for a licensee under this division to allow or permit any known or
reputed gambler, racketeer, narcotic addict, hoodlum, police character or
habitual drunkard to frequent or loiter in the licensed premises.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-548. - Use of rooms restricted.
   It shall be unlawful for the licensee to use or occupy any other room or
space in any building for the purpose of carrying on the commercial billiard or
bowling alley business, except that room or space specified in the application
for license.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-549. - Suspension and revocation.
   (a)   The license authorized to be issued under this division may be
suspended by the chief of police, the director of the department of public
works, or by the health officer for falsifying as to, or misrepresenting, any
statements made in the application therefor, or for concealing any facts by
failing to answer fully any questions in the application, or for violating any
of the provisions of this division or any other ordinances of the city or any
laws of the state or of the United States of America. If such license is
suspended, the license and evidence thereof shall be surrendered by the
licensee and shall be held by the suspending officer until the final
disposition is made of such suspension.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for the licensee or anyone working in his behalf
to operate or conduct any business governed by this division in the billiard
room or room containing bowling alleys while such suspension continues to
exist.
   (c)   In connection with the notice of suspension, a statement in writing
shall be prepared by the suspending officer, setting forth specifically the
charges or grounds for which the license was suspended and the facts on which
such suspension is based, and such statement shall be served on the licensee or
the person in charge of the licensed premises at the same time the notice of
suspension is served.
   (d)   Immediately upon such suspension, the suspending officer shall give a
notice in writing to the licensee or to any person in charge of the licensee's
business at the address designated in the license that a hearing will be held
before the city council at such time and place stated in the notice not less
than three days and not more than ten days from the date of such suspension, at
which time the cause of such suspension shall be investigated by the council to
determine if the basis for the suspension exists. If the council finds that the
cause of suspension is established by the facts, the license shall be revoked
forthwith, but if the cause of suspension is not established by the evidence
submitted, the license shall be reinstated.
   (e)   If a license issued under this division is revoked, such person and
all persons officially connected with such license shall be ineligible to
obtain another billiard room and bowling alley license in the city for a period
of three years from the date of such revocation.
   (f)   It shall be unlawful for any person, either as owner or part owner,
whose license issued under this division has been suspended or revoked, to
operate or work in a billiard room or bowling alley during the period of
suspension or revocation or when such person is ineligible to obtain a license.
(Ord. No. 81-79, § 10, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-550—12-560. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 4. - CARNIVALS AND CIRCUSES **
Sec. 12-561. - Definition.
   For the purpose of this division, the words "carnival" or "circus" shall
mean a transient outdoor show or exhibition in which or in connection with
which are conducted or permitted games of chance or skill, wherein goods are
given or awarded to persons paying a consideration for a chance or opportunity
to win or secure the same as a prize or award, or where concession stands or
amusement stands are operated or maintained and/or ferris wheels, merry-go-
rounds and other similar mechanical amusement rides are operated and/or live
performances are staged by people or animals.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 2, 4-20-82)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-562. - License required.
   No person shall establish, sponsor, operate or conduct a carnival or circus
within the boundaries of the city without obtaining a license in accord with
the provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 1, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-563. - Application.
   The prospective licensee under this division shall submit a written
statement indicating that he desires to operate a carnival or circus within the
city, the proposed location, a brief description of the scope of activities,
the number of days involved in the proposed carnival or circus activities and
the name, address and phone number of the applicant. Such written statement
together with the required license fee, grounds cleanup deposit and proof of
insurance shall constitute the application for a license to establish and
operate a carnival or circus within the city.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 3, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-564. - License fee.
   The license fee for the operation of a carnival or circus within the city
shall be established by section
12-6.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 4, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-565. - Liability insurance.
   The applicant for a license under this division shall be required to provide
proof of having procured a liability insurance policy in an amount not less
than $1,000,000.00 covering the proposed activities and naming the city as
being an insured party under such policy.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 5, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-566. - Grounds cleanup deposit.
   The applicant for a license under this division shall be required to deposit
the sum of $1,000.00 for purposes of insuring the proper cleanup of the area
set aside for purposes of conducting the carnival or circus. No portion of such
deposit shall be returned to the applicant until the director of public works
certifies that the licensee has properly cleaned up and cleared the area in
which the carnival or circus was conducted.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 6, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-567. - Waiver of fee, deposit.
   The city council may waive the license fee and/or the grounds cleanup
deposit required by this division upon a request for such a waiver by the
applicant and after consideration of the following factors:
      (1)   The nonprofit or charitable status of the applicant.
      (2)   The availability of a locally designated representative to insure
property cleanup.
      (3)   Proof of satisfactory performance of cleanup activities by the
applicant in previous years.
      (4)   Whatever is determined to be in the best interests of the city.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 7, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-568. - Issuance; term.
   The license to operate a carnival or circus within the city may only be
issued pursuant to a majority vote of the city council, after a hearing at
which it shall be the burden of the prospective licensee to show that the
operation of the proposed carnival or circus will not unduly disrupt the
surrounding neighborhood in any manner. Any license issued for purposes of
conducting a carnival or circus shall be valid for not more than 30 days.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 3, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-569. - Awards and prizes.
   No awards, prizes, money or property of any nature shall be delivered
directly or indirectly to any person at a carnival or circus unless in strict
conformity with the requirements of state law.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 8, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-570. - Security guard required.
   A carnival or circus shall not be open for business without a licensed
security guard on the premises.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 9, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-571. - Hours of operation.
   No carnival or circus shall be open for business between the hours of 2:00
a.m. and 7:00 a.m.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 9, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-572. - Approval of sanitary facilities.
   Where food and/or beverages of any description are to be dispensed in
conjunction with the operation of a carnival or circus, the approval of the
department of health shall be obtained as to the proposed facilities to be
furnished in the dispensing and handling of all such foods or beverages.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 10, 4-20-82)
Sec. 12-573. - Approval of electrical fixtures and wiring.
   Before and at any time during the operation of a carnival or circus, all
electrical fixtures and wiring, where temporarily installed shall be inspected
and approved by the electrical inspector of the department of building and
safety, and if found improper, the same shall be remedied forthwith. Failure to
so comply shall cause a revocation of such license.
(Ord. No. 82-227, § 11, 4-20-82)
Secs. 12-574—12-585. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 5. - DRIVE-IN THEATERS **
Sec. 12-586. - Definitions.
   For the purposes of this division, the phrase "drive-in theater" shall mean
an open-air theater operated in an established location with or without cover
or roof, displaying or showing moving pictures or giving theatrical
performances for the general public who view the screen or stage while seated
in automobiles or other vehicles. It shall not mean a moving picture theater
established in an enclosed building where seats are provided for the patrons
thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 11-1331, 6-20-11)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-587. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a drive-in theater in the
city without first having obtained a license therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-588. - Application.
   Application for a license required by this division shall be made to the
clerk and shall be made in the name of the person owning or having a part
interest in the drive-in theater to be licensed. It shall also show the
residence addresses of all such owners. If the applicant is a corporation, the
application shall state the names and residence addresses of the officers and
resident agent of the corporation. Each application shall set forth the
location where the applicant proposes to operate a drive-in theater or where
such theater is being operated. It shall also state the name and residence
address of the manager or person in charge of such theater and shall give the
number of cars which such proposed theater is designed to accommodate.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-589. - Investigation.
   (a)   The application for a license required by this division to operate a
drive-in theater shall be referred to the police department, fire department,
department of building and safety, and department of health of the city for an
investigation and report.
   (b)   The police department shall investigate the reputation of the
applicant and its officers, especially with reference to their record of
possible law and ordinance violation. As a condition precedent to the annual
recommending of a license by the police department, the applicant, if an
individual, or if a copartnership, all of the copartners, or if a corporation,
all of the officers and the resident agent thereof, shall file their respective
fingerprints with the police department of the city.
   (c)   The department of building and safety shall investigate as to zoning
compliance and character of the district proposed to be used for the outdoor
theater, and shall see that all ordinances and laws applicable to such business
are enforced which such department is authorized to enforce.
   (d)   The department of health shall investigate as to the sanitary
facilities and health conditions at the location of the proposed or existing
theater and shall enforce all laws and ordinances applicable to such business
which it is authorized to enforce.
   (e)   The fire department shall investigate the need for safety and fire
prevention equipment and the existence of any possible fire hazards, and shall
enforce all laws and ordinances applicable to such business which it is
authorized to enforce.
   (f)   The various departments shall make their reports resulting from such
investigations, together with their recommendations and file the same with the
clerk. No department of the city shall recommend the issuing of a license if
any law or ordinance of the city is being violated by the applicant or if the
applicant is permitting a nuisance to exist on the premises or any conditions
to exist which endanger or are detrimental to the public health, safety, morals
or welfare.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-590. - Action by council.
   The clerk shall submit the application for a license under this division
with the recommendations of the various departments to the city council at its
next regular meeting for the purpose of approving or disapproving the issuance
of such license. If the council approves the issuance of such license, the
clerk shall issue a license. The council shall consider the several
recommendations of the various departments and shall have the power to approve
the issuance of a license contrary to the recommendation of any department.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-591. - Fees.
   Upon the filing of the application for license under this division, the
license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 6, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 11-1331, 6-20-11; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-
8-22)
Sec. 12-592. - Display.
   All licenses issued under this division shall be displayed in a conspicuous
place at or near the entrance to the drive-in theater for which it is issued.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-593. - Nontransferable.
   Each license issued under this division shall cover but one drive-in theater
and shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-594. - Expiration of license.
   All licenses granted under the provisions of this division shall expire at
12:00 midnight following the first Tuesday of April of each year.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-595. - Requirements for operation.
   No drive-in theater shall be maintained or operated in violation of the
following requirements, and it shall be unlawful for the owner, operator or
manager of any drive-in theater or its agents, servants, or employees to
violate or permit violation of any such requirements:
      (1)   Loitering shall not be permitted in or about the entrance to or
exits from any drive-in theater.
      (2)   Quiet and good order shall be maintained upon the premises where
any drive-in theater is operated.
      (3)   No obscene or illegally suggestive advertising, pictures, or
writings shall be permitted on the premises of any drive-in theater, and no
picture or other form of advertising shall be permitted which does not
accurately describe the theatrical performance or moving picture entertainment
being advertised or which misleads or misinforms the public as to the nature of
the picture or entertainment to be exhibited.
      (4)   No drive-in theater licensee shall permit any show, exhibition or
entertainment to remain open to the public between the hours of 3:30 a.m. and
12:00 noon daily.
      (5)   Any children under the age of 14 years admitted to any drive-in
theater shall be accompanied by and in direct personal charge of his parent or
other responsible person.
      (6)   No owner, operator or employee of any drive-in theater shall
maintain, operate or carry on any lottery, game of chance, game of skill, bank
night, screeno, luck-o-grams or any other games of similar nature or engage in
any similar device or plan in connection with the operation of any drive-in
theater.
      (7)   Adequate provision shall be made for sanitary needs of patrons, as
determined by the department of public works, the department of health and all
pertinent laws and ordinances.
      (8)   The parking and driving areas shall be so treated to minimize the
creation of dust either by chemical treatment or hard-surfacing.
      (9)   The operator, owner or manager of a drive-in theater shall furnish
the necessary employees for adequate policing of the drive-in theater so as to
maintain order within the theater and avoid confusion in the movement of cars
in and out thereof.
      (10)   There shall be exits available to public streets or other public
ways from at least two points at all times; provided, however, that the
entrance may be regarded as one of the available exits if one lane of the
entrance is kept clear of parked vehicles at all times. Means of access shall
be made available at all times for fire apparatus, ambulances, or other
emergency vehicles. Drives shall be channelized and limited to not more than
four lanes.
      (11)   Exits and aisles and passageways leading to them shall be kept
adequately lighted at all times when open to the public. Artificial lights
shall be provided whenever natural light is inadequate.
      (12)   Fire extinguishing equipment shall be furnished in such kinds and
amounts and in such locations as may be directed by the city fire marshal and
applicable regulations, ordinances and laws.
      (13)   The electrical system and equipment shall be isolated from the
public by proper elevation or concealed under the ground surface, and all
electrical fuses, contact points, outlets and switches shall be enclosed and
safeguarded by devices and equipment approved by the department of building and
safety works and the fire department. Cables in the ground traversed by the
public shall be placed in trenches or conduits or protected by approved covers.
All electrical installations shall conform to the requirements of the National
Electrical Code and the ordinances of the city.
      (14)   The operator of any drive-in theater shall provide a wall or fence
of adequate height to separate the patrons and cars in attendance in such
theater from surrounding property. The fence shall be of substantial
construction made of wood, metal or masonry and erected solely upon property
used for the drive-in theater purposes in accordance with the requirements
specified by the city engineer and the department of public works, but it shall
not be treated as a partition or line fence. The outside of such fence, as far
as possible, shall be landscaped with suitable plants and shrubbery to preserve
harmony with the appearance of the surrounding property.
      (15)   Individual loud speakers for each car shall be provided. No
central loud speaker or public address system shall be permitted to be used
between the hours of 8:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m. except for emergency announcements
of impending danger such as fire, storm or similar dangers.
      (16)   Any sale of soft drinks, confections or other articles of
merchandise shall be governed by the laws and ordinances pertaining to the sale
of such merchandise and shall require the same license or licenses as if the
sales were conducted elsewhere.
      (17)   It shall be unlawful for any patron of such drive-in theater or
for any licensee under this division to permit or allow any such patron to have
in his possession or drink any alcoholic beverage or beverages on the licensed
premises.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-596. - Suspension and revocation of license.
   (a)   No license issued under this division shall be revoked except for
cause upon sworn proof of charges filed with the clerk by any person in the
several departments of the city above designated who are authorized to enforce
the provisions of this division or to approve the issuance of a license,
specifying with reasonable detail any of the following facts which facts are
hereby declared to be grounds for suspending any such license; facts showing
that the applicant for a license made one or more fraudulent statements or
misrepresentations or concealed material information in the application for
license; facts showing that such licensee has violated or permitted a violation
of this division which injuriously affects the public health, the public
safety, public morals, or the public welfare; that this division has been
violated in connection with operations for which the licensee was responsible
and of which the licensee was aware, or, in the exercise of reasonable
diligence, should have been aware that such violation has occurred; that
licensee has been convicted of any crime which was perpetrated on or in
connection with the licensed premises; or that licensee has carried on or
permitted to be carried on any unlawful or illegal act or acts on or in
connection therewith.
   (b)   Upon the filing of such charges, the person making such charges shall
forthwith suspend the license involved and shall give to such licensee a notice
of such suspension together with a copy of the charges specifying the facts on
which the suspension was made. At the same time such copy of the charges is
given to the licensee or his agent in charge of the premises, an order shall be
served upon such licensee or such agent signed by the director of the
department making the charges, directing such licensee to appear before the
council at a date and place therein specified, which date shall not occur more
than three days from the day of such suspension to show cause why the license
suspended should not be permanently revoked. Upon the filing of such charges
with the clerk, the person making such charges is hereby authorized and
empowered in connection with the suspension of a license to remove and take
into his possession the license or certificate or certificates of such licensee
given to the licensee at the time the license was issued, and to hold them
until the council has determined whether such license should be revoked as
herein provided.
   (c)   The council is hereby empowered and authorized to investigate the
charges set forth in the notice of suspension; subpoena, swear and examine
witnesses and receive other competent evidence in connection therewith, offered
either by the person making the charges or by the licensee; or the council, on
its own motion may make such investigation of the facts as it deems necessary.
The licensee shall be entitled to be represented by counsel. The decision of
the council shall be final and binding as to all questions of fact. If the
council shall find as the result of such investigation that the licensee failed
or refused to show cause, or has not shown sufficient cause why his license
should not be revoked, or if the council finds that such suspension was for a
violation of any of the provisions or requirements of this division, or that
any facts have been shown which constitute grounds for suspending a license
under this division, the council may order such license permanently revoked or
revoked for such period of time as the council deems necessary; but if the
council shall find the charges on which the license was suspended are not
sustained by the proofs, the license shall be reinstated by the council.
   (d)   In the event of any permanent revocation, the former licensee shall be
ineligible to receive any license under this division for a period of two years
thereafter.
   (e)   The council is hereby authorized to make such rules and regulations to
carry out the powers and duties imposed upon it by this division as it may deem
necessary.
   (f)   The clerk shall act as clerk to the council in connection with any
proceedings instituted in connection with the suspension or revocation of any
license.
(Ord. No. 81-81, § 9, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-597—12-615. - Reserved.
   Editor’s note—Ord. No. 17-1577 deleted Div. 6, §§ 12-600—12-609 in its

Ord. No. 07-1126, adopted May 7, 2007, Ord. No. 5039, adopted October 16, 2007,
and Ord. No. 07-1144, adopted Nov. 19, 2007.

   The statute known as Michigan's Food Service Sanitation Statute, Act No. 368

*** ARTICLE XVI. - MECHANICAL EXCAVATING AND GRADING ***
Sec. 12-701. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Business of mechanical excavating and grading shall mean and include any
person who shall furnish for hire the use of mechanical excavating or grading
equipment in the city, whether such person be the owner or the lessee of such
equipment.
   Mechanical excavating and grading equipment shall mean and include steam
shovels, power shovels, drag lines, bulldozers, digging and trenching machines,
scrapers, loaders or any other similar equipment used for excavating, digging
or grading purposes.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-702. - License required, exceptions.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct, manage or carry on the
business of mechanical excavating and grading in the city without first having
obtained a license therefor.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or cause to be operated
any steam shovel, power shovel, dragline, digging or trenching machine,
bulldozer, scraper, loader or other similar equipment used for the digging of
excavations or trenches or for the lifting or lowering of loads incidental to
such enterprise, in the city, unless a license has been first obtained for each
piece of such equipment used or to be used for any of such purposes; provided,
however, that an owner of land, or one having rights of ownership therein or
use thereof, who uses his own mechanical excavating or grading equipment on
such land, shall not be required to obtain a license for such equipment;
provided, however, that if the person engaged in the mechanical excavating and
grading business is the lessee of such equipment and lessor or owner of such
equipment has obtained a license therefor in the city, it shall not be
necessary for such lessee to obtain another license for such leased equipment;
provided further, that if any piece of such equipment is being used by any
person under contract with this city, the City of Detroit, the Board of Wayne
County Road Commissioners, the state highway department or the United States
government, or if any of such equipment is owned or operated by this city, the
City of Detroit, the Board of Wayne County Road Commissioners, the state
highway department or the United States government, and if any of such
equipment is actually working in or upon the public highways or streets or
public places or rights-of-way in the city, any and all of such equipment thus
being used shall be exempt from the licensing provisions of this article; on
condition, however, that the contractor owning or using such equipment, or the
City of Detroit, the Board of Wayne County Road Commissioners, the state
highway department or the United States government, if using their own
equipment, shall furnish to this city insurance certificates in amounts of
coverage satisfactory to the city engineer; provided further, that in lieu of
such insurance certificates, the City of Detroit, the Board of Wayne County
Road Commissioners, the state highway department or the United States
government may file with the city engineer a written statement signed by an
authorized agent agreeing to save the city harmless from any and all claims for
injuries or damages arising out of or incidental to any construction work being
carried on in the city streets.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-703. - Application for license.
   Any person desiring to engage in the business of mechanical excavating and
grading in the city with any of the mechanical excavating or grading equipment
required by this article to be licensed shall file a written application for
the necessary license or licenses with the city clerk. Such application shall
contain the name of the applicant and state whether the owner is an individual,
co partnership, assumed name, association, trust estate or corporation; the
residence address of the individual owner or owners or the individuals who are
officers, if a corporation, or persons acting in a fiduciary capacity in
connection with such business; the business address of such person; the type of
equipment such applicant proposes to use; the serial numbers and manufacturer
of each item of such equipment proposed to be licensed; and shall contain a
sworn statement of such facts. The application shall further contain an
agreement that, if granted a license, such applicant will fully comply with and
observe all statutes and ordinances of the city and all reasonable rules and
regulations of the department pertaining to or involving such equipment.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1041, 6-6-05)
Sec. 12-704. - License fees.
   The annual license fee or renewal thereof for engaging in the business of
mechanical excavating and grading shall be as prescribed by section
12-6 on or before the time the license or renewal thereof is issued. The annual
license fee for each piece of mechanical excavating or grading equipment or
renewal thereof governed by this article shall be as prescribed by section
12-6.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-705. - Issuance of license.
   Any license required by this article shall be issued by the city clerk upon
the filing with the city clerk of the evidence of insurance coverage required
by this article.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1041, 6-6-05)
Sec. 12-706. - Insurance required.
   Every person licensed under the provisions of this article to carry on a
mechanical excavating and grading business in the city, prior to the time of
the issuance of a license therefor, shall file with the city clerk a
satisfactory certificate that insurance has been issued by a responsible
insurance carrier to such prospective licensee for the period of such license
in the amount of $20,000.00 to $40,000.00 public liability and $25,000.00
property damage, insuring the city and all persons who might be in the vicinity
or who own property in the vicinity where such mechanical excavating and
grading equipment is being moved or used, against injury or damage to persons
or property, either private or public, by reason of the moving or using of such
equipment; provided, however, that all persons who carry on a mechanical
excavating and grading business in the city who are employed by any general
contractor with the city, which general contractor has furnished public
liability and property damage insurance in amounts required by the provision of
such contract, shall be licensed as required under this article, but shall not
be required to furnish insurance coverage set forth in this section during the
time they are so employed by such general contractor in the city, it being
hereby determined that the license issued for such employment shall be deemed
to be a temporary license which will terminate at the end of such employment
unless insurance coverage in the amounts and for the purposes above specified
shall have been filed with the city clerk prior to the termination of such
employment.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-707. - License tag.
   The city shall provide a metal tag for each piece of licensed equipment
which the applicant shall display prominently and continuously on each piece of
equipment so licensed, and which tag shall have impressed or painted thereon
the words "City of Dearborn," the license number and the date such license
expires. Such license decal shall not be transferable.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-708. - Expiration of license.
   All licenses issued under this article shall expire at 12:00 midnight
following December 31 of each year, unless otherwise terminated according to
law.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-709. - Permit and fee.
   (a)   Any person owning mechanical or excavating equipment covered by this
article and using such equipment in connection with his own premises, who does
not engage in the business of mechanical excavating and grading within the
meaning of this article, shall be granted permission to transport such
equipment over the streets of the city to such owner's premises when and where
required for use, upon the payment of a permit fee of $1.00 for each piece of
such equipment each time it is transported.
   (b)   The application for such permit shall be made and filed with the
director and shall state the time and place where such equipment is to be moved
in order that proper inspection may be made by the division to insure that no
damage is caused to any street surfaces, curbs, sidewalks, trees, water mains,
sewers, utilities or other public property.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-710. - Moving equipment on streets.
   Any person licensed under the provisions of this article shall, in each
instance when any such mechanical excavating or grading equipment is to be
moved to any location in the city, apply to the division at least 24 hours in
advance of movement of such equipment in order that an inspector from the city
shall be on hand to determine that no damage or injury results to any street
surface, curbs, sidewalks, trees, water mains, sewers, public utilities or any
public property from the transporting of such equipment.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-711. - Suspension or revocation of license—Procedures.
   (a)   Any license issued under this article may be revoked for cause upon
proof of charges filed with the city clerk, specifying with reasonable detail
the facts showing:
      (1)   Carelessness or negligence in the performance of the licensee's
duties in connection with his work.
      (2)   That such licensee has violated or permitted a violation of this
article in connection with work for which the licensee was responsible and to
which the licensee was aware, or in the exercise of reasonable diligence should
have been aware, that such violation had occurred.
      (3)   Intoxication of the operator of any licensed mechanical excavating
or grading equipment while on duty.
      (4)   Incompetency of any such equipment operator.
      (5)   Failure to keep the licensed mechanical equipment in good operating
condition.
      (6)   Falsifying any material fact in the application for license.
      (7)   Any other reason not listed above which will tend to endanger human
life, property or the public safety.
   (b)   Upon the filing of such charges, the city clerk shall forthwith
suspend the license involved, and shall give the licensee holding such license
notice of a hearing upon such charges, which hearing shall be held before a
committee consisting of the mayor, the president of the council and the
director of the building and safety department, or their designee, in not less
than ten days after the date of such notice, unless an earlier date is agreed
upon in writing by the licensees affected. Such notice shall be by personal
service or registered mail, shall state the time and place of such hearing and
shall contain a copy of the charges. If such charges are sustained in the
judgment of the committee, the license in question shall be immediately
revoked, and the city clerk shall notify the licensee in writing of its
revocation, but if such charges are not sustained, such license shall be
reestablished and the suspension lifted.
   (c)   If the license of any person governed by the provisions of this
article is revoked for cause, such person shall not be eligible to obtain a
similar license from the city for a period of at least one year after such
revocation.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 10, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 05-1041, 6-6-05)
Sec. 12-712. - Same—Continued operation prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of mechanical
excavating and grading when and during the time his license is suspended,
revoked or otherwise terminated.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-713. - Excavations.
   (a)   Any person digging an excavation shall provide shoring, sheathing and
other necessary precautions to maintain all public sidewalks, curbs and
pavements, as well as all earth, trees and nature objects on adjoining private
land in place during excavation. He shall also provide substantial railings, at
least four feet high, around such excavation at any point where the public
might be endangered by the absence of such guards.
   (b)   Excavations shall not be made in streets, alleys or other public
property, or extending into any public property, without a permit from the
department. All such excavations shall be backfilled with suitable material,
well tamped in place, and all sidewalks, pavements and other objects, both
natural and artificial, replaced by the excavator in as good a condition as
they were in originally. All public sidewalks and pavements shall be replaced
under the supervision of an inspector of the department, and all fill used
under public sidewalks and pavements shall be cinders, gravel, broken brick or
other material approved by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-714. - Drainage.
   In the construction of basements and cellars, excavations shall be kept well
drained, and, before walls are constructed above the foundations, tile drains
shall be installed and connected to a public sewer or, in case no such sewer is
available, to a sump pit provided with an automatic sump pump designed to
remove the water from the premises.
(Ord. No. 81-74, § 13, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-715—12-735. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XVII. - HOTELS, ROOMINGHOUSES AND LODGINGHOUSES AND BEDS AND
BREAKFASTS ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Secs. 12-736—12-745. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - HOTELS, ROOMINGHOUSES, LODGINGHOUSES
AND BEDS AND BREAKFASTS **
Sec. 12-746. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Cellar shall mean a story of a building partly below the adjoining grade,
but so located that the vertical distance from grade to the floor is greater
than the vertical distance from the grade to the ceiling. If the vertical
distance from the grade to the ceiling is over five feet, such story shall be
rated as a first story.
   Dwelling shall mean any building, or part thereof, occupied in whole or in
part, as the home, residence, or sleeping place of one or more persons, either
continuously, permanently, temporarily or transiently, except that a hotel may
consist of two or more dwellings.
   Family unit shall be deemed to include one or more persons whether related
by consanguinity or affinity.
   Hotel shall mean a dwelling, or part thereof, occupied as the more or less
temporary abiding place of individuals in which the rooms are usually occupied
singly for hire, and in which rooms no provision for cooking is made, and in
which building there are 50 or more sleeping rooms for hire; provided, however,
that a hotel as herein defined may include and have one or more separate
cottages equipped with sleeping rooms for hire which are on land adjacent to
the site of the principal dwelling, and are in common ownership and under one
management with the principal dwelling.
   Lodginghouse shall mean a dwelling, or part thereof, occupied as the more or
less temporary abiding place of individuals in which the rooms are usually
occupied singly for hire, in which no provision for cooking is made, and in
which there are less than 50 and more than five sleeping rooms for hire.
   Multiple dwelling shall mean a building constructed and used, or capable of
being used, by persons who live therein as separate family units, which
building will accommodate five or more family units, and the rooms of which are
so arranged that each group designed to be occupied by one family unit will
have cooking accommodations and toilet and sleeping facilities. This class
includes motels, tenement houses, flats, apartment houses, apartment hotels,
bachelor apartments, studio apartments, duplex apartments, kitchenette
apartments and all other dwellings similarly occupied whether or not
specifically designated herein.
   Roominghouse shall mean any dwelling occupied as a home or family unit where
a certain room or rooms, in excess of those used by the members of the
immediate family, are or can be leased or rented to and occupied by five or
more persons outside of the family, and without any attempt to provide therein
or therewith cooking or kitchen accommodations for persons occupying such room
or rooms.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-747. - Enforcement.
   It shall be the duty of the health officer, the chief of police, the fire
chief, the director of building and safety and their respective subordinates to
enforce the provisions of this article. Refusal by the licensee, his agent,
servant or employee to permit any of the city officials above mentioned, or
their respective subordinates, to examine and inspect the licensed premises
shall be cause for revocation of or failure to approve the license.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-748. - License required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or manage or cause to be used
any dwelling or part thereof in the city as a multiple dwelling, hotel,
lodginghouse or roominghouse, or any combination thereof, without first having
obtained a license for each such building as herein provided.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-749. - Manager's license required.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or manage or cause to be used
any dwelling or part thereof in the city as a multiple dwelling, hotel,
lodginghouse or roominghouse, or any combination thereof without first having
obtained a manager's license therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-750. - Kind of license determined by cubic space used.
   Any person operating, managing or causing to be used any dwelling or part
thereof for one or a combination of the uses coming under this article shall
procure a license for the use occupying the greater amount of cubic space in
such dwelling. No person shall operate, manage or cause to be used any dwelling
or part thereof where a total of five or more persons occupy or can occupy such
rooms or suites or groups of rooms, without first procuring a license for such
use.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-751. - Application for license.
   (a)   The application for a license of a dwelling shall be made by the
owner, operator or manager in writing to the clerk upon a form provided for
that purpose. It shall give all such information as shall be deemed necessary,
including the name and address of the applicant; his interest, if any, in the
dwelling to be licensed and the location thereof; the name and address of the
owner of record of such dwelling; if owner is a partnership, the name and
addresses of the partners; if a corporation, the names and addresses of the
officers thereof, as well as the name and address of resident agent; the number
of rooms or suites available for renting, indicating the size of rooms, number
of beds, bathrooms, shower stalls, lavatories and toilets on each floor, and
shall state whether the rooms are free from rats, mice, bedbugs, roaches, lice
or other vermin or rodents.
   (b)   The application for a manager's license, as herein referred to, shall
be made in writing to the clerk by the person seeking the license upon a form
provided for that purpose. The application shall set forth all such information
as shall be deemed necessary, including the name and address of the applicant;
his financial interest, if any, in the licensed premises where he will work,
showing the address of such premises; if the applicant is not self-employed,
the applicant shall show the name and address of the prospective employer, and
shall state the names and addresses where such applicant has worked as a
manager of a hotel, lodginghouse, or roominghouse during the past five years.
Such application shall also set forth a description of the applicant, such as
the age, sex, height, complexion, color of hair, color of eyes, weight; marital
status, whether single, married or divorced; race; place of birth; length of
time he has resided in the city, if he is a resident; and whether applicant is
a citizen of the United States, and how citizenship was obtained.
   (c)   Such application shall state whether or not the applicant has ever
been convicted of violating any laws or ordinances of any city, state or
county, and, if so, it should state the place of such conviction, the nature of
offense and sentence.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-752. - Investigation of applicant; fee; fingerprints; report; issuance.
   (a)   After filing such application with the clerk, the clerk shall refer
the application for the use of a dwelling through the treasurer, weights and
measures to the health officer, chief of police, fire chief and the department
of building and safety, and the application for a manager's license the clerk
shall refer through the treasurer, weights and measures to the chief of police
for investigation, each of whom shall make a written report and recommendation
through the department of licenses, weights and measures to the clerk within a
reasonable time.
   (b)   As a part of the process of investigating each applicant under the
provisions of this section, such applicant shall submit his fingerprints to the
police department in the discretion of such department for its investigation
thereof. If an application for a dwelling license as herein referred to is
made, the police department in its discretion may require all owners of such
premises and principal officers of any corporation to file their fingerprints
with the police department, as a condition precedent to approving such license;
provided, however, that if the fingerprints of any such person are on file, in
the discretion of the police department, it will not be necessary to file
duplicate fingerprints of such person. No license shall be issued to any person
under the provisions of this division who has been convicted of a felony,
except that the chief of police may approve the issuance of a license when it
shall be apparent that such applicant is at the present time a law-abiding
citizen. The police department is hereby authorized to establish such
additional rules and regulations governing the issuance of a manager's license,
not inconsistent herewith, as may be necessary and reasonable.
   (c)   If each of the officials is satisfied that the applicant is a suitable
person to engage in such business; that the granting of such license will not
be detrimental to the interests of the public; that all of the provisions of
this division and the other ordinances of the city and the applicable
provisions of the Housing Law of Michigan, so-called, have been or are being
complied with; that the granting of such license will not be in violation of
any statute, or any ordinance, rules or regulations of the city; that the
building in which it is proposed to conduct such business is in a safe and
sanitary condition; that it complies with the building, plumbing and electrical
codes of the city; and contains such safeguards against fires as are required
by law, the city clerk shall issue the respective license applied for;
provided, however, the applicant before receiving such license shall pay to the
city treasurer the fees, as prescribed by section
12-6.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-753. - Contents, display of license.
   (a)   Each license issued under this division shall designate the particular
kind of license issued, and the street address in the city where such business
shall be conducted. It shall be unlawful for any licensee to engage in such
business at any place other than that designated in such license, and if a
licensed manager shall change his place of operation or employment in the city,
he shall immediately notify the police department of such change, who shall
