record such change on his manager's license. Such license shall be subject to
all terms and provisions of this division and all other ordinances of the city,
the charter of the city, and the laws of the state and of the United States.
The license of premises shall be always conspicuously displayed on the licensed
premises.
   (b)   Every manager licensed under this division shall be given a license by
the city clerk at the time of issuance thereof, certifying that such person has
been licensed as a manager under this division in the city at the address
stated. Such license shall be carried upon the person of the licensee at all
times while such person is acting as a manager of licensed premises under this
article.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-754. - Nontransferable.
   No license issued under this division shall be assignable or transferable,
and one license shall issue for only one establishment. No person except the
licensee, directly or indirectly, shall do business or be permitted to do
business under such license.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-755. - Expiration.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this article shall expire one
year from date of application, unless sooner revoked or terminated in
accordance with law.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 6a, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-756. - Renewal of licenses.
   (a)   All licenses issued under this article shall expire annually on the
first day of February unless otherwise suspended or revoked. On or before
January 2, the city clerk shall send a notice reminding license holders of the
impending expiration date.
   (b)   All licenses issued under this article shall be renewed by filing an
annual written application with the City Clerk on a form furnished by the
Clerk. The application shall include the following information:
      (1)   The applicant's full true name and any other names used by the
applicant in the preceding seven years. If the applicant is a partnership,
corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity, then all persons
with an influential interest in the entity shall be deemed an applicant and
shall provide the information required by this article. Each applicant must
sign the application, and each applicant shall be considered a licensee if a
license is granted;
      (2)   Current business address or another mailing address of the
applicant;
      (3)   Written proof of identity, in the form of a driver's license or a
copy of a birth certificate accompanied by a picture identification document
issued by a governmental agency;
      (4)   The business name, location, zoning classification, legal
description, parcel identification number, mailing address and phone number;
      (5)   The name and business address of the designated local agent who is
responsible to supervise the premises and activities and who is authorized to
receive service of process;
      (6)   A statement of the status of monies owed to the city including, but
not limited to, water bills, real property taxes, personal property taxes, and
miscellaneous fees; and
      (7)   A statement as to whether any business in which an applicant has
had an influential interest has, in the previous seven years, and at the time
during which the applicant had the influential interest:
         a.   Been declared by a court of law to be a nuisance, as defined by
the Revised Judicature Act, MCL 600.3801; or
         b.   Been subject to a court order of closure or padlocking; or
         c.   Been subject to foreclosure proceedings; or
         d.   Been subject to Nuisance Abatement Board proceedings in
accordance with Article IA of
Chapter 13 of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances.
   The information provided pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (7) of this
subsection shall be supplemented in writing by certified mail, return receipt
requested, to the city clerk within ten working days of a change of
circumstances which would render the information originally submitted false or
incomplete.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 7, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 18-1624, 8-21-18)
Sec. 12-756A. - Issuance of license.
   (a)   Application review. Upon the filing of a completed application, the
city clerk shall forward a copy to the following departments: Department of
Law, Police Department, Fire Department, Department of Economic and Community
Development, Treasury Division of the Finance Department, Water Division of the
Department of Public Works, Property Maintenance and Development Services, and
any other department, to review the application for compliance with the
requirements of this article and all other applicable ordinances and codes.
   (b)   The city clerk shall issue a license to the applicant, or issue to the
applicant a written notice to deny the application. The city clerk shall issue
a license unless:
      (1)   Information. An applicant has failed to provide information as
required by this article, or has falsely answered a question or a request for
information on the application form;
      (2)   Fee. The license application fee required by this article has not
been paid;
      (3)   Code compliance. The subject premises lacks a current certificate
of occupancy or does not comply with applicable building, zoning, plumbing,
mechanical, electrical, health, or fire prevention codes;
      (4)   Unpaid fees. Relevant city departments have indicated that there
are unpaid fees or incurred violations under their purview related to the
subject premises (e.g., nuisance abatement fees);
      (5)   Taxes. The Treasury Division has denied a real and/or personal
property tax clearance pertaining to the subject premises;
      (6)   Ownership/lease. The applicant does not own the premises for which
a license is sought or does not have a lease for the full period for which the
license is sought;
      (7)   Negative police contact.  The Police Department indicates that a
disproportionate amount of police contact is required by the business due to
unlawful activities.
   (c)   License contents; posting; possession. The license, if granted, shall
state on its face the name of the person or persons to whom it is granted, the
number of the license issued to the licensee(s), the expiration date, and, the
address of the business. The business license shall be posted in a conspicuous
place at or near the entrance to the business so that it may be read at any
time.
(Ord. No. 18-1624, 8-21-18)
Sec. 12-757. - Application of housing law.
   The premises licensed under this division shall at all times be occupied and
maintained in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Housing Law of
Michigan.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-758. - Zoning ordinance compliance.
   No license shall be issued under this division for any use which would be in
violation of the terms of the zoning ordinance of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-759. - Bunk beds prohibited.
   No beds or bunks in any premises licensed under this division shall be
placed one above the other.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-760. - Occupancy restricted.
   No licensee under this division shall harbor, accommodate or permit more
persons to use the licensed premises than the number of persons who can be
regularly accommodated in and normally occupy the beds enumerated in his
license application; provided, however, that the occupying of the same bed by
two or more persons in succession in any 24-hour period shall not be allowed or
tolerated unless clean linen is furnished for each such occupancy.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-761. - Sleeping areas, places restricted.
   No person shall be permitted to sleep, lodge or dwell in the cellar of any
premises licensed under this division. No person shall be permitted to sleep
elsewhere than in a bed.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-762. - Cleanliness.
   All premises licensed under this division shall at all times be kept
thoroughly clean and free from all dirt, vermin, garbage and rubbish. The
interior walls and ceilings of every licensed dwelling shall be thoroughly
washed, cleaned or painted at least once a year.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-763. - Maintenance of cooking facilities.
   It shall be unlawful for any person occupying for hire one or more rooms in
a hotel, lodginghouse or roominghouse in the city to provide and maintain
therein facilities and provisions, or either of them, for cooking or the
preparation of meals. It shall be unlawful for any licensed manager to allow or
permit any such person occupying one or more rooms for hire in a hotel,
lodginghouse or roominghouse in the city to provide and maintain therein
facilities and provisions, or either of them, for cooking or the preparation of
meals.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 11a, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-764. - Furnishing of linens, towels.
   Where, under the terms of any rental agreement or lease, it is the express
or implied duty of the licensee under this division to furnish linens, such
licensee shall provide all beds with regulation sheets and pillowcases, and all
sheets and pillowcases shall be laundered at least once each week and shall be
provided clean and laundered for each new patron. Such licensee shall also
provide individual towels, and no common towels shall be permitted.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-765. - Heating of premises.
   It shall be the duty of every licensee of premises coming under this
division to furnish and maintain proper heat temperatures in such licensed
premises from October 1 of each year to June 1 of the succeeding year so that
the occupants thereof may secure, without undue restriction of ventilation, a
minimum temperature of 60 degrees Fahrenheit at 6:30 a.m., 65 degrees at 7:00
a.m. and 68 degrees at 8:30 a.m. and thereafter until 10:30 p.m., averaged
throughout the licensed premises. Written notice of complaint concerning lack
of heat in such licensed premises shall first be given to the owner of such
licensed premises by registered mail before a violation of this section shall
be deemed to exist. The provisions of this section shall not apply in any
instance where the occupant of any licensed premises has expressly agreed with
the licensee as a part of the rental contract or lease that such occupant shall
furnish heat.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-766. - Guest register required.
   (a)   No person shall be allowed to rent accommodations without providing
suitable identification at the time of registration, a copy of which shall be
retained with the record of registration. As used herein, suitable
identification shall mean a government issued photo identification card such as
a driver's license.
   (b)   The true name of all persons occupying rented accommodations shall be
listed on the register at the time of registration. Any person who remains in a
room after midnight shall be presumed to be an occupant.
   (c)   If it is determined that a registration was incomplete or inaccurate,
the rental agreement shall be terminated and all persons occupying the room for
which such incomplete or inaccurate registration was provided shall be evicted.
   (d)   Occupancy by a person who has engaged in illegal activity during a
past period of occupancy on the premises shall be prohibited. For the purposes
of this section, notification from the police department that an arrest for
illegal activity has been made during a period of occupancy shall create a
presumption that illegal activity has occurred; the presumption may be refuted
by evidence that charges were subsequently dismissed.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 14, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 18- 1625, 8-21-18)
Sec. 12-767. - Illegal activities prohibited, report.
   It shall be unlawful for any licensee to permit any illegal act or
occupation to be carried on upon the licensed premises. Any illegal act or
occupation occurring on such premises which shall come to the knowledge of the
licensee, his agents, servants or employees shall be immediately reported by
the licensee to the chief of police.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-768. - Infectious disease.
   It shall be the duty of every licensee under this division to report
immediately to the health officer of the city any infectious disease upon the
premises.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-769. - Manager to be on duty; report of fires.
   It shall be the duty of the licensee of each hotel, lodginghouse and
roominghouse to have upon such premises at all times an adult person, who may
be a licensed manager, who shall be the manager thereof and shall be charged
with the duty of immediately reporting all fires occurring on such premises to
the fire department. In hotels and lodginghouses such person shall be at the
place of registration. In roominghouses such persons shall be available at all
times. Any person in a hotel, lodginghouse or roominghouse discovering a fire
therein shall immediately notify the manager, and if for any reason the manager
is not immediately available, the discoverer of such fire shall promptly report
the same to the fire department. Failure on the part of the licensee to have
such a person on duty and failure to report such fires, as herein required,
shall be a violation of this division and subject the offender to all of the
penalties herein provided.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-770. - Unlawful to set fires.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, in smoking or attempting to light or to
smoke a cigarette, cigar, pipe or tobacco in any form for which lighters or
matches are used, or in the use of flammable liquids, to smoke in bed, while
lying down, or to set fire to, or cause to be burned or partially burned, any
bedding, furniture, curtain, drape, household furniture or furnishings in any
hotel, lodginghouse, roominghouse or light housekeeping rooms, or to set fire
to the licensed dwelling.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-771. - Notices regarding fire to be posted.
   The licensee of each hotel, lodginghouse, roominghouse and light
housekeeping room shall post and maintain, in a conspicuous place in the lobby,
and in each rented or rentable room thereof, a plainly printed notice advising
as to the provisions of this division relating to fire.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-772. - Vermin control.
   (a)   Any licensee under this division having notice or knowledge that his
licensed premises contain bed bugs, roaches, rats, mice or other vermin, shall
report such fact to the health officer within 48 hours.
   (b)   Such licensee shall cause such bed bugs, roaches, rats, mice or other
vermin, as the case may be, to be exterminated by fumigation or other effective
means approved by the health officer within five days from the date upon which
the licensee first had notice or knowledge of their existence upon the licensed
premises, and, upon his failure to do so, such license may be immediately
revoked.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-773. - Furnishings to be kept clean and in repair.
   Where, under the terms of any rental agreement or lease, it is the implied
or express duty of the licensee to furnish mattresses, sheets, pillows and
cases, comforters and quilts, or any of them, for such premises, such licensee
shall maintain such furnishings in clean condition and in good repair.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-774. - Suspension and revocation of license—Procedures.
   (a)   No license shall be revoked except for cause upon proof of charges
filed with the city council by any of the appointing authorities in the several
departments authorized by this division to enforce the provisions thereof and
to approve the issuance of a license, specifying with reasonable detail any
facts which are hereby declared to be grounds for suspending any such license:
      (1)   That such licensee has violated or permitted a violation of this
division, or any ordinances or the charter of the city, or any laws of the
state, or of the United States in connection with the operation of the licensed
premises or in the conduct of the licensee as manager.
      (2)   That the licensee has been convicted of any crime which was
perpetrated on, or in connection with, the licensed premises.
      (3)   That the licensee has carried on, or permitted to be carried on,
either individually or with the aid and assistance of others, any unlawful or
illegal act or acts on, or in connection with, such licensed premises.
      (4)   That the applicant for a license has made any false statements in
such application which were relied upon by any official of the city in
connection with the issuance of such license.
   (b)   Upon the filing of such charges, the appointing authority in the
department preferring such charges shall forthwith suspend the license
involved, and shall give to such licensee a notice of such suspension, together
with a copy of the charges, specifying the facts on which the suspension was
made. At the same time such copy of the charges is given to the licensee, or
his agent in charge of the premises, an order shall be served upon such
licensee, or agent, filed by the person preferring such charges, directing such
licensee to appear before the council at a date and place therein specified,
which date shall not occur more than ten days from the day of such suspension,
to show cause why the license suspended should not be permanently revoked.
   (c)   Upon the filing of such charges with the city council, the official of
the city preferring such charges is hereby authorized and empowered in
connection with the suspension of license to remove and take into his
possession the license, or certificate or certificates of such license, and
hold them until the council has determined whether such license should be
revoked as hereinafter provided.
   (d)   The council is hereby empowered and authorized to investigate the
charges set forth in the notice of suspension; subpoena, swear and examine
witnesses, and receive or produce other evidence in connection therewith,
either by the person making the charges, or the licensee; or the council, on
its own motion, may make such investigation of the facts as it deems necessary.
The licensee shall be entitled to be represented by counsel. The decision of
the council shall be final and binding as to the questions of fact.
   (e)   If the council shall find as a result of such investigation that the
licensee failed or refused to show cause, has not shown sufficient cause why
his license should not be revoked, or if the council finds that such suspension
was for a violation of any of the provisions or requirements of this division,
or that any facts have been shown which constitute grounds for suspending a
license under this division, the council may order such license permanently
revoked, or revoked for such period of time as the council deems necessary. If
the council shall find the charges on which the license was revoked are not
sustained by the proofs, the license shall be reinstated by the council.
   (f)   In the event of any revocation, the former licensee shall be
ineligible to receive any license by this division for a period of two years
thereafter, and no license shall be issued during such period for the
conducting of any business required to be licensed under this division.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-775. - Same—Conduct of business.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct any business or activity
required by the provisions of this division to have a license when a license
has been suspended or revoked.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-776. - Fees not to be refunded.
   Any and all monies paid as fees for licenses issued or to be issued under
this division shall be retained by the city treasurer, and no refund shall be
made if such license is not granted, or if it has been granted and is later
revoked or terminated.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 25, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-777. - Personal property taxes paid.
   No license or renewal thereof shall be issued to any person under this
division unless and until a certificate has been obtained from the city
treasurer to the effect that all personal property taxes levied and assessed
against such applicant for license has been paid in full.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 23, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-778. - Inspection of licensed premises.
   (a)   The appointing authorities in the several departments of the city,
authorized to enforce the provisions of this division, their respective
deputies, or any authorized agents, or employees in the several departments
whose approval must first be obtained before any license shall be issued under
this division, or any authorized inspector or investigator in the city whose
duty it is to enforce the license laws and ordinances of the city, is hereby
authorized and empowered to inspect the premises licensed under this division
at any reasonable hour of the day or night for the purpose of enforcing the
provisions of this division and determining that any and all provisions of all
ordinances, codes and rules and regulations of the city pertaining thereto are
being complied with.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent or attempt to prevent,
or to interfere with anyone herein authorized to make an investigation or
inspection, as above provided.
(Ord. No. 81-84, § 26, 11-4-81)
* Secs. 12-779—12-820.   Reserved. *
*** ARTICLE XVIII. - GOING-OUT-OF-BUSINESS SALES ***
Sec. 12-821. - License required.
   Pursuant to the provisions of Act No. 39 of the Public Acts of Michigan of
1961 (MCL 442.211 et seq., MSA 19.401(1) et seq.), as amended, a license issued
by the city clerk shall be obtained by any person before selling or offering to
sell any goods at a sale to be advertised or held out by any means to be one of
the following kinds:
      (1)   Going-out-of-business sale.
      (2)   Removal-of-business sale.
      (3)   Sale of goods damaged by fire, smoke or otherwise.
Sec. 12-822. - Application requirements.
   A person desiring to conduct a sale regulated by this article shall make a
written application to the city clerk setting forth and containing the
following information:
      (1)   The true name and address of the owner of the goods to be the
object of the sale.
      (2)   A description of the place where such sale is to be held.
      (3)   The nature of the occupancy, whether by lease or sublease, and the
effective date of termination of such occupancy.
      (4)   The dates of the period of time in which the sale is to be
conducted.
      (5)   A full and complete statement of the facts in regard to the sale,
including the reason for the urgent and expeditious disposal of goods thereby
and the manner in which the sale will be conducted; if the application is for a
going-out-of-business or removal sale, it shall also contain a statement that
the business will be discontinued at the premises where the sale is to be
conducted upon termination of the sale.
      (6)   A full and complete inventory of the goods that are to be sold,
which inventory shall:
         a.   Itemize the goods to be sold and contain sufficient information
concerning each item, including the brand name, if any, to clearly identify it.
         b.   List separately any goods which were purchased during a 60-day
period immediately prior to the date of making application for the license.
         c.   Show the cost price of each item in the inventory together with
the name and address of the seller of the items to the applicant, the date of
purchase, the date of delivery of each item to the applicant and the total
value of the inventory at cost.
      (7)   The name and address of the person who will be in charge and
responsible for the conduct of the sale.
Sec. 12-823. - License fee.
   Any applicant for a license under this article shall submit to the city
clerk with his application a license fee, as prescribed in section
12-6.
Sec. 12-824. - Issuance; denial.
   (a)   A license shall be issued under this article on the following terms:
      (1)   The license shall authorize the sale described in the application
for a period of not more than 30 days from the start of such sale; the license
may be renewed not more than twice for a period of time not to exceed 30 days
for each renewal, upon affidavit of the licensee that the goods listed in the
inventory have not been disposed of and that no new goods have been added to
the inventory. The application for renewal shall contain a new inventory
conforming to the requirements hereof.
      (2)   The license shall authorize only the one type of sale described in
the application at the location named therein.
      (3)   The license shall authorize only the sale of goods and merchandise
described in the inventory attached to the application; no person shall order
any goods for the purpose of selling and disposing of the same under any sale
authorized by this article. Any unusual purchase or additions to the stock
within 60 days prior to the filing of the application pursuant to this article
shall be presumptive evidence that the purchases and additions were in
contemplation of the sale authorized by this article.
      (4)   Any license provided for in this article shall not be assignable or
transferable.
   (b)   No license shall be issued under this article to any person:
      (1)   To conduct a sale in the trade name or style of a person in whose
goods the applicant for the license has acquired a right or title thereto
within six months prior to the time of making application for such a license.
      (2)   To conduct a sale, other than sale of goods damaged by fire, smoke,
or otherwise on the same premises within one year from the conclusion of a
prior sale of the nature covered by this act.
   (c)   Subdivisions (b)(1) and (b)(2) of this section shall not apply to any
person who acquired right or title in goods as an heir, devisee or legatee or
pursuant to a court order of a court of competent jurisdiction.
Sec. 12-825. - Display.
   A copy of the application for a license to conduct a sale shall be posted in
a conspicuous place in the sales room where the goods are to be sold; provided,
however, the copy of the inventory attached to such application need not show
the purchase price of such goods; a duplicate copy of the license shall be
attached to the front door of the premises where the sale is conducted. Any
advertisement published in connection with the sale shall conspicuously show
the license number and the date of expiration.
Sec. 12-826. - Prohibited sales.
   (a)   No goods shall be sold on the premises at or during a sale authorized
under this article, except in conformance with the requirements hereof.
   (b)   No goods shall be sold or offered for sale excepting the goods
described in and inventoried in the original application.
   (c)   No goods shall be sold or offered for sale which were purchased in
contemplation of such sale.
Sec. 12-827. - Violations void license.
   Any violation of this article shall void any license issued to conduct a
sale under this article, in addition to any other penalty imposed by this Code.
Secs. 12-828—12-850. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XIX. - MOTORBUSES ***
Sec. 12-851. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Highway shall mean and refer to any and all streets, avenues, boulevards,
public alleys, thoroughfares, public places or highways in the city.
   Highway maintenance and repair fee shall mean that charge which is made by
the city to compensate it for the services rendered by the city which are in
part used and enjoyed by any licensee covered by this article, and shall
include the expenses incurred by the city for maintaining and repairing the
pavements and the highway surfaces traversed by any vehicles of the licensee,
removing snow from such highway surfaces, installing and maintaining adequate
drainage for such highways, lighting and cleaning such highways, and furnishing
and maintaining traffic controls along such highways through mechanical
equipment or police officers.
   Motorbus shall mean any motor propelled vehicle that is operated as a common
carrier of passengers for hire over a fixed or established route in the city,
but shall not include streetcars or motorbuses engaged in interstate commerce.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-852. - License required.
   No person, as owner or otherwise, shall operate or cause to be operated one
or more motorbuses on the highways of the city without first obtaining a
license therefor from the city clerk. The license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
Sec. 12-853. - Compliance required.
   No person shall operate or cause to be operated one or more motorbuses upon
the highways of the city without first complying with the terms and provisions
of this article, and the failure to operate any motorbus in compliance with the
provisions of this article may be cause for the revocation of such license.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-854. - Application for license.
   (a)   An application, either original or renewal, to operate one or more
motorbuses on the city highways, shall set forth:
      (1)   The factory serial number of the buses to be operated.
      (2)   The owner's identifying number printed on the outside of each bus
to be licensed.
      (3)   The number of buses the applicant desires to operate.
      (4)   The proposed route or routes on the city highways.
      (5)   The proposed motorbus schedule.
      (6)   The proposed schedule of fares.
      (7)   The proposed loading stations.
   (b)   Such application shall be filed with the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-855. - Investigation, approvals required.
   The clerk shall refer each application for a license required by this
article to the chief of police and the director of building and safety for
their investigation and recommendation in connection therewith. The route or
routes over which the applicant desires to operate motorbuses shall be strictly
adhered to by the applicant, if and when such route is approved by the city
council. Any route and schedule which the applicant proposes to operate within
the corporate limits of the city must be approved by the city council. Any
changes or revisions to the route or schedule must also be approved by the city
council.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-856. - Issuance of license.
   (a)   The city clerk is hereby authorized to issue a motorbus license or a
renewal thereof to any person as a common carrier in the city upon the approval
of the application therefor by the chief of police and the director of building
and safety, but before such license is issued, or renewed, the proposed route
or routes and schedule shall have been approved by the city council; provided,
however, that any applicant for license which has not qualified for and has not
received a permit from the state public service commission may qualify for a
motorbus license to permit the operation of one or more motorbuses within the
city by complying with the provisions of this article.
   (b)   Any licensee under the provisions of this article, as a condition to
the continuing of such license in force, shall operate the number of motorbuses
set forth in any such approved schedule as a minimum of service upon the routes
approved and described in the application for the license.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-857. - Insurance required.
   (a)   The applicant for a license under this article shall file with the
city clerk a certified copy of the contract of insurance filed with the state
public service commission, with public liability coverage in the amount of
$500,000.00 for each bus.
   (b)   If more than ten motorbuses are operated by the applicant or licensee,
a certified copy of a blanket policy of insurance covering all motorbus
equipment used in the city by the applicant or licensee may be filed in the
following amounts:
      (1)   Public liability coverage of at least $500,000.00.
      (2)   Property damage coverage of at least $100,000.00.
   (c)   If the licensee is a transportation system owned and operated by a
municipality other than the city, it will not be necessary for such licensee to
file the copies of the insurance contract indicating coverage, as above set
forth, but the requirements of this section for insurance will be complied with
if such municipally owned transportation system will file with the clerk an
indemnity agreement where such transportation system agrees to pay and satisfy
any and all legal claims which might arise in connection with the operation of
its transportation facilities in the city.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-858. - Highway maintenance and repair fee.
   Before any license shall be issued under this article, the applicant shall
pay in advance to the city treasurer an annual highway maintenance and repair
fee for each bus to be operated on the highways of the city. Such bus license
fee rate will hereafter be the flat rate of $35.00 per bus for each bus up to
and including 300 buses. There will be no charge imposed as a bus license fee
on any buses in excess of 300 buses per applicant.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-859. - Requirements for vehicles.
   All vehicles which may be operated pursuant to the provisions of this
article shall comply with the following general requirements:
      (1)   Each vehicle shall be maintained in good and safe repair and shall
be subject to inspection by the police department or any inspector in the city
authorized to make such inspection at such reasonable times as may be
necessary.
      (2)   Each vehicle shall be propelled by power generated or contained
within the vehicle itself, or by storage battery, but no power shall be used
which will in its generation or use produce smoke or noxious odors sufficient,
in the opinion of the city council, or its authorized representatives, to
constitute a nuisance.
      (3)   All parts of each vehicle shall be so constructed that excessive
quantities of oil or grease cannot drop on the roadway.
      (4)   All parts of every vehicle shall be so constructed that no undue
noise or vibration shall result from the operation thereof.
      (5)   Every vehicle shall be operated in such manner at all times so as
to comply with all laws and ordinances and the traffic rules and regulations of
the city.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-860. - Identification of vehicles.
   (a)   Every vehicle shall have attached on the outside and in the rear
thereof a license decal furnished by the city clerk showing in legible print
the words, "City of Dearborn, License No. (showing number) Expires (date of
expiration)." Such plate shall be mounted and kept in a conspicuous position on
the vehicle to which it is assigned, and shall not be transferable during the
license year for which it was issued; provided, however, that in the case of
those licensees which propose to and do operate in the city a number of buses
in any license year in excess of 300, it will not be necessary for such
licensee to have attached on each of its buses the license decal above referred
to, but it will be a sufficient compliance with this provision if the rates
herein specified for 300 buses are paid and the license has been issued.
   (b)   As soon as a license number and license decal have been issued to any
licensee under this article, a record thereof shall be given to the department
of licenses, weights and measures in the city, which record shall show the name
of the licensee, the license number of the year in question and the owner's
identifying number on the bus for which such license plate was issued.
   (c)   The name of the owner of every motorbus licensed under this article
shall be printed in plainly legible letters in at least two places on the
outside of every such bus, together with the owner's identifying number
thereon.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-861. - Expiration.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this article shall expire at 12:
00 midnight following the first Tuesday in May of each calendar year, which
date shall be deemed the termination of the license year, unless revoked sooner
as provided in section
12-863.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-862. - Passenger stops.
   Any motorbus licensed under this article may stop to take on or discharge
passengers at such street intersections or bus stops on such route or routes,
as indicated in the traffic rule and regulations promulgated by the chief of
police and approved by the city council, unless temporarily changed by the
chief of police in accordance with the traffic ordinance.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-863. - Revocation, suspension of license.
   (a)   Any license issued under this article may be revoked for cause by the
city council after a hearing thereon before the council; provided, however,
that if any licensee under the provisions of this article shall fail or for any
reason be unable to furnish or provide transportation in accordance with the
provisions of this article and its approved routes and schedules for a period
of one week, without the written consent and approval of the city council, the
license issued to such licensee shall be automatically terminated and canceled
without the necessity for any proceedings involving the revocation thereof.
   (b)   The proceedings for the revocation of any license may be filed with
the council by the chief of police, the director of building and safety, the
city controller, or by the city council, on its own motion, in the form of a
complaint setting forth a brief and concise statement of the facts forming the
basis of such revocation. A copy of such complaint shall be served or caused to
be served upon such licensee forthwith by the city clerk, either personally, or
by registered mail with a return receipt requested, and in connection therewith
a notice of hearing before the city council shall be given, which hearing date
shall be not less than five days nor more than ten days from the date such
complaint is served on the licensee, such notice to set forth the time and
place of hearing on such complaint. At the time of the hearing, the facts
constituting the basis of such complaint shall be presented to the council, and
any evidence in opposition thereto may be presented by the licensee, and the
council shall make its determination as to whether the license should be
revoked. All questions of fact determined by the council shall be final.
(Ord. No. 81-68, § 4, 11-4-81)
Secs. 12-864—12-885. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE XX. - TAXICABS AND OTHER MOTOR VEHICLES FOR HIRE ***
Sec. 12-886. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
[For the purposes of this article, the following vehicles shall be known as
motor vehicles for hire, with the exception of taxicabs.]
   Fleet shall mean 11 or more commercial vehicles used for the transportation
of passengers for hire whether owned or leased by an individual, company, or
corporation operating under one name.
   Limousine shall mean a self-propelled motor vehicle used in the carrying of
passengers and the baggage of the passengers for hire with a seating capacity
of 8 passengers or fewer, including the driver. Limousine does not include a
commercial vehicle. Limousine also does not include a vehicle operated by any
of the following:
      (1)   A county, city, township, or village as provided by law, or other
authority incorporated under 1963 PA 55, MCL 124.351 to 124.359.
      (2)   An authority incorporated under the metropolitan transportation
authorities act of 1967, 1967 PA 204, MCL 124.401 to 124.426, or that operates
a transportation service pursuant to an interlocal agreement under the urban
cooperation act of 1967, 1967 (Ex Sess) PA 7, MCL 124.501 to 124.512.
      (3)   Operating under a contract entered into under 1967 (Ex Sess) PA 8,
MCL 124.531 to 124.536, or 1951 PA 35, MCL 124.1 to 124.13.
      (4)   An authority incorporated under the public transportation authority
act, 1986 PA 196, MCL 124.451 to 124.479, or a nonprofit corporation organized
under the nonprofit corporation act, 1982 PA 162, MCL 450.2101 to 450.3192,
that provides transportation services.
      (5)   An authority financing public improvements to transportation
systems under the revenue bond act of 1933, 1933 PA 94, MCL 141.101 to 141.140.
      (6)   A person that is only operating limousines to provide the
transportation of passengers for funerals.
      (7)   An employer that is only using the vehicle, or on whose behalf the
vehicle is being used, to transport its employees to and from their place of
employment.
   Limousine carrier shall mean a person who, either directly or through any
device, dispatch system, or arrangement, holds himself or herself out to the
public as willing to transport passengers for hire by limousine.
   Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Act shall mean Act 300 of the Public Acts
of 1974, being sections 257.1301 and 257.1340 of the Michigan Compiled Laws.
   Taxicab means a motor vehicle with a seating capacity of 8 passengers or
fewer, including the driver, that is equipped with a roof light and taximeter,
and that carries passengers for a fee usually determined by the distance
traveled. Taxicab does not include a commercial vehicle.
   Taxicab carrier means a person who, either directly or through any device,
dispatch system, or arrangement, holds himself or herself out to the public as
willing to transport passengers for hire by taxicab.
   Taxicab driver means an individual who uses a taxicab to provide
transportation services to potential passengers.
   Taximeter shall mean a mechanical, electronic, or digital instrument or
device by which the charge for hire is mechanically calculated and upon which
such charge shall be indicated by means of figures.
   Transportation network company means a person operating in this state that
uses a digital network to connect transportation network company riders to
transportation network company drivers who provide transportation network
company prearranged rides. Transportation network company does not include a
taxi service, transportation service arranged through a transportation broker,
ridesharing arrangement, or transportation service using fixed routes at
regular intervals.
   Transportation network company digital network means an online-enabled
application, website, or system offered or utilized by a transportation network
company that enables the prearrangement of rides with transportation network
company drivers.
   Transportation network company driver means an individual who satisfies all
of the following:
      (1)   Receives connections to potential passengers and related services
from a transportation network company in exchange for payment of a fee to the
transportation network company.
      (2)   Uses a personal vehicle to offer or provide transportation network
company prearranged rides to transportation network company riders upon
connection through a digital network controlled by a transportation network
company in return for compensation or payment of a fee.
   Transportation network company prearranged ride means the provision of
transportation by a transportation network company driver to a transportation
network company rider, beginning when a transportation network company driver
accepts a ride requested by a transportation network company rider through a
digital network controlled by a transportation network company, continuing
while the transportation network company driver transports the requesting
transportation network company rider, and ending when the last requesting
transportation network company rider departs from the personal vehicle.
Transportation network company prearranged ride does not include a shared-
expense carpooling or vanpooling arrangement or transportation provided using a
taxicab, limousine, or other vehicle.
   Transportation network company rider means an individual who uses a
transportation network company's digital network to connect with a
transportation network company driver who provides a transportation network
company prearranged ride to the transportation network company rider in the
transportation network company driver's personal vehicle between points chosen
by the transportation network company rider.
(Ord. No. 91-55, § 1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 95-637, 5-16-95; Ord. 19-1658, 9-10-19)
State Law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 257.2102
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-887. - Signage, emblem, or department of licensing and regulatory
affairs registration number.
   (a)   Subject to subsection (b), a vehicle subject to this Article shall
display a consistent and distinctive signage or emblem at all times while the
vehicle is being used to provide transportation services or while the vehicle
is being used by a transportation network company driver for a transportation
network company prearranged ride or while the transportation network company
driver is available to receive a transportation request. Subject to subsection
(b), a vehicle subject to this Article may also display a department of
licensing and regulatory affairs registration number. The signage, emblem, or
department of licensing and regulatory affairs registration numbers shall
satisfy both of the following:
      (1)   The signage, emblem, or department of licensing and regulatory
affairs registration number shall be color-contrasted to be visible during
daylight hours from a distance of at least 50 feet.
      (2)   The signage, emblem, or department of licensing and regulatory
affairs registration numbers shall sufficiently identify the limousine carrier,
taxicab carrier, transportation network company, or dispatch system provider
with which the vehicle is affiliated.
   (b)   If a limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, or transportation network
company is providing services in association with a dispatch system provider,
the limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, or transportation network company shall
display its signage or emblem or the signage or emblem of the dispatch system
provider. If a limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, or transportation network
company displays the signage or emblem of a dispatch system provider as
provided in this subsection, it shall also display its department of licensing
and regulatory affairs registration number.
   (c)   If a limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, or transportation network
company displays a department of licensing and regulatory affairs registration
number, the 10-digit registration number shall be displayed with the "#" symbol
prior to the registration number and shall use numbers and symbols that are at
least 1-1/2 inches in height.
   (d)   A person who operates or permits to be operated a limousine, taxicab,
or transportation network vehicle in violation of this section is responsible
for a civil infraction.
   (e)    The license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of this Chapter, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. 19-1658, 9-10-19; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-22)
State law reference - Similar provisions, MCL 257.2111 and MCL 257.2115
Sec. 12-888. - Automobile insurance coverage for transportation network company
driver or transportation network company on driver's behalf.
   (a)   A transportation network company driver, or a transportation network
company on a transportation network company on a transportation network company
driver's behalf, shall maintain primary automobile insurance on a personal
vehicle that recognizes that the transportation network company driver uses the
vehicle as a transportation network company driver or otherwise uses a vehicle
to transport passengers for compensation and covers the transportation network
company driver while he or she is engaged in a transportation network company
prearranged ride.
   (b)   During the time that a transportation network company driver is logged
on to the transportation network company's digital network and is available to
received transportation requests but is not engaged in a transportation network
company prearranged ride, all of the following types of automobile insurance
are required:
      (1)   Residual third party automobile liability insurance as required
under section 3101 of the insurance code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL 500.3101, in
the amount of at least $50,000.00 per person for death or bodily injury,
$100,000.00 per incident for death or bodily injury, and $25,000.00 for
property damage.
       (2)   Personal protection insurance and property protection insurance in
the amounts and of the types of coverage required by chapter 31 of the
insurance code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL 500.3101 to 500.3179.
   (c)   During the time that a transportation network company driver is
engaged in a transportation network company prearranged ride, all of the
following types of automobile insurance are required:
      (1)   Residual third party automobile liability insurance with a minimum
combined single limit of $1,000,000.00 for all bodily injury or property
damage.
      (2)   Personal protection insurance and property protection insurance in
the amounts and of the types of coverage required by chapter 31 of the
insurance code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL 500.3101 to 500.3179.
   (d)   The requirements of subsections (b) and (c) may be satisfied by
automobile insurance maintained by a transportation network company driver or a
transportation network company, or a combination of both.
   (e)   If the insurance required by subsection (b) and (c) lapses or does not
provide the required coverage, insurance maintained by a transportation network
company shall provide the coverage required by this section, beginning with the
first $1.00 of a claim, and the transportation network company's insurer shall
defend the claim.
   (f)   Coverage provided under an automobile insurance policy maintained by a
transportation network company shall not be dependent upon a personal
automobile insurer denying the claim first and shall not require a personal
automobile insurer to deny the claim first.
   (g)   All of the following apply to the automobile insurance described in
subsections (b) and (c):
      (1)   It may be placed with an insurer licensed under chapter 4 of the
insurance code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL 500.402 to 500.480, or, if the
insurance is maintained by a transportation network company, an eligible
unauthorized insurer under chapter 19 of the insurance code of 1956, 1956 PA
218, MCL 500.1901 to 500.1955.
      (2)   The insurance policy satisfies the financial responsibility
requirements described in chapter V of the Michigan vehicle code, 1949 PA 300,
MCL 257.501 to 257.532.
   (h)   A transportation network company driver shall carry proof of the
insurance required under subsections (b) and (c) with him or her at all times
during his or her use of a personal vehicle in connection with a transportation
network company's digital network. The transportation network company driver
may provide proof of insurance by a paper or electronic copy of the certificate
of insurance. If an accident occurs during the time that a transportation
network company driver is using a personal vehicle in connection with a
transportation network company's digital network, he or she shall provide all
of the following information upon request to directly interested parties,
automobile insurers, and investigating law enforcement officers as required
under section 328 of the Michigan vehicle code, 1949 PA 300, MCL 257.328:
      (1)   Insurance coverage information.
      (2)   Whether he or she was logged on to the transportation network
company's digital network or on a transportation network company prearranged
ride at the time of the accident.
      (3)   A person who operates or permits to be operated a transportation
network vehicle in violation of this subsection (h) is responsible for a civil
infraction.
   (i)   If a transportation network company's insurer makes a payment for a
claim covered under comprehensive coverage or collision coverage, the
transportation network company's insurer shall issue the payment directly to
the business repairing the vehicle or jointly to the owner of the vehicle and
the primary lienholder on the vehicle.
   (j)   A transportation network company shall disclose all of the following
information in writing to a transportation network company driver before that
transportation network company driver may accept a request for a transportation
network company prearranged ride on that transportation network company's
digital network:
      (1)   The insurance coverage, including the types of coverage and limits
for each type of coverage, that the transportation network company provides
while the transportation network company driver uses a personal vehicle in
connection with the transportation network company's digital network.
      (2)   That, depending on the terms of the policy, the transportation
network company driver's personal automobile insurance policy might not provide
coverage while the transportation network company driver is logged on to the
transportation network company's digital network or is engaged in a prearranged
ride.
(Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-19)
State law reference - MCL 257.2123
 Sec. 12-889. - Driver's license-Required.
   No person shall drive or operate any taxicab, limousine, transportation
network vehicle, or other motor vehicle for hire upon any street, highway or
public way, including public parking lots in the city, unless such person has
been, and is at the time of such driving or operating, licensed in full force
and effect as an operator or chauffeur under the provisions of the state
vehicle code or by some other constituted authority, in accordance with MCL
257.301 and
Chapter 18, Section
18-189 of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-19)
State law reference - MCL 257.301
Sec. 12-900. - Unlicensed operation.
   It shall be unlawful to permit, and it shall be unlawful for any unlicensed
driver or any driver whose license has been suspended or revoked to operate,
any taxicab, limousine, or transportation network company vehicle, or other
motor vehicle for hire in the city while such suspension or revocation exists.
A person who operates or permits to be operated a limousine, taxicab, or
transportation network vehicle in violation of this section is guilty of a
misdemeanor punishable by a term of jail for not more than 93 days or a fine of
not more than $500.00 or both in accordance with
Chapter 18, Section
18-199 of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. No. 81-55, § 22, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-19)
State law reference - MCL 257.904
Sec. 12-901. - Payment of taxi fares in advance.
   Every driver of a taxicab shall have the right to demand payment of the
legal fare in advance and may refuse employment until so prepaid, but no driver
of a taxicab shall otherwise refuse or neglect to convey any orderly person or
persons upon request anywhere in the city, unless previously engaged or unable
to do so.
(Ord. No. 81-55, § 26, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-19)
Sec. 12-902. - Disputes as to fares.
   All disputes as to the lawful rate of fare shall, upon the request of the
driver or passenger of the vehicle, be determined by a police officer. Failure
to comply with such determination shall subject the offending party to a charge
of disorderly conduct. This provision shall be mandatory, and a police officer
must render such service.
(Ord. No. 81-55, § 27, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 02-923, 11-19-02; Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-
10-19)
Sec. 12-903. - Acceptance of transportation request.
   A transportation network company driver shall not accept a request for
transportation unless the request is accepted through the transportation
network company's digital network. A transportation network company driver who
violates this subsection shall be responsible for a civil infraction.
(Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-10)
Sec. 12-904. - Nondiscrimination and accommodation.
   (a)   A limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, and transportation network
company shall adopt a policy of nondiscrimination with respect to passengers
and potential passengers and shall notify limousine drivers, taxicab drivers,
and transportation network company drivers of the policy adopted under this
subsection.
    (b)   A limousine driver, taxicab driver, and transportation network
company drivers hall comply with all applicable laws regarding
nondiscrimination against a passenger or potential passenger.
   (c)   A limousine driver, taxicab driver, and transportation network company
drivers shall comply with all applicable laws regarding accommodation of
service animals.
   (d)   A limousine carrier, taxicab carrier, and transportation network
company shall not impose an additional charge for providing services to a
passenger with a physical disability because of his or her disability.
   (e)   A carrier, company, or driver that violates this subsection shall be
responsible for a civil infraction.
(Ord. No. 19-1658, 9-10-19)

*** ARTICLE XXI. - PUBLIC MOVING VANS ***
Sec. 12-951. - Definition.
   For the purposes of this article, a "public moving van" shall mean every
vehicle used for the conveyance of household furniture from place to place for
hire.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-952. - License required.
   No person shall keep for hire any public moving van without a license to do
so.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-953. - License fee, issuance; insurance; number plate.
   The city clerk is hereby authorized to grant licenses to any person to
operate a public moving van upon paying the per-vehicle application fee, as
listed iin Section
12-6 of this Chapter, to the city treasury and after the applicant has
furnished satisfactory proof to the city clerk that he carries cargo insurance
of $500,000.00 for each vehicle engaged in the business, public liability
insurance in an amount not less than $500,000.00 and property damage insurance
in an amount not less than $100,000.00. Upon payment of such fee and the
posting of required insurance, the clerk shall deliver to the applicant a
number plate for each vehicle. All licenses shall expire on December 1 of each
year.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 11-1324, 5-16-11; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-
8-22)
Sec. 12-954. - Display of plate; records.
   Every person licensed under this article shall cause the number plate to be
posted in a conspicuous place upon the moving van, and shall keep a record of
the place from and the place to which the household goods of any person is
moved.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-955. - Weekly report.
   On Monday of each week, the owner of each moving van used to move household
goods within the city, or to or from the city during the previous week, shall
file with the police department a statement showing the name of each person who
employed him to move household furniture, the place from and the place to which
such furniture was moved.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-956. - Covering, pads required.
   All public moving vans shall be covered and equipped with standard furniture
moving pads.
(Ord. No. 81-58, § 1, 11-4-81)
*** ARTICLE XXII. - WEIGHTS AND MEASURES[6]  ***
Footnotes:

State Law reference— Weights and measures, MCL 290.601 et seq., MSA 12.1081(1)
et seq.
Sec. 12-971. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Assistant shall mean an assistant to the supervisor.
   Barrel, when used in connection with fermented liquor, shall mean a unit of
31 gallons.
   Commodity in package form shall mean a commodity put up or packaged in any
manner in advance of sale in units suitable for either wholesale or retail
sale, exclusive, however, of an auxiliary shipping container enclosing packages
that individually conform to the requirements of this division. An individual
item or lot of any commodity not in package form, but on which there is marked
a selling price based on an established price per unit of weight or of measure,
shall be construed to be commodity in package form.
   Consumer package or package of consumer commodity shall mean a commodity in
package form that is customarily produced or distributed for sale through
retail sales agencies or instrumentalities for consumption by individuals, or
use by individuals for the purposes of personal care or in the performance of
services ordinarily rendered in or about the household or in connection with
personal possessions, and which usually is consumed or expended in the course
of such consumption or use.
   Cord, when used in connection with wood intended for fuel purposes or
pulpwood, shall mean the amount of wood that is contained in a space of 128
cubic feet when the wood is ranked and well stowed.
   Inspector shall mean a city inspector of weights and measures.
   Nonconsumer package or package of nonconsumer commodity shall mean any
commodity in package form other than a consumer package, and particularly a
package designed solely for industrial or institutional use or for wholesale
distribution only.
   Sell or sale shall mean barter and exchange.
   Supervisor shall mean the sealer of weights and measures for the city.
   Ton shall mean a unit of 2,000 pounds avoirdupois weight.
   Weight, in connection with any commodity, shall mean net weight.
   Weights and measures shall mean weights and measures of every kind,
instruments and devices for weighing and measuring, and any appliances and
accessories associated with any or all such instruments and devices, except
that the term shall not be construed to include meters for the measurement of
electricity, gas (natural or manufactured) or water or devices to measure the
usage of communications services when the same are operated in a public utility
system. Such devices or any appliances or accessories associated therewith, are
excluded from this division.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 3, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 12-972. - Sealer authorized.
   There shall be in the city a sealer known as the supervisor of weights and
measures, and such assistants as he may require who shall possess such powers
and perform such duties as are provided in this division.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 2, 11-4-81)

   The following abbreviations, and none other, may be employed in the quantity
statement on a package of commodity. Periods and plural forms are optional.
Normally, neither periods nor plural forms are used.

(Ord. No. 81-118, § 24, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-974. - Ambiguous terms.
   When the term "ounce" is employed in a declaration of liquid quantity, the
declaration shall identify the particular meaning of the term by use of the
term "fluid," however, this distinction may be omitted when, by association of
terms, the proper meaning is obvious; for example, one pint, four ounces. When
the declaration of quantity is in terms of the dry pint or dry quart, the
declaration shall include the word "dry."
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 25, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-975. - Systems and definitions recognized.
   The system of weights and measures in customary use in the United States and
the metric system of weights and measures are jointly recognized, and one or
the other of these systems shall be used for all commercial purposes in this
city. The definitions of basic units of weight and measure, the tables of
weight and measure, and weights and measures equivalents, as published by the
National Bureau of Standards, are recognized and shall govern weighing and
measuring equipment and transactions in this city.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-976. - City standards; verification; custody; enforcement; records.
   (a)   Weights and measures in conformity with the standards of the United
States, as have been supplied to the city by the federal government or
otherwise obtained by the city for use as city standards, when the same have
been certified as being satisfactory for use as such by the state department of
agriculture, shall be the city standards of weights and measures. The city
standards shall be tested for accuracy by the state department of agriculture
at least once every five years. The supervisor shall have custody of the city
standards and shall maintain such standards in good order and take all
necessary precaution for their safekeeping.
   (b)   The supervisor shall keep an accurate record of all his official acts,
shall enforce the provisions of this division and he shall have general
supervision over the weights and measures offered for sale, sold or in use in
this city.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-977. - Specifications, tolerances and regulations; correct apparatus;
incorrect apparatus.
   The specifications, tolerances and regulations for commercial weighing and
measuring devices, together with amendments thereto, as recommended by the
National Bureau of Standards and published in National Bureau of Standards
Handbook 44 and supplements thereto, or in any publication revising or
superseding Handbook 44, shall be the specifications, tolerances and
regulations for commercial weighing and measuring devices of this city, except
as specifically modified, amended or rejected by a regulation issued by the
state department of agriculture. For the purposes of this division, apparatus
shall be deemed to be "correct" when it conforms to all applicable requirements
promulgated as specified in this section; other apparatus shall be deemed to be
"incorrect."
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-978. - Inspecting and testing of weights and measures.
   (a)   The supervisor may inspect, and test to ascertain if they are correct,
all weights and measures kept, offered or exposed for sale. He shall inspect,
and test to ascertain if they are correct, all weights and measures
commercially used in:
      (1)   Determining the weight, measurement or count of commodities or
things sold or offered or exposed for sale on the basis of weight or of measure
or count.
      (2)   Computing the basic charge or payment for services rendered on the
basis of weight or of measure or count.
   (b)   The supervisor shall inspect and test all weights and measures
enumerated in this division whenever any measure or measures are installed,
renewed or altered in any specified stand, store, conveyance, or establishment
or whenever a request to examine any particular measure or measures is filed
with his office.
   (c)   Fees.
      (1)   A fee shall be charged to the owner of a scale, weights, measure,
or weighing or measuring device for its inspection when:
         a.   The inspection is a regular inspection;
         b.   The inspection is a reinspection of a device that has been tested
and found incorrect; and
         c.   The inspection is performed at the request of the owner.
      (2)   Inspection fees shall be established by the police department and
approved by the chief of police; fees shall be based on costs connected with
the inspections and shall be reviewed on an annual basis.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 7, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 96-665, 4-2-96)
Sec. 12-979. - Investigation of complaints.
   The supervisor shall investigate complaints made to him concerning
violations of the provisions of this division and shall, upon his own
initiative, conduct such investigations as he deems advisable to develop
information on prevailing procedures in commercial quantity determination and
on possible violations of the provisions of this division and to promote the
general objective of accuracy in the determination and representation of
quantity in commercial transactions.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-980. - Weight, measurement, inspection of packages of commodities,
sampling procedures.
   The supervisor, as often as he deems advisable, shall weigh, measure or
inspect packages or amounts of commodities offered or exposed for sale, sold or
in the process of delivery, to determine whether they contain the amounts
represented and whether they be offered or exposed for sale, or sold in
accordance with law. When such packages or amounts of commodities are found not
to contain the amounts represented, or are found to be kept, or offered or
exposed for sale in violation of law, the supervisor may order their sale
discontinued and may so mark or tag them as to show them to be illegal. The
supervisor may employ recognized sampling procedures under which the compliance
of a given lot of packages will be determined on the basis of the result
obtained on a sample selected from a representative of such lot.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-981. - Stop-use orders, stop-removal orders, removal orders.
   The supervisor may issue stop-use orders, stop-removal orders or removal
orders with respect to weights and measures being or susceptible of being
commercially used. He may issue stop-removal orders or removal orders with
respect to packages or amounts of commodities kept, offered or exposed for
sale, sold or in process of delivery, whenever in the course of his enforcement
of the provisions of this division he deems it necessary or expedient to issue
such orders. No person shall use, remove from the premises specified, or fail
to remove from the premises specified any weight, measure, package or amount of
commodity contrary to the terms of any order issued pursuant to this section.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-982. - Approval, rejection, condemnation, confiscation; enforcement,
seizure.
   The supervisor shall approve for use and seal or mark with appropriate
devices such weights and measures as he finds upon inspection or test to be
"correct," as defined in section
12-977. He shall reject or condemn and seal or mark as "rejected" or
"condemned" such weights and measures as he finds upon inspection or test to be
"incorrect," as defined in section
12-977. Sealing or marking shall not be required with respect to weights and
measures of such character or size that such sealing or marking would be
inappropriate, impractical or damaging to the apparatus in question. The
supervisor shall reject or condemn and may seize and destroy weights and
measures found to be incorrect. Weights and measures that have been rejected or
condemned and ordered corrected or disposed of may be confiscated and may be
destroyed by the supervisor, if not corrected as required by, or if disposed of
contrary to the requirements of section
12-984. The supervisor may seize for use as evidence without formal warrant
incorrect or unsealed weights and measures or amounts or packages of
commodities found to be used, retained, offered or exposed for sale, or sold in
violation of law. In the performance of his official duties, he may enter and
go into or upon without formal warrant any structure or premises.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-983. - Delegated powers of inspectors.
   The powers and duties given to and imposed upon the supervisor by this
division are hereby given to and imposed upon his assistants and inspectors
when acting under the instructions and at the direction of the supervisor.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-984. - Rejected or condemned weights and measures; disposition.
   Weights and measures that have been rejected or condemned and ordered
corrected or disposed of under the authority of the supervisor shall remain
subject to the control of the supervisor until such time as suitable repair or
disposition thereof has been made pursuant to this section. The owners of such
rejected or condemned weights and measures shall cause the same to be made
correct within a specified period authorized by the supervisor, or may dispose
of the same but only in such manner as is specifically authorized by the
supervisor.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-985. - Commodities, liquid, nonliquid, measurement; exceptions.
   (a)   Commodities in liquid form shall be sold only by liquid measure or by
weight, and commodities not in liquid form shall be sold only by weight,
measure, or by count. However, liquid commodities may be sold by weight and
nonliquid commodities may be sold by count only if such methods give accurate
information as to the quantity of commodity sold. This section shall not apply
to:
      (1)   Commodities sold for immediate consumption on the premises where
sold.
      (2)   Vegetables sold by the head or bunch.
      (3)   Commodities in containers standardized by a law of this state or by
federal law.
      (4)   Commodities in package form when there exists a general consumer
usage to express the quantity in some other manner.
   (b)   It shall be the responsibility of the supervisor to assure that
amounts of commodities sold are determined in accordance with good commercial
practice and are so determined and represented as to be accurate and
informative to all parties in interest.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-986. - Package labels—Contents; allowable variations.
   (a)   Except as otherwise provided in this division, any commodity in
package form kept for the purpose of sale, or offered or exposed for sale,
shall bear on the outside of the package such definite, plain, legible and
conspicuous declarations of:
      (1)   The identity of the commodity in the package by its common or usual
name, description, or generic term, unless the same can easily be identified
through the wrapper or container.
      (2)   The net quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure or
count, but the term "when packed" or any words of similar import, or any term
qualifying a unit of weight, measure or count, such as "jumbo," "giant," "full"
or the like, that tend to exaggerate the amount of commodity in a package,
shall not be used.
      (3)   The name and address of the manufacturer, packer or distributor in
the case of any package kept, offered or exposed for sale, or sold any place
other than on the premises where packed.
   (b)   The supervisor shall permit reasonable variations which may include
variations below the declared weight or measure caused by ordinary and
customary exposure to conditions that normally occur in good distribution
practice and that unavoidably result in decreased weight or measure. Such
allowable variations shall provide for exemptions for small packages and for
commodities put up in variable weights or sizes for sale intact and either
customarily not sold as individual units or customarily weighed or measured at
time of sale to the consumer.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-987. - Same—Random weights, measures or counts, additional
declarations.
   In addition to the declarations required by section
12-986, any commodity in package form, which package is one of a lot containing
random weights, measures or counts of the same commodity and bears the total
selling price of the package, shall bear on the outside of the package a plain
and conspicuous declaration of the price per single unit of weight, measure or
count.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-988. - Packages—Misleading wrappers.
   Any commodity in package form shall not be so wrapped, nor shall it be in a
container so made, formed or filled as to mislead the purchaser as to the
quantity of the contents of the package.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-989. - Same—Advertisement, declaration of quantity.
   Whenever a commodity in package form is advertised in any manner and the
retail price of the package is stated in the advertisement, there shall be
closely and conspicuously associated with such statement of price a declaration
of the basic quantity of contents of the package as is required by law or
regulation to appear on the package, except that this section shall not apply
to products for agricultural or horticultural use where the custom is to state
the number of objects or amount of area which can be treated per package unit
and the number or area is so stated. Where the law or regulation requires the
declaration of net quantity to appear on the package in terms of more than one
unit of weight or measure, only the smallest unit of weight or measure need be
stated in the advertisement. In connection with the declaration the qualifying
term "when packaged" or any other words of similar import, or any term
qualifying a unit of weight, measure or count, for example, "jumbo," "giant,"
"full" and the like that tends to exaggerate the amount of commodity in the
package, shall not be used.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-990. - Commodities; sale by weight, net weight.
   When any commodity is sold on the basis of weight, the net weight of the
commodity shall be employed and all contracts concerning commodities shall be
so construed.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-991. - Meat, meat products, poultry and seafood sold by weight; food
combination sold by weight, quantity representation by total weight of product
or combination.
   Except for immediate consumption on the premises where sold, or as one of
several elements comprising a ready-to-eat meal sold as a unit for consumption
elsewhere than on the premises where sold, all meat, meat products, poultry,
whole or parts, and all seafood except shellfish, offered or exposed for sale,
or sold, as food shall be offered or exposed for sale and sold by weight. When
meat, poultry or seafood is combined with or associated with some other food
element or elements to form either a distinctive food product or a food
combination, such food product or combination shall be offered or exposed for
sale and sold by weight, and the quantity representation may be the total
weight of the product or combination, and a quantity representation need not be
made for each of the several elements of the product or combination.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-992. - Commodity or service; sale by weight, measure or count;
misrepresentation; display of price including fraction of a cent.
   Whenever any commodity or service is sold, or is offered, exposed or
advertised for sale, by weight, measure or count, the price shall not be
misrepresented, nor shall the price be represented in any manner calculated or
tending to mislead or deceive an actual or prospective purchaser. Whenever an
advertised, posted or labeled price per unit of weight, measure or count
includes a fraction of a cent, all elements of the fraction shall be
prominently displayed, and the numeral or numerals expressing the fraction
shall be immediately adjacent to, of the same general design and style as, and
at least one-half the height and width of the numerals representing the whole
cents.
(Ord. No. 81-118, § 21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 12-993. - Truckloads of commodities.
   (a)   A delivery of any produce, coal, coke, sand, gravel or any other
commodity, product or merchandise sold in bulk form by weight, measure or count
in truckload or partial truckload quantity shall be accompanied by duplicate
delivery tickets, which shall clearly state, in ink or other indelible
substance, the name and address of the vendor, the name and address of the
purchaser, identity of merchandise being delivered and the net quantity of the
