*** ARTICLE III. - SNOW REMOVAL ***
Sec. 13-71. - Sidewalks and areas to be cleared.
   (a)   No occupant of any premises or owner of premises or property shall
fail to keep the sidewalks in front of or adjacent to such premises or property
clear of ice and/or snow, so far as to facilitate pedestrian use. Where there
are no sidewalks, no such occupant or owner shall fail to clear a path free
from snow and ice, when such a path will provide an extension of existing
sidewalk on an adjacent property.
   (b)   Reserved.
(Ord. No. 11-1315, 3-7-11)
Sec. 13-72. - Discarding snow and ice.
   (a)   Untreated snow may be deposited on a neighbor's unpaved property in
such a way that the necessity for clearing paved areas can be met in the most
reasonable way. Homeowners should put the snow closest to their property on
their own property and only use a neighbor's property when reasonable given
proximity and structural barriers. No snow shall be deposited on a neighbor's
property in such a way that windows, vents, driveways, or pedestrian walkways
are blocked.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person, at any time, to deposit any
accumulation of snow or ice upon the traveled portion of any street or highway,
or upon any public sidewalk, or upon any municipally owned or leased parking
lot, anywhere within the city.
(Ord. No. 11-1315, 3-7-11)
Sec. 13-73. - Responsibility for repairs.
   Any person who removes snow for hire within the city shall be responsible
for the repair of any damages to public or private property.
Sec. 13-74. - Violations.
   (a)   If any occupant or property owner shall fail to clear an accumulation
of ice or snow from the sidewalk adjoining his property within a reasonable
time, or shall otherwise permit ice or snow to accumulate on the sidewalk in a
dangerous manner, that person shall be guilty of a violation of this article.
   (b)   Any snowplow operator who fails to repair damages to any public or
private property within the time period agreed shall be guilty of a violation
of this article.
   (c)   Violations of this article shall be punishable by a fine of not less
than $50.00 for each offense, plus the cost of removing snow and ice or
repairing damages to public or private property.
(Ord. No. 11-1315, 3-7-11)
Sec. 13-75. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 11-1315, adopted March 7, 2011, deleted §
13-75, which pertained to waiver of provisions.
Secs. 13-76—13-95. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE IV. - SMOKE ABATEMENT ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 13-96. - Short title.
   The short title of the article hereinafter set forth shall be the "Smoke
Abatement Ordinance."
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 1.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-97. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Air pollution means the discharging from stacks, chimneys, exhausts, vents,
ducts, openings, open bonfires, or material or stock piles, of any smoke, soot,
fly ash, cinders, noxious acids, fumes, oxides, injurious gases, vapors, or
dust that cause contamination in the air in amounts detrimental to the public
health and welfare or to property, in amounts prohibited by this article.
   Baffling means any row, rows, plane or planes of refractory or other
material that causes the gases in a steam boiler or other vessel or device to
assume a definite and predetermined path of travel before reaching the chimney
or smoke stack.
   Board means the board of appeals, as created by this article.
   Cinders means particles not ordinarily considered as fly ash or dust,
because of their greater size, resulting from the process of combustion and
consisting essentially of fused ash or unburned combustibles.
   Combustion equipment means any furnace, incinerator, refuse-burning
equipment, fuel-burning equipment, boiler, apparatus, stoker, device,
mechanism, stack, or structure used in the process of burning fuel or
combustible material.
   Department means the department of building and safety.
   Director means the director of the building and safety department.
   Dust means any gas-borne or airborne particles larger than one micron in
average diameter.
   Dust collectors shall mean cyclone centrifugal effect collectors, screen
cloth (bag type) wet type filters or those using charcoal, spun glass fibers or
other material as a filter. Contact, impact baffled, or adhesive collectors,
spray centrifugal type washers, filter towers, electric precipitators, gravity
type dust or settling chambers, and verticose effect collectors, either single
or in batteries, shall also be included in the meaning of "dust collectors."
   Fly ash shall mean gas-borne or airborne particles larger than one micron
and consisting essentially of fused ash or burned or unburned combustible
material.
   Fumes shall mean gases, vapors, metallic oxides, or odors that are of such
character as to create an unclean, destructive, offensive, or unhealthful
condition.
   Furnace volume shall mean that volume which is above the fuel bed and in
front of the bridgewall. In case of horizontal fire box boilers, it is that
volume measured to the front tube sheet. In the case of vertical tubular
boilers, it is that volume measured to the lower tube sheet.
   Heating surface means any boiler surface having water on one side and hot
gases on the other side not excepting any surface covered by the arches or
refractory used in the construction of the boiler furnace.
   Injurious gases means any gases of such character and quantity which injure
the health or property of the individual or the public.
   Noxious acids means anhydrous or hydrous acids existing in concentrations
high enough to be poisonous or to constitute a nuisance.
   Open fire means any fire wherein the products of combustion are emitted into
the open air and are not directed thereto through a stack or chimney.
   Ringlemann chart means the Ringlemann chart with instructions for use, as
published by the United States Bureau of Mines.
   Smoke means small gas-borne particles consisting essentially of carbonaceous
material in sufficient number to be observable.
   Soot shall mean a collection of particles consisting essentially of
carbonaceous material.
   Smokeless solid fuel means, for the purpose of this article, a fuel, the
volatile content of which is 23 percent or less on an ash and moisture-free
basis; provided however, that if a fuel contains volatile matter in excess of
23 percent on an ash and moisture-free basis, it shall be acceptable under the
terms of this article if it meets the same standards with regards to smoke
production as that of a fuel containing less than 23 percent volatile matter on
an ash and moisture-free basis; provided, further, that the following
conditions shall apply in order to ascertain whether or not such standards are
met in the case of violation:
   First, complete specifications of the fuel and description of its processing
or manufacture must be submitted to the division, and, from time to time, any
additional information that may be reasonably required must also be submitted.
   Second, an adequate supply of the finished product must be made available to
the division to conduct whatever tests are deemed necessary to establish its
value as a smokeless fuel.
   Third, field tests may be required to determine if such fuels can be so
fired as to comply with the provisions of this article.
   Fourth, any person whose product is submitted to such tests must pay all
expenses necessary to the attendant tests, and the division shall furnish such
person a copy of the report showing the results of such tests.
   Fifth, the enforcement of this section, with reference to the volatility
standard for fuel, shall not apply to hand-fired combustion equipment in
buildings containing not more than four one-family dwelling units, until
February 1, 1952, after which date all of the provisions of this section shall
apply to such equipment.
   Solid fuel means any mined, packaged, or prepared coal, coke, petroleum
coke, carbonized coal, either natural or manufactured, synthetic, processed or
patented fuel, not sold by liquid or metered measure.
   Stack or chimney means flue, conduit, or opening arranged for emitting gases
into the open air.
   Surface burning equipment means any combustion equipment in which the fresh
fuel can be thrown directly on the hot fuel bed.
   Umbrascope means an instrument consisting of an open tube through which
observations are made to measure the density of smoke. One end of the tube is
closed except for a small opening serving as an eye-piece. At the other end,
which is open, there are four semicircular glass lightfilters, so adapted as to
cover a maximum of one-half the field of vision, and so arranged as to allow
their use singly or collectively for measuring the relative density of smoke
against the sky. The results are then compared with the Ringlemann chart and
the proper reading obtained.
   Volatile means the gaseous constituents of solid fuel, as determined by the
standard American Society of Testing Materials Procedure, amended or revised to
date.
(Ord. No. 81-73, §§ 1.2, 1.3, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Secs. 13-98—13-110. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT **
Sec. 13-111. - Air pollution unlawful.
   Air pollution caused by the escape of smoke, cinders, noxious acids, fumes,
injurious gases, dust or fly ash is hereby declared to be unlawful and to be a
nuisance. It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to operate or cause
to be operated any combustion equipment in such manner that it produces air
pollution within the meaning of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-112. - Emission of smoke.
   It shall be unlawful within the city for any person to cause, permit or
allow the emission of any smoke from any source whatever of a density equal to
or greater than that density shown by diagram No. 2 on the Ringlemann chart,
set forth in sectiion 13-116; provided, however, this article shall not apply
to:
      (1)   Residences having therein less than four dwelling units.
      (2)   Smoke of a shade of appearance equal to but not greater than that
shown by diagram No. 2 on the Ringlemann chart for a period not to exceed four
minutes in any single period of 30 minutes; provided, further, that the
restrictions in this section herein shall not apply to railroads, roundhouses
and locomotives.
      (3)   A firebox, furnace boiler, or other combustible equipment which is
being cleaned out or in which a new fire is being built and which emits smoke
of a shade or appearance no greater than that shown by diagram No. 3 of the
Ringlemann chart for a period of not to exceed three minutes in any single
period of 15 minutes.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-113. - Escape of soot.
   It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to cause, suffer, permit, or
allow any soot, cinders, noxious acids, fumes, injurious gases, fly ash, or
dust to escape into the air beyond the boundaries of his own property in such
amounts that such soot, cinders, noxious acids, fumes, injurious gases, fly
ash, or dust shall be injurious to the property of others, to any person who is
outside the boundaries of the property from which such materials are escaping,
or to the public; or to endanger the health, comfort, welfare, convenience, or
safety of any such person or of the public; or to escape in such manner or
amount as to cause or have a tendency to cause injury or damage to property or
persons.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-114. - Unlawful to operate equipment emitting fly ash, soot or air-
borne solids: amounts.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to operate or cause to
be operated, maintain or cause to be maintained, any process or operation which
produces gas, airborne solids or fumes, or furnace to combustion device for the
burning of coal or other natural or synthetic fuels, without maintaining and
operating, while using such process or furnace or combustion device, recognized
and approved equipment, means, method, device, or contrivance to reduce the
quantity of gas or airborne solids or fumes emitted into the open air, which is
operated in conjunction with such process, furnace, or combustion device so
that the quantity of gas or airborne solids shall not exceed 0.20 grains per
cubic foot of the carrying medium when corrected to a temperature of 500
degrees Fahrenheit, and adjusted to 50 percent excess air at full load. The
A.S.M.E. test code for dust-separating apparatus, or any other generally
recognized standard or method of measurement which is acceptable to the
division, shall be used for determining the weight of the airborne solids
discharged to the atmosphere.
   (b)   The above regulation shall not apply to incineration units whose
capacity, as rated under this article, does not exceed 60 pounds per hour. The
allowable discharge of fly ash, soot, or air-borne solids to the atmosphere for
incineration units up to 60 pounds per hour per square foot of grate area shall
not exceed 0.30 grains per cubic foot of the carrying medium, when corrected to
500 degrees Fahrenheit and adjusted to 50 percent excess air at full load.
   (c)   It is also hereby expressly prohibited and unlawful for any person to
engage in the burning of any material whatsoever in an open manner, such as
wire baskets or drum type containers, when such materials are the result of any
commercial or industrial operation; provided, however, this regulation shall
not apply to single- and two-family residences; and provided, further, that the
board of appeals may grant a permit to an applicant to burn in an open manner
any such materials when it appears from the application that the materials to
be burned and the manner and plan of burning will not cause such air pollution
as is declared to be unlawful by this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-115. - Smoke inspector.
   (a)   There shall be a smoke inspector who shall be employed in the division
of the department whose qualifications shall be those specified by the
department and the civil service board.
   (b)   The smoke inspector shall make all annual inspections of combustion
equipment, as required by this article. He shall investigate all complaints for
violations of this article. He shall use the Ringlemann chart, or the
umbrascope in correlation with the Ringlemann chart, for the purpose of
determining violations of this article in the emission of smoke.
   (c)   He shall use any generally recognized methods and equipment for the
determination of violations of this article, or the superintendent, with the
approval of the director, may employ qualified experts to make such tests.
   (d)   The smoke inspector shall be responsible for enforcing the provisions
of this article. He may promulgate and advance an educational program for the
prevention or minimizing of smoke and air pollution under the supervision and
direction of the director.
   (e)   The director of the department shall designate one or more persons to
represent the city at any and all meetings of boards or committees organized
for the purpose of discussing or arbitrating smoke disputes involving the city.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-116. - Ringlemann chart and umbrascope.
   (a)   The standard by which the density of smoke is to be measured shall be
as set forth in the six numbered diagrams of the Ringlemann chart, as published
by the United States Bureau of Mines, which diagrams showing the respective
percentages of black area are as follows:
   (b)   Use of the chart will be made by placing it at such distance from the
observer so that the squares appear as even shades of coloring or when no white
spaces between the lines are visible. Comparison of the smoke under observation
with the various shades of the diagrams will then indicate the density of the
smoke. Observation at all times shall be not less than 100 feet nor more than
one-quarter mile from the smoke observed.
   (c)   The umbrascope may be used by the smoke inspector or other observer in
determining the density of smoke, but it shall be used in correlation with the
Ringlemann chart.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-117. - Permits and certificates.
   (a)   No person shall construct, install or alter any combustion equipment,
or any equipment pertaining thereto for use within the city, until an
application including suitable plans and specifications of the combustion
equipment and structures of buildings used in connection therewith has been
filed in the the department of building and safety; has been approved by the
smoke inspector; and an installation permit issued for such construction,
installation or alteration; provided, however, that maintenance repairs or
minor alterations, which do not change the capacity of such combustion
equipment and which do not include any change in the method of combustion and
the expense of which covering labor and materials does not exceed $50.00, may
be made without an installation permit; and provided further, that emergency
repairs for which an installation permit would ordinarily be required may be
made before applying for or securing an installation permit, when necessary if
an emergency arises and serious consequences would result if the repairs were
to be deferred; provided further, that in the case of such emergency repairs, a
permit therefor shall be secured on the first business day following the
starting of such repairs. Permits shall issue to the contractor or person
making the installation, alteration or repair of such combustion equipment.
   (b)   No person shall use, fire, or otherwise operate any combustion
equipment within the city until he has secured a certificate of operation. A
certificate of operation shall be issued only after the combustion equipment
has been installed, and such installation approved by the smoke inspector.
Certificates of operation shall be renewable annually after an inspection of
the combustion equipment by the smoke inspector and his approval thereof.
   (c)   There shall be no charge for an installation permit or for a
certificate of operation. Fees shall be charged for inspections as provided in
this division.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-118. - Preexisting and nonconforming combustion equipment; temporary
certificate.
   (a)   Every person who owns or operates combustion equipment which was
installed prior to November 13, 1981, and for which a certificate of operation
is required, shall apply for a certificate of operation within 12 months from
such date. Upon receiving each application, the smoke inspector shall inspect
the combustion equipment therein described and, if approved by him, shall
recommend issuance of a certificate of operation, valid for one year from the
date of issuance. If the combustion equipment is not so approved, the smoke
inspector shall specify the necessary repairs or alterations which shall be
made.
   (b)   The owner or operator may appeal from the decision of the smoke
inspector to the board. If the board finds that hardship or injustice will be
done in carrying out the charges specified by the smoke inspector, the board
may affirm, modify or reverse the decision of the smoke inspector, and, if it
so decides, it may grant a temporary certificate of operation for the
combustion equipment pending its alteration or repair, but no such temporary
certificate of operation shall be granted for a longer period of time than one
year.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-119. - Annual inspection.
   (a)   An annual inspection of all combustion equipment, dust producing or
dust collecting equipment or any other devices or apparatus connected with or
pertaining to any process or operation which discharges into the air dust,
fumes, soot, fly ash, cinders, noxious acids or gases, as described in this
article, whether or not a previous certificate of operation has been issued by
the superintendent, shall be made to determine that such equipment can be
operated in such manner that it will comply with the provisions of this
article. However, no annual inspection shall be required in cases of furnaces
or other combustion equipment or devices installed to heat buildings used
exclusively for private residences.
   (b)   Upon determining that the equipment complies with the provisions of
the article, a certificate of operation shall be issued, which shall be posted
in a conspicuous place within the building or plant.
   (c)   If at the time of any inspection, it is found that the combustion
equipment is in such condition that it cannot be operated within the provisions
of this article, the smoke inspector shall give notice in writing to the person
owning, operating or in charge of such equipment of the defects found and an
order to correct, repair or replace the defective equipment. Failure to comply
with this order within 30 days from its date shall constitute a violation of
this article, and the smoke inspector may institute the necessary proceedings
to invoke the penalties as hereinafter provided or to abate the nuisance if one
exists.
   (d)   Fees for incinerator installation and annual inspection of dust
collecting equipment will be governed by the building code.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-120. - Railroad locomotives; roundhouses.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful within the city for any person to permit the
emission of any smoke from any railroad locomotive or roundhouse of a density
greater than that density described as No. 2 on the Ringlemann chart; provided,
however, that the following exceptions to the provisions of this section shall
be permitted:
      (1)   Smoke, the shade or appearance of which is equal to but not darker
than No. 3 of the Ringlemann chart, will be permitted for a period of one
minute in any 15-minute period when the locomotive is in service, for the
duration of one year from November 13, 1981.
      (2)   Smoke, the shade or appearance of which is equal to but not darker
than No. 3 of the Ringlemann chart, for a period or periods aggregating three
minutes in every 15 minutes when building a new fire or when breakdown of
equipment in roundhouses occurs such as to make it evident that the emission
was not reasonably preventable.
      (3)   Roundhouses and fire-building stations shall be subject to annual
inspection, as provided in this article.
   (b)   Failure on the part of any person, railroad company, corporation,
association or their agents to provide the necessary means, equipment or device
to prevent the emission of smoke and pollution of air, as prohibited by this
article, or failure to instruct the operating crews, enginemen, firemen,
hostlers or others about proper operation of such locomotives shall be deemed a
violation of this article and shall be subject to the penalties and abatement
as herein provided.
   (c)   Failure of the operating crews, enginemen, firemen, hostlers or others
to comply with the provisions of this article shall be deemed a violation of
this article and shall be subject to the penalties herein provided.
(Ord. No. 81-73, §§ 2.10, 2.11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-121. - Smoke indicators.
   (a)   All combustion equipment that heat boilers having more than 200 square
feet of boiler heating surface, or combustion equipment equivalent thereto,
except combustion equipment which uses gas or electricity as fuel, shall be
equipped with smoke indicators, mirrors or similar devices approved by the
smoke inspector to enable the fireman to observe the top of his stack or stacks
from the boiler room at all times, unless the top of the stack is readily
visible to the fireman from the boiler room without the use of such devices. In
plants where a fireman is not in constant attendance in the boiler room or
furnace room, the smoke indicator shall be of a type which will sound an alarm
or flash a signal to attract the attention of the fireman when smoke is being
emitted that violates the provisions of this article.
   (b)   The owner of any plant which emits smoke prohibited by this article
shall be subject to prosecution pursuant to this article if the owner refuses
for a period of 20 days to comply with the provisions of this section upon
demand by the smoke inspector.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-122. - Smokeless solid fuel.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person or his agents to import, sell,
offer for sale, expose for sale, exchange, deliver or transport for use or
consumption in the city, or to use or consume in the city any solid fuel for
handfiring or intermittent feeding of surface-burning types of equipment which
does not meet the standards of a smokeless solid fuel; provided, however, that
the term "hand firing or intermittent feeding of surface-burning types of
equipment" is hereby specifically declared not to include "downdraft boilers";
provided, further, that the importation, delivery or transportation of such
fuel by railroad companies and other common carriers, in the course of their
common carrier business, shall not be deemed to be a violation of the
provisions of this section.
   (b)   The director shall, upon request, furnish a list of brands or trade
names of smokeless solid fuels, which have been tested for conformity with the
provisions of this article and which, as a result of such tests, have been
approved.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-123. - Solid fuels in mechanical combustion equipment.
   A solid fuel not meeting the requirements of this article for a smokeless
solid fuel may be used or consumed only in approved mechanical combustion
equipment or devices, as specified in this article; provided, however, that
after suitable inspections and tests have proven to the division that any
combination of combustion equipment or devices and fuel satisfactorily comply
with the provisions of this article, the director shall approve the use of such
combination of combustion equipment or devices and fuel. 
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-124. - Duty of owner to report.
   (a)   It shall be the duty of all persons purchasing combustion equipment,
except repair parts and minor accessories, which is required to be connected to
a vent or stack, to report to the division the purchase of every such article
to be installed or used anywhere within the corporate limits of the city. The
report herein provided for shall be in writing and be delivered or mailed to
the division within seven days after such purchase and shall contain the name
and address of the purchaser and the location of the building in which each
article is to be installed or used.
   (b)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this requirement, or
making any false statement or report in connection with the purchase of any
such articles mentioned in this section, shall be subject to the fines and
penalties hereinafter set forth; provided, however, this requirement shall not
apply to wholesale transactions made for the purpose of resale.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-125. - Type of combustion equipment to be specified.
   (a)   No person or his agent shall purchase or contract to purchase for use
or consumption within the city any solid fuel without first informing the fuel
dealer as to the type of combustion equipment or device in which the fuel is to
be used and the type of fuel specified for use in such combustion equipment or
device, under the provisions of this article.
   (b)   The fuel dealer's records shall indicate, among other things, the type
of combustion equipment or devices and the type of fuel specified by the
purchaser and supplied by the fuel dealer.
   (c)   No fuel dealer shall supply fuel to a purchaser that is not approved
for use in the purchaser's combustion equipment or devices as provided in
section
13-133.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.16, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-126. - Plans to be filed for new equipment.
   Except in buildings used exclusively for residential purposes, containing
less than four one-family dwelling units or flats, no new fuel burning plant or
equipment which discharges dust into the air from its operation, or the
reconstruction, repair or addition to any existing fuel-burning plants for
producing power and heat, or either of them, or equipment for refuse-burning,
or equipment which discharges such dust, or any stack or furnace connected with
such fuel or refuse-burning or operating equipment, shall be installed,
erected, reconstructed, repaired or added to, or operated in the city until
plans and specifications for the same have been filed by the owner, contractor,
installer or other responsible person, in the department of building and safety
being so designed that the equipment can be managed and operated to conform to
the provisions of this article, and permit issued for such installation,
erection, reconstruction, addition to, or repair and operation, as specified in
this division.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-127. - Plans, what to show.
   (a)   Plans and specifications shall show the type of installation, the
amount of work and the amount of heating to be done by such fuel- or refuse-
burning equipment and all appurtenances thereto, including all provisions made
for the purpose of securing complete combustion of the fuel or refuse to be
used and the manner in which it is to be burned so as to prevent smoke and
other air pollution, as covered by this article.
   (b)   Such plans and specifications shall also contain a statement of the
rate of burning and kind of fuel or refuse proposed to be used and the manner
in which it is to be burned.
   (c)   Such plans shall further show the dimensions of the room in which such
fuel- or refuse-burning equipment is to be located, and the location and
dimensions of all stacks used in connection with or as a part of such fuel or
refuse-burning plant.
   (d)   The division may require such additional data as is deemed necessary
for the purpose of issuing a permit for the operation of such fuel-burning
devices, or dust producing or dust collecting equipment.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.18, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-128. - Approval of plans; payment of fees; issuance of permit.
   (a)   Upon the inspection and approval of such plans and specifications by
the department and upon payment of the fees set forth in this article, if such
plans and specifications shall show that adequate and approved conditions for
securing complete combustion of the fuel or refuse to be used and for
preventing of eliminating smoke, soot, cinders, fly ash, noxious acids, fumes,
gases or dust have been made, a permit for the installation or for the
construction, erection, reconstruction, repair, or addition to and operation of
such fuel or refuse-burning plant shall be issued.
   (b)   As soon as the permit has been issued, as above provided, it shall be
the duty of the various other inspectors in the department having charge of the
inspection of the premises wherein such fuel- or refuse-burning equipment is
located, to cooperate in seeing that the execution of the work authorized by
such permit is done in conformity with the approved plans and specifications,
and the standards, rules and regulations fixed by the department.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-129. - Failure to submit plans, seal.
   If plans and specifications, as described above, are not submitted to the
department for approval previous to the installation of any new fuel-burning
equipment, addition to or repair or reconstruction of any fuel-burning
equipment for producing power, heat, or either of them, or equipment for
burning refuse or equipment that is dust producing or dust collecting, or any
stack connected with such fuel- or refuse-burning or other equipment, the
division is authorized to seal immediately such equipment until the owner,
contractor, installer or other person has complied with these provisions.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.20, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-130. - Unlawful to use any equipment sealed.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to use any new, reconstructed, or
repaired equipment, or addition thereto, or any equipment duly sealed under the
provisions of this article, for the production or generation of heat and power,
or either of them, or for the burning of refuse or for dust collecting, or that
is dust producing, until he shall have first procured a certificate from the
division, certifying that the equipment is so constructed that it will do the
work required with the type of fuel and equipment used, and that, in the
opinion of the superintendent, it can consistently be operated in compliance
with the terms of this article when burning the type of fuel in the manner
specified in the permit, and until a notice of the size, type, kind of fuel and
the manner of burning the fuel, as specified in the permit, has been
prominently displayed and permanently attached to such equipment, or so it will
not emit dust or fumes contrary to the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-131. - Issuance of permit not to exempt a violator from prosecution.
   The issuance and delivery by the division of any permit or certificate for
the construction, reconstruction, alteration, repair, or addition thereto, of
any equipment, or stack connected with the equipment, or for the operation of
such equipment or stack shall not be held to exempt such person from
prosecution on account of the emission of dense smoke, fly ash, soot, cinders,
noxious acids, fumes, gases or dust caused or permitted by any such person.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-132. - Permit not to issue until plans approved.
   The department shall not issue a building permit for the erection,
construction, reconstruction or alteration of any building or structure where
the plans for such building or structure show any stack in connection with such
building or structure, until such plans have been submitted, the dimensions of
such stack approved as having sufficient capacity and as being suitable for the
type of equipment and fuel to be used.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.23, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-133. - Plans not to be approved if the fuel is not proper.
   The department shall not approve plans or issue permits for the installation
of any fuel-burning equipment or device of the surface-burning type, unless the
fuel to be used in such device shall be a smokeless solid fuel, or a mechanical
fuel-burning or other kind of device is to be used of a type which will so
operate as not to emit dense smoke or permit the escape of soot, cinders,
noxious acids, fumes, gases, fly ash or dust or otherwise pollute the air in
violation of the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.24, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-134. - Three or more violations, authorization to seal equipment.
   (a)   After any owner, agent, occupant, manager or lessee of any premises
has been previously notified of three or more violations of this article within
any consecutive 12-month period, in respect to the emission of smoke, soot,
cinders, noxious acids, fumes, gases, fly ash or dust, the owner, agent,
occupant, manager or lessee of such premises shall be notified to show cause
before the board of appeals not less than ten days after the date of notice,
why the equipment causing such violations should not be sealed, and such board
of appeals is hereby authorized and empowered to seal the equipment against
further use until compliance with the provisions of this article is made.
   (b)   The notice herein provided for may be given by mail directed to the
last known address of the party to be notified, or if such party or his
whereabouts is unknown, then by posting a notice on or near the premises at
which the violations have occurred. Upon such date the violator may appear and
be heard. If the board of appeals finds that adequate corrective means and
methods have not been employed to correct the cause of such conditions, then it
is hereby empowered to order such equipment sealed until such time as a permit
and certificate, as provided in this division, have been applied for and issued
for such plant.
   (c)   It shall be unlawful for any person to break a seal of any refuse-
burning equipment, any boiler or any fuel-burning equipment or device producing
heat or power or for regulating and collecting dust that has been sealed by the
department upon order of the board of appeals.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.25, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-135. - Refusal of certificate; sealing.
   When a certificate of operation is refused in the case of an original
inspection or in the case of an annual inspection, the department is authorized
to seal immediately the furnace or other combustion equipment or device until
the owner, lessee or other person required to procure the certificate of
operation shall have complied with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 2.26, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-136. - Violations.
   (a)   Any person who shall refuse to comply with or who shall violate or
assist in the violation of any of the provisions of this article; who, in any
manner, hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents, or in any way interferes
with the smoke inspector, or any police officer in the performance of any duty
in the administration or enforcement of this article; shall refuse to permit
such inspector, superintendent, or officer from performing his duty by refusing
them, or any of them, entrance at reasonable hours to any premises in which the
provisions of this article are being violated; or shall refuse to permit the
inspection or examination of such building, establishment, premises,
enclosures, or open areas for the purpose of the administration or enforcement
of this article shall be subject to the abatement thereof or to the fines and
penalties provided in this section.
   (b)   Air pollution may be abated by filing injunctive proceedings in the
county circuit court by the smoke inspector. The right to such abatement shall
be cumulative and shall be in addition to the fines and penalties hereinafter
specified.
   (c)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this article shall, upon
conviction thereof, be subject to a fine not exceeding the sum of $500.00 or
imprisonment for a period not exceeding 90 days, or both such fine and
imprisonment in the discretion of the court.
(Ord. No. 81-73, §§ 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 11-4-81)
Secs. 13-137—13-145. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - WORK CODE **
Sec. 13-146. - Chimneys and stacks.
   (a)   Chimneys shall be of such height to produce sufficient available draft
to supply a proper amount of air to burn, without excessive smoke, the maximum
amount of fuel that is to be consumed, and to overcome draft loss or
restrictions in furnace, boiler setting, gas passages, damper openings,
breechings and stacks. The chimney must be of sufficient cross sectional area
to allow the free, unrestricted discharge of the products of combustion.
   (b)   For high pressure boilers the height and dimensions of the chimney
shall be figured in accordance with any acceptable formula, but in no case
shall such height and dimensions be less than that specified in Table 1,
hereinafter set forth, without specific approval of the board of appeals after
hearing thereon, as herein provided.
   (c)   For low pressure heating boilers the height and dimensions of the
stack may be figured in accordance with any acceptable formula, but in no case
shall the height and dimensions be less than that specified in Table 2,
hereinafter set forth, without specific approval of the board of appeals after
hearing thereon, as herein provided.
   (d)   No smokestack or chimney, irrespective of the provisions of the
preceding subsections (b) and (c), shall be installed with less cross sectional
area than those recommended by the manufacturers of the boiler or boilers
connected thereto.
   (e)   All incinerator stacks and other chimneys, smokestacks, or flues which
emit sparks in sufficient amount or size to cause a hazard to buildings or
surrounding property, shall be equipped with a spark arrester of suitable size
and construction to prevent the emission of such sparks.
   (f)   All stacks and chimneys and parts thereof or appurtenances thereto
shall be constructed in accordance with the provisions of the official building
code of the city and of this article.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-147. - Incinerators—Generally.
   (a)   All incinerators creating a nuisance under the provisions of this
article shall be equipped with gas washing devices, settling chambers or other
approved devices for the elimination of the nuisance, if the smoke inspector
determines that such devices will correct the existing nuisance.
   (b)   Hereafter, every building, except single- and two-family residences,
which is built in the city, shall be equipped with an incinerator, or where
alterations to existing buildings require structural changes which increase the
floor area by ten percent, or where the occupancy of an existing building has a
rubbish load in excess of two bushels per day, shall be equipped for burning in
an incinerator, in connection with such building, all rubbish and combustible
material of all kinds which might be produced or picked up or brought into such
building, it being hereby required that such incinerator shall be equipped to
add natural or artificial gas or fuel oil in suitable quantities to supplement,
if necessary, the incineration process, such incinerator shall be of sufficient
size to dispose of all combustible wastes from the premises; provided, however,
that any existing mercantile, manufacturing, business or trade establishment
which shall produce rubbish or wastes in excess of two bushels per day shall be
required to install adequate incineration for same within 90 days from November
13, 1981; provided, further, that if any such existing mercantile,
manufacturing, business, or trade establishment operates in more than one
building or location in the city under the same ownership, the requirements of
this section will be satisfied if one adequate incinerator facility is acquired
by such establishment; provided, further, that if any such existing mercantile,
manufacturing, business or trade establishment shall dispose of all such
rubbish or wastes on or before the close of each business day by dumping or
otherwise disposing of it at a duly authorized location, either within or
without the limits of the city, the requirements of this section will be
satisfied without the necessity of installing or acquiring an incinerator, in
accordance with the provisions of this article; provided, further, that if the
need for storing excess refuse, rubbish, or wastes shall arise at any time,
such material shall be stored only in a separate fireproof inclosure,
consisting of eight-inch masonry walls and four-inch reinforced concrete
ceiling, or equal, with a class A firedoor, in accordance with requirements of
the building code, such inclosure shall always be under lock and key, and such
material shall be removed the following workday.
   (c)   No incinerator shall burn garbage or food waste so as to create a
nuisance. If garbage is burned, secondary fuel will be required.
   (d)   The details of construction of incinerators using over two bushels per
day must be shown on a plan sealed by a registered engineer or architect or on
plans approved by a combustion engineer. Three sets of plans must accompany
each application for an incinerator permit, and the plans shall be checked for
compliance by the plan examiner, civil engineer and smoke inspector.
   (e)   Approved fly ash collection facilities need not be furnished on
installation where the burning rate of such incinerator does not exceed 60
pounds per hour, as outlined under this article, unless it can be demonstrated
that the discharged amounts of fly ash are in excess of those amounts permitted
in this article.
   (f)   Chimneys and stacks shall comply with the requirements of the building
code.
(Ord. No. 81-73, §§ 3.2, 3.2-A, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-148. - Same—Fuel.
   (a)   All incinerators creating a nuisance under the provisions of this
article shall be equipped with gas washing devices, settling chambers or other
approved devices for the elimination of the nuisance, if the superintendent
determines that such devices will correct the existing nuisance.
   (b)   All incinerators which shall be built, altered or remodeled, or those
existing, shall use one of the following classifications of fuels for purposes
of construction design only.
      (1)   Fuel analysis, type 1 fuel. Rubbish, consisting of 75 percent dry
combustible waste and moisture not to exceed 25 percent by weight. The term
"rubbish" means fuel made up of combustible waste such as paper, rags, scrap
wood, cartons, floor sweepings and by-products of industrial waste from
manufacturing operations. In commercial operations it consists of all wrapping
waste and offal from such operations. The 25 percent moisture represents normal
moisture content in dry waste materials. Type 1 fuel is based on not more than
8,000 Btu per pound, having ten percent ash and 65 percent fuel. Secondary
auxiliary fuel may be required in this type.
      (2)   Type 2 fuel. Garbage, consisting of 65 percent wet materials and 35
percent dry materials. The term "garbage" means fuel made up of food wastes and
spoilage from hotels, restaurants, hospitals, markets and like installations.
Seventy-five percent of the wet materials is moisture, and 35 percent of the
total load is rubbish, containing up to 25 percent moisture, ash and
noncombustible eight percent, as charged. This type of fuel has 5,000 Btu per
pound, as fired. Auxiliary fuel must be provided with Type 2 fuel, both primary
and secondary.
      (3)   Type 3 fuel. Refuse consisting of an even mixture of rubbish and
garbage. This type of waste is common to industrial, commercial and
institutional installations combining accumulation of combustible waste and
garbage from cafeteria and food preparation work. Auxiliary fuel must be
provided for Type 3 fuel.
      (4)   Type 4 fuel. Human and animal remains and pathological waste which
require primary and secondary auxiliary fuel, as dictated by individual job
analysis.
      (5)   Type 5 fuel. Byproduct waste, gaseous, liquid or semi-liquid,
noxious or contaminated, of density and viscosity that will be burned through
air or pressure atomizing burner equipment. Btu values must be set on
individual materials to be destroyed.
      (6)   Type 6 fuel. Byproduct waste, semi and solid, toxic or otherwise,
to be direct charged on hearth, or refractory crucible.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-B, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-149. - Classification of incinerators.
   All incinerators which shall be built, altered or remodeled in the city
shall use one of the following classifications for purposes of a permit and
construction only.
      (1)   Class I residential, basement fed, wall and portable, direct fed.
Normal disposal of Type 1 fuel.
      (2)   Class II apartment and multiple dwelling, flue fed destructor type.
Normal disposal of Type 1 and 3 fuel.
      (3)   Class III commercial destructor type, designed for either Type 1 or
3 fuel, as demanded by particular occupancy.
      (4)   Class IV industrial, heavy-duty destructor type, normally
destroying Type 1 and 3 fuel in varying quantities.
      (5)   Class V municipal, destructor type, destroying Type 3, 4, 5, or 6
fuel in large quantities.
      (6)   Class VI crematory and pathological units, normal destruction of
Type 4 fuel.
      (7)   Class VII retort type equipment, designed for specific byproduct
waste fuel, Type 5 or 6.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-C, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-150. - Flue fed incinerators.
   (a)   All apartment and multiple dwellings shall be equipped with an
approved incinerator of a Class II type. Flue fed equipment requires a separate
flue for incinerator use only. Basement installations may be brick set or steel
casing type. All brick set units shall use a minimum 4½ inches of refractory
lining (33 to 34 P.C.E.) for grate burning areas up to nine square feet. Grate
burning areas exceeding nine square feet using a brick setting shall use 4½
inches refractory lining of a 33 to 34 P.C.E. and an eight-inch common brick
exterior wall. Ash pit and secondary combustion areas shall be lined with a
minimum of two inches of approved insulating material where same is constructed
on concrete slab.
   (b)   Minimum flue requirements for new construction shall be 12 inches × 12
inches. Each flue lining shall be built of an approved refractory 4½ inches
thick, 30 feet above the breeching line of incinerator, balance of same to be
teracotta or approved equal. Self-closing hopper doors at each floor shall be
used with daylight opening not to exceed 1/3 of the cross sectional area of the
flue. Any incinerator using Type 3 fuel will be required to furnish secondary
fuel.
   (c)   Evidence of positive draft control must also be furnished. Approved
fly ash collection equipment must also be furnished. The following details must
also be included in the design:
      (1)   Mean design temperature 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit;
      (2)   The volume of the primary combustion chamber shall have a
designated heat release of eight Btu per cubic foot per second;
      (3)   Second combustion chamber to have an area normal to gas path such
that maximum furnace heat release will not exceed 850,000 Btu per square foot
of area, 25 feet per second;
      (4)   Settling chamber to have an area normal to gas path such that
minimum furnace heat release will not exceed 370,000 Btu per square foot of
area, 11 feet per second;
      (5)   Flue cross section area not less than one square foot for each
850,000 Btu's released in the furnace, 25 feet per second;
      (6)   Chimney cross section area not less than one square foot per
780,000 Btu's of heat released in the furnace based on an assumed 50- to 60-
foot stack. The equivalent velocity is about 23 feet per second;
      (7)   Maximum burning capacity of the grates shall be 40 pounds per
square feet per hour;
      (8)   Calculation for combustion air shall be based on figuring zero
excess air:
         Btu × 7.6
          10,000
      (9)   Calculations to include provision for 50 percent excess air;
      (10)   Total weight of products of combustion to equal total combustion
air plus 90 percent of dry fuel;
      (11)   Design of incinerator and its equipment for the disposition of
moisture in the fuel shall also include the computation of the volumes for the
control of velocities including the volume of the super-heated steam at the
design unit temperature, plus the volume of the products of combustion.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-D, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-151. - Units burning over 60 pounds per hour.
   (a)   The following requirements govern units burning over 60 pounds of
refuse or debris per hour: commercial, industrial, municipal and special fuel
burning units. All installations hereinafter erected shall be equipped with
incinerators of a Class III to VII type, designed for the principal waste to be
destroyed. They shall be of a heavy duty construction and shall include primary
combustion chamber designed with a maximum heat release of eight Btu's per
second per cubic feet, secondary combustion chamber to maintain 1,500 degrees
Fahrenheit and final combustion chamber, wherein the gases shall not exceed 11
feet per second, calculated at 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit maximum fuel weight, to
be destroyed on grates not to exceed 65 pounds per square foot per hour. Flue
gas travel changes from primary chamber to breeching shall be 450 degrees.
   (b)   Incinerators handling wet material shall add a drying hearth area
designed for 25 pounds per hour per square feet of hearth and an additional 90
degrees gas directional change.
   (c)   Material charging may be direct, side, end of top charge chutes no
longer than one-half of the height of the incinerator.
   (d)   Refractory linings shall be of a 33 to 34 P.C.E. minimum, using a 4½-
inch lining up to nine square feet of grate burning area, nine-inch lining over
nine square feet and 13½-inch lining on all walls over nine feet in height.
   (e)   When a brick setting is used, a two-inch air space will be required
between the lining and the exterior wall, or in lieu of masonry, a steel casing
with two inches of approved insulation may be applied.
   (f)   All Class III to VII types of incinerators shall have exterior
structural steel framework designed to withstand interior thrusts and the
necessary supports for doors and appurtenant assemblies. Type 1 fuel shall be
burned on approved cast iron grates with cast iron supports. Grate openings are
not to exceed 40 percent of total burning area. Grates may be stationary,
mechanically or manually operated. All incinerators which destroy fuel or any
type in sufficient quantities to be equal to or greater than 750,000 Btu's per
hour input shall be equipped with the following: positive pressure overfire
air, secondary fuel, photoelectric smoke indicator, and indicatory pyrometer.
Refractory coating may also be necessary by the division in order to maintain
maximum furnace temperatures. Type 2 fuel shall be burned on hot drying hearths
with fuel grate burned on combination hot refractory drying hearth and cast
iron grate area, each approximately 50 percent of total burning area. Type 4
shall be burned on hot refractory hearth area over the total burning area. Type
5 may be applied to standard type heavy duty incinerators with safety and
automatic controls for firing. Type 6 fuel shall be burned on hot or cold
refractory hearth or crucible with direct charging to burning area. Approved
fly ash collection equipment must also be furnished in order to meet the
requirements of this article. Units up to 400 pounds per hour total burning
area may be manually operated and controlled, provided the user has an operator
in attendance and a sufficient amount of the time during operation to guarantee
functioning within the code limits. Units over 400 pounds per hour capacity, as
rated under this article shall have control over auxiliary fuel, over fire air,
photoelectric smoke indicator with suitable alarm and indicating pyrometer. All
breeching shall be of high temperature construction refractory lined. Ash pits
and secondary combustion chambers shall be lined with a minimum of two inches
of approved insulation material when same is constructed on concrete slab.
   (g)   The following details must also be included in the design:
      (1)   Mean design 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit;
      (2)   Secondary combustion chamber to have an area normal to gas path
such that maximum furnace heat release will not exceed 850,000 Btu's per square
foot of area, 25 feet per second;
      (3)   Settling chamber to have an area normal to gas path such that
maximum furnace heat release will not exceed 370,000 B.T.U's per square foot of
area, 11 feet per second;
      (4)   Flue cross section area not less than one square foot for each
850,000 Btu's released in the furnace, 25 feet per second;
      (5)   Chimney cross section area not less than one square foot per
780,000 Btu's of heat released in the furnace based on an assumed 50- to 60-
foot stack. The equivalent velocity is about 23 feet per second;
      (6)   Calculation for combustion air shall be:
         Btu × 7.6
          10,000
   based on figuring zero excess air;
      (7)   Calculations to include provision for 50 percent excess air;
      (8)   Total weight of products of combustion shall equal total combustion
air plus 90 percent of dry fuel;
      (9)   Design of incinerator and its equipment for the disposition of
moisture in the fuel shall also include computation of the volumes for the
control of velocities, including the volume of superheated steam at the design
unit temperature, plus the volume of the products of combustion;
      (10)   In the case of steel stack a painter trolley shall also be
provided.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-E, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-152. - Low pressure boilers.
   (a)   Low pressure boilers are hereby determined to include all boilers
carrying a pressure of not more than 15 pounds per square inch of steam
pressure and not more than 30 pounds per square inch of water pressure.
   (b)   Ratings as to combustion volumes for all low pressure cast iron and
steel boilers shall be selected in accordance with the recommendations for low
pressure boilers, as determined by the Heating, Piping and Air Conditioning
Contractor's National Association, Engineering Standards and all rules
contained therein, and amendments thereto, shall apply to all boilers governed
by the provisions of this article; provided, however, that any low pressure
boiler having an approved rating from the American Society of Mechanical
Engineers shall be acceptable under this article. The above provisions apply to
design unit only.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-F, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-153. - Necessary plans.
   (a)   Before the issuing of a permit, the applicant shall submit the
aforementioned plans, specifications and any other data deemed necessary by the
division. This permit shall be issued for construction purposes only. Upon
completion of the incinerator or the repairs or alterations, the applicant
shall call for an inspection.
   (b)   If any unit fails to perform satisfactorily at the time of inspection
and test, the certificate of operation, as required, shall be denied until the
necessary corrections have been made.
   (c)   This section is deemed necessary for the preservation of the public
health and safety of the people of the city and is being enacted under the
police powers of the city for such purpose.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.2-G, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-154. - Breechings.
   Breechings of all boiler combustion equipment shall be of sufficient cross
sectional area to prevent excessive gas velocity and to defeat the obtaining of
complete combustion; and shall have a minimum number of bends and turns.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-155. - Draft fans and venturi stacks.
   (a)   Induced draft fans may be used, where necessary or desirable, provided
the requirements concerning stack or chimney size and height are observed in
accordance with the provision herein specified.
   (b)   The use of Venturi stacks and other stacks or chimneys not deemed to
be within the coverage of this article shall be permitted only upon approval by
the board of appeals after hearing thereon, as herein provided.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-156. - Accumulation of soot and fly ash.
   (a)   Tube areas and gas passages through heating surfaces shall be of
sufficient area to permit the ordinary accumulation of soot and fly ash without
such restriction to draft as would interfere with smokeless operation of the
fuel-burning equipment. Sufficient means must be provided for the removal of
soot, fly ash, dust and cinders from the heating surfaces, tube region and gas
passages; provided, however soot, fly ash, dust and cinders shall not be
removed from the heating surfaces, tube region and gas passages by the use of
compressed air, steam or other agency whereby such soot, fly ash, dust or
cinders shall be forced through the chimney or stack into the open air in
violation of the provisions of this article.
   (b)   Baffles must be of such design, and so installed and maintained, as
not to interfere with smokeless combustion due to the impinging of flame on
heating surfaces where such impingement would result in reduction of
temperature below the ignition point of the combustible gas.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-157. - Furnace volume.
   Requirements for furnace volume shall be as follows:
      (1)   A steam boiler furnace or other furnace using hand-method of firing
shall be provided with a furnace volume of not less than one cubic foot
combustion volume for each rated horsepower, or for each 140 square feet
equivalent direct radiation capacity.
      (2)   Mechanical stokers shall be provided with a furnace volume of not
less than one cubic foot per rated horsepower.
      (3)   Furnaces using fuel oil shall be provided with a furnace volume of
not less than 1.50 cubic feet per rated horsepower, or for each 140 square feet
equivalent direct radiation.
      (4)   Furnaces using pulverized coal shall not have less than three cubic
feet furnace volume per rated horsepower.
      (5)   Wood-refuse burning boilers or furnaces shall maintain a furnace
volume of from six to ten cubic feet per rated horsepower.
      (6)   Refuse-burners and destructor type of incinerators shall maintain a
furnace volume of two cubic feet per square foot grate surface.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-158. - Horizontal return tubular boilers.
   Horizontal return tubular boilers not equipped with mechanical stokers shall
be so set as to provide adequate combustion facilities, and in no case shall
the distance from shell to grate be less than specified in Table 3 hereinafter
set forth.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-159. - Power boilers.
   Power boilers equipped with stokers shall be set in accordance with at least
the minimum dimensions found in Table 4 hereinafter set forth.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-160. - Induced draft fans.
   Induced draft fans may be used provided suitable arrangements are made for
the prevention of the emission of soot, cinders and fly ash.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-161. - Air jets.
   (a)   All high pressure boilers using solid fuel, and not equipped with
mechanical stokers or provisions for using pulverized fuel, shall have at least
one air jet for each 200 square feet heating surface or fraction thereof. In no
case shall there be less than two air jets.
   (b)   Where it is impossible, due to construction, to equip a boiler and
furnace with air jets, it will be necessary to install mechanical stokers on
all boilers having more than 200 square feet heating surface or 2,500 square
feet equivalent direct radiation.
(Ord. No. 81-73, § 3.10, 11-4-81)

Secs. 13-162—13-180. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE V. - DUTCH ELM DISEASE ***
Sec. 13-181. - Obligation to abate.
   (a)   The department of public works is hereby authorized and directed to
inspect, from time to time, all American elm trees in the public parks and
along all streets and highways and on lands privately owned in the city for the
purpose of determining whether any of such trees are infected with the Dutch
elm disease. If such infection is discovered in any such trees in the public
parks and along any streets and highways in the city, the department is hereby
authorized and directed to remove and destroy any and all such infected trees
forthwith.
   (b)   If the department of public works inspects, or caused to be inspected,
such elm trees growing on privately owned land in the city and determines that
any of such elm trees are infected with the Dutch elm disease, the department
of public works is hereby authorized and directed to give notice to the owner
of such premises, as shown by the records in the city assessor's office, to
remove any and all such diseased elm trees forthwith and, upon the failure of
such owner to remove and destroy such elm trees within ten days from the date
of receiving such notice, the department of public works may proceed to remove
or have the diseased trees removed, and the reasonable cost of such removal
shall be charged against the property and, if unpaid, such charges shall be
transferred to the miscellaneous special assessment roll, as provided by
section 16.24 of the City Charter.
(Ord. No. 81-89, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-182. - Duty to spray elm trees.
   The director of public works is hereby authorized and directed to spray with
suitable poisonous liquids all American elm trees in the city, whether
privately owned or publicly owned, for the purpose of preventing any such trees
from becoming infected with such disease. In connection with such spraying of
such elm trees, the director of public works, his agents and employees, are
hereby authorized to go upon private property to spray such trees.
(Ord. No. 81-89, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-183. - Penalty.
   Any person, firm or corporation violating any of the provisions of this
article shall, upon conviction thereof, be subject to a fine not exceeding the
sum of $500.00 or imprisonment for a period not exceeding 90 days, or both such
fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.
(Ord. No. 81-89, § 3, 11-4-81)
Secs. 13-184—13-205. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VI. - NOXIOUS WEEDS AND VEGETATION ***
Sec. 13-206. - Unlawful to permit.
   It shall be unlawful for the owner or occupant or any person having charge
of any lot or parcel of land within the city to permit or allow to grow thereon
vegetation of any kind scattered among which are noxious weeds such as Canada
thistles, wild carrot, ox-eyed daisies, wild mustard, ragweed goldenrod, or any
other varieties which are recognized as inducing hay fever, rose fever, or
other diseases or being in any other way deleterious to the health or comfort
of the community. The presence of such weeds upon any lot or parcel of land
within the limits of the city is hereby declared to be a public nuisance.
(Ord. No. 81-92, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 13-207. - Duty to cut weeds and other vegetation.
   It is hereby made the duty of the owner of unimproved land, or any person
having charge of any unimproved lands within the limits of the city upon which
vegetation is growing or standing, to cut and destroy or cause to be cut and
destroyed all such vegetation growing or standing on such premises as often as
may be necessary to prevent them going to seed and/or reaching a height of six
inches or more. If any owner of unimproved land or any person having charge of
unimproved lands in this city shall knowingly allow or permit any vegetation to
grow upon such lands or shall allow or permit the vegetation to ripen so as to
cause or endanger the spread thereof, he/she shall, upon conviction in any
court of competent jurisdiction, be liable to the penalty imposed in this
article for the violation thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-92, § 2, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 03-945, 3-4-03; Ord. No. 06-1076, 5-15-
06)
Sec. 13-208. - Duty of director to give notice; failure to comply.
   (a)   It is hereby made the duty of the director of public works to give
general notice to the public of the requirements of this article by publishing
a notice in the official city newspaper during the month of March each year.
This notice shall indicate that vegetation reaching a height of six inches or
more will be cut by the city and the owner of the property charged with the
cost.
   (b)   In case the owner or occupant or the person having charge of any
unimproved land in the city shall refuse or neglect to comply with such notice,
or shall refuse or neglect to cut the vegetation, it shall be the duty of the
director of public works, or someone working under his direction, to enter upon
the land as many times as is necessary, to cause all such vegetation to be cut
down and to charge the cost thereof, together with an amount of $150.00 per
invoice to cover administrative costs and contingent expenses, against the
owner or occupant of such premises and against the property itself.
   (1)   Due to the increased administrative costs associated with repeat
offenders (e.g., increased monitoring of property), an additional fee of
$100.00 will be charged against the owner or occupant and against the property
itself for the second and subsequent incidents in a calendar year where the
director of public works, or someone working under his direction, has entered
upon the property to cut vegetation.
      a.   At the request of the owner or occupant, and upon good cause shown,
the director of public works, or his designee, may waive the additional $100.00
fee once in a calendar year.
(Ord. No. 81-92, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1077, 5-15-06; Ord. No. 11-1339, 11-
21-11; Ord. No. 22-1768, 8-23-22)
Sec. 13-209. - Cost to be charged against owner.
   The director of building and safety shall keep a record of the cost of
cutting the vegetation upon each separate lot and parcel of unimproved land by
the city, and shall notify the owner or occupant of the premises by ordinary
mail or otherwise, if the address of such owner or occupant be known, that the
city has cut or caused to be cut and destroyed the vegetation upon the premises
in accordance with the provisions of this article, together with a statement of
the amount due the city. If the costs and charges due the city for cutting and
destroying vegetation upon any lot or parcel of unimproved land, in accordance
with the provisions of this article, shall not have been collected on or before
December 31 of the year in which the expense was incurred by the city, the same
shall be reported by the finance director to the council to be collected by a
special assessment, in accordance with the provisions of chapter 15 of the
Charter of the city.
(Ord. No. 81-92, § 4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1078, 5-15-06)
Sec. 13-210. - Penalty.
   In addition to the remedies described above, any individual who violates any
of the provisions of this article shall be subject to the following:
      (1)   First offense: The individual is responsible for a civil infraction
subject to a fine of $100.00.
      (2)   Second and subsequent offenses committed within a calendar year:
The individual is guilty of a misdemeanor with a mandatory minimum fine of
$500.00.
(Ord. No. 81-92, § 5, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 03-944, 3-4-03; Ord. No. 06-1079, 5-15-
06)
Secs. 13-211—13-499. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VII. - CONSTRUCTION SITE MAINTENANCE ***
Sec. 13-500. - Construction site maintenance provisions for residential and
commercial properties.
   All residential and commercial properties shall comply with the following
provisions while under a valid permit for construction:
   (a)   General. Wherever a building or structure is erected, altered,
repaired, removed or demolished, the operation shall be conducted in a safe
manner and suitable protection for the general public shall be provided.
   (b)   Equipment storage. All construction equipment and materials shall be
stored in an orderly fashion and in compliance with the state construction
code.
   (c)   Airborne materials. All construction shall provide control for on-site
dust, soil and any other airborne materials so that such materials remain on
the job site.
   (d)   Fences. Every excavation and/or area of construction on a site located
five feet or less from the street lot line shall be enclosed with a barrier not
less than six feet high to prevent the entry of unauthorized persons. Where
located more than five feet from the street lot line, a barrier shall be
erected where required by the building official. All barriers shall be of
adequate strength to resist wind pressure as required by the building official.
      (1)   Any area under construction for more than two months, regardless of
its proximity to the street lot line, shall be enclosed by a temporary chain-
link fence to protect the safety of the public and to prevent entry by
unauthorized persons.
   (e)   Watchman. Wherever a building is being demolished, erected or altered,
a watchman shall be employed to warn the general public when intermittent
hazardous operations are conducted across the sidewalk or walkway, where
required by the building official.
(Ord. No. 10-1302, 12-13-10)
Secs. 13-501—13-520. Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VIII. VEHICULAR NUISANCE. ***
Sec. 13-521.   Purpose, intent, and authority.
   (a)   The purpose and intent of this article is to regulate reckless driving
and racing on public streets that endanger the health and safety of people and
property in the city.
   (b)   The city finds that reckless driving and racing pose an immediate
threat to the health and safety of the public, interferes with pedestrian and
vehicular traffic, creates a nuisance as defined in Section
13-1 of this Code, and interferes with the right of individuals and private
business owners to enjoy the use of their property within the city. Individuals
involved in the type of activity prohibited in this article engage in
activities and behaviors without regard to the safety of oncoming traffic,
pedestrians, property, or vehicles parked or moving nearby.
   (c)   Because reckless driving and racing are a nuisance, the city finds it
necessary and appropriate to take additional and immediate steps to protect
public health and safety. The city may take action to abate the public
nuisance, including impoundment and forfeiture of the vehicle(s) involved as
well as any tractor or trailer used to transport the vehicle(s) to and from the
racing site; or any tools or equipment used to service, maintain, or repair the
racing vehicle(s); or any proceeds of racing.
   (d)   The provisions of this article are authorized by The Home Rule City
Act, Public Act 279 of 1909, more specifically but not limited to MCL 117.30).
   (e)   By adopting this article the city is not opting out of Chapter 207 of
the Wayne County Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-522.   Definitions.
   (a)   Excessively high rate of speed means any speed that is 15 mph or more
over the posted speed limit.
   (b)   Owner of a vehicle means a person in whose name the vehicle is titled,
and any chattel mortgagee or assignee or other lien-holder whose lien has been
filed in the office of the Secretary of State or the office of the Wayne County
Register of Deeds prior to the commencement of the action, as well as a person
who is deemed by law to be a constructive owner.
   (c)   Person means any individual, firm, partnership, corporation, company,
association, joint stock association, or joint venture or combination acting as
a unit, and the plural as well as the singular number, and includes any
trustee, receiver, assignee, or other similar representative thereof.
   (d)   Public street means a street, freeway, highway, alleyway, public
parking lot, private parking lot open to the public, or any other paved surface
that is open to the public, including a private paved surface which is used
without the owner’s permission, which has not been specifically designed for
racing vehicles.
   (e)   Racing means either:
      (1)   Race a vehicle either against another vehicle or against a time- or
speed-measuring device, whether or not there is an agreement to race; or
      (2)   Drive a vehicle at an excessively high rate of speed or
acceleration or in another recklessly dangerous manner in an exhibition of
driving prowess, such as drifting, sliding, or donuts (involving the loss of
traction and/or repeatedly driving in circles or figure-eights or in a sideways
motion in circles or figure-eights) that is recklessly dangerous and could
cause serious injury or death, and /or is an impediment to traffic.
   (f)   Reckless driving or recklessly means the operation of a vehicle
without due caution and circumspection, and in willful or wanton disregard of
the rights or safety of person or property, or in a manner so as to endanger or
be likely to endanger any person or property. Examples of reckless driving or
driving recklessly includes, but is not limited to, drifting, sliding, donuts
(involving the loss of traction and/or repeatedly driving in circles or figure-
eights or in a sideways motion in circles or figure-eights), and burnouts (also
known as peel out or power brake, practice of keeping a vehicle stationary or
relatively stationary and spinning its wheels, with the resultant friction
causing the tires to heat up and smoke).
   (g)   Vehicle includes, but is not limited to, every device in, upon, or by
which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon public
streets, including self-propelled devices. Vehicle does not include devices
exclusively moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails or
tracks or power-driven mobility device when that power-driven mobility device
is being used by an individual with a mobility disability.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-523.   Nuisance prohibited.
   (a)   A person or their agent or employee, who owns, leases, operates, or
maintains a vehicle shall not use that vehicle, nor allow the vehicle to be
used, for reckless driving or racing in violation of this article.
   (b)   Any violation of this article, including a first-time offense, is a
nuisance if the reckless driving or racing is recklessly dangerous to health,
safety, and/or property, and/or impedes traffic.
   (c)   A person who violates any prohibition in this article is guilty of a
nuisance. The vehicle involved in the violation and its contents, including any
tractor or trailer used to transport the vehicle to and from the racing site;
or any tools or equipment used to service, maintain, or repair the racing
vehicle; or any proceeds of racing are also declared a nuisance.
   (d)   Any vehicles driven recklessly or involved in racing in violation of
this article, including the vehicle’s contents, shall be sanctioned, enjoined,
and abated as set forth in this article and by Wayne County Third Circuit Court
rule.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-524.   Enforcement.
   (a)   This article may be enforced by a civil action filed in the Wayne
County Third Circuit Court to abate the public nuisance; to perpetually enjoin
a person, his or her agent or employee from using or allowing a vehicle to be
used for the purposes declared a nuisance in this article; or to provide for
the seizure, impoundment, continued impoundment, sale, or forfeiture to the
seizing agency of a vehicle or its contents, including a tractor or trailer
used to transport the vehicle to and from the racing site, or allied
maintenance or transportation equipment or tools, or any racing proceeds, which
is a nuisance.
   (b)   A civil action may be initiated in the name of the city by the
Attorney General of the State of Michigan, the Wayne County Prosecuting
Attorney, or the Corporation Counsel for the City of Dearborn.
   (c)   In a civil action brought under this article, any chattel mortgagee or
assignee or other lienholder whose lien has been filed on the property with the
Michigan Secretary of State or the Wayne County Register of Deeds shall be
joined as a party defendant.
   (d)   In a civil action brought under this article, evidence of the general
reputation of the owner or operator of the vehicle; the vehicle; or of the
place, area or building in which the racing activity took place is admissible
to establish the existence of the public nuisance.
   (e)   Proof of knowledge of the existence of the public nuisance on the part
of the owner, or his or her agent or employee, or any of them, is not required.
   (f)   In a civil action brought under this article, any monies found on the
driver, passengers, or others directly involved in the racing activity are
presumed to be proceeds of said racing. This presumption may be rebutted by
clear and convincing evidence that the monies are unrelated to the racing.
   (g)   In a civil action brought under this article the operation of two or
more vehicles either at speeds in excess of prima facie lawfully established
speeds or rapidly accelerating from a common starting point to a speed in
excess of such prima facie lawfully established speed is prima facie evidence
of racing.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-525.   Judgment and order.
   (a)   Upon finding that a public nuisance exists, the Wayne County Third
Circuit Court may render judgment and enter an order of abatement.
   (b)   Any vehicle that has driven recklessly or been used for racing upon
