public streets in the city in violation of this article, including the
vehicle’s contents or any tractor or trailer used to transport the racing
vehicles to and from the racing site; or any tools or equipment used to
service, maintain or repair the racing vehicle; or any proceeds of racing may
be impounded or continue to be impounded for a period of up to one year,
ordered to be sold in the manner provided for the sale of chattels under
execution, or forfeited to the seizing agency.
   (c)   Upon the sale of the vehicle or its contents, or a tractor or trailer
used to transport the racing vehicle to or from the racing site, or any tools
or equipment used to service, maintain, or repair the racing vehicle, the
proceeds shall be disposed of in the following order of priority:
      (1)   To pay for the costs of keeping the property and the expenses of
the sale.
      (2)   To pay all bona fide secured interests and liens on the property,
provided that the secured party or lienholder had no knowledge or notice that
the property was being used to maintain a public nuisance.
      (3)   To pay for court costs and to reimburse appropriate units of
government for the costs of enforcing and prosecuting the action, including any
costs of incarceration not otherwise reimbursed which are generated due to a
contempt charge against the owner or an agent or employee of the owner arising
from the abatement order.
      (4)   The remaining balance shall be deposited in the city’s general fund
or distributed as ordered by the court.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-526.   Time period to commence action, storage of vehicle, settlement
conference, and consent order.
   (a)   If a vehicle is seized pursuant to this article, a civil action under
this article shall be commenced within 30 days after the seizure. Pending trial
of a public nuisance action, the court may order that the vehicle, including
its contents, and any tractor or trailer used to transport the vehicle to and
from the racing site, or any allied equipment or tools, be impounded or
continue to be impounded and held in secure storage. The vehicle or its
contents, including any tractor or trailer used to transport the vehicle to and
from the racing site, or any allied equipment or tools may be released upon the
defendant posting a bond equal to the fair market value of the property.
   (b)   A defendant in a public nuisance action brought under this article may
enter into an out-of-court settlement agreement with the Wayne County
Prosecuting Attorney or the City's Corporation Counsel.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-527.   Notice of seizure and intent to forfeit; redemption of property;
forfeiture pursuant to law.
   (a)   If a vehicle and/or property is seized for violating the provisions of
this article, the seizing agency shall provide notice of seizure and intent to
forfeit to the owner of the vehicle and/or property on a form designated for
such purpose.
   (b)   Upon receiving notice of seizure and intent to forfeit, the owner of
the vehicle and/or property may contest the seizure in the Wayne County Circuit
Court.
   (c)   The owner may contest the seizure or, if agreeable to the Wayne County
Prosecuting Attorney (if the matter is being pursued by the Wayne County
Prosecutor’s Office) or the City’s Corporation Counsel (if the matter is being
pursued by the corporation counsel), enter into a settlement agreement to re-
claim the vehicle and/or property. Such settlement agreement may, at the
discretion of either the Wayne County Prosecuting Attorney or Corporation
Counsel (depending which authority is pursuing the matter), include a
redemption fee schedule as follows:
      (1)   $900.00 for a first seizure, plus towing and storage fees.
      (2)   $1,800.00 for a second seizure, plus towing and storage fees.
      (3)   $2,700.00 for a third seizure, plus towing and storage fees.
   Depending on which authority is pursuing the matter, either the Wayne County
Prosecuting Attorney or Corporation Counsel for the City of Dearborn will
decide whether to seek abatement/forfeiture of the vehicle and/or property or
what redemption fee applies.
   (d)   Exemption for drag racing. The redemption fee schedule does not apply
to drag racing cases in violation of MCL 257.626a and/or Dearborn Code of
Ordinances Section
18-249 or other serious cases, depending up on the facts and circumstances of
each case, after review by the Wayne County Prosecuting Attorney or Corporation
Counsel for the City. The Wayne County Prosecuting Attorney or Corporation
Counsel, depending on who is pursuing the matter, will decide whether to seek
abatement/forfeiture of the vehicle and/or property and what redemption fee
applies.
   (e)   Failure to file a claim of interest within 30 days of receiving notice
of seizure and intent to forfeit will result in automatic forfeiture of the
vehicle and/or property pursuant to
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-528.   Provisions in addition to other law.
   The provisions, sanctions and remedies set forth in this article are in
addition to the sanctions and remedies provided in state and other municipal
law, and are not intended to comprise, substitute for, or place a limitation
upon those other laws.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-529.   Provisions severable.
   If any provision of this article shall be declared by a court of competent
jurisdiction to be void, invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, then such
voidness, invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any
other provision in this article, and all remaining provisions shall continue to
be of full force and effect.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
Sec. 13-530.   Liberal construction.
   The purpose of this article is to promote and protect the health, safety and
welfare of the county and the citizens of the county, as such, it shall be
liberally construed in order to effectuate that purpose.
(Ord. No. 22-1762, 7-26-22)
* Secs. 13-531—13-540. Reserved. *
ARTICLE IX. BULK SOLID STORAGE AND HANDLING
** DIVISION 1. PURPOSE, DEFINITIONS, AND APPLICABILITY **
Sec. 13-541.   Purpose, intent, and authority.
   The purpose of this article is to regulate the storage of bulk solid
material at facilities in the city that store, handle, load, unload, stockpile,
or process such bulk solid material.
   The city finds that activities associated with these facilities have the
potential to create, or contribute to the creation of, fugitive dust and/or
debris, and the proliferation of such fugitive dust and/or debris have the
potential to create negative impacts on both residents and property. These
include, but are not limited to, potential health hazards associated with
inhaling fugitive dust and/or, which include pulmonary inflammation, asthma,
and fibrosis.
   This article prescribes reasonable regulations to minimize fugitive dust
and/or debris coming from facilities that store, handle, load, unload,
stockpile, or process bulk solid material, including any person that transports
materials to, from, or within these lots.
   The provisions of this article are authorized by and adopted pursuant to
part 55 of the Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act,
Public Act 451 of 1994, titled “Air Pollution Control,” particularly Sections
5540 and 5542 being MCL 324.5540 and 324.5542.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-542.   Definitions.
   For the purposes of this article, the following words and phrases shall have
the meanings respectively ascribed by this section. Words and phrases not
defined in this article shall the meanings as defined in Part 55 of the
Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, PA 451 of 1994,
MCL 324.5501 et seq., or Michigan Administrative Code, R 336.1101 et seq., and
any subsequent amendments to either:
   (a)   Alternative operating plan. Means any of the following:
      (1)   An operating program for a fugitive dust source or potential
fugitive dust source under Section 5524 of the Natural Resources and
Environmental Protection Act, being MCL 324.5524. An operating plan includes a
fugitive dust control program under Rule 336.1371 and 336.1372 of the Michigan
Administrative Code.
      (2)   An operating plan for a fugitive dust source or potential fugitive
dust source under a state permit to operate, state renewable operating permit,
or similar authorization.
      (3)   An operating plan for a fugitive dust source or potential fugitive
dust source under a federal permit or similar federal authorization.
      (4)   An operating plan for a fugitive dust source or potential fugitive
dust source under a state or federal consent order, environmental consent
order, consent judgment, consent decree, or any other equivalent.
   (b)   Asphalt millings. Also known as asphalt grinding or RAP (Reclaimed
Asphalt Pavement), means the fine particles of bitumen and inorganic material
that are produced by the mechanical grinding of bituminous concrete surfaces.
   (c)   Bulk solid material. Means:
      (1)   Any solid substance or material that can be used as a fuel or as an
ingredient or component in a manufacturing or construction process that may
create fugitive dust and that, except for carbonaceous material, is accumulated
in an amount of 50 cubic yards or more at any one time. Bulk solid material
shall include, but is not limited to, ores, iron slag, steel slag,
metallurgical coke, or limestone.
      (2)   Any carbonaceous material regardless of the amount but does not
mean material stored in nurseries, garden centers, and farm supply stores.
   (d)   Carbonaceous bulk solid material facility. Means a source, site, or
facility where carbonaceous material is stored, loaded, unloaded, stockpiled,
handled on-site, blended, processed, or otherwise managed.
   (e)   Carbonaceous bulk solid material. Means bulk solid material that
includes carbonaceous material.
   (f)   Carbonaceous material. Means a solid substance that occurs naturally
or exists as a result of human-made process that is rich in carbon.
Carbonaceous material includes, but is not limited to, petroleum coke,
metallurgical coke, coke breeze, and nut coke.
   (g)   Coke. Means a solid carbonaceous material derived from the
distillation of coal (including metallurgical coke) or from oil refinery coker
units or other cracking processes (including petroleum coke), and includes, but
is not limited to, nut coke and coke breeze.
   (h)   Department. Means the city’s Department of Economic Development.
   (i)   Director. Means the Director of the Department of Economic
Development.
   (j)   Facility. Means all contiguous land, structures, and other
appurtenances, and improvements on the land, used for storing, handling,
loading, unloading, stockpiling, or processing bulk solid and/or carbonaceous
material.
   (k)   Fugitive dust. Means any solid particulate matter that becomes
airborne or otherwise moves beyond the lot, facility, building, or structure
property line or, if being transported by a vehicle, moves beyond the confines
of the vehicle, by natural or human-made activities, excluding engine
combustion exhaust and particulate matter emitted from a properly permitted
exhaust stack equipped with a pollution control device.
   (l)   High wind conditions. Means when average wind speeds exceed 20 miles
per hour on an hourly average.
   (m)   Internal road. Means any route within a facility that is not located
in an area normally used for staging or storage of material and that has
evidence of repeated prior travel by, or is otherwise regularly used by,
vehicles for transporting materials to, from, or within a facility.
   (n)   Metallurgical coke or metcoke. Means a carbonaceous material resulting
from the manufactured purification of coal.
   (o)   Opacity limit. Means the highest degree to which visibility of a
background is reduced by fugitive dust shall be permitted, expressed as a
percentage where 0% represents no interference by fugitive dust and 100%
represents zero visibility due to complete interference by fugitive dust.
   (p)   Owner or operator. Means any person, whether owner, occupant, tenant,
lessee, agent, or other person who: has legal or equitable title to any
facility; who has charge, care, or control of any facility; who is in
possession of any facility; or who is entitled to control or direct the
management of any facility.
   (q)   Person. Means an individual, partnership, co-partnership, firm,
company, limited liability company, corporation, association, sole
proprietorship, joint venture, joint stock company, trust, estate, political
subdivision, state agency, owner, operator or generator, or any other legal
entity, or its legal representative, agent, or assigns.
   (r)   Petroleum coke or petcoke. Means a solid carbonaceous residue produced
from a coker after cracking and distillation from petroleum refining
operations, including such residue produced by petroleum upgraders in addition
to petroleum refining.
   (s)   PM10. Means particulate matter that has an aerodynamic diameter less
than or equal to nominal 10 micrometers, as measured by a reference test
specified in 40 CFR Part 51, Appendix M.
   (t)   Process or processing. Means any chemical, industrial, commercial, or
manufacturing operation or activity that causes, or has the potential to cause,
the emission of airborne particles, including but not limited to, blending,
mixing, crushing, screening, breaking, wet or dry cleaning, thermal drying, and
chemically treating.
   (u)   Reportable action level. Means the positive difference between the
level of PM10 measures at the upwind monitor(s) at a facility and the level of
PM10 measured at the downwind monitor(s) at a facility that will trigger
response activities under a contingency plan pursuant to Sec. 13-547 as
established in the fugitive dust plan submitted by a facility. The reportable
action level shall be the difference of 20% based on the concentration of PM10
detected at the downwind monitor(s) at a facility.
   (v)   State. Means the State of Michigan.
   (w)   Track-out or tracked material. Means any mud, dirt, soil, debris, or
material stored at a particular facility on vehicle wheels, slides, carriages,
or undercarriages that is carried from a facility onto a public road, right-of-
way, or property of another.
   (x)   Transfer point. Means the location at or within a facility where bulk
solid material is moved, carried, conveyed, dropped, or deposited.
   (y)   Vehicle. Means any car, truck, railcar, vessel, or any other device
in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported.
   (z)   Vessel. Means every description of watercraft used or capable of being
used as a means of transportation on water.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-543.   Applicability.
   Except as otherwise stated in this article, any facility that processes,
handles on-site, transfers, loads, unloads, stockpiles, or stores bulk solid or
carbonaceous materials shall comply with all of the requirements in this
article.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 2. PRE-EXISTING FACILITIES AND ALTERNATE COMPLIANCE **
Sec. 13-544.   Pre-existing facilities; temporary certificate of operation.
   (a)   Except as otherwise stated in this article, and subject to subsections
(b) and (c) of this section, all facilities subject to regulation under this
article that operate with a valid certificate of occupancy issued by the city
on the effective date of the ordinance enacting this article, and do not have
any outstanding violations or fees owed to the city, shall be issued a
temporary certificate of operation, and may continue to operate for a period of
90 days following the effective date of this article. During this period, a
pre-existing facility shall apply for a certificate of operation pursuant to
one of the following application procedures:
      (1)   If the pre-existing facility operates pursuant to a alternative
operating plan for the facility, as that term is defined in this article, the
owner and/or operator must apply for an certificate for alternate compliance
under the application procedure outlined in this division of this article.
      (2)   If the pre-existing facility does not have an alternative operating
plan for the facility, the owner and/or operator must apply for a temporary
certificate of operation under the application procedure outlined in Division 3
of this article.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-545.   Alternative compliance for qualified solid bulk materials;
application process; certificate of alternate compliance; fee.
   (a)   Application and eligibility for certificate of alternative compliance;
renewal; alternative operating plan; exception to standards set forth in
article; conditions.
      (1)   The owner or operator of a facility that processes, handles on-
site, transfers, loads, unloads, stockpiles, or stores qualified bulk solid
materials shall be deemed in compliance with this article, and shall receive a
certificate of alternative compliance from the department director, if the
owner or operator meets all the terms and conditions of this section.
      (2)   Exception to default standards. If the facility has an alternative
operating plan, as that term is defined in Sec.
13-542, the standards set forth in the plan for fugitive dust sources or
potential fugitive dust sources shall control and be enforceable under this
article if they are subject to enforceable permit condition(s) or enforceable
order(s) as part of the plan.
         a.   Pile height standard exempt from exception. Regulations that
address pile height for outdoor storage of bulk solid materials, including pile
height of combustible materials, are exempt from the exception stated above,
and control over any similar regulations found in an alternative operating
plan.
         b.   A pattern of violations under applicable local, state, or federal
law related to the requirements of this article; or a pattern of violations of
the standards set forth in the alternative operating plan, may result in the
loss of the exception under this section, in which case all terms and
conditions of this article that deviate from those set forth in the alternative
operating plan shall become enforceable.
   (b)   Submission of alternate operating plan for facility. The owner or
operator must submit an alternative operating plan for the facility, as that
term is defined in Sec.
13-542, subject to the review and approval of the department director or their
designee.
   (c)   Compliance with alternative operating plan. The alternative operating
plan, including any amendments, must be approved by the issuing authority, in
effect at the time of submission, and the owner or operator must be in
compliance with the plan.
   (d)   Fee. A non-refundable fee of $2,500.00 is due at the time an
application for a certificate of alternative compliance or renewal is submitted
to the department, which shall cover the costs of application review,
inspections, and compliance monitoring conducted pursuant to this section and,
if applicable, the article. The department reserves the right to increase this
fee if it no longer covers the aforementioned costs. This fee is not inclusive
of other fees that may be required by the Code of Ordinances, the Zoning
Ordinance, or applicable law.
   (e)   Contents of alternative operating plan. The applicant may submit one
of the following alternative operating plans, subject to the following terms
and conditions, as part of the application under this section:
      (1)   Reliance on alternative operating plan under MCL 324.5524(5) with
additional information. The state operating plan includes the information
required by section 5524(5) of the Natural Resources Environmental Protection
Act, being MCL 324.5524(5), and all of the following additional information is
included in (i) the state operating plan, (ii) included in an active national
pollutant discharge elimination system or active groundwater permit for the
facility issued by the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality or Michigan
Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy or successor agency, or
(iii) included with any supplemental information filed with the department with
an application for a certificate of alternative compliance under this section:
         a.   A site map for the facility, drawn to scale, in conformance with
the requirements and standards of Zoning Ordinance Section
32.02, and providing the following additional information:
            1.   Facility boundaries;
               a.   All buildings, internal roadways, and utilities on facility
property;
               b.   All roadways and transportation corridors within one
quarter mile of the perimeter of the facility that are used for transport of
material to or from the facility;
               c.   The location of all floor drains, storm drains, and storm
water outfalls;
               d.   All potential emission points at the facility, including a
depiction of the footprints of all bulk solid material storage piles, transfer
points, conveyors, and roadways; and
               e.   The location of all fugitive dust control devices and
monitoring devices, including the fugitive dust monitor and wind monitor.
            2.   A description of the facility’s operations, including a list
of all bulk solid materials that are construction bulk solid materials handled
at, processed at, or transported to, from, or within the facility;
            3.   A description of the control measures, devices, and
technologies to be used to minimize and control fugitive dust at the facility
consistent with any applicable standard for density of emissions under Rule
336.1301 of the Michigan Administrative Code, a description of how all control
measures, devices, and technologies will be maintained and calibrated to ensure
their continued effectiveness, and a description of the training provided to
staff regarding the proper application and operation of the control measures,
devices, and technologies;
            4.   A description of the owner or operator’s system for
recordkeeping compliant with the following requirements:
               a.   The facility owner or operator shall record all roadway
cleaning and street sweeping daily.
               b.   The facility owner or operator shall record the application
of water and/or chemical stabilizers, as applicable, as well as any instances
when such application was suspended for any reason, including, but not limited
to, weather conditions.
               c.   The facility owner or operator shall maintain a schedule
for routine inspections, maintenance, and testing of all fugitive dust control
measures, devices, and technologies, including a schedule for inspection of
bulk solid material piles, inspection of all monitors, and inspection of off-
site areas for the presence of dust, and identify the person or persons
responsible for conducting such inspections, maintenance, and testing.
               d.   The system of recordkeeping for the owner or operator’s
compliance with Secs.
13-545(e)(1)a.2. and
13-545(e)(1)e. of this section, and compliant with a requirement that the owner
or operator keep and maintain the records described in this subparagraph at the
facility and available for inspection by the department for at least 3 years
after creation;
         b.   A description of the owner or operator’s measures to comply with
any applicable setback requirements under state law, rule, or permit, or
applicable under the city’s Zoning Ordinance;
         c.   A description of measures to comply with the following height
limits and screening requirements relating to piles, as outlined in Sec.
13-556:
            1.   The vertical distance from the grade immediately adjacent to a
pile to the highest point of that pile shall be no greater than 25 feet. Piles
shall be screened from view from adjacent rights-of-way and properties at the
level of the right-of-way.
               a.   Exception for combustible materials. Combustible materials
capable of self-ignition through chemical action of its constituents shall be
no greater than 15 feet. Piles shall be screened from view from adjacent
rights-of-way and properties at the level of the right-of-way.
         d.   A description of protection for waterways consistent with the
requirements of any applicable state law, rule, operating plan, or permit, or
the requirements of this article, City Code, or a permit issued by the city;
         e.   A description of the owner or operator’s measures to monitor wind
speeds at the facility and to suspend disturbance of piles of qualified solid
materials, including, but not limited to, outdoor loading, unloading, and any
other processing, during high wind conditions unless alternate measures are
implemented to effectively control dust in accordance with any applicable state
operating plan or permit; and
         f.   A description of storm water management, erosion, sediment
control, and drainage measures to control runoff or migration at or from the
facility in a manner consistent with requirements under any applicable state
law, rule, operating plan, or permit, or with any requirement of this article,
City Code, city permit, or both.
      (2)   Reliance on state operating plan. If the owner or operator is
relying only upon a state operating plan for compliance with this section, the
owner or operator must file a copy of the state operating plan and any
amendments to document compliance with this section and all of the following
apply:
         a.   Within 45 days of receipt, the department must review the
operating plan and any amendments and inspect the facility for compliance with
the requirements of this section to determine whether the operating plan and
any amendments satisfy the requirements of this section and are adequate to
protect the public health and the environment and to prevent the emission of
fugitive dust that causes unreasonable interference with the comfortable
enjoyment of life and property;
         b.   Within 45 days of the inspection the department director, or
their designee, shall determine and notify the owner or operator of the
facility in writing that the owner or operator of the facility is in compliance
with this section; and
         c.   The owner or operator shall remain in compliance with this
section.
      (3)   Reliance on state permit not part of state operating plan or
supplemental filing in addition to state operating plan. If the owner or
operator is relying on a state permit not part of a alternative operating plan
or other supplemental information filed with the department in addition to a
alternative operating plan for compliance with this section, the owner or
operator shall comply with all the following:
         a.   The owner or operator shall file with the department a copy of
the state operating plan and any amendments and supplemental information to
document compliance with this section along with an application for alternative
compliance under this section on a form determined by the department;
         b.   Within 45 days of receipt, the department or designee:
            1.   Review the application and other documents submitted;
            2.   Inspect the facility for compliance with the requirements of
this section to determine whether the application and other documents submitted
satisfy the requirements of this section and are adequate to protect the public
health and the environment and to prevent the emission of fugitive dust that
causes unreasonable interference with the comfortable enjoyment of life and
property; and
            3.   If applicable, issue a certificate of alternative compliance
confirming compliance with this section; and
         c.   The owner or operator remains in compliance with this section.
The department director may revoke a certificate of alternative compliance
issued under this section if an owner or operator does not remain in compliance
with this section.
   (f)   Local enforcement of state violation. If an owner or operator of a
facility violates the requirements of the alternative operating plan or permit
for the facility, or otherwise violates section 5524 of the Natural Resources
and Environmental Protection Act, being MCL 324.5524, or Rule 336.1371 and
336.1372 of the Michigan Administrative Code, as amended, and the Michigan
Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (“EGLE”), a successor
agency, or another state officer or agency does not act to remedy or penalize
the violation, the violation may be enforced as a violation under Sec.
13-562.
      The city reserves the right to notify EGLE, or its successor agency, of
any violations pursuant to this subsection for enforcement action.
   (g)   Nothing in this section shall be an exclusive remedy, or be construed
to impair or bar any cause of action or legal or equitable remedy of any person
or the public under applicable laws and regulations.
   (h)   Application renewal. The owner or operator of a facility subject to
this section shall apply for a renewal of a certificate of alternative
compliance whenever their applicable alternative operating plan is renewed,
modified, or amended. Renewal shall be made in the same manner as the initial
application, and is subject to all applicable terms and conditions of this
article.
      (1)   The owner or operator shall have 30 days from the date their
alternative operating plan is renewed, modified, or amended to submit an
application for renewal.
   (i)   Inspections. The department shall conduct semi-annual inspections for
the purpose of monitoring compliance with this section and may conduct other
inspections for the purpose of monitoring compliance with this article. If the
department determines that an owner or operator is not complying with the
requirements of this article, including, but not limited to this section, the
department director shall require the owner or operator to take action to
comply with this article, and shall impose fines authorized by Sec. 13-503 of
this article for each day the owner or operator fails to take the action
required by the department.
   (j)   Non-compliance. An owner or operator of a facility not in compliance
with this section at any time must comply with the standards set forth in
Division 4 of this article. An owner or operator of a facility shall not be
deemed in compliance with this section if one or more of the following apply:
      (1)   The state or other applicable authority determines that the owner
or operator is not in compliance with an alternative operating plan or state
permit applicable to the facility;
      (2)   The department determines that owner or operator has not complied
with the requirements of this section; or
      (3)   The owner or operator of the facility violates Rule 336.1901 of the
Michigan Administrative Code.
   (k)   Section definitions. For purposes of this section, the following words
and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this
section. Words and phrases not defined in this section shall have the meanings
as defined in Sec.
13-542 or in Part 55 of the Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental
Protection Act, Act 451 of 1994, MCL 324.5501 et seq., or Michigan
Administrative Code, Rule 336.1101 et seq.:
      (1)   Qualified bulk solid materials. Means bulk solid materials that
satisfy all of the following:
         a.   Are bulk solid materials as defined in Sec.
13-542;
         b.   Are not carbonaceous bulk solid material; and
         c.   Are a fugitive dust source or a potential fugitive dust source.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 3. APPLICATION (STANDARD COMPLIANCE), CERTIFICATE OF OPERATION, AND
FUGITIVE DUST PLAN **
Sec. 13-546.   Certificate of operation; initial application for temporary
certificate of operation; fees; minimum standards for control of fugitive dust.
   (a)   Initial application. Except for applications filed pursuant to
Division 2 of this article, an owner or operator of a facility regulated by
this article shall file an application for a certificate of operation to
operate pursuant to this article. Such application shall be filed with the
department on a form furnished by the department. The initial application by an
owner or operator shall include the following:
      (1)   Applicant contact information, including address, phone contact,
24-hour emergency contact information, and email address.
      (2)   Name and address of the facility.
      (3)   A non-refundable fee of $5,000.00. This fee is not inclusive of
other fees that may be required by the Code of Ordinances, the Zoning
Ordinance, or applicable law.
      (4)   Information required by for a fugitive dust plan under this
division.
      (5)   If applicable, information required by for an enclosure plan under
this division.
      (6)   An attestation, signed by the owner or operator of the facility,
that they have read and reviewed this article.
      (7)   Such other data and information as required by the department
pursuant to provisions and regulations of this article and applicable law.
   (b)   Application review. Upon the owner or operator filing a complete
application, the department director, or their designee, shall review the
application and any supporting materials and documents for compliance with the
requirements of this article and all other applicable laws, ordinances, and
codes.
      (1)   In determining whether to approve a fugitive dust plan and issue a
certificate of operation, the department shall solicit comments from the
department of public health and the water and sewerage department.
      (2)   The department shall evaluate the information provided in the
application to meet the requirements of this article.
   (c)   Approval, conditions, and renewal. Upon the owner or operator
providing evidence of compliance with the provisions of this article, including
where applicable, submitting an approved fugitive dust plan or an approved
enclosure plan, or both, and upon payment of the application fee established by
this article, the department director or their designee shall issue a
certificate of operation.
      (1)   Approval and expiration. The certificate of operation shall be
conditioned upon continued compliance with this article, and shall expire
annually from the date the certificate is issued.
      (2)   Conditions. The department director may attach reasonable
conditions to the certificate of operation to ensure minimization of any
adverse impacts, as long as such reasonable conditions comport with the
standards and requirements of this article and applicable law. Subject to Sec.
13-545 and any provision of this article to the contrary, these reasonable
conditions may include, but are not limited to, dust control and enclosure
requirements if the director finds that the facility has failed to demonstrate
its ability to control fugitive dust.
      (3)   Renewal. An application for renewal shall be made in the same
manner as the initial application, including payment of a non-refundable fee of
$5,000.00.
   (d)   Reservation of authority. Notwithstanding anything in this article to
the contrary, no applicant has a right to the issuance of a certificate of
operation. The city and department hereby reserve the right to determine who,
if anyone, shall be entitled to a certificate of operation, based on the
criteria listed in this article and all other applicable laws, ordinances, and
codes.
   (e)   Basis for denial of application. The department director shall deny an
application if it is incomplete or if the application does not demonstrate
compliance with the requirements of this article.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-547.   Fugitive dust plan; change or expansion in operations;
submission and review; public notice; contents.
   (a)   Fugitive dust plan. The fugitive dust plan shall be submitted along
with an application for a certificate of operation. Every owner or operator of
a facility must prepare, submit, and follow a fugitive dust plan that complies
with the following requirements:
      (1)   Pre-existing facilities. Subject to Sec.
13-544, all facilities operating pursuant to a valid certificate of occupancy
on the effective date of the ordinance that enacted this article, the first
fugitive dust plan shall be submitted within 90 days of the effective date of
the ordinance that enacted this article along with the initial application for
a certificate of operation.
      (2)   New and expanding facilities. For new facilities, or expansions or
changes of existing facilities, that come into operation after the effective
date of the ordinance that enacted this article, except those portions of
expanded facilities in operation on the effective date, the first fugitive dust
plan shall be submitted with the facility’
3.00 shall apply.
      (3)   Change or expansion in facility operations. If any part of the
facility’s operation changes or expands, then, at least 30 days before the
expansion or change in operation, the facility owner or operator shall notify
the department director, submit an application to amend the certificate of
operation, and submit a revised fugitive dust plan or establish to the
department director’s satisfaction that the expanded or changed operation will
be compliant with the existing fugitive dust plan. For purposes of determining
whether an existing facility has expanded, the criteria set forth in Zoning
Ordinance Article
3.00 shall apply.
      (4)   Annual plan updates. Every owner or operator of a facility shall
update their fugitive dust plan on an annual basis as part of the annual
renewal application for a certificate of operation. The annual update shall be
due one year to the date that the previous plan was approved by the department.
      (5)   Review of fugitive dust plan and public input. The department shall
review and approve all fugitive dust plans and all updates to fugitive dust
plans. The department shall not approve any fugitive dust plan or any update to
a fugitive dust plan required under this article until the public has had an
opportunity to submit written comments on the fugitive dust plan.
         a.   Public notice. The department shall post public notice of any new
fugitive dust plan or any amendment to an existing fugitive dust plan on the
city’s website. The department shall accept comments for a period of not less
than 30 days from the date of the notice. The department shall not make a
decision on the proposed fugitive dust plan or amendment until after the close
of the public comment period.
         b.   Disapproval of plan. If the department finds that the submitted
fugitive dust plan is missing any required information or is insufficient to
ensure compliance with this article, the department shall reject the fugitive
dust plan. The applicant may resubmit a fugitive dust plan for review subject
to the public notice and comment requirements of this subsection.
      (6)   Approval requirement. Subject to the provisions of this article, an
approved fugitive dust plan is required in order to obtain a certificate of
operation.
      (7)   Fugitive dust plan contents. Each fugitive dust plan must include,
at a minimum, the following:
         a.   The name and address of the facility.
         b.   The name, address, and contact information of the owner or
operator responsible for implementation of the fugitive dust plan, including
phone contact, 24-hour emergency contact information, and email address.
         c.   A site map, drawn to scale, in conformance with the requirements
and standards of Zoning Ordinance Section
32.02, and providing the following additional information:
            1.   Facility boundaries;
            2.   All buildings, internal roadways, and utilities on facility
property;
            3.   All roadways and transportation corridors within one quarter
mile of the perimeter of the facility that are used for transport of material
to or from the facility;
            4.   The location of all floor drains, storm drains, and storm
water outfalls;
            5.   All potential emission points at the facility, including a
depiction of the footprints of all bulk solid material storage piles, transfer
points, conveyors, and roadways; and
            6.   The location of all fugitive dust control devices and
monitoring devices, including the fugitive dust monitor and wind monitor.
         d.   A description of the facility’s operations, including a list of
all bulk solid materials handled at, processed at, or transported to, from, or
within the facility.
         e.   A description of the truck routes within one quarter mile of the
perimeter of the facility that are used to transport material to and from the
facility, including an explanation of how dust will be minimized during
transport (e.g., travel on paved roads where possible, minimize truck speeds,
etc.), and a description of the measures that will be used to ensure trucks are
cleaned of loose material before they leave the facility.
         f.   A calculation showing the facility’s maximum total outdoor bulk
storage material storage capacity in tons or cubic yards. In the first fugitive
dust plan, due within 90 days after the effective date of the ordinance that
enacted this article, the calculation shall be certified by signature of an
authorized representative of the owner or operator and shall be accompanied by
evidence of authority to sign on behalf of the owner or operator.
         g.   A description of all control measures, devices, and technologies
to be used to minimize and control fugitive dust, a description of how all
control measures, devices, and technologies will be actively maintained and
calibrated to ensure their continued effectiveness, and a description of the
training provided to staff regarding the proper application and operation of
all such control measures, devices, and technologies.
         h.   A dust monitoring plan that describes:
            1.   A description of the type, placement, operation, and
maintenance of PM10 monitors.
            2.   The schedule and plan for quarterly testing to ensure
compliance with this article. Such testing shall be:
               a.   Conducted by a professional trained and certified to read
opacity in accordance with the measurement method specified in Sec.
13-548; and
               b.   Conducted during a range of weather conditions to ensure
that representative conditions at the facility are covered.
            3.   A description of the facility’s recordkeeping system, which
shall include a schedule for routine inspection, testing, and maintenance.
         i.   A contingency plan describing the owner’s or operator’s planned
response activities when PM10 exceeds the reportable action level. The response
activities should consist of a range of increasingly aggressive measures
appropriate to different levels of exceedance.
         j.   A contingency plan for an alternative method of monitoring in the
event of malfunction or failure of any required PM10 monitors.
         k.   Other information as the department may require to facilitate its
review of the fugitive dust plan.
         l.   A fact sheet or executive summary of the fugitive dust plan
designed to inform the public of the facility’s plan to control and minimize
fugitive dust, which may be posted on the city’s website.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 4. MINIMUM FACILITY STANDARDS * **
   *Editor’s note—When applicable, the standards set forth in this division are
subject to the terms and conditions of Sec.
13-545.
Sec. 13-548.   Control of fugitive dust; opacity limits; measurements.
   The facility owner or operator shall control the discharge of dust into the
atmosphere as specified below:
   (a)   Visible dust. The facility owner or operator shall not cause or allow
any fugitive dust that is visible beyond the property line of the facility.
   (b)   Opacity limit. The facility owner or operator shall not cause or allow
any fugitive dust within the property line of the facility at any bulk solid
material storage pile, transfer point, roadway, or parking area that exceeds 5%
opacity. An owner or operator shall not cause or allow any fugitive dust beyond
the property line of the facility that has an opacity greater than 0%.
   (c)   Measurement of opacity. Opacity shall be determined by reference test
method 9d, as defined in section 5525 of the Michigan Natural Resources and
Environmental Protection Act, PA 451 of 1995, being MCL 324.5525(j).
   (d)   Testing of visual emissions and opacity limits. The facility owner or
operator shall, on at least a quarterly basis, perform tests of visual fugitive
dust and opacity in accordance with the protocols set forth in the facility’s
approved fugitive dust plan.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-549.   Conveyors and transfer points.
   (a)   All conveyors shall be covered or enclosed in order to reduce fugitive
dust emissions.
   (b)   The facility owner or operator shall maintain all material transfer
points in compliance with one of the following measures:
      (1)   Total enclosure; or
      (2)   Water spray system sufficient to control fugitive dust emissions.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-550.   Truck transport.
   (a)   When transport is by truck, the facility owner or operator shall
ensure that:
      (1)   All vehicles and off-road equipment adhere to the posted speed
limit within the facility, which shall be no more than 8 miles per hour;
      (2)   All outgoing material transport trucks, whether loaded or empty,
are cleaned so that any part of any tractor, bed, trailer, or tire exterior
surface, excluding the inside of the beds or trailer, are free of all loose
material; and
      (3)   All outgoing material transport trucks, whether loaded or empty,
pass through a wheel wash station and pass over rumble strips that will vibrate
the trucks and shake off loose material and dust, unless the approved fugitive
dust plan specifies other measures to ensure that the trucks will not cause any
track-out materials onto any public roadway.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-551.   Vehicle covering and other dust control measures; leaking
fluids.
   (a)   The facility owner or operator shall ensure that all trucks carrying
bulk solid material cover all truck beds and trailers before leaving the
facility in one of the following manners:
      (1)   A solid sliding cover or stackable cover on the top of the truck
bed or trailer that is kept completely closed except during loading; or
      (2)   A continuous tarp that completely covers the truck bed or trailer
and that is installed or constructed to prevent wind from entering over the
leading edge of the bed or trailer to prevent wind from entering over the
leading edge of the bed or trailer rim into the interior of the bed or trailer.
   (b)   The facility owner or operator shall load railcars and vessels in a
manner that will control dust through the use of best management practices,
such as, but not limited to, the use of solid covers, the application of dust
suppression agents and/or water, and the profiling of materials to prevent wind
erosion.
   (c)   Facility owners and operators shall not load material into truck beds,
trailers, railcars, or vessels such that a vehicle leaks material or liquid, or
emits fugitive dust during travel.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
* Sec. 13-552.   Truck loading and unloading. *
   (a)   Enclosed carbonaceous materials. For enclosed carbonaceous bulk solid
material storage piles, the facility owner or operator shall conduct material
truck loading and unloading only in an enclosed structure that is either
equipped with a water spray system to be used as needed to prevent visible dust
emissions or vented to permitted air pollution control equipment that is
operated during loading and unloading activities. The ends of the structure
shall have overlapping flaps that reduce the opening, sliding doors which shall
remain closed except to allow the trucks to enter and leave, or other equally
effective devices.
   (b)   Outdoor bulk solid materials. For outdoor bulk solid material storage,
the facility owner or operator shall ensure that truck loading and unloading
occurs in compliance with the requirements for transfer points specified in
this division.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-553.   Railcar loading and unloading.
   (a)   Enclosed carbonaceous materials. For enclosed carbonaceous bulk solid
material storage piles, the facility owner or operator shall conduct railcar
material loading and unloading only in an enclosed structure that is either
equipped with a water spray system operated to prevent visible dust emissions,
or vented to permitted air pollution control equipment that is operated during
loading and unloading activities. The ends of the structure shall have
overlapping flaps, sliding doors, or other equally effective devices, which
shall remain closed except to allow the railcars to enter and leave.
   (b)   Outdoor bulk solid materials. For outdoor bulk solid material storage,
the facility owner or operator shall ensure that railcar loading and unloading
occurs in compliance with the requirements for transfer points specified in
this division.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-554.   Vessel loading and unloading.
   The facility owner or operator shall conduct vessel material loading only
through an enclosed chute that uses a water spray system, or an air pollution
control system or other mechanism described in the approved fugitive dust plan,
in order to control fugitive dust emissions during operations. Vessel unloading
shall be conducted in a manner that will minimize dust in accordance with
measures set forth in the fugitive dust plan and in compliance with the
requirements for transfer points specified in this division.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-555.   Roadway cleaning and tracked material.
   (a)   In order to clean roads of spilled and tracked material, the facility
owner or operator shall use a street sweeper to clean any paved road that is
used to transport material inside or within one quarter mile of the perimeter
of the facility.
   (b)   The street sweeper shall be equipped with a water spray for use during
nonfreezing weather, and a vacuum system to prevent fugitive dust during street
sweeping.
   (c)   The facility owner or operator shall utilize a street sweeper meeting
the requirements described in this section to clean any paved road that is used
to transport material inside or within one quarter mile of the perimeter of the
facility at least once per day. The facility owner or operator shall document
whether street sweeping has been conducted at least once per day, and the
record shall show the date and time when street sweeping was performed.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-556.   Outdoor storage of bulk solid material other than carbonaceous
materials; height limits and screening; protection of waterways; high wind
events; dust suppressant system; runoff management.
   (a)   Outdoor bulk solid material storage. A facility owner or operator may
maintain outdoor storage of bulk solid materials other than carbonaceous
materials if the facility meets all of the requirements of this section.
   (b)   Height limits and screening. The vertical distance from the grade
immediately adjacent to a pile to the highest point of that pile shall be no
greater than 25 feet. Piles shall be screened from view from adjacent rights-
of-way and properties at the level of the right-of-way.
      (1)   Exception for combustible materials. Combustible materials capable
of self-ignition through chemical action of its constituents shall be no
greater than 15 feet. Piles shall be screened from view from adjacent rights-
of-way and properties at the level of the right-of-way.
   (c)   Protection of waterways. Outdoor storage piles shall be set back at
least 100 feet from a waterway, except that material in the process of being
unloaded from or loaded to a vessel may be located within 100 feet of a
waterway for a period of time not to exceed 24 hours so long as no materials
are allowed to fall, erode, be thrown, discharged, dumped, disposed of, or
deposited in the waterway at any time.
   (d)   High wind events. The disturbance of outdoor bulk solid material
piles, including but not limited to outdoor loading, unloading, and any other
processing shall be suspended during high wind conditions, unless alternate
measures are implemented to effectively control dust in accordance with the
approved fugitive dust plan.
   (e)   Dust suppressant system. The facility owner or operator shall apply
chemical stabilizers and/or maintain and operate a wind screen, water spray
bars, a misting system, water spray systems, and/or water trucks to prevent
fugitive dust emissions in violation those standards set forth in this
division, in accordance with the following requirements:
      (1)   Except as otherwise stated in subsection (e)(3) below, the dust
suppressant system shall be operable and able to dispense water, water-based
solutions, and/or chemical stabilizers at all times unless all bulk storage
material piles are covered or protected by wind screens.
      (2)   When the temperature falls below 32 degrees Fahrenheit, the
facility must use chemical stabilizers and/or water heating systems to ensure
that dust suppression continues.
      (3)   If any part of the dust suppressant system is undergoing
maintenance or otherwise becomes inoperable, the facility owner or operator
must suspend disturbance of bulk solid material piles that would be controlled
by the same inoperable portion of the dust suppressant system until such time
as the system becomes operable again.
   (f)   Runoff management. The facility owner or operator shall install and
maintain storm water management, erosion, and sediment controls, pursuant to a
written plan, sufficient to:
      (1)   Prevent runoff from the pile onto neighboring parcels, public ways,
or any water bodies.
      (2)   Prevent runoff from entering into public sewers or any entry point
into the storm water collection system, unless such discharges are in
compliance with all applicable discharge permits.
      (3)   Address timely and effective ways to respond to spills and/or
visible migration of pollutants that could occur onsite or offsite.
      (4)   Demonstrate that the site is graded in such a way as to ensure
proper drainage and to prevent pooling of water.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-557.   Carbonaceous bulk solid material facilities; enclosure of
carbonaceous materials; enclosure plan; enclosure requirement for existing,
new, and expanding facilities; enclosure deadline; interim requirements.
   (a)   General enclosure requirement. Except as authorized in Division 7, the
owner or operator of a carbonaceous bulk solid material facility that requires
the enclosure of carbonaceous bulk solid materials shall maintain all
carbonaceous bulk solid material in a fully enclosed structure in accordance
with the enclosure requirements described in this section.
   (b)   Enclosure plan. The owner or operator of any carbonaceous bulk solid
material facility that requires the enclosure of carbonaceous bulk solid
materials shall submit to the department for review and approval a plan for the
total enclosure of all carbonaceous piles, conveyors, transfer points, and
processing areas at a facility. The plan must include:
      (1)   A construction schedule prepared using the critical path method for
completion, procurement, permitting, and construction of the enclosure.
      (2)   An interim fugitive dust plan that complies with all of the
requirements of Sec.
13-547.
   (c)   Enclosure requirement. Fully enclosed structures for all carbonaceous
bulk solid material facilities that require enclosure pursuant to this section
must comply with the following requirements:
      (1)   Structures that are used to store, handle, or transfer carbonaceous
material shall be completely roofed and walled structures or buildings with
impermeable floors that entirely surround the carbonaceous bulk solid materials
and shall be designed, permitted, and constructed in accordance with applicable
building code requirements, zoning requirements, and other applicable laws,
ordinances, and regulations.
      (2)   Structures used to store, handle, or transfer carbonaceous bulk
solid materials hall be properly maintained and shall be equipped with and
shall use a permitted air pollution control system and/or the ability to apply
water to materials within a structure sufficient to control fugitive dust
emissions at designed vents and at any other openings, including entrances and
exits.
      (3)   Entrances and exits for material or vehicles shall have overlapping
flaps, sliding doors or other devices, which shall remain closed except to
allow material or vehicles to enter and leave or to allow people to enter and
exit, provided that if devices other than overlapping flaps or solid doors are
used, then the performance for dust control as the openings must be shown in
the fugitive dust plan to be equivalent to or better than that of the
overlapping flaps or sliding doors used in conjunction with the required air
pollution controls as determined by the department.
      (4)   Fully enclosed structures in compliance with this section need not
comply with the fugitive dust monitoring requirements of Division 5.
   (d)   Enclosure exemption and abatement for existing facilities; enclosure
deadline for new facilities, expanded facilities, and recommencement of
operation.
      (1)   Enclosure exemption. Subject to the terms and conditions of Sec.
13-545, facilities continuing in operation on the effective date of the
ordinance that enacted this article are exempt from the enclosure requirements
of this section. This exemption is subject to continued compliance with the
provisions of this article, including but not limited to those concerning the
control and mitigation of fugitive dust.
      (2)   For new facilities, expansion or recommencement of operation of
existing facilities, compliance with the enclosure requirements is a condition
to receiving a certificate of operation.
   (e)   Interim requirements. During the implementation requirements described
in this section, carbonaceous bulk solid material may be maintained in outdoor
piles subject to the following requirements:
      (1)   The facility owner or operator must comply with the approved
interim fugitive dust plan.
      (2)   The owner or operator of the facility must comply with all
requirements described in Sec.
13-556.
      (3)   Pre-existing facilities. All facilities operating pursuant to a
valid certificate of occupancy on the effective date of the ordinance that
enacted this article are exempt from the requirements of this subsection (e)
for a period of 180 days following the effective date. By the expiration date
of 180 days, such facilities shall conform to all requirements of this
subsection (e).
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 5. MONITORING AND COMPLIANCE **
Sec. 13-558.   Fugitive dust monitoring.
   (a)   Unless, pursuant to the variance procedure set forth in this article,
the facility owner or operator establishes that the facility’s operations do
not and will not result in off-site fugitive dust emissions, or if the facility
qualifies as exempt under Sec.
13-545, the department shall require the facility owner or operator to install,
operate, and maintain, according to the manufacturer’s specifications,
permanent, continuous, federal equivalent method (FEM) real-time PM10 monitors
around the perimeter of the facility in accordance with the requirements
specified in this section.
   (b)   First year of monitoring; placement of monitors. During the first year
of monitoring, at least one monitor shall be placed along each side facing the
four cardinal directions (north, south, east, and west) around the facility to
monitor for fugitive dust in the ambient air around the facility.
   (c)   Subsequent years of monitoring; placement of monitors. During the
second and all subsequent years of monitoring, monitors shall be placed in
accordance with the fugitive dust plan based on the data observed in the first
year, with monitors located at a minimum of two upwind and two downwind
locations and additional monitors as appropriate depending on the size of the
facility and other relevant factors, such as variability of wind direction at
the site and the proximity of neighborhoods.
   (d)   A data logger shall be attached to the monitors to record readings
from the monitors, and the facility owner or operator shall notify the
department in writing within 24 hours each time the monitors exceed the
reportable action level, and any time monitoring equipment has malfunctioned
preventing readings or logging of data.
   (e)   The facility owner or operator shall maintain a log of all maintenance
and calibration activities associated with each fugitive dust monitor.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-559.   Wind monitoring.
   The facility owner or operator shall install, operate, and maintain,
according to manufacturer’s specifications, a weather station or other
permanent device to monitor and log wind speed and wind direction at the
facility at an unobstructed, unsheltered area, centrally positioned in relation
to the storage piles, and at a minimum height of 10 meters above ground level.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-560.   Recordkeeping; quarterly review; record retention.
   (a)   The facility owner or operator shall record all roadway cleaning and
street sweeping daily.
   (b)   The facility owner or operator shall record the application of water
and/or chemical stabilizers, as applicable, as well as any instances when such
application was suspended for any reason, including, but not limited to,
weather conditions.
   (c)   The facility owner and operator shall record any instance when
activities were suspended due to high winds.
   (d)   The facility owner or operator shall record results of the continuous
monitoring for PM10, indicate any instances when a monitor detected PM10 that
exceeds the reportable action level, and record the action taken to respond to
the exceedance of the reportable action level.
   (e)   The facility owner or operator shall record the results of the tests
of visual fugitive dust and opacity.
   (f)   The facility owner or operator shall maintain a schedule for routine
inspections, maintenance, and testing of all fugitive dust control measures,
devices, and technologies, including a schedule for inspection of bulk solid
material piles, inspection of all monitors, and inspection of off-site areas
for the presence of dust, and identify the person or persons responsible for
conducting such inspections, maintenance, and testing.
   (g)   All records required to be kept pursuant to this section shall be
submitted to the department on a quarterly basis, and kept and maintained at
the facility and be available for inspection for a minimum of three years.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 6. INSPECTIONS, ENFORCEMENT, AND PENALTIES **
Sec. 13-561.   Inspections.
   (a)   Inspections for the purpose of monitoring compliance with this article
shall be conducted by the department on a semiannual basis.
   (b)   The department may conduct inspections for the purpose of monitoring
compliance with this article in response to any complaints received by the
department, or the department’s reasonable suspicion of a violation of this
article.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-562.   Enforcement.
   (a)   Illegal dumping and nuisance. Except for activities in accordance with
this article, any dumping, storing, depositing, or transporting bulk solid
material on any private property, public property, right-of-way, or surface
water or around any approved or portable container is illegal dumping, is a
nuisance violation, and is subject to the fines and penalties provided for in
this ordinance.
   (b)   Notice of violation. If a violation or condition(s) causing or
contributing to a violation of this article is discovered, a notice of
violation shall be issued. Such notice shall inform the owner or operator of
the facility of the nature of the violation, and require the owner or operator
of the facility to eliminate and correct the violation or condition(s) causing
or contributing to the violation within 30 days of notification.
   (c)   Violation and penalty. Failure to correct a violation within the time
permitted after receiving notice under subsection (b) shall constitute a
violation of this article, which is punishable as a civil infraction subject to
a fine of $1,000.00, plus any additional costs and/or conditions imposed by the
court.
   (d)   Repeat violation. An increased fine schedule shall be imposed for
repeat violations of this article. As used in this section, “repeat violation”
means a violation committed within 90 days of an admission or determination of
responsibility for a violation of this article occurring upon the same
property. The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall be a civil fine of
$2,500.00, plus any additional costs and/or conditions imposed by the court.
   (e)   Each day that a violation of this article continues shall be a
separate violation.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 7. DEVIATIONS AND APPEALS **
Sec. 13-563.   Variances; application; requirements; review; revocation and
appeal; change in operations; public notice.
   (a)   No variance from alternative compliance plan allowed. Facilities
operating pursuant to an alternative compliance plan, as that term is defined
in Sec.
13-542, may not seek a variance from any standard, requirement, or condition of
that alternative compliance plan.
   (b)   Application for variance. Unless otherwise stated, a facility owner or
operator may apply to the department for a variance from any requirement set
forth in Secs.
13-549 to
13-560, in accordance with the provisions set forth in this section. The
department shall establish a schedule of fees pursuant to which a variance
review fee may be assessed per application.
   (c)   Requirements for a variance application. A request for a variance
shall be submitted to the department director, in writing and must set forth,
in detail, all of the following information:
      (1)   A statement identifying the provision or requirement of this
article from which the variance is requested.
      (2)   A description of the process or activity for which the variance is
requested, including the pertinent data on location, size, and the population
and geographic area affected by, or potentially affected by, the process or
activity.
      (3)   The quantity and types of materials used in the process or activity
in connection with which the variance is requested, as appropriate.
      (4)   A demonstration that issuance of the variance will not create a
public nuisance, a public health hazard, or adversely impact the surrounding
area, surrounding environment, the surrounding residents, or surrounding
property uses.
      (5)   A statement explaining why compliance with the requirements in this
article imposes an arbitrary and unreasonable hardship, why compliance cannot
be accomplished during the required timeframe due to events beyond the facility
owner or operator’s control such as permitting delays or natural disasters, or
why the proposed alternative measure is superior or preferred.
      (6)   A description of the proposed methods to achieve compliance with
the regulations and a timetable for achieving that compliance, if applicable.
      (7)   A discussion of alternate methods of compliance and of the factors
influencing the choice of applying for a variance.
      (8)   A statement regarding the person’s current status as related to the
subject matter of the variance request.
      (9)   For any request for a variance from the enclosure deadline, the
applicant must submit, in addition to the other information required by this
section, fugitive dust monitoring reports for the four (4) months prior to the
date of the variance application, and, if the variance is granted, monthly
fugitive dust monitoring reports for the duration of the variance which shall
be due 14 days following the end of the month which the report covers.
   (d)   Criteria for reviewing applications.
      (1)   In determining whether to grant a variance, the department will
consider public comments received pursuant to this section, as well as input
and comments from the Public Health Department director or designee, and will
evaluate the information provided in the application to meet the requirements
of subsection (c) of this section. Particular consideration will be given to
the following information:
         a.   Inclusion of a definite compliance program;
         b.   Evaluation of all reasonable alternatives for compliance;
         c.   Demonstration that any adverse impacts will be minimal.
      (2)   The department director shall deny the variance if the application
for the variance is incomplete or if the application is outside the scope of
relief provided by variances.
      (3)   The department director may deny a variance, may grant a variance
in whole or in part, and may attach reasonable conditions to the variance to
ensure minimization of any adverse impacts.
      (4)   Granting a variance is at the sole discretion of the department
director. A variance may be revoked at any time if the department director
finds that operation of the facility is creating a public nuisance, a public
health hazard, or otherwise adversely impacting the surrounding area,
surrounding environment, surrounding residents, or surrounding property uses.
         a.   Notice. The director shall issue a written notice to revoke a
variance to the facility owner or operator. The notice shall provide the
grounds for revocation, the effective date of the revocation, and that the
facility owner or operator may, within 20 calendar days, request in writing an
appeal hearing before the Building Board of Appeals.
         b.   Request for appeal. The facility owner or operator may request an
appeal hearing before the Building Board of Appeals for the revocation of a
variance granted pursuant to this section. The request for hearing must be in
writing and must be submitted to the City Clerk within 20 calendar days of
receiving notice of revocation.
         c.   Notice of hearing. Upon receipt of a request for appeal, the
Building Board of Appeals shall provide the facility owner or operator with
notice and an opportunity to be heard. The Board shall serve notice upon the
facility owner or operator by certified mail, not less than 20 calendar days
prior to the hearing date. The notice shall state:
            i.   The date, time, and place of the hearing.
            ii.   A statement that the facility owner or operator may present
evidence and testimony, and may be represented by an attorney.
         d.   Hearing and decision. The hearing shall be conducted by the
Building Board of Appeals no later than 30 days after the day on which the
request for appeal was filed, and shall be open to the public. The Board shall
decide the appeal at the public hearing. Within 14 calendar days of the public
hearing, the Board shall provide the licensee with a copy of its decision which
shall include the specific grounds for its decision.
      (5)   Change in facility operations. If any part of the facility’s
operation that is the subject of the variance expands or changes, then, at
least 30 calendar days prior to the expansion or change in operation, the
facility owner or operator shall notify the department director and either
apply for a new variance or notify the department director of the owner or
operator’s intent to comply with the requirements that were the subject of the
variance, in which case the variance will automatically terminate. For purposes
of determining whether an existing facility has expanded or changed, the
criteria set forth in Zoning Ordinance Article 3.00 shall apply.
      (6)   Notice of variance applications; comments from the public. The
department director shall not grant any variance under this section until after
the public has had an opportunity to submit written comments on the requested
variance(s). The department director shall provide notice of all variance
applications by the following methods:
         a.   By posting on the City’s website; and
         b.   By mailed or delivered notice to all addresses located within 300
feet of the boundaries of the facility seeking the variance. Such notice shall
include information on where to access information regarding the requested
variance(s).
      The department director shall accept written comments for a period of not
less than 30 days from the date of publication of the notice. The department
director shall not make a decision until after close of the comment period.
Notice of the decision shall be posted on the city’s website.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-564.   Appeals.
   (a)   Application procedure. With the exception of appeals governed by Sec.
13-563 of this article, any facility owner or operator aggrieved by any
decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order issued by the department
pursuant to this article may appeal same to the Building Board of Appeals,
which is empowered and authorized to hear and consider such appeal, as follows:
      (1)   A person wishing to file an appeal pursuant to this section shall
file a written appeal requesting such hearing and setting forth a brief
statement of the grounds for appeal and the relief requested. Such appeal shall
be filed with the director of the department within 20 days after the decision,
ruling, interpretation, notice, or order complained of. The director shall
transmit to the board the following:
         a.   The written appeal and any papers, materials, and documents that
are included with the submittal at the time of submission.
         b.   All papers, materials, and documents associated with the
decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order being appealed.
      (2)   Upon receipt of the petition for appeal, the Building Board of
Appeals shall set a time and place for such hearing and shall give the
appellant written notice thereof.
   (b)   Scope and procedure of appeal.
      (1)   Scope of appeal. The appeal procedure is intended to provide
limited relief from the decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order
issued by the department pursuant to this article, where a strict application
of same creates an unnecessary hardship affecting a substantial property right.
This procedure is intended to address extraordinary, exceptional, or unique
situations that were not caused by an act or omission of the applicant or the
applicant’s predecessor in title, employee, or agent. Relief is not to be
granted merely on the basis of inconvenience or financial burden.
      (2)   The Board has the authority to hear and decide appeals where it is
alleged there is an error in any interpretation, requirement, decision, or
determination made by the department in the enforcement, interpretation, or
administration of this article.
      (3)   Any appeal or variance from the requirements of the Zoning
Ordinance shall be heard by the Zoning Board of Appeals pursuant to Sec.
32.05 of the zoning ordinance.
      (4)   Any appeal or variance pursuant to Sec. 13-519 shall be heard
pursuant to the provisions of that section.
   (c)   Fee. A non-refundable fee of $250.00, as specified in Chapter 9, Sec.
9-38 of the Code of Ordinances, shall be paid to the City Treasurer at the time
the appeal is filed.
   (d)   Hearing. At the hearing the appellant is entitled to legal
representation by an attorney, and shall be given an opportunity to be heard
and to show why such decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or order should
be modified or withdrawn. The hearing shall be held at the next scheduled
Building Board of Appeals meeting or at a special meeting of the Board, not
later than 30 days after the day on which the petition was filed; provided that
upon application of the appellant or the department, the Board may postpone the
date of the hearing for a reasonable time beyond such 30-day period, if in the
judgment of the Board the requesting party has submitted a good and sufficient
reason for such postponement.
   (e)   Action by Board of Appeals. After the hearing, the Board shall
sustain, modify, or withdraw the decision, ruling, interpretation, notice, or
order being appealed, depending on the Board’s findings to whether the
provisions of this article and of the rules and regulations adopted pursuant
thereto have been complied with. If the Board sustains such decision, ruling,
interpretation, notice, or order, it shall be deemed to be an order.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
** DIVISION 8. PUBLIC HEARINGS, DESIGNATED FUND, SEVERABILITY, AND EFFECTIVE
DATE OF ORDINANCE **
Sec. 13-565.   Public hearings.
   Public hearings conducted pursuant to this article shall be governed by the
Open Meetings Act, PA 267 of 1976, MCL 15.261 et seq., as amended.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-566.   Designated purposes fund.
   (a)   The designated purposes fund is created as a separate depository fund
that shall consist of the following:
      (1)   Money deposited in the designated purposes fund under subsection
(c);
      (2)   Money appropriated or allocated to the designated purposes fund by
ordinance, Council resolution, or the Code of Ordinances; and
      (3)   Donations of money to the designated purposes fund from any other
source.
   (b)   Money in the designated purposes fund at the close of a fiscal year
will remain in the fund and not revert to the general fund.
   (c)   Notwithstanding a contrary provision of this code, a penalty or fine
paid to the city for a violation of this article must be credited and deposited
in the designated purposes fund.
   (d)   The Department of Public Health and Department of Economic Development
may expend money from the designated purposes fund upon appropriation only for
activities promoting the public health and wellness of residents of the city
and to mitigate negative health impacts of pollution on residents of the city,
including, but not limited to, enforcement of this article, purchasing,
installation, use, and maintenance of air monitoring equipment, installation of
vegetation to buffer the impact of activities subject to regulation under this
article, and conducting health impact assessments.
   (e)   A grant or other donation to the designated purposes fund must be
accepted by City Council and is subject to any conditions on the grant or
donation.
   (f)   An agreement or contract for expenditure of money from the designated
purposes fund must be approved by City Council.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-567.   Applicability of other laws.
   The requirements of this article in no way affect the responsibilities of
the facility owner and operator to comply with all other applicable federal,
state, or local laws, ordinances, regulations, or code requirements, including
but not limited to those regarding the zoning, construction, operation,
maintenance, and closure of the facility, whether or not such other laws are
specifically referenced in this article.
(Ord. No. 24-1815, 4-23-24)
Sec. 13-568.   Severability.
   If any sentence, paragraph, section, clause, article, division, or provision
of the ordinance from which this article is derives shall be declared to be
