123.51 et seq.
*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 15-1. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate the use of parks and park
property owned or maintained by the city in order that all residents and their
guests may enjoy and make use of such parks and park property, and to protect
the rights of those owning property adjacent to such parks.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 2, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-2. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Department shall mean the city department of recreation.
   Director shall mean the director of the department of recreation.
   Major park shall refer to the following public parks and buildings and
facilities thereon: Town Hall Park, Civic Center Park and Ford Field Park.
   Neighborhood park shall refer to all other parks, public buildings,
recreation and playground areas and buildings and facilities thereon not
designated as a "major park."
   Park shall mean any public park, or recreation or playground area, or
building or facility thereon, within the city, owned or maintained by the city
as a public park, or recreation or playground area, whether or not such areas
have been formally dedicated to such purpose.
   Park ranger shall mean an ordinance officer assigned to enforce the
provisions of this chapter.
   Permit shall mean the written permission that must be obtained from the
director or his designated agent to carry out a given activity in a park.
   Vehicle shall mean any motor driven device designed to transport persons or
property.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 3, 11-7-85; Ord. No. 05-1048, 7-5-05)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 15-3. - Ejection from park.
   In addition to general criminal penalties, any person found violating any
provisions of this chapter may be ejected from the park and/or have their
permit confiscated and park privileges suspended for a period to be determined
by the director.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 20, 11-7-85; Ord. No. 05-1048, 7-5-05)
Secs. 15-4—15-20. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - PARK RULES AND REGULATIONS ***
Sec. 15-21. - Hours; exception.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to use, occupy, frequent, loiter
or be in any park between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., unless
otherwise posted at the park or unless a special permit for such use or
occupancy has been previously given by the director of recreation of the city
therein, or unless such person is participating in a scheduled recreation
department activity. At the closing hour of the parks, all persons within the
parks shall immediately depart therefrom. No person, having been directed to
leave the park at the closing hour by any city employee, shall fail to depart
therefrom immediately.
   (b)   Exception. The parking of vehicles after 10:00 p.m. by customers and
employees of area businesses shall be permitted in specified areas of Ford
Field Park, subject to the posted regulations. After 10:00 p.m., these
individuals may enter Ford Field Park for the parking of vehicles only.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 8, 11-7-85; Ord. No. 04-1000, 4-20-04)
Sec. 15-22. - Unlawful conduct.
   No person while in or about the parks shall engage in any conduct
threatening, endangering or impairing the safety, health or comfort of others,
or shall indulge in profane or indecent language, any improper or indecent
conduct, or any unduly boisterous or offensive conduct of any character.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 9, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-23. - Noise.
   No person shall operate or cause to be operated any source of loud or
unusual noise in any park which disturbs the peace and quiet of any park or
which causes any discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal
sensitiveness in such park.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 10, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-24. - Picnic areas and use.
   (a)   The director shall designate those areas of a park where picnicking is
permitted. No person shall picnic other than in a designated area.
   (b)   Picnickers shall not leave a picnic area before all trash in the
nature of boxes, papers, cans, bottles, garbage and other refuse is either
removed from the park or placed in a disposal receptacle.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 11, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-25. - Alcoholic beverages.
   No person shall bring into, consume or sell alcoholic beverages in a park,
except:
      (1)   Alcoholic beverages may be sold by persons operating under a
concession from the city, subject to the regulation and control of the
director.
      (2)   Alcoholic beverages can be consumed at family or group picnics or
functions, provided a permit for such consumption is obtained.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 12, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-26. - Camping.
   No person shall camp in a park without first obtaining a camping permit from
the director or his designated agent.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 13, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-27. - Fires.
   (a)   No person shall start or maintain in any park any outdoor fire except
in designated picnic areas. Fires shall be limited to cooking fires started and
maintained only in a stove, fireplace or barbecue pit maintained by the
department or in a portable camp stove.
   (b)   No person starting or maintaining any fire in a park shall leave the
area where the fire is located without first completely extinguishing the fire
or placing hot coals in a receptacle provided by the department and designated
for that sole purpose.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 14, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-28. - Animals and pets; exception.
    (a)   No domestic animals or pets, with the exception of verified service
dogs, shall be permitted in a park, other than the Dearborn Dog Park, unless a
written permit is obtained from the director.
   (b)   Exception: Dogs shall be permitted in Crowley Park, Geer Park, Oxford
Park, Penn-Vassar Park, Schemansky Park, Summer-Stephens Park, and Ten Eyck
Park, subject to the conditions and requirements of this section and applicable
federal, state, and local laws.
   (c)   Use in parks identified in subsection (b).
      (1)   Dogs must be on a leash of suitable strength and no longer than six
feet in length and held by the owner or other responsible person.
      (2)   Dog handlers shall immediately pick-up and properly dispose of pet
waste.
      (3)   Dogs are restricted to the track and area immediately adjacent to
the track of each permitted park, and are not allowed in public buildings or
other park areas, including but not limited to areas under and immediately
adjacent to play structures and play equipment; the playing surface and area of
ball fields, soccer fields, basketball courts, tennis courts, outdoor ice
rinks, and sledding hills; pavilions and stages; pool areas; and in areas
designated for City permitted events and functions.
      (4)   Dog owners/handlers must stop any accompanied dog from digging and
must fill any holes caused by an accompanied dog.
      (5)   It shall be unlawful for any owner/handler to bring a dog that has
a contagious condition, disease, parasites, or fresh wound into the parks.
   (d)   Bites, scratches, and aggression in parks identified in subsection
(b).
      (1)   All bites and scratches by a dog in the parks must be reported to
the Dearborn Police Department. It shall be unlawful for any owner/handler to
fail to report a bite or scratch by an accompanied dog of another person or
another dog within 24-hours of the incident.
      (2)   All dog bites shall be reported in accordance with Sec.
4-31 of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances, entitled "Dog Bite Reporting
Requirements."
      (3)   Dogs showing aggression towards people or other dogs must be
removed from the parks listed in subsection (b) immediately. It shall be
unlawful for any owner/handler to fail to immediately remove any dog showing
aggression from the park. Dogs that exhibit aggressive behavior are not allowed
in the parks at any time.
      (4)   It shall be unlawful for any person to bring any dog deemed to be a
vicious dog or a dangerous dog by any state or local government or agency into
the parks listed in subsection (b).
   (e)   Penalties.
      (1)   Any person who violates this section shall be subject to the
following:
         a.   First offense: The person is responsible for a civil infraction
and shall be fined $100.00;
         b.   Second offense: The person is responsible for a civil infraction
and shall be fined $250.00;
         c.   Third offense: The person is responsible for a civil infraction
and shall be fined $500.00; and
         d.   Fourth and subsequent offenses: The person is guilty of a
misdemeanor as defined in section
1-9.
      (2)   In addition, any person found violating any provisions of this
section may be ejected from the park and/or have their permit confiscated and
park privileges suspended for a period to be determined by the director of
recreation.
   (f)   The owner of a dog shall be liable for damages for any and all
injuries to a person or property caused by such dog, to be determined and
collected in appropriate civil proceedings, and nothing in this chapter shall
be construed to impose any liability upon the city, its agents or employees,
for damages caused by such dog in accordance with section
4-22 and state law, MCL § 287.321, et. seq. and MCL § 287.351.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 15, 11-7-85; Ord. No. 16-1550, 10-4-16; Ord. No. 17-1575,
3-21-17; Ord. No. 19-1666, 11-26-19)
Sec. 15-29. - Games.
   No person in a park shall take part in or abet the playing of any games
involving thrown or otherwise propelled objects such as balls, stones, arrows,
javelins, kites or model airplanes except in areas set apart for such forms of
recreation. The playing of organized games such as football, baseball and the
like is prohibited except on fields, courts or areas designated for such use.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 16, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-30. - Operation of vehicles.
   (a)   No person shall operate a vehicle in a park except upon designated
paved or improved park roads or driveways, or in and upon designated areas or
trails set aside for use by such vehicles, unless directed by a law enforcement
officer or recreation employee to do so, or by official signs or markings.
   (b)   No person shall operate a vehicle within the park in excess of 15
miles per hour, except upon those roads or driveway where official signs or
markings designate a different speed limit.
   (c)   All applicable state and local vehicle and traffic laws and ordinances
shall continue in full force and effect in any park, and shall be enforced by
any law enforcement officer.
   (d)   There shall be no loitering within a parked car for any purpose.
   (e)   No person shall park a vehicle on park property other than in areas
designated for parking that type of vehicle.
   (f)   No vehicle shall be left parked on park property after park closing
hours without obtaining a permit from the director, except as provided for in
subsection
15-21(b).
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 17, 11-7-85; Ord. No. 04-1000, 4-20-04)
Sec. 15-31. - Contributions.
   No person shall solicit contributions in a park for any purpose.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 18, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-32. - Merchandising, advertising and signs.
   No person in a park shall:
      (1)   Expose or offer for sale or hire any article, thing or service, nor
station or place any stand, cart or vehicle for the transportation, sale or
display of any article, thing or service, unless a permit has been obtained
from the director.
      (2)   Paste, glue, tack or otherwise place any sign, placard,
advertisement or inscription in a park, unless done pursuant to regulations
promulgated by the director.
(Ord. No. 85-330, § 19, 11-7-85)
Sec. 15-33. - Designated playing fields, courts.
   No person shall enter onto a designated playing field or court while a
sporting event is in progress.
(Ord. No. 05-1048, 7-5-05)
Sec. 15-34. - Motorized vehicles.
   Motorized vehicles are not permitted in any city park. "Motorized vehicle"
shall include, but not limited to: gopeds, mopeds, pocket bikes, motorized go-
carts and motorized skateboards.
(Ord. No. 05-1048, 7-5-05)
Sec. 15-35. - Enforcement.
   All officers of the police department, as well as city employees designated
as ordinance officers or park rangers, are hereby charged with enforcement of
this chapter and are authorized to issue violation tickets for any violation of
this chapter.
(Ord. No. 05-1048, 7-5-05)
Sec. 15-36. - Smoking in parks and other city-owned property; regulations.
   (a)   For the purposes of this article, smoke or smoking means possessing a
cigarette, e-cigarette, cigar, hookah, or pipe that contains tobacco or any
other product that is lighted or burning; lighting a cigarette, e-cigarette,
cigar, hookah, or pipe that contains tobacco or any other product; or exhaling
smoke from burning tobacco or any other burning product that is contained in a
hookah, pipe, cigar, cigarette and/or e-cigarette.
   (b)   Community and neighborhood parks. Smoke or smoking is prohibited
within 15 feet of the outermost edge of any play structure that has been
erected in a community or neighborhood park.
      (1)   Community and neighborhood parks are:
         •   Ford Community and Performing Arts Center;
         •   Crowley;
         •   Hemlock;
         •   Ford Field;
         •   Lapeer;
         •   Ford Woods;
         •   Levagood;
         •   Anthony;
         •   Argyle-Williamson;
         •   Bennington;
         •   Edison;
         •   Schemansky;
         •   Oak;
         •   Geer;
         •   Oxford;
         •   Penn-Vassar;
         •   Summer Stephens;
         •   Ten Eyck;
         •   Whitmore Bolles;
         •   York.
   (c)   Mini-Parks with play equipment. Smoke or smoking is prohibited within
any mini-park that has play equipment.
      (1)   Examples of mini-parks are: Cherry Hill, Dearborn High, Martha-
Myrtle, Tannahill, Palmer-Jerome, Riverdale and Morningside.
   (d)   Smoke and/or smoking is prohibited on the city-owned property known as
West Village Commons Plaza.
   (e)   A violation of this section shall constitute a civil infraction, which
shall be punishable by a fine of not more than $50.00 and costs. In the
discretion of the court, community service may be ordered in lieu of a $50.00
fine and costs.
(Ord. No. 16-1532, 4-12-16; Ord. No. 17-1586, - -17)
Secs. 15-37—15-50. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - DEARBORN DOG PARK ***
Sec. 15-51. - Location; purpose.
   The Dearborn Dog Park is located at 16301 Michigan Avenue, Dearborn and is
available for use by Dearborn residents only. The dog park is located in the
green space south of the Henry Ford Centennial Library parking lot.
   The dog park is a location set aside for dogs and their owners to exercise
and play off leash in a controlled (i.e., fenced) environment.
   Users of the dog park do so at their own risk. Dog behavior can be
unpredictable around other dogs and strangers. Dog owners/handlers are strictly
liable for any damage or injury caused by their accompanied dog(s).
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-52. - Dog park season.
   (a)   The dog park shall be open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. The dog
park may close periodically for routine maintenance.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for anyone to loiter, idle, wander, stroll or
play in the dog park when it is closed. However, if anyone applies for
permission to carry out an activity in the dog park during the hours it is
closed, and the director of the recreation and parks department determines that
such activity will not create a disturbance or public nuisance, the director
shall have the authority to issue a special permit for such activity.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-53. - Dog park use, generally.
   (a)   A permit is required to use the dog park.
   (1)   Registration to obtain a permit can be completed by mail or in person
at the city clerk's office. Once payment is received, a key fob and dog tag
will be issued allowing access to the dog park. Permits shall be issued to
Dearborn residents only and shall expire annually on March 1.
      a.   Permit fees will be waived for verified service dogs.
   (2)   A copy of the Dearborn Dog Park Rules and Regulations can be obtained
at the Ford Community and Performing Arts Center or at the city clerk's office.
   (b)   Dogs under six months of age are not allowed in the dog park.
   (c)   Only dogs accompanied by an owner/handler at least 16 years of age are
permitted to be in the dog park.
   (d)   It shall be unlawful for any person to bring a dog weighing 30 pounds
or more into the designated "small dog area" of the dog park.
   (e)   It shall be unlawful for any person to bring a dog weighing less than
30 pounds into the designated "large dog area" of the dog park.
   (f)   An owner/handler may not accompany more than two dogs in the dog park
at any one time.
   (g)   Dogs must wear collars (no pronged, pinched, or spiked collars) or
harnesses bearing a current City of Dearborn dog license and a dog park tag at
all times while in the dog park.
   (h)   Dog owners/handlers must be in possession of a leash or other means of
physical restraint at all times. Dogs must be on leash to and from the dog park
access points.
   (i)   Dog owners/handlers must limit their use of electronic devices so that
the use does not interfere with their ability to actively monitor their dog's
behavior.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16; Ord. No. 17-1579, 5-23-17; Ord. No. 24-1816, 4-23-
24; Ord. No. 24-1828, 10-22-24)
Sec. 15-54. - Care of the dog park.
   (a)   Dog owners/handlers are required to remove and properly dispose of all
animal waste immediately. It shall be unlawful to leave the dog park without
first cleaning up and disposing of all animal waste left by an accompanied dog.
   (b)   Dog owners/handlers must stop any accompanied dog from digging and
must fill any holes caused by an accompanied dog. It shall be unlawful for a
dog owner/handler to leave the dog park without first filling any holes caused
by an accompanied dog.
   (c)   Dog owners/handlers/visitors are responsible for properly using all of
the elements provided in the dog park including, but not limited to, the
fencing, the gates, the benches, the fountains, the exercise apparatus, etc.,
and will be responsible for the costs to repair any element that is not
properly used.
   (d)   Dog owners/handlers/visitors are responsible for reporting any
activity that violates any provision of this article. Violations shall be
reported to the police department or at the Ford Community and Performing Arts
Center.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-55. - Dog park health rules.
   (a)   Full current immunizations (rabies, DHLLP or DAPPL, and bordatella) of
all dogs are required.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any owner/handler to bring a dog that has a
contagious condition, disease, parasites, or fresh wound into the dog park.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-56. - Bites, scratches, and aggression in the dog park.
   (a)   All bites and scratches by a dog in the dog park must be reported to
the Dearborn Police Department. It shall be unlawful for any owner/handler to
fail to report a bite or scratch by an accompanied dog of another person or
another dog within 24-hours of the incident.
      (1)   All dog bites shall be reported in accordance with section
4-31 of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances, entitled "Dog Bite Reporting
Requirements."
   (b)   Dogs showing aggression towards people or other dogs must be removed
from the dog park immediately. It shall be unlawful for any owner/handler to
fail to immediately leash and remove any dog showing aggression from the dog
park. Dogs that exhibit aggressive behavior are not allowed in the dog park at
any time.
   (c)   It shall be unlawful for any person to bring any dog deemed to be a
vicious dog or a dangerous dog by any state or local government or agency into
the dog park.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-57. - Children in the dog park.
   Dog handlers must be 16 years of age or older. Children under 16 are not
allowed in the dog park unless accompanied by an adult.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16; Ord. No. 17-1579, 5-23-17)
Sec. 15-58. - Unlawful possession.
   (a)   While in the dog park, it shall be unlawful:
      (1)   For any person to possess food for humans or dogs, including dog
treats.
      (2)   For any person to possess/use tobacco products, herbal products,
alcoholic beverages, or glass containers.
      (3)   For any person to possess dog toys.
      (4)   For any person to possess or unleash an animal other than a dog.
      (5)   For any person to possess/use a skateboard, skates, a bicycle, a
scooter or any other wheeled apparatus. The operation of a non-motorized
wheelchair or motorized mobility device by a person with physical disabilities
is exempt from this sub-section.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Sec. 15-59. - Penalties.
   (a)   Any person who violates this section shall be subject to the
following:
      (1)   First offense: The person is responsible for a civil infraction and
shall be fined $100.00;
      (2)   Second offense: The person is responsible for a civil infraction
and shall be fined $250.00; and
      (3)   Third and subsequent offenses: The person is guilty of a
misdemeanor and shall be expelled from the dog park.
   (b)   In addition, any person who fails to comply with dog park rules and
regulations may be subject to expulsion from the dog park, revocation of their
dog park permit, and/or dog impound.
      (1)   Any person who is expelled from the dog park, whose dog park permit
is revoked, or whose dog is impounded under this subsection may appeal the
action to the recreation and parks commission, whose decision shall be final.
(Ord. No. 16-1551, 10-4-16)
Chapter 16 - SOLID WASTE[1] 
Footnotes:
--- (1) ---
State Law reference— Sewage disposal, water supply and solid waste management
system authorities, MCL 124.281 et seq., MSA 5.2769(51) et seq.
*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 16-1. - General authority.
   The department of public works, established by charter, shall have vested in
it all powers provided by state law, the city charter and this chapter to
provide for the removal and disposal of solid waste and recyclable materials
accumulated or stored in the city and to enforce the terms, provisions and
penalties of this chapter. The director of public works shall prepare and file
a solid waste management plan, as required by law.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 1, 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-2. - Police powers.
   The director of public works and those assistants and employees designated
in writing by the director shall be authorized to issue warning violations and
bring court complaints, civil or criminal, for violations of the provisions of
this chapter. When enforcing the provisions of this chapter, the director of
public works and the assistants and employees shall be and are hereby
constituted ordinance officers and shall have all the powers conferred upon
ordinance officers by the general laws of this state for the purpose of
enforcing this chapter.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 2, 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-3. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Acceptable waste shall mean solid waste, but excluding unacceptable waste.
   Act 641 shall mean Act No. 641 of the Public Acts of Michigan of 1978 (MCL
299.401 et seq.), as amended, and the administrative rules promulgated
thereunder from time to time by the state department of natural resources.
   Facility or facilities shall mean either the material recovery facility
(MRF) or the landfill, or when used in the plural, means both the MRF and the
landfill.
   Hazardous waste shall mean:
      (1)   Any material or substance which, by reason of its composition or
characteristics, is:
         a.   Toxic or hazardous waste, as defined in either the Solid Waste
Disposal Act, 42 USC 6901 et seq., or section 6(e) of the Toxic Substances
Control Act, 15 USC 2605(e), or any laws of similar purposes or effect, and any
rules, regulations or policies promulgated thereunder; or any laws of similar
purpose or effect, and any rules, regulations or policies promulgated
thereunder;
         b.   Special nuclear or byproducts materials within the meaning of the
Atomic Energy Act of 1954;
      (2)   Any waste managed under Act No. 64 of the Public Acts of Michigan
of 1979 (MCL 299.501 et seq.), as amended, being MCL 299.501 et seq., and known
as the Hazardous Waste Management Act;
      (3)   Any other materials which the state department of natural resources
or any governmental agency or unit having appropriate jurisdiction shall
determine from time to time is ineligible for disposal in the landfill, whether
by reasons of being harmful, toxic or dangerous or otherwise.
   MRF shall mean a material recovery facility.
   Person shall mean any area used for residential, commercial or industrial
purposes, separately or in combination, to which a separate street address,
postal address, tax roll description or other similar identification has been
assigned to or is in use by a person having control of the area.
   Recyclable materials shall mean commingled and/or presorted materials that
are designated to be separated from solid waste prior to the collection of
solid waste from a site of generation and delivered to the MRF, including but
not limited to: plastics, glass, cans and newspapers.
   Rubbish shall mean the miscellaneous waste material resulting from
housekeeping and ordinary mercantile enterprises, trades, manufacturers and
offices and stores.
   Site of generation shall mean any premises in the city in or on which solid
waste or recyclable materials is generated by any person.
   Solid waste shall mean waste which may be disposed of in a type two sanitary
landfill, pursuant to Act 641 and any regulations, rules or policies
promulgated thereunder.
   Unacceptable waste shall mean:
      (1)   Hazardous waste.
      (2)   "Unacceptable waste" shall include drums, barrels, containers,
explosives, including but not limited to dynamite, hand grenades, blasting
caps, shotgun shells, fireworks, gasoline, kerosene, turpentine, waste oil,
ether, batteries, naphtha, acetone, solvents, paints, alcohol, hydraulic oil,
petroleum, caustics, sewage or process wastewaters, leachate, sewage sludge,
foundry sand, dusty type material, flammable or volatile liquids, any other
liquids, chemical liquid wastes, acids, paste or sludge, asbestos, infectious,
pathological, chemotherapeutic, biological and other medical waste, ashes of
any kind including but not limited to fly ash or incinerator ash, radioactive
materials, human or animal remains, agricultural and farm machinery and
equipment, tar, tree stumps or tree limbs over three inches in diameter, tires,
and vehicular bodies, and any other material determined from time to time to be
unacceptable by the landfill.
   Waste hauler shall mean any person engaged, in whole or in part, in the
business of collecting, transporting, delivering or disposing of solid waste
and recyclable materials generated within the city. "Waste hauler" specifically
includes the contractor hired by the city to collect, process and dispose of
solid waste and recyclable materials.
   Yard waste shall mean fallen leaves, cut grass or other organic debris that
may be composted.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 3, 6-19-90)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 16-4. - Construction; rules and regulations.
   It is the intent of the city that this chapter be liberally construed for
the purpose of providing a sanitary and satisfactory method of collecting,
processing and disposing of solid waste and recyclable materials. The director
of public works is hereby authorized to make such rules and regulations as from
time to time appear to him to be necessary to carry out this intent; provided,
however, that such rules shall not be in direct conflict with this chapter or
other ordinances of the city.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 4, 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-5. - Containers—Required, specifications.
   Between collections of solid waste and recyclable materials by the city or a
licensed waste hauler, each person who is an owner, lessee or occupant of any
site of generation shall store such materials as follows:
      (1)   Receptacles. Every owner, occupant, tenant or lessee using any
building, house or structure for any purpose whatsoever where refuse
accumulates shall utilize and maintain city-approved 96- or 64-gallon refuse
containers of sufficient number and size in order to store such refuse tending
to accumulate on such premises. Refuse, recycle or yard waste containers that
fail to meet the requirements of this section may be claimed as refuse and,
after due notice to the parties responsible for such container, shall be
collected as refuse by the department of public works.
   Yard waste will be collected as part of the curbside service of waste
removal. Yard waste shall be placed in 32-gallon waste containers provided and
maintained by the owner, occupant, tenant or lessee, or placed in approved
paper compost bags. Individuals placing yard waste in 32-gallon containers
shall place the city "yard waste" sticker on the container.
   Separate and apart from the refuse cart program, it is the intent of the
city to continue curbside service of bulk waste removal. As part of this
service, every owner, occupant, tenant or lessee using any building, house or
structure may place up to five bulk items (e.g. chair, refrigerator) per week
at the curbside for removal.
      (2)   Domestic refuse carts. Each owner, occupant, tenant or lessee
receiving domestic refuse collection service shall utilize the 96-gallon or 64-
gallon refuse cart provided by the city. Disposable paper or plastic bags
containing refuse placed outside of the carts provided by the city will not be
picked up.
   Occasionally, if necessary, each owner, occupant, tenant or lessee may put
additional bagged trash into a covered 32-gallon container for pick-up. Each
owner who puts out an additional container more than once for any two of three
months will be required to lease an additional 96-gallon refuse cart at cost.
No additional collection charge will apply to the additional refuse cart.
      (3)   Domestic recycle carts. Recyclable materials, other than yard
waste, shall be stored in the 96- or 64-gallon recycle carts provided by the
city for pickup.
      (4)   Commercial refuse containers. Each owner, occupant, tenant or
lessee receiving commercial refuse collection service provided by the city
shall use the 96- or 64-gallon cart provided by the city. Commercial
establishments that generate more than two 96-gallon carts of refuse weekly
must contract for refuse dumpster service at their own expense. Commercial
establishments that generate more than two 96-gallon carts of refuse on a
weekly basis and are deemed by the city unable to reasonably provide for refuse
dumpster service may use the 96- or 64-gallon refuse cart service provided they
contract with the city's authorized refuse collection vendor.
   Rubbish that is so large that it cannot be contained in receptacles, must be
securely tied in compact bundles not to exceed four feet in length and 50
pounds in weight, and placed in a location convenient for collection.
      (5)   Apartment complexes. For the purpose of this section, apartments
are deemed commercial establishments. Apartment complexes of four units or less
shall have city-provided refuse collection. A 96- or 64-gallon trash and
recycling cart will be provided by the city for each unit. Apartment complexes
exceeding four units are required to provide their own trash collection
service. If it is determined by the city that utilization of such dumpster
service is unreasonable due to site limitations, the apartment complex may use
the 96- or 64-gallon refuse cart service provided they contract with the city's
authorized refuse collection vendor.
      (6)   Schools and churches. For the purpose of this section, schools and
churches are deemed commercial establishments and shall have city-provided
refuse collection at the same volume as provided commercial businesses. A 96-
or 64-gallon refuse cart will be provided by the city for each school and
church. Any church or school that generates more than two 96-gallon refuse
carts of refuse weekly must contract for refuse dumpster service at their own
expense. Any church or school that generates more than two 96-gallon carts of
refuse on a weekly basis and are deemed by the city unable to reasonably
provide for refuse dumpster service may use the 96- or 64-gallon refuse cart
service provided they contract with the city's authorized refuse collection
vendor.
      (7)   Storage of containers. All refuse containers shall be located
within private property lines and not in the alley, or upon public property,
except that in the case of existing structures which extend to the alley line,
such containers may be placed in a public alley, after written permission has
been granted by the department of public works. No person shall disturb the
contents of waste receptacles or bundles, nor shall persons leave receptacles
or contents thereof in a condition other than this provides. All receptacles
must be maintained in a sanitary condition.
      (8)   Penalties. An individual who violates this section will be issued
one written warning. Thereafter, an individual who violates this section is
responsible for a civil infraction or misdemeanor as follows:
         a.   For the first offense, the individual is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be fined $100.00.
         b.   For a second or subsequent offense committed within one year from
the date of a previous conviction, the individual is guilty of a misdemeanor
and shall be fined $300.00.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 5(b), 6-19-90; Ord. No. 03-926, 1-21-03; Ord. No. 10-1288,
8-16-10)
Sec. 16-6. - Same—Location for collection.
   (a)   All solid waste and recyclable materials from a site of generation
intended for removal from the premises shall be placed in one or more
containers and shall be placed on the grass easement in front of the premises
or, in the case of an adjacent through alley, at the edge thereof. No refuse or
recycle carts shall be placed in the public street. Such containers shall be
placed at that location prior to 7:00 a.m. on the day scheduled for collection
from the premises but in no case shall any containers be placed on the easement
or edge of the alley, as the case may be, prior to 5:00 p.m. of the day
preceding the scheduled collection day. Containers must be removed from the
easement or edge of the alley prior to midnight on the scheduled collection
day. Such containers shall be placed in the manner indicated on the refuse or
recycle cart. The department of public works shall have the authority to
designate the location of refuse and recycle carts.
   (b)   An individual who violates this section will be issued one written
warning. Thereafter, an individual who violates this section is responsible for
a civil infraction or misdemeanor as follows:
      (1)   For the first offense, the individual is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be fined $100.00.
      (2)   For a second or subsequent offense committed within one year from
the date of a previous conviction, the individual is guilty of a misdemeanor
and shall be fined $300.00.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 5, 6-19-90; Ord. No. 03-939, 1-21-03; Ord. No. 10-1288, 8-
16-10)
Sec. 16-6a. - Reserved.
Editor's note— Ord. No. 1433, adopted August 24, 2014, provided: "This

Sec. 16-7. - Recycling program.
   (a)   Mandatory recycling. All persons who are owners, lessees or occupants
of any site of generation shall separate recyclable materials, excluding yard
waste, from solid waste and place them in the recycle cart.
   (b)   Mandatory composting. All persons who are owners, lessees, or
occupants of any site of generation shall separate yard waste from solid waste
and place the yard waste for pickup on the scheduled collection day. This
provision shall become effective 30 days after notice to persons who are
owners, lessees or occupants of any site of generation of the city's contractor
assuming such pickup responsibilities.
   (c)   Antiscavenging. Recyclable materials shall become the property of the
city at the time the recyclable materials are placed on the easement or edge of
the alley, as the case may be. It shall be a violation of this section for any
person other than the city or its licensed waste hauler to collect, remove, or
pick up, or cause to be collected, removed, or picked up any such recyclable
materials.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 6, 6-19-90; Ord. No. 10-1288, 8-16-10)
Sec. 16-8. - Disposal restriction generally.
   No person shall dispose of any solid waste or recyclable materials generated
within the city other than by means of the city's collection service, if
applicable, or a waste hauler duly licensed. This provision shall not prevent a
person from transporting solid waste from the person's private property to a
transfer station.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 7(a), 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-9. - Collection of domestic waste.
   (a)   All domestic solid waste and recyclable materials complying with the
terms and conditions provided for herein will be collected by the department of
public works or the contractor hired by the city to collect, process and
dispose of solid waste and recyclable materials; provided, however, that the
city shall not be responsible for damage to receptacles.
   (b)   The department of public works may issue a license/permit to any
person to collect and transport solid waste and recyclable materials, provided
all the rules and regulations applicable thereto are strictly observed.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 7(b), 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-10. - Collection of commercial waste.
   Reasonable and ordinary quantities of commercial waste, both garbage and
rubbish, to the extent of two 96-gallon refuse carts per week, from any
establishment or business as herein after described, will be collected at a
uniform charge by the department of public works.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 7(c), 6-19-90; Ord. No. 10-1288, 8-16-10)
Sec. 16-11. - Waste hauler license.
   No person shall engage in the business of collecting, transporting,
delivering or disposing of solid waste or recyclable materials generated within
the city without first obtaining a waste hauler license. Waste hauler licenses
shall be issued upon application to the city clerk on forms provided therefor
and upon payment of a license fee to the city. The contractor hired by the city
to collect, process and dispose of solid waste and recyclable materials shall
be considered to have complied with this requirement by satisfying contract
specifications concerning licensing.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 7(d), 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-12. - Conditions of waste hauler license.
   It shall be an express condition of each waste hauler license that the waste
hauler shall comply with all the following:
      (1)   All provisions of this chapter.
      (2)   All applicable federal, state, county and local laws, statutes,
rules and regulations, including but not limited to thereunder, pertaining to
the collection, transportation, delivery, and disposal of solid waste,
recyclable materials and yard waste.
      (3)   All applicable provisions of the agreement and the rules and
regulations adopted from time to time by the landfills for the administration
and operation of the facilities.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 7(e), 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-13. - Transportation.
   (a)   Vehicles or trailers conveying rubbish must be of such construction
and so operated that contents shall not spill upon the public streets or alleys
or otherwise create a nuisance.
   (b)   All rubbish, solid waste and recyclable materials transported through
the streets, alleys or other public places of the city shall be enclosed in
watertight, closed metal boxes approved by the department, and all such boxes
or receptacles shall be purified as often as, and in such manner as, the
director of public works or his agents may direct.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 8, 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-14. - Litter.
   No person shall deposit or cause to be deposited, sort, scatter, throw, drop
or leave any waste, rubbish or garbage on any public or private place in the
city.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 9, 6-19-90)
Sec. 16-15. - Dumping on public, private property.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to throw, dump or deposit or cause
or permit to be thrown, dumped or deposited any bottles, glass, crockery, cans,
scrap metal, junk, waste paper, garbage, old automobiles, or parts thereof;
refuse of whatever nature, rubbish, either domestic or commercial or any
noxious things on or along any public highways, streets, alleys or public
places; within the limits of any highway, street or alley right-of-way; on land
or waters adjoining a public highway or street without the consent of the
owners of such land and the director of public works. It shall be unlawful for
any person to throw, dump or deposit or cause or permit to be thrown, dumped or
deposited any such refuse or thing hereinabove referred to over the sides or
approaches of any bridge or culvert or into any stream, canal, ditch,
watercourse or body of water; provided, however, any person maintaining or
living in a household shall be permitted to place or deposit any such refuse or
thing hereinabove referred to in a suitable container or containers either in
the front or in the rear of his home in a public way preparatory to being
collected by the city.
   (b)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this section shall be
deemed to have committed a nuisance, and the motor vehicle, or other type of
conveyance, which was used in committing such nuisance shall be seized by the
police and shall be impounded and held until such time as the nuisance shall
have been abated by cleaning up and removing from the city or property
disposing of all such material constituting such nuisance. All charges or
expense incurred by the police in abating such nuisance shall be paid to the
police department, including towage and storage of any such vehicle, before
such vehicle will be released to its rightful owner.
(Ord. No. 90-495, § 10, 6-19-90)
Secs. 16-16—16-30. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - RETURNABLE BEVERAGE CONTAINERS ***
Sec. 16-31. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Beverage shall mean a soft drink, soda water, carbonated natural or mineral
water or other nonalcoholic carbonated drink; and beer, ale or other malt drink
of whatever alcoholic content.
   Beverage container shall mean an airtight metal glass, paper or plastic
container, or a container composed of a combination of these materials, which,
at the time of sale, contains one gallon or less of a beverage.
   Dealer shall mean a person who sells or offers for sale to consumers within
this state a beverage in a beverage container, including an operator of a
vending machine containing a beverage in a beverage container.
   Distributor shall mean a person who sells beverages in beverage containers
to a dealer within this state, and includes a manufacturer who engages in such
sales.
   Manufacturer shall mean a person who bottles, cans or otherwise places
beverages in beverage containers for sale to distributors, dealers or
consumers.
   Nonreturnable container shall mean a beverage container upon which no
deposit, or a deposit of less than $0.10 has been paid, or is required to be
paid upon the refund, or a refund of less than $0.10 is payable by a dealer or
distributor in this state of that beverage in beverage containers. A beverage
container certified by the Michigan Liquor Control Commission shall not be
deemed a nonreturnable beverage container if the deposit is at least $0.05, and
the requirements of the first sentence of the definition of "returnable
container" are met in all other respects.
   Operator of a vending machine shall mean equally its owner, the person who
refills it and the owner or lessee of the property upon which it is located.
   Returnable container shall mean a beverage container upon which a deposit of
at least $0.10 has been paid, or is required to be paid upon the removal of the
container from the sale or consumption area, and for which a refund of at least
$0.10 in cash is payable by every dealer or distributor in this state of that
beverage in beverage containers. A beverage container certified by the Michigan
Liquor Control Commission shall also be deemed a returnable container if the
deposit is at least $0.05, and the requirements of the preceding sentence are
met in all other respects.
   Sale or consumption area shall mean the premises within the property of the
dealer or of his lessor where the sale is made, within which beverages in
returnable containers may be consumed without payment of a deposit, and, upon
removing a beverage container from which, the customer is required by the
dealer to pay the deposit.
   Within this state shall mean within the exterior limits of the state and
includes the territory within these limits owned by or ceded to the United
States of America.
(Ord. No. 80-2, § 1, 7-1-80)
Sec. 16-32. - Container regulations.
   (a)   A dealer shall not, within this city, sell, offer for sale or give to
consumers a nonreturnable container or a beverage in a nonreturnable container.
   (b)   A dealer who regularly sells beverages for consumption off the
dealer's premises shall provide on the premises, or within 100 yards of the
premises on which the dealer sells or offers for sale a beverage in a
returnable container, a convenient means whereby the containers of any kind,
size and brand, sold or offered for sale by the dealer, may be returned by and
the deposit refunded in cash to, a person whether or not the person is the
original customer of that dealer, and whether or not the container was sold by
that dealer.
   (c)   A dealer shall not refuse to accept from a person an empty returnable
container of any kind, size and brand sold by that dealer, nor refuse to pay to
the person its full refund value in cash, except as provided in subsections (d)
and (f) of this section.
   (d)   A dealer who does not require a deposit on a returnable container when
the contents are consumed in the dealer's sale or consumption area shall not be
required to pay a refund for accepting that empty container.
   (e)   A distributor shall not refuse to accept from a dealer an empty
returnable container of any kind, size and brand sold by that distributor, nor
refuse to pay to the dealer its full refund value in cash, except as provided
in subsection (f) of this section.
   (f)   Every beverage container sold or offered for sale by a dealer within
this state shall clearly indicate by embossing or by a stamp, or by a label or
other method securely affixed to the beverage container, the refund value of
the container and the name of this state. A dealer or distributor may, but is
not required to, refuse to accept from a person an empty returnable container
which does not state thereon the refund value of the container and the name of
this state. This subsection shall not apply to a refillable container having a
refund value of not less than $0.10 which has a brand name permanently marked
on it. Each container of this type shall clearly indicate by a method securely
affixed to the container that the container is returnable for deposit.
   (g)   A dealer within this state shall not sell, offer for sale or give to
consumers a metal beverage container, any part of which becomes detached when
opened.
(Ord. No. 80-2, § 2, 7-1-80)

*** ARTICLE II. - SPECIAL EVENTS[2]  ***
Footnotes:
--- (2) ---
Editor's note— Ord. No. 08-1182, adopted Oct. 6, 2008, amended Art. II in its
entirety and enacted similar provisions as set out herein. The former Art. II
derived from Ord. No. 89-450, §§ 1, 2, and 4—6a, adopted May 2, 1989; and Ord.
No. 03-979, adopted Aug. 19, 2003.
Sec. 17-26. - Purpose.
   It is determined by the City of Dearborn that the right of all citizens to
make reasonable use of the streets and sidewalks must be preserved to the
greatest extent possible.
   It is further found that certain areas of the city suffer from serious
traffic congestion, both vehicular and pedestrian and that in order to assure
essential movement of persons and vehicles and to protect the rights of all
members of the public, traffic laws and regulations have been enacted and must
be enforced uniformly.
   It is further found that, during rush hour, areas of the city suffer from
extreme traffic congestion, requiring the strict enforcement of traffic laws
and regulations in order to protect the rights of all persons to move upon the
city streets.
   It is further found that various groups, associations and organizations
desirous of holding all public parades, marches and processions, wish to be
exempted from complying with the laws and regulations relating to traffic
controls, including but not limited to one-way street patterns, traffic lights,
traffic signals and signs, and various standard rules for the operation of
persons and motor vehicles.
   It is further found that such organizations, groups or associations often
desire and/or require police escorts to assure clear and safe passage for the
parade, march or procession.
   It is further found that it is the policy of the City of Dearborn to permit
waiver of enforcement of traffic laws and regulations relating to vehicular and
pedestrian traffic in certain conditions where such a waiver or variance in
normal procedures would not unreasonably obstruct or interfere with free
ingress and egress to and from public and private property or to and from
various areas of the city and will not present an unreasonable hazard to the
public. It is also found that a reasonable, short-term obstruction of ingress
and egress may be required for public safety on certain occasions.
   It is further found that the planning for, scheduling of personnel for, and
the carrying out of all necessary preparations for, and executions of, parades,
marches and processions in regard to which requests are made for waiver or
variance of laws or regulations relating to pedestrian or vehicular traffic
restriction of parking on the parade route, change of traffic patterns, or
provision of police escorts, require advance notice to the City of Dearborn and
require the expenditure of public funds.
   It is further found that unless adequate preparation is made and adequate
personnel are provided, it is both unsafe and impractical for parades, marches
or processions to move in or about the City of Dearborn's streets and sidewalks
unless in strict compliance with all laws and regulations relating to the
movement of pedestrian and vehicular traffic.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-27. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning.
   Assembly shall mean any event designed, promoted or conducted in order to
encourage the gathering of 15 or more people upon public property at a
specified location and shall include any, ceremony, show, demonstration,
exhibition, street dance, pageant, party, circus, concert, sporting event, game
or similar activity, except that a residential block party (section
17-110 et seq.) shall not be considered an assembly for the purposes of this
article, nor shall any event taking place entirely on property designated as a
city park.
   Chief of police includes any representative designated by the chief of
police.
   Exempted property shall mean public property where no special event permit
is required. In the City of Dearborn, exempted property means: The city-owned
land adjacent to the Ford Community and Performing Arts Center, the Police and
Court buildings, and the Henry Ford Centennial Library. Such use shall avoid,
to the degree possible, disruption of other normal or scheduled activities at
those facilities.
   Parade shall mean a procession of any kind, having a common purpose or goal,
which moves from place to place upon public property along a specified route
and shall include any march, race, walk-a-thon, bike-a-thon, demonstration, or
similar activity. The following processions are not included in the definition
of "parade":
      (1)   Processions composed wholly of the military or naval forces of the
United States or the State of Michigan;
      (2)   Processions incidental to a funeral;
      (3)   Processions composed of one or more governmental officials or
candidates accompanied by security personnel to which such officials or
candidates are entitled by virtue of their office or candidacy.
   Public property shall mean any street, alley, sidewalk, park, or parking lot
owned, controlled or managed by the city.
   Special event shall mean any assembly, or parade held on public property as
defined in this article. "Special event" shall not include events for which all
participants use sidewalks, observe traffic safety and safety regulations and
do not interfere with the safe and orderly movement of pedestrians, vehicles
and funeral processions.
   Sponsor shall mean the person who has applied for a permit under this
article. The sponsor shall be the person to whom the permit is issued.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 11-1317, 3-21-11; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-
13; Ord. No. 15-1457, 3-17-15)
Sec. 17-28. - Permit required; procedure.
   (a)   Any person desiring to sponsor a special event on any street of the
city shall first obtain a permit therefore from the chief of police.
      (1)   Written application for such permit should be made to the chief of
police at least 30 days in advance in order to insure timely appeal of a denial
of the application.
      (2)   All applications for permits shall be processed by the chief of
police so long as they are received at least 15 working days in advance of the
proposed date of the event.
      (3)   However, when the proposed event designates a route that passes
through a business district, extends over an area which involves more than five
intersections (not including alleys) anticipates a number of participants
exceeding 250, the applicant shall apply at least 30 days in advance of the
proposed date.
      (4)   The chief of police may grant a permit to an applicant who applies
less than 15 working days in advance if the chief of police determines that the
permit application requires no substantial investigation or preparation of the
route.
   (b)   Application shall be made on a form provided by the chief of police
and shall include (if applicable):
      (1)   The name, business address, home address, business phone number and
home phone number of the applicant (who shall be a natural person), the sponsor
of the event, and the event organizer (the person responsible for managing and
organizing the details of the event);
      (2)   The relationship of the applicant to the sponsor;
      (3)   Proof of the applicant's authority to act on behalf of the sponsor;
      (4)   A description of the route of the event;
      (5)   The names of all of the streets to be used;
      (6)   The number of participants anticipated;
      (7)   The starting time and expected finishing time of the event;
      (8)   A proposed plan to provide necessary parking, security, crowd
control, traffic control, sanitation facilities, noise control, and clean-up of
the area of the event;
      (9)   Any other information requested in order to enable the chief of
police to verify the information required in this subsection.
   (c)   Application for a permit shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable
permit application fee of $50.00.
   (d)   The chief of police may issue a permit immediately upon approval of
the permit application and execution and receipt of the indemnification
agreement or certificate of insurance if required by section
17-33.
   (e)   The chief of police shall, as appropriate, transmit copies of any
special event permit issued to the mayor's office, the fire department, the
department of public works, the finance department, the legal department, and
any other effected departments.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-29. - Exceptions.
   (a)   The time limitations prescribed above for the filing of a permit
application may be waived by the chief of police if the applicant can show that
the proposed special event is for the purpose of spontaneous communication of
topical ideas that could not have been foreseen in advance of the required
period or that circumstances beyond the control of the applicant prevented
timely filing of the application.
   (b)   No permit shall be required if a special event occurs on exempted
property as defined in this article.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-30. - Criteria for issuance.
   The chief of police shall issue a special event permit when, from
consideration of the application and from such other information as may
otherwise be obtained, it appears that:
      (1)   The conduct of the special event will not substantially interrupt
the safe and orderly movement of other traffic contiguous to the special event;
      (2)   The conduct of the special event will not require the diversion of
so great a number of police officers to properly police the special event and
the areas contiguous thereto as to prevent normal police protection to the
city;
      (3)   The conduct of the special event will not prevent normal ambulance
service to portions of the city other than that to be occupied by the special
event and contiguous areas;
      (4)   The conduct of the special event will not interfere with the
movement of firefighting equipment;
      (5)   The conduct of the special event is not reasonably likely to cause
injury to persons or property, to provoke disorderly conduct or to create a
disturbance;
      (6)   The special event is scheduled to move from its point of origin to
its point of termination expeditiously and without unreasonable delays en
route; and
      (7)   Approval has been obtained from the owners of all property on which
the special event is scheduled to occur; and
      (8)   The applicant for a permit, the sponsor of the event, and the event
organizer have not violated the terms of any previous special event permit,
have not caused undue traffic congestion and/or police problems under any
previous special event permit, and are current on any fees charged in
conjunction with any previous special event permit.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-31. - Notice of denial; appeal.
   (a)   If the chief of police denies an application for a special event
permit, notice of denial shall be mailed to the applicant. Such notice shall
state the reasons for the denial of the permit.
   (b)   Denial of an application for a special event permit may be appealed to
the city council. The appeal shall be filed within five business days after the
notice of denial is received.
      (1)   The city council shall consider such appeal and may either concur
in the action of the chief of police or overrule such action and order that the
permit be approved. If the city council orders that a permit be approved, it
shall have the authority to impose only such conditions as are recommended by
the chief of police.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-32. - Payment of city services.
   (a)   The sponsor of a special event who accepts a permit thereby consents
to the formation of a contract between the sponsor and the city for payment of
costs for city services and equipment as set forth in this section.
   (b)   Within 21 days of the conclusion of the special event, the city will
send the sponsor a bill for the actual amount of the direct and reasonable
costs incurred by the city to provide additional police and public works
services for the special event.
   (c)   Within 14 days after the date of the bill, the sponsor shall pay to
the city the direct and reasonable costs incurred by the city to provide
additional police and public works services for the special event.
   (d)   The requirements of this section shall be waived if the applicant can
show that the proposed special event is a constitutionally protected event.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Sec. 17-33. - Insurance or indemnification requirement; exception.
   The applicant, the sponsor of the event, and the event organizer shall
provide one of the following:
      (1)   An insurance certificate that (1) shall be subject to the approval
of the legal department as to company, form and coverage; (2) evidences general
liability coverage that is primary to and non-contributory with all other
insurance and self-insurance maintained by the city, naming the city as an
additional insured; (3) evidences an endorsement to include a waiver of
subrogation in favor of the city; and (4) protects the city from any and all
claims and risks in connection with any activity performed pursuant to the
special event permit and/or any use and occupancy of the property authorized by
the special event permit.
      (2)   An executed hold harmless agreement that (1) shall be subject to
the approval of the legal department; and (2) indemnifies, defends, and holds
the city, its elected officials, officers, boards, commissions, employees and
agents harmless from any and all claims, actions, suits, proceedings, damages,
costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorney fees) whatsoever arising out
of the use and occupation of the public property authorized by the special
event permit and any act or omission of the sponsor holder or any of its
officers, employees, agents, licensees, or the invitees of any of the same
(collectively referred to as "actors") or arising out of or relating to any
concurrent act or omission of any of the above-referenced actors and the city
or any city officer, elected official, employee or agent. Nothing herein shall
be construed as requiring the sponsor to indemnify the city against liability
for bodily injury or damage to property caused by or resulting from the sole
negligence of the city or any of its officers, elected officials, employees, or
agents. The indemnification obligation set forth in this subsection shall
survive the expiration or early termination of the special event permit.
      (3)   The requirements of this section shall be waived if the applicant
can show that the proposed special event is a constitutionally protected event.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08; Ord. No. 13-1413, 11-26-13)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 13-1413, adopted November 26, 2013, renamed §
17-33 from indemnification agreement to insurance or indemnification
requirement; exception
Sec. 17-34. - Revocation of permit.
   (a)   The chief of police may revoke a special event permit if an emergency
arises which makes it impossible to assign the necessary personnel to the event
and still provide the personnel required elsewhere to protect the public, or if
information is received after the permit is issued from which the chief of
police reasonably concludes that the permit should not have been approved.
   (b)   If participants violate any conditions contained in a special event
permit, the chief of police or the police officer assigned by the chief of
police as the officer in charge of overseeing personnel necessary to police the
event may, after warning the participants and providing them with an
opportunity to follow the permit conditions, revoke the permit.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08)
Sec. 17-35. - Unlawful to sponsor or participate in a special event without a
permit.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to sponsor a special event unless a
permit has been issued for the event, or for any person to participate in such
an event with the knowledge that the sponsors of the event have not been issued
the required permit or with the knowledge that a permit has been issued and
subsequently revoked.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08)
Sec. 17-35A. - Parade safety.
   (a)   Ladders, scaffolding or any type of platform or portable elevating
devices are prohibited on the street of any parade route between the curbs or
on the sidewalks. Such devices shall also be prohibited between the curbs or on
the sidewalks of any street intersecting with the parade route.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person, at any time, to place or cause to
be placed, any type of obstruction, including, but not limited to ropes, tents,
scaffolds, barricades or vehicles, which may act as an impediment to vehicular
or pedestrian traffic on any right-of-way along a parade route without first
securing permission from the council.
   (c)   It shall be unlawful for any person who is not a parade participant to
place or carry any type of banner, sign, or placard within the parade route.
   (d)   It shall be unlawful for any person to throw or spray an object at or
to any participant, vehicle or animal in a parade.
   (e)   It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to ride on or use
skates, skateboards, roller blades, bicycles, unicycles, or any other type of
cycles within 50 feet of any parade route.
(Ord. No. 11-1317, 3-21-11)
Sec. 17-36. - Film making.
   (a)   Purpose. The state has adopted legislation that encourages the
production of movies and TV shows, the creation of film industry
infrastructure, and the hiring of Michigan workers for the wide range of jobs
that exist in the film making industry. The goal of the legislation is to
benefit the economy statewide.
   The city encourages the production of motion pictures and television within
its boundaries. This section provides the basis for the rules and regulations
governing filming, video taping and related activity within the city. This
section is intended to ensure that filming/video taping is done consistent with
public health and safety and the protection of property.
   (b)   [Waivers.] The chief of police, or his designee, in his discretion,
may waive the requirements of this article and may authorize the use of any
city street, right-of-way, park, public area, or public building/structure, for
use in the filming, taping, or production of any film project, including but
not limited to movies, television, commercials or training films.
      (1)   The chief of police or his designee shall have full control over
the general location, hours, and use of public streets, buildings, equipment
and personnel while being used for filming, taping, or production purposes.
      (2)   The chief of police or his designee shall have the full and
absolute right to prohibit and/or order the cessation of filming, taping and/or
the production of any project if such acts are determined to be detrimental to
public health, safety and welfare.
      (3)   The chief of police or his designee may negotiate charges for
direct and reasonable costs incurred by the city to provide additional police
and public works services needed to respond to the film making request.
      (4)   The chief of police or his designee shall have the right to impose
additional regulations under this section for the protection of public safety
and welfare.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08)
Sec. 17-37. - Penalty.
   A violation of this article shall be prosecuted as a misdemeanor offense.
(Ord. No. 08-1182, 10-6-08)
Secs. 17-38—17-50. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - CURB CUTS ***
Sec. 17-51. - Permit required; fee.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to cut, alter or change any concrete or
other curb in or upon any city street or city road without first having
obtained a permit therefor. In all cases such a permit shall only authorize
such work to be done by a licensed contractor upon payment to the city
treasurer of a permit and inspection fee, as established by section
12-6.
(Ord. No. 81-124, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-52. - Specifications; approval.
   All cuts shall be made according to specifications provided by the
department of building and safety. All cuts shall be approved by an inspector
after the setting of concrete forms and prior to the placing of concrete. All
curb cuts for any one opening of more than 35 feet must be approved by the
department of building and safety and the city engineer. All requests for
permits for curb cutting of over 35 feet for any one opening must be
accompanied with three copies of a sketch showing the proposed curb opening and
the adjacent property involved.
(Ord. No. 81-124, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-53. - Apron between curb, sidewalk.
   No permit to cut any curb shall be issued by the department of building and
safety unless and until the applicant shall agree in such application, as a
condition to the issuance of the permit, to install a concrete apron between
the curb and the sidewalk within 30 days after completion of the cut. Failure
to comply within the time limited therefor shall be and constitute a violation
hereof, subject to the penalties prescribed in section
1-9.
(Ord. No. 81-124, § 2, 11-4-81)
Secs. 17-54—17-70. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE IV. - STREETS ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Secs. 17-71—17-95. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - OBSTRUCTIONS **
Sec. 17-96. - Scope.
   The naming of any article or thing in this division as an obstruction or
encroachment shall not be construed as limiting the scope of this division to
such particular articles or things, but all materials and things of every kind
and nature located in any street, alley or public place, constituting an
obstruction or encroachment thereof, shall be deemed a violation of this
division, unless a permit therefore has been obtained in accordance with the
terms of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-97. - Prohibited generally.
   No person shall obstruct any street, alley or other public place within the
city with animals, boxes, barrels, posts, poles, fences, buildings, building
material or thing whatsoever, except as herein otherwise provided, and no
person shall permit to remain or maintain, by encroachment or otherwise, in any
street, alley or public place, any building, structure, posts, poles, fences,
gasoline pumps, oil pumps, tanks, air services, awnings, marquees, stairways,
coal chutes, areaways, gratings, excavations, vehicles or signs.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-98. - Minimum specifications.
   Any items placed within the public right-of-way, particularly unpaved walk
area, shall not be permitted unless the following specifications or conditions
are observed:
      (1)   No obstruction shall be permitted or so located unless at least 30
inches high above grade level.
      (2)   No obstruction shall be permitted closer than 24 inches from the
curb line.
      (3)   The space between obstruction and lot line side of sidewalk shall
never be less than 48 inches.
      (4)   Obstruction shall never be permitted to exceed 20 percent of paved
walk areas.
      (5)   All such obstructions, if permitted, shall be of a decorative
nature and should not advertise or suggest the wares or services provided by
adjacent businesses.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-99. - Permitted obstructions.
   (a)   Permits may be granted under this division for the following:
      (1)   The erection of signs, awnings and marquise when attached to and
supported by a substantial structure on privately owned property if not
projecting beyond curb line.
      (2)   Coal chutes, if provided with tight cover without openings when the
same do not project above the sidewalk level nor extend below the sidewalk
grade more than three feet, nor project out into public property more than 18
inches.
      (3)   Temporary obstruction of a sidewalk in front of a business building
for the purpose of erection or alteration of such building, as provided for in
the building code.
      (4)   Moving buildings or other structures upon streets and alleys,
provided, however, that the application for a permit to move buildings along
public thoroughfares shall first be approved by the chief of police and chief
of the fire department.
   (b)   No permit shall be issued under this section by the director of public
works, the city engineer, or one of their designees, unless the applicant shall
pay to the city treasurer the sum of $100.00, and in addition thereto shall
file a sufficient bond, in amount to be approved by the director of public
works, the city engineer, or one of their designees, conditioned to indemnify
the city against all losses and damages that may result from the use of the
permit granted, or by reason of the negligence of the person to whom such
permit is issued, his agents, servants and employees.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 15-1489, 9-22-15)
Sec. 17-99.1 - Temporary obstructions.
   (a)   Permits may be issued by the director of public works, the city
engineer, or one of their designees, under this division for the following:
      (1)   The temporary obstruction of a public right-of-way for construction
related activities.
   (b)   No permit shall be issued under this section unless the applicant
shall pay to the city treasurer the sum of $100.00, and in addition thereto
shall file a permit application which shall indemnify the city against all
losses and damages that may result from the use of the permit granted, or by
the reason of the negligence of the person to whom such permit is issued, his
agents, servants, and employees.
(Ord. No. 15-1489, 9-22-15)
Sec. 17-100. - Permits; application, review, etc.
   An application for a permit to place items within the public right-of-way
shall be made to the director of public works. The proposed design shall be
reviewed by the city engineer, city planner and city beautiful commission and a
recommendation made to the director of public works prior to issuance of a
permit. If a state or county road or right-of-way is affected, the applicant
shall submit in writing the approval of the appropriate jurisdiction for the
proposed project prior to issuance of a permit.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-101. - Gasoline tanks, pumps.
   No person shall occupy any part of any street, alley or other public place
in the city for the installation, operation or maintenance of any gasoline tank
or pump or any other device dispensing flammable liquids or oils of any nature.
(Ord. No. 81-57, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17-102. - Snow removal.
   (a)   Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this
section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except
where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
      (1)   Person shall not include the state, a political subdivision of the
state, an employee of the state or a political subdivision of the state
operating within the scope of his duties.
      (2)   Safety vision means an unobstructed line of sight enabling a driver
to travel upon, enter, or exit a roadway in a safe manner.
   (b)   A person shall not remove, or cause to be removed, snow, ice or slush
onto or across a roadway or the shoulder of the roadway in a manner which
obstructs the safety vision of the driver of a motor vehicle other than offroad
vehicles.
   (c)   A person shall not deposit, or cause to be deposited, snow, ice, or
slush onto or across a roadway or the shoulder of the roadway in a manner which
obstructs the safety vision of the driver of a motor vehicle.
   (d)   A person shall not deposit, or cause to be deposited, snow, ice or
slush on any roadway, highway or sidewalk.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.10, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.677a.
Secs. 17-103—17-109. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2A. - BLOCK PARTIES **
Sec. 17-110. - Definitions.
   The following words, phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly
indicates a different meaning:
   Block party shall mean or refer to an organized group of residents gathered
in a specified area on a public street or right of way within a neighborhood,
not to exceed two blocks.
   Sponsor shall mean or refer to a designated resident within the specified
block party area of the neighborhood who shall be held responsible for the
activities within that area for the duration of the block party.
(Ord. No. 04-1001, 4-20-04)
Sec. 17-111. - Permit required.
   It shall be unlawful to organize or participate in any block party in the
city unless a permit has first been obtained from the city clerk’s office.
(Ord. No. 04-1001, 4-20-04; Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17)
Sec. 17-112. - Application for permit.
   An application for a permit for any block party regulated under this article
shall be made to the city clerk’s office, at least 48 hours prior to the event,
on a form provided therefor. The application shall contain the following
information:
      (1)   Name, address, and telephone number of the sponsor organizing such
party.
      (2)   Location of the block party, including those streets to be
barricaded and the cross streets involved.
      (3)   Date(s) and time(s) for the party and alternate date(s) in the
event of inclement weather.
      (4)   Date and location of any past block party organized or participated
in by sponsor.
      (5)   A petition signed by at least 50 percent of the people who reside
on the streets requested to be barricaded. A form for the petition must be
obtained from the city clerk’s office.
(Ord. No. 04-1001, 4-20-04; Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17)
Sec. 17-113. - Permit fees.
   The license fee, listed in Section
12-6 of Chapter 12, must be paid before the license is issued.
(Ord. No. 04-1001, 4-20-04; Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17; Ord. No. 22-1724, 2-8-
22)
Sec. 17-114. - Barricades required.
   (a)   Barricades obtained from the department of public works must be
utilized to secure streets. The sponsor will be charged $60.00 per barricade if
the barricades are not returned or returned in a damaged condition.
   (b)   Barricades must be returned to the department of public works within
five days of the date of issuance. Failure to do so will result in a $60.00
charge to the block party sponsor for each missing barricade. Failure to pay
any invoice generated to cover the cost of missing or damaged barricades within
30 days will accrue interest at the established city rates. Any such charges
that remain uncollected as of December 31 of the year in which the invoice was
generated shall be reported by the Finance Director to the Council to be
collected by special assessment, in accordance with the provisions of
Chapter 15 of the Charter of the city.
(Ord. No. 04-1001, 4-20-04; Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17)
Sec. 17-115.   Access to streets.
   (a)   Street access shall not be blocked by motor vehicles, picnic tables,
trash receptacles, etc.
   (b)   Street access must remain available for emergency vehicles at all
times.
   (c)   Non-participating residents must be allowed access to their property
at all times.
   (d)   All streets must be cleared and re-opened for traffic no later than
midnight on the day of the party.
(Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17)
Sec. 17-116.   Revocation of permit.
   The chief of police or his designee shall have the authority to revoke a
block party permit if it is deemed to be in the best interest of the residents
of the city.
(Ord. No. 16-1565, 1-17-17)
Secs. 17-117—17-120. - Reserved.
