rules referenced above, the city specifically reserves the right to amend and
or terminate this article and all related agreements, policies, and procedures
undertaken in furtherance hereof.
(Ord. No. 22-1749, 6-7-22)
Sec. 17-275.   Effective date.
   This article shall take effect when published and recorded according to law.
(Ord. No. 22-1749, 6-7-22)
Chapter 17.5 - SUBDIVISIONS
Sec. 17.5-1. - Purpose.
   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate and control the subdivision of
land within the corporate limits of the city in order to promote the public
health, safety, comfort, convenience and general welfare, and to provide for
the orderly growth and harmonious development of the city consistent with the
objectives of the master plan, the zoning ordinance and the city building code,
to secure adequate traffic circulation so as to lessen congestion on the
streets and highways; to ensure adequate provisions for public and private
utilities; to achieve the maximum utility and livability of individual lots and
to carry out the provision of Act 288 of Public Acts of 1967 of the State of
Michigan.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-2. - Definitions.
   Act 288 means the Act 288 of the Public Acts of 1967 of the State of
Michigan, which is known as the Subdivision Control Act of 1967. For the
purpose of this chapter, those definitions provided in section 102 of Act 288
will govern where those terms are used.
   Final plat means the map or chart of a subdivision of land which is
submitted to the municipality in conformance with section 131 through 173 of
Act 288.
   Master plan means of the Official Master Plan of the City of Dearborn as
amended.
   Preliminary plat means the map showing salient features of a proposed
subdivision submitted to a municipality in conformance with section 111 through
120 of Act 288.
   Zoning ordinance means the Official Zoning Ordinance of the City of
Dearborn, as amended.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-3. - Preliminary plat.
   (a)   The proprietor shall submit a preliminary plat to the city council, to
be referred over to the city plan commission, for review of lot size, lot
orientation, street layout, street width and overall compliance with the zoning
ordinance and the master plan of the city.
   (b)   The preliminary plats shall be drawn to a scale of not more than 100
feet to one inch (section 111(2) of Act 288).
   (c)   The proprietor shall submit ten copies of the preliminary plat to the
city clerk (section 112(1) of Act 288).
   (d)   There shall be an examination fee of $5.00 per lot or $100.00,
whichever is greater, submitted with all preliminary plats, payable to the
treasurer of the city. No additional examination fee will be required on
submittal of final plat (section 246(1) of Act 288).
   (e)   Within 60 days subsequent to the submitting a preliminary plat, the
proprietor shall submit to the city plan commission the written comments of all
private utility companies, indicating whether the private utility companies can
serve the area utilizing the easements as proposed on the preliminary plat.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-4. - Final plat.
   (a)   The proprietor shall submit one copy of the final plat on polyester
film in conformance with section R560.104 of the Plat Rules of the State
Department of Treasury to the city clerk, accompanied by:
      (1)   Ten copies of plat on paper.
      (2)   Petition to the common council asking approval of the plat.
      (3)   A check payable to the county treasurer for $20.00, being the
filing and recording fee (section 241 of Act 288).
      (4)   Copies of any deed covenants of other documents covering use and
maintenance of private areas on plat which are set aside for common use of
owners within the subdivision (section 258 of Act 288).
      (5)   An abstract of title to date or title insurance policy, or a title
insurance commitment dated not more than 30 days prior to submission.
      (6)   Certification by city treasurer that there are no due or unpaid
real property taxes or special assessments.
   (b)   All easements shall be dedicated to the public and shall be indicated
as "public easements," on the final plat.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-5. - Monuments and markers.
   (a)   The city engineer may, with the approval of the common council, waive
the placing of required monuments and lot markers for one year from date of
plat when it is determined that proposed construction within the subdivision
will endanger the monuments and markers. If placement is waived, a minimum
deposit of $25.00 per monument and $10.00 per lot marker shall be deposited
with the city treasurer.
   (b)   If horizontal control for construction and other uses is required
during the waiver period, the city engineer may require that surveyor's stakes
or markers be set by the proprietor at all locations requiring a monument and
that these stakes or markers be set prior to waiving the placement of monuments
and lot markers.
   (c)   Upon receipt of a survey's certificate that monuments and markers have
been placed, the city engineer will check for accuracy of placement and approve
the refund of any deposited monies.
   (d)   In the event the proprietor defaults, the city engineer will promptly
place the required monuments and markers. Necessary costs for such placement
shall be deducted from the deposit previously required.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-6. - Minimum lots sizes.
   The following requirements shall apply in the determination of minimum lot
sizes (section 186 of Act 288):
      (1)   When public sewer and public water are available in single-family
residential zones, the width, depth and area of lots shall generally conform to
or exceed the width, depth and area of other residential parcels in the
surrounding neighborhood, provided that not lot shall be platted at a width or
area that is less than the minimum lot size required for the zoning district,
as established by the zoning ordinance of the city, as amended at the time the
preliminary plat is submitted. If a proposed lot is located in more than one
zoning district, the width, depth and area shall comply with the requirements
of the more restrictive zone.
      (2)   When public sewer and public water area available in two-family and
multiple-family residential zones, the width, depth and area of lots shall
generally either conform to or exceed the width, depth and area of other
residential parcels in the surrounding neighborhood but must be of a size
sufficient for the types of structures which may be erected, to meet the
requirements of the zoning ordinance and building code, as amended at the time
the preliminary plat is submitted. No lot shall be platted at a width or area
that is less than the minimum lot size required for the zone in which said lot
is located, as established by the zoning ordinance. If a proposed lot is
located in more than one zoning district, the width, depth and area shall
comply with the more restrictive zone.
      (3)   Lot size requirements may be waived by the city plan commission if
the property is presently developed and if the proposed plat would create
parcels conforming to existing individual building units.
      (4)   In areas which are zoned for nonresidential purposes, the minimum
lot width shall be as set forth in the zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-7. - Street local and width (section 186 of Act 288).
   (a)   The proposed subdivision shall provide adequate street widths, as
determined by the objectives of the master plan of the city as amended at the
date of submitting of the preliminary plats.
   (b)   The plats shall not be isolated from or isolate other land from
existing public streets unless other suitable access is provided (section 182
(4) of Act 288).
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-8. - Utility easements.
   Adequate easements shall be provided for full service of public utilities to
every lot within the subdivision. When determined necessary by the city plan
commission to comply with the development objectives in the area, certain
easements may be limited to underground utilities only.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-9. - Public improvement.
   This section sets forth and defines the public improvements which may be
required to be constructed by or at the expense of the proprietor as conditions
for final plat approval (sections 182 and 188 of Act 288). All constructions
shall conform to the codes and ordinances of the city and to the current
standards of the various involved departments and workmanship shall be
inspected and approved by the city departments having jurisdiction over the
installation. Standards shall be those in effect at the time the preliminary
plat is submitted.
      (1)   Sanitary sewers and storm drainage. When a proposed subdivision is
located adjacent to, or reasonably near, a public sanitary or combined sewer,
the sanitary sewers and other required appurtenances thereto shall be installed
in such a manner and be connected to the existing system so that all lots,
regardless of their size, will be adequately served. An adequate storm drainage
system, including necessary storm or combined sewers, drain inlets, manholes,
culverts, bridges and other appurtenances, will be required to remove
stormwater from the area being subdivided.
      (2)   Water supply. An adequate water supply system, including necessary
mains, water gates, manholes, fire hydrants, meters, and other required
appurtenances shall be installed in such a manner as to adequately serve all
lots shown on the plat for domestic, commercial or industrial use, as well as
fire protection.
      (3)   Streets and alleys. All streets and alleys, whether public or
private, shall be paved in accordance with the standards of the city in effect
at the time the preliminary plat is submitted. This shall include sidewalks and
drainage structures, if required.
      (4)   Public utilities. Power lines and telephone lines shall be
constructed underground, including service lines to individual buildings,
unless above ground construction is expressly authorized by the city plan
commission. If such an exception is made by the city plan commission, the costs
to the proprietor shall be those costs required by the respective public
utilities at the time of installation.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-10. - Areas of common use.
   Where the proposed plat includes provisions for setting aside areas for the
private but common use of owners of property within the subdivision, deed
covenants or other documents covering the use and maintenance of same shall be
filed and recorded with the final plat and shall be subject to review and
approval by the corporation council and the appropriate city departments
(section 258 of Act 288).
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 17.5-11. - Division of existing platted lots.
   (a)   Any person, or persons owning platted lots who wish to further divide
such lots into not more than four parcels shall:
      (1)   Make written request signed by all parties in interest showing the
legal descriptions of the resultant parcels of the requested real property
division to the department of assessment.
      (2)   Submit two plot plans showing dimensions of said resultant parcels
to said department.
      (3)   For commercial or industrial property, pay a fee of $100.00 for the
department plan review and $75.00 for each new parcel created.
      (4)   For residential property, pay a fee of $100.00 for the department
plan review and $50.00 for each new parcel created.
      (5)   Submit a tax memo from the city treasurer to said board of all lots
involved.
   (b)   The board of assessors may permit division of lots into two, three, or
four parts when resulting parcels equal or exceed the area and width of
original platted size.
   (c)   The board of assessors may permit the division of lots into two,
three, or four parts when the city plan commission has certified that the
resulting parcels satisfy the minimum lot size requirements of this chapter
and, in the case of a residential parcel, the commission has further certified
that the width, depth and area of the resulting parcels either conforms to or
exceeds the width, depth, and area of other residential parcels in the
surrounding neighborhood.
   (d)   Where there are unusual or unique circumstances, the common council,
after report and recommendation from the city plan commission, may approve
division of lots into two, three or four parts when resulting parcels are less
than original size of lots and when resulting parcels do not satisfy minimum
lot requirements of this chapter. The report of the city plan commission must
indicate that the proposed division of a platted lot would allow the
development of the land in such a manner as to be compatible with surrounding
land use and development and not contrary to the spirit and purpose of this
chapter and the zoning ordinance, or that the property is presently developed
and the proposed division creates parcels conforming the existing individual
building units.
   (e)   In no event shall a division of real property descriptions be made
upon the rolls where there are any due and unpaid city taxes or special
assessments.
   (f)   In no event shall a division of real property be considered until a
finding by the corporation counsel that parties signing the request have the
necessary interest in the property to request the division thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 11, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 02-900, 5-21-02; Ord. No. 15-1511,
12-8-15)
Sec. 17.5-12. - Urban renewal plats.
   Urban renewal plats shall conform to all of the requirements of this chapter
except as follows:
      (1)   On submission of preliminary plat, the examination fee will not be
required:
      (2)   Prior to submitting final plat, approval of common council will be
required authorizing the mayor and the city clerk to certify the plat:
      (3)   The following items shall be included when a final plat is
submitted to the city clerk by the housing commission or its authorized
representatives:
         a.   One copy of the plat on polyester film.
         b.   Ten copies of the plan on paper.
         c.   Petition to common council asking approval of the plat.
         d.   A check payable to the county treasurer for $20.00, being the
recording fee.
(Ord. No. 81-138, § 12, 11-4-81)

*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 18-1. - Attempt to commit violation.
   (a)   The court shall impose a criminal penalty for a conviction of an
attempted violation of this chapter in the same manner as if the offense had
been completed.
   (b)   This section shall take effect October 1, 1999.
(Ord. No. 99-792, 9-21-99)
Secs. 18-2—18-25. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - TRAFFIC COMMISSION **
Sec. 18-26. - Established.
   There is hereby created and established in and for the city a commission to
be known as the traffic commission which shall consist of seven members to be
appointed by the mayor in accordance with the provisions of the Charter;
preference shall be given to members of the Dearborn Parent Teacher
Organization, members of the Federation of Neighborhood Associations, and
senior citizens. The members of the commission shall qualify by taking an oath
of office to be filed with the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 81-83, § 1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 00-810, 2-1-00; Ord. No. 16-1559, 11-
15-16)
Cross reference— Boards and commissions, §
2-351 et seq.
Sec. 18-27. - Organization.
   The traffic commission shall organize by annually electing a chairman, vice-
chairman and secretary from its membership and shall adopt such rules and
regulations as may be necessary to carry out its powers and duties. The chief
of police shall furnish such secretarial help as may be needed to keep the
minutes of the commission and preserve such records and information in
pertaining to the functions of the commission as may be necessary.
(Ord. No. 81-83, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-28. - Duties.
   (a)   The traffic commission shall have the following duties and
responsibilities:
      (1)   It shall study, survey, investigate and make recommendations to the
mayor, council and police chief on all phases of the vehicular traffic problems
in the city and particularly those relating to parking both onstreet and
offstreet, eliminating traffic hazards, establishing or changing appropriate
speed limits in various parts of the city, establishing or abolishing one-way
streets, establishing or abolishing stop streets, establishing or eliminating
red and green traffic lights, constructing grade separations, establishing or
relocating truck routes in and through the city, and speeding up or slowing
down traffic flow on any city streets.
      (2)   It shall study and investigate the establishing of expressways
through and across and locating one or more bypasses around the business
sections of the city.
      (3)   It shall determine the necessity for and make recommendations with
reference to conducting an overall traffic survey in and through the city in
connection with Eno Foundation and Northwestern University and any other
organization qualified to make such surveys.
      (4)   It shall study, investigate and make recommendations concerning the
locating of the main traffic arteries across the undeveloped areas of the city.
   (b)   All of the duties and responsibilities hereinabove specified shall be
carried on in such manner that the work of this commission shall not invade or
supplant the duties or functions of any department, commission or board
heretofore established by the city charter.
(Ord. No. 81-83, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-29. - Council to provide personnel, equipment and supplies.
   The city council shall provide such quarters, equipment and personnel for
the proper functioning of the traffic commission as it shall deem necessary.
(Ord. No. 81-83, § 4, 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-30—18-50. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE II. - TRAFFIC CODE ***
** DIVISION 1. - GENERALLY **
Sec. 18-51. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
Sec. 18-52. - Accessory.
   Accessory means any accessory, equipment, additional part or replacement
part for a vehicle for which a certificate of title is required to be issued
under the Michigan Vehicle Code Act No. 300 of the Public Acts of Michigan of
1949 (MCL 257.1 et seq., MSA 9.1801 et seq.), as amended.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.2(a), 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.1a.
Sec. 18-53. - Alley.
   Alley shall mean a public way within a block primarily intended for service
and access to abutting property from the rear thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-54. - Authorized emergency vehicle.
   Authorized emergency vehicle means the following:
      (1)   Vehicles of the fire department, police vehicles, ambulances, or
privately owned motor vehicles of volunteer or paid fire fighters if authorized
by the chief of an organized fire department, or privately owned motor vehicles
of volunteer or paid members of a life support agency licensed by the
department of consumer and industry services if authorized by the life support
agency.
      (2)   For purposes of section
18-155.5, a road service vehicle giving a visual signal by means of a flashing,
rotating, or oscillating red or amber light. As used in this subdivision, "road
service vehicle" means a vehicle that is clearly marked and readily
recognizable as a vehicle used to assist disabled vehicles.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 04-1002, §§ 1, 2, 5-18-04)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.2.
Sec. 18-55. - Axle.
   Axle shall mean the common axis of rotation of one or more wheels, whether
power driven or freely rotating, whether in one or more segments and regardless
of the number of wheels carried thereon.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.5, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.3.
Sec. 18-56. - Bicycle.
   Bicycle shall mean every device propelled by human power upon which any
person may ride, having two tandem wheels, either of which is over 20 inches in
diameter.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.6, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.4.
Sec. 18-57. - Bus.
   Bus shall mean a motor vehicle designed for carrying more than ten
passengers and used for the transportation of persons; and a motor vehicle,
other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for
compensation. It does not include a school bus or a bus equipped and used for
living or camping purposes.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.7, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.4b.
Sec. 18-58. - Bus stop.
   Bus stop shall mean the space in a street or highway and along the curb or
edge thereof set aside for the exclusive use by a bus for the loading or
unloading of passengers, which bus stop shall be plainly marked by appropriate
signs.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-59. - Business district.
   Business district shall mean the territory contiguous to a highway or street
where 50 percent or more of the frontage thereon for a distance of 300 feet or
more is occupied by buildings in use for business.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.9, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.5.
Sec. 18-60. - Civil infraction.
   Civil infraction shall mean an act or omission prohibited by law which is
not a crime, as defined in section 5 of Act No. 328 of the Public Acts of
Michigan of 1931 (MCL 750.5, MSA 28.195), as amended, and for which a civil
sanction may be ordered.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.11(a), 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.6a.
Sec. 18-61. - Civil infraction determination.
   Civil infraction determination shall mean a determination that a person is
responsible for a civil infraction by one of the following:
      (1)   An admission of responsibility for the civil infraction.
      (2)   An admission of responsibility for the civil infraction, "with
explanation."
      (3)   A preponderance of the evidence at an informal hearing on the
question.
      (4)   A default judgment, for failing to appear at a scheduled informal
hearing or at a scheduled formal hearing.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.11(b), 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.6b, MSA 9.1806(2).
Sec. 18-62. - Commercial sound advertising.
   Commercial sound advertising shall mean the use and operation of sound
amplifying equipment in promoting the sale of any goods, wares or merchandise
or the patronage of any business establishment.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-63. - Commercial vehicle.
   (a)   Commercial vehicle shall mean and include all motor vehicles used for
the transportation of passengers for hire; constructed or used for
transportation of goods, wares or merchandise; and/or all motor vehicles
designed and used for drawing other vehicles and not so constructed as to carry
any load thereon, either independently or any part of the weight of a vehicle
or load so drawn. Commercial vehicle does not include a limousine operated by a
limousine driver, a taxicab operated by a taxicab driver, or a personal vehicle
operated by a transportation network company driver.
   (b)   The terms limousine, limousine driver, taxicab, taxicab driver, and
transportation network company driver shall have the meanings given to them in
Article XX of the Dearborn Code of Ordinances titled “Taxicabs and Other Motor
Vehicles for Hire,” §
12-886.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.11, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19-1659, 9-10-19)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.7, MSA 9.1807.
Sec. 18-63.1. - Commercial motor vehicle.
   Commercial motor vehicle shall mean a bus; school bus; a school
transportation vehicle; a motor vehicle, except a motor home, having a gross
vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating of 26,001 or more
pounds; a motor vehicle towing a vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of
more than 10,000 pounds; or a motor vehicle carrying hazardous material and on
which is required to be posted a placard as defined and required under 49
C.F.R. parts 100 to 199. A commercial motor vehicle does not include a vehicle
used exclusively to transport personal possessions or family members for
nonbusiness purposes.
(Ord. No. 93-577, 12-21-93)
Sec. 18-64. - Crosswalk.
   Crosswalk shall mean:
      (1)   That part of a roadway at an intersection included within the
connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks on opposite sides of the
highway measured from the curbs or in the absence of curbs, from the edges of
the traversable highway.
      (2)   Any portion of a street or highway at an intersection, or elsewhere
distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the
surface.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.13, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.10, MSA 9.1810.
Sec. 18-65. - Driver.
   Driver shall mean every person who drives or is in actual physical control

(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.14, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.13, MSA 9.1813.
Sec. 18-66. - Explosives.
   Explosives shall mean any chemical compound or mechanical mixture that is
commonly used or intended for the purpose of producing an explosion and which
contains any oxidizing and combustive units or other ingredients in such
proportions, quantities or packing that an ignition by fire, friction, by
concussion, by percussion, or by detonator of any part of the compound or
mixture may cause such a sudden generation of highly heated gases that the
resultant gaseous pressures are capable of producing destructible effects on

(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.15, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.15, MSA 9.1815.

Sec. 18-74. - Intersection.
   Intersection shall mean:
      (1)   The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the
lateral curblines, or, if none, then the lateral boundary lines of the roadways
of the two highways which join one another at, or approximately at, right
angles, or the area within which vehicles traveling upon different highways
joining at any other angle may come in conflict.
      (2)   Where a highway includes two roadways 30 feet or more apart, then
every crossing of each roadway of such divided highway by an intersecting
highway shall be regarded as a separate intersection. If such intersecting
highway also includes two roadways 30 feet or more apart, then every crossing
of two roadways of such highways shall be regarded as a separate intersection.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 1.23, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar definition, MCL 257.22, MSA 9.1822.

Sec. 18-117. - Traffic.

Secs. 18-126. - Low-speed vehicles.
   (a)   The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section,
shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the
context clearly indicates a different meaning:
   (b)   "Low-speed vehicle" means a self-propelled motor vehicle to which all
of the following apply pursuant to Public Act 300 of 1949, MCL 257.25b:
      (1)   That is 4-wheeled;
      (2)   Whose speed attainable in 1 mile is more than 20 miles per hour and
not more than 25 miles per hour on a paved surface;
      (3)   Whose gross vehicle weight rating or GVWR is less than 3,000
pounds. GVWR means the value specified by the manufacturer as the loaded weight
of a single vehicle.
   (c)   Each person riding a low-speed vehicle upon a roadway has all of the
rights and is subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a
vehicle under all state statutory regulations and this chapter, except for the
provisions of this chapter that by their nature do not apply.
   (d)   A person operating a low-speed vehicle shall ride as near to the right
side of the roadway as practicable and shall exercise due care when passing a
standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.
   (e)   A person operating a low-speed vehicle shall not pass between lines of
traffic, but may pass on the left of traffic moving in his or her direction in
the case of a 2-way street or on the left or right of traffic in the case of a
1-way street, in an unoccupied lane.
   (f)   A low-speed vehicle shall not be operated on a sidewalk constructed
for the use of pedestrians.
   (g)   A low-speed vehicle shall be operated at a speed of not more than 25
miles per hour, and shall not be operated on a highway or street with a speed
limit of more than 35 miles per hour except for the purpose of crossing that
highway or street. The state transportation department may prohibit the
operation of a low-speed vehicle on any highway or street under its
jurisdiction if it determines that the prohibition is necessary in the interest
of public safety.
(Ord. No. 19-1657, 9-10-19)
State law reference - MCL 257.25b, MCL 257.657, MCL 257.660.

** DIVISION 2. - ENFORCEMENT **
Sec. 18-146. - Duty to obey chapter; police orders and directions.
   This chapter is adopted in the interest of public safety, convenience and
welfare. Every person shall comply with, observe and obey, when applicable to
him, all the provisions, requirements and regulations contained in this chapter
and the regulations and orders adopted or issued in pursuance hereof. No person
shall refuse to obey or comply with any lawful order, signal or direction of a
police officer, it being hereby determined that all temporary orders and
directions, or either of them, by an authorized police officer for the
guidance, control or regulation of traffic shall supersede the provisions of
this chapter or of any and all traffic control signals and devices.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.1, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provisions, MCL 257.602, MSA 9.2302.
Sec. 18-147. - Enforcement personnel.
   The police department shall enforce and administer the provisions of this
chapter and the rules and regulations herein authorized, except as herein
otherwise provided.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-148. - Failure to obey.
   If any person shall do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required
by this chapter or by an authorized police officer while directing traffic, or
by the rules and regulations established under this chapter, such person shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor or responsible for a civil infraction, as
provided for under the terms of the Michigan Vehicle Code, Act No. 300 of the
Public Acts of Michigan of 1949 (MCL 257.1 et seq., MSA 9.1800 et seq.), as
amended.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-149. - When council approval required.
   (a)   The city council shall approve all traffic rules and regulations
authorized by this chapter that will be in effect for more than 365 days. The
council shall also approve and locate by resolution all bus and taxicab stands.
   (b)   Failure to obtain city council approval shall not be a defense to the
underlying traffic offense.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.4, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 18- 1616, 7-17-18)
Sec. 18-150. - Function of chief of police.
   (a)   It shall be the duty of the chief of police to formulate the general
policy for the direction, flow and control of traffic or parking of vehicles on
any highway, alley or public place in the city, in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter.
   (b)   The chief of police shall have the power and he is hereby authorized
to promulgate, amend or rescind traffic rules and regulations pertaining to the
following matters:
      (1)   Designate the streets or parts of streets upon which there shall be
no stopping, standing or parking of vehicles at any time; upon which there
shall be stopping, standing or parking for a limited time, or during certain
hours or on certain days and; prescribe generally the manner and duration of
parking, standing or stopping of vehicles throughout the city, including
regulation and location of parking meters.
      (2)   Allow or prohibit angle parking in designated places.
      (3)   Cause limit lines and lanes to be marked upon pavements and
sidewalks or adequate signs to be erected for the direction of pedestrians and
operators of vehicles.
      (4)   Regulate turns by designated vehicles at designated locations and
during designated hours.
      (5)   Prohibit U-turns by vehicles in designated street areas.
      (6)   Designate fire routes and prohibit standing or parking thereon
where such street or highway is especially required for use in attending fires.
      (7)   Temporarily close any highway or portion of same or restrict the
use thereof when required for public safety and convenience, or by reason of
construction or repair work thereon, or for the purpose of designating
temporary play streets. Traffic may be restricted or prohibited on such streets
or portions thereof during the hours of such use for any of the purposes
specified in this section.
      (8)   Establish quiet and safety zones along the streets.
      (9)   Establish certain alleys or parts thereof which are restricted to
one-way traffic.
      (10)   Issue permits for parades or processions in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter.
      (11)   Safety zones, building entrance zones, taxicab stands and bus
stops and bus stands, with appropriate signs providing therefor, may be erected
and established, when approved by the council, to allow standing of any vehicle
for loading and unloading of passengers, provided the standing of vehicles for
the purposes designated shall be permitted for a reasonable time only.
      (12)   Loading zones, with appropriate signs providing therefor, may be
erected and established, when approved by the council, to allow standing of
vehicles for the loading and unloading of merchandise; provided, however, the
standing of vehicles for such purposes shall be permitted only during the hours
specified on such sign, and the regulations establishing such loading zone
shall be effective only during those hours when such building or properties are
open for business; provided, further, that the establishing of a loading zone,
as herein described, shall be permitted only in those cases which will avoid
hardship to the owner or occupant of the adjacent premises and without undue
hardship to the driving public.
      (13)   Designate the streets, boulevards or parts thereof which shall be
prohibited from use by any commercial vehicle which, together with the load it
carries, exceeds two tons in weight; provided that the chief of police is
hereby authorized to designate an emergency truck route or routes for the
purpose of avoiding excessive damage to lightly paved streets which ordinarily
might be used in obtaining ingress to or egress from any particular location.
      (14)   Designate through streets.
      (15)   Determine and designate those intersections where a particular
hazard exists and determine whether vehicles shall stop at one or more
entrances to any such stop intersection and shall erect a stop sign at every
place where a stop is required.
      (16)   Determine and designate intersections where conditions warrant
requiring traffic to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic and to determine
whether vehicles shall yield the right-of-way at one or more entrances to any
such intersection. A yield right-of-way sign shall be erected at every place
where approaching traffic is required to yield the right-of-way.
      (17)   Determine and designate one-way streets and direct the appropriate
signs indicating the direction of travel on such streets.
      (18)   Establish, increase or decrease speed regulations for the streets,
alleys, public parks, cemeteries and any and all other roadways commonly open
to the public.
      (19)   Prescribe and locate all necessary official traffic control
signals, devices, markers and signs.
      (20)   Designate no passing zones on streets or parts of streets and
place and maintain official signs or markings on the roadway to indicate such
zones.
      (21)   Designate and issue permits to persons authorized to operate
emergency vehicles.
      (22)   Promulgate rules and regulations governing the operation, parking
without fees and the speed of motor vehicles upon the property owned by or
under the control of boards of education or school districts or other
educational institutions; provided, however, that no such rules and regulations
shall be promulgated without first receiving a resolution requesting the
adoption of such rules and regulations from the board of education, school
district or educational institution over whose property such rules and
regulations shall apply.
State Law reference— Operation of motor vehicles on school district property,
MCL 257.961, MSA 9.2660.
      (22A)   Promulgate rules and regulations governing the operation, parking
and the speed of motor vehicles upon privately-owned property in residential
subdivisions; provided, however, that no such rules and regulations shall be
promulgated without first receiving a request for the adoption of such rules
and regulations from the owner of the privately-owned property in the
residential subdivision.
      (23)   To make such other reasonable rules and regulations as shall be
consistent with state law and not violative of the powers of the city council.
   (c)   All rules and regulations adopted in accordance with this section
shall be documented in a record maintained by the chief of police with a copy
filed with the city clerk. Rules and regulations may be issued by the chief of
police on his own authority, but when so issued shall be known as temporary
rules and regulations. Rules and regulations will be considered permanent after
the passage of 365 days with the approval of the city council.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.5, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 06-1090, 6-19-06; Ord. No. 18-1629,
9-11-18)
Sec. 18-151. - Parades or processions.
   No parade or procession, excepting the forces of the United States Army or
Navy, the military forces of this state, and the forces of the police and fire
departments, shall occupy, march or proceed along and upon any street or
highway, without first obtaining a permit therefor from the chief of police.
Such permit shall contain a specification of the route of the proposed parade
or procession, and the chief of police, in his sole discretion, may specify any
and all routes to be traversed within the city for such parades or processions.
Whenever such parade or procession is likely to promote riot or disorder in the
city, permission to conduct the same may be denied by the chief of police;
provided, however, a procession of funeral cars through and along the streets
or highways of the city shall not be required to obtain a permit therefor;
provided, further, each vehicle composing such funeral procession, shall be
identified as such by the display, on the outside of each vehicle, of a pennant
of the type permitted by law, and each driver of such funeral vehicle shall
drive as near to the righthand edge of the street as practicable, and follow
the vehicle ahead as closely as is safe.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-152. - Application to pushcarts, animals.
   Every person propelling any pushcart or riding or leading any animal upon a
roadway, and every person driving an animal-drawn vehicle shall be subject to
the provisions of this chapter applicable to the driver of any vehicle, except
those provisions of this chapter, which by their nature can have no
application, shall not apply.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.7, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.604, MSA 9.2304.
Sec. 18-153. - Application to emergency vehicles.
   (a)   The provisions of this chapter applicable to the drivers of vehicles
upon the highways shall apply to the drivers of all vehicles owned or operated
by the United States, this state or any county, city, town, district, or any
other political subdivision of the state, subject to such specific exceptions
as are set forth in this chapter with reference to authorized emergency
vehicles.
   (b)   The driver of an authorized emergency vehicle, when responding to an
emergency call, but not while returning therefrom, may exercise the privileges
set forth in this section, but subject to the conditions herein stated.
   (c)   The driver of an authorized emergency vehicle may:
      (1)   Park or stand, irrespective of the provisions of this chapter.
      (2)   Proceed past a red or stop signal or stop sign, but only after
slowing down as may be necessary for safe operation.
      (3)   Exceed the prima facie speed limits so long as he does not endanger
life or property.
      (4)   Disregard regulations governing direction of movement or turning in
specified directions.
   (d)   The exemptions herein granted to an authorized emergency vehicle shall
apply only when the driver of any vehicle, while in motion, sounds an audible
signal by bell, siren or exhaust whistle, as may be reasonably necessary, and
when the vehicle is equipped with at least one lighted lamp displaying a
flashing, oscillating or rotating red or blue light visible under normal
atmospheric conditions from a distance of 500 feet to the front of such
vehicle. Only authorized emergency vehicles operated as police vehicles shall
be equipped with a flashing, oscillating or rotating blue light which, when
activated shall be visible under normal atmospheric conditions from a distance
of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, except where it is deemed advisable
not to equip such authorized emergency vehicle operating as a police vehicle
with a flashing, oscillating or rotating light. At other times, drivers of
authorized emergency vehicles shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or signal.
This provision shall not operate to relieve the driver of an emergency vehicle
from the duty to drive with due regard for the safety of all persons using the
highway.
   (e)   No driver of any authorized emergency vehicle shall assume any special
privileges under this chapter except when such vehicle is operated in response
to an emergency call or in the immediate pursuit of an actual or suspected
violator of the law.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.8(a)—(d), (f), 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provisions, MCL 257.603.
Sec. 18-154. - Application to workmen, equipment.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to persons, teams, motor
vehicles and other equipment while actually engaged in work upon the surface of
a highway but shall apply to such persons and vehicles when traveling to or
from such work. The provisions of this chapter governing the size and width of
vehicles shall not apply to vehicles owned by public highway authorities, when
such vehicles are proceeding to or from work on public highways.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.8(e), 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-155. - Duty upon approach of emergency vehicle.
   (a)   Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle
equipped with at least one lighted flashing, rotating or oscillating lamp
exhibiting a red or blue light, visible under normal atmospheric conditions
from a distance of 500 feet to the front of such vehicle, and when the driver
is giving audible signal by siren, exhaust whistle or bell: the driver of every
other vehicle shall yield the right-of-way and shall immediately drive to a
position parallel to and as close as possible to, the righthand edge or curb of
the roadway clear of any intersection and, shall stop and remain in such
position until the authorized emergency vehicle has passed, except when
otherwise directed by a police officer.
   (b)   This section shall not operate to relieve the driver of an authorized
emergency vehicle from the duty to drive with due regard for the safety of all
persons using the highway.
   (c)   A person who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.9, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19- 1651, 5-21-19)
State Law reference—Similar provision, MCL 257.653.
Sec. 18-155.5. - Duty upon approaching and passing a stationary authorized
emergency vehicle.
   (a)   Upon approaching and passing a stationary authorized emergency vehicle
that is giving a visual signal by means of flashing, rotating, or oscillating
red, blue, or white lights, the driver of an approaching vehicle shall exhibit
due care and caution, as required under the following:
      (1)   On any public roadway with at least two adjacent lanes proceeding
in the same direction of the stationary authorized emergency vehicle, the
driver of the approaching vehicle shall proceed with caution, reduce his or her
speed by at least ten miles per hour below the posted speed limit, and yield
the right-of-way by moving into a lane at least one moving lane or two vehicle
widths apart from the stationary authorized emergency vehicle, unless directed
otherwise by a police officer. If movement to an adjacent lane or two vehicle
widths apart is not possible due to weather, road conditions, or the immediate
presence of vehicular or pedestrian traffic in parallel moving lanes, the
driver of the approaching vehicle shall proceed as required in subsection (2).
      (2)   On any public roadway that does not have at least two adjacent
lanes proceeding in the same direction as the stationary authorized emergency
vehicle, or if the movement by the driver of the vehicle into an adjacent lane
or two vehicle widths apart is not possible as described in subsection (1), the
approaching vehicle shall proceed with due care and caution and reduce his or
her speed by at least ten miles per hour below the posted speed limit, or as
directed by a police officer.
   (b)   A person who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be ordered to pay a civil fine of $400.00.
(Ord. No. 01-849, 5-1-01; Ord. No. 01-849, 2-16-04; Ord. No. 19-1651, 5-21-19)
   State Law Reference—Similar provision, MCL 257.653a

(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.11, 11-4-81)

(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.12, 11-4-81)

Sec. 18-159. - Traffic control signal legend.
   (a)   Whenever traffic is controlled by traffic control signals, exhibiting
different colored lights successively, one at a time, or with arrows, the
following terms and lights shall indicate and apply to drivers of vehicles, as
follows:
      (1)   Green indication. Vehicular traffic facing the signal may proceed
straight through or turn right or left unless a sign at such place prohibits
either such turn. But vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or
left, shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles and to pedestrians
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time such
signal is exhibited.
      (2)   Steady yellow indication. Vehicular traffic facing the signal shall
stop before entering the nearest crosswalk at the intersection or at a limit
line, when marked, but if such stop cannot be made in safety, a vehicle may be
driven cautiously through the intersection.
      (3)   Steady red indication. Vehicular traffic facing a steady red signal
alone shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the
intersection or at a limit line, when marked, or if not, then before entering
the intersection and shall remain standing until a green indication is shown,
except as provided in subsection a.
         a.   Vehicle traffic facing a steady red signal, after stopping before
entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or at a limit line
when marked or, if there is not crosswalk or limit line, before entering the
intersection, may make a right turn from a one-way or two-way street into a
two-way street or into a one-way street carrying traffic in the direction of
the right turn; or a left turn from a one-way or two-way street into a one-way
roadway carrying traffic in the direction of the left turn unless prohibited by
sign, signal, marking, light or other traffic control device. The vehicular
traffic shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent
crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
      (4)   Arrow indications: 
         a.   Green arrow (steady). Vehicular traffic facing a green arrow
signal, shown alone or in combination with another indication, may cautiously
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by such arrow, or
such other movement as is permitted by other indications shown at the same
time. Vehicle traffic shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully
within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the
intersection.
         b.   Red arrow (flashing). When a red arrow is illuminated by rapid
intermittent flashes, drivers of vehicles shall stop before entering the
nearest crosswalk at an intersection or at a limit line when marked, or if none
then before entering the intersection and shall then be privileged to make the
movement indicated if no interference is offered pedestrians or vehicles
lawfully on the highway.
   (b)   If a traffic control signal is erected and maintained at a place other
than an intersection, the provisions of this section shall be applicable,
except as to those provisions which by their nature can have no application.
Any stop required shall be made at a sign or marking on the pavement indicating
where the stop shall be made, but in the absence of any sign or marking the
stop shall be made at the signal.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.13, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 93-580, 12-21-93)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.612, MSA 9.2312.
Sec. 18-160. - Flashing red or yellow signals.
   Whenever flashing red or yellow signals are used they shall require
obedience by vehicular traffic as follows:
      (1)   Flashing red (stop signal). When a red lens is illuminated by rapid
intermittent flashes, drivers of vehicles shall stop before entering the
nearest crosswalk at an intersection or at a limit line, when marked, and the
right to proceed shall be subject to the rules applicable after making a stop
at a stop sign.
      (2)   Flashing yellow (caution signal). When a yellow lens is illuminated
with rapid intermittent flashes, drivers of vehicles may proceed through the
intersection or past such signal only with caution.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.14, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.614, MSA 9.2314.
Sec. 18-161. - Imitation, obstruction of signs, devices prohibited, nuisance;
advertising.
   (a)   Except with authority of a statute or of a duly authorized public body
or official, no person shall place, maintain, or display along any highway or
upon any structure in or over any highway any sign, signal, marking, device,
blinking, oscillating or rotating light or lights, decoration or banner which
is or purports to be, is in imitation of or resembles, which can be mistaken
for a traffic control device or railroad sign or signal, which attempts to
direct the movement of traffic, or which hides from view or interferes with the
effectiveness of any traffic control device or any railroad sign or signal.
   (b)   No person shall place or maintain, nor shall any public authority
permit, upon any highway any traffic sign or signal bearing thereon any
commercial advertising.
   (c)   No person shall place, maintain or display along any highway any
blinking, oscillating or rotating light or lights sufficiently similar in color
and design that they may be mistaken for the distinguishing lights authorized
by law for emergency vehicles or that creates a hazard for the safety of
drivers using the highways.
   (d)   Every such prohibited sign, signal, marking device, decoration or
banner is hereby declared to be a public nuisance, and the authority having
jurisdiction over the highway is hereby empowered to remove the same or cause
the same to be removed without notice.
   (e)   Decorations or banners which may be placed over the traveled portion
of any street or highway shall be placed not closer than ten feet on either
side of traffic lights or signals and shall be so placed as to not obstruct a
clear view of such traffic lights or signals.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.15, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.615, MSA 9.2315.
Sec. 18-162. - Interference with traffic control devices or railroad signs or
signals.
   No person shall without lawful authority attempt to or in fact alter,
deface, injure, break, knock down or remove any traffic control device, any
railroad sign or signal or any inscription, shield, or insignia thereon, or any
other part thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.16, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.616, MSA 9.2316.
Sec. 18-163. - Driving on streets partially or completely closed.
   Whenever any street is partially or completely closed to the use of traffic,
and is so indicated by authorized signs or barriers, no vehicle shall proceed
into such street or any portion thereof closed to traffic, except as directed
by such signs.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.17, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-164. - Excessive noise and smoke.
   No person while operating or in charge or control of any vehicle shall make
with such vehicle, or any device connected therewith, any noise so excessive as
to annoy the public; unnecessarily race the motor while running or idling;
permit to be opened the muffler on any vehicle; or permit such vehicle, or any
device thereon, to emit an unreasonable quantity of smoke or noxious gases or
vapor. It shall be unlawful to operate a motor vehicle at any time on the
streets of the city with the so-called "cut-out" open, or to operate a motor
vehicle with a muffler from which one or more baffles have been removed.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.18, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Mufflers generally and noise levels, MCL 257.707 et seq.,
MSA 9.2407 et seq.
Sec. 18-165. - Zone of quiet.
   Whenever authorized signs are erected, indicating a zone of quiet, no person
operating a motor vehicle within any such zone shall sound the horn or other
warning device on such vehicle, except in an emergency.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.19, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-166. - Littering; public and private property.
   (a)   No person shall knowingly dump, deposit, place, throw or leave, or
cause or permit such dumping, depositing, placing, throwing or leaving of
litter, including all rubbish, refuse, waste material, garbage, offal, paper,
glass, cans, bottles, trash, debris, nails, tacks, wire or other foreign
substance of every kind and description on any public or private property or
waters, other than property designated and set aside for such purposes, without
the consent of the owner or public authority having supervision thereof.
   (b)   No person shall knowingly cause any litter or object to fall or to be
dropped into the path of or to hit a vehicle traveling the highway, street or
alley, and such person shall immediately remove it or cause it to be removed
therefrom.
   (c)   Any person removing a wrecked or damaged vehicle from a highway or
street shall remove any glass, metal or other injurious substance dropped upon
the highway from such vehicle.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.20, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Littering act, MCL 752.901 et seq., MSA 28.603(1) et seq.
Sec. 18-167. - Commercial advertising by sound truck prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate, or cause to be operated, any
sound truck on or along the streets in the city for commercial sound
advertising purposes with sound amplifying equipment in operation.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.21, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-168. - Where driving prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful to operate or drive any motor vehicle, including
motorcycles and motor driven cycles:
      (1)   On or over any sidewalk, curb, safety zone, barricade or authorized
structure in any highway, street, alley or public place.
      (2)   Across any parkway, island or unimproved portion of the highway,
either in the center thereof or at the side of the roadway, except at regularly
established crossings.
      (3)   Across private property or driveways to evade established public
ways and regulations.
      (4)   Through or upon any drive-in restaurant or parking lot driveway,
for purposes other than those for which they were constructed.
      (5)   Across, through or upon any public or private property not normally
in use and designed and intended for use by vehicular traffic, except by the
permission of the owner or lessee thereof.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.22, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-169. - Enforcement of traffic regulations, emergencies.
   (a)   Officers of the police department, or such police officers as are
assigned by the chief of police, are hereby authorized to direct the traffic by
voice, hand or signal in conformance with traffic laws, this chapter, and the
rules and regulations pertaining thereto; provided, however, that in the event
of a fire or other emergency, where it is necessary to expedite the flow of
traffic or to safeguard pedestrians, officers of the police department may
direct traffic as such conditions may require, notwithstanding the provisions
of the traffic code.
   (b)   Officers or employees of the fire department in the city, when at the
scene of a fire, may direct or assist the police in directing traffic thereat,
or in the immediate vicinity.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 2.23, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-170. - Police officer's authority to enforce Code on boundary streets
and highways.
   A police officer of the city may exercise authority and powers outside the
city when he is enforcing this chapter of the Code on a street or highway which
is on the boundary of the city as if he were in the city.
(Ord. No. 94-589, 3-16-94)
Sec. 18-171. - Committing a traffic offense while using a hand-held mobile
phone prohibited.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to commit a traffic offense while
operating a motor vehicle on any public roadway, or area open to the general
public, while using a hand-held mobile phone.
   (b)   Violation of this section is a civil infraction.
   (c)   The enforcement of this section shall be accomplished only as a
secondary action when the driver of a motor vehicle has been detained for a
suspected violation of another section of this chapter of the Code.
(Ord. No. 07-1122, 2-20-07)
Sec. 18-172. - Reading, typing, or sending text message on wireless two-way
communication device prohibited; exceptions; violation as civil infraction;
fine.
   (a)   Except as otherwise provided in this section, a person shall not read,
manually type, or send a text message on a wireless two-way communication
device that is located in the person's hand or in the person's lap, including a
wireless telephone used in cellular telephone service or personal communication
service, while operating a motor vehicle that is moving on a highway or street
in this city. As used in this subsection, a wireless two-way communication
devices does not include a global positioning or navigation system that is
affixed to the motor vehicle.
   (b)   Subsection (a) does not apply to an individual who is using a device
described in subsection (a) to do any of the following:
      (1)   Report a traffic accident, medical emergency, or serious road
hazard.
      (2)   Report a situation in which the person believes his or her personal
safety is in jeopardy.
      (3)   Report or avert the perpetration or potential perpetration of a
criminal act against the individual or another person.
      (4)   Carry out official duties as a police officer, law enforcement
official, member of a paid or volunteer fire department, or operator of an
emergency vehicle.
   (c)   An individual who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction and shall be ordered to pay a civil fine as follows:
      (1)   For a first violation, $100.00.
      (2)   For a second or subsequent violation, $200.00.
(Ord. No. 10-1287, 8-16-10)
Sec. 18-173. - Prohibited use of a cellular telephone by a person issued a
level 1 or level 2 graduated driver license; exceptions.
   (a)   Except as provided in this section, an individual issued a level 1 or
level 2 graduated license under MCL 257.310e shall not use a cellular telephone
while operating a motor vehicle upon a highway or street. For purposes of this
section, "use" means to initiate a call, answer a call, or listen to or engage
in verbal communications through the cellular telephone.
   (b)   Subsection (a) does not apply to an individual who is using a device
described in subsection (a) to do any of the following:
      (1)   Report a traffic accident, medical emergency, or serious road
hazard.
      (2)   Report a situation in which the person believes his or her personal
safety is in jeopardy.
      (3)   Report or avert the perpetration or potential perpetration of a
criminal act against the individual or another person.
   (c)   Subsection (a) does not apply to an individual using a voice-operated
system that is integrated into the motor vehicle.
   (d)   An individual who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction.
   (e)   This section shall become effective on March 28, 2013.
(Ord. No. 13-1387, 3-19-13)
Secs. 18-174—18-185. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - REGISTRATION AND LICENSES **
Sec. 18-186. - Operation of vehicle without registration plates.
   (a)   No person shall operate, nor shall an owner knowingly permit to be
operated, upon any highway, street, public way or other place open to the
general public in the city, any vehicle, including low-speed vehicles, required
to be registered under the provisions of the state vehicle code unless there
shall be attached thereto and displayed thereon, when and as required by the
state vehicle code, a valid registration certificate and registration plate
issued therefore for the current registration year. No registration plate or
plates shall be required upon any wrecked or disabled motor vehicle being
transported upon the highway by a wrecker or a registered motor vehicle.
   (b)   Except as otherwise provided in this section a person who violates
subsection (a) of this section is responsible for a civil infraction. However,
if the vehicle is a commercial vehicle which is required to be registered
according to the schedule of elected gross vehicle weights under MCL 257.801(1)
(k), the person is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not
more than 90 days or a fine of not more than $500.00, or both.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.1, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 99-758, 2-16-99; Ord. No. 03-988,
10-21-03; Ord. No. 19-1657, 9-10-19)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.255.
Sec. 18-187. - Unlawful use of certificate of title, registration certificate,
plates or permit.
   (a)   No person shall lend to another any certificate of title, registration
certificate, registration plate, special plate or permit issued to him if the
person desiring to borrow the same would not be entitled to the use thereof;
nor shall any person knowingly permit the use of any of the same by one not
entitled thereto; nor shall any person carry or display upon a vehicle any
registration certificate or registration plate not issued for such vehicle or
not otherwise lawfully used thereon under the state vehicle code.
   (b)   Except as otherwise provided in this section, a person who violates
this section is guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by imprisonment for not
more than 90 days or by a fine of not more than $100.00, or both.
   (c)   A person who displays upon a commercial vehicle, which is required to
be registered according to the schedule of elected gross vehicle weights under
MCL 257.801(1)(k), any registration plate not issued for the vehicle or not
otherwise lawfully used under this act is guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable
by imprisonment for not more than 90 days or by a fine of not more than
$500.00, or both.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.2, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.256.
Sec. 18-188. - Alteration or forging of documents.
   It shall be a misdemeanor for any person to do any of the following:
      (1)   To alter with fraudulent intent any certificate of title,
registration certification of registration (license) plate, issued by the
secretary of state;
      (2)   To forge or counterfeit any such document or plate purporting to
have been issued by the secretary of state;
      (3)   To alter or falsify with fraudulent intent or forge any assignment
upon a certificate of title;
      (4)   To hold or use any such document or plate knowing the same to have
been so altered, forged or falsified.
(Ord. No. 89-449, § 3.2(a), 5-2-89)
Sec. 18-189. - Operators, chauffeurs must be licensed.
   (a)   No person, except those expressly exempted by law, shall drive or
operate any motor vehicle, including a low-speed vehicle upon any street,
highway or public way, including public parking lots in the city, unless such
person has been, and is at the time of such driving or operating, licensed in
full force and effect as an operator or chauffeur under the provisions of the
state vehicle code or by some other constituted authority.
   (b)   No person shall be permitted to have more than one valid operator's
license at any time.
   (c)   No person shall drive a motor vehicle, including a low-speed vehicle,
in the city as a chauffeur unless he holds a valid chauffeur's license, but any
person holding a valid chauffeur's license need not procure a valid operator's
license.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.3, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 19-1657, 9-10-19)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.301.
Sec. 18-190. - License endorsement for motorcycles.
   Every person, before operating any motorcycle or motor driven cycle upon any
highway, street or public way in the city, shall procure a motorcycle
indorsement on the operator's or chauffeur's license. Such license shall be
issued, suspended, revoked, canceled or renewed in accordance with and governed
by the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act (MCL 257.1 et seq.), as amended.
Licenses issued prior to June 1, 1970, shall be valid for the duration of the
license period.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.3(a), 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.312(a).
Sec. 18-191. - Investigation of license application.
   Before the application, either new or renewal, for an operator's license or
chauffeur's license will be accepted and processed by the city police
department and sent to the secretary of state's office, the records in the city
must show that there are no traffic violation tickets or notices of traffic
violations which have been issued by the police department or by any other
authorized agency in the city which are not settled or disposed of according to
law as of the date of such application. If the police department discovers any
such traffic violation tickets or notices of traffic violations against such
applicant, or if any such violation tickets or notices of traffic violations
exist, the application of any such person for a driver's license and
chauffeur's license, or either of them, will not be processed or forwarded to
the secretary of state until all such traffic violations have been settled or
disposed of according to law.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-192. - Falsification of license application.
   (a)   It is unlawful for any person to:
      (1)   To use a false or fictitious name or give a false or fictitious
address or birthdate in any application for an operator's or chauffeur's
license, or any renewal or duplicate thereof.
      (2)   Knowingly make any false statement, or knowingly conceal any
material fact or otherwise commit a fraud on any such application.
   (b)   Any person applying for either an original, renewal or duplicate
operator's or chauffeur's license and any person requesting a change of address
for either an operator's or chauffeur's license shall sign an affidavit
swearing and affirming that the statements and answers given by him in such
application for an operator's or chauffeur's license or for change of address,
as contained therein, are true.
   (c)   Any license for any operator or chauffeur issued upon an application
which is untrue or which contains false statements as to any material matters
shall be absolutely void from the date of issuance, and the operator or
chauffeur shall be deemed unlicensed and the license so issued shall be at once
taken upon request or order of the police department.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.10, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.324.
Sec. 18-193. - Motor vehicle insurance; evidence of insurance.
   (a)   The owner or registrant of a motor vehicle, including a low-speed
vehicle, who operates or permits the operation of the motor vehicle or low-
speed vehicle on any highway, street, public way, or other place open to the
general public in the city, shall produce under subsection (b), on the request
of a police officer, evidence that the motor vehicle or low-speed vehicle is
insured under Chapter 31 of the Insurance Code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL
500.3101 to 500.3179.
      (1)   Subject to MCL 257.907(14), an owner or operator of a motor vehicle
or low-speed vehicle who fails to provide evidence of insurance on request
under this section is responsible for a civil infraction.
      (2)   An owner or operator of a motor vehicle, low-speed vehicle, or
motorcycle who fails to have motor vehicle or motorcycle insurance as required
by MCL 500.3102 is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment of not
more than 93 days, or a fine of not more than $500, or both.
   (b)   If an individual displays an electronic copy of his or her certificate
of insurance using an electronic device, the police officer shall only view the
electronic copy of the certificate of insurance and shall not manipulate the
electronic device to view any other information on the electronic device. An
individual who displays an electronic copy of his or her certificate of
insurance using an electronic device as provided in this section is not
presumed to have consented to a search of the electronic device. A police
officer may require the individual to electronically forward the electronic
copy of the certificate of insurance to a specified location provided by the
police officer. The police officer may then view the electronic copy of the
certificate of insurance in a setting in which it is safe for the officer to
verify that the information contained in the electronic copy of the certificate
of insurance is valid and accurate. The City of Dearborn, the Dearborn Police,
or an employee of the City or Dearborn Police is not liable for damage to or
loss of an electronic device that occurs as a result of a police officer's
viewing an electronic copy of a certificate of insurance in the manner provided
in this section or state law, regardless of whether the police officer or the
owner or operator of the vehicle was in possession of the electronic device at
the time the damage or loss occurred.
   (c)   The failure of a person to produce evidence that a motor vehicle,
including a low- speed vehicle, or motorcycle has in full force and effect
security complying with state statutory requirements on the date of the
issuance of the citation, creates a rebuttable presumption in a prosecution
under this section that the motor vehicle or motorcycle did not have in full
force and effect security complying with this section on the date of the
issuance of the citation.
   (d)   A certificate of insurance, paper or electronic form and issued by an
insurance company, that certifies that the security that meets the requirements
of sections 3101 and 3102 of the Insurance Code of 1956, 1956 PA 218, MCL
500.3101 and 500.3102, is in force is prima facie evidence that insurance is in
force for the motor vehicle or low-speed vehicle described in thecertificate of
insurance until the expiration date shown on the certificate. The certificate,
in addition to describing the motor vehicles or low-speed vehicles for which
insurance is in effect, must, if applicable, state the name of each individual
named on the policy, policy declaration, or a declaration certificate whose
operation of the vehicle would cause the liability coverage of that insurance
to become void.
   (e)   An owner or operator of a motor vehicle who knowingly produces false
evidence under this section is guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by
imprisonment for not more than 93 days, or a fine of not more than $500 or
both.
   (f)   A nonresident owner or registrant of a motor vehicle or motorcycle not
registered in this state shall not operate or permit the vehicle to be operated
in the city for an aggregate of more than 30 days in any calendar year unless
he or she continuously maintains security for the payment of benefits pursuant
to the Insurance Code of 1956, 1956 PA 218.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.12, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 94-614, 11-1-94; Ord. No. 99-759,
2-16-99; Ord. No. 17-1594, 9-12-17; Ord. No. 19-1657, 9-10-19; Ord. No. 21-
1716, 8-17-21; Ord. No. 23-1791, 6-13-23)
State Law reference—Similar provision, MCL 257.328, 500.3101, 500.3102
Sec. 18-194. - Violation of restricted license.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a motor vehicle in any manner
in violation of the restrictions imposed in a restricted operator's or
chauffeur's license issued to him under the provisions of the state vehicle
code, or by some other constituted authority.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.11, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.312, MSA 9.2012.
Sec. 18-195. - Possession of license; display.
   The licensee shall have his operator's license in his immediate possession
at all times when driving a motor vehicle, and shall display the same upon
demand of any uniformed police officer or field deputy or inspector, or other
duly authorized law enforcement official, who shall identify himself as such.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.4, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.311, MSA 9.2011.
Sec. 18-196. - Unlawful acts in use of licenses.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to:
      (1)   Display, cause or permit to be displayed, or to have in possession
any operator's or chauffeur's license, knowing the same to be fictitious or to
have been canceled, revoked, suspended, altered or mutilated.
      (2)   Lend to any other person or knowingly permit the use of, by one not
entitled thereto, any operator's or chauffeur's license issued to the person so
lending or permitting the use thereof.
      (3)   Display or to represent as one's own, any operator's or chauffeur's
license not issued to the person so displaying the same.
      (4)   Fail or refuse to surrender to a law enforcing official, upon
demand, any operator's or chauffeur's license which has been suspended,
canceled or revoked, as provided by law.
      (5)   Use a false or fictitious name or give a false or fictitious
address in any application for an operator's or chauffeur's license or any
renewal or duplicate thereof, or knowingly to make a false statement, knowingly
to conceal a material fact or otherwise commit a fraud in any such application.
      (6)   Alter or otherwise cause to be altered any operator's or
chauffeur's license so as to knowingly make a false statement or knowingly
conceal a material fact in order to misrepresent as one's own the operator's or
chauffeur's license.
      (7)   Use or have in possession in committing a crime an operator's or
chauffeur's license that has been altered or that is used to knowingly conceal
a material fact in order to misrepresent as one's own the operator's or
chauffeur's license.
      (8)   Furnish to a peace officer false, forged, fictitious, or misleading
verbal or written information identifying the person as another person, if the
person is detained for a violation of this chapter.
   (b)   Any license for an operator or chauffeur, issued under the provisions
of this division upon an application which is untrue, or which contains false
statements as to any material matters, shall be absolutely void from the date
of issuance. The operator or chauffeur who was issued the license shall be
deemed unlicensed, and the license issued shall be at once taken upon request
or order of the department.
   (c)   The secretary of state shall suspend the license of an operator or
chauffeur upon conviction of one of the prohibited practices described in this
section, or of this chapter, for 90 days. A second violation within a period of
seven years shall result in a suspension for one year.
(Ord. No. 81-103, §§ 3.5, 3.5a, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.324, MSA 9.2024.
Sec. 18-197. - Driving by unlicensed minor.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to cause or knowingly permit any minor
under the age of 18 years to drive a motor vehicle upon a highway as an
operator, unless such minor shall have first obtained a license to so drive a
motor vehicle under the provisions of the state vehicle code.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.6, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.325, MSA 9.2025.
Sec. 18-198. - Permitting violations.
   No person shall knowingly authorize or permit a motor vehicle owned by him
or under his control to be driven by any person in violation of any of the
provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 3.7, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.326, MSA 9.2026.
Sec. 18-199. - Operating vehicle if license, registration certificate, or
designation suspended, revoked or denied; penalty; extending period of
suspension or revocation; informing court of record and status; applicability.
   (a)   A person whose operator's or chauffeur's license or registration
certificate has been suspended or revoked, whose application for license has
been denied, or who has never applied for a license, shall not operate a motor
vehicle upon a highway or other place open to the general public or generally
accessible to motor vehicles, including an area designated for the parking of
motor vehicles, within this city.
   (b)   A person shall not knowingly permit a motor vehicle owned by the
person to be operated upon a highway or other place open to the general public
or generally accessible to motor vehicles, including an area designated for the
parking of vehicles, within this city by a person whose license or registration
certificate is suspended or revoked, whose application for license has been
denied, or who has never applied for a license, except as permitted by state
law.
   (c)   Except as otherwise provided in this section, a person who violates
subsection (a) or (b) is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable as follows:
      (1)   For a first violation, by jail for not more than 93 days or a fine
of not more than $500.00 or both. Unless the vehicle was stolen or used with
the permission of a person who did not knowingly permit an unlicensed driver to
operate the vehicle, the registration plates of the vehicle shall be canceled
by the secretary of state upon notification by a peace officer.
      (2)   For a second or subsequent violation, by jail for not more than 1
year or a fine of not more than $1,000.00 or both. Unless the vehicle was
stolen, the registration plates of the vehicle shall be canceled by the
secretary of state upon notification by a peace officer.
   (d)   This section does not apply to a person who operates a vehicle solely
for the purpose of protecting human life or property if the life or property is
endangered and summoning prompt aid is essential.
   (e)   A person whose vehicle group designation is suspended or revoked and
who has been notified as provided in MCL 257.212 of that suspension or
revocation, or whose application for a vehicle group designation has been
denied as provided by state law, or who has never applied for a vehicle group
designation and who operates a commercial motor vehicle within this state,
except as permitted under this ordinance, while any of those conditions exist
