Sec. 18-526. - Obedience to signal indicating approach of railroad train.
   (a)   Whenever any person driving a vehicle approaches a railroad grade
crossing under any of the following circumstances, the driver shall stop within
50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad, and
shall not proceed until he can do so safely:
      (1)   A clearly visible electric or mechanical signal device gives
warning of the immediate approach of a railroad train.
      (2)   A crossing gate is lowered or when a human flagman gives or
continues to give a signal of the approach or passage of a railroad train.
      (3)   A railroad train approaching within approximately 1,500 feet of the
highway crossing gives a signal audible from such distance and the train, by
reason of its speed or nearness to such crossing, is an immediate hazard.
      (4)   An approaching railroad train is plainly visible and is in
hazardous proximity to the crossing.
   (b)   No person shall drive any vehicle through, around, or under any
crossing gate or barrier at a railroad crossing while such gate or barrier is
closed or is being opened or closed.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 13.6, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.667.
Sec. 18-527. - Certain vehicles to stop at grade crossings.
   (a)   Except as provided in subsections (b), (c), and (d) of this section,
the driver of a motor vehicle carrying passengers for hire, before crossing a
railroad track at grade, shall stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less
than ten feet or not less than fifteen feet in the case of a vehicle carrying
hazardous materials on which a placard is required to be posted pursuant to 49
CFR 171.100—171.199, from the nearest rail and, while stopped, shall listen and
look in both directions along the track for an approaching train and for
signals indicating the approach of a train, and shall not proceed until the
driver can do so safely. After stopping as required in this subsection, and
upon proceeding when it is safe to do so, the driver of the vehicle shall cross
only in a gear of the vehicle that does not require changing gears while
traversing the crossing. The driver shall not shift gears while crossing the
track or tracks.
   (b)   A stop need not be made at a railroad track grade crossing where a
police officer or a traffic control signal directs traffic to proceed.
   (c)   A stop need not be made at an abandoned railroad track grade crossing.
As used in this subsection, "abandoned railroad track" means a railroad track
which meets all of the following requirements:
      (1)   The track has been abandoned pursuant to state or federal law.
      (2)   The track has been covered or removed.
      (3)   All signs, signals, and other warning devices are removed.
   (d)   A stop shall not be made at a railroad track grade crossing on a
freeway or limited access highway where the crossing is protected by a clearly
visible signal, crossing gate, or barrier at a time when the signal, crossing
gate, or barrier is not activated.
   (e)   A person who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction.
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.669.
Sec. 18-528. - Unusually heavy, constructed vehicles at grade crossings;
procedures.
   (a)   No person shall operate or move any caterpillar tractor, steam shovel,
derrick, roller, boiler, machinery, or any structure or object upon rollers or
any equipment or structure, which, because of the limited power thereof, or the
weight or character of the same or of the load thereon, shall have a normal
operating speed of four miles or less per hour, or which shall have a vertical
load or body clearance of less than nine inches above the level surface of the
roadway upon or across any tracks of any steam railroad at grade level without
first complying with this section; provided, however, that this section shall
not apply to the movement of electrically propelled cars on fixed rails nor to
their loads.
   (b)   Notice of such intended crossing shall be given to the nearest agent
or officer of such steam railroad in time to afford protection to its
locomotives, trains or cars at such crossing.
   (c)   Before making any such crossing the person operating or moving any
such vehicle or equipment shall first stop the same not less than ten feet nor
more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of any such track and, while so
stopped, shall listen and look in both directions along such track for any
approaching train and for signals indicating the approach of a train, and shall
not proceed until the crossing can be made safely.
   (d)   No such crossing shall be made when warning is given by automatic
signal, crossing gates or a flagman or otherwise of the immediate approach of a
railroad train or car.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 13.9, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.670.
Sec. 18-529. - Trains blocking streets, highways.
   No railroad corporation or company operating a railroad in this state shall
permit its engines, cars or trains to obstruct any public street or highway for
a period longer than five minutes at any one time; nor permit successive train
movements to obstruct any vehicular traffic on any public streets or highways
until all vehicular traffic previously delayed by such train movements has been
cleared or a period of five minutes has elapsed between train movements. Any
railroad company, railway engineer or railway conductor violating any of the
provisions of this section shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $100.00 or
by imprisonment not to exceed 90 days, or both such fine and imprisonment in
the discretion of the court.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 13.10, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 466.22.
Sec. 18-530. - Loitering on railroad property prohibited.
   (a)   No person shall loiter on the premises of any railroad company or
about any railway cars, nor shall any person get on, under or between such
cars, except in the ordinary transaction of business.
   (b)   A violation of this section is a civil infraction subject to a fine of
$200.00.
(Ord. No. 15-1495, 10-20-15)
Secs. 18-531—18-550. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 14. - PEDESTRIANS **
Sec. 18-551. - Right-of-way at crosswalks.
   Where traffic control signals are in place or in operation, the driver of a
vehicle shall yield the right-of-way, slowing down or stopping if need be, to
yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway within any marked
crosswalk at an intersection, except as otherwise provided in this chapter. And
when any vehicle is stopped to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway, the
driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear, shall not overtake and
pass such vehicle.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-552. - Crossing at other than crosswalks.
   Pedestrians shall not cross the street or roadway at any point, other than
at the crosswalks at intersections. Notwithstanding the provisions of this
section, every driver of a vehicle shall exercise due care to avoid colliding
with any pedestrian upon any street or roadway, and shall give warning by
sounding the horn when necessary, and shall exercise proper precaution upon
observing any person, and especially a child or any confused or incapacitated
person upon a street or roadway.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-553. - Use right half of crosswalk.
   Pedestrians shall move, whenever practicable, upon the right half of the
crosswalk.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-554. - Driving through safety zone.
   The driver of a vehicle shall not at any time drive through or over a safety
zone when such safety zone contains any person therein.
(Ord. No. 81-103, §13.4, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.666.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-555. - Handicapped persons; white canes.
   Blind persons or persons incapacitated to the extent that their movement on
foot is retarded shall be given the right of way over all vehicles and
pedestrians, by holding out horizontally a white cane in the direction they
desire to travel over crosswalks or sidewalks on any street in the city. The
use of white canes is hereby exclusively reserved to blind persons or other
persons incapacitated to the extent that their movement by foot is retarded.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-556. - Obedience to traffic control signals; pedestrian control
signals.
   (a)   Whenever special pedestrian control signals are not utilized, the
regular traffic control signals, as indicated in section
18-159, shall apply to pedestrians as follows:
      (1)   Green indication. Pedestrians facing such signal may proceed across
the roadway within any marked or unmarked crosswalk.
      (2)   Steady yellow indication. Pedestrians facing such signal are
advised that there is insufficient time to cross the roadway, and any
pedestrian then starting to cross shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles.
      (3)   Steady red indication. Pedestrians facing such signal shall not
enter the highway unless they can do so safely and without interfering with any
vehicular traffic.
      (4)   Red with arrow. Pedestrians facing such signal shall not enter the
highway unless they can do so safely without interfering with any vehicular
traffic.
   (b)   Whenever special pedestrian control signals are installed, they shall
be placed at the far end of each crosswalk and shall indicate a "walk" or
"don't walk" interval. These special signals shall apply to pedestrians only to
the exclusion of any regular traffic control signal or signals which may be
present at the same location.
      (1)   Walk interval. Pedestrians facing such signal may proceed across
the highway in the direction of the signal and shall be given the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.
      (2)   Don't walk interval (steady burning or flashing). No pedestrian
shall start to cross the highway in the direction of such signals, but any
pedestrian who has partially completed his crossing on the "walk" interval of
such signal shall proceed to a sidewalk or safety island while the "don't walk"
interval of the signal is showing.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.6, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.612, MSA 9.2312.
Sec. 18-557. - Duty at uncontrolled crossings.
   (a)   When traffic control signals are not in place or not in operation, the
driver of a vehicle shall yield the right-of-way, slowing down or stopping if
need be to so yield, to a pedestrian crossing the roadway when the pedestrian
is upon half of the roadway as to be in danger, but no pedestrian shall
suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of
a vehicle which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.
   (b)   Whenever any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at any
unmarked crosswalk at an intersection to permit a pedestrian to cross the
roadway, the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear shall not
overtake and pass such stopped vehicle.
   (c)   Before entering any street or roadway, a pedestrian must come to a
full stop at the curb or edge of the roadway and then look for oncoming
vehicles, and it is hereby declared to be unlawful for a pedestrian to cross a
street against a red light or to cross a street at some place other than a
crosswalk so as to interfere with vehicular traffic, except that a pedestrian
is not required to make such stop when crossing with a green or "walk" signal,
or at the direction of a police officer. For additional rights and duties of
pedestrians see section
18-159.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-558. - Walking on highways.
   Where sidewalks are provided, it shall be unlawful for pedestrians to walk
upon the main traveled portion of the highway. Where sidewalks are not
provided, pedestrians shall, when practicable, walk on the left side of the
highway facing traffic which passes nearest.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.8, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Similar provision, MCL 257.655, MSA 9.2355.
Sec. 18-559. - Interference with flow of traffic.
   (a)   No person, without authority, shall block, obstruct, impede or
otherwise interfere with the normal flow of vehicular or pedestrian traffic
upon a public street or highway in this city by means of a barricade, object or
device, or with his person. This section shall not apply to persons
maintaining, rearranging or constructing public utility facilities in or
adjacent to a street or highway.
   (b)   Subsection (a) and any provision of the Michigan Administrative Code
that prohibits a person from standing in a roadway other than a limited access
highway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, employment, or business from the
occupant of any vehicle do not apply to a person who is soliciting
contributions on behalf of a charitable or civic organization during daylight
hours, if all of the following are satisfied:
      (1)   The charitable or civic organization complies with applicable
regulations which include, but is not limited to, a resolution approving the
solicitation passed by the City Council.
      (2)   The charitable or civic organization maintains at least $500,000.00
in liability insurance.
      (3)   The persons soliciting contributions are 18 years of age or older.
      (4)   The persons soliciting contributions are wearing high-visibility
safety apparel that meets current American standards promulgated by the
International Safety Equipment Association.
      (5)   The portion of the roadway upon which the solicitation occurs is
not a work zone and is within an intersection where traffic control devices are
present.
   (c)   A local government or road authority that has jurisdiction over a
roadway upon which solicitation occurs as described in subsection (b) is not
liable for any claim for damages arising out of the use of the roadway as
described in subsection (b).
   (d)   A person who violates this section is responsible for a civil
infraction.
   (e)   As used in this section, "charitable or civic organization" means a
nonprofit organization that is qualified under section 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4)
of the internal revenue code, 26 USC 501, or a veterans' organization that has
tax-exempt status under the internal revenue code.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 14.9, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 17- 1595, 9-12-17)
Secs. 18-560—18-575. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 15. - VIOLATIONS BUREAU **
Sec. 18-576. - Created; jurisdiction.
   There is hereby created and established under the supervision, direction and
control of the district judges of the city, a violation bureau, to be
administered by the clerk of the court and such deputy clerks as are designated
by him to assist with the clerical work, such violations bureau being hereby
authorized to handle all such minor ordinance violations which the judges may
designate, including traffic violations other than failure to stop in the event
of an accident, driving while under the influence of intoxicating liquors or
narcotics, reckless driving, or speeding in excess of 35 miles per hour.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 15.1, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Authority to establish a parking violations bureau, MCL
600.8395, MSA 27A.8395.
Sec. 18-577. - Determination of fines.
   The district judges shall jointly from time to time determine a schedule or
amendments thereto setting forth the fines to be paid for minor violations of
any and all ordinances in the city, provided such fines, as so designated, do
not conflict with any of the provisions of the charter or the ordinances of the
city, and provided further such fines are within the limits established as
penalties under the law. Acceptance of the prescribed fine by the bureau shall
be deemed to be complete satisfaction for the violation, and the violator shall
be given a receipt which so states.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 15.2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-578. - Duties.
   The following duties are hereby imposed upon the violations bureau:
      (1)   It shall accept designated fines and issue receipts.
      (2)   It shall receive appearances of persons who must or wish to be
heard in court, enter the time of their appearance on the court docket and
notify the arresting officer.
      (3)   It shall have no discretion for the determination of the guilt or
innocence of the person notified to appear before it, and shall have only the
right to receive a plea of guilty and to receive the fine therefor.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 15.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-579. - Records, reports.
   The violations bureau shall keep appropriate records and shall, on or before
the tenth day of each following calendar month, submit summarized monthly
reports to the controller, city treasurer, chief of police and to each judge of
all violation notices settled, of all fines collected by the bureau, and of the
final disposition or present status of every case of violation for which a
violation notice issued, during the calendar month covered by the report. Such
records shall be so maintained as to show all types of violations, the total
number of each and the total fines received therefrom. The violations bureau,
through the clerk of the court, shall make a daily report and remittance to the
city treasurer of all such fines collected and received by it.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 15.5, 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-580—18-595. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 16. - PENALTIES AND MISCELLANEOUS **
Sec. 18-596. - Penalties.
   (a)   Any provision of this chapter which describes an act or omission which
constitutes a civil infraction under the terms of the Michigan Vehicle Code
shall be processed as a civil infraction, and any person found to have
committed a civil infraction may be ordered to pay a civil fine of not more
than $100.00 and costs in accordance with section 907 of the Michigan Vehicle
Code.
   (b)   Violation of any other provision of this chapter not constituting a
civil infraction, as herein provided, shall be punishable by a fine of not more
than $500.00 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or by both such fine
and imprisonment.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 16.1, 11-4-81)
State Law reference— Limitation on penalties, MCL 257.678, MSA 9.2378.
Sec. 18-597. - Opening door into roadway.
   No person shall open a door of a motor vehicle on the side facing the
traveled portion of the roadway in such a manner as to interfere with vehicles
lawfully proceeding on such public roadway.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 16.3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-598. - Splashing.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a motor vehicle recklessly,
willfully, wantonly or carelessly, or in such a manner as to splash snow, rain,
water, mud, dirt or debris on any person who is then upon a sidewalk,
crosswalk, safety zone or bus stop, or who is lawfully upon the surface of any
street.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 16.4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-599. - Hedges, plants or shrubs at intersections.
   (a)   No hedges, plants or shrubbery shall be allowed on private property,
including corner lots, adjacent to a public street or sidewalk in such a manner
so as to obstruct the view of any driver of a motor vehicle approaching a
street intersection or entering or exiting from a private or public driveway,
alley or apron leading to any street.
   (b)   It shall be the duty of the police department or the department of
building and safety in such cases to order the owner of such hedge, plant or
shrubbery to cut the same within ten days to the maximum legal height of 36
inches above street level.
   (c)   If such owner shall fail to cut such hedge, plant or shrubbery to the
lawful height within ten days after having been notified so to do, the police
department or the department of building and safety shall report such failure
to the department of public works, who shall then cut such hedge, plant or
shrubbery to the height specified, and the cost of such work shall be levied
against such owners and shall be collected by special assessment.
(Ord. No. 81-103, § 16.5, 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-600—18-615. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE III. - STOPPING, STANDING AND PARKING ***
** DIVISION 1. - IDLING **
Sec. 18-616.   Intent and Purpose.
   (a)   The City of Dearborn has determined that the unnecessary operation of
internal combustion engines poses a number of public health concerns. In
particular, airborne pollutants from engine emissions cause or aggravate
pulmonary diseases, including asthma, lung cancer, bronchitis, acute
respiratory infections, and emphysema. In addition to public health concerns,
idling engines also impose economic costs, including wasted energy, consumption
of non-renewable resources, and business and personal expenses for medical care
and loss of productivity due to pollution-related illness. Idling engines also
reduce citizens' quality of life due to noise, odor, and air pollution.
   (b)   The City has determined that unnecessary idling contributes to general
environmental degradation by emitting greenhouse gases, hydrocarbons, nitrogen
oxides, and particulate matter, and that City Council has determined that
although technological refinements have mitigated some of the adverse effects
of internal combustion engines, their use continues to increase and many older
engines continue in service, offsetting many of the benefits of new technology.
City Council recognizes that activities within Dearborn impact the environment
both locally and regionally.
   (c)   The City is committed to eliminating air toxins, criteria pollutants
and persistent bio-accumulative toxins, as well as eliminating net greenhouse
gas emissions and other destabilizing climate impacts.
   (d)   It is the intent and purpose of this chapter to regulate the operation
of internal combustion engines within the City of Dearborn in order to protect
public health and the environment, conserve energy and resources, promote
economic efficiency, and improve quality of life
(Ord. No. 22-1751, 7-12-22)
Sec. 18-617.   Definitions.
   For the purposes of this division, the following words and phrases shall
have the meanings described in this section:
   Commercial vehicle shall have the same meaning as in the Michigan Motor
Vehicle Code, MCL 257.1 et seq., as amended, means all motor vehicles used for
the transportation of passengers for hire; constructed or used for
transportation of goods, wares or merchandise; and/or all motor vehicles
designed and used for drawing other vehicles and not so constructed as to carry
any load thereon, either independently or any part of the weight of a vehicle
or load so drawn.
   Idle or Idling means to operate a motor vehicle's internal combustion engine
while the motor vehicle is stationary.
   Motor vehicle means any vehicle that is propelled by an internal combustion
engine, including but not limited to automobiles, motorcycles, buses,
recreational vehicles, trucks, tractors, earth moving equipment, hoists,
cranes, boats and other watercraft, snowmobiles, self-propelling lawnmowers,
and off-road vehicles. This definition of motor vehicle includes commercial
vehicles.
   Official traffic control device means a sign, signal, marking, or device,
placed or erected by authority of a public body or official having
jurisdiction, for the purpose of regulating, warning, or guiding traffic.
   Operator means a person who has actual control of an internal combustion
engine.
(Ord. No. 22-1751, 7-12-22)
Sec. 18-618.   Regulation of motor vehicle idling; exceptions.
   (a)   No operator of a commercial vehicle shall cause or permit the
commercial vehicle to idle:
      (1)   For any period of time while the commercial vehicle is unoccupied;
or
      (2)   For more than 5 minutes in any 60-minute period while the
commercial vehicle is occupied.
   (b)   No operator of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the motor vehicle
to idle within a posted “No Idling” zone designated by the Chief of Police or
designated pursuant to local, state, or federal law:
      (1)   For any period of time while the motor vehicle is unoccupied; or
      (2)   For more than 5 minutes in any 60-minute period while the motor
vehicle is occupied.
   (c)   Exceptions. Unless otherwise noted, the provisions of subsections (a)
and (b) of this section shall not apply in the following circumstances:
      (1)   Armored and mail delivery. An armored or mail-delivery vehicle
idles while in the course of business.
      (2)   Auxiliary and special equipment. Idling is necessary to power
auxiliary or special work equipment that is actively in use, including cargo
refrigeration units with perishable goods; waste collectors/compactors;
vehicles operating special equipment, such as lifts, winches, pumps,
compressors, drills, mixers, and safety and other construction equipment;
wheelchair lifts in buses, vans, or other motor vehicles that require engine
power to operate; “bucket” trucks that allow a worker to reach wires on a
telephone or utility pole or tree branches for trimming. Auxiliary work
equipment does not include equipment primarily intended for vehicle cabin
comfort, such as air conditioning, heating, radio, TV, or kitchen appliances.
      (3)   Diesel engines. When idling is necessary in the warm-up or cool
down of diesel engines in accordance with instructions from the manufacturer
for proper operation. This exception shall not apply if the vehicle in question
is parked or otherwise stopped in a “No Idling” zone designated pursuant to
this division.
      (4)   Emergency, law enforcement, and military vehicles. An emergency or
law enforcement vehicle, including police, fire, ambulance, public safety, and
military vehicles, or any vehicle being used in an emergency capacity, idles in
the course of or in preparation for its emergency or law enforcement duties.
      (5)   Maintenance, service, repair, etc. Idling is necessary for any
maintenance, service, repair, inspection, research and development, or
diagnostics.
      (6)   Mandated rest or sleep period. An occupied vehicle idles primarily
for purposes of air conditioning or heating during a legally mandated rest or
sleep period, if the vehicle has no functional alternative power source (e.g.,
an auxiliary power unit or generator), and it is not within 25 miles of a
parking facility with available truck stop electrification or shore power
compatible with the vehicle’s equipment. This exception shall not apply if the
vehicle in question is parked or otherwise stopped in a “No Idling” zone
designated pursuant to this division.
      (7)   Manufacture recommended. An engine is operated in accordance with
instructions from the manufacturer for proper operation.
      (8)   Other law. Applicable federal, state, or local law requires idling.
      (9)   Passenger transport. A motor vehicle designed to carry 16 or more
passengers idles to maintain comfortable cabin temperatures while non-driver
passengers are on board for up to 10 minutes before a scheduled embarkation.
      (10)   Remote start. Per MCL 257.676, a motor vehicle that is standing in
place and is equipped with a remote start feature, if the remote start feature
is engaged.
      (11)   School busses. When idling is necessary for school buses to
operate flashing lights or other safety equipment while picking up or dropping
off passengers.
      (12)   Security vehicles. A licensed private security provider idles a
vehicle in the course of performing security duties.
      (13)   Traffic conditions. When a motor vehicle is forced to remain
stationary because of an official traffic control device, direction of a law
enforcement officer, or traffic conditions beyond the operator’s control,
including but not limited to traffic congestion, railroad crossings,
construction zones, security checkpoints, and vehicle queues for drive-through
goods and services.
      (14)   Weather and comfort conditions.
         a.   Idling is necessary to operate defrosters, heaters, air
conditioners, or other equipment to prevent a safety or health emergency for
human or animal occupants.
         b.   If idling is necessary to provide heat to an occupied motor
vehicle when the outside ambient temperature is below 32 degrees Fahrenheit and
there is no accessible temperature- controlled area within a reasonable
distance; or idling is necessary to provide cooling within the cab of the
vehicle if the outside temperature is more than 80 degrees Fahrenheit and there
is no accessible temperature-controlled area within a reasonable distance.
         c.   Idling is necessary to power heaters or air conditioners to
maintain the comfort of vehicle occupants while waiting for assistance when a
vehicle is immobilized due to mechanical problems beyond the operator’s
immediate control.
(Ord. No. 22-1751, 7-12-22)
Sec. 18-619.   Regulation of generators and other internal combustion engines.
   (a)   Excluding motor vehicle, no internal combustion engine shall be
operated except when it is providing power or electrical energy to equipment, a
tool, a machine, or an appliance that is actively in use.
   (b)   This section shall not apply in the following circumstances:
      (1)   Engine operation is necessary to prevent a health or safety
emergency, or to provide power to a residence, business, or building due to a
power outage.
      (2)   Engine operation is necessary for any maintenance, service, repair,
inspection, research and development, or diagnostics.
      (3)   An engine is operated in accordance with instructions from the
manufacturer for proper operation.
(Ord. No. 22-1751, 7-12-22)
Sec. 18-620.   Penalties; repeat violation; rebuttable presumption.
   (a)   Each violation of this division shall be a civil infraction punishable
by a fine of $250.00, plus any additional costs or conditions imposed by the
court.
   (b)   An increased fine schedule shall be imposed for repeat violations of
this division. A repeat violation shall mean a violation committed within 30
days of an admission or determination of responsibility in court for a
violation of this division. The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall
be a civil fine of $500.00, plus any additional costs or conditions imposed by
the court.
   (c)   Where a responsible operator is not immediately apparent, there shall
be a rebuttable presumption of responsibility on the part of the person in
whose name the offending motor vehicle or engine is registered at the time of
the violation.
(Ord. No. 22-1751, 7-12-22)
Secs. 18-621 - 18-670. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 2. - PARKING LOTS **
* Subdivision I. - In General *
Sec. 18-671. - Definition.
   For the purposes of this division, an "automobile parking lot" or an "open
parking station" shall be construed to be any plot, piece or parcel of land
used for the purpose of storing or parking more than two motor vehicles and
shall include such premises where shelters that are not completely enclosed are
erected. Such establishments shall be classified as follows:
      (1)   Class I. Such automobile parking lots wherein space is let leased
for a fee or other consideration for the storage or parking of more than two
motor vehicles.
      (2)   Class II. Such automobile parking lots that are maintained and
operated by any person in the city in connection with and for the benefit of
patrons or customers of any establishment, store, theatre, amusement, dance
hall, apartment, hotel or other business or enterprise.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-672. - License required for Class I.
   No person, except the city, shall maintain or conduct an automobile parking
lot or an open parking station within the city of Class I without first having
obtained a license therefor from the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-673. - Permits required for Class I parking lots.
   (a)   Permits shall be obtained before starting work on development of all
Class I parking areas.
   (b)   The fees to be paid for permits shall be in accordance with chapter 9,
article XVI, section
9-262.
(Ord. No. 81-125, §§ 2a, 2b, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 07-1141, 11-5-07)
Sec. 18-674. - Application for license.
   (a)   Applications for licenses to conduct an automobile parking lot of
Class I shall be made by the persons intending to conduct such business upon
forms to be furnished by the city clerk, and shall set forth:
      (1)   The name under which and the place where the parking lot is to be
operated.
      (2)   Whether the applicant is an individual, partnership or corporation.
      (3)   If an individual, the name and business and residence address of
the applicant.
      (4)   If a partnership, the name, business and residence address of each
partner; if a corporation, the name, date and state under which such
corporation was organized, the amount and value of the capital stock, and the
names, business and residence addresses of the officers, managers in charge and
directors thereof.
      (5)   Whether the premises to be used as a parking lot are owned or
leased by the applicant, and, if leased, the name and address of each owner
thereof.
      (6)   The maximum number of motor vehicles which may at any one time be
stored upon the premises.
      (7)   The hours during which such motor vehicles may be stored thereon.
      (8)   A complete schedule of the rates to be charged for storing motor
vehicles.
   (b)   Such application shall be signed and verified under oath by the
applicant, if an individual or by a duly authorized agent, if a partnership or
corporation.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-675. - License, annual inspection fees.
   An annual license and inspection fee shall be paid to the city treasurer
prior to the issuance of any Class I license under this division as follows:
      (1)   Lots accommodating 10 cars or less ..... $ 10.00
      (2)   Lots accommodating 25 cars or less, but more than 10 ..... 20.00
      (3)   Lots accommodating 50 cars or less, but more than 25 ..... 50.00
      (4)   Lots accommodating over 50 cars shall pay $50.00, plus an
additional license fee for each car over 50 ..... 1.00
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-676. - Issuance of license.
   Each applicant for a Class I license under this division, together with all
employees and servants to be employed or subsequently thereto employed on the
licensed premises, shall, for the purpose of identification, be fingerprinted
at the record bureau in the police department and shall prior to issuance of a
license, pay the requisite fee to the city treasurer, whereupon the council may
grant a license to conduct an automobile parking lot if the chief of the police
department shall certify that the applicant is a fit and suitable person, which
license shall continue in full force and effect until 12:00 midnight following
the first Tuesday in May of each year, or until such license is revoked.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-677. - Entrance, exits, paving.
   Prior to the issuance of any license for a Class I parking lot, the building
and safety department shall cause an inspection to be made of the proposed
parking lot and shall certify that the entrances and exits thereto from the
public way have the proper curb cuts, and the space between the sidewalk and
curb, where it is adjacent to a concrete roadway, shall be paved with cement
concrete. In the case of Class I parking lots, the parking surface and aisles
shall be covered with a pavement of asphaltic or cement concrete and shall be
graded and drained to catch basins connected to the city sewer. Driving of cars
across curbs or sidewalks at any location other than a proper driveway entrance
or exit is prohibited at any time.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-678. - Signs required.
   Each Class I licensee shall maintain at the entrance to such automobile
parking lot a permanently affixed sign of sufficient size and suitable to
apprise persons using such parking lot of the name of the licensee, the hours
of the day and/or night during which such places are open for storing motor
vehicles, the rates charged and the closing hour of such parking lots.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 7, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-679. - Unauthorized operation of parked cars prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any Class I licensee, his agent, servants or
employees to drive, or suffer or permit to be driven by any other person, from
the licensed premises, any parked or stored motor vehicle without the consent
of the owner.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 8, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-680. - Claim checks.
   (a)   At the time of accepting a motor vehicle for storing or parking in an
open parking lot by a Class I licensee, the person conducting the same, his
agent, servant or employee shall furnish such person parking his motor vehicle
a distinctive check which shall be numbered to correspond to a coupon placed
upon such motor vehicle, which check shall contain the name and address of the
person owning or operating such open parking lot and upon which shall be
written or stamped the date and the license number of the motor vehicle.
   (b)   The above provisions shall not be applied where automobiles are stored
on a weekly or monthly fee basis.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 9, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-681. - Notification to police of claims.
   (a)   Each Class I licensee shall immediately notify the police department
of any claim made by reason of any loss, theft or conversion occurring upon his
premises or of any claim for damages arising from the operation of such parking
lot.
   (b)   The obligation created by this section of any person operating or
conducting an open parking lot, under the terms of this division to the owner
of a motor vehicle parked therein, is not extended beyond the regular posted
hours of attendance, as posted upon such open parking lot and printed upon the
regular receipt furnished to such motor vehicle owner.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 10, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-682. - Limitation of liability.
   No contract, agreement, lease, receipt, rule or regulation shall exempt any
person operating an open parking station of Class I from damage or loss caused
by the neglect of such person or any employee of such person, or while in the
employment of such person.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 11, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-683. - Revocation of license.
   The council may revoke any Class I license if at any time:
      (1)   A licensee has knowingly made any false or materially incorrect
statement in the application.
      (2)   A licensee knowingly violates or knowingly permits or countenances
a violation of any provisions of this division.
      (3)   A licensee knowingly violates or knowingly permits or countenances
the violation of any provision of any penal law or ordinance regarding theft,
larceny or conversion of a motor vehicle or the operation of a motor vehicle
stored on such parking lot without the owner's consent; whether such licensee
or other person is convicted of such an offense or not.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 12, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-684. - Fire hazard prohibited.
   Class I parking lots licensed under this division shall be equipped with
proper fire extinguishing apparatus, subject to the approval of the fire
department. All motor vehicles shall be so stored that they may be readily
reached in case of fire or other emergency.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 13, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-685. - Dust control.
   Class I parking lot licensees shall keep the parking lot at all times free
from dust by frequent sprinkling with water or the use of calcium chloride or
other means so that the parking lot shall not become a nuisance to adjoining
property owners or others.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 14, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-686. - Vending of goods, wares or merchandise.
   No Class I parking lot licensee shall sublet, sublease or otherwise permit
any parking lot or any portion thereof to be used by any vendor of goods, wares
or merchandise or services for the conduct of such vendor's business, unless
the same is conducted in a permanent building or structure.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 15, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-687. - Regulation of class II parking lots.
   Automobile parking lots of Class II shall not need a license for their
operation or maintenance, but shall be subject to the following regulations,
failure to observe which shall subject violators to the penalties set forth in
section
1-9.
   (1)   A permit will be required and shall be applied for on forms to be
furnished by the department of building and safety.
      a.   A plot plan shall be submitted with the application which shall show
size of lot, property lines, street and alley lines, adjacent building lines,
location and size of entrances and exits and drainage facilities and any other
information pertinent to the construction.
      b.   The fees to be paid for permits shall be in accordance with Chapter
9, Article XI, Section
9-262.
   (2)   Such parking lots shall be laned and provided adequate ingress and
egress for automobile parking so that in case of fire or other emergency each
vehicle may be easily reached or removed.
   (3)   Entrances and exits from such parking lots shall be only at properly
established curb cut driveways with paved cement concrete aprons from sidewalks
to curb. Driving of cars across curb or sidewalk, except at curb cut driveways,
is prohibited.
   (4)   The parking surface shall be covered with asphaltic or cement concrete
pavement and shall be graded so as not to drain on adjoining property or across
the city sidewalk.
   (5)   All parking lots shall be kept free from dust, ruts and pits and shall
have a seal coat applied wherever necessary.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 16, 11-4-81; Ord. No. 07-1142, 11-5-07; Ord. No. 25-1859,
9-23-25)
Sec. 18-688. - Barriers.
   A barrier consisting of a concrete wall, precast concrete, or bituminous
curb of a steel guard rail not over 18 inches high above the grade, as
established by the city, shall be maintained on all parking lots between the
parking area and the side yards abutting any partition fence and along any part
of the area which abuts a public street or highway. All such barriers shall be
placed a sufficient distance from adjoining property lines to prevent car
bumpers from projecting over such property lines.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 6(a), 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-689. - Specifications for asphaltic concrete pavement.
   (a)   All pavement shall consist of a base course constructed of good
quality 100 percent crushed stone, 100 percent crushed slag or 100 percent
natural aggregate, uniformly spread upon a prepared subgrade and compacted with
a power roller weighing not less than eight tons to a minimum depth of six
inches after compaction.
   (b)   To the base course shall be applied a minimum thickness of two inches
of hot asphaltic concrete applied in two courses; a binder course of 9a or 25a
aggregate and a surface course of 31a aggregate. In the case of parking lots of
6,000 square feet or less, the asphaltic surface pavement may be placed in one
course of 1½-inch minimum thickness, using 31a aggregate. All materials,
methods of construction and mixing of asphaltic concrete shall be in accordance
with the standard specifications for parking lot construction of the city on
file in the city engineer's office and available there for public inspection.
The construction shall be subject to inspection by the division of building and
safety.
(Ord. No. 81-125, § 16(e), 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-690—18-705. - Reserved.
* Subdivision II. - Shopping Centers *
Sec. 18-706. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this subdivision, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Duly posted regulations shall mean a sign or other traffic control device
shall be deemed duly posted in compliance with the requirement of this
subdivision if:
      (1)   Such sign or traffic control device is placed within the shopping
center parking area in a manner so as to adequately advise any person of the
restricted conduct and is of size and shape and contains lettering approved by
the police department.
      (2)   Such sign or traffic control device is placed within the shopping
center parking area after a request for such sign or traffic control device has
been made to the police department by either the owner or the person in charge
of the general operation and control of the parking area, and the police
department determines that such regulation is required by local conditions for
the safety and convenience of the public or the users of the shopping center.
      (3)   Such sign or traffic control device shall be purchased, installed
and maintained at the sole expense of the property owner.
   Parking area shall mean an area near or contiguous to a shopping center,
used by the public as the means of access to and egress from the stores and
business establishments at the shopping center and for the free parking of
motor vehicles of patrons of the shopping center.
   Shopping center shall mean a minimum area of three acres of land on which
there is located one or more stores or business establishments and where there
is provided a parking area.
(Ord. No. 81-110, § 1, 11-4-81)
Cross reference— Definitions and rules of construction generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 18-707. - Enforcement.
   The police department of the city shall enforce this subdivision and have
the power and authority to issue citations for any violation pursuant to this
subdivision.
(Ord. No. 81-110, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-708. - Unlawful acts.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to drive or operate a motor vehicle in a
shopping center parking area in violation of any of the following duly posted
regulations or operative control devices in the shopping center parking lot:
      (1)   Stop signs, yield signs or other traffic control devices erected at
specified entrance or exit locations to a shopping center or at any
intersection in the parking area.
      (2)   Directional signs prohibiting or regulating the turning of vehicles
or specified types of vehicles at intersections or other designated locations
in the parking area.
      (3)   Signs regulating the crossing of any roadway in the parking area by
pedestrians.
      (4)   Directional signs designating any separate roadway, drive or lane
in the parking area for one-way traffic.
      (5)   Signs prohibiting, regulating, restricting or limiting the stopping
or parking of vehicles in specified areas of the parking area.
      (6)   Signs designating safety zones and other restricted area in the
shopping center.
      (7)   Signs prohibiting, regulating, restricting or limiting the flow of
traffic and/or parking in such shopping center parking area where such
prohibition, regulation, restriction, or limitation is reasonably required by
local conditions for the safety and convenience of the public or of the users
of the shopping center.
(Ord. No. 81-110, § 2, 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-709—18-725. - Reserved.
* Subdivision III. - Handicapped Parking *
Sec. 18-726. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this subdivision, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Duly posted regulations shall mean a sign or other traffic control device in
a parking area shall be deemed duly posted in compliance with the requirement
of this subdivision if:
      (1)   Such sign or traffic control device is placed within the parking
area in a manner so as to adequately advise any person of the restricted
conduct and is of size and shape and contains lettering approved by the police
department.
      (2)   Such sign or traffic control device is placed within the parking
area after a request for such sign or traffic control device has been made to
the police department by either the owner or the person in charge of the
general operation and control of the parking area, and the police department
determines that such regulation is required by local conditions for the safety
and convenience of the public or the users of the parking area. Such sign or
traffic control device shall be purchased, installed and maintained at the sole
expense of the property owner.
   Handicapped shall mean a person who has a physical characteristic
categorized as a handicap, which limits ambulation or necessitates the use of a
wheelchair for mobility, or a person who is blind.
   Handicapped parking space shall mean a parking space 12 feet wide, marked
off in traffic paint and inscribed with the international wheelchair symbol, or
a reasonable facsimile thereof. A sign located approximately six feet
abovegrade inscribed with the international wheelchair symbol, or a reasonable
facsimile thereof, shall identify the handicapped space and shall contain
notice of the possible fine for violation of the provisions of this subdivision
and a statement that a permit, certificate of identification or a special
registration plate, must be displayed.
   Parking area shall mean an area used by the public as a means of access to
an egress from, and for the free parking of motor vehicles by patrons of a
shopping center, business, factory, hospital, institution or similar building
or location.
   Shopping center shall mean a minimum area of three acres of private land on
which there is located one or more stores or business establishments, and where
there is provided a parking area.
(Ord. No. 82-262, § 1, 12-7-82)
Sec. 18-727. - Penalty.
   Except as otherwise provided, a person who violates this subdivision shall
be found to have committed a civil infraction and may be ordered to pay a civil
fine of not more than $100.00. As part of the penalty imposed for violation of
this subdivision, the district judge shall order the certificate of
identification and/or special registration plate confiscated and returned to
the secretary of state, together with a certified copy of the sentence imposed.
(Ord. No. 82-262, § 4, 12-7-82; Ord. No. 96-668, 4-16-96)
Sec. 18-728. - Handicapper spaces.
   The city council shall provide, by local ordinance, for parking spaces
specifically designated for handicappers, in numbers to conform with the
requirements of MCL 125.1352, MSA 3.447(122), in each shopping center parking
area within its jurisdiction. If on March 30, 1979, a shopping center is in
compliance with a local ordinance relating to the number of parking spaces
which the shopping center is required to provide, the shopping center shall not
be held in violation of that ordinance if the designation of parking space
required by this section reduces the number of parking spaces below the minimum
number required by the local ordinance.
State Law reference— Similar provisions, MCL 257.942a, MSA 9.2642(1).
Sec. 18-729. - Use of space; identification.
   (a)   Except as otherwise provided in this section and this chapter, a
vehicle stopped or parked upon a highway or street shall be stopped or parked
with the wheels of the vehicle parallel to the roadway and within 12 inches of
any existing righthand curb.
   (b)   A local authority may by ordinance permit parking of vehicles with the
lefthand wheels adjacent to and within 12 inches of the lefthand curb of a one-
way roadway.
   (c)   A local authority may by ordinance permit angle parking on a roadway,
except that angle parking shall not be permitted on a state trunk line highway.
   (d)   The state transportation commission, with respect to state trunk line
highways, and the board of county road commissioners with respect to county
roads, acting jointly with the director of the department of state police, may
place signs prohibiting or restricting the stopping, standing, or parking of
vehicles on a highway where, in the opinion of the officials as determined by
an engineering survey, the stopping, standing, or parking is dangerous to those
using the highway or where the stopping, standing, or parking of vehicles would
unduly interfere with the free movement of traffic on the highway or street.
The signs shall be official signs, and a person shall not stop, stand, or park
a vehicle in violation of the restrictions stated on the signs. The signs shall
be installed only after a proper traffic order is filed with the county clerk.
Upon the application to the state transportation commission by a home rule city
affected by an order, opportunity shall be given to the city for a hearing
before the state transportation commission, pursuant to the administrative
procedures act of 1969, as amended, except when an ordinance of the home rule
city prohibits or restricts the parking of vehicles on a state trunk line
highway; when the home rule city, by lawfully authorized official action,
requests the state transportation department to prohibit or restrict parking on
a state trunk line highway; or when the home rule city enters into a
construction agreement with the state transportation department providing for
the prohibition or restriction of parking on a state trunk line highway during
or after the period of construction. Traffic control orders, so long as they
affect parking upon a state trunk line highway within the corporate limits of a
home rule city, are considered "rules" and, upon application for a hearing by a
home rule city, the proceedings before the state transportation commission
shall be considered a "contested case" within the meaning of that act.
   (e)   A handicapper is entitled to receive, and the secretary of state may
issue, under the rules and upon the application as the secretary of state
prescribes, a serially numbered transferable certificate of identification for
the personal use of the handicapper. The rules shall provide that if the
handicapper personally applies at a branch office of the secretary of state and
if it appears obvious that the handicapper has a qualifying handicap, the
handicapper shall not be required to present a medical statement attesting to
the handicap. The secretary of state may issue a certificate of identification
valid for a period of not less than one month to a handicapper who has a
temporary handicap or a certificate of identification valid for at least four
years to a handicapper who has a permanent handicap. An original certificate of
identification issued to a handicapper with a permanent handicap shall expire
on the handicapper's fifth birthday after the date of issuance. A renewal
certificate issued to a permanent handicapper shall expire on the handicapper's
fourth birthday after its issuance. A person holding a certificate of
identification, at any time within 45 days before the expiration of his or her
certificate, may make application for a new certificate as provided for in this
section. However, if the person will be out of state during the 45 days
immediately preceding expiration of the certificate or for other good cause
shown cannot apply for a certificate within the 45-day period, application for
a new certificate may be made not more than six months before expiration of the
certificate. This new certificate, when granted shall expire as provided for in
this subsection. Upon application as prescribed by the secretary of state, a
handicapper may be issued a duplicate certificate of identification for a fee
of $10.00. The certificate may be used by a person other than the handicapper
for the sole purpose of providing transportation to the handicapper. An
organization which provides specialized services to handicappers may apply for
and receive a handicapper certificate of identification to be used in motor
vehicles used by the organization and used to transport handicappers who
receive services from the organization. If the organization ceases to provide
specialized services to handicappers, the certificate shall be returned to the
secretary of state for destruction.
   (f)   A handicapper holding a certificate of identification, a person having
special registration plates issued under MCL 257.803d, MSA 9.2503(4), a person
holding a special registration plate to which a handicapper tab is attached,
issued under section 803f, a handicapper holding a similar certificate of
identification from another state, or a person having special handicapper
registration plates from another state shall be entitled to courtesy in the
parking of a vehicle, including free parking in a metered parking space, which
courtesy shall relieve the handicapper or the person transporting the
handicapper from liability for a violation with respect to parking, other than
in violation of this act. A local authority may, by ordinance, prohibit parking
on a street or highway for the purpose of creating a fire lane or to provide
for the accommodation of heavy traffic during morning and afternoon rush hours,
and the privileges extending to veterans and physically handicapped persons
under this subsection shall not apply on streets or highways where and at the
times the parking is so prohibited.
   (g)   A certificate of identification issued, as provided in subsection (d),
shall be displayed on the lower left corner of the front windshield of the
vehicle while being parked by or under the direction of a handicapper pursuant
to this section. Upon conviction of an offense involving a violation of the
special privileges conferred upon holders of the certificates of
identification, a magistrate or judge trying the case, as a part of any penalty
imposed, may confiscate the serially numbered certificate of identification and
return the certificate of identification to the secretary of state together
with a certified copy of the sentence imposed. Upon receipt of a certificate of
identification from a judge or magistrate, the secretary of state shall destroy
the certificate, and the handicapper to whom it was issued shall not receive
another certificate until he or she submits a completed application and
presents a current medical statement attesting to his or her handicap. A
person, other than a handicapper to whom the certificate of identification was
issued or a person who used a certificate of identification for the sole
purpose of providing transportation to a handicapper, who uses a certificate of
identification for the purpose of parking a vehicle as permitted by this
subsection is guilty of a misdemeanor, and a law enforcement officer who
observes this misuse of a certificate of identification may immediately
confiscate the certificate and forward it to the secretary of state, who may
return it to the handicapper.
   (h)   A person who intentionally makes a false statement of material fact or
commits or attempts to commit a deception or fraud on a medical statement
attesting to a handicap, submitted in support of an application for a
certificate of identification or a special registration plate or handicapper
tab under this section or section MCL 257.803d, f, MSA 9.2503(4), (6), is
guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not more than $500.00 or
imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both.
   (i)   A person who commits or attempts to commit a deception or fraud by one
or more of the following methods is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a
fine of not more than $500.00 or imprisonment not more than 30 days, or both:
      (1)   Using a handicapper certificate of identification issued under this
section or by another state to provide transportation to a handicapper, when
the person is not providing transportation to a handicapper.
      (2)   Altering, modifying, or selling a handicapper certificate of
identification issued under this section or by another state.
      (3)   Making a false statement of material fact to obtain a certificate
of identification under this section, a special registration plate or a
handicapper tab.
(Ord. No. 96-668, 4-16-96)
Secs. 18-730—18-745. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 3. - TRAFFIC VIOLATION NOTICES **
Sec. 18-746. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Traffic violation notice shall mean a notice given by a member of the police
department to an alleged violator or attached to a parked vehicle, and which
can be disposed of in the violation bureau by payment of a prescribed penalty.
   Traffic violation summons shall mean a notice given by a member of the
police department to an alleged violator notifying such person to appear at the
court which has jurisdiction upon a date certain, and which notice cannot be
disposed of in the city violation bureau.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 1, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-747. - Form of notices.
   Traffic violation notice forms and traffic violation summons forms shall be
bound in books and shall be in a form prescribed by the chief of police and
corporation counsel. Books of notice forms and summons forms to be used for
traffic ordinance violations shall be provided by the chief of police.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 2, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-748. - Records.
   The record bureau of the police department shall maintain a record of all
blank traffic violation notices and summonses in the possession of each and
every member of the police department.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 3, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-749. - Issuance.
   (a)   All traffic violation notices and traffic violation summonses shall be
issued in triplicate, one copy thereof shall be given to the violator or
affixed to his vehicle, as authorized by ordinance, and two copies shall be
filed in the record bureau of the police department.
   (b)   Within three days of the issuance of any such notice, the chief of
police, in the absence of any mitigating circumstances, shall cause to be filed
one copy with the violations bureau.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 4, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-750. - Payment of fines.
   Upon the issuance and filing with the violations bureau of any traffic
violation notice, it may be disposed of by payment to the traffic violation
bureau of the penalty prescribed for such alleged offense and in accordance
with the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 5, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-751. - Disposition.
   Upon the issuance and filing with the court of a traffic violation summons,
the same may be disposed of in the same manner as other complaints regularly
made in such court.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 6, 11-4-81)
Sec. 18-752. - Violations.
   Any person who cancels or in any manner disposes of any traffic violation
ticket or traffic violation summons in any other manner than as provided in
this division shall be guilty of a violation of this division; provided
however, that nothing contained in this division shall operate to preclude any
violator from his right of appeal or to pursue any remedy afforded by law.
(Ord. No. 81-131, § 7, 11-4-81)
Secs. 18-753—18-759. - Reserved.
** DIVISION 4. - PAID PARKING **
Sec. 18-760. - Installation and operation of parking meters.
   Parking meters shall be placed adjacent to each parking place. Each parking
meter shall display a signal that the adjacent parking space is or is not
legally in use. Each parking meter shall display, on deposit of a United States
coin of the denomination stated on the meter, a signal indicating legal parking
for that period of time which may be established for that area in which the
parking meter is installed and which is permitted for the deposit of the
specific coin inserted. Upon the expiration of the time limit the parking meter
shall indicate by a signal that the lawful parking period has expired, and in
such cases, the right of the motor vehicle to occupy such space shall cease and
the person having control of the vehicle shall be subject to designated
penalties.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-761. - Space marking.
   The chief of police shall place or cause to be placed lines or marks on the
curb, street or other area about or alongside of each parking meter to
designate the parking space for which the meter is to be used, and no person
shall park or stand any vehicle across any such line or mark or park the
vehicle in such way that it will not be within the area so designated by the
lines or markings.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-762. - Parking by curb painted yellow.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to park any vehicle alongside any curb
painted yellow.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-763. - Time limits.
   (a)   The following time limits shall apply to parking spaces adjacent to
parking meters during the hours specified on the meters each day except Sundays
and holidays:
      (1)   Whenever a vehicle is parked in the space adjacent to a parking
meter, the operator of the vehicle shall immediately deposit or cause to be
deposited a coin of the United States in such parking meter of a denomination
specified on the parking meter except when the time on the meter has not yet
expired. He shall also place such meter in operation by turning or pressing any
lever, handle crank or other device provided upon such meter. Thereupon said
parking space may be lawfully occupied by such vehicle only until the meter
indicates the time limit has expired.
      (2)   No person shall leave any vehicle in a metered space for longer
than the maximum time permitted by the meter. Each successive period of parking
longer than said maximum time period constitutes a separate offense. The time
limit is applicable regardless of whether or not the parking meter indicates
the time limit has expired.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-764. - Offenses.
   (a)   No person shall:
      (1)   Deposit or cause to be deposited in any parking meter any slug,
device or metallic substitute for a United States coin.
      (2)   Remove, deface, injure, tamper with, open or willfully break,
destroy, or impair the usefulness of any parking meter.
   (b)   A person who violates this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor
punishable by imprisonment for not more than 93 days or a fine of not more than
$500.00 or both.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-765. - Gated parking facilities; failure to pay parking fee.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit a vehicle to enter a
gated facility without paying the parking fee if the facility is equipped for
payment of the fee on entering.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit a vehicle to enter a
gated parking facility without first obtaining a parking permit at the entrance
to the facility if the facility is equipped for such permit, which permit shall
indicate the time and date of entrance of the vehicle.
   (c)   If the facility is equipped for issuance of parking permits at the
entrance to that facility, it shall be unlawful for any person to permit a
vehicle to exit from the facility without first presenting said permit to the
attendant or inserting said permit in any device provided for measuring the
period during which the vehicle was parked.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-766. - Uses of entrance and exit.
   No person shall enter any municipal off-street parking lot over any area or
driveway or the portion between any curb returns which is not marked with the
work "entrance" or otherwise indicated by arrows, signs, or words that it is a
driveway or place for the entering of such parking lot.
   No person shall move any vehicle from any such parking lot into any public
way over any area except an area marked with the word "exit" or otherwise
indicated by arrows, signs, or words that it is a driveway or place for the
leaving of such parking lot.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-767. - Prima facie evidence; parking violators.
   In any proceeding for violation of the parking provisions of this division,
the registration plate displayed on such motor vehicle shall constitute in
evidence a prima facie presumption that the owner of such motor vehicle was the
person who parked or placed such motor vehicle at the point where such
violation occurred.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-768. - Towing of vehicles.
   Whenever any vehicle shall be found parked in any parking meter space
overtime and beyond the period of legal parking time established for such
space, or shall be found parked therein during any period when parking is
prohibited, or shall be found parked in violation of any of the provisions of
this division, the enforcing officer may serve upon the owner or operator of
such vehicle, or attach or fasten to such vehicle, a parking meter violation
notice; and may, in addition, cause such vehicle to be removed by, or under the
direction of, any person authorized to enforce this division by means of towing
the same, and such removal shall be at the risk and expense of the owner.
   Whenever any vehicle shall be found parked in a non-designated and/or
improper parking area, it shall be removed by, or under the direction of, any
person authorized to enforce this division by means of towing the same, and
such removal shall be at the risk and expense of the owner.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
Sec. 18-769. - Enforcement and penalty.
   (a)   The provisions of this division may be enforced by any police officer
and/or ordinance officer and/or private parking administrator so designated by
the chief of police.
   (b)   Every person convicted of a violation of any provision of this
division or any rule or regulation promulgated pursuant to this division for
which no other penalty is provided shall be responsible for a civil infraction.
(Ord. No. 06-1085, 6-12-06)
** DIVISION 5. - RESIDENTIAL PARKING PERMITS **
Sec. 18-770. - Parking in nearby residential areas to avoid paid parking.
   (a)   In order to protect nearby residential areas from the negative effects
of the parking of vehicles in those areas to avoid paid parking, a system of
residential parking permits shall be established. The goal of a system of
residential parking permits is to avoid the harm to residents that may be
caused by individuals attempting to avoid paid parking, not to grant any
additional privileges or entitlement to particular public parking spaces.
   (b)   Residential parking district shall be any public or private road and
private parking lot located within 1,500 feet of the downtown parking district.
The downtown parking district is defined as all of the business frontage north
and south of West Village Drive, Michigan Avenue, and Garrison between Oakwood
and Military. The downtown parking district includes all of the business
frontage south of Morley between Monroe and Mason. It also includes the city-
owned parking lot south of the railroad between Monroe and Mason.
   (c)   It shall be unlawful to use the private parking of another business or
unmetered public streets in residential parking districts to avoid paid parking
when visiting, shopping, working, or recreating in the downtown parking
district.
   (d)   Downtown parking district. 
      (1)   A downtown parking district may contain multiple zoning
classifications; however, permit parking shall apply to public roads.
      (2)   Permits shall not be issued to businesses located within the
downtown parking district.
      (3)   Residential parking permits shall only be available to property
owners within residential A, B, C, D, E and residential preservation zoning
districts. However, residential parking permits will not be issued to property
within those zoning districts that are being used for office purposes.
   (e)   Residential parking permits; process. 
      (1)   Residential parking permits shall be available for vehicles owned
and operated by persons living full-time in the residential parking district.
      (2)   Residential parking permits shall be renewed annually.
      (3)   Residential parking permits are non-transferable and non-
assignable.
      (4)   A residential parking permit will be issued to a vehicle upon a
showing of the following:
         i.   Picture identification;
         ii.   Proof of residency in the residential parking district; and
         iii.   Vehicle registration.
      (5)   A maximum of four residential parking permits may be issued for a
dwelling zoned residential A or B and located in the residential parking
district. A maximum of two residential parking permits may be issued to the
occupant(s) of a dwelling zoned residential C, D, or E and located in the
residential parking district.
      (6)   A residential parking permit does not guarantee parking in any
particular location on the public street, but only reserves the right to park
on the public street during paid parking hours equal to the rights of any other
resident who lives in the residential parking district.
      (7)   If a resident requires more than four residential parking permits,
the resident may appeal to the parking advisory commission. An appeal for
additional residential parking permits will be considered only upon a showing
of the following:
         i.   The property provides the amount of off-street parking required
by the Dearborn Zoning Ordinance;
         ii.   Unique circumstances exist, and
         iii.   The resident demonstrates a critical need based on the lawful
use and occupancy of the property.
      (8)   Residential parking permits shall only be required during the hours
that paid parking is in effect.
      (9)   Temporary residential parking permits for guests may be obtained on
a daily or weekly basis so long as the total number of combined residential
parking permits and guest parking permits does not exceed six spaces on any
given day. Temporary residential parking permits are limited to four weekly
permits and 20 daily permits per year. Any resident requiring additional
temporary residential parking permits shall follow the appeal procedure set
forth in subsection (e)(7) above. An appeal for additional temporary
residential parking permits will be considered only upon a showing of the
following:
         i.   The occurrence of an event that does not exceed one day in
length; and
         ii.   The event at issue is one that is traditionally considered a
family event. This may include, but is not limited to: a birthday party,
graduation celebration, picnic, barbecue.
      (10)   Residences that have contracts for home health care or other
professional services on a regular basis may obtain a residential parking
permit for the individual providing those services upon a showing of the
following:
         i.   Proof of the contractual relationship, and
         ii.   The total number of permits issued to the residence shall not
exceed four.
   If the contract is for services provided one day per week, up to 52
temporary residential parking permits may be issued (an exception to subsection
(e)(9) above).
   If the contract is for services provided more than one day per week,
residential parking permit rules apply.
      (11)   This section shall not apply to commercial vehicles when the
parking of such is necessary for the purpose of making deliveries, picking up
persons, materials, goods, or merchandise, or providing service.
      (12)   There shall be no fee for residential parking permits or temporary
residential parking permits.
      (13)   Applications for parking permits may be obtained from the parking
office located in the east parking deck or on the city's web site. Completed
applications, along with supporting documentation, shall be delivered to the
parking office. Permits will be issued by the police department or its
designee.
      (14)   No provision in this section shall be interpreted to supersede
existing zoning laws.
      (15)   The requirements of this section shall be waived during any
special event sponsored by the city.
(Ord. No. 06-1086, 6-12-06; Ord. No. 06-1091, 8-7-06)
*** ARTICLE IV. - REGISTRATION OF BICYCLES ***
Sec. 18-771. - Required.
   Every person who shall own any bicycle in the city shall register such
bicycle, as provided in this article.
(Ord. No. 80-5, § 1, 7-15-80)
Sec. 18-772. - Application.
   The owner of a bicycle shall apply to the police department for registration
of such bicycle, and such registration shall be on a form furnished and
prescribed by the police department and shall provide a full description of
such bicycle, the former owner's name and the manufacturer's serial number.
(Ord. No. 80-5, § 2, 7-15-80)
Sec. 18-773. - Issuance of certificate.
   Upon registration of any bicycle, the owner thereof shall be given a
registration certificate. A duplicate of such certificate shall be kept in the
police department, and the owner shall preserve such certificate and present
the same upon demand of any officer of the police department to identify and
establish title to such bicycle.
(Ord. No. 80-5, § 3, 7-15-80)
Sec. 18-774. - Issuance of license.
   Upon registration of any bicycle, the owner thereof shall be furnished with
a license, the number of which shall correspond with the registration
certificate, such license to be permanently exhibited on the rear of such
bicycle.
(Ord. No. 80-5, § 4, 7-15-80)
Sec. 18-775. - Transfer.
   Any person owning a registered bicycle and desiring to sell or dispose of
same shall immediately execute the assignment upon the reverse side of the
certificate issued under this article and shall deliver the certificate to the
purchaser or recipient of such bicycle; such purchaser or recipient shall,
within five days from the assignment of such bicycle, re-register such bicycle
with the police department.
(Ord. No. 80-5, § 5, 7-15-80)
Secs. 18-776—18-795. - Reserved.

Sec. 18-796. - Motor carrier safety regulations; adoption by reference.
   The purpose of this article is to promote safety upon the public highways by
regulating the operation of certain vehicles, to establish the qualifications
of persons necessary for the safe operations of such vehicles, to limit the
hours of service of persons engaged in operating such vehicles, to require the
keeping of records of such operations, to provide for the assessment of fees,
and to provide penalties for the violations of this article. In so doing, Act
No. 181 of the Public Acts of 1963, as amended by Act No. 339 of the Public
Acts of 1990, and Public Act 98 of 2000, are adopted by reference, as though
set forth herein in full.
   In adopting these Public Acts, where the term "department of state police"
appears, it refers to both the department of state police and to the Dearborn
Police Department, except in those sections referencing licensing, appeals or
waivers which fall under the sole authority of the department of state police.
