*** ARTICLE VI. - WRECKERS; WRECKER AND TOWING SERVICES ***
Sec. 18-810. - Definitions.
   The following words, when used in this article, shall for the purpose of
this article, have the following meanings:
   Operator : Any person operating a wrecker or a towing vehicle for a wrecker
and towing service.
   Wrecker : Any motor vehicle adapted to or designed for towing, transporting,
conveying or moving any and all types of vehicles which are unable to be or
actually are not operated under their own power, such towing or transporting
being accomplished by means of lifting the towed vehicle totally or partially
off of the ground.
   Wrecker and towing service : The business of providing the services of one
or more wreckers for hire or use to tow, transport or move motor vehicles on
public streets.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-811. - Application of article.
   The operation of a wrecker or wrecker and towing service within the limits
of the city shall be subject to the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-812. - Identification.
   Every wrecker shall be identified by letters showing the name under which
the wrecker and towing service is operated. Such identification shall be
clearly and permanently attached on both sides of the wrecker and shall be
visible at all times.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-813. - Duty of driver to clean streets when removing wrecked vehicle.
   Whenever any driver of a wrecker removes a motor vehicle from the scene of
an accident on a public street, it shall be his duty to simultaneously remove
and carry away from the public street all glass, metal and debris, which may
have been cast upon the street as the result of the accident or collision.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-814. - Required consent or authorization to remove vehicle from street.
   It shall be unlawful for any wrecker and towing service or operator to tow
or otherwise move a vehicle from any area or portion of a public street without
either the consent of the owner or custodian of such vehicle or authorization
by a policeman or other designated official of the city.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-815. - Required request to remove vehicle from private property.
   It shall be unlawful for any wrecker and towing service or operator to block
the movement of or tow or otherwise move a vehicle from any private road,
driveway of other privately owned land or property within the city except:
      (1)   When requested to do so by the owner or custodian of the vehicle.
      (2)   When specifically requested to perform such towing service by an
owner, his agent or licensee (other than the owner, employee or agent of the
wrecker and towing service) of the private property on which the vehicle is
parked.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-816. - Notice of police department when vehicle moved without consent
of owner or custodian.
   It shall be unlawful for any wrecker or towing service or operator to fail
to notify the police department within one hour of the removal of a vehicle
from public or private property, when such vehicle was removed without the
consent of the owner or custodian of the vehicle.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-817. - Blocking movement of vehicle by its owner or custodian.
   It shall be unlawful for a wrecker and towing service or operator to block
the movement of any vehicle, other than when on the property of the wrecker and
towing service, to prevent the movement thereof by its owner or custodian who
has appeared and desires to move the vehicle.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-818. - Refusal to release vehicle prepared for towing from private
property.
   It shall be unlawful for a wrecker and towing service or operator to refuse
to release a vehicle to its owner or custodian after it has been prepared for
towing from any private property, provided that the vehicle has not yet been
towed onto a public street or highway, and further provided such owner or
custodian pays a service run fee, if demanded, of not more than the maximum
amount for such service authorized by the city council.
   For purposes of this section, "prepared for towing" means the attaching to
the vehicle of any device or object designed or intended to assist in the
moving of that vehicle.
   In the event that the owner or custodian of the vehicle demands its release
prior to the time it has been prepared for towing, it shall be unlawful for the
wrecker and towing service or operator to refuse to release the vehicle,
provided that the owner or operator promptly removes the vehicle from the
property where it is parked.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-819. - Maximum charges.
   (a)   The city council shall establish maximum service fees and charges for
wrecker and towing services involving the removal of vehicles from private
property at the direction of the property owner without the consent of the
owner or custodian of the vehicle. These fees and charges shall not apply to
the removal of commercial motor vehicles, as that term is defined in section
18-63.1 of this code, from private property at the direction of the property
owner without the consent of the owner or custodian of the vehicle.
   (b)   A towing or wrecker service provider which removes a vehicle from
private property without the consent of the owner or custodian of that vehicle
between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. shall, at the time it impounds the
vehicle, be open to the public 24 hours per day, seven days per week in order
to provide the owner or custodian of the impounded vehicle with an opportunity
to promptly reclaim the vehicle.
   (c)   A towing or wrecker service provider which removes a vehicle from
private property without the consent of the owner or custodian of that vehicle
shall accept any major credit card.
   (d)   A towing or wrecker service provider, or an employee of such a service
provider, who removes a vehicle from private property without the consent of
the owner or custodian of that vehicle, or which returns a vehicle which has
been prepared for towing from private property, shall provide a receipt when
payment in full for all charges due is received. This receipt shall contain the
following language in at least 11-point type: "The removal of vehicles from
private property, including all fees and charges related to that service, is
regulated by the City of Dearborn. Further information on these regulations and
on permitted fees can be obtained by calling the Dearborn Police Department at
(313)943-2240."
   (e)   Violation of this section constitutes a civil infraction punishable by
a civil fine of $1,000, plus costs imposed by the court. Increased fines shall
be imposed for repeat violations of this section by a person, agent,
partnership, corporation, association, company, or business.
      (1)   As used in this section, "repeat violation" means a violation
committed within six months of an admission or determination of responsibility
for a violation of this section committed by the same person, agent,
partnership, corporation, association, company, or business.
      (2)   The increased penalty for a repeat violation shall be a civil fine
of $2,500, plus costs imposed by the court.
   (f)   The chief of police, or their designee, shall review the maximum
allowable service fees and charges from other municipalities for wrecker and
towing services involving the removal of vehicles from private property at the
direction of the property owner without the consent of the owner or custodian
of the vehicle, and on an annual basis, provide a summary of their findings to
city council with a recommendation of whether the fees authorized under
subsection (a) of this ordinance should be amended.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06; Ord. No. 23-1784, 1-24-23)
Sec. 18-820. - Exception from sections 18-815 through 18-820.
   The provisions of sections
18-815 through
18-820 shall not apply when a wrecker and towing service or operator is acting
as an agent in a legal repossession of a vehicle.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Sec. 18-821. - Protection of impounded or stored vehicles and contents thereof;
insurance.
   (a)   Vehicles impounded, stored or held by a wrecker and towing service,
without the consent of the owner or custodian of the vehicle or the direction
of the police, must be protected from theft, vandalism or damage of any type
and the wrecker and towing service operator or his employees shall do nothing
to render the vehicle inoperable other than to remove the ignition key and lock
the vehicle. Items of personal property in the vehicle, but not attached or
accessory thereto, shall be safeguarded and must be surrendered or delivered to
the owner or custodian of the vehicle upon demand or release of the vehicle.
The wrecker or towing service has no lien upon personal property not attached
to or accessory to the vehicle.
   (b)   Any wrecker and towing service doing business in the city shall
maintain a garage keeper's legal liability insurance policy with an occurrence
limit of not less than $35,000.00, in addition to any insurance required under
the laws of the State of Michigan.
(Ord. No. 06-1067, 4-3-06)
Secs. 18-822—18-849. - Reserved.
*** ARTICLE VII. - MOTOR VEHICLE CODE—ADOPTION BY REFERENCE ***

effective in this state are incorporated and adopted by reference.
(Ord. No. 10-1298, 10-25-10)

City of Dearborn.
(Ord. NO. 10-1298, 10-25-10)
Sec. 18-852. - Notice to be published.
   The city clerk shall publish this code amendment in the manner required by
charter and law and shall publish, at the same time, a notice stating that a
complete copy of the Motor Vehicle Code is available to the public at the
office of the city clerk for inspection.
(Ord. No. 10-1298, 10-25-10)
Sec. 18-853. - Penalties.
   The penalties provided by the Motor Vehicle Code are adopted by reference.
(Ord. No. 10-1298, 10-25-10)
Sec. 18-854. - MCL 257.625(1)(c); adoption by reference; penalty.
   (a)   MCL 257.625(1)(c), which prohibits a person from operating a vehicle
while having a bodily alcohol content (BAC) of 0.17 grams or more per 100
milliliters of blood, 210 liters of breath, or 67 milliliters of urine, is
incorporated and adopted by reference.
   (b)   A violation of this section is punishable by one or more of the
following:
      (1)   Community service for not more than 360 hours.
      (2)   Imprisonment for not more than 180 days.
      (3)   A fine of not less that $200.00 or more than $700.00.
(Ord. No. 12-1353, 3-27-12)
Chapter 19 - WATER AND SEWERS[1] 
Footnotes:
--- (1) ---
Charter reference— Department of public works, § 10.18.
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, Ch. 5; streets, sidewalks
and other public places, Ch. 17.
*** ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL ***
Sec. 19-1. - Definitions.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   Director shall mean the director of public works.
   Premises shall include a lot or part of a lot, a building or a part of a
building, a structure, a project or any parcel or tract of land whatsoever, to
which water is being, or is to be, supplied.
   Private sewer means a drain or sewer that extends from the house or
commercial structure to the public sewer, including the wye and sewer tap.
   Public sewer means a common sewer controlled and maintained by a
governmental agency.
   Water supply system shall mean the feeder and supply mains, service pipes,
hydrants, meters and all their appurtenances, through which the city supplies
water to its consumers.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 2, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 03-986, 10-21-03)
Sec. 19-2. - Scope; enforcement.
   Every consumer of water, every owner, occupant or person in possession,
charge or control of any building, structure or premises having water service
from or through the water supply system shall be governed and be subject to the
provisions of this chapter and such rules and regulations governing or
concerning the use of water as may, from time to time, be adopted. It is hereby
made the duty of the director of water supply to enforce the provisions of this
chapter and any rules and regulations that may be adopted.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 1, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-3. - Supervision, control of work.
   (a)   No water main shall be tapped, or service laid, within the street
boundaries by other than the duly authorized employees of the division of water
supply, and only under the authority of the director; provided, however, if a
labor or help shortage has been determined by the director to exist in the
division of water supply, the director in his discretion may authorize any
person qualified to do the work, to lay and install the service pipes and
connections within the street boundaries, subject to the supervision and
direction of the director or his assistant; provided further, that the work of
tapping the city water mains shall be done only by the division of water
supply.
   (b)   The person to whom permission is granted to connect to any service or
supply pipe under the provisions of this section shall see to it that the
service or supply pipe shall be turned off at the curb stop and such service
shall not be turned on until permission is granted by the division of water
supply.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 3, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-4. - Application for service.
   When the introduction of water service is desired from the water supply
system for any building, structure or premises and before any service pipe is
laid or any connection made with any service or supply pipes of the water
supply system, an application in writing shall first be made to the division of
water supply.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 3, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-5. - Water service to premises outside city limits.
   If the owner of premises situated outside, but adjacent to the corporate
limits of the city, may desire to connect such premises to the sewer facilities
of the city so as to dispose of the sanitary sewage originating on or in
connection with such premises, and if such premises are serviced by water mains
with meters attached which are under the control and supervision of the city,
such owner may apply for a permit to install or cause to be installed the
necessary tap and connection to such sewer and the disposal of the sanitary
sewage originating on or in connection with such premises under the following
terms and conditions:
   (1)   An application in writing shall be made therefor setting forth such
information as may be required by the terms of this chapter and by the
department of public works in the city.
   (2)   The applicant and all persons claiming to be owners or occupants of
the premises to be serviced by such sewer tap and connection shall specifically
agree that they will at all times be subject to and abide by the terms and
provisions of this chapter and all other ordinances of the city, including the
zoning ordinance, building code and plumbing code, together with the reasonable
rules and regulations issued by the department of public works in the city
governing such sewer tap and connection, including the payment of the
established sewage disposal rates.
   (3)   The applicant shall pay a permit fee to the city in the amount of
$300.00 for each sewer tap for which application is made, in addition to the
cost of the service installation, at the time of making application for service
for each lot or part of lot to be serviced.
   (4)   The applicant and all persons claiming under or through him shall
further agree to and shall pay to the city quarterly and within 21 days after
the bill therefore is rendered by the city, a sewerage disposal fee based on
the amount of water consumed on such premises, as determined by the quarterly
reading of the water meter, such sewage disposal fee to be computed at the rate
of $50.20 per 1,000 cubic feet or fraction thereof, of water consumed, for all
bills rendered on or after the effective date of this section.
   (5)   No building, alteration or addition shall be permitted to be connected
to and serviced by the sewer herein authorized, unless such building is on land
adjacent to the corporate limits of the city and unless a special permit is
issued by the city for such sewer connection, and a permit fee is paid as
provided in subsection (3) of this section.
   (6)   The applicant and all persons claiming under or through him shall
further agree in writing that such applicant will, on demand of the city and
within six months after the time that facilities are available in the township
or other unit of government to the premises covered by such application for the
disposal of sanitary sewage originating thereon, discontinue the sewage
disposal service herein authorized and disconnect the sanitary sewer from the
city sewer.
   (7)   The applicant and all persons claiming under or through him shall
further agree in writing to submit the plans for any proposed building,
alteration or addition to be connected to the city sewer to the department of
building and safety in the city for its approval before any permit for sewer
tap is issued, and further agree that the department of building and safety be
allowed access to any of such buildings, as it may require from time to time
after construction is completed, to make inspections as to the quantity and
quality and sewage flow entering the sewer connection herein authorized.
   (8)   The city reserves the right to deny any application for sewer service
and facilities involving any property covered by this section, and further
reserves the right to decline to furnish a water supply to such premises and to
turn off the water supply if any of the charges for sewage disposal in this
section as set forth in this section, as well as the charges for the water
consumed on the premises, remain unpaid and delinquent for more than 60 days
after becoming due and payable.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 4, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 89-456, § 4, 6-20-89; Ord. No. 90-496,
6-19-90; Ord. No. 92-536, § 4, 7-21-92; Ord. No. 95-639, 7-5-95; Ord. No. 96-

Sec. 19-6. - Sewer disposal charge when water obtained from city.
   (a)   If the owner of premises situated outside, but which are abutting, the
corporate limits of the city receives the supply of water for such premises
from accessible city water mains, and the sanitary sewage from such premises is
not emptied directly into the city system but rather is emptied into the system
of an adjoining township or municipality and ultimately comes into the city
system for disposal, and if the cost for disposal of such sewage has not been
paid by such owner directly or indirectly to the city, the city shall collect
as a charge for such sewage disposal a sum based on the amount of water
consumed on such premises, as determined by the quarterly reading of the water
meter, such sewage disposal fee to be computed at the same rate per MCF and
with the same billing and equivalent meter charges as imposed on the residents
of the city.
   (b)   If such owner declines to pay the charge for sewage disposal, the
city, acting through the director of the water division, may discontinue and
cut off the supply of water being furnished to such owner.
   (c)   The department of public works is hereby authorized and directed to
issue a bill quarterly to every owner, as above described, for such sewage
disposal.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 5, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-7. - Service pipe specifications.
   All service pipe laid in the city shall be of not less than one inch
diameter, and all pipes of one-inch and two-inch diameter shall be of copper
tubing and of a quality to conform to the standards recommended by the United
States Bureau of Standards of the Department of Commerce for copper tubing for
water services, or any substitute approved by any government agency. All
service pipe over two-inch internal diameter shall be of cast iron and shall
conform to the specifications of the United States Bureau of Standards of the
Department of Commerce for cast iron pipe.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 6, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-8. - Prohibited connections, cross connections.
   In no case shall there be any connection between water pipes receiving their
supply from the city mains and pipes and pumps or tanks receiving their supply
from any other source. The use of such connection is prohibited whether or not
it is provided with one or more check valves.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 7, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-9. - Master plumber to make connections.
   No person shall make any attachment or connection with the pipes of the city
water supply system nor make any repairs, additions to or alterations of any
fixtures connected with the service pipes, unless registered as a master
plumber by the department of public works.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 8, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-10. - Suspension or revocation of master plumber's registration.
   The registration of any master plumber may at any time be suspended or
revoked by the director of public works for violation of any city rules,
regulations or ordinances. Plumbers must comply with such regulations as the
department of public works may adopt from time to time. No plumber shall allow
his name to be used by any other person for the purpose of doing work or
obtaining permits under his license.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 9, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-11. - Inspection of work.
   All work performed by plumbers under this chapter shall be subject to
inspection by the division of water supply, which has authority to order any
part of such work to be discontinued or changed in order that the same shall
comply with the regulations and requirements of the division of water supply.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 10, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-12. - Connection charges.
   (a)   The fees to be charged for water connection installations shall be
paid in advance to the city, and shall be in accordance with the following
schedule of service connection charges:

   (c)   Tapping sleeve and valves. Taps that utilize tapping sleeves and

   (d)   County and state road taps. Taps along all county and state roads

      (3)   Restoration bond.

Sec. 19-13. - Repairs at expense of person receiving service; notice of
shutoff.
   Every person having service from the water supply system shall, at his own
cost and expense, keep in repair all service pipes, including private pipes
leading from the shutoff stop to the building or premises, and prevent all
waste of water from such pipes. If any such pipes be permitted to remain out of
repair, the division of water supply may, after two days' prior notice in
writing, shut off the water from such premises, and whenever the water is so
shut off, it shall not be permitted to be turned on again until such pipe have
been placed in proper repair. The notice herein provided for may be served by
personal service or by mailing to the owner or occupant or person in
possession, charge or control of the premises.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 12, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-14. - Repair of sewers and drains.
   (a)   [Notice to be given.] In all cases where private drains and sewers
shall be obstructed or damaged or shall cause the obstruction or damage to any
lateral or public sewer so as to produce, in the opinion of the city engineer,
a necessity for repair, the department of public works shall give notice to the
owners or parties in interest of the disrepair, and proceed as follows:
      (1)   The city shall make the repairs to the public or lateral sewers, or
public property damaged incidentally thereto, and shall be reimbursed for such
repairs in the manner provided below.
      (2)   If the owners or parties in interest of the private drains or
sewers fail to effect the necessary repairs to the private drains or sewers
within ten days of receipt of notice of disrepair, the city shall have the
right to enter on the premises of property connected with and serviced by the
private drains or sewers and cause the necessary repairs to be made. Such
expenses incurred for repairs shall be charged to the owners or parties in
interest of the properties connected with and serviced by such private drains
or sewers in a ratable proposition, and, if not paid, the same shall be
assessed against the premises connected with such drain or sewer as a special
assessment.
   (b)   Cost assessed to owners or parties in interest. A uniform cost for
sewer repair shall be established by the city engineer at the beginning of each
fiscal year. The uniform cost for sewer repair shall include the restoration of
the grounds after repair shall be required, including appropriate soil grading
and grass seeding where applicable, but the cost for such restoration shall be
excluded from the uniform cost calculation.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 12(a), 6-4-85; Ord. No. 09-1261, 12-14-09; Ord. No. 23-
1796, 9-12-23)
Sec. 19-14.5. - Payment for repairs; options.
   If the amount of the assessment shall be $250.00 or more, the property owner
shall have the option of paying such assessment in installments over a period
not to exceed five years, each installment to bear interest at a rate not to
exceed eight percent as determined by the city council, provided further, that
any annual installment not paid within 30 days shall be assessed against the
property as a special assessment in accordance with the provisions of chapter
15 of the Charter of the City of Dearborn. The provisions of this subsection
shall apply to residential, commercial and industrial property owners.
(Ord. No. 92-535, § 12(b), 7-7-92; Ord. No. 05-1045, 6-20-05)
Sec. 19-15. - Meters—Required.
   All connections with the water mains must be prepared for the use of water
through a meter. A suitable place shall be provided for the installation of
meters that will be agreeable to the division of water supply and that will
comply with the rules and regulations of the department of public works.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 13, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-16. - Same—May have single connection.
   Meters for terraces and apartment houses may have a single connection with
meter for all connecting houses, or separate connections to each.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 14, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-17. - Same—Meters purchased from city.
   (a)   The city will furnish the meters for all service connections at a cost
plus ten percent. The meter charge shall be paid at the time service
application is made and installed at the expense of the user. Such charges
shall be in lieu of a meter service charge. The control and ownership of all
water meters shall remain with the city at all times.
   (b)   More than one meter may be used for business property occupied by more
than one tenant; any additional meters shall be paid for by the property owner
and an agreement must be signed by the owner, holding the city harmless against
any damages incurred as a result of treating the property as an entirety,
should a shutoff be required to enforce the payment of rates.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 15, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-18. - Same—Removal; prohibition.
   All persons are forbidden to interfere with or remove a water meter from any
service connection without first receiving permission from the division of
water supply. Whenever a meter is removed by permission, it must be immediately
returned to the department under penalty of having the water shut off or the
plumber's registration canceled.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 16, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-19. - Same—Responsibility of owner.
   The owner of any premises where a meter is installed shall be held
responsible for its care and protection from freezing or damage by hot water,
and from injury of interference by any person. The owner of any premises where
a meter is installed shall be liable for the full replacement costs of any
five-eighths-inch, three-fourths-inch, one-inch, one and one-half-inch and two-
inch meter that has been damaged or lost. For meters larger than two inches,
the property owner shall be liable for applicable repair or replacement costs.
These charges will be applied to the water bill.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 17, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 04-1006, 6-15-04)
Sec. 19-20. - Taking of water without permission.
   No person shall take water from any fire hydrant, valve, faucet, pipe or any
other opening connected with the water supply system, nor shall any person open
any such fire hydrant valve or faucet for the purpose of taking water, or for
any other purpose, unless such person shall first have made application for use
of water for such purpose and received permission from the fire department, or
unless such person is an employee of the city and is acting in the discharge of
his duties as such.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 18, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-21. - Lines for firefighting purposes.
   Fire lines in private property that are equipped with detector check meters
are to be used for firefighting purposes only. The quarterly water and sewage
billing for fire lines will be computed at the rate per MCF of water used, plus
the billing charge and equivalent meter charge based on the size of the water
service line instead of the size of the meter on that line except for
residential properties that do not exceed three stories in height where fire
lines are required. For those residential properties, the billing charge will
be computed based on the size of the back flow device on that line. If it is
found that the fire line is being used for any other purposes, without the
express permission of the water division, the owner of the premises shall be
subject to penalties provided for violation of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 18, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 86-368, 10-7-86; Ord. No. 10-1263, 1-
5-10)
Sec. 19-22. - Supplying water to other premises prohibited.
   No person, whether owner or occupant, or in possession, charge or control of
any building, structure or premises, in which water service is introduced, or
to which waste is supplied through the water supply system, shall be allowed to
supply other persons or families or to supply any water from such building or
premises to a building, structure or premises other than the one for which such
water service is introduced, unless permitted to do so by the division of water
supply.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 19, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-23. - Service shutoff, turn on.
   Where the water supply to any building, structure or premises shall have
been shut off or stopped by or under the direction of the division of water
supply, or in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, the water shall
not again be supplied to such building, structure or premises, or permitted to
be turned on therein, or thereto, unless a permit is first issued for that
purpose by the division.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 20, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 08-1170, 6-16-08)
Sec. 19-24. - Severance of connection.
   (a)   If it shall be found that the water supply has been turned on or into
any such building, structure or premises, in violation of the provisions of
this chapter, the division of water supply shall have the authority to order
the severing of the service or supply pipes by and through which the water is
supplied to such building, structure or premises.
   (b)   Where service or supply pipes are severed, in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter, such severing or cutting off shall be done at the
water mains or as near thereto as practicable, and no water shall again be
supplied to such building, structure or premises, or be permitted to be turned
on therein or thereto, until the cost and expense of such severing, and also
any other unpaid rates that may be still outstanding, have been paid.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 20, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-25. - Right of entry; inspections; repairs.
   (a)   The officers of the division of water supply and any and every person
delegated or authorized by the director of water supply shall have free entry
and access to every part of any building, structure or premises being serviced
by the water supply system, whenever such entry or access is deemed necessary
or advisable. In case any person in possession, charge or control of any such
building, structure or premises, into which any such officer or person shall
desire entry or access, shall refuse to permit such entry or access, or shall
do or cause to be done any act or thing for the purpose of preventing such
entry or access, the division of water supply may turn off the service from
such building, structure or premises, until notice shall have been given the
division, in writing, that entry or access will be permitted or provided, and
until such entry or access has been accomplished.
   (b)   The division of water supply shall have the power and authority to
inspect and make an examination of all pipes and fixtures connected with the
city water system and shall have the power and authority to require any pipes
or fixtures to be repaired, removed, replaced or changed, where the same are
defective or not in compliance with the provisions of this chapter, the
ordinances of the city or the rules and regulations of the division.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 21, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-26. - Obstruction to premises being serviced.
   No person shall in any manner obstruct, cause or permit to be obstructed,
access to any stop-cock, water meter, proportional, indicating or recording
device, Buffalo or shutoff box, or connection with any water main or service
pipe, by any means whatsoever, and if the owner or person in possession, charge
or control of such premises, after proper notifications, shall fail to remove
such obstruction, the division of water supply may withhold water service to
such building, structure or premises, until the obstruction shall be removed.
The division of water supply shall have the power to require that an outside
reading device be installed at the owner's expense if access to the water meter
is deemed hazardous to the representatives of the division of water supply.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 22, 6-4-85)
Sec. 19-27. - Deductions or rebates prohibited.
   (a)   No deduction shall be made or rebate allowed to any consumer of water
by or on account of any leakage or alleged leakage in any water pipe, tank or
other apparatus or device, provided that the utility manager of the water and
sewer division, department of public works, may make an adjustment not to
exceed 50 percent of the amount of the leakage and for a period not to exceed
one quarterly billing, per calendar year. Such adjustments shall be made only
for the water portion of the bill, unless the consumer can demonstrate to the
satisfaction of the utility manager that none of the water leakage entered the
sewer system. To become eligible for such adjustments, consumers must
demonstrate that the leak has been properly repaired.
   (b)   An adjustment in excess of 50 percent of the amount of the leakage
shall be at the discretion of the director of public works.
      (1)   The property owner must show the existence of extraordinary
circumstances not of the property owner's making or due to the failure of the
property owner to act.
         i.   "Extraordinary circumstances" shall not include ability to pay
but will include unusual circumstances or events that could not have been
avoided by reasonable action or behavior on the part of the water division
customer. Failure to observe an apparent defect or to mitigate such defect once
observed shall not constitute extraordinary circumstances.
      (2)   No further adjustment will be permitted.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 23, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 04-1006, 6-15-04; Ord. No. 10-1278, 6-
21-10)
Sec. 19-28. - Rates, when payable.
   Water rates shall be paid quarterly. The following rates for water supply
and service shall be charged on all bills rendered on and after the effective
date of July 1, 2025.
   The rate for non-fireline accounts per MCF for water is $35.20 plus a
capacity charge of $18.72, per equivalent factor based on the meter size as
shown in the following schedule. The rate for fireline accounts per MCF for
water is $35.20, plus a capacity charge of $28.39 per equivalent factor based
on meter service size as shown in the following schedule.
THE RATE PER MCF FOR WATER IS $35.20 PLUS A CAPACITY CHARGE OF $18.72 PER

ACCOUNTS. THE RATE PER MCF FOR SEWER IS $50.20 PLUS A CAPACITY CHARGE OF $44.44

Sec. 19-29. - Sewage treatment rates.
   (a)   Volume of flow. The charges for sewage treatment shall be based upon
water consumption, as indicated on the water bill and shall be billed
quarterly. Such rates shall be computed on the basis of $50.20 per MCF of water
used and a quarterly basic service charge of $44.44 per equivalent factors
based on meter size as shown in the schedule in section
19-28. These rates will be effective on all bills rendered on or after July 1,
2025.
   (b)   Industrial waste control (IWC) and high strength surcharge. In
addition to the aforementioned volume of flow rate of $50.20 per MCF, specific
industrial and commercial firms identified by the Great Lakes Water Authority,
and contributors of certain pollutants in concentrations which exceed normal
sewage, will be surcharged quarterly. The surcharge rates established and
adopted by the Great Lakes Water Authority shall be passed through to the
identified industrial and commercial firms with the same impact and effective
dates as adopted by the Great Lakes Water Authority.
   (c)   Industrial waste control charge. In addition to the aforementioned
volume of flow rate and the high strength surcharge, specific industrial and
commercial users identified by the Great Lakes Water Authority will also be
charged an industrial waste control charge.
   (d)   Nonresidential flow surcharge. For funding of the activities of the
industrial waste control section, a monthly charge shall be assessed. The
surcharge rates established and adopted by the Great Lakes Water Authority
shall be passed through with the same impact and effective dates as adopted by
the Great Lakes Water Authority.
(Ord. No. 85-326, § 25, 6-4-85; Ord. No. 91-517, § 25, 7-2-91; Ord. No. 92-536,
§ 25, 7-21-93; Ord. No. 95-639, 7-5-95; Ord. No. 96-679, 7-16-96; Ord. No. 97-
706, 6-17-97; Ord. No. 98-726, 6-16-98; Ord. No. 99-771, 7-6-99; Ord. No. 00-
822, 6-20-00; Ord. No. 01-853, 6-28-01; Ord. No. 02-903, 6-18-02; Ord. No. 03-
970, 6-17-03; Ord. No. 04-1006, 6-15-04; Ord. No. 05-1045, 6-20-05; Ord. No.
06-1080, 5-15-06; Ord. No. 07-1131, 6-18-07; Ord. No. 08-1170, 6-16-08; Ord.
No. 09-1230, 6-15-09; Ord. No. 10-1273, 6-7-10; Ord. No. 11-1332, 6-20-11; Ord.
No. 12-1358, 6-12-12; Ord. No. 13-1402, 6-11-13; Ord. No. 14-1427, 5-20-14;
Ord. No. 15-1465, 5-14-15; Ord. No. 16-1541, 6-14-16; Ord. No. 17-1580, 5-23-
